0.1: Welcome to Tracen Academy! (Character Generation Part 1)

"Yo. You want one?"

Daylight. The scent of fresh green grass on the air, a swathe of clear blue skies high up. The face of a mysterious umamusume dangling upside down mere centimeters from your face, a carrot half-way between her grinning wide mouth.

You do the obvious thing and stare. It's an umamusume about the same age as you, perching from the sheer force of her ankles and soles atop some type of marble statue. The gentle trickling of water brushes your ears, but it's the least of your concerns. The girl has a dimpled nose, short triangular shaped uma-ears, a daisy as her cravat—and that's all your mind registers before she widens her grin, chomps down in the center of the carrot with a loud, audible crunch, and you realise with an electrifying jolt that you indeed exist.

You scramble backwards with your tail stiff as a board, and she bursts into laughter.

"Sorry, sorry!" The mysterious stranger calls amidst a second bite, as your arms proceed to imitate a windmill in a hurricane. "You were standing there in front of the fountain, spacing out with this blank look in your eyes. I thought you were sleepwalking. The vice-president gets mad at students who do that, so began trying all kinds of tactics. I waved my hands in front of you, poked you in the shoulder, even tried to shove you off into the water but I didn't want to get you a cold and you weren't budging even with the few droplets I flicked on you, so—"

She leaps off her soles of her feet, pirouetting through the air in a clean loop and lands to a solid finish on the stones in front of you, dropping into a mild curtsy.

"I thought you were praying to the Three Goddesses."

Only the last part of the sentence makes any lick of sense to you. You put some distance with a shuffle backwards, your ears straightened and folded slightly back, keeping your legs crouched in the preparation for a sprint. This is wariness. Behavior in the face of so many questions, biased towards neither umamusume nor human. Your brow wrinkles in the face of the girl's cheeky smile. Who is she? What's her deal getting so close and dangling a delectable treat in your face? It's a nice carrot, crunchy and delicious and you could really do with one—no.

Where exactly in Japan are you? As much as you enjoy bright sunlight on your skin, you're not sure about being suddenly transported into the middle of nowhere.

The mysterious umamusume, in response, winks. She steps aside, sweeping her right arm outwards. The scene in front of you unfolds like a great diorama. You stare. You blink. Your heart, which has only just calmed down, begins to beat fast again.

Three stoic great umamusume, clad in ancient flowing robes, each one pouring a small waterfall to the basin of the fountain. The water is crystal-clear and smells of a freshness that thrums with the strings of nostalgia within you. Behind it: a grand school building, of sturdy navy rooftops and pristine brick walls, topped by a bell tower and a giant steel running shoe enshrining a running shoe. The sun shines from behind the building, casting a great shadow across the pathway and the surrounding trees.

You crane your neck upwards, swallowing with a hefty, excited gulp. Your hand flies to your chest. This should be a dream, but the scents, the ambient sounds—could this be…?

"Yep!" The mysterious umamusume smiles. She spreads her arms wide. "Welcome to Tracen Academy, newbie!"

The excitement steadily building up inside of you threatens to explode out of your chest. If your tail was stiff before, it's damn near about to detach from your hind bones and rocketing over the place now.

Tracen Academy. Tracen Academy!

Any umamusume worth their salt living in Japan needs no further explanation about the history of this place, but your mind is swimming so fast, the blood pumping so loud, that you cannot help but replay everything you know about the academy in its head. For starters, Tracen Academy isn't technically its full name. In actuality, it's the main branch of an organization called Japan Umamusume Training Schools and Colleges, located in Fuchu, Tokyo. The academy comprises eighty hectares, contains over two thousand students inside its top-class facilities and fully dedicates itself to the art of umamusume racing.

But, don't believe for a second this is just some second-rate college borrowing the local park. Tracen Academy is an institution that absorbs the worthy and sculpts the elite. You either need to pass a grueling combo of entrance exam and interview, or receive a direct invitation for a regional —the chances of either being inarguably slim. Once you enter, there's no slacking. It's lessons, scrimmages and intense physical training all the way down amongst students with just as if not more ambition as you. But, once you break past it all and step onto the racetrack with that support and experience behind you…

"Dreaming about winning a G1 already, newbie?" The mysterious umamusume chimes in.

You blink, then blush. Dreams of gold and confetti flash out of your mind. Goodness, were you saying all of that out loud?

She giggles. "Not really. But I could see it on your face. You're not the first uma I've seen with stars in their eyes. Every newbie dreams about winning a triple tiara, right?"

Heck, even a G3 win would put your name on the board alongside some mighty fine cash. That's a tall reach for most racing academies. Inside Tracen? It's standard. Students enter and come out with G2s and G1s under their belt. The best ones go onto the Triple Crown circuit and become small billionaires with all the prize money and connections. Few other institutions internationally can compete. Tracen's motto includes the term 'eclipse' for a damn good reason.

And you're here. You're here. Standing behind those hallowed gates, enrolled, prepared, tuition fees paid and ready to fulfil your dream as the best umamusume racer in all of Japan!

You punch a fist and barely restrain from screaming out loud. This is the best day of your life!

"Whoa, whoa!" The mysterious umamusume says, clapping her hands. She steps forward and pats you solidly on the shoulder. "Hold yourself, newbie. Take a moment to relax. The academy doors aren't flying off their hinges. We don't want you keeling over—again!"

She winks, and you blush again. It's at this point you notice she's dressed in the standard Tracen Academy uniform of purple-lilac with a long, white skirt. A racing-shoe shaped buckler holds up the large ribbon at the front. Since she's in the uniform and you're not, this umamusume is obviously your senpai.

"Besides." Her grip grows a tad bit steadier. "I don't think we've introduced ourselves. Do you know who I am?"

Should you?

"Take a guess." She says, her tone lighthearted.

You ponder, taking your time in fear of flubbing the answer and disappointing your new senpai. Firstly, she's not a human, so that rules out a trainer or any of the faculty. She has brown hair, a confident disposition and is clearly a senior figure here, having met your in person, so she must be…Air Groove, the vice-president of the school council here!

"Nope. Not serious enough."

…the honored school president Symboli Rudolf!

"I'm not awful at making puns, so wrong again."

Okay, so authority figures are out. You How about…the up-and-coming rookie with a smile on her face, Special Week!

"Still no. Getting warner, though."

You're starting to feel an uncomfortable feeling down your back. The type that involves prickling of tail hairs and trailing of sweat and often occurs when you reach for a nice dandelion candy and instead find the wrapper instead.

You raise a trembling finger. G-Gold Ship, notorious trickster and shockingly gifted racer, in a disguise…?

Your new senpai smiles. "Close, but…"

…no cigar.

You deflate and your new senpai chuckles.

"Sorry, sorry, but you've got such cute cheeks that I had to play that little prank on you. You won't find my name in the papers or even online. This uniform…" She tugs at the side of her skirt with a gentle smile, inspecting it for a second. "…is more of a cosplay. I'm older than I look, see, and take the role of more of a supporter mixed in with bureaucrat. Good job on the trivia, though."

You rub the back of your neck. You can't call yourself interested in Tracen if you can't name some of its prominent racers.

"That's not to say the umamusume you mentioned are not at this academy. They are. They're just busy with their own duties at the moment, so here I am," Your new senpai says. "Please don't call me a teacher, though. I'm fine with being a mere senpai. As for my name…"

Your new senpai raises a coquettish finger to her lips and winks again.

"You can call me Plain Jane!"

Plain Jane. It's a good name. It rhymes off the tongue. It sounds strong, despite the theme of normality. It also sounds vaguely foreign.

"And I promise to help make your new life here absolutely MAGICAL!"

Her words burst through the air, echoing off the statue and the surrounding buildings. Her arms are stretched wide again, as if to embrace you from this short distance. You smile back, your emotions soaring. Hope fluttering. The wind rustles the grass, and clouds float gaily across the clear sky. Your blood pumps in a steady rhythm inside your heart.

The academy bell remains quiet. So does the rest of the academy grounds. That's strange, you think to yourself. It's the middle of the day. There should be students in the classrooms, or practicing on the turf, or enjoying lunch in the sunshine, and so on. There's not even a bird chirping in the air.

"Hey, newbie. One quick question." Plain Jane says, cutting your wandering thoughts off. "How'd you arrive at this academy?"

You rack your brain, feeling a cold sweat on your brow. That's such an easy question, isn't it? It shouldn't require this much brainpower. You…

You were…

You are halted by a shift in Plain Jane's gaze. On the surface, it's normal. Playful, gentle, yet now there's something lurking beneath it. It's not sinister, you don't think she intends to harm you, but strangely expectant. As if she's dug into your past and unearthed a treasure, before you could even lay your hands on the shovel.

Before you can respond, Plain Jane takes out a clipboard and pins a paper form to it. She whips out a pen and snaps it open with a sharp click.

"I think this is a good time as ever to get your paperwork sorted out." Plain Jane's grin stretches. "Question one. Name and birthdate…"

>>ON YOUR MARKS, GET SET…CHARACTER GENGERATION!

FAQ & 1st part of Chargen
FAQ

What's an Uma Musume?

Uma Musume is a gacha/sports-anime franchise from Japan in which anime girls based on racehorses compete in thrilling and exciting races. Idol singing is available too. Knowledge about it isn't necessary for this quest, but the mobile game is free and the anime is easily accessible online (and are both of decent quality). Start with Season 1 if you're watching the anime, since that gives the best overview of how the world works.

What mechanics will this quest be running?

A mildly simplified version of AGG. Make choices, get into encounters, win EXP, upgrade self with AP points and repeat. There may be some dice rolling for components of the races like in the mobile game. Feel free to make suggestions or post criticism since this is both my first quest in a while and my first AGG one.

Where does the magical girl component come in?

Soon. The tone won't be anything close to the level of Madoka Magica (or my other quests). It'll probably be as dark as Persona, if that helps draw comparison.

Magical umamusume stuff has special stats, which will be revealed later.

Do the umamusume have to idol dance?

Yes. Are you going to tell them they can't? They can run faster than cars, you know.

Where's my trainer?

You'll meet them eventually.

Why do the Golds (Gold Ship, Orfevre etc.) act like a family in this story when they're not much in canon?

Due to the stipulation listed in the Fallen Heiress backstory (see below). At the time, I was struggling to come up with a third major family alongside the Mejiros and the Symbolis and created the Gold Clan to fill that hole. The reasoning was that their greater proliferation of interactions within canon (more so than other names, such as the Naritas) made them more appropriate. It was a decision made when I was less familiar with Umamusume and I'm not certain I would've made it today, but it is what it is so we're sticking with them.

Bear in mind my version of the Gold Clan is fanon for the purposes of MagiDerby and shouldn't be taken as canon.

How much do the umas adhere to their canon personalities?

I strive to adhere to canon personalities as much as possible. For some characters, that's unfortunately not an option (you'll know who they are when you see them).

If your perception of canon characters is corrupted by the versions I write...um, try not to let that happen.

Can I support this fanfic?

You bet you can! Read, comment, vote, or you can donate to my Ko-Fi here.

Alright, let's get Part 1 of Character Generation underway.

Firstly, all umamusume are female. There will be no selecting of gender today. Secondly: the name. The only restrictions on the name are to not make it too meme-worthy (I will not be writing an uma called Skibidi Rizz) and also to not imply a relationship with an existing canon character (unless a selected Archetype allows it).

Your character possesses the following Core Attributes representing their innate aptitudes. They are:

NameDescriptionExample RepresentativesSpeedRepresents how fast and agile you are.Silence Suzuka, Tokai Teio, Sakura Bakushin OStaminaRepresents physical durability and toughness.Oguri Cap, Super Creek, Mayano Top GunPowerRepresents raw physical strength.Narita Brian, Mejiro Ryan, GentildonnaGutsRepresents mental fortitude and willpower.Special Week, Grass Wonder, Daiwa ScarletWitsRepresents intelligence and/or wisdom.Agnes Tachyon, Air Groove, Eishin FlashPsycheRepresents charisma and the ability to socialize.Mejiro McQueen, Symboli Rudolf, Nice NatureInsightRepresents knowledge and resonance with mysterious forces.Gold Ship, Manhattan Cafe, Matikanefukukitaru

All attributes will benefit you in your racing and magical umamusume career in one way or another. They will start at 8, which is the average for newbies at Tracen. For reference, the average male human has 3-5 for Speed/Stamina/Power/Guts.

You may select two Attributes to tag. Tagging will raise an Attribute it by 1, codify it as among your best strengths, and improve its scaling for any associated skills (+3 for every Attribute point instead of +2). You cannot tag the same Attribute twice.

Then, pick your starting Archetype. This will define your background.

Honor Student

Study. School. Sleep. That was how your parents charted the course of your life for the past decade, as Japan is a competitive nation that grinds up the lazy into fertilizer for the elite. Yet, as you struggled through backbreaking exams and endless school duties, you firmly held onto your dreams of becoming a top umamusume racer in your heart. Then, your parents allowed you to go to Tracen Academy, because they offer scholarships that can save a lot of money. Problem solved?

You were a diligent student growing up. Gain more points to distribute amongst your Intellectual skills. You also unlock another Intellectual skill. You excelled in all sorts of studies. +1 to Wits. Your parents taught you how to optimize your time. Increased EXP gain when performing Intellectual or Social feats.

Devotee

With legacy comes legend, and with legend comes religion. The Three Goddesses, Lady Epona, Sleipnir…the hands of these divine authorities extend around the globe, as not even umamusume are exempt from the desire to be guided by a higher power. You were born into an organization dedicated to one of these deities, then raised to serve its greatest ideals—including racing, hence your enrollment into Tracen Academy as part of an exchange program. How will you adapt to this institution of free-spirited, ambitious umamusume?

You were raised in myth, scripture and ceremony. +1 to Guts and Insight. The seniors back home dropped hints about mysterious forces in the world. Gain more points to distribute amongst your Esoteric Skills. The fulfilment of your religious duties is not a request. It is an absolute. The quest will now enforce religious obligations upon you (dependent on which religion you pick in the next phase of chargen). Complete them to receive bonus rewards, such as EXP, skill upgrades and more. Starting Perks will take on a religious theme.

Little League Boss

Oh, how the world felt small. How the other kids on the block rose up against you in the face of your ambition. And what did you do in response? You crushed them. Broke the chains that bound you, then broke the spirits of your rivals in competition. Then, you gathered them all under one banner, beneath which parties were had, havoc was wrought and many adults grew searing headaches. But, you quickly became aware you were more than aware you were a big fish in a tiny pond, and so you packed your bags and headed for Tracen Academy to make your name known…

Physical force was the name of the game back home. Gain more points to distribute amongst your Physical skills. You beat all the other kids through the school of hard knocks. +1 to Speed, Stamina or Power. (your choice). Racing skills also start off at a higher default value. The other kids flocked to your innate charisma. You may also take any rivals you beat completely as your underlings, earning their obedience and allowing them to perform checks for you (this counts as a Perk).

Umafluencer

You think racing alone is enough to make it as a top umamusume? Nah, nah. This is the modern world, sweetheart. We've got ads in the sky, races on the big screen, big data and information flowing faster than the speed of light! We've got uma and human stealing hearts and making names without catching an eye of their audience in person. And while you're a minnow in the big virtual sea, a whole 100+ followers to your name, that doesn't mean you can't try. So draft those Umatter posts and snap those Umastagram photos, because Tracen Academy's gonna be the stage for your racing AND online debut!

To influence is to understand (and manipulate) others. +1 to Psyche. You trained yourself to socialize like mad. Gain more points to distribute amongst the Social skills. Unlocks an extra Social skill. The Internet hovers at your fingertips and you know how to put on a good show. Unlocks a unique Perk involving gaining social media followers for benefits, such as EXP, skill points and best of all—information. Prestige (i.e. how famous you are) is easier to gain. Just don't get cancelled online.

Outcast

Your mother was a formidable racer in her time. A true burgeoning flower. However, at the cusp of winning the famed Triple Crown, she committed a truly heinous act—she cheated. Sabotage, performance-enhancing drugs…the exact details don't matter. Her legacy was tarnished, her crimes publicized, and you were caught in the crossfire. Scorned and shunned all your life, Tracen Academy is your last-ditch attempt to escape your mother's shadow and forge a path of your own.

Life was harsh, and you had to learn fast. Increased EXP gain for everything. The world refused to get your mother's sins. Difficulty increased. Those who are familiar with your mother will start off with a negative opinion of you. Yet, you were defiant to climb to the top. You practiced like a madman. Select one of the following: +1 AP, Tag an extra Racing skill, +30 starting bonus to any skill (your choice).

OPTIONAL SPECIAL CONDITION: THE FALLEN HEIRESS.

For the Outcast, You may take the family name of Symboli, Gold, Satono or Mejiro. By doing so, your mother will now be a exile from one of those prestigious umamusume families. This means all existing characters belonging to that family (including friends, servants and associates) will now possess a negative opinion of you. Some will shun you. Others will try to stomp you out from running altogether.

Repeat all of the Outcast's effects again. You may choose differently for the repeat of effect #3. All members of your ex-family will begin their Social Links at Rank -2 or lower. Rewards for progressing their Social Links are increased. Note: The Gold family includes: Gold Ship, Stay Gold, Orfevre, Dream Journey, Fenomeno, Nakayama Festa

Amnesiac

A room you do not recognise. Keys that do not fit in any lock. You know nothing, hence you ARE nothing—save for the sole goal of entering Tracen Academy and racing to the top. Where this motivation comes from, or who bequeathed upon you this precious uniform is something you'll have to discover by yourself.

You may choose a family name of a canon character for this option. (This will have no initial effect, unlike Outcast)

The fool starts off on her journey. Restrictions on skill tagging are lifted (other Archetypes must one tag in all skill categories except Esoteric; you can choose as many tags as available in any category). Luck will appear as an Esoteric skill. An empty bottle is easily filled. Alignment shifts will occur more quickly. +1 AP. Fragmented memories: Gain an extra starting Perk.

0.2: Your name is Satono Ruby (Character Generation Part 2)

Satono Ruby.

Your name is Satono Ruby, daughter of…

[X] Plan Uma Lock

-[X] Name: Light Chase Satono Opal

-[X] Guts

-[X] Speed

-[X] Outcast

--[X] Tag: Pain Threshold

…Satono Opal.

To give her some credit, Plain Jane's smile does not shrink. She does not turn on her heel and walk off. There is still a familiar hesitation, an awkwardness to your very nature that you become all too accustomed over the breadth of your life.

Anyone vaguely in touch with the umamusume racing industry knows the name of Satono Opal. The red-haired stepchild of the previous Satono head who showed surprising promise. The up-and-coming winner of multiple G3s and G2s who broke her own body's limits time and time again. The chosen daughter who against all odds was destined to finally break the Satono family jinx, and then did so in a magnificent photo finish—until her pre-race actions were investigated, and she was discovered to have laid sabotage to several of her opponents.

Lucifer himself couldn't have fallen harder from grace.

Flashes from the past bleed in your mind's eye. Walls of newspaper pages depicting your mother's kowtow, screams and shouts behind heavy ornate doors, masses of faces that were once friendly suddenly ripping off their masks to reveal the bitter and the cold. To cheat in an industry where fairness is paramount, whose history extends back to the era of umamusume tribals racing on the ancient steppes, is a path not even asylum patients dare tread.

She didn't even get twenty-four hours to say her goodbyes before the Satono family estate slammed its gates and locked her out together. You were collateral, and thus you soon followed.

Flash-forward. Give the pot years of the same treatment. Stir in the yearning of unanswered questions, then sprinkle in salt of an uphill battle that seemingly extends with each passing month. The end result bears an oxymoron. Her daughter has joined the very same academy that built her stardom, to pursue similar dreams, against what the rest of the world might call common sense.

A bitter smile stretches over your mouth. Were this in public, you might have laughed.

"I'm sorry."

You blink in response.

"I'm sorry for how society treated to you, Satono Ruby." Plain Jane says. She bows her head slightly. "You are not your mother. You didn't deserve to be shunned and mistreated for her own actions."

You almost scoff. These are mere platitudes. Plain Jane is a complete stranger. She doesn't know you, or what you've been through since your exile from the Satono family.

Plain Jane smiles sadly. "They are. But I thought I might as well lay the truth bare, since we are both aware of your circumstances. A young student like you should have one companion at this academy, at the very least."

She then advances. She's fast, even for a slight movement, and also half a head taller than you. You find this out as she gets close and pats you on the shoulder again, then gives you a gentle caress along with it. It's ticklish. It's filled with a sense of compassion and warmth that you don't find often from strangers. Your heart flutters despite your brain scrambling to put up your usual barriers.

You suppose you appreciate the honesty.

Plain Jane then picks out a carrot candy from her uniform's pocket and hands it to you. You hold it up in the sunlight and recognise the brand as an expensive one. They sell these types packaged in pretty little boxes that are sold in high-class department stores. They're the same type you and your sisters Satono Crown and Satono Diamond used to sneak out from the mansion pantry behind the maids' backs, once upon a time.

Your sisters' faces flash in your head, firstly blurry memories from childhood, then television reports on the big screen as young teenagers. Charities. Social events. Apologies to the sponsors for not winning a G1 over the Mejiros or the Gold clan. They still couldn't do it, even with all the advanced training regimes, business deals and the purge of your mother's existence from the family history.

You bite down on the candy. The slick core spurts out from its fragile shell. There's a bitterness inside.

Satono Crown's already enrolled. Satono Diamond will make her debut soon. You suppose you will meet them on the track once the debuts end and the real competition starts. It will be a meeting of a lifetime. It will be first contact in ages. It will be…

…you're not sure. What will you even say to them? What are they going to say to you? Crown was just as scandalized when the old man explained the full details. She looked at you as if your face had suddenly sprouted spider legs. Diamond was too young to understand—you remember her crying a lot—but surely she's grown accustomed to the family routine. To treat your mother like a punching bag when her name is ever mentioned at all. Does the famed Satono charity extend to their own misfortune?

It's funny. Such dwelling on the past should incite clenched fists or a tightness in your chest, yet your mind is clear-headed today. Perhaps it's the lack of stares and points from your new classmates. Perhaps the entire academy is at an assembly, or a mass school trip, thereby granting you some measure of peace.

You're not going to question it. Not yet.

"There are good umamusume in this academy, Satono Ruby. I think you might like the young Mejiro heiress, and that Oguri miss will gladly share a table if you buy her a free rice ball. The student council president is both fair and strict, as is the rest of her council. They will tolerate many antics, but never discrimination, even from the Trainers."

Plain Jane beckons with her hand.

"Come on. The day's great, and we've got plenty of time. I'll show you around."

And so you follow.

The hallways and the classrooms remain still as you go through your little tour. The front hall, the gymnasium, the turf and more flash by in a blur. Plain Jane bounces along in front, rattling off facts and anecdotes with an excited sparkle in her eye. The wide expanse of this academy is traversed in seemingly no time at all.

You're excited. You truly are. Honest.

Plain Jane recognises your trepidation. She's kind enough not push back on it. Instead, she asks you about your history, and you find yourself inclined to answer, just a bit…

[The Outcast: Fallen Heiress Archetype was selected. Difficulty raised. Difficulty raised even further! Acquired 2 extra tags for Racing Skills! Tags set to Dodge and Racing Tactics.]

[Tagged Attributes set as Speed and Psyche.]

Here are your Attributes. Tagged ones are marked with a *

Welcome to part 2 of Character Generation. Before we talk about skills, we need to talk about some other stats.

Firstly: Prestige. This represents how famous you are. You gain it from placing well in races, winning awards, progressing Social Links and anything else that gets your name out there. The more Prestige you accumulate, the more doors and opportunities open for you.

Secondly: Mood. Players of the mobile game will recognise this. This stat represents how well your mental state is. The better you feel, the easier checks become (and the opposite is true). The range of Mood states from worst to best are: Awful, Bad, Normal, Good, Great.

Thirdly: Alignment. You have two axes: Lawful to Chaotic & Light or Dark. The first pair is standard. Lawful characters abide by the order and authority, whereas Chaotic characters disregard said order for personal freedom and autonomy. They are wholly defined by your own actions.

Light and Dark, however, are representative of society's perspective of you. Light characters are treated as the heroes, whereas Dark characters are seen as villains, similar to the face and heel terms from wrestling, respectively. A favorite such as Tokai Teio, who is seen as the hero of the turf, would receive the Light alignment. Rice Shower, despite being a sweet and gentle girl in reality, would receive the Dark alignment for destroying multiple winstreaks and crushing the hopes of fans.

Light and Dark are not equal to good and evil. The only measure of good and evil that matters is your very own.

Now we can talk about skills. They measure your various techniques, talents and competencies. Tagged ones are also marked with a *. Here they are:

Racing Skills

Racing is the soul of an umamusume. No matter who you are or what you become, these skills will always be here for you.

NameDescriptionScalingValueAccelerationGo fast or go slow. Optimize your spurts and paces.POW26BreathingControl your internal pacing. Reduce fatigue.STA26Dodge*Evade the competition. Zip out of tight spots.SPE52FrenzyProject your fighting spirit. Disrupt and debuff your opponents.PSY37NutritionRefine your own physiology. Eat like a champion.STA26Pain ThresholdEndure the body's agony. It won't slow you down.GUT26Racing Tactics*Chart the path to victory. Then enact it on the fly.WIT41TraversalWeather, grounds and starting positions. Conquer them all.INS26

Physical Skills

Skills related to the usage of your physical body (outside of racing).

NameDescriptionScalingValueBrawlPut your guard up. Then deflect and inflict punishing blows.POW26DancingThe artform of the body. Impress with terrific moves.SPE37Hand-Eye CoordinationReady? Aim and fire.INS26SneakDampen your presence. Avoid detection.SPE37

Intellectual Skills

Skills that require the usage of intellect, wisdom and general brainpower.

NameDescriptionScalingValueForeign LanguagesMaster the multilingual. Understand all kinds of people.PSY37LogicThe study of correct reasoning. Put puzzle pieces together.WIT26HistoryExcavate the past. Bring its treasures to the future.WIT26Visual MathematicsCreate mind models from numbers. Estimate and calculate inside your head.WIT26

Social Skills

Skills focused on communicating and socializing with others.

NameDescriptionScalingValueComposureKeep a stiff upper lip. Stonewall them out.GUT26IntimidateInstill fear in others. Dominate them into submission.POW26PersuasionConstruct powerful arguments. Sway your opposition with words.PSY37SubterfugeLie, cheat and deceive. Nothing matters except that you win.WIT26

Esoteric Skills

Skills that activate or focus around the mysterious forces in the world.

NameDescriptionScalingValueArtistryWork your creativity. Create masterpiecesINS26InspectionPeer into the corners of the world. Uncover hidden secrets.INS26InstinctGut feelings, hunches and paranoia. Anticipate the unexpected.GUT26

Skill values were calculated at 10 + (ATTRIBUTE VALUE x SCALING). Tagged Skills were then given a +15 bonus. You can increase your skills by levelling up, completing objectives and raising Social Links.

You may assume the following about Skills and Attributes:

0 is nothing, 20-25 is beginner, 40-50 is average, 80-100 is good, and 120-150 is great. Checks will use multiples of 10. Tagged skills automatically gain +5 whenever you level up. More skills may be unlocked in the future. The list is not exhaustive. There will be checks exclusive to Attributes or Skills (similar to the Fallout games). Not all checks are related to racing. Racing skills may be applicable outside racing. Reassigning a skill's scaling is possible.

Now let's talk about Traits. These are your Starting Perks, based on potential histories.

Gifted

Your mother's genes passed down well. You were born so strong you were able to course through the early stages of your life on sheer innate aptitude alone. In exchange, you neglected to work on learning new skills. This may or may not come to bite you back in the ass.

Round the values of all skills down to the nearest ten (e.g. 26 becomes 20, 32 becomes 30). -15 less initial Skill points to distribute. Fewer skill points will be available when levelling up. Gain 9 points to spend on +1 for any Attribute (cannot go over +3 for a single Attribute). More chances to increase Attributes or improve their scaling will appear. (This effect is applied after the above) Cannot be taken with Skilled.

Skilled

Your birth was underwhelming, to say the least. A frailer body, a poorer constitution, slower legs—these failings should not have happened much, if it weren't for your mother losing her support network post-scandal. To compensate for your poor genetics, you worked extra hard on learning new skills.

-1 to all Attributes except tagged ones. Tagged Attributes will lose their improved scaling (i.e. goes from x3 to x2) +10 to all skills. Tagged skills will now gain automatic +10 when levelling up. More opportunities to gain skill points will become available. Cannot be taken with Gifted.

Eater of Umillions

*munch* *chomp* *slurp* Whaddaya want? Can't you see I'm busy here? *chomp* *munch* Hah…fine. You're an umamusume. You like eating. You like it A LOT. You feel better and get stronger when eating. The reverse is true. Now can you piss off and let me get back to my… *slurp* *gurgle* *burp*

Gain a temporary buff of +1 to tagged Attributes and +10% to tagged Skills after eating well. Gain a temporary debuff of -1 to tagged Attributes and -10% to tagged Skills while starving. +10 to Nutrition. Gain the Eating skill (Physical, scales with POW)

Orphaned

Let's not mince words. Your mother abandoned you as a child. Didn't even bother to leave a note, or give you a kiss on the forehead before she up and vanished, leaving you behind in the Satono family mansion all by yourself. You escaped soon after. You spent a great deal of your childhood drifting from street to street, foster home to foster home. As a result, you grew some unconventional smarts, as well as a tendency to favor those your own age…

Social Links with academy students and other underaged individuals are easier. Social Links with Trainers and other adult individuals are harder. +15 to all Social skills and +1 to Wits.

Punctuality

People took one look at your mother's name and immediately found an excuse to trash you. You refused to give them another. You pride yourself on your punctuality, arriving at appointments nary a second early or late. This extends to the race track too. Also, if you can be on time, why can't anyone else?

Late starts in races will never happen. Early starts in races will never happen. Mood may decrease if someone you know is late. +15 to Inspection.

Madness Enhancement

You don't remember how it happened—only that once the haze faded from your eyes, a vending machine was busted, several trees were knocked down, and all the poor souls haranguing with you had gone stark-white with fear...or were flat on their face. It seems that once your emotions swing high or low enough, a rush akin to an ancient berserker's fury overtakes you, and you lose rationality in exchange for enhanced capabilities on the track.

+1 to Power and Stamina. +15 to Frenzy. Unlocks the Ecstatic Mood (above Great) and the Horrendous Mood (below Awful). Control of self begins to slip at Great and higher or Awful and lower; gain +1 to all Attributes except Wits and Psyche when this happens. You cannot be easily intimidated under this influence.

Internalized Stigma

Your mother was ashamed of herself. You, her daughter, perhaps even more so. All the jeers, death threats and missed opportunities coalesced in a self-flagellating desire to make up for your mother's sins. They wouldn't accept you for who you were/ so you concocted an alter ego of an upstanding, model umamusume citizen, who helps at the drop of a hat—even at the cost of her own well-being.

Creates an alias for yourself (please specify a name). While using that alias, negate any consequences of your real self's reputation, gain +1 AP and shift your alignment to Light-Law. Social Link progression and Social skill checks become easier under this alias. Prestige for this alias is tracked separately and starts off at 20. Be warned, there will be nasty consequences if your alias is discovered... +15 to Subterfuge.

Micro Cosmos

Dreaming dead, waking life. Stress and hardship built up to a breaking point, whereupon a piece of your mind detached from its fleshy prison and began orbiting around your soul. Vividness stains your dreams. There are now shadows that lengthen under the sun; and thrums and pulses neither human nor umamusume around you seem to hear. On the plus side, your artistic capabilities are flourishing.

More mysterious, occult and/or paranoid choices and encounters will occur. More dreams (and nightmares) will occur. Grants you the World Resonance skill (Esoteric, scales with INS). You will communicate with things that should not be communicated with... +20 to Artistry.

Anego

A man in a fine suit discovered you huddled on the street, took your hand, treated you to ramen, and things escalated from there. You joined an organisation of 'problem-solvers' who took 'direct' and 'alternate' methods of keeping the peace around Tokyo's inner wards. This organization was never at the peak, but it was good enough, and you conducted your new role of urban soldier with swiftness and excellence, earning you more than a measure of respect. In fact, you earned a position of mild seniority. Men twice your age have to bow their heads and watch their tongues in front of you…

Immediately grants you the Dark-Neutral alignment. You will have a harder time progressing Lawful character Social Links. +15 to Brawl and Intimidation. The organization may occasionally make requests of you. Fulfill them or suffer the consequences. *Note: Anego is the female equivalent of aniki.

**Note: This organization does not condone what your mother did.

Underground Umaidol

Why do umamusume sing and dance? Because they can, alright? You're telling me if you had the opportunity to dress in gorgeous outfits and sing your heart out to attract the attention of thousands, you wouldn't take it, you utter numbs—Ahem. Anyway, you decided to join the underground idol industry to get a headstart on the whole theatric side of the umamusume racing gig. Your past slowed your progress, of course, but you found out plenty of idol fans are willing to overlook past sins if their oshi has a pretty face and a cute pout.

Gain the Social Media skill (Social, scales with PSY). This lets you perform umafluencer feats, such as posing for sick photos and ratioing someone on Umatter. You can gain additional Prestige this way too. +15 to Dancing and Foreign Languages. But idols have to look cute and adorable, so -15 to Intimidate. You still have some old contacts, including fans who still worship you as their oshi. That's worth something...right?

Baseball Fanatic

There is no fancy description. You love baseball. You would beat the shit out of the guy who insults your fave team, then team up with him to kill the bastard who insults baseball as a whole. There is nothing that will stop you from loving baseball as a fallen heiress and upcoming track star, not even the Chairwoman herself!

Start out with a free starting gift of a baseball bat. It's exactly what it says on the tin. (Does not count to the Starting Gift choice). +15 to Hand-Eye Coordination. You are automatically obliged to get into fights with anyone who insults baseball or your favorite team. (You may specify what this team is)

Did you get all of that? I hope so, because it's now your turn.

Firstly, pick 1 to 3 Traits.

Secondly, pick four skills to tag. You must possess at least 1 tagged skill in the Physical, Intellectual and Social categories. If a new skill was learned from a trait, you may tag it. Previously tagged skills cannot be tagged again.

Thirdly, distribute 80 skill points amongst your skills. (65 if you picked Gifted as a trait). You may not raise a skill above 100. It may be helpful to specify how much of each skill was raised.

Lastly, choose a starting gift from the following:

A very faded letter of recommendation for a Trainer, who is described as 'unscrupulous' and a 'bloodthirsty hound'. A silver bullet on a keychain. A trinket you picked up that you feel brings good luck. Your mother's old running shoes. They're sturdy, comfortable and most of all: recognisable. An old map of the Satono family mansion, including hiding spots and secret passages. A sunglasses, scarf and hat set that near-perfectly disguises your face. This will be the last phase of character generation. I realise this seems like a lot, but for a Fallen Heiress you will need it. Plan voting is once again allowed. Now go!

0.3: What kind of umamusume are you? (Character Generation Part 3)

Plain Jane leads you to the academy infirmary. She sets you down on a bed and measures your temperature, then takes your blood, then asks you to perform some basic back and leg stretches. Just as you are about to ask what the point of all this is, she pulls out a boombox, slams it down on the table and slips a fresh CD inside.

The opening notes bleed out in a tinny static-filled whine. Plain Jane smile tenses at the edges, before she raises her fist and slams it straight down onto the boombox's front. The great black machine shudders and splutters, almost with in indignation, before spitting out the rest of the song at an upbeat tempo.

A small grin blooms on your face and you lean back in your chair, exhaling a satisfied breath. Now, this is treatment. This is where you belong. It's sometimes hard to explain to sponsors, but through rain and snow, exhaustion and the ecstasy, music has guided you, inspired you, pointed you to food, lodging and fulfilment and most of all has never abandoned you, unlike certain adult figures in your life. You lean back, allow the notes to wash over you as the tempo swings and—

Wait.

That chorus sounds familiar. You perk up your ears, listen closely, and feel an invisible stone drop in your gut.

No, it can't be. Your new senpai wouldn't. I mean, think about it. She's a respectable umamusume. She lives in the modern age. She's employed by the finest racing academy the world has constructed, which means for all these reasons and more, she'd never have the sheer audacity to play the orchestral track from your underground idol debut directly in your face!

"Goodness, this is quite a 'bop', isn't it?"

Oh, dear god.

Plain Jane is enjoying this. She's humming along to the music, tapping one foot on the ground. She's pulling out ink-blot cards from a box and re-arranging them on the table. You're now covering your face with your hands, an act as effective as trying to get your old producer to stop eating instant ramen all the damn time. Can you wake up now?

A couple of new rules:

Firstly, all skills are currently capped at 100, except those that scale with tagged Attributes—they have a cap of 150. There may be opportunities to raise this cap in the story. The bar for being great at a skill has been raised from 120-150 to 130-150, since it's more difficult to go from good to great than it is from average to good.

Secondly, Mood states will now modify check difficulties. You currently have not unlocked means of granting yourself the Fantastic and Horrendous mood states.

[Outcast: Fallen Heiress difficulty selected -> Positive mood effects have decreased!]

Apologies for not setting these rules earlier. I only came up with them after reading the many discussions in this thread. I'm also afraid I won't be reassigning any skills and tags because I do want to get on with our story at some point.

Andmeuths said:

Decent enough that given a few years, she might have had a solid chance of breaking into the aboveground and entering the mainstream. It's likely the Satonos would have made moves to block her (the joke in the Japanese fandom is that the Satonos are basically Sega at their peak). Still, with decent dancing, persuasion skills to reduce conflicts in her team, a good social media presence and a measure of English fluency attracting foreign fans, Ruby would have been an attractive young umadol.

By the way, she's entering Tracen as a junior, same as Satono Diamond.

Now, please answer these questions to help our dear Satono Ruby out.

0.4: And do you know what it means to lose or win?

"Perhaps I went a little too far."

You do not respond. This is because a miniature tuba has crawled down your throat to blare out the deepest, loudest groan an orchestra can muster.

"But I'm serious. I meant what I said. Your debut song, though unrefined as expected, was quite a 'bop'. Very 'fresh'. Those melodies—I found them nostalgic." Plain Jane says. She raises her finger, still smiling as chipper as a chipmunk can be. "In fact, I had a friend who was quite into that form of orchestra back in the day. The contrast between old and new, the melding of dualities contrasted from Alice in Wonderland and the darkness inside a sapient creature's soul; there really is something exquisite there—"

"Really?" You mumble.

"Pardon?" Plain Jane asks.

You incline your head. "Did you really enjoy my music, senpai? You think I'm good at singing?"

She grins. "You mean despite as 'cringe' as it was?"

You nod. She nods back. It's an affirmation then, which makes you feel better, even if the previous five minutes were an exercise in cruel and unusual punishment. You were so sick of kami and Shinto imagery about the time you ditched the shrine for the Tokyo underground, but did you have to swing the pendulum that far forward?

"That's so Maruzensky of you."

Plain Jane laughs. "Come now, young Ruby, I'm not—wait, she also emphasizes those kinds of words, doesn't she? That's…"

Aha. Now it's senpai turn to look flushed. To those not in touch with the Japan umamusume racing circuit, you're speaking nonsense. Allow yourself to elucidate them, then. The concept is simple. Maruzensky is a fantastic sprinter with a whole swath of modern accolades to her name. Her preferences are the stuff of late-night Umastagram and Umatter memes. If you're pulling a Maruzensky, it means you're a time traveler, a retro vehicle fetishist or a NEET who somehow survived with their internet access cut off.

Take that, Plain Jane senpai. Stutter. Blush. Suffer as you did for blasting that Alice-in-Eviland schtick you were obsessed with as a preteen, screeching synthesized violins, harsh guitar shreds and all. Now, you can kick the chair over, tower over her cringing form and call her hair a—alright, that's going too far.

Maybe you'll just mail her a copy of your latest enka album, since she likes dualities so much. Someone has to correct this woman's music tastes. If she enjoys it, that's a fair bonus.

"Anyway!" Plain Jane shoves that blasted boombox away so fast it practically vanishes out of existence. She claps her hands together. "We're looking good here! Congratulations, Satono Ruby. Your psychological evaluation is all done. You're in the clear."

You have the faintest impression there should be party poppers and confetti raining down. There aren't. It feels underwhelming.

You glance down at a nearby table where a set of ink blot cards and paper forms are stacked neatly on top. Fresh ink—your handwriting—is neatly written on the lines and within square boxes. The answers are straightforward: Strongly Agree for entertaining others, a tick for a picture that seems like a shadow looming in a doorframe, an association of 'commitment' to word association of responsibility. A more spaced-out section of writing for the relationship you had with your family. Hesitation in the writing.

Huh, this is you indeed. Yeah, you must have written these answers amidst the sheer mortification of hearing your old work. Rather swiftly, too. Was this a wacky psychological trick on the part of your new senpai? Whatever. It's over. Throw a coin in the donation box and sing Ebisu's praises. You'd rather take these kinds of tests a cool and cute senpai over a frustrated social worker who totally has your best interests in mind, promise.

"Just got to finish a bit more paperwork…" Plain Jane says, taking out a fresh page on her clipboard and raising a pen. "Please bear with me."

Now it's your turn to make conversation.

"You're the academy psychologist as well?" You ask.

"Nope. I just help out with odd jobs here and there. It's a relatively unappreciated job, but it greases the wheels and gets the kids' shoes polished on time, so I take satisfaction in it." Plain Jane answers. She pauses midway through a line and looks up. "I must say, it's been a while since we had a professional singer enter our ranks."

"Geez, you're making it sound like Tracen's is a military academy." You remark.

"We've got the competitiveness of one." Plain Jane says. "Last time our best recorded a training video for the Spring Tenno Sho, it transformed into an impromptu scrimmage as they simply couldn't let their competitive spirits rest for a fraction of a second."

Oh, you remember that one. The one with Symboli Rudolf, Biwa Hayahide and the other 'monsters' of Tracen, starting off all smiles and flowers before one of the girls stepped in front of another and it all careened downhill from there. Almost broke your ribs giggling in the middle of the night.

"Still, calling me a professional? You're flattering me, senpai."

"I'm serious." Plain Jane says. "Anyone who sells music for money is a professional in my book. It's a not-so-obvious advantage, this talent of yours. Since you'll probably get out of singing lessons, which means more time to run on the track! Lucky you."

You can't help but preen a little. That's right. You are a professional. Handshake events, CDs on the shelves, actual merchandise bearing chibified versions of yourself and the other girls—the whole works. You earned money. You talked to people, did a good hustle. It's a legitimate good point of yours, even if it is somewhat detached from the whole racing goal.

You'll have plenty of time to work on that.

"You must have started early."

"I did." You say.

"Where, if I may be so bold as to ask?"

You hesitate for a moment before shrugging. "Shrine maiden training."

Plain Jane grins. "I would have guessed karaoke. You're from the outskirts, then? Traditional singing from such a young age. How exotic!"

You shrug. It was boring at times. Lots of homework. Strict eating and sleeping every day. Zero chance of singing your own pieces. But you don't want to bore your new senpai with your life story, so you sit right there, twiddling your thumbs and swishing your tail left and right, twitching your ears at the sound of the pen writing, as Plain Jane gets whatever new form she has out done. You reach for your phone, idly scrolling on social media, then reach down your collar, as you have done so many times in the past.

There it is: your necklace. A silver bullet attached to a silver chain. Thirty-eight millimeters of mythical ordnance from across the sea. A notch rests on one side, cutting through the mechanically allocated grooves. You run your fingers across the surface, reminiscing about its history.

Yes, that's the correct word. This is no bargain-bin find. This silver bullet has history. You were young then, barely a preteen, when you were sweeping the front yard of the shrine. You saw the glint in the corner of the eye and opened the box to check. The silver bullet lay in the corner, tucked far away from the rest of the coins. It was love at first sight. Fearing the head miko would confiscate it, you slipped it under your clothes and made off to your quarters.

Fast-forward a few years. You found a chain. You discovered ways to hide it beneath your clothes and store it in places prying eyes won't touch. You picked it among the first things to pack when preparing for your escape out of the shrine. The silver bullet's your lucky charm, a cornerstone of peace amidst the chaotic world. Whenever nerves strike before a concert, or you need help navigating a new scene, you clutch the silver bullet in the center of your palm and your mind clears.

Yes, you are aware of the obvious connotation with a particular wealthy umamusume family. And you don't care. This silver bullet is yours. It bequeaths your fortune. The evidence? It has hardly gotten dirty in its almost-decade lifespan.

You'll need that fortune, stepping into the most prestigious racing academy in Japan's history.

As you ponder, you hold up the bullet, pinching it between your thumb and index fingers. The positioning is ripe for a ray of sunlight to shine on the surface, casting an elongated, shining reflection off the bullet's outer shell.

A jolt strikes your brain.

[Insight check: 9/8 -> Success. +10 EXP.]

"Hey, senpai, where did you find that CD?" You ask.

"Why did you ask?" Plain Jane asks back.

"It was from my debut. Only a little under two dozen guys turned up. It's not something you find lying around at a merch desk."

"You'd be surprised what you can find floating around LANE these days." Plain Jane replies, not missing a beat.

You frown. "Yeah. Keys for merch deals and pirated stuff, I get you, but we never released physical copies of that song. We dumped it onto streaming. It only got numbers after my group switched to enka and got our first lucky break. Even then, hardly any of my fans have listened to it. Did you burn it on a CD just for me?"

Plain Jane falls still.

The sight is so abrupt it takes you off guard. She's not the angry type of still, where it's clear the person's thrumming with the desire to punch your face in. Nor is it the deer-caught-in-headlights frightened type of still, like that time Saya was caught sneaking extra sweets behind the manager's back. Rather, she's wearing an expectant look, as if waiting for you to finish the punchline of your joke.

The jolt from earlier hits you again.

You stand up, pushing your chair aside with a squeak, and inspect a calendar hanging from the wall. The page is blank white, devoid of any information. "Shouldn't the school get a new one?"

Plain Jane puts her pen down. "We're done here."

"Pardon?"

"You heard me, Satono Ruby. We're done."

"Sorry? Sorry!" You yelp. "Did I hit a sore spot? Wait, I didn't fail, did I? Oh gosh, I'm not expelled, am I?"

Plain Jane shakes her head. "No. None of that. In fact, you've exceeded expectations."

"How?"

"By noticing."

You stare at her before letting out an awkward chuckle. "Senpai, you can burn my songs. I won't tell. I graduated from my group, anyway! Heck, they'd call it free advertising."

Plain Jane ignores that. She's muttering to herself. "Plus, you've found your voice now, haven't you?"

You open your mouth to object that, duh, of course you have a voice. What kind of underground idol doesn't have one? Memory hits you in a flash, and you suddenly recall being curiously silent throughout this whole tour.

Why? You're not an introvert. You love making conversation. You'll do it to anyone who doesn't immediately turn up their nose upon hearing your real name. It's the reason your handshake events grew popular, since you knew how to talk about the ordinary, the boring and most importantly of all—the relatable to your fans.

"I…"

Plain Jane stands up. She redoes her collar and smooths the wrinkles in her skirt. She puts away the papers, tucks the pen back into a case and zips it shut, before standing up and stretching her back muscles. Her grimace is pensive and tight.

"That's the trouble with meeting me like this. Some square pegs need some sanding to fit into round holes, and that takes time and acceptance, both of which are in short supply these days. You're close, Satono Ruby. Closer than many of the so-called greats that pass through Tracen's halls. I'm ever so grateful for that. Yet the presence of this mental gap always, always stings."

"Senpai, you're not making sense." You say, now feeling real concern. "If you've got a problem with me, just say it. I can't improve myself if you don't give me a reason!"

"You learn more by doing."

"Of course! That's how I practice."

"Typical of an umamusume. Good choice, then. It's better if you see what lies ahead with your own two eyes."

"Are you talking about my future?"

"Indeed."

You roll your eyes, chuckling again. It sounds hollow. It takes effort. "Geez, if you wanted to treat me to a movie about a G1, you could have said so."

Plain Jane's cheeks bulge, and she emits a soft choking sound, as if she can't decide between laughing or sighing in exasperation. The former wins you. She titters, clutching the side of a nearby chair for mild support. Yet it's tinged with a gentle sorrow you're sure is for you, of which you can't decide if it's insulting or not.

Tension in your gut. It's definitely not a positive thing.

"I'll see you soon, Satono Ruby. Thank you for meeting me today."

Off goes the light switch. Your new senpai pulls the infirmary door open half-way and disappears behind its frame. Her steady footsteps recede gently down the hallway.

You do the obvious thing and follow.

The door seems to whine as you push it aside. An empty hallway extends before you, the rows of closed windows and doors silent as the shrine in the dead of night. You stalk forward, surveying for any sign of Plain Jane or anyone in general. It passes you by: Classrooms, classrooms, stairwell and more classrooms. The blackboards are spotless. The furniture is arranged neatly as if by a machine. The doors are locked shut. Not a single hair nor hide of an umamusume is present.

And—okay. You're well aware of your heritage. You know how her foolishness shamed the academy, caused untold reputational damage to her friends and family, lost the industry millions of yen, yada yada. But this level of inactivity is getting ridiculous. It's as if everyone decided to take a vacation at once. Tracen is home to valuables like top-notch sporting equipment and trophies. Shouldn't there be a security guard moseying around?

The less you see, the worse you feel. The worse you feel, the faster you're determined to search for some damn answers. You only realise you've been running at full pelt when you screech to a halt in front of the faculty room and wrench the door open with a single pull.

That's when the switch hits.

The temperature drops several degrees. The atmosphere shifts, a haze mind going blank before it reasserts itself with the memory of your fellow idol Miki yelling at you to stop dozing off, Ruby! The first thing you see: graffiti. Vulgar lines spray-painted in black with a visceral leering cartoon figure. You recoil. A cold wind whistles through the broken window and wraps around you, and you smell bitter mold.

Wha—

A ceiling panel crashes to the ground, mere centimetres beside you.

You stare at it, then lurch back out the door in haste.

It's a mistake. Fear jacks up your acceleration, hones those primal instincts to slam your pretty little back into the wall. A variety of filth falls upon you: plaster chunks, dead insects, wads of dust. It goes down your collar and into your carefully combed hair. You slap them all off your clothes with a squeal and a squeak, then frantically look around you with your mouth hung open in a call for help, which soon dies in your throat.

It's gone. The academy is gone. In its place is a sight of urban devastation. Dirty glass shards litter in piles in front of broken windows. Rusty hinges creak in the wind, and in the distance you hear the faint drip-drip-drip of rainwater. Time has ravaged once pristine halls, leaving behind cockroaches, looting opportunities, and a smell worse than several dumpsters mixed with rainwater.

What?

What, what, what the hell? The questions zoom through your mind as you stand there, gaping like a fish, back mere millimetres from touching the filth on the walls. What is this place? When did you get here? Who the hell pulled this magician's trick right in front of your eyes?

In response, something thin and wet slaps you in the face. You pull it off with a disgusted snarl and find it is a newspaper. The headline bleeds in thick, heavy black.

CLOSURE OF TRACEN ACADEMY FINALIZED

A photo, an article, a date pointing to several years in the future. This is…incomprehensible! Obscene! How could Tracen—no. Clickbait. Get it out of here. You hurl the paper aside, where it flies off down the hall, only to be replaced with another careening down the desolate hallway.

EMBEZZLEMENT SCHEME THE LAST NAIL IN COFFIN FOR ONCE-PRESTIGIOUS AKIKAWA FAMILY

The sight of a young girl clinging to the gates of the academy, a set of policemen grabbing her by the shoulders. Your hands tremble. A great terror seizes you, and you run down the ruined corridor as if the spirits of Yomi are nipping at your heels.

They follow you. Not just from behind, but from around you. Pages, articles, blurry photos with taunting, burning black headlines pop out from the rotting woodwork, a cocoon of disaster and misfortune you comprehend down to the last word.

WAS UMAMUSUME RACING THE PROBLEM THIS WHOLE TIME?

ACCUSATIONS OF HUMAN-UMAMUSUME XENOPHOBIA AND VIOLENCE WITHIN THE STUDENT BODY

PANDEMIC HALTS ALL TRACEN ACTIVITY FOR THE WINTER

SPONSORS BACK OUT DUE TO DISASTER AT NAKAYAMA RACECOURSE

SATONO OPAL: A TRUE INVESTIGATION

The stairs fly down in sets of twos and threes. You kick the door open, flying straight out into the courtyard. Night's out. Thick clouds blanket the sky, and a metallic, rusty ringing echoes from the gates ahead. You do not go there, bypassing the rows of dead trees until you reach the most precious place of all: the racetrack.

You stumble through the entrance, stumble on a rock and tumble down a grassy slope slick with moisture. An iron bar slams into the side of your head at the end. You pick yourself up with a wince, taking a second to regain your bearings before looking ahead. Your heart sinks.

Tracen's racetrack, its meticulously manicured turf a symbol of pride and accomplishment, has been overrun with weeds and swathes of tall grass. Even this sacred place was left to rot.

This is a nightmare, right? The abandoned junkyard of a building can't be Tracen Academy. The future wasn't supposed to be like this!

You were supposed to make a fresh new start there. There were going to be festivals. Exciting races. Studies to complete, three square meals a day, fun roommates to gossip with. Friends who shared your hobbies of singing and racing and dancing. You were meant to experience them all, train like a beast, burn like a wildfire on the track and show the world your heritage didn't matter, because your soul shone just as brilliantly as the best of the best. You could bring immeasurable joy to all who watched you!

And now…

What was the point of holding onto her running shoes? She was supposed to see them when you got up on stage, wasn't she?

Rustling the distance. Your tear-stained face lifts. Shadowy figures lurk in the distance, flitting amongst the weeds. They point. They giggle. They grin horrid smiles with leering white teeth—the only distinctive part visible. And they hurl the newspapers against you. The ink trails down off the pages and stains your best clothes.

The connection is obvious. These shadows are the enemy. The cause of Tracen's destruction. How and why, you don't understand, only that the truth is now imprinted in your mind.

It's this thought that wipes your face blank and cranes your neck to the sky. Lifts you to your feet. Puts those gangly hands into tight grips. It urges a roar from deep within your throat as you force strength down into your legs and kick off like a rocket.

There's no destination, nothing but an expanse of darkness in sight, but you don't care. You're flying down the endless overgrown turf, tearing past prickle and thorn with your bare hands, heart hammering, mouth screaming not a song but raw deranged euphoria. Your legs howl mercy, mercy give up please give up you aren't meant for this kind of sprint yet but you can't stop, won't stop, because you are umamusume and running is both victory and conquest, and thus you smash through the shadowy figures like bowling pins.

Let the inferno of your dreams blaze out of control. Stand defiant in the face of horror. If the enemy exists, you will fight. This is what the Three Goddesses created you for!

The shadows loom and lurch greater and taller. They meld themselves into a seething mass, blocking your path and threaten to swallow you up. You charge forward to meet them. A thousand hands burst forward and grab you by the torso. You struggle, bite and flail like a mad bull; just as they are about to pull you apart, your silver bullet necklace pops out of your collar.

A gentle caress. A blinding light. The howl of evil as it touches the forces of good, fleeing and cowering back into the ancient caves from which it dwells. Cloth elongates, muscle snaps into focus and extends out of your back, and you catch a glimpse of stars.

It's bright. It's so very, very vivid.

You curl in a ball, charge up a swell of power deep within you, throw your arms forward with a mighty lunge and—

BEEP BEEP BEEP.

Your eyes slam open.

Capsule motel. Five in the morning. Uniform on the bed, luggage packed and ready to go in your locker. The alarm app on your phone rings shrilly before you muster the energy to slam a thumb on the off switch.

Breathe in. Breathe out.

You lay an arm on your face, sweat trickling down your cheeks.

You were dreaming. The wisps are fading. Fragments of imagination-memory leaking out of your head. You scramble to latch onto them and manage to snag a few important details.

One. You need to get to Tracen as fast as possible. Two. The silver bullet is more important than ever. Three. Senpai is waiting for you.

Who?

You can't recall, but she exists. She definitely exists. You are not crazy.

You sit there in silence, rubbing your head, before a number Four makes itself loudly known. Hunger. Time for breakfast, then. Budget's tight, so bread should do.

[Nutrition check: 26/30 -> Failure.]

But first, you groan to yourself as you reach for your bag, it's time to write a brand new dream diary entry.

[World Resonance has increased by 2.]
