0.5: Senpai (Bonus)

Special Week is feeling perturbed.

Yes, you heard that right. Special Week, little miss sunshine compressed into umamusume form, is perturbed. Concerned. Look at her, sitting in her seat in the cafeteria. She's poking at her several bowls of rice with her chopsticks, her feet tapping absentmindedly on the floor, all while wearing a frown that can't decide if it's confused, frightened or just plain sad.

It's not hard to see why. Gaze upon the interior of Tracen's esteemed academy. The round tables are all full. The scent of rice, eggs and miso floats deliciously through the air. A television hanging from the ceiling blares the latest news, advertisements and cartoons. First impressions say this is yet another beautiful, gluttonous morning in the finest racing academy in Japan, yet the tension here has laid so thick a heavy industry drill couldn't cut through it.

"Did someone break both their legs?" Special Week asks, raising her hand.

Her tablemates, one Daiwa Scarlet, one Tokai Teio, Vodka, and the notable and infamous duo of Mejiro McQueen & Gold Ship—they all turn to look at her.

"Haven't you heard?" Scarlet asks.

"Heard what?"

"The daughter of Satono Opal. She's arriving soon as a first-year."

Special Week lets out a hushed gasp. She nods her head slowly. She grabs a wad of rice and egg between her chopsticks, shoves it in her mouth, chews it slowly and asks, "Who?"

Imagine you're halfway through a giggle with your friends, when your newest friend comes up and politely asks what the joke is about. The natural reaction is to point and laugh at him, good-naturedly of course. This is what happens. Teio laughs, Scarlet and Vodka snicker—in tandem, mind you—and McQueen simply sighs and mutters about how Special Week would do well to pay attention to more gossip and not her food.

"Guys!" Special Week whines. "Tell me! I'm from the countryside, remember?"

Not wanting to leave her friend in the dark, McQueen begins an impromptu history lesson. The conversation ceases to lose all humor in a heartbeat. Our dear Hokkaido ex-bumpkin is now mortified.

"S-s-she cheated?"

"Yep. Did it right at the cusp of winning her G1 and killing her family jinx for good. Put all of her past victories into question." Vodka says.

"But why?" Special Week asks.

"Dunno. Bribes? Revenge? Couldn't be assed to put in the effort to actually win. They never found out."

"Understatement of the century." Scarlet mutters.

"But…" Special Week places her chopsticks down. She kneads her forehead muscles as she thinks. "McQueen, you said in the press conference she said she wanted to win."

"It's a PR tactic." McQueen says, her tone soft and measured. "The goal is to say as little as possible to avoid further repercussions. Goodness knows she was in enough when her sabotage plot was discovered."

"Oh…"

"Never mind that, Spe. The real point is this: she let so many people down!" Tokai Teio huffs. She angrily stabs a piece of honey-drenched bacon on her plate. "Can you imagine it, Spe? We were all so super duper proud of you for beating Bronya and defending Japan from the French menace. El basically cried into your uniform. Your mom brought the picture of your other mom to watch the whole race. Then imagine if all of us, including everyone watching on the TV, suddenly discovered out of nowhere the entire race had been fake!"

She punctuates the last statement by tearing off a piece of bacon, presumably having discovered the motion from a late-night gangster movie with the dorm. The effect is not dissimilar to popping the bubble on a juicy ghost story. Vodka's cocky grin fades. Scarlet glares into her plate. Silence reigns as everyone at the table takes in Teio's words.

Now, if the cosmic forces aligned, and the universe generated a version of Special Week who did cheat, she'd do it out of the misguided attempt to make her deceased mother, her fans and her friends happy. This means that, back in our world of reality, there is a tiny fraction of Special Week that does relate to Satono Opal. It's microscopic, to give it some greater context. The rest of her is too busy going white as a sheet.

"Spe? You're crying?" Scarlet exclaims.

"No! I mean, yes! Sort of!" Special Week chokes. There are definitely wet spots around her eyes. Those adorable triangular ears are drooping like wilted daisies in the summer. That's a real sniffle coming out of her mouth too. She hurriedly shoves another fried egg into her mouth, which doesn't help matters. "When Teio said all of that, I just imagined you guys and our trainer looking the most disappointed I've ever been—Suzuka too and it was just—"

She lets out another sniffle and washes her sorrows down with a steaming hot gulp of her tea. It burns her throat, obviously. Here comes the coughing fit.

"Teio!" McQueen scolds. She puts down her teacup with a glare right as Vodka runs over to the nearest table for cold water.

"I-I didn't know that was going to happen! It's all Opal's fault, not mine. I was just saying a hypothetical, right!" Teio exclaims. When that fails to placate McQueen, she gulps and reaches over the table and pats Special Week on the back. "I'm sorry, Spe! It was just a joke. We know you'd never cheat like her, so chin up, yeah?"

Special Week downs the water in another single gulp. "Thanks, Teio…" She blubbers.

Crisis averted, and thank goodness for that! To bring such a good girl like Special Week to tears is a most grave offense. The topic of conversation has already been brought up, and it lingers in the air like a bad smell, so why not comment on it?

"But you've gotta admit, it was real uncool for Opal to do that." Vodka says.

"Yeah. It's like giving a starving man in the desert water and then yanking it away at the last second. I can't imagine how her family felt." Scarlet says. "Tachyon told me from Digital that the jinx is something the Satonos really believe in."

"Hell, even if it didn't exist, I'd never be able to face myself in the mirror." Vodka adds darkly.

"Prez would kill me!" Tokai Teio cries. She grips the sides of her head, then drops them to the table. "Then the rest of you would finish the job."

"Oh, lovely to know we'll be digging such a fine grave for you." Mejiro McQueen says, without venom, and goes to butter her toast.

Our heiress is remaining silent here. Decorum has taught her not to carelessly sling her words around, lest a stray comment spiral into a public relations disaster. She's a willful lady, our McQueen is, ever-so-polite yet so admirable from afar. But, if you built her relationship with her more, then dug a bit into the online archives, you'd know that the Mejiros and the Satonos once had a great working relationship. They used to collaborate in setting up hotel and racing tournament infrastructure. Some of their current eldest children—one Mejiro Titan and another Mejiro Aurora—were kouhais to the senpai of Satono Opal.

Opal's betrayal must have felt like a true knife in the back. The bond between kouhai and senpai can extend beyond mere friendship. Some of that enmity was passed down to McQueen, but only tenuously. She was merely a child back then. We can't expect her to truly understand a sin's gravity when that person has disappeared from the limelight.

McQueen's silent. The rest of the cafeteria is not. See, Special Week's no longer the bumbling upstart who lucked her way into second-place. She's popular now. She's now an unwitting conduit of the flow of conversation. Most of the students here have reached the same conclusion: Satono Opal is awful. Let's trash Satono Opal. Call her garbage. Call her a disgrace. Spit in your soup bowl out of shame, then throw pity upon the pyre for poor Satono Diamond and Crown, who are innocent swans who have never, ever done anything wrong in their well-bred lives. Call up the prez, and have her terrible daughter expelled before she sends a blight to us all!

If these insults were smoke, we'd soon see the academy erupt into flames.

"But…"

Special Week raises her hand, now back to feeling concerned again. There's a mild dip in the conversation as the other students pay attention. The bread and circuses halts.

"That's only the mother, right?"

"So?" Daiwa asks.

"The daughter's not the same. She hasn't done anything wrong yet," Special Week says. Her ears droop. "I feel sorry for her. My mom was so kind to me, and yet…"

The other girls look at each other. Yes. Special Week is correct. It's blindly obvious, yet a few of them let themselves be caught up in the atmopshere.

"Yeah, true. She was just born unlucky. No clue what the kid's like. Didn't Satono Opal vanish into thin air after she was expelled?" Vodka asks.

"Good on you, Spe," McQueen says. Her mouth twitches in a small smile. "Innocent until proven guilty, I say."

"If she really has done something wrong, the prez should expel her!" Teio states.

"Don't be stupid. The academy's not going to expel her for no reason." Scarlet says.

"I mean, if she's like her mom. If she tries to cheat in the tryouts, then she's out of the gate, pronto! I'll be watching her."

You'll have to excuse Tokai Teio. She's a bit immature, and she adores the sport to the degree of obsession. It's not the best combination here. She hasn't truly been blindsided by loss yet.

"Wait, McQueen," Vodka says. "Isn't that Satono Diamond girl a friend of yours?"

McQueen pauses halfway through lifting a fork of egg. She places it down, wipes her mouth and clears her throat. "An acquaintance, Vodka, who so happens a high opinion of me. We've met at charity galas before. I've found her to be a compassionate, if slightly naïve, girl."

She's one to talk. However, that's a topic for another time.

"Geez, McQueen, I don't envy you. You're gonna have to decide between both siblings." Vodka says.

"I have no association with Satono Ruby!" McQueen counters. "The two of us have never met. I merely said she deserves a fair shot. She'll have to earn results for herself if she wants any respect around here. I'm certain our Trainers feel the same."

That is only partially accurate. McQueen would be disappointed if she heard that, but it's not anything she has any hope of controlling.

"And you?" McQueen asks, not at Special Week, Teio, Vodka or Scarlet. If you've been paying attention, you'll notice that a single umamusume has remained conspicuously silent throughout this whole conversation.

That umamusume does not respond. McQueen waits for three seconds before she coughs into her fist. "Gold Ship?"

"Now, this is gas."

The moment the grey-coated umamusume utters that, a pinch throbs in McQueen's forehead. Goddesses in heaven, it's going to be one of those days.

"Did someone…" McQueen glances at Special Week, who shakes her head back and forth.

"This is fire." Gold Ship says. Her eyes are shut, and she's leaning slightly in her seat, humming to herself.

Our heiress is struck by the sudden, violent urge to grab her teammate by the collar and plead if she act like a normal umamusume for five bloody seconds. She won't. It'd be playing into whatever tomfoolery Gold Ship insists on a daily basis. Instead, she uses observation. Logic. Gold Ship isn't looking at anyone in particular. She's wearing this dreamy expression, the type when one wears when lost within their own world, which she has felt whenever she purchases a tasty parfait, or whenever she loses herself in the thrill of the track.

McQueen looks up, and notices Gold Ship's slender ears twitching.

Fast as lightning, McQueen shoots out with her hand and dives her fingers into Gold Ship's left ear. She rips out a small, plastic object with a single yank.

"Hey!" Gold Ship cries, scrabbling for the lost airbud. "McQueen! I was listening to that!"

"Listening to…" McQueen holds the airbud up to her ear and grimaces. "I can't begin to guess, but you're really going to do it when we're having a conversation?"

"It was important, alright?" Gold Ship protests, trying to snatch back the airbud from her friend's grip, to no avail. "It was enka."

"Enka?" McQueen raises her eyebrows, frowning. "This is nothing like enka."

"Modern enka, duh. Oh, don't tell me you don't know. It's about tradition! Modernity! Guitar strums and neon bright lights on a theater stage. We've got carps jumping through the heavenly gate surrounded by lightning!" She spreads her arms wide, as if said carp has materialized between her palms. She glances around the table. "Everyone gets modern enka, right guys?"

The other three umamusume have no idea what their friend is talking about. They smile and nod anyway.

"We were talking about Satono Opal," McQueen stresses.

"Yeah. That's her daughter singing there." Gold Ship says.

"Ridiculous. That can't be true. This sounds like a grown woman." McQueen scoffs. "Satono Ruby wouldn't be older than sixteen!"

"Idols can do that. That's why they train their voices, dummy." Gold Ship says, and shrugs. " And I guess she lied about her age then. Kind of a grey area, but it happens all the time in the music industry."

The idea of anyone not following the law down to the letter is inconceivable to our heiress's ears. She begins to stutter and bluster out how that's a terrible thing to do and how it could have resulted in untold damage to Satono Ruby's reputation, right to work, and returns on investment. It is a perspective of the highborn wealthy, who cannot and might not ever know what it means to scrimp and struggle to survive, all originating from a girl who believes she has already experienced her absolute lowest.

(That's losing semi-important races, by the way. Don't you worry. McQueen will grow up soon.)

By the time she's recovered, Gold Ship has snatched the airbuds back and handed them out to her other friends.

"Wow, that's some voice," Vodka says. Her head bobs up and down in time with the beat. "Yeah, this is seriously cool!"

"It's alright." Scarlet admits, though she's giving off a faint smile. "I suppose it means this Ruby has a good work ethic. Respect."

Gold Ship claps her hands in delight. She bolts up from her seat, raising a fist to her heavens with a snarl of exhilaration. Steam is practically firing out of her nostrils. "I've decided! This is exactly what the school needs."

"Please don't." McQueen groans.

"It is?" Special Week gasps.

"You heard me, Spe! We need spirit. We need energy. Most of all, we need to reconcile the history of our academy's greats with the grassroots movements and training of our present. This album from the underground is the very best—no, it's the divine epitome of everything us umamusume strives to achieve. It's the very soul of Eden!"

McQueen did not think her heart could sink any lower.

"The entire school must hear these beats!" Gold Ship shouts. "To the broadcasting room I go!"

McQueen lunges out of her seat in a flash. She slams one palms on the table, then grabs Gold Ship by the wrist, yanking the protesting umamusume back. "Did you not listen to anything we've discussed in the past ten minutes?"

"Huh? Who cares about that?" Gold Ship says.

Special Week speaks up. "Uh, Golshi, McQueen's got a point. Knowing Opal's reputation, that might not go down well with the staff…"

"The kid's not her mom." Gold Ship says. She puts her hands behind her head in an easy-going fashion and sticks out her tongue. "So I don't care!"

It's astounding, I find, how members of the Gold Clan will commit the most audacious, ridiculous and self-sabotaging acts, only for them to make complete sense in the end. Remove any notion of online tomfoolery from your mind. Gold Ship is not just some quip-spouting machine. Look at where she's positioned. She's shouting at McQueen yes, but she's angled the direction of her voice so that her words ring out through the majority of the cafeteria. Gold Ship knows full well that results mean everything in Tracen; when an achiever of multiple G1s speaks, the rest of the room listens. Doesn't matter if she's the court jester or not.

Lo-and-behold, the rest of the students quieten. The bread and circuses halt. Some of them are wearing guilty expressions.

McQueen has realised this. She falters.

Gold Ship grins. She strides to the exit with a whistle on her lips. McQueen regains her bearings and chases after her with a snarl, which means balance has been restored to the universe. Special Week is laughing and smiling again. All is well.

That concludes this debacle. I suppose this is the point where the curtains fall and the actresses bow out.

But Special Week is not the center of the academy, is she?

Please don't get me wrong. I like Special Week. She's a respectable and accomplished umamusume who is well deserving of her title of the Supreme Commander of Japan. Her entire first year could be compressed into a best-selling book. But look around you. The many faces contain many stories. Tracen is home to thousands of students. It hasn't had a student body with such a level of accomplishment in decades. It'd be a shame if I limited myself to supporting only one child, no?

The morning is still young. There are so many avenues of this one topic to explore.

So, stand up. Clean your plate, and then push your chair in nice and tight. It's time for a morning walk.

I exit the cafeteria, narrowly brushing between a pair of students along the way. Down the corridor I go, after which I take a turn left, and I'm walking into the courtyard. The sakura trees are blooming, pink and white floating down in soft waves of petals. The sky is bright and blue, like countless others I've experienced at this academy.

I step off the asphalt and take a moment to drink deep from the crisp, cool air. Around and in front of me are dozens of students full-swing through their morning routines. Training, relaxing, and chatting. The usual, except the tension from earlier has pervaded here too.

"Tell you what, Natie! I'm gonna to be the first girl to beat Satono Ruby on the track!"

"I thought your rival was Teio."

Twin Turbo, ever so energetic and ever so garish with that long-tailed hairstyle, hesitates at her friend and teammate's comeback. She recovers in a flash.

"Then I'll beat both of them!" She proclaims.

"You can't have two rivals."

"Nuh-uh. No-one says I can't! I'm gonna beat two prodigies in both G1s and make everyone respect me! Aren't I smart for figuring this out?"

The other girl is Nice Nature. The coverings on her ears remind me of old-fashioned Christmas trees. Point this out to her, and she'll be upset. She's already halfway there, with that long-suffering look painted on her round features.

"You don't even know what Ruby is like. She could be a complete rookie, and then it'll look as if you're bullying her." Nice Nature says.

"Wait, what?" Twin Turbo yelps. Oh no, she realises, horror-struck. Her teammate has a point. "No! That's not fair. I don't want to be a bully. I want to beat her fair and square. Help me, Natie!"

She rushes to Nice Nature's side, who desperately tries to fling the energetic girl off.

Down the path, near a flowerbed, there's a yelp in the distance, drawing heads and then is promptly ignored. I go because I find the contrast surrounding this girl's disposition and prowess delightful. Her whims are well known.

"Oshi, anti, oshi, anti, oshi, anti…" A dandelion has its petals plucked one by one, before being thrown to the ground alongside a scream of frustration.

"I can't decide!" Agnes Digital wails, nails raking down her cheeks. "Curse my compulsive tendencies!"

"I don't want her here!" Nearby, a girl in a witch hat screams into her phone. Sweep Tosho. "She's going to mess up my spells. I just know it! Make her go away, Papa!"

Farther on, past the stump where the losers of the week scream their woes into, we have a purple tent erected, embroidered with gold and pomp. The interior is the mysterious kind of dark that brings upon soft tinkling chimes and the scent of incense, yet has enough room for half a dozen to stand and bump shoulders without interrupting the proceedings at all. It's comfort, in an eerie sense. My spot's at the back.

"Help us, great Matikanefukukitaru! The cursed daughter of the foul heretic will soon grace our academy's sacred grounds!" One of the girls behind a velvet-decorated table cries. She clasps her hands and bows her head. "Tell us we won't suffer misfortune in the upcoming scrimmage."

Matikanefukukitaru—did you get her name? Matikanefukukitaru. The umamusume with the daruma hairpin chuckles energetically and grinds her palms together. "Have no fear, my lambs. Lord Shiraoki is in a merciful mood today. Last night, her teachings came to me in a dream, where she told me just how to counter the accursed airs put upon by Satono Ruby's curse. Doto! Bring my crystal ball!"

"R-right away!"

The heavy crystal ball slams on the table, causing the two girls to yelp. I exit through the tent flap.

So far, we've had competition, conflict and fear. Now we will experience true hate.

The shrine. The front gate where Miss Tazuna is standing. The line of journalists eagerly waiting outside to capture pictures of the new year. There's a time for such triteness, and it's not within my schedule, so I turn my back to the flashing lights and stalk inwards.

This might surprise you, but the academy halls have become part of my favorite routes. True, there's not as much sunshine or fresh air, but crowds can be calming in themselves. You can get lost in them. You can subtly eavesdrop on topics that might stimulate your imagination. You can bask in the shared sound and warmth and not feel completely alone.

Hello, Rice Shower. Shadowing another one of your favorites? A bold strategy. I hope it pays off in the upcoming tryouts. Don't drop that dagger, dear.

"Permission requested."

The indoor gym thrums and grunts with the squeak of plastic and metal.

"What do you want?"

"My family informed me that I should attempt to improve my communication directives. Sending conversation request."

"I have no time to play your games, Bourbon." Duramente grits her teeth as she pulls forward on the cable machine. The muscles on her shoulder and back strain up with exertion. Her golden earring gently swings through the effort. The intruder, one Mihono Bourbon stands next to her like a displaced streetlight.

"Satono Ruby."

"What?" Duramente growls.

"Do you have an opinion of her?"

Duramente glowers at her, allowing herself to relax and hold the pull-bar in place. "Her mother was a cheater. She was weak and disgusting. Her daughter is likely the same. End of story."

"Estimating fluctuation in mood dependent on acquaintance Satono Crown."

"One more word, and I will break this bar off its hinges and hurl it at you."

Mihono bows her head. "Absconding immediately."

Even a cyborg knows how to beat a hasty retreat. Excuse her manners. She's had a peculiar upbringing. Lucky for her, it wasn't Gentildonna she was interrupting. Even I shudder to think what horrors that girl could inflict upon her ire.

South corridor. East staircase. I navigate through a slowly thickening crowd before reaching the Trainers' break room. I know it'll be filled right about now. The morning is a period of relative rest for them, where they can finish paperwork, write plans and drink coffee as their trainees complete their schoolwork. It looks plain on the surface: some sturdy tables, a dozen or so plastic chairs, cupboards filled with tea, sugar and coffee and a fridge stocked with multiple boxes of packed lunches.

Don't be fooled. This place is a gold mine of intel. Tracen only hires the best of the best. The future of Japan's racing circuit is constructed behind this single locked door. Naturally, I want to listen in, so I phase through the door and take my place against the water cooler.

The topic is—who else? A trainer's job is to be mindful of their trainees' mindset.

"We're placing a hell lot of suspicion on a girl who hasn't even debuted yet." This comes from a man with tanned skin and an undercut on his somewhat messy chestnut hair. He's normally a casual fellow. Today he's anything but. Back straight, hand tight on his coffee mug. His usual lollipop is absent from his mouth.

He has a real name. Everyone calls him Okino.

"Satono Opal's misdeeds caused a massive scandal." A younger trainer says. Her name is Aoi Kiryuin, and she's on the outer circle of the throng of conversation. She fidgets with her energy bar. It's clear she doesn't feel like she deserves to be here, amidst the giants who trained Oguri Cap or Symboli Rudolf. She clears her throat. "It brought so much of what she did, what the Satonos did, and Tracen's own regimes into question. I heard from my parents that the fallout took months to clear up. There are all sorts of rumors floating around now."

"It is what it is." Hana Toujou mutters, her arms folded.

Okino turns to her. "Harsh, Hana."

Hana fixes him a steely look. "You know what I mean. We can't mind-control the student body into liking her. Like it or not, Satono Ruby has a stigma attached to her. It'll be up to her and her Trainer if she'll be available to overcome it. If she doesn't, it's not as if she can't find a life outside of Tracen."

"They're not going to bully her, are they?" Aoi asks. "My Happy Meek…"

"Team Rigil won't, if I have anything to say about it." Hana says darkly.

But the others might is the unfortunate truth that goes unsaid. The trainers share uneasy glances with each other. Most of them are sympathetic, or at least pitying, towards Satono Ruby's state, yet they don't relish having to deal with childish quips and drops in their trainees' mental states.

"I'll speak a word to my girls and tell them not to approach her with a prejudiced mindset." Okino rubs the back of his neck. His gaze then sharpens. "And remember what the Chairwoman said last week. We're playing fair. I better not catch any of you guys screwing her over."

Hana scoffs. "Who do you think we are, Okino?"

"It's called being careful. Nothing else."

He speaks this in a general direction of one certain trainer, dark-haired and dressed in a maid's uniform, who rises to the occasion.

"It won't be a problem."

This woman's name…for some reason, it tends to slip everyone's minds. But she does have one: Akiko. That's not as important as the fact that she's the Satono family's personal trainer.

"The Satono group has already put out a statement. We have no intention of interfering nor supporting Satono Ruby's endeavours. Her life is her own. I will aim to keep Diamond and Crown as far away from her as possible."

"Good." Okino grunts.

"However…" Akiko looks steadily forward, and Okino and the rest flinch. The normally cheerful maid-trainer, who always greets her peers with a salute and a smile, affixes upon them with eyes as cold as the icy caverns beneath the arctic. Nothing resembling warmth lies within. "We will be watching the opposite. If Ruby dares replicate Opal's misdeeds, the Satono Group will take prompt action on her and anyone who has assisted her. I hope that makes things clear."

Okino tenses. He instantly dislikes this side of his colleague. This is no mere schoolteacher's dislike. It is a darkness that has sunk further and deeper than what should be considered acceptable. However, Okino is a smart man. He has guile. Anyone who has trained Gold Ship for that many years must cultivate a degree of pragmatism if they want to survive. So, he drops the issue, side-eyes Akiko as a finishing word, and drinks his coffee in silence. The rest of the trainers follow.

He's a decent man, this Okino. He brought Special Week to victory. He didn't give up on Silence Suzuka when most trainers would have. The Mejiros, who are so strict, approve of him by permitting him to watch over McQueen. Ah, but he's seeking to poach Kitasan Black, isn't he? She's Satono Diamond's best friend. That might be a problem.

The conversation switches gears to timetables and scheduling, topics that I would take great interest in if I were human and not an umamusume. I walk out through the closed door, go back down the staircase and notice from a nearby classroom clock that it's almost time for homeroom. Bodies are petering in from the outside. It is no issue for me. We still have one more sight to see. Fear not. It's not as negative. Almost the opposite. I'll give you a quick hint: trainees here love squeezing every last drop of training time out of the sieve.

I sprint towards the window and power through it, letting the wind carry me to my destination. It lands me exactly where I want to be: a prime observation spot near the finish line of the racetrack. Most are packing up their bags and leaving, but a few are hanging around to watch the center. Two umamusume in their standard red tracksuits storm down the turf, during which grass flies up and lungs burn, and a howling sound erupts from their mouths as they round the final corner.

It's a close match, both of them giving it their all even in this impromptu scrimmage, yet the end result is a dead heat. With no cameras to spot the difference, the result is:

"A tie! Another one! Ugh, that's worse than losing."

Grass Wonder slumps to the ground next to her friend. Her long chestnut hair splays out on the manicured grass. She inhales the fresh scent through deep, ragged breaths. "You were acting off today, Seiun."

"Same to you!" Seiun Sky retorts, groping for her water bottle. She takes a long drink before gasping out the answer. "But it's obvious why, isn't it?"

"Yes." Grass Wonder replies. "I've tutored her a dozen times, and I'm still astounded how Spe is so terrible at maths."

"Not that!" Seiun waves her hand. "The other thing."

"We're back to that conversation again?"

"C'mon, indulge me here."

"There's homework I should get a headstart on..."

"Please?"

"Seiun! I've heard enough of that tripe, thank you very much." Grass Wonder sits up and narrows her eyes. "And you already know my opinion. It's not her fault her mother ended up like that."

"Hey, you don't need to tell me that. I already know. But…"

"But?"

Seiun Sky, still lying with her back on the grass, gestures to the bleaches above her. "You don't like how it's messing with everyone's heads."

Grass Wonder frowns. Her friend has a point. She persists in her stance. "I rather enter a competition where my opponents aren't distracted by tabloids from yesteryear."

Seiun whistles. "Same."

"And she's coming to the academy soon, which means the problems will get worse." Grass Wonder says, disdain evident.

"Yup."

Grass Wonder eyes her friend critically. "You've dodging around the point. If this has anything to do with another prank, then you know you've been scolded for—"

"What? No, no, no!" Seiun shoots up, frantically motioning with her hands. "Stop it, Grass. What kind of uma do you take me for?"

"I was just checking."

"That part of my life is over. Over!"

"Then what point are you making?"

Seiun scratches her cheek. She hesitates first. "Satono Opal used to be pretty good. She cheated, yeah, but she couldn't have won all those races through sabotage. People would've caught on way too early. She had some good talent and hard work in there before she decided to ruin it all, no doubt about it. Her daughter should have inherited some of her genes."

"And?"

"She's a first-year. We're second-years." Seiun sits up and nudges closer to Grass Wonder. She gazes at her friend, upon which her smile morphs into an expression truly devilish. "Isn't our job to help her cut her teeth on something?"

Grass Wonder opens her mouth to reprimand her friend. She doesn't. It'd be easy enough, but she doesn't. As refined and ladylike as she tries to portray herself, the fire of a competitor burns hot and intense behind that silk. She can't deny there's an allure in Seiun's words, even if it means putting the target of their conversation through a couple of very painful trials.

"We can find out if she's truly a cheater that way." Seiun finishes.

The question that hangs in the air is, of course, whether to interfere.

The warning bell rings. The two girls' ears prick up. They rush to their feet, grab their gear and scramble full pelt up the track. I'm left sitting next where they sat, alone.

There you have it, Satono Ruby. You cannot hear me, yet I shall speak to you as if you were here, for there is no-one else otherwise. Tracen Academy. A school full of umamusume who are wary, angry at or flat-out hate you. Do you think it's too much? Perhaps an explanation is in order.

You have to understand: umamusume are born to run. We've compressed the barbaric acts of war down into a form where no-one can be hurt, yet where dominance can be objectively shown. We've converted our innate instincts into a rite of sanctity. These races are our gods. Imagine if you had a shrine dedicated to the world's creator, and you maintained it with tender love and care over the decades, only for someone to burst in and throw fecal matter and urine all over the place, before knocking over the altars and burning the paintings, and concluding it all by fornicating with your mother.

Project that thousandfold into the public eye, and you have us umamusume's treatment towards race cheaters. The number of souls who have tried over the past thousand years barely exceeds two dozen. Our Satono Opal is the unlucky dead last. A human equivalent would be if a son of an infamous dictator tried to attend a regular high school. Do you believe the media, or wider society, would dare let him forget what his father did?

It's extreme. It's also reality. These are not excuses, merely explanations.

I stand up, begin walking a circle around the track, and half-way through your face pops into my head, and I cannot help but belch out a laugh.

Most of the deck is stacked against you, and yet you are due to arrive! Against the wishes of society, against the entire Satono conglomerate, against your own fear and better judgment, you have gathered what meager resources you possess and will stride through those gates with a bright smile on your insolent little face!

I'm grateful for that. I also must apologise again.

I apologise for revealing the future with such lack of subtlety and grace. I apologise for implanting the idea into your head with your current inability to truly process it. Time is of essence. Very few grains live in the hourglass. Watch as I extend my hand, and the world shifts. Watch as the gloom and the desecrated overlay atop the realm of the living.

It shimmers and swirls, this realm of horror and terror, of crumbling buildings and cracked roads and greedy shadows leering with their razor-sharp fangs. It vanishes like a mirage at night, as abruptly as it came. Please do not mistake me for a shaman or some grand wizard; I did not conjure that image, only that I predicted it. It is not a welcome thought, so see storm clouds gather on the horizon, yet unable to halt their torrential downpour.

They say for evil to triumph, good men must do nothing. What use is that good if it is unable to comprehend said evil at all?

That's why you're special, Ruby. You're so close to the edge. So infuriatingly close to sliding into that groove I dug. It took a great chunk of my restraint not to thrust you into my world straight off the bat. My better judgment reminded me you can't hasten such developments, nor do you deserve such trauma.

I was young before. I know how much you desire the springtime of youth. Your life has been hard enough already.

So, go. Begin your exciting school life. Attend the school ceremony and meet your roommate. Endure Tracen's lessons, and leap for joy as you taste the sweet grass of the turf. Meet all the umamusume I've mentioned prior and form your own opinions of them. I, your senpai, shall watch over you for a while longer before we truly can talk face-to-face as fellows.

You should make it at least as far as the try-outs, I believe.

I stride towards the school gates, where the wind whips my plain brown hair, and I sense your presence distant in the city. Your dear senpai's hands are clasped in a blessing just for you.

May you strive for greatness.

May you find companionship and sanctuary amidst Tracen Academy.

May you achieve all you have planned in your head since the day you could read and write, unburdened by stress, envy or sabotage.

May you exhaust yourself in the best way possible.

>>END OF PROLOGUE.

>>ACT 1.

1.0: Academy of Hopes and Dreams

Early Morning, April 2nd, 20XX

"More coffee, ma'am?"

"No, thank you, I'm on a budget."

"Are you sure? We've got a half-off on cappucinos. Buy two, get a chocolate muffin free!"

"I'll be fine. I'm, um, just checking my Umastagram feed. It's taking a bit, so if you may…"

The coffee house streets over from Tracen Academy is half-empty. Smooth jazz music skirts the edges of cherry-colored table-tops in an imitation of an American joint, as a nearby patron slugs down a hot matcha. The coffee machine behind the counter produces a whirring note, as if strumming a musical instrument at speeds such objects are not meant to be strummed.

Before you: the dregs latte, a half-eaten piece of melon bread, and a sad little carrot stick. Your name is Satono Ruby, daughter of the worst umamusume to ever exist. You are fifteen years old and attempting to get this waitress to leave you alone.

[Psyche check: 9/6 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

You flash her a gentle smile, and she does. Relieved you're not one of those gluttons or plain nasty in general. Thank goodness for that. Now you can get back to checking that Umastagram post. You sent it ten minutes ago. Curiosity has made you check, against your better judgment.

Just checked out of the motel. Heading out to my next grand adventure. ❤️❤️❤️ to everyone who supported me!

#newhorizons #tracenacademy #readytorace!

>figleaves345 (30sec): FUCK OFF AND DIE

>figleaves345 (1m): Neck yourself 😹

>oshiiiiimasta (2m): nooooooo don't go sing for us more PLEASE

>seventysevens (2m): break both of them in fact! Tracen doesn't want you!

>tripleterror (3m): break a leg for real plz

>kitasansnstrongestsoldier (4m): your mom's doing av rn btw

>deepdarkstageofficial: The enka scene won't be the same without you. Drinking in your honor. 👏👏👏

>mikisanofficial (7m): ignore the antis, rubi! we're all cheering you! We all love you!

>fgfhjdis123 (10m): Brilliant and New Tail Growth Gel Available! Click on this link to learn more…

Your account has received repeated reports. Posting will be locked until a thorough investigation is conducted.

You lift your finger and…

[Social Media check: 52/35 -> Success! +5 EXP]

…swipe Umastagram away. Social media is terrible, and so is everyone who engages in it. An The best way to counter its bad vibes is to look at something positive.

You reach into your knapsack and pull out a cardboard card. It's decorated with a plastic red rose and simple smiley faces and ribbons are drawn on with highlighter markers. Though it's only under a week old, the corners are beginning to fray from the amount of times you've flicked through it.

Farewell, dear Ruby! May the turf bloom beautifully beneath your feet.

~ Saya

Don't stay a stranger. Hit us up whenever you need to chat. We're still sisters forever!

~ Miki

I should have cut your legs off so you'd be with us forever. Just kidding. Give them hell like Izanami upon Izanagi.

~ Hotaru

You're not in the underground anymore, Ruby. Don't lie about your age to adults. Eat food outside of instant ramen and actually make some friends who won't steal your belongings from your pod. Tracen's in the top 1%. You won't get another chance like this ever again.

~ Sincerely, Manager Suzuki

Ignore his tone. Manager's being tsundere. He was crying into his drink about how he could've made you sing at the Tokyo Dome and how you're too good for those Tracen snobs. He even bought you a half-year train pass. Come back to Shibuya on the weekends and sing for us again. We're all going to miss you so so SO much!!!!

~ Kaede

I'll send your regalia to your dorms later. XOXO

~ Seamstress Sugar

It's childish. You can't help it. This is the farthest you've ever been from home, after all. You clutch the letter to your chest and allow the wetness gather in the corner of your eyes.

Precious memories from the past two years wash over you. Meetings at the station. Concerts under blaring lights. Miki pestering Kaede with her pranks and the others laughing madly, including you. Dinners where the manager pulled out his wallet and let the whole group eat good beef and fresh carrots for a change.

These people from the underground were good to you. They could have exploited a naïve brat like you for quick cash at any time, yet they saw your musical talents, extended a hand and lifted you into brief indie stardom. You could have stayed in the underground forever. Would've, since numerous times you felt like you owed them that. They knew your childhood dream, as briefly mentioned as it was, and let you graduate with a smile on your face and your favorite song rushing past your lips.

You'll miss those guys a lot. You'll probably dream about them. Feel homesick, perhaps.

What you cannot do, however, is reverse those goodbyes.

You are no longer Satono Ruby the underground idol. You are Satono Ruby, Tracen Academy's newest student. You earned that place fair and square after completing the basic fitness exam and passing multiple rounds of interview, maternal heritage be damned.

It doesn't matter how daunting the academy building looms, or how fast your heart is pounding. It's time to stop stalling and take your first steps into the academy of your dreams!

[Social Media Presence: +1 to starting Prestige.]

[Mood has become Good.]

[Regalia outfit sidequest skipped! +50 EXP.]

[Half-year pass to Tokyo obtained. Encounters involving Tokyo's wards might appear.]

You down the last of the latte, chomp through the carrot stick, and leave the coffee house. Past a few blocks and over a traffic laneway lies Tracen Academy, its bell-tower visible amidst the throngs of the buildings. Cherry blossoms line the streets. The silver bullet rests coolly against the skin beneath your shirt. You grasp it and knead it between your fingers.

Today, you hope, will be a good day.

1.1: Miss President

>>Meet the student council president, Symboli Rudolf, in order to formally introduce yourself.

Mood: Good

EXP: 70/100

You knock twice on the heavy, ornate door, a persistent force strumming the strings of your heart.

The chatter on the other side halts. A couple of footsteps, a muffled whisper-esque sound that your ears strain to pick up, and then the all-commanding word is given, clearer and louder than the chatter bouncing out of the nearby classrooms.

"Come in."

There's no going back now. You grab the brass handle, pull the door open and enter.

The moment you close the door behind you and face forward, a sense of trepidation washes over you, the type that demands you tread carefully on the heavy floorboards, lest you create an entire percussion quartet with your feet and make an absolute fool of yourself. It grows as you take in the room more: thick wallpapers, patterned rugs, a bitter yet fulfilling varnished smell radiating from the polished mahogany furniture. In contrast with the modernized hallways you passed by, this office is a blend of gothic Western and authoritarian prestige.

It's very fitting for the umamusume sitting behind the desk.

You bow once. "Apologies for the intrusion."

"No worries. We were about to finish up here, anyway. Come closer so I can get a proper look at you."

You step around a pair of Western-style velvet-lined sofas on opposite ends of a glass tea table. A display cabinet full of awards and trophies gleams in the sunlight streaming behind the desk and its occupants. The air is tinged with pine-scented air freshener and the sweetness of roses from nearby flowerpots.

This is the wrong thought to be dawdling amongst in this situation, but it's true. Some of it is from your underground idol debut, where you dressed up as obedient maids and twisted villainesses amidst cheap stage props bearing these exact same themes, but also from muddy memories in the past. Mansion hallways that seem to stretch on forever, filled with the laughter from gifts of fresh chocolate and the pitter-patter of tiny umamusume feet, locked away by a family who'd rather slice off their own fingers than ever dare entertain the notion of welcoming you back again.

It should edge you. Were this room empty, it definitely would have. You stand in front of the desk and instead find yourself struck with pure awe.

Three umamusume face you. One seated behind the desk, with the other two flanking her like vanguards. Their faces and names leap out at you.

[History check: 32/20 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

First, there's Air Groove, the sharp-eyed, no nonsense 'Empress' who serves as the vice-president to the student council. Opposite her is Narita Brian, a Triple-Crown winner and famed loner on the track. Lastly, in the president's seat between them both, the white blazing streak amidst the refined chestnut akin to a flash of white-hot fire caught mid-flight: Symboli Rudolf, the indominatable, almighty Emperor.

All three of these umamusume are beloved students of Tracen Academy. All are legends on the track. If you weren't interrupting their work—they're dressed in clean, neat sets of Tracen's purple-white uniform; papers are held in Air Groove's hands and Rudolf's laptop is out—you'd be squealing with delight inside and fumbling with your phone for a picture.

"Satono Ruby." Symboli Rudolf declares. Her tone is smooth and cool, a rich family's accent propped up with leadership and authority. Her lips quirk in the beginnings of a welcome smile. "What a surprise. I did not expect you would come to meet me first."

Your heartbeat soars. The Emperor is talking to you. The umamusume whose races you used as motivation for your daily runs is talking to you.

You've pretended this umamusume was running alongside you in the local park.

Oh. Oh god, what are you supposed to do? Stammer out a greeting? Ask for an autograph? Beg for mercy?

None of that, Diplomatic face, you tell yourself. Diplomatic face! You came here for a purpose. Put away that inner fangirl and pretend this is another meeting with the higher-ups.

[Composure check: 52/50 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

You take a breath and speak in a composed tone. "Thank you for taking the time to greet me, President Rudolf."

Rudolf lets out a light chuckle. "There's no need for such formality. You're one of us now. Just call me 'Prez' like the rest."

It's a cordial gesture, and you'd be delighted to accept it as such if it weren't for the two umamusume flanking Rudolf. They seem less than pleased at your arrival. Air Groove's slanted eyes are narrowed at you, while Narita Brian chews on a stalk of buckwheat, her arms folded yet her angled slightly towards the edge of the desk, as if ready to charge at any moment.

It's not revulsion. You are an expert at spotting that. It's wariness, which honestly is the prelude to the former.

That thought grounds you. Cools you down.

Sunlight streams from the window behind them, casting their figures in light like the divine, and threading shadows that reach out to you. Tendrils that lick at your feet and spell out lines and words as they stretch across the papers and the furniture. They remind you of your place, of who you are.

That's right, you remind yourself, elation ebbing like foam on a beach, you didn't come here to geek out. You don't possess the privilege for that. Truth is, it doesn't matter if you're a businessman, or a yakuza, or even a newbie singer in the group. Newbies in town pay respect to the boss.

Tracen is no different.

You allow yourself to advance forward a single step. You tuck that placid smile away. Then, you straighten your back, stiffen the muscles in your back and shoulders, and bow as low as you can without your legs bending or your weight falling forwards.

There's a faint intake of breath. It's soon drowned out by your talking.

"I understand that this alone cannot make up for the reputational, social and financial disruption and damages my mother inflicted upon Tracen Academy with her misdeeds. As her daughter, I feel a sense of regret and responsibility and would like to express my apologies on her behalf, as she is now absent. I do not expect forgiveness. I acknowledge my enrollment here is controversial, and intend to carry myself here with dignity and respect befitting of a model Tracen student."

[Wits check: 8/6 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

There it is. The apology you rehearsed with Manager Suzuki, who was gracious to take time out of his busy schedule to teach you and the rest of the girls. He told you that in the digital age, it's more optimal not to waste a bureaucrat's time. You took this to heart, crafting this apology to be as succinct as you hoped it could be. You doubt he intended for you to be answering to the daughter of a powerful politician.

A silence strains itself. It's so thick, it tempts you to peek upwards. You refrain from doing so.

"Stand up." Rudolf says. When you do, she's stopped smiling. "Satono Ruby—"

"Oh, for the love of crud…" Narita Brian interrupts with a dark snarl. She rips the grass stalk out of her mouth, scrunchies it up and hurls it into a nearby wastepaper basket. "This was what all those brats were getting their bloomers in a twist about?"

You swallow a gulp. "I'm sorry. Did I offend you?"

Narita Brian keeps on going. "All the rumors, all the phones ringing—"

"No," Air Groove quickly says, cutting off Narita Brian. She glances at her two fellows, then reaffirms. "No, you did not. We simply did not expect you to lead with that."

"I thought it would be better if I made my intentions known." You reply. "It was what I was taught. I know I might not deserve to be here—"

Narita Brian lets out a growl. "Quit it."

"Pardon?" You ask.

"You heard me, rookie. Quit saying that crap and stand up straight, for crying out loud!"

Before you can react, Narita Brian has stepped out of her position flanking her boss. She's stomped forward until the two of you are almost face-to-face. You gulp as she sizes you up, her grimace twisting further with each passing second.

Somewhere within your perception, you notice Air Groove frown and make a move to advance, only for Rudolf to raise her hand and halt her.

Narita Brian looks you square in the eye. Her tone is flinty and hard. "Judging by that stunt you just pulled, you're real scared of pissing people off, aren't you?"

You try to respond.

[Guts check: 8/10 -> Failure.]

You fail to respond.

This has become an interrogation between you and her, and you have no clue what put you in the handcuffs.

To answer her question deep inside the confines of your own head, you are. More so than most as to start neither argument nor altercation in public. You were thirteen at the time, being lectured by the manager about your new smartphone meant information travelled at the speed of life, and that journalists were chomping at their own teeth to snap a candid photo of you and generate clicks from a story about the daughter of the most umamusume's daughter. Politeness was not just a means of making connections. It was self-defense.

Before you can argue this point, Brian leans slightly forward, you find yourself captivated by the older girl, in the same way a bull rearing to charge becomes very attractive to the nearby matador.

A vein throbbing in her forehead. Rage burning behind that glare. She's almost as tall as you are, yet she makes you feel like an ant. The gap in musculature between her thick biceps and your skinny form is a reminder of the cruel difference set about by the laws of physics. Forget sprints and miles. One light tap from that arm and you're down and out.

[Intimidation check: 28/80 -> Failure.]

You cannot counter this.

"Word of advice, rookie: you're going to be doing a hell lot more of that if you keep bowing and scraping like that stunt earlier." Narita Brian hisses. "Do you realise how many kids I saw bawling their eyes out because they couldn't step through the gates of this place?"

"I…I don't understand." You stammer.

"Think." Narita Brian demands.

[Logic check: 45/40 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

"Dozens? Hundreds?" You answer, weakly. You recall passing multiple stages to get into the exercise part of the exam. The higher you go, the less room there is available.

"Hundreds is correct." Narita Brian says. "Now take a good look at yourself."

You actually do this out of pure bewildered instinct.

Narita Brian rolls her eyes, dumbfounded by your inability to predict what she's thinking.

"You took the exam, kid. You passed the exam. Crawled out of the gutter, flew past goddamn near everyone who wanted your tail out the door, and managed to land a seat at the best racing school in the world, all before giving a single thought about setting foot in a regional." Narita Brian continues. She curls her fist, tight and powerful. "A year ago, if someone had told me some random Shibuya amateur accomplished all that, I would've decked them square in the nose."

You wonder if this senior, this umamusume packed with brawny racing muscle, is about to do that. Grab you by the shoulders and shake you until your bones and cowardice fall out, or she'll cut to the chase and strangle you with her hair rope.

Narita Brian leans forward until your noses are almost touching. "Don't you dare forget that."

"Brian!" Air Groove shouts. She yanks Narita Brian back. "That's enough! You're acting out of line!"

"Don't touch me." Narita Brian hisses.

"Exploding at a first year? Have you no shame?" Air Groove retorts.

Narita Brian grunts, shoving Air Groove's grip off with her muscular arm. They both share a heated glare, before Brian yanks her head away from her colleague with a scowl.

"She's a Tracen student, Groove. She'd better start acting like one. This was a favor." She then raises her hand, tilting her head back towards the front desk. "I'll leave this to you, Prez. Going back to class now."

Air Groove bristles. It's too late. Narita Brian brushes past you and heads for the door.

Air Groove reaches out to her, then looks back at Rudolf, who merely lifts her head and nods once. An entire string of orders is carried out in that silent exchange, within which don't follow is among one of them. Air Groove understands. She walks over, and you're now face to face with another esteemed senior. This time, it's with sympathy. Acuity and diligence renowned for enforcing discipline and terrorizing rivals soften as she examines you.

"Are you feeling alright? Should I take you outside for a bit?" Air Groove asks.

"Oh. Oh no." You mumble out, eyes wide. "That's…not a problem to me. I'm fine. Really."

"Allow me to apologise on behalf of Narita Brian," Air Groove says. There is irony here that you have no room in your head to perceive at present. "She should not have spoken in that tone."

"I'll take care of her, Groove. We'll make this a private meeting." Rudolf interrupts. She waves at the door. "Go and check on the dorm managers. We might have a couple of jokesters running about."

Air Groove bows once towards Rudolf, before following her head.

The door slams shut with a thud. You are left in the room, still dumbstruck and grounded in place, alongside one of the greatest athletes Tracen has ever produced, and you remain as such, listening to the ticking of a desk clock, until fingers snap.

It's Rudolf. She has stood up from her desk, having brushed her laptop away. She's holding a clipboard with paper on it. The sight of it is strangely familiar.

"Why don't you take a seat over there?" She says.

There happens to be one of the maroon couches in the center of the room. Each one is stacked with pillows in muted colors. You plonk yourself down on the one closest to the exit, knees tucked together and your hands in your lap. This would be a great place to take a nap, if you weren't busy being mired in absolute shock. Talk about a welcoming party.

Rudolf doesn't join immediately. She busies herself around the room, pulling out a thermos flask from under her own desk. Next, she opens a miniature fridge from inside a cupboard and withdraws a platter full of sandwiches. Hot lemongrass spills into two mugs, filling the air with a citrusy presence. The sandwiches, you notice, have been neatly cut into almost perfect triangles.

"Sorry about Brian." Rudolf says. She takes the couch opposite her. "She's been stressed out lately. First her Trainer fell down with a nasty illness, then she kept receiving calls over the past few weeks from people trying to contact me. She's more of a soldier, than a politician, if that makes sense. She still shouldn't have blown up at you."

"No. It's fine." You say woodenly. "I think she might've had a point."

Rudolf examines you. She lets out a soft sigh. "Please don't take what she said too personally."

You fear that might be impossible. Narita Brian's words keep bouncing inside the cavities of your head. They're sinking deep into the bedrock. Brash, loud, not a dream and totally uncalled for—and yet, in a strange, roundabout way, they weren't negative. Was she actually complimenting you? It sounds stupid. If it's true…

Maybe the two of you can be friends, once she calms down and you snag some actual achievements? Maybe. The apology was still necessary, just to be on the safe side.

Your nose trembles. Your gaze travels down to the sandwiches.

"I usually keep them there for a quick snack after work." Rudolf explains.

You completely understand. These are not ordinary sandwiches. They're important political meeting party platter sandwiches. Real butter, fresh cheese and ham, lettuce as green as the grass itself and, oh god, they even have juicy tomatoes. Your old group would've to put on a showstopper to receive this fare. Drool's gathering like runoff from a broken dam inside your mouth.

"C-can I?" The question slips from your lips before you can control yourself, or ponder the insanity of the Symboli Rudolf, a seven Crown winner, handing you a packed lunch in disguise.

Rudolf just pushes the plate forward with a mild chuckle. "Help yourself."

And so you do. There's no room to count calories or ponder whether a slice of tomato is secretly giving you a funny look. You chew and chomp and devour until the third sandwich is well tucked away inside your belly, and even then, the assortment of freshness combined with the savory meat and the slick butter swirls and tingles on the tip of your tongue, tempting you for more. This cannot be a bribe. It's whatever the opposite of it is. Please don't let yourself wake up from this dream.

Rudolf waits for you in silence. She sips her tea and wears an amused half-smirk you think is tinged with nostalgia. She also watches your pace with intent, because when you finish the fourth sandwich—somehow not dropping a crumb in the process—she's already placed her cup down and straightened herself up. "Finished?"

You nod, brushing the sides of your mouth with a napkin. You recognise the shift in atmopshere from many backstage meetings. It's serious time.

"I'll be frank with you, Satono Ruby. Tracen is an institution that receives its funding from many sponsors as well as the government. Big sportswear companies, banks, even think-tanks in the highest echelons of the government that draft legislation, for example." Rudolf's gaze grows more severe. You tense in return. "We received many a request to not admit you."

This time, you swallow the information without paling. "I understand."

"No thoughts?" Rudolf asks.

You shrug, mildly. "I guess it makes some things clearer in hindsight."

"Enlighten me, then. Tell me your story."

This is a personal question, one that you are hesitant to answer, especially if it could inconvenience one of the highest authorities present in Tracen whom you admired on occasion. This whole affair is surreal beyond your wildest dreams.

"Nothing. Nothing much, Prez! I'm already here anyway, so it doesn't matter…" Rudolf's brows furrow, and a frown begins to form. The terrible thought of disappointing the head of the academy you're now enrolled in, who is also an umamusume you've admired like so many others, beats you over the head, so you hastily add, "It's not much. My physical evaluation was put off until the last moment. I thought they wouldn't do it, but there was this nice old man who took it for me at a racecourse right as the sun was about to go down. There was also the interview, which wasn't done for me in person. Oh, but the AI interviewer was very interesting. The way they strung together sound bites was cool. I didn't know they could use computers like that…"

"I've found those things to be unreliable." Rudolf comments, folding her arms, her frown deepening. "Not so much newfangled as prone to letting paperwork get lost in the scuffle."

There's no humor, no levity, in that. Disdain, more like. Weren't there rumors of the Emperor enjoying terrible, outdated puns like Maruzensky? Guess they must be false.

"I—"

[Psyche check: 9/6 -> Success! +5 EXP]

You tuck the apology you are about to respond and switch gears. "I am here now." You say, in a small, self-depreciating voice.

"You are," Rudolf affirms.

You shrug in what you hope is an appreciate matter. "For better or worse."

"All the way from an umadol." Rudolf finishes. She rests a hand on her knee, the other cupping her chin. "A decently successful one, I've been led to believe."

You pause. "I don't suppose you're a f—"

"Unfortunately not."

Yeah. That checks out. The daughter of the prestigious Symboli family listens to classical piano all the time, probably. They'd throw your records in the trash before they even got past the front gate.

"I do know the reviews about your performance were positive and your albums sold well. Your manager was also fair to the talents under his command, which is sadly uncommon in the industry. One would think you had secured a promising career there."

This time, you don't miss the implications.

No grudge against Rudolf, for this is a question you've asked and been asked many times by acquaintances and friends. The idol industry was a demanding, volatile beast that chews up cotton candy dreams and spits out tears. It was also the one place where you found your success after running away from the shrine and risking your entire existence on Tokyo's unknown.

You wonder if Narita Brian was aware of that too. The fact you threw away stability to leap into the great unknown; a great insult to the failed rejects who struggled through local and regional tournaments.

It doesn't matter, you tell yourself. You want to be in Tracen. You're confident about it. Totally, iron clad, one hundred and one percent. Receiving the acceptance letter in the office mail sent you into a fit so tizzy Manager Suzuki brought out his phone to call an ambulance. There's no other stage in the world you'd rather land your feet in.

It's just that—

Well—

Do they really have to ask all those questions?

By they you mean everyone you passed by on the way to the office. It was midway through the first class, the teachers watching their students like hawks, yet you felt the attention pinprick on your skin like a thousand invisible needles. Peeks from behind books, fingers tapping at phones, smirks falling outside of huddles. Verbal pokes and prods, audible from behind the glass windows via the channel of imagination and experience.

Is that her?

I can't believe it. The audacity of this bitch.

Heard she's never even stepped on the track. We could knock her dead.

She's so skinny. Like Curren Chan, but a million times worse. I bet she can't even run a full spurt.

Why'd we have to get the worst Satono as well? Diamond's so cute, and she's—ugh.

You look at Rudolf, who is waiting patiently, and from that nobility and sternness you feel the past creeping back, as if she's repeating those same taunts and snarks. Stay in the underground. Stay in front of the microphone. You're not a racer. Satono Opal was, and you carry her blood, so what were you expecting?

You think you can survive in this den of poisonous snakes?

You grip your arm tightly and purse your lips, suddenly feeling a great hesitation to open your mouth and embarrass yourself in front of the academy's number one.

"I…" You stutter. "I, um…"

You trail off, heat blooming in your cheeks. You can't do it. Even as part of you shrinks back, another shakes its head and bemoans who this is so uncool of you.

God, what are you doing?

Eclipse first, the rest nowhere.

Your ears twitch up. There's someone to your right. A woman's voice, airy and casual. You turn your head—

Eclipse first, the rest nowhere.

[World Resonance check: 47/30 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

—and find empty air. But above it, a banner hangs on a wall. Framed in gold, the text written in extravagant calligraphy: Tracen Academy's school motto. It burns at the forefront of your mind like a religious mantra.

Eclipse first, the rest nowhere.

Taken to its literal meaning, the motto means to run so fast, excel so greatly, the bridge between you and your rivals is built over less of a gap and more of a yawning chasm. You can easily project it onto the greats: the tyrannical Orfevre, or the lightning-fast Silence Suzuka, or even the capricious Gold Ship. Umamusume who have embedded themselves in Tracen's history.

What about you? You, who threw herself into the lion's den. You, whose blood is tained with a toxic and magnificent what-could-have-been?

Rudolf notices you staring at the banner. She relaxes and continues her silence.

You read the banner over and over again, trying to find inspiration.

Eclipse first, the rest nowhere.

Five words and one comma. The motto says nothing else. It remains eternal and still.

[(World Resonance check: 47/100 || Insight check: 9/14) -> Failure.]

It leaves its statement up to the reader's interpretation. It is what it is.

Something resembling a click pings in your head. You let out a small, crooked and shaky smile.

"I get it. I mean, I think I have something."

"What did you get?" Rudolf asks.

You face forward and take a deep breath. The words start tumbling out.

"I'm not an expert, so I don't know if this really makes sense, but think I should continue behaving as an idol. Sort of. It's the best of my roots, and the track and the stage aren't that different when you take their audience sizes or their function into account. They were both designed to make the audience happy." You reply. You press your hands together. "I really loved doing that, ever since I got into the groove and learned to properly sing. The concerts I had with my group the best afternoons and nights of my life."

Rudolf nods. "Anything else?" She prompts. She's observing you intently.

"Well..." You let out an awkward chuckle. "I can't really do any of that if I don't knuckle down and learn, train and compete at my best, right? Bet all my senpais said the same thing."

You pause and think for a second.

"Oh, I hope I can make friends too."

The moment in which Rudolf contemplates this seems to stretch on forever. You are struck with the sudden realisation this meeting has transformed into an impromptu final interview.

You're confident what you said wasn't a correct answer. There may not be a single objective, correct answer. The umamusume who preceded you surely gave out answers far surpassing your amateur brainpower. It's so easy to say those lines to someone who is willing to receive and not predisposed to sneer and snark; for platitude to remain unchallenged, unexamined.

But, it may have been enough, because Rudolf smiles for real.

[Persuasion check: 72/60 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

"There you have it." Rudolf says. "You are a Tracen student. You are enrolled. Brian said the rest."

She really was complimenting you, if her own ornery way.

You exhale and force your knees to stop shaking. You hadn't realised they'd started that. That…took a lot out of you. And you feel a pleasant, warm feeling fluttering beneath your breast.

"For the record, Tracen is not an institution that discriminates based on one's prestige. Heritage and fortune only pull so much weight. Not even the Satonos nor the Mejiros, nor any outside influence can change that. That is a tenet that stretches back to the founding days." Rudolf explains. "The only means of gaining respect around these parts is results."

"I understand."

"We're both aware of your mother's reputation. You will have extra eyes on you. Your behavior will be examined under a microscope for any misdemeanor."

Rudolf then grimaces. Frustration. You've seen it on Manager Suzuki when he had to act as the bearer of bad news, usually whenever the higher-ups were about to enforce some stupid new rule.

"I do not tolerate bullying in Tracen. I can define what the standards are and enforce them as best as I can with the vigilance of my council. I'm proud of what we have built and achieved. However, I cannot control the minds of others. I cannot be everywhere."

She's not your guardian angel. Her hands are tied in her own ways. It's a little disappointing on a reactive, emotional level, yet it makes sense. A lesson you learned from mythology is that the loftiest peaks rattle with their own chains.

If you ever encounter harassment, you'll have to deal with it yourself. No preferential treatment.

"That's said…" Rudolf smiles a wolfish grin with teeth. "There's nothing stopping me from ensuring a student begins on relatively equal footing with her peers."

"What do you mean?" You ask.

"I have resources. I also have the wiggle room to allocate them." She raises a coquettish finger to her lips at that.

"All for me?"

"Yes. Your education was stunted." Rudolf says bluntly.

You sputter. A metaphorical arrow through the heart. "It wasn't that bad." You protest.

"You barely passed the written exam by two points." Rudolf counters. She flips a page on her clipboard and squints at it, frowning. "The examiner concluded the multiple-question parts were filled partially based on luck."

Lungs, kidney, tailbone! You're bleeding hard! "I…was busy with running practice? And I answered some questions..."

"Your report also states you did not graduate from middle school."

Your soul has collapsed in a heap and is breathing smoke out of the shrunken pores. Look, the last vestiges of your fortitude wish to say. Listen here, president. The umadol life requires sacrifice. The average middle-schooler's education was among the first on the chopping block. You were tall for your age, which let you pose as a short umamusume adult. If you kept answering questions about your education, they'd deduce you were still a middle school student!

(Ignoring that Manager Suzuki did eventually find out and allow you to stay, bless his glorious, magnanimous heart.)

"Although, good work on the Foreign Languages component. Your English is at a decent level."

Because you thought it could attract a foreign audience…

"T-thank you…"

"You're not the worst student I've had the pleasure to grade."

"But I'm up, or down, there?" You ask, weakly.

Rudolf gives you that half-smirk again. You guess that means yes.

"To get back on topic, it is a serious issue we have here." Rudolf lectures. "Tracen requires its students to perform competently at a standard education so they are not left stranded upon graduation. We will not have you be the exception."

She picks up a pen and writes notes on the paper on her clipboard. "You will need to attend remedial lessons. Mathematics, literature, Japanese, a couple of electives—you might have to start a grade behind on some subjects. We'll need to improve your diet as well. I'll write you a pass to get out of lessons today so we can get this all sorted out."

She stands up, taking the teacups and sandwich platter away. "Follow me."

"Where are we going?" You ask.

"To begin." Rudolf replies.

So, a day of sitting at a desk in a private room, listening to lectures that bore you out of your skull. You can't exactly complain, given it's coming straight from the student council president's own generosity. She wasn't exactly wrong about your studies. Who knows, you think, maybe you'll find a subject you actually enjoy, now that you'll be learning from professionals and not impatient shrine attendants.

Rudolf doesn't lead you back to the classrooms. She takes you outside. The whispers are noticeably quieter on the way down, replaced with gobsmacked looks, and you are grateful for that and Rudolf for being with you. The pointing still happens.

Your confusion only grows as you and Rudolf leave behind the building and head towards the racetrack.

"Have you ever raced against anyone before?" Rudolf asks.

You think for a moment, then shake your head. They didn't let you at the shrine, fearing that any replication of your mother's talents would exacerbate the Satono jink, and you were mostly too busy during your umadol career. The few umamusume you did work up the courage panicked or spat at you upon learning your full name. You stopped pretty quickly after that. You were a solo runner. Listening to replays of old G1 races and imagining yourself running amidst far-away tracks was as good as you got.

"I thought as much. It truly is a shame. There's nothing like the wind of competition pushing at your back." Rudolf chuckles. "That changes now."

You step onto the turf, and your jaw threatens to unhinge itself. The urge to rub your eyes like some cartoon character is inexplicable. Rudolf has brought you an umamusume to race against. But not just any umamusume. Oh no, the president has brought a prominent racer in this academy, with proven results and a solid presence on Japan's racing stage. You'll be running against her alone, with no onlookers or hecklers to interrupt you.

You're obviously not going to win against her. You will, however, learn something through experience, as you always have. Could this also be the start of a wonderful friendship…?
