1.2: Student Mentorship

>>Grass Wonder, the embodiment of silk hiding steel, who bursts out of the pack like a demon! (May improve Acceleration and/or Power)

>>I want to taste the power of a true champion. Do your worst!

Mood: Good.

EXP: 20/100

You see an umamusume stretching her arms on the spot at the side of the racetrack. Her standard Tracen tracksuit winks red from the distance; as you approach, you spot more detail. Long ears, a mane of silky, flowing light-chestnut hair desired by fashion magazines, and a gold, shield-shaped buckle adorned with red and blue ribbon around one ear.

She looks up, sees you and Rudolf approach close, and lifts a hand for a gentle wave.

"President. Satono Ruby." The umamusume's voice is a measured, elegant one. She bows her head. "Good morning, and pleased to meet you."

"Thanks for coming out here on such short notice." Rudolf says, also sounding pleased. "Everything all sorted out in class?"

"Yes. My teachers were understanding of my new schedule. I've also told Hana that I'll be spending extra time training Miss Ruby here."

Your memory finally catches up with the mention of your name.

[History check: 32/30 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

"You're Grass Wonder!" You exclaim.

The two umamusume look at you. Your cheeks turn slightly pink.

"You've heard of me?" Grass Wonder asks.

The cat's out of the bag. Might as well spill the rest of your excitement.

"Of course! You're a G1 winner, you're famous on the Umanet for your sense of style, and—" Your own smile can't help but brim as you speak. "You won the Takarazuka Kinen last year. We were listening over the radio during a break, and the whole office caught on fire when you burst out to take the lead at the end."

Grass Wonder titters, one slender-fingered hand coming to press against the bottom of her lips. "My, my, to think a newcomer would still remember Takarazuka last year. It was quite an achievement, wasn't it? I'm flattered, Miss Ruby. Thank you."

Such modesty. Such grace. Your head briefly fills with the pink carnations grown in your old shrine's gardens. You giggle back, trying not to let any awkwardness creep onto your face. The reason said office caught on fire was because Manager Suzuki used to be a massive Special Week fan, and flat-out boasted he'd treat the entire group to deluxe ice-cream two blocks down if she lost in the Takarazuka Kinen. Hotaru and Miki clung to that promise like flies on carrion. The absolute dumbstruck horror carved onto his stony face when Grass Wonder shot forward and claimed victory was priceless and beautiful and is still floating around the group chat somewhere. The chocolate had been so good too.

You'd hug Grass Wonder just for that. You're not sure if she'd take that or the story behind it well, so you instead ask Rudolf another question.

"Um, president?"

"Yes?" Rudolf answers.

"I'm super happy I get to meet Grass Wonder, but…" You attempt to gesture towards your new senpai in a fashion that doesn't involve pointing and staring. "Not to be rude or anything, but am I really racing against her?"

"Is there a problem with that?" Rudolf says, smirking.

"Well…" You stammer. "She's a G1 winner, and I haven't raced anyone in my life. She'd pulverise me into a dumpster."

"I'd be lying if the thought hadn't crossed my mind." Rudolf comments. Grass Wonder titters again. You gulp. "But thoughts like those have a place. It's called the first draft. No, you're not racing against Grass in any official capacity. You're here to be taught."

That, you feel, is almost as ludicrous, but far more manageable.

It's a student mentorship program, Rudolf goes on to explain, modeled after the ones found in most competent universities. As for the reason behind its origin, examine the two main ways of entering Tracen. The first is to pass the entrance exam, consisting of several grueling rounds of academics, athleticism and psychological profiling, each one designed to cut out swathes of applicants until the best remain. The second way is to accomplish a great feat at a regional level, such as winning the Tokai Derby, and be scouted by Tracen itself.

Standard aptitude distribution modeling dictates that the majority of successful applicants are located within the below-average or higher. The problem arises when applicants become positioned at the negative tail end of the curve. For example, a hypothetical student who passed borderline in all stages of the entrance exam because she was homeschooled, then ran away, and then pretended to be a legal adult for the sake of making money as an underground idol. She would find herself ill-positioned to begin proceeding with the first stages of her education at Tracen.

"For students who were poor in academics but highly successful at a regional level, we've relied on teachers and private tutors to help them cover their gaps. That would have been the case for you in the past. However, we've discovered some students work better than taught by their peers, thus we devised this program. I chose Grass Wonder because she's proven to be reliable in terms of both ranked results and academic grades, and she's taught her peers before." Rudolf explains.

"It was nothing short of a privilege to be chosen." Grass Wonder adds. "Rest assured, Miss Ruby, you are in good hands."

"We'll be able to catch up faster as fellow members of Team Rigil, too." Rudolf says. "I should mention this is still a trial system. A beta run, if you will. Should it prove successful, we'll expand the scope of application."

"I get that…" You say, scratching your cheek, "But aren't I supposed to have a trainer?"

"Normally, through being scouted at the bi-monthly tryouts." Rudolf responds. "The way you are now, you might have some trouble accomplishing that."

It stings a little to hear. You can't deny it. Compared to students who bled and sweat through regionals, or had a stable education, you've gone 0 for 0 and scraped by via energy-drink-slugging cramming and listening to online umafluencer podcasts. No wonder the examiners thought you coasted by on luck. It was probably true!

"Don't worry." Grass Wonder says, snapping you out of your thoughts. "If you made it into Tracen, it means you possess potential. We'll make you a first-class umamusume out of you yet."

She extends her hand. You hesitate before gripping it and giving Grass Wonder a firm handshake back, exactly as the umadol biz taught you.

She's got long fingers, Grass Wonder does. The type Hotaru has, good for calligraphy or piano playing. The callused palms tell a different story, sculpted muscle hidden beneath her elegance and friendliness, and a tinge of wariness creeps to the forefront of your mind. Where would someone develop their palms during a race, you wonder. Clenching them too hard during running? Gripping dumbells during weight training? Some strange side-event where she pulls out a stick and starts whacking her opponents?

…maybe you're overthinking this. Grass Wonder seems nice enough. She probably practices iajutsu or archery in her spare time. It's nothing you should be concerned about, especially when you're getting the opportunity to learn from a G1 winner.

"Please take care of me!" You say and bow your head.

Grass Wonder does not remark about you about your mother. She just smiles and takes you aside closer towards the track, while Rudolf hangs in the back, observing. You're grateful to both.

You don't start running immediately. Even a nigh-dropout like you understands you need to warm-up first. Grass Wonder doesn't open with that—no, she pulls out a small notebook from inside her tracksuit pocket and begins quizzing you on the basics. What are the basic rules for a race? Start from the gate and cross the finish line without interfering. What are the four track lengths? Sprint, mile, medium and long. Why is running in the inner post risky? Because you might get boxed in or be swamped in traffic if you don't break out fast enough.

So on, and so forth.

[Racing Tactics check: 52/30 -> Success! +5 EXP]

You pass the quiz at a competent enough level. Grass Wonder takes you through a series of warm-up stretches. When you struggle through your arm lunges, she takes your limbs and guides you through the motions.

"You're quite limber." Grass Wonder remarks.

"Thank you." You say, trying not to sound strained from the exertion.

"Did you work out before?"

"Umadol life. Lots of dancing." You wince as piece of meat inside you pulls over a nub.

"Lots of minute dexterity and agility. Not so much for long-distance running, but it does have its perks. You won't be freezing on stage, that's for sure." Grass Wonder muses. She lets go and watches you repeat the motions, unattended. "I suspect I'll have to watch you for your footwork on the field."

You preen at the praise. She's right. Since you were dancing all the time, you thought you might as well incorporate a few tricky steps from routines during your practice. It was against imaginary opponents, mind, but it's the thought that counts.

Grass Wonder takes a spare tracksuit and a pair of running shoes out of a duffel bag and hands them to you. They're backup supplies for tardy students or special exceptions. You, of course, have your own set waiting for your back at your new dorm room. Neated and folded straight out of the academy shop. Wearing someone else's gift is sacrilege back in the underground arena. Times are changing—literally. No way in hell you're not about to waste time fetching them now. You'll endure the mildly sweaty smell in exchange for taking a minute longer in the shower once this training session is over.

The clothes fit like a glove. You twist your torso, feel the sturdy fabric shift and wrap around your undershirt like a glove. There are no mirrors here, no pools of clear creek water to gaze into and watch your form shimmer. If you could see yourself now, you'd like to think of yourself as capable. Clad in a strong uniform, groomed and clean, muscles springy and relaxed for what your physique was always meant to achieve.

It's a far cry from the loose robes of your old shrine maiden outfit. That just makes you happier.

Alright, you think to yourself, pumping a fist. This is good. This is fantastic. The day might've started out with yelling and screaming, but the winds of fate are switching directions, blowing in your favor. You're obviously not going to win against Grass Wonder, but you'll get out there, show your guts and make her proud!

You take a single step towards the starting line—a cardboard cutout of the classic racetrack gates.

That's when you feel it.

[(Instinct check: 32/40) || (World Resonance check: 47/45) -> Success! +10 EXP.]

Footsteps. A presence. A hole in the air, in which weight and brute strength and the scent of scorching hot volcanic ash steams and scalds. It freezes you in place, this sensation of your pathetic soul moments before a train materializes out of thin air and splatters you across the tracks. You crick your neck. You finally gather the courage and look behind.

It's—

Ashen grey hair, eyes with blue like the fading of dawn, and a yellow diamond headband. Only one umamusume throughout modern history is styled like that. Her name is—

"Oguri." Rudolf says, walking towards you.

Ashen Beast, Hero of Kasamatsu, the URA mover and shaker Oguri triple-goddesses-damned Cap herself strolls up to you, Grass Wonder and Rudolf, one hand raised in greeting and a vaguely lost expression on her face. "Morning, Prez."

"Good morning to you, Oguri." Rudolf says, grinning in spite of herself.

You stand. You stare. Your mouth is a mountainous desert.

This is real and happening.

[Guts check: 8/5 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

Your ego lifts its hand and backhands your id across the cheeks. Of course, Oguri Cap's here. She's a Tracen student. She lives on campus. She and Rudolf were friends when you were still scraping yen off the floor of the Shibuya underground for coffin motel fees!

"This is a surprise. I thought you were in lessons." Rudolf remarks. "Did you need me for something?"

"Brian told me to come." Oguri replies.

"Oh?"

"Yeah. Something about a little 'chibi' you were taking care of in some new program of yours. She was…" Oguri cups a finger beneath her chin as she thinks. "You know when you get in the mood where you're mad at something, and it's not that something's fault so you can't be super duper angry, but you're still kinda mad regardless? That's how Brian felt like to me."

"Prickly as ever…" Rudolf clicks her tongue. She falls into a thoughtful silence. When it's clear she's not talking, Oguri directs her attention onto you and Grass.

You remain silent in fear of making another esteemed senpai of yours explode again. Grass Wonder does not.

"Hello, Oguri."

"You're Grass Wonder." Oguri says, not skipping a beat.

"You've heard about me," Grass Wonder states.

Oguri nods, a thoughtful, controlled movement. "Jo told me a bit about you. He was there when you did your second round of try-outs and also for a couple of your races. He said you were pretty good. The trainers all call you the second coming of Maruzensky."

It's high praise coming from an umamusume still considered a fan favorite and a living legend amongst the racing scene, especially since Maruzensky was so talented her opponents sometimes flat-out refused to face her. Any normal umamusume would be jumping with joy. Grass Wonder merely keeps her hands pressed in front of her. She bows her head in the same fashion she did towards Rudolf, an action you notice takes a second longer this time. "I'm honored to hear that."

It's stiffness, you realise. These two umamusume are not even acquaintances. This is the first real conversation they've ever had.

"Good job at the Takarazuka last year." Oguri says.

"Same for you at the Arima Kinen back then." Grass Wonder responds. "I wish I could have seen it. A miracle comeback, they called it."

God, this is exactly how Manager Suzuki and Miki spoke to your rivals backstage. It's not exactly anger, nor as deep as hatred, more akin to the manifestation of raw, grinding curiosity beneath masks and smiles. It's respect born from the desire to clash talent against talent. The bud's sprouting and blooming deep down. If you weren't present, these two would be making strides towards the track.

Is this how G1 champions act on a daily basis? Wow.

"So where's the chibi?" Oguri asks.

"I don't know what Narita Brian means by that, but isn't it obvious?" Grass Wonder gestures to you. "You're looking at her."

Oguri fixes you a look. Her neck rotates. You straighten your back in response, hands falling to your side.

"She's too tall." Oguri concludes.

…huh?

"Pardon?" Grass Wonder says.

"Chibis have round heads and small bodies. This girl's is, um, her name is—"

"Satono Ruby." You answer.

"Satono Ruby isn't anything like that. She's only a bit shorter than Creek," Oguri says. She folds her arms and grins. Her tail, long and a shade lighter than her hair, swishes back and forth. "Plus, she sounds like the mystery girl on the PA system."

You lack context, yet you know that sentence is one of the worst you've ever heard.

"PA system?" You repeat, a note of dread creeping into your tone.

"Didn't you hear it? Wait, you're new. Sorry. Someone played a song over the PA system for fifteen seconds before lots of kicking and screaming occurred and the song cut off. It sounded pretty good, and I think the singer was you. Chibis can't sing."

[Composure check: 52/80 -> Failure.]

[Guts check: 8/11 -> Failure.]

That guttural howling you hear? It's your soul, rattling around the confines of its ethereal cage, as your muscles slacken and all the blood takes a holiday from the vicinity of your stupid face. Oguri Cap blinks. Grass Wonder stares. You stare down at the grass, hoping a solution will manifest from the denizens of the legendary mole poeple.

Your songs—over the PA system—for the entire school—

Ebisu! Are you screwing with me? Was that coin not enough, you bastard?

"Oguri..." Rudolf says. She's smiling, but her tone is one of warning. "May I remind you that Ruby is a new student at Tracen? Speak with a little more tact next time, please. Don't glorify accidents either."

"Sorry, Ruby…" Oguri rubs the back of her neck, embarrassed. "But it really was good. It reminded me of home. The mountains and the forest hikes and stuff like that."

"Tell me…" You mumble from your metaphorical pit of darkness. "Tell me it didn't involve violins."

"I don't think so? I'm not super great at music, either, so…"

Oh, good. It was a song you enjoyed making and which your fans considered good. If it had been your debut track, you'd never be able to look any of these umamusume in the eye ever again.

…this conversation sounds strangely familiar, for whatever reason. Someone, somewhere, is giggling.

Oguri just shrugs and turns to Rudolf. "So, you don't need my help, prez?"

"No."

"Oh, okay, I'll be off—"

"No, as in, I think you should stay." Rudolf clarifies.

Oguri is half-way through turning around when her tail shoots up and she switches gears, kicking up a small patch of dust. Grass Wonder is equally puzzled.

"Grass is helping Ruby get prepared for the tryouts as part of her student mentorship program. We could use another participant, since the races will be conducted with trios at minimum," Rudolf says.

Grass Wonder raises her hand. "President Rudolf, if I'm sharing my duties with Oguri here—"

"Oguri isn't part of the program. She's not the focus here. Ruby is." Rudolf interrupts. "Remember, Ruby has never raced against anyone before, so in my opinion, the more participants she must accustom herself to, the better. The rest of the lesson plans going forward will be up to you, including if you want Oguri to return or not."

"You've never raced against anyone before? Not even back home?" Oguri reaches out and pats you on the shoulder. "I'm so sorry. It must have been hard."

It was. It's also condolences you're incapable of processing right now.

"You're more than free to deny this idea if you think it won't work." Rudolf says towards Grass Wonder.

Grass Wonder opens her mouth, then lowers her hand and sighs. "You do have a point. Very well. It's a good thing I packed spares."

"Oguri?" Rudolf asks.

"I'll do it!" Oguri cries. Her ears wiggle with what you assume is delight. "I've always wanted to teach first-years. This will be fun."

Rudolf chuckles and rips off a pass slip from her clipboard paper, which Oguri grabs and holds in both hands like a fresh lottery card. Grass Wonder pulls over the duffel bag and digs out a plastic box. The cover flips open. Pairs of metallic grey cleats, along with a small work hammer, lie inside.

That's how you're left to complete the rest of your stretches as Grass Wonder and Oguri hammer the new cleats onto their own running shoes. Grass Wonder utilizes the nearby railing to support her cleat like a blacksmith with an anvil. Oguri prefers the grass, sitting cross-legged nearby and humming as she whacks. Metallic ringing fills the air.

"Hey, Grass, how hard are we running?" Oguri asks.

"We're preparing Ruby for the try-outs." Grass Wonder calls back. "Around that level will do."

"I didn't do those." Oguri replies. "Regional level, then?"

"A little lower than your standards, I'd imagine. We're not here to annihilate her." Grass Wonder finishes hammering in the cleat, then grabs her altered shoes and walks towards you. "Your thoughts, Ruby?"

"Me?" You squeak.

"We have a surprise visitor today. I was wondering if you had any objections."

"Not really?" You say. When Grass Wonder's expression doesn't change, you hurriedly continue, "I mean, it must be off-putting for Miss Oguri to barge in from your end, though I'd be lying if I said I didn't appreciate the chance to learn from someone as good as her. Not that you're bad or anything…"

"I don't blame you." Grass Wonder says. She gazes off into the racetrack. "Her record far surpasses mine. I dare say this is a rare opportunity for the both of us."

"Isn't she retired from the Twinkle Series?"

"Allegedly. These things change. It's a true shame she was cut off from the Japanese Derby back then." Grass Wonder says. "I would have liked to see her there."

You're not sure what to comment about that, since Oguri's famous performance was a bit before you got interested in the whole racing business, so you opt for glancing down at the shoes in Grass Wonder's hands. "What are those cleats for?"

"These? They'll handicap us with their weight. That's it." Grass Wonder says. She studies you and frowns. "Is something the matter?"

"Nothing."

"Ruby." Grass Wonder says, "I live with El, as in El Condor Pasa. You might not know this, but she is horrible at covering up her true feelings when flustered. I'd appreciate it if you spoke honestly to me, your mentor."

[Orphaned Trait -> Exists.]

It's a fair enough question, and you appreciate it coming from someone your own age, rather than a middle-aged fuddy of a Trainer.

"This might sound stupid…" You begin, feeling yourself blush again. "I was hoping you and Oguri would go full berserk on me. I want to see the power of a true champion up close."

Grass Wonder blinks. A soft sound escapes from her mouth before she lifts her hand again—balancing the heavy cleat-infused shoes on her other—and lets out a round of full-on chuckling. It sounds exactly like ten minutes ago. It sends a shiver bolting down your spine.

"Ruby, I think you possess some misconceptions about how training works. You wouldn't tell an apprentice to spar with Miyamoto Musashi, correct?"

"Guess not." You say warily. "He's not gonna learn anything. Musashi's too fast."

"Right. If Oguri and I blasted right out of the starting line, we'd leave you in the dust, unable to learn anything from our stride, stance, pacing, and so on. You need to walk before you can run, in a manner of speaking." Grass Wonder says. "Now, I can't speak for Oguri, but to me it seems like you thought I'd be going easy on you."

A bead of sweat gathers on your brow. "That's not happening, is it?"

Grass Wonder smiles. "Do you know why they started calling me, Spe, El, Halo and Seiun the Golden Generation?"

[Logic check: 45/45 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

It wasn't for their victories later on. That's not 'starting'.

"Because you guys demolished the competition at your tryouts?" You reply, the mugshots of those other G1 champions filling your head.

"Clever girl." Grass Wonder coos. She pulls back, her hands clasped behind her back in what should otherwise be a cheeky, mischievous fashion, yet only deepens the nerves bristling in your gut. "There's more to a race than raw strength and endurance. I intend to teach you that today."

You swallow and glance over Grass Wonder's shoulder to where Oguri lurks. She holds up one of the cleats, stands up, and then drops it from waist level. The cleat smashes to the ground, crushing the grass and cracking the earth. Satisfied, Oguri picks it back up.

She flashes you a quick thumbs up. Good luck. She mimes.

Your free hand instinctively scrabbles for the space above your silver bullet necklace beneath your tracksuit. That…might not cut it here.

[40 EXP gained in total.]

EXP: 60/100

[Grass Wonder's Speed, Stamina and Power has sharply decreased!]

[Oguri Cap's Speed, Stamina and Power has sharply decreased!]

>>All participants, please make way towards the starting line…

Name: Your first practice race

Location: Tracen Academy

Participants: Satono Ruby, Grass Wonder (handicapped; Late Surger), Oguri Cap (handicapped; Pace Chaser)

Length: Mile

Goal: Reach the end (1 lap).

edit: This vote will dictate your racing affinities. Choose wisely.

Edit: brief overview on the four styles:

Front Runner: Starts and ends the race trying to be the leader of the pack. Speed is king. Power is also used for final spurts. Pace Chaser: Stays towards the front of the pack, trying to keep up with the leader, requiring Stamina to do so and then Power to overtake. Late Surger: Starts at the back of the pack and then accelerates to the front at the final straight. Needs a lot of Power but can conserve somewhat on Stamina. Guts is also used to ensure the final burst of acceleration. End Closer: Starts at last place and then overtakes everyone at the end when they're tiring. Needs Speed, Stamina and Power. You can assume Guts, Wits, Psyche and Insight are applicable to all styles.

(How do you run? Select a dominant style at A-rank and a backup style at B-rank. Your Power will most likely increased by 1 after this race. Note: If the two options tie, the most popular Dominant option will be chosen alongside the second-most popular Backup option.)

[] [Dominant] I'll open fast and lead the pack from the start! (Front Runner)

[] [Dominant] I'll follow the lead runners and overtake them when ready! (Pace Chaser)

[] [Dominant] I'll hang at the back of the pack to conserve stamina, then at the end I'll smash through with a burst of power! (Late Surger)

[] [Dominant] I'll trail everyone for most of the race, then surge past when they're all tired and out of gas! (End Closer)

(Select a backup style.)

[] [Backup] Front Runner

[] [Backup] Pace Chaser

[] [Backup] Late Surger

[] [Backup] End Closer

(Pray before starting? This option will have no effect on your stats.)

[] Pray to the kami.

[] Pray to the silver bullet.

[] Pray to your mother's running shoes (currently not with you)

[] Do not pray.

[] Write-in.

1.3: Tutorial Race

>>[Dominant] I'll follow the lead runners and overtake them when ready! (Pace Chaser)

>>[Backup] Front Runner

>>Pray to the silver bullet.

Mood: Good

EXP: 60/100 (1 Level Up pending…)

"Pace chasing. I'll run as a pace chaser."

Oguri declares this to thin air, unprompted. Her ears wiggle. She snorts once. She slams her fist into the center of her palm with the fervor and smile of someone who has thought up the best idea in her entire life.

You raise one hand. "Are you sure you're meant to tell me that?" You ask.

Oguri turns her head, blinking those round, bluish-gray eyes. "What's the problem?"

The problem, you think from your kneeling position, tugging the string on a recently tied knot atop your borrowed running shoes, is that if the living legend less than a meter to your right announced her strategy to her opponents back in her day, and then won anyway, you might be in the mind for surrendering on the spot. It's already surreal enough that she's standing here and acting all casual and, dare you say it, friendly? Rudolf's watching from a few meters away, clipboard in one hand and a ballpoint pen in the other, so you tuck that intrusive thought away and say something sensible instead.

"Doesn't everyone keep their running style a secret before the start?" You continue.

Oguri blinks. She tilts her head. "We're practicing. You're going to run against all four styles one day, anyway. Pace chasing is a pretty common sight."

"Right," you reply, trying not to sound like you're arguing back, "But this is a mock..."

"Oh," Oguri says. She cracks her neck side to side, stretching it. "You're precise."

You let out an awkward giggle in response. "I think I kind of have to be?"

"You really are serious about this."

You're not sure if that's a compliment or an insult, coming from a former trailblazer with a poker face to put the Shinjuku pachinko dwellers to shame. It's the truth, either way. This field, with its wide open space and lack of any onlookers? It isn't actually empty. A reservation fills the gap, a form of hospitality. One lesson you learned early on as a coffin-dweller and a struggling up-and-coming underground idol is to never take hospitality for granted. Especially when it's made to benefit you.

This is despite the butterflies bouncing inside your stomach. Any longer, and caterpillars are going to start worming out of your ears.

Oguri thinks, then grins. "That's okay, because this is also part of the mock."

"It is?" You ask.

"Yup. No-one really trains alone in Tracen. There's always umas walking around, passing by, sharing training spaces and times here and in the gym and stuff. Word gets around that way."

You nod, following along. Makes sense. Tracen Academy is big. It's not privacy-for-two-thousands big. The only time you'll be alone, you assume, is if you train during the early morning hours a second past curfew.

"Plus, we bump shoulders with our rivals through classes, taking scrimmages, watching their races through the course or with records back at the dorm. There's a lot of good info to take in. By the time we reach the gates, we already have an idea of how they're running." Oguri explains.

"It's that accurate?" You say.

Oguri scratches the side of her head. "It's not always the full picture, but it's usually a general idea. Sometimes that's good enough. Training with rivals is also super helpful. You don't have fr—er, haven't been here long, so you probably won't have any real rivals yet. You also won't have Trainers and friends in the press either…" She pauses. "Wait, do you?"

"My umadol work?"

"Yeah. I don't usually watch those, so…"

Yes, you reply inside your head. If you count various online blogs and the creators of indie newsletters as 'press' and the nether-do-wells behind them as 'friends'.

"Is that a no?" Oguri asks.

You tilt your hand to the side, then drop it in a thumbs down. The frown accompanying it seals the deal.

"Darn." Oguri lifts her head to the sky and ponders. "What if I pretended to be the Trainer for a change?"

You try not to snort. The Ashen Beast herself as a Trainer? All the competition would withdraw, or so many spectators would show up it'd force the URA to build three new racecourses. The amount of money would be obscene.

"Nah. I'd make Kitahara jealous." Oguri concludes. "Let's pretend you drew a good fortune from the shrine and then wandered around and came upon me practising."

"Or," Grass Wonder's voice creeps up behind you, smooth as the silk of the kimono she once wore on a sports magazine cover. It leans down to tickle your ear. "It's a fake. A deception. Oguri Cap is intentionally planting the seed of an idea in your head, just so it can burst open with deadly nightshade when she switches to front-running when the race begins."

[Instinct check: 32/50 -> Failed.]

You almost snap your skin taut and silly in your haste to stand back up.

Grass Wonder stands adjacent to you, parallel to Oguri. Her blacksmithing is complete, the grey rim of the heavy cleats poking out from beneath her spotless running shoes. Lead, iron—whatever it is, it weighs heavier than an entire band kit, and she still sneaked up on you. A fact she seems to take amusement from, as she giggles softly.

"Sorry. Was I too close?"

"Maybe?" You squeak.

"I do apologise. I must have spent more time with Seiun than I thought." Grass Wonder says. "Well, it's just a little thing to think about."

The image of a red spider lily, its petals fresh and full in bloom, pops into your head.

"Grass. We shouldn't be mean." Oguri says, frowning.

Grass Wonder's smile widens. "In fact, that too could be part of the act—"

"Hey…"

"—and whether it's deception or not is something you'll have to judge by yourself."

Oguri folds her arms. She stares straight at Grass Wonder. "We're doing that layer of the information game already?"

Her tone comes out firmer than you thought she was capable of. The creased brow and look of mild disdain, more so. It halts the shivers down your back, if only to replace it with awareness. Your ears twitch in their direction.

"Yes, we are." Grass Wonder says, her voice going steady, the humor fading. "The earliest try-outs start in a couple of weeks."

"That short?" Oguri says. She glances across the turf quickly, then at Rudolf, who nods in what you assume is confirmation. "Sheesh. Time flies."

"Even with the last try-out, we only have until the end of next month. The faster Ruby can pick up on these things, the better. Her background, as I heard, was very busy with activities unrelated to running."

"Yeah." You interject, and while you're not sure where this conversation is going, you begin counting off your hand. "Lots of dancing, walking around the city with the ground, umadol stuff like handshaking, even tried being a v-umatuber once. Running was basically my other hobby."

Five for five. The sixth finger doesn't exist. It's not a state of affairs you're proud of. Money and board, however, proved to be more important.

"You've had it rough." Oguri states, looking at you. She bends one knee, flicking her foot up and down. Testing the weight of her cleats. Her frown is gone, replaced with a calm thoughtfulness.

"I appreciated you telling Ruby about the rumors and her rivals, and such." Grass Wonder adds.

"Thanks." Oguri Cap twists her shoulders, balancing one arm in a bend formed by the other. "Guess we'd better get started."

Grass Wonder, you notice, has not said a single thing about what style she's running in this discussion. You assume it's part of the bit. The cheeky wink she gives you only confirms it. What was it you said about her? That she was nice? Gentle? You think you might be taking that back now.

That said, Grass isn't being unreasonable. She reminded you of why Manager Suzuki and Kaede, the oldest and de facto leader of the group, used to hang out in afterparties or go bar-hopping on the weekends. It was simply for the chance of gaining an edge over your old rivals. Information is a tool sharper than any blade or sturdier than any shoe. You're not surprised to find how Tracen is the same. You figure you'd have been a lot more upset a few years ago; newbies don't enjoy learning that raw effort isn't enough to succeed in a highly competitive industry.

It's a good reminder, you think with pursed lips, because you think discussion might have a habit of drying up whenever you stroll around Tracen in the future.

"All participants! The race is about to begin. Proceed to the starting line!" Rudolf calls.

You give your shoelaces one final tug, smooth down the sides of your tracksuit trousers, and approach the cardboard cut-out of some tanned umamusume you've never met. Grass Wonder and Oguri follow. The ground thumps with the weight of their cleated shoes. Once again, you stop and listen in awe. They're so heavy as to create sound on soft grass. Yet, the two veteran umamusume work their legs as if nothing is out of the ordinary. Oguri slapped the cleats straight on and pranced about on the spot, pumping her legs up and down like some kaiju from an old B-movie. Her leg muscles must be as thick as steaks.

Then again, this means they've been restrained. Shackled. Brought down to your level, so maybe you'll be fine. Possibly?

You can hear Saya, chill and lazy Saya with pocky in her pocket, slapping you on the back and telling you to calm down. It's only a mock. Rehearsal under a different name. Save your energy for when the actual fighting starts.

Alright, you tell this imaginary Saya, fair point, except look around you. Recall what Manager Suzuki lectured you at your farewell dinner in the beef banquet parlor. He said you needed to find good friends to mingle with. Not just in terms of character or entertainment, but also with results. A G3 winner, if you were lucky. Now, take a gander back. A G1 champion, a retired legend with like a dozen more wins than her, and the Emperor herself! This is like being teleported into UKB48's training facility right as you're wrapping up the last encore at 3am in the morning!

[Artistry check: 52/30 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

And half the idols there were secretly fans of your tunes—

Shut up! You yell at this imaginary Saya. She cackles and poofs out of existence.

Are you being too hysterical? No. Not really. You've accepted this is reality. Narita Brian's words have successfully punched their hole in your psyche. You're just being self-aware of how surreal this whole day is.

"I've rolled the dice." Rudolf calls again, holding up her smartphone at the edge of the track. A red flag is clenched in her other hand. "Oguri: outer, Grass: inner, and Ruby in the center. Go."

Grass Wonder and Oguri exchange brief glances, then swap places. You're left standing still in the middle.

"Remember, Ruby: this is only a practice run." Grass Wonder says as she takes her place next to you. "It is not the real thing. If you ever feel an abnormal pinch in your body, or any sharp jolts of pain more intense than muscle strain, stop immediately so we can get it looked at in the infirmary. Do you understand me?"

You nod back. It's a common precaution. Grass Wonder, satisfied, directs her attention down the turf, a sharp focus entering her.

"Listen up, Ruby! A race does not start immediately after the runners enter the gates. Last-minute checks must be done, announcements are made, and participants are given a brief moment to gather their focus or raise any last-minute objections." Rudolf says. "We'll be simulating that too. You all have a minute!"

Longer than expected. Suitable for a rookie. You gaze forward.

Tracen's turf extends in front of you, kilometers upon kilometers of lush, evenly-cut grassy perfection, only blemished by distance posts and the rings of solid metallic rails. A warm spring sun beats down, strengthening the sweet scent of the grass below. You inhale it in, mouth and nose. The dry moisture tinges your wet tongue. You taste the drying moisture on a wet tongue.

It is nothing like Yoyogi Park, you think. The way is clear. Speed limits are a distant memory. No onlookers to point or squint, just the simple and immediate future of full steam ahead. You gulp. Your stomach clenches in a semi-comfortable fashion. A swell and a thrum pulses from the cavities of your physiology to your ears and tail, and they're unfurling, flicking back and forth, as if saying finally, finally, finally!

You've dreamed of this moment ever since you cradled your mother's old running shoes in your arms and learned where she forged them from.

Yet, there is also instinct. The ramrod stiffness of intimidation. The level of curation and optimization on display here is staggering. It's the perfect roundness of a gun barrel aimed at the bridge between your nose. The two veteran umamusume beside you are the bullets.

To your left, Oguri Cap shakes an invisible something off her shoes. She twists her neck, bushels of her long ashen hair pinwheeling and flaying in the gentle breeze. She drops into a stance, knees bent and body angled forward. Grass Wonder does the same, her chest barely rising and falling. You copy. Minute differences must exist in these postures, but you can't spot them, only imitate them and wish you had Hotaru's full-length mirror, hoping for the best.

There's no way in hell you can beat these two. That's logical.

It's not fun to lose. That's emotional.

Shove them together and you find yourself with the desire to not the waste the time of these senpais, who have skipped their own classes to give you a chance to taste the real deal. The student council president, too. You told Rudolf to her face you were willing to learn. You have to at least try for second.

It'll do. It'll do for now.

So, think. Think about the turf the same way Manager Suzuki and Kaede taught you about venue sizes, or the flow of the audience's psyche at night and midnight. Even go as far back as those fogeys at the shrine, who grumbled about weather and seasons. What do you have? What's the absence of that?

[Racing Tactics check: 52/50 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

You're in the middle post, for starters. That's a good start. You won't be boxed in against the rail, nor will you be forced to run the extra distance outside. You have the flexibility to switch between inwards or outwards, depending on the situation. There's no need to worry about being boxed in with only three participants.

As for your opponents—Oguri. She's not lying. You can tell when people are doing that. The girl's surprisingly transparent and honest for an umamusume with such an illustrious racing career. You choose to believe Oguri's she's running as a pace chaser. With such a shrunken participation capacity, alongside the fact heavyweight cleats are unlikely to slow her physique enough, it means she'll most likely be setting the pace today. Not as far as a front runner, but she will be ahead in the first couple of stretches.

You'll have to stick closely behind. A second pace chaser. It's almost ironic. But you think you can do it. Speed and precision are your forte. You measured your lap times in Yoyogi, and the flat-cap wearing old trainer back at the exam grounds confirmed the same. You'll just have to stick ahead of Grass Wonder.

That could be a problem.

You don't know that much about Grass Wonder, to be honest. Stupid trivia, maybe: rumors on the Umanet about how past opponents pissed themselves mid-race against her, the disparity of her glaring mugshot between King Halo and El Condor Pasa's confident smiles in a news article, the bewildered newscasting of her berating an exhausted Special Week at the end of the Takarazuka Kinen. There's little here about she actually ran. You cared about what she did, rather than how she did it.

[History check: 32/40 -> Failed.]

You feel a little guilty about that. You want to grab the sides of your head and shake, except there's no time for that. Think. Think! Grass Wonder…came up from fifth and accelerated past the competition to overtake Special Week. That's late surger material. It's too early to be end closer. But it could also be pace chasing. The best athletes don't stick rigidly to one style—they flow between them.

"All participants, get ready!" Rudolf shouts. She raises the red flag upright. It's starting. Oh God, it's starting. Fine! Whatever! If Grass Wonder's late surging, you'll just keep an eye on her and accelerate before she does. If she's pace chasing, you'll trail from behind and wait until she's tired. Training against those phantoms from the radio had to have done something!

You clutch the silver bullet around your neck and mouth a silent, abridged prayer with your lips. A mix of urban spiritualism and Shinto myth, dedicated to banishing evil spirits and bad luck, all wrapped in a package that is uniquely you. The full version is hidden somewhere in your dream diary.

The prayer works. A small degree of calm washes over you.

"On your marks, get set…"

You bend your knees and prepare to send force down into your heels and feet.

"Go!"

The flag comes down. Nonexistent gates burst open. You spring forth from the ground and run.

[Rolled a 91. An immediate start! Great job!]

[Speed check: 9/8 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

Blood rushes to your cheeks. Wind whips your face. You lean against it, arms swinging and legs pumping. Tracen Academy disappears into a blur as you charge down the turf, with the sight of an incoming corner careening ahead.

Immediately, you encounter a problem.

It's not your stride, nor your form. Those are acceptable enough. It's not the fact that strands of your fringe cling to your scalp as your neck tries to steady your bobbing head. It's Oguri and Grass Wonder. They exist.

This whole racing deal? It's not done with phantoms. It's done with actual umamusume, with pumping legs, fleshy physiques and swinging arms bearing pure momentum. Their elbows are jackhammers. The moment one hits your face, you're flying backwards, disqualified at best and concussed in the head at worst.

A spark of instinctual fear seizes your brain.

[(Composure check: 52/45) || (Guts check: 8/8) -> Success! +10 EXP.]

You tell it to piss off. It's fine. It's just nerves. Back on the stage, you were careful not to hit Kaede or the rest with your moves. The turf's the same, only faster. You're in a place where rehearsal must be put into practice, an underground beneath the clear blue sky, so accept it, and move!

[Acceleration check: 28/25 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

You shift slightly to the left, and find a place to avoid Oguri's swinging arms.

[Dodge check: 54/40 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

The first corner rounds ahead. You take it, putting a burst of power into your stride, and round it with no issue. You drop back into the middle lane, then check around you. Oguri's to your right, her ashen ponytail streaming like a balloon attached to a speeding train, her footsteps thumping loudly against the turf. The same is heard behind you—Grass Wonder.

Her eyes burn a hole in your back. A tingle at the back of your neck, like a crawling cicada dropping out of nowhere, threatening to disrupt you—

[Frenzy check: 52/50 -> Success! The enemy's Frenzy was nullified. +10 EXP.]

—but you endure it. It's the same sensation as being monitored on stage. You've still got this.

(Not bad, Ruby.)

(Grass did it before I could, eh…)

You run down the second straight. The lineup is as you predicted. Oguri sets the pace with her long strides, a length or so ahead of you. You're following. Grass Wonder tails you both from behind. Their footsteps ring audibly across the rushing air—the cleats doing their job. The situation's at equilibrium, with no-one slipping or falling behind.

It's too early to make a move. Steady, steady.

[Breathing check: 42/35 -> Check success. +10 EXP.]

The second corner whips around. The same story. In comes the third straight. The posts whip by. Burning creeps up into your lungs.

[Pain Threshold check: 32/40 -> Failure.]

And you wince. It's affecting you, slowing you down. Luckily, your legs have carried you past enough. The next corner's coming up. This…is a good enough spot, you scramble to think. This is where you can unleash your trump card, assuming a rookie like you has the audacity to call it that!

The ground swerves beneath your feed. Oguri accelerates, skirting to the outside to round the track with ease. You follow, except you keep to your lane.

Gravity drags you to the right. You lean your weight towards the center of the track. Down goes your foot.

Strain immediately shoots up your right leg. Your core of balance begins to slip like a ball rolling off a seesaw. It doesn't matter. You are a scioness of the Shibuya underground. An indie darling who danced, twirled and leaped across crowded stages blaring with ballad and rock, all for the sake of sleeping under a roof every night. There's so much open space here!

[(Acceleration check: 28/50 && Power check: 8/10) || (Dancing check: 72/70) -> Success! +10 EXP.]

The swinging sensation drapes your back. You kick off with your right foot, pump the rest of your body upwards and explode forth.

(What. She used the centrifugal force?)

(My my, I was right about your flexibility, Ruby. If you keep that up—)

You tear across the homestretch, the wind whipping at your face faster than ever. One second passes. Two seconds. There's fire in your lungs, stinging smoke flowing through your legs, but in the distance: the cardboard cut-out of the dark-skinned umamusume. The finish line's in sight.

For a fleeting moment, your heart soars, and you dare to believe you might win against these champions.

(Playtime's over.)

A thud. A heavy stomp mid-run. The image of the grass tearing, the ground fragmenting amidst shortwaves—and a blur of white and grey slams past you, its dark-blue eye tearing a deadly trail in mid-air.

Behind you, a second presence bursts free, just as deadly.

(I told you, Ruby—we wouldn't be going easy on you.)

It all goes downhill from there. Oguri overtakes you. Grass Wonder is less than a second behind, popping in from behind. The space you conserved on your turn—she must have repurposed it. The sharpness of the turn hadn't affected her at all. She surges forward, and the two champions are now battling for dominance as grass and dirt fly back from their powerful stomps.

Your advantage has been crushed in less than a second. Your heart falters.

[Guts check: 8/10 -> Failure.]

You're lagging behind, trying to force your legs to run faster, accelerate more, but it's futile.

[Acceleration check: 28/65 -> Failure.]

[Power check: 8/10 -> Failure.]

Your breathing comes out ragged and frantic.

[Breathing check: 42/65 -> Failure.]

The stitch in your side is threatening to burst out.

[Pain Threshold check: 32/65 -> Failure.]

You don't have enough speed to outpace Oguri.

[Speed check: 9/11 -> Failure.]

And only a few drops trickle out of your internal tanks.

[Stamina check: 8/10 -> Failure.]

Your momentum slows, and you can only struggle on against Oguri and Grass Wonder's retreating forms as they blaze towards the finish line.

(Do step aside.)

(No. You step aside!)

You end up at third place…

[Visual Mathematics check: 32/50 -> Failure.]

…at God knows how many lengths behind.

"The race has ended! Grass Wonder and Oguri Cap have tied!" Rudolf yells.

"What?"

"Excuse me?"

"That was not a tie."

"President, I would like to raise an objection—"

"I was not recording! There will be no photo finishes, because otherwise we'd be here all day!" Rudolf shouts back.

"Fiiiine…" Oguri groans.

You stagger past the finish line and feel yourself topple. By force of will, you manage to plant your hands on your knees and keep yourself steady. Your lungs are a different matter. You gulp down deep breaths, sweat rolling down your hot, hot cheeks. The tracksuit feels like an inferno.

A rustle. Movement. Grass Wonder stands over you, a water bottle in her hands. Your mouth waters at the sight. She hands it over. You barely restrain yourself from gulping the first mouthful, taking slow sips as you were taught.

"How do you feel?" Grass Wonder asks. She's barely out of breath, you notice.

You take a second gulp, and your brain starts working again.

Look at you.

Your heart is hammering. Your back is slick with sweat. Adrenaline's wearing off, and the pain's about to set in soon. You will wake up tomorrow feeling aches like never before. This first race you dreamed of so much has ended in your complete and utter loss.

There will be thoughts later. Opinions. Yet, coming off this high, staring into the face of a senpai and a champion, you can only speak from the instincts stirring deep within your soul, sated yet salivating for more.

"Can we go again?" You ask.

Of course, you don't go again. A mile has already tired out well enough. Any more and you'd overexert yourself and wind up with muscle damage. Grass Wonder takes you on a cooldown walk, picking apart your technique with a calm, elegant finesse. First up are your good points. You have good form and speed for an amateur. You put thought before the race and enacted a plan. Your footwork—Grass Wonder sounds legitimately impressed at this—is the kind of secret trick all good Tracen runners employ throughout their careers.

She then makes you recite what you thought before the race. Another ten good-girl points for you.

But, she raises a finger before you can puff out your chest or whatnot, you possess a smorgasboard of faults. Your stamina, for example, is something to be desired. No amount of tactics will work if the body itself cannot enact them. She also has criticism of how you're controlling your acceleration. It's inefficient, to put it shortly. Your musculature isn't defined enough—a fact Oguri points out by squeezing your thighs, after receiving permission.

You will need to invest in your body. Eat more protein. Don't skip out on calories. Oguri pales with horror when you mention you couldn't afford even instant ramen and went to practice with a rumbling stomach. Grass Wonder says you are under no circumstances allowed to skip meals anymore, then rattles off some morning and afternoon exercises and makes you promise to take them. She will check.

You nod, still partially in awe of how fast the two of them were, even with the restrictions placed upon them. If they sprinted at their full power, you'd have choked from the kicked-up dust. Terrifying.

The last exercise of the session is a light jog around the same turf.

"Geez, if all the girls at tryouts are that strong…" You half-ask, half-pant as you round the corner where you tried to pull off your centrifugal trick.

"They're not." Oguri interjects.

Grass Wonder shoots Oguri a grimace. Oguri either doesn't notice or pretends not to. You look between them and are left feeling confused.

"Wait, they're not as fast as today? I thought neither of you were going easy on me."

"We weren't." Grass Wonder says.

"Same here." Oguri says.

"This was a mock race."

"So…" You start.

"We were mimicking how the level I was at back at my tryouts. The best of the rookies that year. That's the standard we agreed on beforehand, remember?" Grass Wonder says. It's no boast, only facts. "The president and I want you to do well."

Oguri raises her hand. "Me too."

"The president, Oguri Cap and I all want you to." Grass Wonder corrects. "We want you to get scouted."

She stresses that 'want', an inflection just strong enough for you to take notice. Is there a reason behind it, these two or three veteran umamusume working together to support you? It's a boon you'd expect given to a star prodigy, like Mejiro McQueen, instead of an umaidol who barely clawed her way past the entrance exams. You shoot a quick glance at Grass Wonder. She looks back. You look away, an almost anxious response. You...

[Subterfuge check: 45/50 -> Failure.]

...decide to not spend more energy wondering about it. All that sprinting has thrown your brain for a loop. There's a straightforward explanation, anyway. A G1 champion tutors her new student to a high standard. The student council president provides assistance to those lagging behind. Sometimes, random new people appear out of nowhere. These are normal happenstances.

Taken together, it's almost an alternative path to being coached by a Trainer. Thankfully, Grass Wonder seems reasonable enough to explain new concepts well and not push you until past your breaking point.

You rather not think ill of her, not when she's been so helpful today.

"But isn't that going to happen, anyway?" You ask, as the homestretch approaches. "Don't all students get a Trainer?"

"No." Oguri says, bluntly again. "They don't."

That's a surprise to you. It must show on your face again.

"There simply aren't enough trainers to go around." Grass Wonder adds. "Not everyone can be like Hana, or Team Spica's trainer. One is usually enough for most of them."

You shrug. You're an adolescent girl, and even you'd admit your kind isn't exactly smooth sailing to handle. Manager Suzuki got enough headaches managing you and the rest of the idols, and half of the group worked part time.

"There's real competition." Oguri says.

"I was scouted early by Hana. Oguri here…"

"I had Kitahara right off the bat. Then, when I came to Tracen, I had his uncle Roppei." Oguri continues. "We were both lucky."

"It pains me somewhat to say it, but the competition this year seems fiercer than the last. I've heard rumors a few select individuals have already been scouted by trainers and are merely using the tryouts as a combination of formality and practice." Grass Wonder says, gazing across the turf to Tracen's main building. "It'll be an event, alright."

The blurred-out face of a certain Satono heiress pops into your head. You shudder. All levity is gone in an instant. The praise you received from Grass Wonder earlier doesn't feel as fulfilling.

[Mood has gone down to Normal.]

Your mood remains grounded as you finish the job, do some more stretches, and get changed back into your new school uniform. Grass Wonder watches you enter your new exercises in your personal calender and save it.

Thus, the first of your mentorship sessions ends.

You're about to lean onto the outside railing for a breather, when Grass Wonder comes over.

"Ruby."

"Yes?"

The older umamusume hesitates, as if debating whether to talk at all, before clearing her throat and speaking. "Please don't fret so much."

"Pardon?"

"Ha. That sounds odd coming from me, doesn't it? I'm serious." Grass Wonder says. "Tryouts won't start for a month and they happen every week after the starting date. They're also not exclusive to the start of the year. The start is where most of the new students arrive. We do have time for you to improve."

You nod. It's a relief to hear.

"President Rudolf told me what Narita Brian said to you."

Your eyes widen slightly. "That's…"

"I agree with her." Grass Wonder says. She doesn't elaborate further.

That's…a good thing, you suppose? Narita Brian was trying to compliment you in a roundabout way. The part about you being pathetic—that can be left out. Please.

"If you keep up the same effort you showed today, you'll be ready in no time."

You blink, propping yourself off the railing. "Does that mean I did an okay job, then?"

"I wouldn't be talking to you like this, if you hadn't. Oh, and…" Grass Wonder extends her slender hand. This time, she initiates, grasping your hand and shaking it firmly. "Congratulations on running your first race. You did well."

A professional veteran is acknowledging you. A G1 champion is acknowledging you. You shake Grass's hand up and down as your tail wags like the happiest dog on the planet.

"I'll do a good job. I'll work hard, I promise!" A faint wetness seeps into the corner of your eyes."

Grass Wonder giggles. She lets go of your hand. "I still won't go easy on you."

"That's okay. That's one hundred percent okay." Your exclaim, your ears wiggling in joy. You break out into a massive smile and pump your fists. "Give me everything you got, teach!"

"I'm counting on you, Ruby."

More than the exhilaration of the first race, more than the sheer scale of opportunity placed upon you, it is the knowledge that you have not let your new mentor down that fills you with hope.

[Power has increased by 1.]

[Acceleration has increased by 8.]

[Unlocked Grass Wonder's Social Link! She will now appear in encounters.]

[Mood has gone back up to Good.]

[Grass Wonder's Speed, Stamina and Power has returned to normal.]

[Oguri Cap's Speed, Stamina and Power has returned to normal.]

Hang on. Isn't there someone you're forgetting? She certainly hasn't.

"Oguri."

The ashen-haired umamusume stamps her feet on the ground. "The cleats are off. We can run freely now."

Rudolf doesn't budge an inch. One palm is on her forehead. "You have classes. Both of you."

Oguri obstinately points at Grass Wonder's retreating form in the distance. "Grass won a G1. She's right there, Rudolf. Five minutes. It'll only take five minutes."

"Oguri, please."

"It'll be a learning experience for Ruby here!"

You're standing off to the side, wondering if you should whip out your phone. The Ashen Beast is acting like a petulant bunny. Kaede is never going to believe this.

Rudolf sighs. She massages her temples and lapses into silence. You and Oguri wait. Just as you are about to ask something, Rudolf suddenly breaks into a smile so bright and sunny it could melt butter; she strides forward, leans forward and lays a solid hand on Oguri's shoulder.

Oguri's ears perk up. She gazes back at her long-time friend. "Rudolf."

"Oguri." Rudolf's voice comes out in a breathy whisper. "I heard…"

"Yes?" Oguri leans forward, smiling in turn. Sparkles fill the air between them.

"I heard Mr. Kitahara is running a swimming lesson with your name on it."

Somehow, you hear a faint cracking sound. Oguri shuffles back, her hands held up and her face pale again. "I'll be good." She whines.

Rudolf sweeps her arm out like a waiter. "Off you go, then."

The Ashen Beast of Kamamatsu slumps and trudges away, but not before you giving you a second thumbs-up. You give a friendly wave in response.

It's just you and Rudolf now. The student council president surveys the deep footprints left in the turf, shakes her head in what you assume is a bemused fashion, then turns to you.

"How was it?" Rudolf asks. "This mentorship session."

"It was good." You reply. "I think I can learn a lot from Grass. She's a good teacher so far."

"I'll consider this first session a success, then which means that'll be the end of my involvement. Grass will be handling things here from hereon out."

"Thank you for your time, President Rudolf."

Rudolf chuckles. "Only doing what I was elected for. Oh, but I would appreciate it if you wrote a report about your experiences by the end of next month. Something about the ups and downs, flaws or benefits in terms of content, scheduling, teaching styles and the like. This is still a trial process, after all."

She look at the staircase of the turf towards the bleachers. "Shall I walk you back?"

"No, no, it's fine. You've done enough for me." You don't want the president get dragged down in whatever rumors are circulating about you, even if she could handle them by herself.

"Very well. I'll see you, Ruby. If you need anything, my office is always open." Rudolf gives you a wave and turns around to head off. You wave back.

You then think of a question when she's about to take her first step up the staircase and feel like an idiot.

"Wait!" You cry out.

Rudolf turns around. "Yes?"

"Sorry for asking, but…" You gulp. "Do I have a senpai here?"

Rudolf's brows furrow. "A senpai. You mean like Grass or Oguri?"

"No, not like that. Was there anyone waiting for me at Tracen before I arrived?"

Rudolf now looks even more befuddled. She walks back over to you. "Ruby, you're not talking about Satono Crown?"

You blanch at the name and wave your hands around, shaking your head furiously. Bad memories. Bad memories lie down that path.

"No. Absolutely not!"

"I'm afraid I'm at a loss then." Rudolf says, concerned. "Are you talking about one of the staff?"

You blush, continuing to shake your head. "I must be tired. Or thinking of someone else back in the big city. One of the other. Sorry for bothering you."

[Persuasion check: 72/35 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

Rudolf frowns. She doesn't press it, and leaves after you bow your head again. You scurry up to the nearby changing rooms and drown your embarrassment in lukewarm shower water.

Next, you head over to Ms. Tazuna to sort out your lessons. Green is your first impression. Weird is the second. The woman is the friendly, albeit slightly overworked sort, who flies through her laptop files and archives to write you up a plan. The speed at which she types is frankly unnerving. It's also…

[(Insight check: 9/15) || (Inspection check: 34/140) -> Failure.]

…nah, it's nothing. At least she's helpful. The childcare system could use a dozen adults with her enthusiasm. The amount of maths and the literature homework you've been assigned though…you seriously do not want to think about the last time you attended an actual school. And this all has to be done alongside your intense catchup training with Grass Wonder. Great. Wonderful. These next few mornings are going to suuuuuck.

At least there's nothing left for you to do today, besides settle into your new dorm room. Before that: lunch-time.

Dread sinks to the pit of your stomach.

It's not the food. You're not the picky type, couldn't be with such a small budget, and Tracen hires the type of line cooks who can stand for days on end, serving up platters upon platters of meat and rice to starving umamusume. No, the issue lies in the cafeteria itself. It's full of other students, who have no doubt heard about your mother's reputation; whose rumor mill has churned endlessly; and whose enmity towards you cannot be expressed in words, because you'd be expelled for violating some kind of obscenity law.

You're standing in front of the cafeteria doors right now. They're orange. They're wide. They're making you gulp again and again as your mind wrestles with what to do.

The air seems to shimmer, twisting itself into tendrils and encroaching rotting hands that grip and grasp. A migraine blooms in your forehead.

You…

You don't know what people will say. What they might to do you while you wait in line. If the other Satonos are there, or their friends, they—they'll…

No. Please no.

But, part of you reminds yourself. You told Grass Wonder you would build muscle and grow stronger. You told President Rudolf you'd do your best. Narita Brian said you were a Tracen student.

You open Umastagram and check the latest feed. Maybe it won't be bad as you thought?
