1.4: Lunchtime

>>Calmly. You are a Tracen student. You deserve to be in there.

>>You want a rematch.

Mood: Good

EXP: 40/100 (2 LEVEL UPs pending...)

You clap yourself on the cheeks and find you don't care if anyone notices.

No, you tell yourself as the sting on your cheeks fades. You're not doing this again. Once was a mistake, twice meant you needed reinforcement, thrice means enough with this wishy-washiness! This is lunch you're talking about. Lunch. What's the alternative: you scrounging by on vending machine junk like a sewer rat, eternally seething in envy as you watch your classmates fill themselves with meat and bread and all the good treats needed to build themselves at athletes in this very prestigious racing academy?

For goodness's sake.

It's a school cafeteria, not a prison camp, and it belongs to you just as much as Narita Brian, Grass Wonder, Oguri Cap or any other of the thousands of students who call Tracen their home.

You'll deal with Diamond or Crown if your paths ever cross. It'll be awkward, tiresome and involve a lot of screaming near the end, but at least it'll be done on a full stomach. End of story.

[Alignment did not change.]

You take a deep breath and stride forward. No need to grasp your silver bullet this time. You push open the double doors, and the cafeteria entrance unfolds for you.

The first impression that strikes you is hotel. Not the dingy, dimly-lit hallways of coffin motels, nor the two-room eateries in three-star hotels Manager Suzuki rented out whenever the group was fortunate enough to travel to Tokyo's outer ring. No. this is a proper banquet hall. The room's proud about it. It sucks you in as you enter, its walls high, bright sunlight streaming in from tall windows with round tops and thin, tasteful metallic frames. Your heels click on a polished parquet floor as you advance between rings of round tables, four to five plush-seated chairs to each. A small incline, and to your left: atop a raised platform, a large circular area, showered in homely yet bright lighting provided by wall sconces atop supporting brick pillars.

You imagine the space a hundred years ago: the grand dining room of some manor long ago, its windows draped in velvet curtains and a glass chandelier swinging from the ceiling. Modernity has replaced antiquity. A TV nearby you warbles out the morning weather, and posters on the brick pillars advertise scrimmage times alongside running shoe brands. Most prominent of all are the students. You arrived early due to not attending lessons, yet this dining room is already swimming with umamusume. A sea of purple-white uniforms and ears of multiple shapes and sizes.

You step around fellow students, keeping a brisk pace. Neither Diamond or Crown are present, thank goodness. The scent of fried meat and fresh rice wafts and sets off an earthquake in your stomach. A table full of serving trays approaches. You grab one along with a set of wooden chopsticks and a spoon. Into the queue you go.

So far, so good. Then, it's not as good. The queue is at the front of the room, where traffic naturally flows towards. Heads turn, and somebody finally notices.

[Insight check: 9/6 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

"Is that her?"

"Who?"

"Look! Up the front, last in the queue. Long dark hair and the fake crown on the left. That's a dead-ringer from the Umatter pics. It's Satono Opal's kid."

"Holy crap, you're right. No way—she actually exists?"

It was nice while it lasted, you muse, as you reach out a hand to snag a nearby menu off a holder attached to a pillar.

One chatterbox opens another. More whispers sound off behind your back. The queue inches forward, one slow umamusume at a time.

"I thought she was a myth. Like a ghost story, or a black cat in America."

"What is she doing here? Doesn't she know her mom's a filthy cheater?

"Duh. Of course, she knows. She doesn't care. Thinks what happened didn't matter."

"That bitch…"

You hear that last one. It's close by, behind you at a table length and a half. The word grazes you. That's all it does.

[Composure check: 52/40 -> Success! +10 EXP]

Don't look. Don't acknowledge. Not even a single cock of your ear, you demand your instincts. Remember Shibuya, Shinjuku. Contrast the past with the present. No-one here is allowed to grab your wrist, or blackmail you with old pics from the shrine, or heckle you with the usual jeers.

"I thought Tracen told her to go away. Was that just rumors?"

"No way. Rudolf's got a reputation to uphold. Bet she's just as pissed as the Satonos are. There was an entire press conference and everything."

"Damn it, was hoping to catch a glimpse of Crown today. She's so cool…"

"Can she even run with legs like sticks?"

They're not even allowed to invade your personal space without permission. Compared to the streets, Tracen is practically a paradise.

You busy yourself by perusing the nearby menu. It's laminated, printed in neat rows and columns. Pictures accompany some items. Nutrition data is included. The more you read, the more you regret it, because you think your stomach is now busy devouring its stomach lining in an attempt to stay alive. Rice bowls, meat platters, near-unlimited supplies of miso soup, even foreign foods like toast and porridge…the amount of food available is utterly staggering. You've had hunger dreams that weren't this comprehensive.

In fact, when the line does progress, and the aged lunchlady dumps your choice onto your tray without giving you a second glance, it takes actual volition not to stick your finger into the steaming hot rice and scoop up a mouthful on the spot.

"Excuse me?"

"Yeah?" The lunchlady drawls back. Grey-haired, a bun in her hair on the back, and a white uniform marked with oil stains and stray crumbs. Her skin, wrinkled as it is, is almost spotless.

You gesture to the plate of chicken. "I think you might have given me too much."

The lunchlady leans over, frowning. She eyeballs the stack of chicken slices, then at you. She guffaws.

"Girl, I know shrunken cheeks when I see 'em." The lunchwoman cackles, and your cheeks turn pink at the assertion. "You'll burn this all off when you start running. Now git!"

You find yourself ushered away by the lunchwoman's confidence alone. Strangely, you feel a little fuzzy inside.

There's more food than the last two meals combined on your plate. Time to find a place to sit. Pick a table, any table. Grass Wonder is absent. You hoped she'd be here, but she does have lessons and you did arrive early; and you doubt the Rudolf eats here when she's swamped with work all the time. You don't want to sit with someone you don't know, nor do you want to find an empty seat in the middle. Too many prying eyes. Too many chances to be asked about your mother. You are not in the mood for an interview.

You look towards the outer rim.

Not that table; the lighting's off. The floorboards are giving me funny looks over there, not really much of a sun…ah, that one. I like the fern there.

[World Resonance check: 47/45 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

It's like the slender green leaves are waving at you. Patting an invisible seat. Air wavering akin to a heat haze, except in a friendly manner. There's a clear path there, too.

Smiling, you prepare to head over, when three bodies suddenly block your path.

"Hi there!"

"Hello." You say cautiously.

"You're the girl who sang on the PA system for fifteen seconds, right? Satono Ruby."

A trio of umamusume. The tall one has pierced her ear with silver; the other two have a blue ribbon and a bow-tie, respectively. Their faces are the stuff of movie extras in an out-of-focus shot.

Your grip slightly tightens on your tray. You realise there is no way to quickly discard it without throwing it aside, thereby breaking the first rule of the cafeteria displayed on the rules outside: FOOD WASTERS WILL BE STRICTLY PUNISHED.

"You know about me?" You ask.

"'Course. How can we not after that stunt? The whole school's been talking about you." Pierced-Ear says.

"That song was…" Blue-Ribbon struggles with the right word. "…so cool!"

"Sit down with us," Bow-Tie chimes in. "Tell us what being an umadol is really like!"

"You guys have names?" You ask.

Pierced-Ear grins, revealing teeth with thin braces. "We'll do that after we sit down. Don't want to keep you hanging."

It's a nice gesture, except it's rude not to introduce yourself when you have already called out someone else's name. It's also the most transparent attempt to pull the rug from under you. The leader's got an okay front, but her smirk is oil, and her two lackeys are trying and failing to hide their snickering behind their leader's back. They could at least hide their faces from you.

You side-eye the surrounding tables. Other students are watching. Sneaking glances while half-buried in their food. Some have their smartphones out. You have an audience, but not necessarily any allies.

This is your debut, you realise. A litmus test to determine whether you're a pushover or not. You don't exactly a history of passing those. Seven-year-old you would have shivered and hid inside the bathrooms. Thirteen-year-old you had Kaede or Manager Suzuki to hide behind. If these three were the first girls you met at Tracen today, you'd be flustered, spluttering, maybe apologizing.

Today, you were yelled at by a Triple-Crown winner, fed sandwiches by the Emperor, and raced with a G1 victor and the Ashen Beast herself. You heart beats with the fervor to rematch Grass Wonder and Oguri Cap, handicapped or not. You extended a hand to giants and they shook your finger back. This all happened in a few hours.

These three, to put it lightly, aren't much at all.

Feel that? The solid sensation propping up your chest? It's what the biz calls confidence. You know what to do.

"May I?"

"Sure. C'mon here."

Pierced-Ears beckons you to follow. Gets half-way turning around. You are nowhere near her. You quickly deposit your tray on a nearby table and snatch up a napkin. You whip out the convenient pen respectable umadols all carry, unhook the cap with a pop, move your hands and Voila! A sketch of your mugshot with wide, mad eyes and half-obscured by a long kimono sleeve. You top it off with your signature in quick-style calligraphy, then surround it with miniature suns, gohei strips and shrine bells.

Satono Ruby ~ Tomorrow is FAITHFUL. Thank you for being my fan!

[Artistry check: 52/35 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

There should be a time listing the approximate date of the group's next performance. Obviously, you don't know what that is. It's good work, if you say so yourself.

You present it to Pierced-Ear. She grips the autograph like a discarded, soggy tissue.

"What." She states.

"I'm sorry. I haven't eaten much since breakfast—" Technically not a lie; Rudolf's sandwiches were more quality over quantity, and you're intentionally stretching the definition of quantity here. "So the interview will have to wait. Take this as a token of my apology."

"The hell are you giving me this for?" Pierced-Ear barks.

"It's an autograph."

"I know that. I didn't ask for it!"

You tilt your head and twist your mouth into the shape of a small pout. "But you said my music was good. Are you actually not a fan of mine? All my other fans squeal with joy when I write them my autograph…"

Blue-Ribbon speaks up. "Hey, you can't just—"

"Shut up!" Pierced-Ear interrupts her. Her face is turning redder. Tomato-esque, even. She jabs a finger in your direction. "You think you're so smart, don't you?"

"Not really." You reply. "I think of myself as perfectly average. An average umamusume with an average rumbling stomach. I do take pride in my drawing skills."

"What, your mom teach you those?"

"Is that a rhetorical question? Do you know something I don't? That's a common pattern—random people saying stuff about my mother that I've zero clue about. Most of the time, they don't stick around to explain whenever I pester them with more questions. It's so weird!"

You snap your head in the direction of Bow-Tie, still wearing your practiced, placid, welcoming umadol-smile. "Do you know something about my missing mom, miss?"

"No!" Bow-Tie exclaims. She stills as she realises her mistake.

[Psyche check: 9/7 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

The best way to deal with hecklers, you've found, is to play their games in a way they don't expect. Swivel the board to your advantage. They're so focused on eliciting a reaction they can't handle it when the same's sprung upon them, much like the leader of these would-be bullies here. They were unprepared for you pushing back.

You think Kaede and the other girls would be proud.

"You!"

Pierced-Ear raises her arm. You bend your knees slightly, anticipating the dodge from your own instincts. To the right, near the posters. The aggressor will track your movements, but not completely, and thus won't hit your food. She'll break the taboo. Not you.

Before blows start flying, someone else interrupts. A loud and pointed clearing of the throat. Another umamusume stands behind them, hands on her hips. You can't help but compare this new girl to Grass Wonder. Where Grass Wonder was elegant and slender, this new girl is top-heavy and sturdy, with long orange-red twintails and fluffy blue hair ties.

"Would you three be so kind to put a raincheck on whatever it is you're doing?" The twin-tailed umamusume demands, glowering at the would-be bullies. "You're blocking the way out."

She points towards the queue, where several students holding their own stacked trays are glaring at the trio, and not you, with annoyance. The lunchlady looks none too pleased, either.

"Well?" The new umamusume demands. "Step aside, please."

"Hey." Pierced-Ear says. "Who do you think you are?"

"Who do you think you are?" Miss Twintails snaps back. "And don't bother answering. I know for a fact that I've never seen you at any of my G2s or G3s, never mind a G1, so clearly you're not so special as to put the rest of the cafeteria on hold!"

Pierced-Ear freezes up. Miss Twintails means business, if she can join a G3. She's smarter, tougher, and most of all: stronger.

"That's…"

You notice Blue Ribbon glancing up at Miss Twintails's head. She pales. She tugs on her friend's sleeve, whispering into an ear. "We gotta go."

"Why?"

"She's one of the Spica girls, you dolt. Those guys are insane; haven't you heard the rumors? The grey-coated one—Gold something—kidnapped a Mejiro in a sack and brainwashed her into joining their team! A Mejiro!" Blue-Ribbon shakes her head frantically. Bow-Tie shrinks back, trembling. "I didn't come here to tangle with psychos!"

"I can hear you, you know." Miss Twintails growls. She takes a step forward.

That's the final straw. Your would-be bullies retreat back a step, then turn tail to scamper off, completely forgetting about you in the chaos. Miss Twintails watches them go with a sigh and a roll of her round eyes.

"Honestly…"

"Thank you." You say.

Miss Twintails stiffens upon hearing you speak. She turns around, hands still on hips, and examines you. Something soft that might have been pity or sympathy flickers across her haughty attitude.

"No worries." She says. "If those three come back, just tell Air Groove. She'll sort them out quickly."

"I will. Thanks for the advice."

She gives you a stiff nod. "Enjoy your lunch."

She brushes past you and goes to meet her supposed friends. You give her a slight bow in her direction. That was a nice girl, you muse. Pretty-looking and well-groomed too. The tiara perched on her head is a bit odd. It's pristine and polished, and there are enough fashion trends to create an entire ocean of styles. You dressed in kimonos and hopped around on stage screaming your lungs out. No reason to judge.

A G2 and G3 participant too, from the sounds of it. You'll have to keep an eye out for her in the future.

"Eh...she kept her cool. Thought she would fold."

"Did that girl save her? Nah. Just a coincidence."

"Looks like the black sheep has a bit of a spine, after all."

"Hey, that table she's going to. Isn't that...?"

No-one bothers you after that. You grab your tray and finally take a seat at your chosen table. You still can't believe what in front of you is actually yours. An entire bowl of fluffy white rice, a plate stacked high with fried chicken strips, fresh miso soup with tofu chunks, multiple whole steamed carrots and a square of cheese to top it off. It's almost too precious to touch. You snap a photo for once your Umastragram account gets unlocked, grab your chopsticks and dig in.

Juice seeps from the chicken. Not a single hint of plastic-tasting preservatives in the carrots. The meal's good. It's so good. Tears are gathering in your eyes. To hell with fast food joints and konbini snacks. You're never eating outside this cafeteria ever again.

A heavy slam on the table. You jerk up, annoyed. It transforms into pure bewilderment as what appears to be a mountain of fried rice wafts steam in front of you. It doesn't end there. A pair of hands then drops a half a dozen slabs of salmon stacked atop each other next to it. An entire box of fresh croquettes and sushi rolls. Three whole two-litre bottles of carrot juice. Your immediate front is smothered in protein and carbs.

"You again." Oguri Cap, peeking over the avalanche.

"Hi…?" You say. You swallow. "You're going to eat all that?"

"Welcome to nationals." Oguri grins. "You'll never have to eat instant ramen again."

She plonks herself down and begins shovelling the fried rice at a rate that should break the muscles holding up her stomach.

[Oguri Cap's Eating check: 180/150 -> Success!]

It doesn't.

You feel like you should be disgusted. A small part of you is. But wait—Oguri Cap won most of her races. She's a notorious glutton, but she never grew permanently fat. Her nutritional needs were fulfilled somehow. Is it possible to scale her meal sizes down to fit your needs?

You spend the rest of the meal half-observing the Eater of (U)billions in front of you.

[Nutrition has increased by 7.]

"Sorry! Did I keep you waiting?"

"Nah, Prez let me know you'd show up around this time. C'mon. Let's get your room sorted out."

The cardboard cut-out of the tanned umamusume at the racetrack has a name, and it's Hishi Amazon, head of one of Tracen's two student dorms. She unlocks a door behind the front reception and disappears inside. She emerges bearing your luggage, which consists of a single duffel bag containing your meager belongings and a small steel-lined and combination-locked case.

That last one is particularly important. You are so relieved it wasn't stolen.

You offer to help her carry. She politely rejects it and leads you up the stairs to your new room. She tells you the rules along the way. Dorm managers have full authority over the management and well-being of the dorm. Curfew at eight, lights-out at nine. Permission to go out overnight must be granted by the dorm heads. Failure to obey the rules results in punishments such as cleaning duty or the loss of access to the recreation room.

"No Trainers allowed, either. They need permission from the faculty or us to enter."

"Why?"

"Long story." Hishi Amazon says. "There were a couple of incidents in the past…people got injured and expelled. You'll have to ask the Prez or the Chairwoman for the full story. Just assume the dorms are umas-only unless we say so."

You reach your room after a few stair climbs. Hishi Amazon drops your bags down on the ground and takes a key out of her pocket.

"Brief word of warning, Ruby. Your room was already occupied by a pair before you arrived. One of them made some last minute plans and moved elsewhere, so it was decided you'd share your new room with the other girl."

"To fill in a slot?"

"Yeah, pretty much."

"What happened to the other girl?" You ask.

"Took leave of absence. Didn't say much, just did. I didn't know them well outside managing their room." Hishi Amazon says. She inserts the key into the door's lock. "Nothing personal about this arrangement, either. Just the faculty not wanting to leave the other girl alone for long."

The door is unlocked. You enter. Inside is…

[Total EXP gained: 35.]

EXP: 75/100 (2 LEVEL UPs pending...)

1.5: Roommate

[X] Plan Shonen

-[X] Name: Cavalry ?

-[X] Attributes (Tagged): Stamina, Guts

-[X] Skills (Tagged): Traversal, Intimidation, ?

-[X] Archetype: Little League Boss

--[X] +1 Stamina Speed

- [X] Traits: Vigilante, ?, ?

Mood: Good.

EXP: 75/100 (2 LEVEL UPs pending...)

Hishi Amazon turns the key. The lock clicks open. She gives the door a push, and it swings open, revealing your new room.

Sunlight streams through an open window. It envelops a rectangular space in natural warmth. You look upon the room, and instantly compare and contrast it to the pods and manga cafes you've hopped to and fro during your umadol days. There's enough space to stand up and stretch your arms; and enough width to perform push-ups. Each bed has a small bedside drawer with three whole slots. Next to the bed, an entire shelf for books—and a small footlocker, too!

It's beautiful. Except for one small detail. There are people here. People, as in plural.

"So, then I said, you better not touch my tail with that metal detector, or I'll nab it and ram it up your stupid human ass!"

"You did not say that."

"Yeah, I bet you let that security guard twirl your strands with that little metal rod, because that's what you do whenever you meet a hot guy, Pelte."

"Hell no, I didn't! It wasn't a rod; it was some kind of small bat thing, and the guard was fat and spotty like a creepy otaku loser. His nose dripped with more oil than the kitchens of a WcDonalds. I'd never date someone like him."

A thoughtful nod. "What you mean is that they need to hire hotter guards at the airports."

"Yeah, exactly! Movie stars!"

"Give us some eye candy while we're in the queue, Like Tim Voyage!"

"Jewel, you're so right."

"I'm more of a Albert Levin girl myself…"

"I'd date a Trainer." A fourth umamusume chimes in.

Silence. Then, a round of oohs and aahs. Hands flying to face in faux indignant outrage. A clap on the back from another source.

"That's saucy, boss."

"Wow. Already shooting for the stars."

"It's forbidden love!"

"They're disciplined. They know us umas ins and out. My sisters told me the ones that do well at the national level earn a lot of money. There are worse choices after graduation."

"Smart. That's logical. They're, like, celebrities too."

"Nooo!" A playful moan. "Don't leave us so soon, boss!"

"Y'know, the Canopus Trainer wouldn't be bad looking if he got out of that suit and did his hair better…"

A round of laughter. Amazon clears her throat. It's drowned out. She slams her foot hard on the floorboards, and that does the trick. The laughter dies in an instant. Shoulders clench. Tails bolt up ramrod stiff. Four necks rotate towards the front of the room.

They look at you. You look at them. The curtain at the back of the room flutters in the breeze. The mysterious fourth umamusume nicks into an apple with a pocket knife, a piece of rind falling into a small wastepaper bin, as Amazon's grip on your duffel bag grows tighter and tighter and you are afraid she might crush the strap into fabric strands at the same time she crunches her own teeth into bits.

Somewhere out in the yard, a 10-yen coin falls.

"You!" Pierced-Ear shouts, bolting up from the bed.

"You!" Blue-Ribbon and Bow-Tie cry out.

"You guys again?" You say, frowning.

"Who?" The fourth umamusume asks. She's the only one out of the quartet not bugging her eyes out in pure surprise.

"Oh." She says. "You're my new roommate."

I guess?

This is drowned out not a second later.

"For the love of…" Amazon snarls. She drops your belongings. They thump to the ground. She stomps forward. The girls shrink back. She lashes out one firm hand, grabs the silvery edge of a half-eaten bag of potato chips and tears it straight out of its owner's grip in a flourish. "I told you bastards not to keep sneaking in here!"

Blue-Ribbon and Bow-Tie shriek and cling to each other. "It's the pigs!" They wail.

"I'm a dorm manager, not a cop!" Amazon roars.

The room promptly descends into chaos, by which you mean you're standing in the doorway, bewildered, as your would-be bullies from the cafeteria yelp and scramble to hide from Amazon's wrath. It's futile. The bed is small. The window is multiple stories off the ground and practically far away. Amazon is not only an umamusume of authority; she's a professional. She swats aside any pleading hands, then zips through the limited space with minute twists of feet that far exceed your dexterity. Her hands shoot out like bullets to snag more chip bags and empty soda cans and slam-dunk them into the wastepaper bin at the knees of your new roommate.

A vicious energy boils around her. Your mind conjures the image of flames. Angry, angry flames surrounding her body and licking at the air, powerful enough to scorch newborn Kagatsuchi. You think you saw them last when Kaede yelled at Miki's old stalker. You couldn't extinguish them if you tried.

It doesn't take long for the bed to go from occupied to clean, save for the crumbs and a few soda stains.

"Give me that." Amazon demands.

"No!" Blue-Ribbon cries. She shoves a colorful plastic bag behind her. She presses her back against the wall, palms flat, as if she could phase through it.

"Give me that bag now."

"They're limited snacks from Ireland! Please, Madam Amazon, have mercy!"

Amazon dips her head. A low chuckle gurgles out from her throat. "Mercy? You want to talk to me about mercy? You, of all people?"

Blue-Ribbon and Bow Tie's squirm. Their ears flatten themselves against the sides of their heads. Amazon sweeps her arm across.

"This room was supposed to be clean. It was supposed to be ready for Ruby over there to put her bags down and settle in without fuss. And yet. What do I find? What do I see? Three layabouts who have persistently broken curfew time and time again, getting crumbs, sugar and stains all over the nice, clean sheets Ruby was meant to sleep on. Do you know how easily ants and lice get into sheets? I'm responsible for ensuring everyone in Miho gets a good night's sleep. You tell me if I'm meant to show mercy to that!"

Her voice booms through the room. The walls tremble. Wind trips up and streaks her hair like bushels of miniature war banners in your mind's eye. Her teeth are tiger fangs and her glare is heavily bloodshot. Blue-Ribbon and Bow-Tie do the sensible thing and bow their heads and submit. They bring out packets of candies from behind their backs and hold them up in both palms. An offering from the subservient slave to the mighty goddess of war.

Amazon snatches them up. These don't go into the bin, but rather into her own pockets where you assume they'll be disposed (or distributed) later. It's a nice gesture. Wasting food is never great.

Two down, two to go. One makes a stand.

"Wait. Wait, wait, hold a minute." Pierced-Ear says. She launches off the bed and marches up until she's at eye level with your severely irritated dorm manager. "Forget them snacks. You're telling me she's rooming with the boss?"

Said boss of your would-be bullies is on her bed. Sitting down, still peeling that apple with her pocket knife in hand. Twintails like…Miss Twintails back in the cafeteria, except slimmer and knotted into braids wih cleat-esque pins. A hairclip in the shape of a blue orb with a purple stripe around its center is attached at the base of one of the twintails. The hairdo is finished off with white ribbons at the base. She's looked up only to watch.

"Yup." You say, re-directing your attention back to Pierced-Ear and giving her the thumbs up. "This is my room now."

Pierced-Ears clenches her hands into fists. "This is bull!"

"Nice assessment." Amazon deadpans. ""I'm failing to understand why it's your problem."

"It's my problem when it involves my boss!"

"Come back when you're part of the student council, I guess."

"Oh, come on! Isn't it obvious?" Pierced-Ear argues. She shoots you a glower, throwing her hands up in exasperation. "Think about it. Don't you know who she is?"

Amazon folds her arms and levels a cold stare back at her .

"Do you?" She asks.

Pierced-Ear flinches. She tries to start something, gets quelled again. She's trembling, knows she wants to back down. Her pride won't let her, and so she tries to stand.

"Satono Ruby." Her boss interjects. "Daughter of Satono Opal."

Amazon throws her glare down at her. She doesn't budge.

"That's me." You say.

"I heard your song on the PA this morning. Didn't know what it was about. My sister told me about it later."

"Want an encore?" You ask.

The boss continues to shear her apple. She answers a second late. "I like pop more."

Oh. Mainstream tastes. Apples and oranges, except enka is more of a traditionally grown watermelon in your case. Convincing newcomers to listen is always a tricky business. People hear the word 'traditional' and close out without listening to a single note. It's frustration.

The boss lifts her head more, and you stiffen. That's an intense stare she's got. Deep-set eyes. A void of dark amidst stark-white sclera. A mouth that is tightly shut when not speaking. Were she not working on that fruit, you'd have thought she was a statue.

"No offence."

"None…taken?" You say, warily.

She doesn't sound angry. Not like her underlings. Her tone is soft and controlled, almost uncaring. That, or she has one whammy of a poker face. A quiet person for such confrontational umamusume. Is she an introvert? But why would she be leading a group of extroverts? Something's off here.

"Yeah, exactly! We know whose kid she is. I don't want the boss catching strays." Pierced-Ear gulps and stands her ground. "She's got a lot of nerve coming here after—"

This is when you notice Bow-Tie has been shaking her head back and forth, mouthing the word 'no' with desperate frustration. It's Blue-Ribbon who's got more brains, who takes initiative. She jumps off the bed, kicking her own deposited shoes into the nearby bedside cabinet in her haste to run straight to her friend. Their heads almost collide. She slams one hand over Pierced-Ear's mouth, drowning whatever insult into a series of muffled, gagging sounds. They've remembered a dorm manager is part of the staff, too.

"After what?" Amazon demands.

"Nothing!" Blue-Ribbon cries.

"The way you're spitting makes me think it wasn't nothing."

"No, it was something, Miss Amazon. We did nothing to her! Ruby! Absolutely nothing at all! It's not a double negative."

Bow-Tie nods frantically.

Amazon glares at this motley trio for a moment longer before whipping her head to the boss. "Do you have anything to say?"

The boss looks up. She points to herself. "Me?"

"Yeah, you. This, and the fact you let them in here today."

The boss's response is a second late. "I invited them for homework."

Amazon blinks. She narrows her eyes. "Homework."

"For homework." The boss repeats.

"With junk food and snacks?" Amazon says, disbelievingly. That's annoyance born from deja vu. This isn't Amazon's first run-in with these troublemakers.

"It was a reward." The boss says. "My sister gave me a whole boatload of them, and I couldn't eat them all. Pelte, Tomoe and Jewel wanted to learn how to measure distances and calculate angles. It's covered under self-study."

She gestures to a pile of worksheets on the far side of her bed.

"They did good work. I wanted to give them an apple, too."

She lifts the fruit. It's the size of a baseball. It's not the bargain-bin kind you've scrounged from supermarkets, judging by how ripe the remaining skin looks. The scent, too. It's so juicy. You're faintly jealous.

"Congrats. You let them ruin your new roommate's bedsheets." Amazon says. "Ants are gonna get in them."

"I know. I'm sorry. It won't happen again." The 'boss' replies. "They won't bother Satono Ruby."

"Is that an again?" Amazon presses.

"If they have, they won't do it anymore. If they aren't, they won't start. That's that."

You raise your eyebrows. Sounds like she wasn't aware of what happened at lunch. Was she even around? Do we have a negligent leader here? Or, did those three act on this girl's behalf? The weak buttering up the strong.

Amazon and the boss lock eyes. It's a proper contest this time. A crushing fist against a wall of stone. A deadlock. Maybe not. A vibration through your new roommate's tail. Her teeth clenched down askew on her right side. It's a stalemate crumbling into a loss from the would-be bullies end. They've realised it. Behind Amazon, Bow-Tie looks straight at you. Batting lengthened eyelashes from some cheap salon in a market street. Begging, pleading. Save us.

This is the same gaggle of girls who, hours ago, wanted to dump soy sauce in your hair or some other nefarious deed in the corner of the cafeteria. They're so desperate they're turning to their would-be victim to cover for them. Should you?

You take a moment to think about this, and not because you want them to squirm—although that is a nice bonus, a dark corner of your psyche whispers. The gist is as thus. You enjoy pleasing people. You love it when others smile because of you. It's why you got attracted to the umadol business. How you got scouted. Manager Suzuki wanted someone who could blow kisses and exchange handshakes and have some of it come genuinely from inside their heart. He caught you singing your heart out for free in front of Hachiko, Scramble Crossing. The third time you pranced on stage, you saw the faces of FAITHFUL's then-dozen or so fans light up with glee and felt your own soul flutter with joy. That's when you knew you'd done it.

But—and this is not an insignificant but—unpleasant people suck. Bullies. You can't make them smile, not in the way you'd like. You don't understand them. Unwanted flowers on a desk, rusty nails inside a shoe locker, an entire textbook of drawings soaked black in ink—these are actions to hurt, to wound. To push the little guy down instead of uplifting them up, even if wrapped in thorns like Narita Brian did. And for what? Because misery loves company? So do love and joy.

Even after moving to the big city, the land of endless possibilities, you encountered them. Beneath the tall skyscrapers and the glittering night lights of Shibuya and Shinjuku lies an underbelly that taught you if you give certain folks an inch, they'll take a mile, and then some. Seedy coffin motel receptionists. Wannabe paparazzi. Fanatics who see young men and women as pieces of meat, not sentient beings. Terrible people.

It was Hotaru, gloomy-eyed, occult-loving Hotaru, who pulled you aside for a coffee one afternoon, after you apologised profusely to a greasy-haired journalist, and told you can't please everyone, 'cause we live in an age where we judge based on whispers and half-refractions in the mirror. Not even God himself can sort all this muck out.

Hypocrite, you thought and pouted. Didn't she spend an hour searching in the gutter for her little sister's lost phone strap?

It's not hypocrisy. It's me giving more than two craps about that rascal. It's doing what I can when I can. Priorities—that's the crux. We've only got two hands, two legs, one mouth, and who knows many footsteps to seek and to express ourselves. She gazed up at the skyscrapers touching Tokyo's skyline. Not even UKB-48 is loved by all of Japan.

It was a somber lesson from the woman who always attended practice on time. Discard those who scorn you. Drop the mean and the hateful and save your energy for those who will love you. That's the biz. That's what you must do as Satono Opal's unwanted daughter.

Yet, their 'boss' is your roommate. You will spend an awful lot of time around her, around them. And despite what you've dwelled on, you can't help but feel a twinge at their pleading gaze. You are still a young girl who wants people to like her.

Those stories about enemies turning into friends can't all be false, right?

['Positivity' chosen for Life.]

[+1 to Light Alignment points. Overall Alignment did not shift.]

"It's okay. Nothing happened between me and them." You state.

Blue-Ribbon and Bow-Tie gasp. Amazon whips her head around.

"Are you sure?" She's suspicious, but concerned. You can tell.

"Yep. Nothing much happened, really. We only had, like, one passing conversation." You top it off with a shrug. Amazon squints. She doesn't buy it. Probably has dealt with lots of students covering for each other in her role. It's your word alongside theirs—Bow-Tie's sparkling with joy and Blue-Ribbon's knees are clasping her hands akin to prayer—so there's not much she can do.

You smile, hoping she accepts it.

"Fine. That's good, Ruby. That's real good," Amazon says.

Blue-Ribbon lets go of Pierced-Ear's mouth. Pierced-Ear scowls, on the verge of spitting an insult out, only for Amazon to stride forward again and shove a single knuckle beneath Pierced-Ear's chin. She tips Pierced-Ear's head up. Pierced-Ear chokes. The soft skin around the would-be bully's neck stretches and holds. The wind is squeezed out of her lungs.

"Because if I caught any girl in my dorm being so damn stupid as to discriminate against the new kid for circumstances beyond her control, such as, I don't know, the idea of her being born, I might have to deal with them. I might have to drag their sorry asses straight to the Prez's office for a refresher on how to treat their fellow Tracen kids. There's been a lot of heat around that area these past months and she and I have just about run out of patience."

She leans in to whisper the final blow into Pierced-Ear's trembling ear. "Capiche?"

"Yeah." Pierced-Ear croaks.

Amazon yanks her knuckle away. Pierced-Ear stumbles back, coughing. She's caught by the boss, who lets Pierced-Ear lean against her. Alright. Time to act the good cop now that they're aware of the score. You clap your hands to catch everyone's attention.

"It's not that serious!" You say, putting on your umadol act. Eyes forward, gentle smile, and don't lean too far. "Look, let's just get the elephant in the room out of the way. I know what my mom did. I agree that it was a horrible thing to do, and I definitely get why some people would be so mad. But I'm just a normal girl like the rest of you. I came to Tracen to learn how to race. I want to do well, put on a good show, and make a lot of friends. Wouldn't it be cooler if we just put aside our pasts and lived in the present? We might actually have a lot in common!"

You extend your hand to seal the deal.

[Persuasion check: 72/40 -> Check success. +5 EXP.]

Blue-Ribbon is the first to shake your hand. She does it up and down with pure gratitude. Bow-Tie's next, blubbering her thanks. Whatever you saved them from must be truly horrendous. Pierced-Ear treats your fingers as if they end in wriggling cockroaches. She sticks out her tongue.

"Pelte. Do it."

"But, boss…"

"Please do it." The boss says, in that steady, soft voice.

Pierced-Ear obeys. It's barely a grip. Fingers dangling and brushing rather than interlocking. She yanks it back and wipes her fingers on her skirt. You can't win them all.

The boss is the last. Her grip is not just firm. It's heavy, full of resolute energy, like Grass Wonder, like Oguri Gap. Ah, you realise, this is a strong girl. The headiness in the muscles, the soul-searching of those blue-violet eyes. You're back in the concert halls for a small moment. This is raw energy of an achiever and, perhaps, a rival.

Amazon pinches her forehead. She exhales heavily. The adrenaline is flowing out. Anger is a truly exhausting state of mind.

"I'm bringing over new sheets and blankets. You're gonna put them on for Ruby, then clean the room, and then the three of you are going straight to detention to write an essay on why messing up a new kid's room is unacceptable."

"No way!"

"That's so boring…"

"It's fine." The boss says, and the trio shuts up again.

Amazon arrives back with a broom and a set of new blankets and sheets. She sits there in a chair, eyeballing your would-be bullies and their boss as they sweep crumbs away and replace the stained sheets with the new ones. Anyone caught slacking off is promptly put back into place with a single glare. The process takes less than a few minutes.

"Ruby, I'm so sorry about today." She apologises, once the trio has filed out.

"No. It's okay. I'm just so glad to have such a nice room. Thanks for bringing my bags over, too."

Amazon claps you on the shoulder. "Anyone tries to give you crap about your history, you come to me. I won't tolerate that nonsense in my dorm."

You don't doubt it. It's flattering, encouraging, to know the manager of the entire Miho Dorm is in your corner regarding this issue. She's much better than your primary school teachers. But, and you think this is something a veteran like Amazon or the rest of your senpais would agree with, you must fight your own battles, as well.

Amazon hands you the room keys. She leaves. You take a seat on your new bed. You lean back and plop down on your new bed. It's soft. The sheets smell like rosy shampoo. The mattress isn't hard as a rock. Cap it off here—life won't get any better than this.

Your bags wait in the corner. Their presence is like an annoying miko with her hands on her hips. Go away. Flip an imaginary finger. You're going to bask in this ocean of relaxation for a while longer.

"My friends shouldn't have said those nasty things to you."

You sit up. It's your new roommate. She's peeling an apple—again. The first one was handed to Pierced-Ear as a gift.

"You knew all along?" You ask.

Your new roommate shakes her head. Her twintails sway. "No. I guessed. They were talking about it last night. Sorry about that."

"They apologised."

"I didn't. They call me 'boss'. So I must."

She's serious, if nothing else. You chuckle.

"It's okay. You weren't there. Not your fault. Your friends did try to pull something over me, but they sorta failed before they even started. This other girl then came in to deal with them for me. She had hair like yours, just thicker and more orange. I don't think they'll try again."

Your new roommate makes a grunt.

"No hard feelings."

"I know. Want me to talk to them?"

"That's not necessary."

"Okay."

She keeps shearing with the knife, a slow, methodical process. The spiral of peel extending down from the fruit is almost circular in its loops. A minute skritch-skritch fills the gap between beds. It's almost relaxing to listen. It must be for her.

"Do you get it often?" She asks.

"Get what?"

"People asking about Opal. About your mother."

You breathe in and out. Talk about dragging the elephant back into the room. How best to answer this? Honestly. That should do. "All the time."

"From middle school?"

"From elementary school." And 'ask' is too kind of an understatement.

Her eyes widen a fraction. It was that bad? You nod. It was. In a world where the common folk of multiple nations halt their daily business to watch the Japan Cup, the existence of a cheater like Satono Opal is not just heresy. It is an aberration that must be examined, its cancer eradicated. The Satonos exiled you to the countryside as a means of appeasing the URA and the rest of the masses. Time let the wounds scar, and the public directed its attention to other scandals. The press didn't forget. They're always out to excavate the past for the latest story.

The mainstream media calls idol fans losers, creeps, deranged otaku. Some of it is true. You won't ever fully agree with them, because those same idol fans helped shield you from those horrid wannabe paparazzi.

"But it's okay now." You say.

"Is it?" Your new roommate asks.

"Yeah. I got into Tracen. I'm finally at the academy of my dreams." You tip your head back to look up at the ceiling. It's so high. "I shouldn't have to worry about those types any longer. Today was a good day."

Your new roommate nods, following along. You wonder if you should tell her what's on the tip of your tongue. It might not sound plausible, but—oh, why not? Another olive branch. Word will get around, like it always does. Gossip is fun.

"Hey. Guess what happened to me?"

"What?"

"I met with President Rudolf today."

She blinks. "Wow."

"Yeah. This goes back to my mom thing. I didn't know how she'd react, being the leader of Tracen and all, so I thought it'd be best if I introduced myself with an apology. I kinda got myself yelled at by Narita Brian. It was kinda a backhanded lesson? Like she was telling me to stop waggling my ears about and inject some motivation into my veins. Oh, Air Groove was nice to me too. The two of them fought for a bit."

"And then?"

You wink. "Guess."

"Again?" Your roommate says. "I don't know."

You lean forward, grinning like a loon. "I got to race."

"With Symboli Rudolf herself?"

You laugh. "No, I'd totally lose that. It was against Grass Wonder."

"I remember her. She won Takarazuka last year. It was a big deal."

"Right, right? And then Oguri Cap showed up. The Ashen Beast herself! I thought They put on these super heavy cleats to even the playing field with me, and I still got my ass kicked. But, it was fun." You let out a dreamy sigh. "Very, very fun. My first race ever."

Your new roommate finishes peeling the apple, tossing the rest of the peel into the bin. She takes a big, crunchy, juicy bite out of the apple, chewing slowly before swallowing with a big gulp. You've run out of things to say now. But you're still smiling.

She takes another bite. Chews. Swallows again. She lapses into silence. You press your legs together, waiting.

"Hokkaido." Your new roommate utters.

"Pardon?"

"That's where I'm from. Hokkaido. It's a tough region. The competition is fierce."

"Is it?" You're…

[History check: 32/40 -> Failure.]

…not too certain on the details. A lot of good umamusume are produced in Hokkaido, such as Special Week. It also snows quite a bit. That's about as much as you know in regard to the second largest island in Japan…and you understand why Rudolf said you needed supplementary lessons. Geez.

Your new roommate glances down at her feet. Her lips purse. "I was small."

"Oh. I was, too." You say. "I got my growth spurt early."

"Smaller than the others. Softer than the others. They picked on me, called me a twerp, a stick insect for my skinny limbs. Sometimes, they'd steal my bag and my toys and leave them hanging on a tree high up where I was too afraid to climb. I couldn't do anything."

Her tone wavers. Her grip tightens on the apple. It produces a squelching sound. Fruit juice begins to trail, drop by drop.

You reach out. "Hey—"

"Except run. I could run."

A steel edge in her voice. You find yourself closing your mouth and listening.

"Running was better than throwing fists. It showed you were better at being an umamusume. It gave you status and prestige among the playground. So, I ran." Your new roommate says. "I ran in the baby circuits. I exercised every day. I ran in the local circuits. My tormentors became my rivals. They taunted me the same. I slammed my head against their walls again and again until they broke into pieces and I left them in the dust, over and over and over again. All the way up to the Hidaka regionals."

You blink, surprised. Entering a regional racing tournament is no mean feet. It's practically a guarantee to skip the first part of Tracen's entrance exam, at the very least.

"I won that regionals. I became Hidaka's strongest. And then—"

She goes quiet.

"And then?" You ask.

She jerks her up. You recoil. A pressure exudes from the umamusume before you, vibrating the air, shaking the floorboards. It's less potent, but no less similar from what you felt from Oguri Cap when she overtook you on the racetrack.

"My rivals. My tormentors. They followed me after I beat them. They called me 'boss'. Swore themselves to me as their underlings in a…a constantly looping cascading waterfall of events. And it worked." Your new roommate's fingers carve themselves into the shapes of claws. "I went to regionals. I conquered them two lengths ahead. No-one back home dared to push me around again."

She crushes the apple, sending chunks of yellow-white flesh flying across the floor and her bed. One drop lands beneath a shelf full of books, a silver lock puzzle, a small medallion on a red velvet loop and, overshadowing them all, a large cloth banner displaying a stylized ひ, circled with dozens upon dozens of crude signatures.

GOOD LUCK BOSS! KICK THEIR BUTTS! It reads. HIDAKA RUNS ALONGSIDE YOU.

Your roommate stands up. She fetches a cloth from her beside drawer and wipes the splattered apple chunks away. She drops the cloth in the bed and opens her footlocker. She takes out a pair of grey running shoes.

"I'm going to train."

"Ah, right." You say. "You go do that."

She nods stiffly, and heads for the door. You let out a breath you didn't know you were holding. Okay. That was…your new roommate wasn't what you respected. She's focused. Very intense. Not pissed off, at least not at you. Her deal is…

[(Psyche check: 9/12 || Intimidation check: 30/65 || Subterfuge check: 45/70) -> Failure.]

…no clue. Well, it's okay. You're most likely not figuring out the ins and outs of someone on the first meeting. Those plans for staying up night, drinking (juice) and eating cake like you did with Kaede and the other girls a few years ago? You might want to wait on those.

Something then occurs to you.

"Wait."

Your new roommate halts in her tracks.

"I haven't gotten your name." You say. How embarrassing.

She stands there, silent, unmoving. She suddenly tilts her head back, her twintails dangling, eyes swivelling in their sockets to eyeball you over her shoulder.

"Meisho Tabaru." She says.

"Meisho Tabaru." You repeat.

Her tone has gone quiet again. All that ranting released whatever stress had been building up inside her.

"Meisho Tabaru, daughter of the Gold clan. One day, I will stand among my sisters, Orfevre and Gold Ship."

1.6: Whispers

It's calm once Meisho Tabaru leaves. It still feels unreal. Half of an entire three-star hotel-worthy room just for you. A mirthful giggle rises from your throat. You want to wriggle around on your bed, hands and legs waving up and down like a starfish to mess up your sheets just because you can. Alas, you have responsibilities. Luggage to unpack.

There's not a lot, you will admit. Your casual clothes, an assortment of tops, hoodies, skirts and jeans scrounged up from department store bargain bins. A toiletries set pieced together from freebies at motels. A portable charger pack from Akiba. Your wallet. A small makeup kit with perfumes and lip gloss as a gift from Miki. An e-book reader from Saya. The codes to a website where free literary material is available to download behind the government's back from Hotaru. A whole stack of discount cards for groceries, train fares and other services bundled by Kaede and Manager Suzuki. The farewell card. The train pass. Pens and a small pack of cookies.

You fold your clothes and squeeze them into the bedside drawer. Electronics and kits go on the shelf. Your valuables are tucked inside the footlocker. It's all nice and snug. A job well done!

And then there was one.

You pick up the steel-lined, combination-locked case. It's as heavy as the day you set it up. It cost you several months' worth of money from the umadol biz and donations from a brief-lived streaming career. It's an affront to your frugal lifestyle. Yet, every single yen was worth it.

You enter the combination. Six numbers, changed every fortnight without fail. You undo the locks and open the case.

Relief wraps around your heart. There they are: Satono Opal's old running shoes.

You take them out and hold them in your hands.

The shoes are a miracle of athletic engineering, even more than fifteen years later, possessing a firm midsole and a spike plate to prevent sinking on the turf. They're light to reduce load. The outer shell is waterproof to resist the moisture on rainy and snowy days. They fit perfectly on your feet. That's how you know these things. You tested them again and again. Someone tried to steal them after seeing you run in them, and that's the few times you remember using your umamusume strength so vividly. The thief fell down and didn't get back up. You didn't wait around to see if he did.

Would you do that again? Your fingers wrap around the collar of one of the shoes. A lump in your throat. Yes. Of course. Without a doubt. I'd break his nose twice if I had to.

You stand off the bed. You go to the window, and open it. The wind lifts the curtains. Cool and crisp air blows within. From far off, you hear the laughter of students and the cries of migrating birds. Beyond that: the afternoon sundown of Fuchu, a tableau of pinks and oranges behind Tracen's firm walls.

Your mother's shoes have those colors. They're on the side in the stripes, mixed in with turquoise. The patterning is cloudy yet eternally bright by some engineering magic. The rest of the frame is dyed crystalline-white, much like her namesake. Much like the hope of the Satono family what feels like a thousand years ago, pure and ever-transforming to whatever obstacle may have stood in Satono Opal's way.

There are four dots on the left side for the G3s. Three circles beneath that for the G2s. An empty box for a non-existent diamond.

We'll make our family shine!

— S.O. & H.D.

You read that line. You burn it into memory once again. You hug the shoes close to you, smelling the familiar musk that never leaves no matter how many times you've hand-washed the. Then, you walk over to the open window and hold those shoes in the direction of the sun.

Warm rays caress your cheeks like a palm. The breeze laps at your forehead like stray fingers. You stand there, gazing out towards Tracen, feeling the weight of your mother's running shoes, feeling a steady moisture gather at the corners of your eyes. You close them, and let yourself drift off.

Long ago, filtered through the haze of memory that drowns out the sky and lavishes the scenery in sepia, you are standing on your tippy-toes at the edge of a vast paddock. A grand mansion lies in the distance. A single umamusume in shorts runs laps around the edge, panting and wheezing all the while. Long black hair whips in the wind. Her shoes leave stardust along with grass and dirt in her wake.

A timer clicks, and she screeches to a halt. Her hands fly to her knees as she almost topples over. The moment she notices you, she's back on her feet, tail wagging, jumping up and down and calling your name in this soundless landscape. You are small, your legs stumpy and your arms twigs, and you squirm under the fence and run over to that umamusume one childish step at a time.

She lifts you up. Her cheeks are drenched in sweat, and a smile blossoms between her rosy cheeks. She holds you close, kisses you on the forehead, and in that moment you feel that you are very loved and very safe, and you know it's all real.

…

Only kidding. You're still asleep right now. I do believe some of this information about your rivals will trickle down as part of your lovely intuition. I also do believe I shall join in on the fun. Some may conceive this as cheating. I prefer to refer it as a lonesome soul's rambling, and those individuals departed Tracen long ago, regardless.

If you were to take the conceptual forms of all those rivals, squish and stitch them together into some blasphemous yet extremely capable Frankenstein-experiment of an umamusume, you'd receive the perfect Tracen trainee. Say the base attributes of this trainee—speed, stamina, physical strength and whatnot—can be measured from a scale of 0 to…let's say 25 for now. She'd possess 12 in every single one of them. As for her aptitudes, the techniques and skills she's trained and learned, we'll measure with a scale of 0 to 200. She'd possess at least 65 in all of those skills. 75 or higher, for her strengths. She'd also be packing with whatever innate abilities from her long, storied (and contradictory) history.

This perfect trainee does not exist. If she did, Tracen would be out of a job. However, your rivals do exist within her. The raw strength of Kawakami Princess, the quick-thinking of Satono Diamond, the speed and acceleration of Kitasan Black…and so on, so forth.

Does this thought experiment help? I hope it does. I'm looking forward to your tryout race. Your wonderful senpai has purchased a kiss of luck from the goddess of victory, and she's blowing it straight at you~!

Was that 'hip' with the 'kids'? Hee-hee-hee.

Goodnight Ruby. I'll see you soon.

"The last of the cherry blossoms are due to fall in Sendai within three days' time. Tsutsujigaoka Park is swamped with tourists…"

>>ENCOUNTER #2: START.

Early Morning, April 3rd, 20XX

You wake up to a buzzing noise in your ears and a thrumming against your chest. It's your phone. You hugged it as you went to sleep last night. Not an uncommon occurrence ever since the incident with the foul-mouthed granny and the coffin motel at six in the morning. The screen says it's five-thirty, however.

That's early, your bleary mind moans. I need to run laps follows. A non sequitur. There isn't any room near the office. Yoyogi Park is too far away. Did you set your alarm wrong? Oh, it doesn't matter. You know yourself—once you wake up, you can't go back until you exhaust yourself. As the sole umadol representative of Tomorrow is FAITHFUL, you need to take a shower, brush your hair and tail, put on some basic makeup and perform your morning stretches, so that you appear presentable and peppy even when travelling outside work hours. The corner store should have half off on yesterday's bread. Maybe Hotaru will be at the office, finishing up that new ballad she was composing…

The sheets fall off you. They're heavier and softer. The ceiling is high, visible through the gloom. You rub your eyes and turn to the side, where faint, natural light streams in from a gap in the curtains. Oh. Oh, that's right. This isn't a coffin motel. This is your new room at Tracen Academy. You just spent your first night in here safely!

Yes!

You pump a fist. It feels good. It's good you could do it again, which you do. The first night is more than well-deserved beauty sleep. It's tangible proof of your enrolment at Tracen. Who's laughing now, Umastagram? Ho ho ho.

You reach for your clothes—your uniform—and halt with your hand half-way outstretched. Right. You're not meant to do that. Grass Wonder, your new student mentor, wrote an exercise regime to get you sorted before tryouts. One of the items involved an early morning jog around the Tracen grounds, followed by a few rounds of strengthening exercises. The two combined are more than your routine back in your umadol days, on a good day.

You stick your tongue out. On the one hand, it's chilly outside. On the other hand, you don't want to be expelled for subpar results. Yep. It's not a contest.

You push aside your uniform and slip on your tracksuit. You take your running shoes—not your mother's; those are too valuable for mere training—and slide those on, too. A cereal bar awaits inside your bedside drawer.

[Nutrition check: 40/30 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

This is a tip you picked up from Grass Wonder. Eat some carbs and protein before a morning workout. Your blood sugar levels lower overnight, which might make you sluggish and light-headed during the workout. It's one of those health tips that sounds so obvious to anyone in the know, but might as well be space language from Mars to anyone who isn't. Which you were.

You unwrap the cereal bar, bought en masse from within Tracen's own shop using your student budget, and bite into it. The grain is crisp. The yoghurt carries a lemony tinge. You chew, swallow, chew again, and your tongue melts with the taste.

Is…is this what good living feels like? God. You could drown in it.

You leave your room and head downstairs through the Miho dorm, careful not to step too loudly. The exit door creaks open. Early morning air whips you in the face. You inhale it in, lolling the chill around your tongue. It's fresh. It's sharp, lacking the fumes of the Tokyo roads. The sky above is still dark, aside from a few rays poking through a pool of clouds.

Ten leg swings against a fence. Twenty seconds of high knees. Eight leg lunges per side, and then some. That's some good heat flowing down your muscles. You take a quick walk around the block, then whip out your trusty silver bullet necklace from beneath your tracksuit. Now, which direction should you run? There's only one way to find out.

You grip the bullet between two fingers, and give it a spin.

[World Resonance check: 55/35 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

To the right it is. That bush over there is sprouting a lucky flower. It's pretty.

Alright! It's time to umamusume, and I'm all out of johns to give!

Imaginary Saya cackles at you reciting awful B-movie lines as you kick off the asphalt and run.

You jog through the empty Tracen grounds, keeping your eyes and ears open for any other runners. There aren't—at least, initially. Most students are still asleep, for a bevy of reasons, you assume. The silence is punctuated by bird chirps and the rustle of incoming breezes. You have a clear way of passage for a good fifteen minutes. Then, you round a corner and notice a figure spread on fours on the grass.

"Tabaru!"

Your new roommate freezes. She lifts herself off the ground with her palms and feet. Push-ups. She's working out near…what appears to be a cut-down tree stump?

"Hey, Tabaru!"

She stands up and tilts her head backwards to face you, exactly the same as she did yesterday. "Ruby."

You grin as you jog over to her. "Good morning! You're out exercising?"

"Yeah." She says. "You're the same?"

"You bet!"

Your roommate merely turns around in response, still wearing that cool, neutral look. It'd be intimidating, but you're too flushed from burning energy to care.

"I didn't expect you'd be running this early." She states.

From the sweat on her brow, Tabaru's been doing those push-ups for some time.

You laugh lightly, hopping from one foot to another to keep your momentum going. "Told you I needed those catch-up lessons. The better I pound myself into shape, the better I'll do at those tryouts and find the best Trainer out there."

"Most students don't run this early at all." Tabaru remarks.

"Besides you!" You reply.

"And you, too."

"Did your sisters tell you that?"

"About umas not coming out so early? Yeah. They're the ones that ran when they didn't. I had a visit from one of them when I left the room last afternoon. Right as I was done with my laps, she put her arm around me and gave me a noogie, then took me out for a coffee. She said she was thinking about buying a segway." Tabaru's brow furrows. She sounds concerned. You're simply bewildered. A segway? That's a type of scooter, right? Those aren't fast. The reason an umamusume would ever want one eludes you.

It's probably a gift for someone else. A human. Anyway, you actually did some research about Tabaru's family—the Gold Clan—last night. The searching itself was a holdover from the idol lifestyle; you were expected to hold quick conversations with your fans. The best way to smooth them over was to look into topics they talked about during prior meetings. The same applied to your new roommate, you thought. The two of you had…an unorthodox first meeting, to say the least. Not something a handshake and an autograph could fix. More ice needed to be broken.

[Social Media check: 52/40 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

Turns out Tabaru's family was more than a gaudy-sounding name. The Gold Clan was not just famous in the racing world. It was infamous. Reports of body-slamming on the turf and public altercations worthy of comedians at the Dome scrolled down your screen alongside successive Tracen enrolments and a bevy of G2 and G1 victories. Their lineage stretches back to old umamusume heroes from the West. A couple missed claiming the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe by a nose! For you, who had scraped your way past the finish line, this was like pressing your cheeks against the glass of a fancy restaurant and staring at a banquet of all your favorite meats and pies.

Unlike the Mejiros, who built a business empire off their athletic pedigree, the Gold Clan kept itself informal. They don't live in fancy manors. Their retirees hold regular jobs like police officers or accountants. They've scattered their extended family across Japan's major regions like flying spores, only uniting as rivals on the racetrack or as fellow family members at gatherings in secret hideouts. Rumor has it the future of any immediate G1 is decided then and there…which means a complete blowout victory or a massive crash and burn. The media salivates either way.

A couple of Tabaru's sisters already attend Tracen with multiple G1 victories under their belt. Umastagram and LANE were very quick to offer material about that.

Dream Journey won't do anything. Someone's ringing my doorbell it's

When U Late Start. BOTTOM TEXT

Join Team IKZE. Umas with violent tempers are gladly welcomed! Orfevre, please don't kill me!

Memes aside—you will never say that phrase out loud, you have actual dignity—you understand why Tabaru acts so intense. Her sisters are legitimate champions. She has an entire legion of followers looking up to her from back home. Forget pressure on her shoulders. The expectations are compressing the curvature of her spine.

Still. She does have a large family. She has more friends than you could ever dream of. You admit: you felt a surge of jealousy when you read all that research and imagined Tabaru being fed candied carrots at a fancy restaurant by Orfevre's fancy mom, or something. That's not her fault, though. You're not one to blame others for circumstances beyond their control. Anyway, now that you've done your research, it's time to put the material into practice.

Tabaru stretches her body from side to side, then her shoulders. She begins hopping up and down.

"So, you're ready to run too?" You ask.

"Yeah. I'm going to head out into town for that." Tabaru replies. She points to the horizon, then towards the pavement nearby. "The roads here are sturdy. I think I'll do it every morning, like back home."

You see a chance and seize it. "Mind if I join you?"

"Every morning?"

"Well, I'm already out here, and I desperately need the practice, so sure!

This gives Tabaru pause, though that only appears as a quick flicker across her composure. "You think you can keep up?" She asks.

"Why?"

"The girls back home couldn't. Some of them tried. They still couldn't in the end. And you said you were still catching up on homework, so…" She tilts her head slightly, and goes back to stretching her shoulders.

A twitch in your own forehead. Oh my, is she challenging you? Does she not see the depth of your work ethic? Meisho Tabaru. Dear Meisho Tabaru. Your new roommate was an umadol. She lived, breathed, dug her manicured, polished nails into the bowels of the underground music industry. Those that do not show up for extra dance and signing practice are kicked below the surface, never to rise to the top of the indie charts again. Besides, never let it be said you don't have a smidgen of competitive spirit as an umamusume racer. The events from yesterday have merely bolstered that!

You face her and straighten yourself. "I won't know until I try."

She hums. "Fair enough."

Huh. That was easy. Time for part two.

"And…" You grow yourself a smile, bashfully nudging a clump of grass with your foot as you do so. "This might sound embarrassing, but I never had the chance to run alongside anyone for training."

Tabaru snaps her fingers. "Right. You said the one with Grass Wonder and Oguri Cap was your first ever race."

"Unbelievable, isn't it?"

She just shrugs. "Weirder things have happened before."

Like crashing into someone halfway through a race and sending them flying into the inner post, thereby earning a disqualification. Obviously, you do not say this to Tabaru. You have a better reason.

"You're my roommate." You state.

"And?" Tabaru asks.

"That's it." You say. "I want to start with you."

Tabaru stops stretching. She inclines herself in your direction. Gets a good look at you, and waits.

"I just want to be friends with you." You elaborate, feeling slightly nervous. "I think that'd be cool."

A thumbs up seals the deal. You hope.

Tabaru holds that intense gaze upon you as she reflects. You stiffen a little in response. It's as if even the orb in her hair is searching past your flesh into the recesses of her psyche. Did you offend her? Is she searching for a particular item in your speech? No, your instincts then remind you, honed from years of social activity in the underground, it's what you're abstaining from saying. That's more important. You can't imagine what; you just said an ordinary gesture of friendship.

Befriending the boss of your bullies is unusual, to be fair. Tabaru seems disconnected from Pierced-Ear and her kind, however. Not fully in sync. She could have joined in and talked smack about you until the sun went down. She didn't. You're not receiving negative vibes from her, like you did with those other journalists and hecklers in the underground concert arenas.

She's secretive and introverted. Not mean.

For a brief moment, you're worried she will say no. But she does nod back, and the side of her mouth quirks up. It's a smile back. It's done by someone not used to smiling. She believes you.

You pump another fist inside your head. Who cares about the reason? The result is what matters in the here and now. Yes, you think. Today will be a good day.

2.1: Daily Life

Morning, April 8th, 20XX

A pale light shines down from above. Four walls box you in. Your rear feels like a wooden plank is being shoved up your tailpipe, and that's definitely chalk dust wafting from the massive, black, imposing rectangle on the far side of the room. It twitches your nose. You almost sneeze. Welcome to hell, Satono Ruby, also known as a classroom.

"Now, class, I know it's only been a few weeks since we started the curriculum, buuut I really wish to know how much you've all been taking in the basics. You know what they say: practice makes perfect!"

A loud groan goes up from the class. You and the girls who gave you nasty glares when you arrived. Today, you are united. The archdemoness in charge, one Ms. Sana or whatever, walks through the rows of desks and whips out paper sheets like a printer merged with a gun. They're placed face down, so as not to give any watching eyes a head-start on thinking time. You glumly stare down at yours. Black uniform text on a white background.

The last time you stepped foot into a classroom was back in the countryside, when you were still trained at the shrine. You were a meek little umamusume who nobody liked nor wanted to associate with. Now, you have enrolled in Tracen as a student that mostly nobody likes or wants to associate with. Baby steps.

"Your time starts…now!"

You turn over the page. The first question balls up its psychic fist and punches your psyche in the gut. Oh no. Oh god, oh no. Bind a rock with ofuda and seal you in the mountains alongside Tamamo-no-Mae, because you have never been less prepared for this formal education business.

Rudolf was right. You really do need remedial lessons. At least you might learn something from this test...

(What's the test on?)

[] [Event 1] Mathematics and calculus.

[] [Event 1] The history of umamusume.

[] [Event 1] English literature.

[] [Event 1] Motion and physics.

[] [Event 1] You don't care. You're going to sleep.

Afternoon, April 10th, 20XX

Every afternoon, when most of your new classmates prepare for the gym, you're down on the turf or in the exercise room subjecting yourself to Grass Wonder's mercy. She has none. She wears the same graceful smile from the tabloids and orders you to run consecutive laps, deadlift weights heavier than a supermarket trolley, and engage in a horrendous scientific term called plyometrics that stretches and bends your muscles and sets them aflame from the inside.

You protest on third day after another lap around the turf. The amount of sweat pouring out of your skin was salting your tracksuit into fabric jerky.

"Did…"

"Pardon, Ruby?"

"Did your Golden Generation all go through the same—"

"Are you giving up?"

She interrupts you, her tone unwavering, nary a sweat trickling from behind those elegant bangs, despite having run alongside you with those same extra-heavy cleats bolted to her shoes. Her eyebrows raise a fraction.

"N-no?" You ask.

"Then you shouldn't be doubting my expertise."

Whatever protest was about to come up in your throat dies a sickly death. The message is clear: no mercy for you.

And so the days flow. You attend the sessions. You wobble away with shaking knees. Grass Wonder devises new and interesting methods of torturing you. The muscle ache persists through classes, fogs your head so much so that you barely listen to any of the whispers circulating you every time you enter the classroom.

You crash into your bed, sleep, and wake up to your vibrating phone, sore all over. Dancing worked you up a sweat, but this? This is pure destruction and regeneration. Grass Wonder is smelting your physique brick by brick. You remember how you once watched a human baseball player's autobiographical movie with FAITHFUL on a bored Sunday. How comfortable you were sitting back with a lemonade in your hands as the man on screen groaned doing sit-ups in the gym. You could die laughing now.

The only respite comes from your meals, which you chow down with a boar's ferocity, and your morning jogs with Tabaru. She's a silent one, barely speaking or emoting and always leading. She does keep an eye on you, though. She places a hand on your shoulder or helps you up when you're about to stumble, granting you a nod of understanding afterwards.

It was the same back home, you assume. The same with her legendary sisters. Maybe there's respect in Tabaru's gaze, too.

But you don't quit. You can't. Tracen gave you a warm bed and three square meals a day. Tomorrow is FAITHFUL still cheers you on through Umastagram DMs and LANE messages. Grass Wonder believes in you. She projects the same high expectations as Manager Suzuki did. The faith that you may be slow and weak and pathetic now, but under their guidance you will not stay that way.

You will not let their trust be misplaced. Gradually, the improvement arrives.

You acclimatize to the persistent ache. Keeping focus is easier, enough for you to answer Grass Wonder's questions about strategy through exercises. An odd form of relaxation seeps deep into your body during the opening stages of the run, in which you don't need to drag your muscles to work against their will. You ask, and they obey. This is demonstrated when you kick off the starting line and feel bouncy on your feet, as if invisible springs are now strapped there. Before, it felt like dragging them through the dirt.

Grass Wonder also has her stopwatches. She measures your times. They improve by seconds in the later weeks. It's an objective measurement.

"Ruby."

"Y-yeah?"

"Good work today. It's time you took a break. Come with me."

Grass Wonder is merciless. However, she's not a slave driver. An umamusume's body will not develop if it's burned down to a husk.

She takes you to the side of the training track, where a cooler box lies next to her exercise bag. You initially wondered why she had brought it. Grass Wonder placed her finger to her lips and told you to get running instead.

"Here. Drink this."

The answer turns out to be a cold flask, from which Grass Wonder pours an orange liquid into two cups. You take the offered cup and sip it. Fizzy sweetness and a mild vinegar-esque sourness laps at your tongue. This is…

"It's kombucha!" You exclaim.

Grass Wonder smiles. She sips from her own cup. "Good, isn't it? It'll replenish those lost salts and help with digesting all that food you're eating by way of probiotics."

"It's good. So fresh. Did you brew it yourself?"

"I did as part of Tracen's home economics program." Grass Wonder says proudly. "They're letting us brew these health drinks alongside regular cooking with the academy's homegrown crops."

"Wow. So Tracen grows its own food."

"Partially. Next month, get in line early at the cafeteria. It'll maximize your chances of getting the Tracen-grown carrots. They're delicious." Grass Wonder takes a delicate sip of hers. She hums. "As for the kombucha, I could have bought it from the store, yet I simply could not waste this opportunity to brew as the agriculturalists of yore did. They gave this drink to old umamusume empresses all the way back in 500 AD to cure their digestion cramps, you know."

[History check: 40/55 -> Failure.]

You're no expert in Japanese history, but you do enjoy this drink. Half of it is gone before you know it.

"It reminds me of back home." You mumble.

"Back home?"

"Yeah. There was an old man who came to make donations for his veggie crops, and he'd always bring in drinks for us. He said a little of sugar was needed for a kid like me to grow up."

"Donations, hm?" Grass Wonder thinks. "You must have hung around a shrine a lot. Sounds like it was your playground."

[Guts check: 8/9 -> Failure.]

"Nah, not really. They made me work." You mumble absentmindedly.

That was a mistake. It was done out of exhaustion. You realise this far too late.

Movement. The hairs on the back of your neck prickle. Grass Wonder has nudged closer, and her eyes are…you cannot phrase this any other way: they're sparkling. Stars gleaming with pure unadulterated interest. Her ears twitch forward at yours. Oh no. She's put two and two together.

"Ruby. Are you a miko?" Grass Wonder asks. "An actual one?"

"Uh, um…"

Grass Winder beams at you. "We've never had a miko uma at Tracen before. Fukukitaru doesn't count. Goodness, I never thought I'd get the chance to meet one personally in this day and age!"

You want to moan out loud.

"That's…" You stammer.

"Yes?" Grass Wonder inquires.

Why couldn't you keep your dumb mouth shut? This is Ebisu's fault. Somehow.

Grass Wonder presses closer. Her tail swishes from side to side. She's seconds from gripping your hand, intertwining her fingers with yours and crushing your bones in her pursuit of her answers. The cat has fled the bag and disappeared into the bowels of the nearby tuna factory.

It's strange, though. Why is Grass Wonder so interested in shrines, anyway? Doesn't she go to one during New Year's like the rest of Japan? If not, how has she not met one already? You were under the assumption she was born into those old-fashioned aristocrats, who live in those wide-spanning traditional houses in towns outside of the capital and support themselves via an ancestral stockpile of wealth.

[Instinct check: 30/40 -> Failure.]

That is where Grass Wonder comes from, right? How else is she so much of a yamato nadeshiko?

…well, someone had to find out about your childhood eventually. Your student mentor isn't a terrible choice. Telling a bit about yourself might pull the two of you closer…

(What did you like the most about your life as a miko-in-training? Choose up to two.)

[] [Event 2] The festivals.

[] [Event 2] The cleaning.

[] [Event 2] The dancing.

[] [Event 2] The mythologies.

[] [Event 2] The offerings to the gods.

[] [Event 2] The purification rituals.
