Noon, April 20th, 20XX

Shockingly, Meisho Tabaru's underlings possess names! Duo Pelte for Pierced-Ear, Tomoenagae for Blue-Ribbon and, lastly but not leastly, Jewel Azurite for Bow-Tie. The trio are juniors at Tracen, like you, and share a common history attempting to gang up on Tabaru, before she annihilated them on the track with her front-running skills.

Why is this relevant? Because Tabaru sometimes comes to sit with you during lunchtimes. She doesn't announce it. She just pulls up a chair, plonks down her tray and begins eating. The trio soon follows.

Today is one of those days.

"I don't want her here." Pelte hisses.

You lift your head, the vestiges of a mouthful of miso soup swirling down your gullet. "Sorry, am I slurping too loudly?"

Pelte scowls as Jewel lets out a soft groan. "Sure. Why not? Take your goddamn toilet bowl of a pie-hole elsewhere."

A soft punch to the shoulder. It's Tomoe. "C'mon, Pelte. That's rude. Don't be like that."

"Yeah. Ruby's mom might be awful and a filthy cheater, but not all of it passed down onto her kid. She got us out of more cleaning duty, remember?" Jewel adds.

"That's not the damn point." Pelte hisses.

Tomoe rolls her eyes. "Then what is?"

Pelte gulps down her soda in a single chug. She spears a chunk of bloody steak into her mouth and talks over the relentless chewing. The rind is visible.

"She doesn't deserve to be here. You and I and Jewel—we got scouted by the boss herself—"

"Scouted?" Jewel repeats, disbelievingly.

"We all tried throwing our weight around and got reamed into oblivion. That's natural. That's how things should go. It's step one and two in earning our places by her side." Pelte snarls. She cocks a thumb on her free hand. and places it on her chest. "Hell, I followed her all the way from Hokkaido. I was the only one who got high enough in the regionals to earn a spot at Tracen when the rest of those bozos went home crying to their mommies about how a little running was too difficult!"

She slams her palm on the table. The cutlery rattles.

"Like hell I'm gonna let some newbie, let alone some cheater's precious little daughter, waltz up to the boss and get all chummy with her!" She finishes.

[Composure check: 50/40 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

"I'm her roommate." You say.

Pelte glares daggers back. "Only because the academy said so. There's a nice storage room in the dorm waiting for you."

"And you can drag her in there yourself." Duo mutters. "Not risking another visit from Amazon."

"Pelte, aren't you taking this too seriously?" Tomoe asks.

"This is serious! Our boss's reputation is at stake. We've got to uphold it. Grow it." Pelte retorts. She curls a fist, a heaviness settling into her expression. "You guys don't know what it was like back at Hidaka. Every time boss tried to relax, some moron or half-rate racer would come up and kick her juniors, steal her shoes or whatever bullshit of the week was. And that was just regionals! Tracen is nationals. So many monsters roam the halls. Special Week, Tosen Jordan, that devil bitch Curren Chan—boss's good, but she's not invincible, and those bastards gonna take advantage of her if we don't fortify ourselves!"

She's standing up from her seat by the end of her rant.

Tomoe and Jewel share a glance. You can't decide if they're moved by their friend's speech, or considering sinking into their chairs, resting their faces in their rice and hoping the nearby tables stop staring.

You're eating your chicken. It's good food. Crisp and crunchy. The chefs at Tracen are truly magnificent. It can't last forever. Fine, you will actually deal with this problem.

So, Pelte thinks you don't deserve to be in Tracen? That's familiar. It reeks of hazing. Hotaru and Miki used to give you a hard time before you cultivated enough singing talent. Manager Suzuki expressed he had his doubts about you for a year straight, privately. It's also ironic, considering that apology you handed to Rudolf. Doubt it'll work here, though.

You turn to your left. "Hey Tabaru, want to do something after lunch?"

Tabaru slurps up her udon first. She utters her first word in this entire conversation. "Sure."

Pelte looks as if someone slapped her in the face. That's fine. She's a girl who respects power. You'll demonstrate that by challenging Tabaru, her boss, and doing well. This will earn Pelte's grudging respect. Eventually, it might blossom into a genuine friendship. Yep, you're so smart.

Morning, April 27th, 20XX

You hear about the academy shrine from Grass Wonder. She doesn't order you to go there—no, you are to lift your hands behind your head and perform stair jumps up the staircase leading to the shrine. It's more plyometrics, designed to build explosive leg power for race starts and spurts. Not exactly how you intended on spending your weekend, but fine. Training is your duty.

You then rock up to the base of the staircase that Saturday morning, crane your neck upwards and count the steps one by one. They disappear past the horizon somewhere within the fifties. Dread trickles into your soul like water out of a leaking faucet. Of course, it wasn't going to be easy.

Here goes nothing…

By the time you reach the torii at the top, your legs are screaming their imaginary lungs hoarse and filing several lawsuits against your sense of determination. You ignore them. You step through the torii and onto the layered stone path.

The wind blows your hair. Trees rustle in the distance. Insects chirp.

[Inspection check: 32/25 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

The shrine is clean. That's not an easy task, given how exposed this one is to the mountain wind and the nearby forestry, but it's true. No stray leaves crunch beneath your feet on the path. The surrounding grass is devoid of trash. The cleansing pool smells fresh; its water clear. It rained a few days ago, yet the lion statue and the stone lantern holder flanking the entrance are free of moss or mold. The only aberration is the slight wearing of the thickened rope above the donation box. It's a sign of generous use. Even that can be remedied with an afternoon of shaving.

You rest your hand on the donation box. It's half-full. Coins glint in the darkness behind the bars.

The shrine is too small to house a permanent resident. Lodging must exist nearby. Its tatami mats should need cleaning this afternoon.

But not by me.

That's not my responsibility anymore.

Your hand falls to your side. Whatever was drifting onto your lips drains away, replaced by an uneasy coldness divorced from the chill of the wind. You press down the memories of familiar faces beneath the surface of your misbegotten childhood. Standing around here is a waste of time. There's homework to catch up on after your morning training.

"Satono Ruby!"

You whirl around, eyes wide. Someone's here. An umamusume—a complete stranger. Her hair is short and amber-orange with two hairclips on opposite sides: a daruma and a lucky clover. The Tracen uniform lies on her back.

"T-the most grievous omen has found its way to our shrine! This is terrible. No, it's a complete disaster!" The girl shrieks. Her hands fly to her head, before she presses them in prayer. "O Lord Shiraoki, give me strength, because this lowly disciple of yours is cowardly, a fool, but she must sacrifice herself for the sake of Doto and the rest of her friends. She could truly use help right now!"

"Who are you?" You ask.

The girl staggers back, her tail trembling and stiff. "She approaches!"

"I…kind of have to?"

"Stay back! Back, I say! I know the purification arts, and I'm not afraid to use them!"

She lifts her hands and circles them in the air, an action akin to groping invisible floating apples or charging up an energy blast from a late-night action anime.

"Satono Opal cannot hurt me. Satono Ruby cannot hurt me. My life will not be swamped in misery! I will not start late in the next scrimmage!"

You just stare. This girl ranks among the most unhinged weirdos you've met in your life, and you worked as an umadol.

Your legs burn again. Nope, you're too tired to deal with this nonsense. Yet, this girl doesn't seem like she'll budge unless she completes whatever rite she's attempting to pull off, and you don't have the time for that. You decide to try pulling your fortune at the shrine to prove to her that you're not some omen of disaster.

The coin clanks inside the donation box. A pull of the rope, and the results come in. They surprise you. Your fortune isn't just okay. It's looking pretty good! What does it say?

>>[Event 1] Motion and physics.

Morning, April 8th, 20XX

You stare at the test and arrive at a simple conclusion. It is secretly a yokai manifest from the depths of a…a…what is the name of the yokai that lurked around abandoned scholar houses, the one Hotaru identified with—kyorinrin. That's the one. The test was stripped out of a kyorinrin's ass for the sole purpose of sinking its invisible dragon claws into your brain and tearing it apart chunk by chunk.

There is a 5-kg mass hanging from a rope. What is the tension in the rope if the acceleration of the mass is zero?

A runner accelerates from rest at 2 m/s² for 5 seconds. What is their final velocity?

A feather is dropped on the moon from a height of 1.40 meters. The acceleration of gravity on the moon is 1.67 m/s2 . Determine the time for the feather to fall to the surface of the moon.

Malformed shapes and diagrams form in your mind's eye. Each and every single one is terrible. What is this? Why is this? How, for the love of all that is sacrosanct and holy, is this meant to prepare you for the wider world?

You hang your head. Your pen slides from your grip and threatens to roll off the table. It's no use. You're paralyzed. The only equation you're solving is that formal learning plus you equals massive headache.

"Twenty minutes left, class! Make sure you've filled in all the answer boxes!"

[(Visual Mathematics check: 45/50 || Wits check: 9/11) -> Failure.]

You bomb the test so hard they have to scrape the beach for the remnants of your shattered pride.

The teacher is helpful with her corrections, though.

[Classroom Learner: Exists.]

[Visual Mathematics has increased by 4.]

>>[Event 2] The dancing.

>>[Event 2] The purification rituals.

Afternoon, April 10th, 20XX

In the face of Grass Wonder's sudden spurt of enthusiasm, you turn your head and pray you groomed yourself well enough so that your long bangs hide the grimace growing on your face.

This is quite a pickle, and you're trying to hide the fact you bit it straight down the middle. Down, tail. Eyes, stop shifting to the side. Hey ears, can you do the brain a favor and act all floppy and natural for once in your—oh, who are you kidding? You think you can lie to Grass Wonder? A G1 champion? You've only known her for little under a month, yet you understand. Such patience she runs with on the track. Such perseverance she guides you with over your stumbling blocks. Hardly anyone gave her crap for mentoring you; when one unlucky soul dared, Grass Wonder took them aside and sent them off running away in tears.

Make no mistake. Grass Wonder cuts through nonsense like a samurai with his blade, and you blurted your childhood out loud straight at her.

[Logic check: 62/25 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

President Rudolf is on her team, too. Team Rigil. The two colluded to set up this student mentorship. Now, your childhood probably isn't as important as your mother's sins. If Grass Wonder wanted to dig deeper and decided a chat with the school administration was faster than the Internet, well…

"Ruby?" Grass Wonder asks.

"Um…" You stammer. "Er, that is to say…"

She's leaning in closer. The tingle on the side of your cheek is either her breath or the wind breezing by, taunting you. You're sucking on the inside of your cheek like it's a slice of a lemon.

So. Lying is off the table. There's still a way out. Deny Grass Wonder. Slap down the standard polite umadol denial (a trusted tool in Manager Suzuki's massive PR arsenal) and switch the topic back to training. You've got a shopping list of excuses. Try-outs are coming in a little over a month. Time can't be wasted. The countryside is like a million kilometres away, full of crumbling walls and trees filled with moss and bugs, which is very old-fashioned and so not like Tracen with its relentless competition and cutting-edge facilities. Super uncool.

Oh, but her smile. Her enthusiasm. It's palpable through the grip she has on your fingers. You haven't seen this level of passion since Miki bought tickets to the Tokyo Dome. It'd be so rude to leave her hanging after dangling a treasure right in front of her eyes. Mikos don't interview much these days. Too many bad apples amongst tourists. Besides, it's not as if you're utterly divorced from your childhood—your influence over FAITHFUL was proof enough.

The wind brushes your locks. You taste the ghost of dew on bamboo leaves, hear the chirp of cicadas amidst the rustling of the grass. Nostalgia thrums within you, soft yet sour. Your childhood wasn't the best. It's why you rarely talked about it…

[Guts check: 8/8 -> Success. +10 EXP.]

…but rarely is not zero. It wasn't as if you were abused back at the shrine. Far from it. It was simply a stricter upbringing than the rest.

You gently prise Grass Wonder's fingers off yours. Then, you flash a thumbs up and give a somewhat-forced cheery grin.

"Nope, you totally got me! You're right. I used to be a miko." You say.

Grass Wonder lets out a gasp, one hand flying to her mouth. She makes a delightful sound. You give an exaggerated shrug of your shoulders.

"Guess I made it pretty obvious, me stating it outright like a dummy aside."

"No, no, you did a good job hiding it. I wouldn't never have guessed if you hadn't let it slip. My, oh, my…" Grass Wonder says. She opens her mouth and closes it again. A faint blush on her cheeks. "Goodness, now that you've revealed the truth, I don't know which question to ask."

"You've been looking forward to this, huh?" You say.

"My parents have always respected how dignified and dutiful Japanese mikos behave. They passed on their interest to me. A miko is on the checklist of people I wish to meet, alongside respected figures like Saint Lite." Grass Wonder replies. She taps the side of her head. "These things are always at the back of my mind."

That mild awkwardness from someone so superior to you helps ease a bit of the tension. You rub the back of your neck. "Hate to disappoint you Grass, but I'm not actually a full miko. You have to train a lot and basically become an adult for that to happen. Kids like me are still in training."

"I still would like to hear about it!" Grass Wonder exclaims. She then blinks. She pulls herself back, clears her throat softly and places her hands back on her lap.

"If that is alright with you, Ruby. These sessions are for your benefit." She adds.

"It might take a while." You warn.

"We've got time. You've been doing well so far. We'll say you deserve a longer break than usual," Grass Wonder replies.

You try not to snort. That's an excuse, if you've ever heard one, considering Grass has counted down your breaks in the previous sessions to the last second. Still, it's lovely of her to offer.

How hard can it be?

"Shoot. Ask me anything."

Grass Wonder doesn't say anything immediately. She ponders for a while, tapping the side of her cheek with a gentle finger—no doubt trying to sift through the obvious questions.

"I must say, it's fitting for a young miko to perform enka on stage." She eventually says.

"Is that a question?" You ask.

"Yes. I'm curious about your performance. How much inspiration did you take from your childhood?"

"Did I tell you about my music?"

"We talked about it with Miss Oguri, didn't we?"

You contemplate this, rewinding back to your first day. "Nope. I don't remember telling you what genre it was. Only that it playing on the PA made me want to sink into the ground and die."

Grass Wonder giggles. "It wasn't that bad. I dare say it left me wanting more."

"I could've done a live at a school festival or something. Shown off my moves, got the girls back from Shibuya…" You fake-groan. "But it seems like you recognised it was enka. You're smart, Grass. Most call it the classics, generic rock or both when they first hear it."

The trouble of existing in a niche genre. Grass Wonder smiles in pride, then frowns in distaste at this traditional and intricate artform being mistaken for generic corporate-brand pop. So do you. One refined palate recognizes another. In that moment, you and your mentor synchronize, resulting in giggles all around.

She wants to hear the song? You're fine with that. More than willing, in fact. You reach for your phone and flip open your private music playlist. FAITHFUL's old songs are arranged in a neat list for inspiration and rehearsal. You scroll down to the one that was played over the PA and hit the button. Tinny shamisen notes fill the space between you and Grass Wonder, bouncing alongside the percussion. Guitar chords shred as the chorus arrives, and deep in the past on an underground stage beneath crimson lights, Kaede hoists the microphone and roars.

You notice Grass Wonder tapping her foot against the ground to the beat.

"That was wonderful, Ruby. It's so authentically passionate," Grass Wonder gushes once the song concludes.

You can't help but preen a little. "Thanks. The entire team put a lot of heart into it."

"I do take pride in my eye for passion. I can tell when something is done with effort." Grass Wonder gives you a coquettish grin. "Spe can testify to that."

Spe. Special Week. The story behind your new mentor beating her friend sounds like a horror story from the perspective of the monster—so still kinda scary.

Now that you're in interview mode, you feel obliged to keep talking.

"Want to hear how we wrote the song?"

"A behind-the-scenes exposure? How can I say no?"

You readjust your position, relaxing your posture and taking a few quick breaths to calm yourself down. This will involve a lot of talking. Suzuki's words ring in your head. Don't rush. Take as much time as you need within what's acceptable. Make sure the onus is on their understanding, not just listening. Yep, you got this.

[Artistry check: 52/50 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

You go back to your phone, tapping on the song's icon: a picture of your friend Kaede, dressed in a costume resembling a kimono crossed with a rocker's kit, photoshopped in front of a wheat field with her hands behind her back and her tongue sticking out. "Okay, so this song is about offering faith to a kami or else you'll be cursed, right? My unit, Tomorrow is FAITHFUL, took inspiration from folklore from Nagano. Ever been to Lake Suwa?"

"On holiday with my parents. I was young." Grass Wonder says, somewhat wistfully. "Very young. Sadly, I don't remember much of it. My parents told me it was a beautiful place."

"We're in the same boat. I had to get Kaede to walk me through it. She also visited there." You say. "Anyway, the lake's tied to an ancient clan that lived there around a thousand years ago. The ancestor, who's basically his own kami had this point, had to perform these rites to command these earth spirits called the Mishaguji. They're found inside bamboo leaves and trees and rocks, and they're important for fertility and the harvest. Most of all, they get super, super upset if they're not properly worshipped. I had to learn about those guys as part of my miko training."

"Your song didn't mention them." Grass Wonder says.

"That's because their form is…"

Said form pops into your head. Your cheeks turn pink. Heat flares in them. Grass Wonder looks at you quizzically; you slap your psyche inside your head until the image vanishes.

"Uh, not that relevant." You say.

"Are you sure?"

"Totally. One hundred percent. Forget I brought that up—anyway! Their form isn't as important as what they represent. I know it rarely seems that way on the surface, especially to the audience that only knows about kami from movies and games and such—no offence to you, by the way—but the kami can be pretty spiteful and wrathful like us modern people." You clench and unclench a fist, feeling your nail of your thumb dig into your skin. "In the old stories, aside from the ones about yokai, they hold grudges, form rivalries and get into fights. If you don't maintain your connection by neglecting them, they'll turn that ire on you. Storms, floods, broken communities and all sorts of other nasty stuff."

"I see. Despise and you'll be despised in return. How fitting." Grass Wonder says. "Then, do the kami attack us, or do we force them to? That's how the usual cursed shrine story goes, right?"

"That's a chicken and egg situation, I think. We didn't get into that question when writing the song." You say. You take another gulp of kombucha to quench your thirst. "Going back, if the kami are appeased, if the connection is made by showing respect or celebrating what they represent, they're calmer. Happier. They bless you and make your fortune better. It's a benefit for both sides. But that's also a result of us mortals being closer to each other. The kami aren't that dissimilar to us in that regard."

You press a small button beneath the music player, bringing up lyrics on screen.

"We wrote the song from the perspective of the Mishaguji and sort of their boss goddess. Remember how the song starts cheery at the start, but at the half-way mark, it goes all dark and intense with the chords and the lyrics about curses, then goes back to us mortals trying our hardest in front of the goddess? This duality and irony is the core of the song. That's the kind of detail FAITHFUL puts into its performance."

You pause. A warm feeling inside you, blooming into a delicious hotness. It tastes like pride.

"That's also what I learned as a miko." You add.

Never stop maintaining connections with others, no matter how vast the world is, or how hard the act itself was. You brought that to the big city from the countryside, if nothing else.

"Then we mixed in some background details about the festival and the harvest, gave it a few mixes, and…the song was done." You conclude. You take your phone aside and swallow. "That's it. That's the backstory. I hope I covered everything."

Please don't let that be cringe a part of you begs. You drown out its sounds by slugging down the rest of the kombucha. This is the most you've talked about the group's work in a while. Certainly not to a minor celebrity like Grass Wonder. Normally, it's Kaede or Suzuki who talks about upcoming performances and teasers. Their imaginary versions give you…a six. That's being generous. It's not terrible for a first try. It's not as harrowing as the fact that you showed off your work. That's always the tough part. It's like exposing a piece of your heart to be scorned.

Grass Wonder takes your words, absorbing and ruminating over them with soft nods of her head, before asking again.

"Are you sure you're not a real miko?"

You splutter, waving your hands around. "I'm not! Honest!"

"But you did such a good job. I'm frankly astounded." Grass Wonder says, smiling again. "You might have to repeat this to some of my friends after I show them your work."

You laugh, feeling more of the tension deflate It almost makes you feel lightheaded. "Want my autograph as a gift?"

Grass Wonder giggles. "I'll be sure to have you sign the certificate Rudolf will give me, once we get you try-outs. I believe I also owe you a story one day."

You decide to indulge your mentor a bit more. She's proved herself to be a good listener so far. It's time for a crash course about the shinme—the umamusume miko. Her role is not too dissimilar from a human miko. The responsibilities are the same: wake up at dawn, offer prayers, sweep the shrine grounds, help make the amulets and protective charms, help the priests at ceremonies and so on and so forth.

A shinme differs in what she represents: the connection between kami and the mortal world through umamusume. Go back to Japan's ancient era, where fledgling civilisations categorized the forces beyond their walls as human or not. With their superior strength and agility and their superficial resemblance to humans, umamusume were treated as minor deities. They too were codified into the set of texts that history acknowledges as the earliest Shinto myths.

Consider the most famous myths. Their depictions float inside your mind's eye, portraits and paintings on reed and stone: the radiant sun goddess Amaterasu descending to earth at the behest of the umamusume in white; her apoplectic brother, Susanoo, rampaging around her halls with his umamusume best friend representing chaos and power. When summer soars and the droughts arrive, the umamusume of white switches her garb to become of umamusume of black, calling the blessed rains upon the cracked earth. It is undeniable that umamusume are just as vital to faith as the kami themselves.

As a shinme, your job was not just to assist in ceremonies or take care of the shrine. You were to act as a conduit through which the kami of the shrine traveled. A gentle reminder on ordinary days, a projection of the descent from heaven to earth in ceremonies. The priests dressed you in white robes with red tassels and walked you through the nearby village, where you blessed fields, scattered blessed water, and were cleansed with salt amidst much chanting and singing.

"The festivals were awesome. After I was done with all the walking around, I got to throw off the robes, run around town and visit as many stalls as I wanted. The old grandpas and grannies were nice to me. They let me play some games for free. I shot so many targets with the toy rifle. The soba was handmade and mixed with the best sauce." You say, and sigh dreamily. "It was to die for."

"My, Tracen has competition. I'll be sure to let the stallholders know you're coming to inspect this fall." Grass Wonder remarks. "It sounds like a fun day.

You wave your hand. "Oh no. No, no, no. It was just the afternoon."

"Goodness, the procession's that long?"

"Yeah. Super, super long. When the shrine says they'll cover the whole village, they mean it down to the last field. There was lots of backtracking, which meant we started early to make sure we covered the whole countryside."

"As in…"

"Five in the morning."

Grass Wonder looks taken aback. "I thought you said were an apprentice."

"I was. There weren't any other permanent umamusume around the village. I had to fill in the shinme role."

Grass Wonder frowns. "I hope they didn't tire you out so much. All that walking around at dawn as a child…"

You shrug. "I did these rites when they were like eight or nine. It wasn't bad. I got used to them after half a dozen. Keeping the rest of the festival in mind always helped, and I got to use the material from the rites in my umadol work. It could have been worse."

Grass Wonder taps on her phone. Her notes. She's been quietly jotting down your answers throughout this conversation. "And what about running? Did you ever get a chance to exercise as a child? I'm curious as to how much of a foundation you built as a child."

"The shinme don't run." You answer.

Grass Wonder's finger hovers above the screen. She lifts her head slowly. "Really?"

"I didn't." You reply.

"You said the shinme are modelled after mythical umas, yes? Emperor Jimmu trained his umamusume empress, and she ran across the fields in many battles. I assumed the shrine would have tried to replicate that."

You shrug. You do it again. There's a lull as you scramble to find the appropriate words. It's one that Grass Wonder notices and begins to narrow her eyes.

"Well…back in the countryside, far away from the government and stuff—all those donations had to go to fixing the shrine and buying food and clothes for the caretakers and me. There weren't any racecourses nearby, either."

"Surely, you had at least one empty field in the countryside."

"I didn't have good running shoes."

"Neither did Oguri Cap." Grass Wonder counters. "I heard she almost tore her old ones to bits."

"If a shinme gets injured, that's considered bad fortune and an offence to the kami. Nope, the head miko didn't want me running around into some ditch in the forest. She was super strict. That's how a miko lives!"

Your chuckle rings hollow. A bell with an underside too large. There's another reason. Of course there is. You don't like dwelling on it, and you refuse to say it out loud, because it's like a demon's name from the West. The moment you say it, it will lodge itself in your mind. You will spiral down that dark descent of dreadful thoughts. This interview has lurched sideways. There's a rapid knock on a door in your mind. Trying to forget it won't work, for abstinence deepens temptation. Your mind will devour itself first.

Telling Grass Wonder isn't necessary. She has figured it out. She's staring at you, genuinely at a loss for words.

[Composure check: 50/55 -> Failed.]

"But who cares about that? I made it to the city. I'm in Tracen now." You exclaim. You stand up and flex your legs. "I can run as much as I want!"

"Yes. Yes, you are, Ruby. A proper Tracen student." Grass Wonder says. She stands up too. The excitement she radiated has been replaced by a steely coolness. "Running is your absolute right."

Is that…a touch of fury in her tone? It's gone in a flicker.

"Go for another jog, Ruby," Grass Wonder advances to you. She pats you on the shoulder and lets her touch linger there for a brief moment. "We'll take our time with this one."

[Grass Wonder's Social Link has increased to Level 2. Effect: +1 to all Acceleration gains outside of LEVEL UPs.]

>>[Event 3] Dancing.

Noon, April 20th, 20XX

"Let's dance." You announce.

"Huh?" Pelte growls. "You kidding me? You wanna waste our boss's time on—"

Meisho Tabaru lifts her hand, silencing her underling. She lifts a piece of vegetable in her udon with chopsticks and shoves it in her mouth. The chewing is soft. She swallows it with an audible gulp.

"Is that a challenge?" She asks.

You grin and scoot closer. "You won the Hokkaido regionals."

"I did."

"You performed the winning live in front of thousands."

"And?"

You hiss the words with exhilaration. "Show me."

Tabaru holds her gaze. She reaches down with her chopsticks and slurps up more noodles. Her twintails cascade as she tilts her neck back to swallow the lot.

"It's your funeral." She states, wiping her mouth.

You only grin wider, a fire stoked in your heart. Electricity flies between the two of you. It's unbreakable. None of the underlings dare to object.

The stage is set. Not the outdoors one—that's booked. Four in the afternoon, you and Tabaru and the rest head to one of the common dance rooms for a round of indoor practice. The smell of polish that hits you is like a big welcome hug. Firm floorboards, an entire wall of full-sized mirrors, and a stereo system that connects to any electronic device without buffering for an eternity. There's no rent. It's perfection.

Why are you not challenging your roommate to a race? Because you've already run alongside her enough in the morning. Tabaru is a front-runner. She loves bursting forth out of nowhere and zooming past her competition. There's not much else you can learn from her, scrimmage or not. Both of you are working on your trump cards for the try-outs and will definitely not reveal them in front of each other. So, dancing it is.

Now, after every race, the umamusume participants get on stage and a dance routine called the Winning Live. The style varies; the Japanese tend towards pop, Americans rock it out, Mongolians throat-sing. What surpasses borders is the runners going up on stage sweaty and tired and maybe with their hearts shattered, yet they do it anyway. This has a rich tradition in—who cares? Right, but the effect this has on the industry is—shut up!

Umamusume don't need a reason to move their bodies. They are creatures that dream on their feet. If they can, they will.

The 'competition' starts off innocuously enough. Five-star rating. The first one to win five sets wins. But what's this? The audience is biased towards one Meisho Tabaru. They don't need to be paid off by the URA. They'll rig the results themselves. Tabaru could accept this fake victory. She doesn't. What a stern talking-to she gives Duo Pelte and the rest. Look at those hands on those hips, that intense glare. One look and they fold.

In hindsight, this was a crap idea. Art is a matter of taste. No, you are not necessarily calling your ondo dances superior to Tabaru's breakdancing. You're saying that if you were to place this competition in front of a panel of qualified judges, they'd side with you. Totally. Definitely. You are not upset.

"What now?" Tabaru asks after she finishes giving her underlings the business. Tight-lipped as ever.

An idea crosses your mind in a flash. Taste is subjective. Time is not. Slam down that UNLIMITED IMPACT and get into position. You'll ad-lib these moves. Ready, steady…

[Dancing check: 80/60 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

"I can't!" Jewel wails.

You bark out laughter, fingers twirling, hair swaying as you sidestep back and forth. "C'mon, Jewel! Put those hands up! Don't bend your elbows. They're not right angles. This isn't maths class!"

Jewel moans loudly, sweat pouring down the sides of her hands. Tomoe tries to follow your steps—left step, raise left, hop on the spot—succeeds in crossing her feet and almost crashing to the ground. She pants and sweats and tearfully eyes you.

"You're insane!" Tomoe cries.

"It's regular idol stuff!" You grin cheekily.

"How? Just—how? My legs are on fire! This is impossible!" Tomoe splutters.

You shake your head. "This is regular idol stuff. All the girls back in my unit danced like this for hours! Dancing is one of the few exercises where humans and umamusume are equal!"

Umamusume can run faster than bicycles and lift entire boxes of concrete without breaking a sweat. Following a set of instructions to a beat? That's constrained by dexterity and the song's tempo. No blitzing past the finish line—the audience has to actually see what you're doing.

"Boss…" Pelte seethes through gritted teeth.

Tabaru doesn't answer, at first. She's next to you, performing her own dance that's slower, more thoughtful, where she sways her arms and guides her torso. She doesn't have as fine control over her form like you. Her lithe form trembles with exertion.

"Are you guys saying you're weaker than my human friends?" You crow.

Tabaru whirls around to you, red in the face.

"Like hell I am." She snarls. That intense glare of her burns. "This…isn't over!"

"Then…" You huff a deep breath, shaking a fist. "Bring it on! Feast yourself, I shall shoot through with all my might—"

"You're singing, too?" Tomoe cries.

It's the raising of a flag. Pelte lets out a guttural roar (more of a cat's hiss in your opinion) and forces more vigor back into her steps. Tomoe and Jewel begrudgingly follow. They line up and stop flailing about. You laugh and continue spinning, sliding, bouncing amidst the curvature and rhythm of your musculature. It is joy incarnate.

By the end, the five of you are slumped over against the mirror and the ground, sweating enough to soak a dozen towels. You call it a rousing success. It was fantastic to do better than your peers for a change!

[Everyone danced umazingly!]

[Classroom Learner: Exists.]

[Dancing has increased by 3.]

>>[Event 4] You will gain more time.

Morning, April 27th, 20XX

Your fortune states you will gain more time. Not in a literal sense, obviously. You don't have magic. No, what this fortune means is that your mundane matters will wrap up faster, allowing you to spend more time on what's important. You tuck the fortune slip in your tracksuit pocket with a huff of satisfaction. A solid result.

[+1 AP for the next LEVEL UP only.]

The umamusume next to you is not so lucky.

"W-w-what do you mean, a massive curse?" The newcomer throws her hands to her head and screeches to the heavens. The fortune slip falls to the floor. "This cannot be possible! M-my long-held summer doll charm and my lucky herb kit said I'd find great luck today—unless the great Shiraoki has abandoned me? Inconceivable!"

Her scream blares in your ears. You wince and stumble back. A rooster in heat has less volume than this girl.

To think she was so fired up before. Rubbing her hands with glee, salivating at the thought of beating you, the avatar of curses and misfortune and whatever, only for fate to shove the middle finger up her nose. Give her a couple more minutes and she'll be slumped over in the fetal position, sucking her thumb. You're torn between consoling her and slowly backing away to leave her alone. The former wins out.

"Um, so…" You hold up a paper slip. "I got a good fortune. That means I'm not a cursed soul, right?"

"I suppose it does. Unless…" This hysteric weirdo narrows her eyes. She points an accusing finger at you. "You arrived here earlier, after all. You could have walked in and sucked all the good fortune out of this shrine and left none for me!"

You fold your arms and fix her a look. A raised eyebrow. No roof tiles detach, fall and cave your skull in.

"…that didn't happen, did it?"

"The door's locked. I don't have the keys."

Her shoulders slump again. "Never mind."

You sigh. "Look, I don't know if my mom did anything to your family—"

"She didn't. I'm being silly again. I…came here hoping things would be better." The hysteric weirdo lets out a whimper. She crashes to the ground and pulls her knees up to her chest. "Oh, Lord Shiraoki, why have you abandoned me in these trying times…"

She's so despondent you can't help but sit down next to her.

"What's your name?" You ask.

"Matikanefukukitaru." The girl replies. "Tracen's one-and-only fortune teller."

Firstly, you've never heard of Tracen having a fortune teller on the web. Secondly, Matikanefukukitaru? That's inane, even by umamusume naming conventions. You're calling her Fukukitaru.

[Psyche check: 9/7 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

There's a lilt in her words. On normal days, she'd shout her title loud and proud. Today, she can barely work herself up. You've been there before.

"Want to talk about it?"

Fukukitaru hesitates, clearly still grappling with relation to the dreaded Opal, then gives a solemn nod. Better than nothing, she supposes. Together, the two of you sit down on the steps. "One of my clients quit."

"Quit? Quit what?" You ask.

"She quit Tracen." Fukukitaru says.

You gasp, "She was expelled?"

"No. She left by herself. Nobody forced her to do anything."

"But why?"

"I don't know!" Fukukitaru cries. She wrings her hands, squeezing her lips tight, before the words spill out. "I don't understand. Last week she was acting preppy and super enthusiastic about her next open. All of a sudden, she comes up to me with all her charms and some money, hands them over to me and bids me farewell. Her cheeks were pale, and there were these enormous bags beneath her eyes. It was as if she hadn't slept in days!"

You find this…

[Instinct check: 30/50 -> Failure.]

…unfortunate, but a normal facet of the racing world. For every winner, there are at least a dozen losers. It's a sobering reminder that you need to keep up your training.

Still, to leave Tracen of her own volition? To put these wonderful facilities and free meals behind? You can't understand. That girl must've lived a privileged life.

"I'm sorry to hear that."

"Thanks." Fukukitaru says, glumly. "I hope she's doing well in whatever happens. I'm sorry for accusing you too."

She perks up a little when you show her your silver bullet. Then, it's back to hopping down the staircase.

Morning, April 31st, 20XX

And that concludes your first month at Tracen. Four straight weeks of backbreaking training and studying, sprinkled with the odd happenstance here and there. It was harrowing at first, but you persisted. You've emerged from the cave of trials fitter and smarter, ready to slay the dragon. The future's looking bright!

2.3: Fuchu Time

>>Oguri Cap

>>Speed

>>An athletics store in town.

EXP: 35/130 (1 LEVEL UP pending...)

Morning, April 30th, 20XX

You're sitting with Grass Wonder on the gym benches one fine afternoon before your life is thrown into disarray.

"Ruby. Do you have any plans for the weekend?"

You pause, half-way guzzling down a bottle of water. You tear it away from your lips, creating a mild pop. "Nope! Just training and homework as usual. Do you have something for me? Marathon push-ups? More deadlifting? Another run against you?" You pump a fist, flexing a bicep now filled with actual muscle, and not the hopes and dreams fueled by late nights of instant ramen and energy drinks. The rush of the intense workout runs hot through your veins. "Give it to me, senpai. I can take on the world with you!"

Grass Wonder just chuckles, composed as ever. "I'm pleased you're so enthusiastic. Sadly, I don't have anything for you."

You blink. "Excuse me?"

"In fact, I have the opposite idea. You should take the whole Saturday off."

It's not as bad as the time when Miki announced she'd start eating meat again, but it's still a shocker. You stare.

"But…" You protest, putting down your water bottle next to your sweaty leg. "Try-outs are happening in a few weeks."

Grass Wonder raises a finger. "Therefore, it's extra important you don't over-exert yourself and let fatigue sink deeper in your core. That's how long-term damage accrues. Let's not mince words: I've been running you like a bloodthirsty hound this past month. You need the rest. Refraining from doing so might cause injuries later down the line."

You nod slowly. Makes sense. She's the expert here. "Then what should I do?"

Grass Wonder hums as she thinks. She glances out the nearby window, towards the direction of the school gates, and the buildings beyond. An idea blooms in her head.

"Have you visited Fuchu recently?"

You shake your head.

"Have you walked around Fuchu at all?"

"Like, a single night where I checked into a coffin motel, then a morning where I had a coffee before enrolling." You reply.

Grass Wonder smiles. She claps her hands. "I think we've found your trip for the weekend."

Morning, May 1st, 20XX

That's how you end up spending the first day of the weekend not in the gym, nor in some quiet corner of the academy library, but rather in the heart of Tracen's very own home city. One quick bus ride from outside the academy entrance, and you're there. Your clothes? A pair of jeans with a stitch down one leg and a blouse whose logo and mauve colors were maximum trendy around five years ago. A simple shirt is thrown beneath the blouse. The three pieces smell fresh with soap—you shoved them in the washing machine, marvelling at how free the washrooms in Tracen are—yet the feel (and mild itch) of their fabric carries a nostalgic tint. Almost strange, after spending so many hours in Tracen's uniform.

You also signed the Miho dorm's leave register at the reception. If you're not back by curfew, there will be consequences.

So, now that you're leaning against a bridge railing in broad daylight, listening to the thrum of traffic below and the gentle hubbub of the weekend crowds, as the gentle spring sunshine laps at your hair and neck and the view in front…what do you know about Fuchu?

[History check: 40/40 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

A little from a spot of research: a quick Internet search followed by a scroll on Umastagram. The city is located in Tokyo's west and serves as a commercial center and commuter town for big-city workers. It was once the capital of the ancient Musashi Province, which encompassed present-day Tokyo, Saitama, and Kanagawa Prefecture. It's home to the shrine of Okunitama, a respectable kami who you might have visited if you were a tourist and not a student. The city's flag is a circle with a seal running through it, and it's famous for its black rice dishes and soba shops. There are museums, scenic routes, wholesale markets, jazz festivals and many other sights perfect for any visitor going off the beaten path. Finally, Tokyo Racecourse is here. That's a big deal.

Fuchu also received a somewhat-recent boost in funding and tourism ever since Tracen Central marked itself as one of the best umamusume academies in the world. The streets become packed whenever there's a graded race on. The city council has invested the increase into fixing up roads and modernizing public facilities such as street lights and drainage systems, which in turn has encouraged more private property investors to develop here. You passed by a skeleton of a shopping mall, draped in tarps and surrounded by steel mesh fences on your way here. There's even talk of building an amusement park. It'll take years, and it won't beat the one in Bunkyo, but the idea is there!

You lean against the railing, breathing in the urban air. Petrol, paper and sugar. Home. Reflective glass windows on a nearby office block shimmer with the view of the clear blue sky above. A nearby poster warns pedestrians to watch their step. This overhang splits in four directions, and down those lanes, more paths branch off, and then again and again, like the roots of a flattened, metal and concrete tree. Calculating the optimal path would require a brain the size of the sun. You're spoiled for choice.

Welp, there's only one thing to do.

Spin the bullet. Yeah!

You take out your trusty charm and give it a whirl. One revolution, two revolutions, three revolutions—north-east! Towards the multi-storied building with colorful banners flying down the front. With a smile and a hop in your step, you walk across the bridge, take the staircase down and your day goes from there. Fuchu is no inner Tokyo, you quickly find. There's no scramble like Shibuya, no glittering lights and bursting side streets of Shinjuku or Ikebukuro. For every modern road or building, there's at least another old-fashioned one. You still find much to enjoy.

You wander down this street and that lane. You buy ice-cream from a vendor and juice from a vending machine and eat them together. You check out the latest records in a music store, spending an hour listening to rock and classic samples on the free headphones, and bemoan the presence of the latest pop sludge on the top of the markets and not the actually unique Eurobeat track made with love and care. When the stench of gas fumes gets too much for you, you find a nice park to plonk yourself down and watch the trees and ducks.

You even take a few photos for your Umastagram account.

Taking a break from all the hard exercise. Now strolling around Tokyo…hope I can find a yummy place to eat

#fuchu #tokyo #exploring #tracenstudentweekends

>hsj_san (11 sec): fucking WHORE your mom was a WHORE

>tripleterror (40 sec): heard the ramen on keio is good

>oshiiiiimasta (1m 10 sec): cute cute CUTE

>kaedekunofficial (2m 15 sec): Ooh, is that muscle I see? Miki's gonna wanna arm wrestle you again

[Social Media check: 52/35 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

It came out well, if you do say so yourself.

Best of all, hardly anyone pays you attention on the streets. In Tracen, you are the daughter of Satono Opal the heretic. Whispers surround you. Teachers and students linger their gaze on you for seconds longer, their wonder if you'll end up breaking the rules like your mother as obvious as a red sore. Out on the streets, no-one cares. The crowds are full of teenagers, parents, bakers, train station attendants and a hundred different other palettes of lives. Not everyone is attuned to the racing scene.

It's a nice change of pace. Grass Wonder was right. You did need this break.

A quarter to noon, you feel your stomach fidgeting and head to a nearby mall. It's not quite lunchtime yet, so you end up strolling around the floors, window-shopping for clothes and cosmetics. You stumble across an athletics store in the center. My Big Body! The header proudly says, its mascot of a cartoonish tanned umamusume twirling a basketball. You recognise the colors as the striking sort from American comic books. We've got sports for all sorts!

[Artistry check: 52/30 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

As an up-and-coming Tracen student, you are drawn to the store like a moth to a flame.

Bright crisp lighting shines down as you enter. Upbeat rock plays from an invisible radio. You poke your nose between the wide lanes of tables and display racks, grinning with wonder and mild envy. They've got human and umamusume mannequins wearing the latest running gear; an entire shelf dedicated to shoes radiating that fresh smell; racks of T-shirts, pants and hoodies that you'd squeal if you won one of them in a raffle; and an entire area styled after a modern pantry, with fridges stocked with energy drinks and fresh carrots.

Advertisements are hung on the walls. They're the modern kind with those flat-screen televisions. You spot the figure of an umamusume with short brown hair doing the peace sign floating up. Her racing uniform is a regal, military-inspired sort, with blue-white colors and a single gold epaulette. It's as imposing as it is adorable.

Road to the invincible! The banner beneath the photo says. My legend is just getting started!

Your memory jogs. Right! This is Tokai Teio. She promised the world she'd win the Triple Crown this year and began by winning the Satsuki Sho a few weeks ago. You were busy exercising on that day and had to watch the replay on your phone afterwards. What an amazing scramble to the finish that was! Ah, if only you could be so fast one day. It'd be so lovely to win even a G3 and hear those cheers and perform the winning live…

"Oh, it's you."

A sudden voice. A sudden presence. It smashes your joyful daydreaming with a sledgehammer, a blue flame smouldering from the ashes. The color is colder than ice, yet it burns raw hot. Gulping once, you turn around slowly and carefully.

"Oguri—"

She whips out a finger and presses it against your lips.

"Shh…"

You splutter, pulling your head back. "Wha—"

"Call me mysterious Uma X." Oguri Cap says.

"Excuse me?"

"Mrs. Uma X." Oguri Cap pauses. "Hang on, I'm not married yet. Ms. Uma X, then."

"Why?" You ask.

Oguri Cap, dressed in a strangely familiar flat cap, a plain pale brown coat and a pair of sunglasses, glances around the store. "Public still recognises me. I'm trying to remain incognito today."

[Sneak check: 43/20 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

She's not doing a good job, you think, as you follow her. The human clerk is frantically typing away on her phone while sneaking glances in Oguri's direction. She won't bother Oguri—no-one wants to be the guy or gal who ends up being accused of being the nosy paparazzi type—but you can see the incoming Umatter and Umastagram posts in your mind's eye. You think about telling Oguri this. She stares back firmly, and you reconsider.

"Alright. You got it Og—Miss X. Good to see you…for the first or second time, whatever suits you." You say, giving her a slightly nervous smile. "So, what's up?"

"Walking around. Enjoying the sunshine, alone. All my other friends are off busy preparing for the Taurus Cup."

That's from the Dream Trophy league. Umamusume who achieve well in the Twinkle Series circuit go there. The races are not as prestigious, and the identities and levels of contestants varies each year, resulting in a swathe of mixed bags when it comes to content. It's still a fun watch.

"I'm planning on eating lunch later." Oguri says. She takes a strip of dried carrot from a bag and bites into it. "You?"

"Same as you. Just enjoying my weekend. I…" don't have as many friends you finish in your head. No, you can't say that. It's killing the mood.

"…thought it'd be best to take a look around Fuchu, since I'm going to be essentially living here for the next few years."

"Smart idea." Oguri says.

"Some of my classmates are from Fuchu. I thought it might help build rapport." You shrug.

"Tracen also does charity events and promotions. Always good to give back to your roots." Oguri holds out the bag. "You want one?"

"Sure!" You take the snack. It's crunchy and slightly sweet. Delicious. "Did you ever meet with Grass again?"

"Again? Oh, you mean from the day you first came here." Oguri thinks for a second. "We've bumped shoulders a couple of times in the hall. We haven't had the chance to rematch yet. It's a real shame. I'd love to jump into a practice run with her or the rest of Rigil."

"She's been training me."

"I've heard."

"It's been hard. Super hard. I've been broken down and remade like those statues sculpted by Renaissance artists." You grin. "But she must be pleased, because she gave me a day off."

"You're pleased."

"Grass is a good teacher. I mean, she did win a G1. Short of getting an actual Trainer, she's the best I have. Thanks to her, I'm more confident about the try-outs now."

"Rudolf wouldn't pick someone stupid." Oguri states.

You nod. "Right."

"You were in the good hands the moment she chose you and Grass. Maybe slightly late—we could have used a program like that back in my peak—but things were different back then. The Prez used to be scary. The pressure was immense. Less people around, too."

"Miss X ran with the likes of Super Creek and Tamamo Cross?" You grin cheekily.

"Yep. And she was better than all of them." Oguri says, with the type of ironclad, blank-faced confidence that makes casinos weep. She stares down towards your feet.

"Are those comfortable?"

"Eh?"

It turns out Oguri Cap likes shoes. Or, to be more accurate, her long-time friend from the sports science division, who served as her assistant during Oguri's Twinkle Series career, was born, molded and forged in the sports equipment lifestyle and so passed down her passion onto Oguri like a samurai clan's teachings, or an infectious virus. She guides you around the shelves until she finds the row that fits your size.

She lifts a sample off the shelf, and you imagine her wearing a teacher's cap with a whiteboard pointer in her free hand.

"Shoes are like car engines." Oguri says.

"Do you know anything about cars?" You ask.

"I survived Maruzensky's ride. Twice." Oguri smirks. You can't help but clap. That's outstanding. No sarcasm about it.

"Are you going to tell me shoes actually have oil and wires?"

"No, but they're complex machines all the same." Oguri looks a little affronted at your joke. She clears her throat. "Shoes look familiar on the surface. We put them on every morning, think little of the way we tie our shoelaces, and assume they'll work the same each day. They're wrong. On the track, even the most minute details, such as a minor hint of discomfort, can determine the deciding factor between victory and loss."

[(Traversal check -> 32/35 || Wits check -> 9/7): Success! +5 EXP.]

"Because the wearer places their focus on that discomfort and loses a quarter of a second of precious spurting time?"

"Correct. Or they'll slide too far around a corner because the lugs aren't strong enough. Think of purchasing a new shoe as a decision triangle of fit, cushioning and traction. None of them will be perfect, but you better get a pair with as best of the three corners as possible. That means doing your homework.

"You're so right, Miss X-sensei."

"Whenever I see a kid who tears off her shoes uselessly, I weep."

She sounds so dramatic. And yet so serious. Is she re-enacting a scene from a movie? Or, you ponder, if she planning on becoming a teacher at Tracen? This lecture would be practice, then. The Ashen Beast herself as a private athletic tutor…she'd be drowning in so much cash her bank account might explode.

"Ruby. Do you have a good pair of shoes?" Oguri asks.

You just smile. "I do. They fit me very well. They don't slip or skid, and I can run forever in them. They're the best pair I could ever ask for."

"Good. Because if you don't, just ask the academy staff. They have backup shoes. They won't be as familiar as yours, and they won't carry whatever faith or trust you've placed in them, but they are there." Oguri says. "Once you get your Trainer, you can ask him or her for any pairs of shoes and they'll have to pay out of their own pockets. It's their duty."

You hear distant wailing beyond the store music. You're not sure why.

Oguri then drags you around the store in what is either her working off her boredom or an expansion of her impromptu shoes lesson. The amount of budget Tracen grants you is limited. A majority of the products in the store are marketed towards the average human and umamusume, brimming with flashiness over function, and are therefore unsuited towards the elite runners you will hopefully be one day. You still learn a few tips. Oguri tells you which shirts and pants are suited for quick switches between leisurely walks and brief jogging sessions. She asks the clerk for sample cleats, then helps you compare them to the feet, followed by informing you which brands are trustworthy or trash. She then takes you to the food and health section.

"No. Bad Ruby."

"It's just an energy drink."

Oguri carefully prises the can out of your grip and places it back in the fridge. "Energy drinks are terrible."

"But I drank them all the time as a umadol—"

"Look at that sugar. Those sweeteners. Look at those banned additives."

"Those exist?"

"You can get kicked out of the race if you drink too much of them!" Oguri exclaims. That shuts you up. She keeps lecturing you. "They're not even good for you in the first place. You want caffeine? You drink matcha, have tea, even a coffee is better. You don't eat mass-produced protein powder; you eat tuna and chicken. All natural, all the time, starting with those fresh carrots over there. That's how I won my G1s!"

Trust Tracen's glutton to be so hyped about nutrition…

Oguri plucks a malt-based breakfast drink off a shelf and presses you to try it. True to her word, it doesn't contain any of those nasty additives. It's all-natural protein and plant-based nutrition. The only artificial component is some vitamin powder. The white-haired umamusume on the label is attractive, in a refined beauty sense. You have no idea who this is.

"You don't know Folkqueen? Even though she won the Japan Cup? Impossible…" Oguri lifts her hand to her forehead, muttering with what you assume is now horror. "Am I…turning into Maruzensky?"

[Nutrition has increased by 2.]

To placate her, you collect a six-pack of that milk drink and promise to drink them at some point. Lastly, you consider purchasing a bag of carrots. Very few umamusume troubles cannot be solved with a fresh carrot in your pocket. Oguri sniffs one and gives the thumbs-up. They are indeed fresh. As you open the fridge and begin sifting through the available stock, a pair of voices float down from the store's front.

"Hey, is that place new?"

"I think it is. Didn't there used to be a coffee shop over this way?"

"Want to go in and take a look?"

"Why not?"

"Wow, it looks brand new! So much variety here. They've even got the new Pallas sneakers!"

They sound young, their chatter audible over the shop's radio. You don't pay them much mind. Neither does Oguri.

[Instinct check: 30/35 -> Failure.]

The two of you select fresh carrots and place them in a bag. You get a box of tea powder that supposedly helps bone growth, then investigate the yoghurt section. The energy drinks remain alone and unwanted in the fridge. By the time you're done, the two unknowns are closer. Their voices are louder.

"Hey, check it out! There's a step counter that measures based on your heart rate. It's even got barometric functions. This'll be great when we train at summer camp."

"Let me see…oh my. You're right."

"There're tons of mountain walks up there. We'll be so efficient on our jogs. Technology sure is amazing these days."

"Now, now, Kita, we must not spend worthlessly on trinkets. The simplest method is usually the best."

"That's rich coming from you. Literally. Wait, did I just pun you?"

"You did."

"I did!"

"You're so silly!"

"It was good, wasn't it?"

"I don't think Teio would be appreciative of that."

"What? Say it isn't so!"

That voice, the calmer one, has a polished accent. A delicate, genteel voice, with crisp diction and more formal words. It sounds familiar.

Your tail goes stiff. Sweat beads on your forehead. Oguri doesn't notice a single thing.

"You are not buying that!"

"I'm tempted to."

"C'mon, just because it has McQueen on it…"

"Why you—you're the one who started drooling over that bottle with Teio on it!"

"It's not just merch. It's legitimately a good water battle! You're just jealous, Dia!"

"You should bring it the next time you visit Spica HQ and see how she reacts."

"Wait, wait, but that'll be—nooo!"

Dia. D-I-A…M—

No.

—O—

No, no, no.

Don't come this way. Go somewhere else.

"Ooh, a third-off on carrots. Let's go and grab some!"

A terrible tightness constricts your ribs. Its breath chokes in its throat. It must have been audible, because Oguri swivels her head, worry creasing her brow, but you ignore her. You're already swinging your bag around, rushing in the direction of the store counter. You pray that these two feet have the sheer dexterity to squeeze between these shelves in the span of less than a second, before these two umamusume arrive and meet you face to face.

[Dodge check: 65/85 -> Failure.]

They do not. You are too late. You should have left a whole minute ago.

"Excuse me, may we—"

You skid to a halt, stopping less than a meter in front of the girl. Her words die in her throat.

Light brown hair against your pitch-black. An emerald-green dress woven from fine silk, its shoulder and neckline white ribbons worth more than your entire outfit and shopping combined. A blue-gemstoned cuff shines with pristine polish atop her right ear; the notches on your miniature crown must deepen at the sight. These are not impossible sights, perhaps not even unusual if you visited Harajuku, and you cling to the faint hope that this person is just another stranger who heard your mother's reputation and will brush past you with scorn and disdain. But, as if to insult you, to degrade you, to reveal the ineptitude of your entire efforts today and tomorrow, you see that white diamond mark atop her bangs, glaring straight into the depths of what makes up you.

There is no mistaking this girl. She is Satono Diamond, heiress to the Satono conglomerate, and your estranged sister.

The two of you stare at each other. Her eyes are wide, and her mouth is tight. Your tongue is frozen to the roof of your mouth. Your breath comes in ragged gasps. One, two, one two. Each one is the beat of a drum.

"Hey, Dia? What's going on? Who's blocking the way?"

Her friend approaches. Shoulder-length black hair, styled in a bob cut with bangs. A red rope tied into a ribbon hangs from her right ear. Her left ear, a pink flower. Her outfit is more casual, more middle-class than Diamond's. She's wearing a blue jacket with a white top half and a pair of yellow shorts. She freezes, mouth dropping open when she sees you.

You saw her photo in an Umastagram post, once. She wore her uniform then. Kitasan Black, the favored rookie of the year, and Satono Diamond's most trusted friend. She, too, can only stare.

Dead silence reigns.

You should move. Twitch a finger. Bow your neck. Lift your leg, land your foot on the ground, larynx forming the words to politely exit. Twist your body around and talk about garbage with Oguri right next to you. Nothing's happening. The gears in your brain jam. They clank against each other fruitlessly. Pitiful sparks fly towards the surface.

"Ruby! Let's go and play!"

"Ruby! Crown sneaked out these secret choccies for us. Don't tell your Mama, okay?"

"I beat you again, Ruby! Guess I'm gonna break the family curse before you, ehehe…"

The sparks are bright. They illuminate long-forgotten photographs and sheets of paper. They ignite the tinder and burn you up from within.

"Ruby…why do all the grown-ups look so angry at you? Did you do something wrong?"

"Papa said I can't have lessons with you. It's—I don't understand! Ruby, if you really did something bad, you should apologise! Promise me. Crown, too!"

"Ruby…it can't be true? Your Mama, she…she hurt those other runners? She ruined their shoes, too?"

[World Resonance check: 55/55 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

The tarp on the trapdoor. Burned away. The hinges creak open. And, back then, when the shrine was abandoned beneath the mountain, when you scrounged pocket change to stay another night at the coffin motel, there was a lane of upper-class shops, the concrete smelling fresh from a recent downpour, a limo was parked on the street, its door opening

"Do I know you?"

"I…"

"Is there something you need? Are you cold?"

"We have."

"So you are cold. Um, here, take this change for a nice, hot meal."

"No! I mean, we've met before. It's me."

"I'm sorry, I don't think we've met."

"I'm…I'm your sister. My name is Ruby. Do you remember me?"

Blank-facedness morphing into shock and fear and then something you don't see because black-suited bodyguards hustle her back into her seat and the door slams shut and the engine spits petrol and gas in your dirty face and you can't find her in the rear-view mirror—

"Ruby."

"Diamond." You rasp.

Satono Diamond clasps her arms in front of her. She straights her back, looks you in the eye. Every last drop of levity and warmth and anything good and kind about her has vanished, replaced with a frigid cordiality.

"I didn't expect to see you here." She says.

[Total EXP gained: 40.]

EXP: 75/130 (1 LEVEL UP pending...)

(What will you do?)

[] Hug her.

[] Attempt to smile.

[] Glare at her.

[] Hit her.

[] Offer a carrot.

[] Do nothing.

[] Leave. Just leave.

[] Ask Oguri for help.

[] Write-in.
