2.4: Satono

>>Offer a carrot.

EXP: 75/130 (1 LEVEL UP pending...)

Mood: Normal

"I never expected to see you here," Satono Diamond, your long-estranged sister-cousin says, and the sole voice that rings in your head is a simple neither did I.

[Composure check: 50/60 -> Failure.]

The last time you saw Diamond was not on that moist, summer-scorched street, nor within the sprawling halls of the Satono family mansion. It was in Tracen, a week or so post-enrollment. Maths class had finished, and you were pushing and shoving your way through a hallway teeming with other students, when you saw Diamond and Crown pop around a corner. They strolled down the hallway on the other side of the building, parallel to your own. They chatted and giggled with each other and wore casual smiles.

They were distant, barely visible amidst the sea of lilac and white uniforms, yet your heart was struck. You stopped. You watched. Crown pulled a card or a piece of paper out of her sleeve with a flourish, so dazzling in its execution it made Diamond clap and titter. Her lips moved in praise. The crowd's chatter dimmed, drowned out in hazy mush, and in your ears you heard the echo of Crown's younger self. Hands on her hips, chest puffed out, promising to be taller, faster and stronger than anyone in the entire world.

You wondered if she had achieved that, as you saw Crown's shiny skin, that slender physique, and eyes that looked straight at challengers with confidence. Except at you. Not you. Never at you.

An urge gripped you. Run up to them and grab Crown's wrist before they vanished like an apparition. Let them know Satono Ruby was alive, and that she existed. It was a fleeting thought. The fear of retaliation and the memory of that limousine speeding away, leaving your dirty past self to choke on exhaust fumes—they halted your feet. Diamond and Crown crossed down the hallway, and the rest of the crowd swallowed their presences up. It was a relief. It was agony.

You were older now. More confident, more accomplished—to a degree. Tracen is neutral ground. You could have said something that could have brought the three of you together.

Such were your hopes. Now? It's as if fate is testing you.

You think you might be failing.

"Excuse me." Someone speaks to you. The person next to Diamond. Her name is Kitasan Black, and she's wearing a grimace. "You're Satono Ruby, right? Did you hear what my friend said?"

"I…uh…" You stutter. A bead of sweat collects itself at the back of your neck. More follow.

Hi there, Kitasan Black. Nice to meet you. I liked your shoes on your promo poster. May I mention that I am so not ready for this?

You want to flee into the depths of the mall. You want to hug Diamond until your arms strain. You want to grab her by the collar and demand with shouts and maybe a few tears why she left you in the dust on that day two years ago. And you have no clue how she'd react to any of this, because she gazes at you with that mask of politeness, an icy composure that numbs and slips off any of your usual feelers. She's true to her namesake—a brilliant sight to the eyes, and more impenetrable than steel.

You've always taken pride in knowing how to talk. It was one of your selling points as an umadol. Look at a person, figure them out, and then chat them up. Talk about their hairstyle, the ring on their finger, the coffee cup in their hands—anything, and lead from there. The issue with that is that you need a basic understanding, to interpret a thousand words of backstory from posture and appearance alone; and you had that with the common folk of Shibuya and Shinjuku and more through immersion and osmosis. Regular umadol work, waitressing, side jobs in the motels gave you a lot of talk about.

Not with Diamond, nor Crown, nor their parents and family members. Your world is as far from theirs as Earth is from Mars.

You're caught in a web of indecision. It's frightening.

A nudge in your side. It's sharp and pointed. It's Oguri, her blue eyes flickering to meet yours. She reaches out with her hand and squeezes you on the shoulder. It's a gentle reassurance. Your hand flies to your collar, where your lucky silver bullet nestles beneath the cloth. You feel its familiar grooves beneath the fabric, and it settles your beating heart just enough to let sense blow back into your brain and fall back onto the absolute basics.

Satono Ruby: Tracen student, former underground umadol, member of society and a young girl accompanying the legendary Oguri Cap in disguise. Blend them together, and you have absolutely no clue what flavor this smoothie tastes, except that you must, at the very least, try.

You take out one of the fresh carrots from its plastic bag and hold it out. Diamond and Kitasan stare at the carrot. It's long as a school ruler, colored bright orange, and it smells of the earth. You force your lips into an approachable smile.

"You…want one?"

This is an offering of food. It is a universal sign of good faith and humility among most cultures, Japanese included.

"You haven't paid for that." Kitasan states.

And it's treated as well as an earthworm in a lettuce salad.

"Oh."

"We can't eat from the store. It'd be stealing."

You once heard Kitasan's voice in an online interview. She was peppy, cheery. She rambled about how much she looked up to Tokai Teio in Team Spica, acting as if she was about to jump out of her skin with excitement. Hearing that same voice, now flat with annoyance and a hint of accusation, is disconcerting.

She's right. You can't go around eating groceries off the shelves. At least not in these brand stores. These aren't the countryside markets run by old grandpas and grannies who don't mind if you take a bite, as long as you pay for it afterwards.

"It's a recommendation. A recommendation! Sorry, sorry! I was so caught up in how fresh these carrots smell I forgot I hadn't bought them yet. Happens to everyone, right?" You clear your throat. "They're good. Super good. Almost as good as Tracen's home-grown ones, honest."

"That's…a boast and a half." Kitasan remarks.

"Try it and find out!" You exclaim, and press the carrot forward. With a few more gestures, Kitasan folds. She tentatively reaches out and takes the vegetable. She does not break eye contact with you the entire time.

"If I'm wrong, I'll swallow my own cleats." You say and wink.

[Persuasion check: 80/40 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

Kitasan sniffs the carrot. Her eyes widen in surprise. Her ears twitch. She doesn't smile, but two out of three isn't bad. It's affirmation. You've made a sale…is what you would say if you were working here.

Diamond isn't reacting. That's okay. She must be caught with surprise, too. You're still in the game.

"O—I mean, Miss Uma X over here thinks so." And you gesture to your partner.

"Miss Uma X?" Kitasan echoes.

Oguri raises her hand. "I'm Mysterious Uma X."

"She helped me pick out the carrots." You add. "They're on special, too."

"Uh-huh…" Kitasan says, squinting at your partner.

"We were going to buy a bunch together. Yogurt and tea, too!" You say, opening your bags for a view.

Diamond and Kitasan ignore you. They examine Oguri instead. She tilts her head. They spot her trademark headband peeking out beneath her obviously borrowed flat cap, those unique silver locks, and come to the same conclusion as you did.

"No," Kitasan begins, raising a finger. "I'm pretty sure that's—"

"Mysterious Uma X." Oguri repeats.

"She's not mysterious, she—"

"I am. I am a mysterious umamusume from a mysterious part of Tokyo, therefore my name is Mysterious Uma X. That is my identity, and I'd like you to respect that." Oguri takes a step forward. It thumps audibly on the enamel floor. She looks down at Kitasan, her neck bent at an angle to stare the younger umamusume down. That aura of searing-hot fire wraps around her form for a second, as Kitasan gulps. "You got that?"

Kitasan retreats. She holds up a hand. "Whatever you say, miss."

That's not an admission of Oguri's disguise. It's her being unwilling to start a fight over something so trivial. The truth still holds. Oguri Cap couldn't bluff her way through a shopping mall if her life depended on it.

"We weren't following you two, by the way."

Oguri says this so abruptly, it clocks the three of you off guard. Eyes go wide. Tails cease to swish. You jerk your head around, mouthing the word what?

"Following? Hey! C'mon, Dia and I aren't not accusing either of you of anything." Kitasan blusters.

"No, you do." Oguri says.

"You can't just say that!"

"You've got the look of someone wondering what we're doing here and if we're about to do anything with you. I don't like that kind of behaviour. I think it's too sneaky, too paranoid. This is an athletics shop, not the locker rooms." Oguri continues. She folds her arms. "I will tell you this first up: my meeting Ruby here was also a coincidence. I was walking around the mall, looking for snacks, when I spotted her in the store thinking of buying something as terrible as an energy drink for her exercises. As her senpai, I just had to help her."

"With her shopping." Diamond speaks up. It's her first word in this entire conversation, barring the opening.

"I'm gonna take her to look at cleats again." Oguri says.

"And is that all?"

"What does it look like to you?"

"I believe it seems like the two of you are good friends."

Oguri glances your way, then back at Diamond. She gives a deliberate shrug. "You're not my mom."

A hint of steel in Oguri's tone. It's almost cold. It's threatening. Kitasan moves instinctively, now a step in front of her friend, her stance growing firm. Half of her left shoulder covers half of Diamond's right.

You grip your bags tighter in your hands. An argument is brewing. This is the Satono heiress Oguri is speaking back to. She's not a political player like Rudolf, or the Tracen Academy administration. There are consequences that come with offending a conglomerate with its hands in so many pies of Japan's industry.

You're relieved she's speaking up on your behalf. Not many people have done that. You still have to put out this fire before it spreads.

"Come on, everyone." You say, voice going shaky. "It's not a big deal. We shouldn't be fighting in public like this. We're all Tracen students, right? It'd look bad on the academy. Miss Uma X was telling me how the Prez used to be totally scary back in her day. We don't want to wake that side of her up, right? I think people are watching."

The clerk at the counter has her phone out. A human man in a baseball cap is side-eying this exchange while pretending to browse through a rack of logo'd T-shirts. The stage is ripe for a PR disaster with a sprinkling of bad Umatter tweets.

"Dia, people are…" Kitasan nudges her friend on the shoulder. "Maybe we should go. Forget about Ruby here."

"You can," Diamond says.

"Pardon?"

Diamond folds her arms. She looks at you. "I want to talk to Ruby here."

Oguri blinks. Kitasan gapes. You take a moment to comprehend what you just heard, because think you might be dreaming.

"Eh?" Kitasan gasps. "But, Miss Akiko said—"

Diamond raises her hand. It's small, yet the fingers are slender. A piano player's fingers. "I know what she said."

"You're still going to do it?" Kitasan objects.

"We're fellow Tracen students, like Ruby said. There shouldn't be an issue with meeting together in public." Diamond says. "In fact, one might call this meeting fate."

Kitasan gives up at that, grimacing as she shrinks back. You're replaying Diamond's words over and over in your head in an attempt to detect any mistakes. Diamond wants to talk to you. Your long-estranged sister wants to talk to you!

Hold on, the logical side of your brain chooses this moment to speak up. Aren't you forgetting something. Diamond's the heiress, yet this Akiko has authority over her. It's not an umamusume name, so she's either an aunt from the human side of her parentage, a high-ranking servant, a private tutor, or perhaps a future trainer. She means business, considering Kitasan is wary of her, and Diamond had to judge whether to go against her. The fact Diamond spent the past few minutes ignoring you, yet suddenly wants to 'catch up'? Sounds suspect. It's not exactly an invitation to sit on the tatami mat and exchange tea and snacks.

Rudolf never officially stated which party tried to prevent your enrollment at Tracen. You'd need to axe most of your brain cells to deny the truth. Only one family in the whole of Japan treats Satono Opal and her daughter as complete persona non grata.

['Hope' chosen for Life.]

But, you can't help yourself, can't stop the swell of hope pulsating in tune with your heartbeat. The olive branch brandishes its leaves. There's a chance that Diamond doesn't hate you, and by God, you're seizing it before it vanishes into the ether.

"Okay! Lead the way, Diamond!" You exclaim.

"Follow me, then." She says, and turns around. Kitasan gives you a wary look, then skips ahead to join her friend at the front. You make a move to follow.

"You know." Oguri says, loudly and with a grunt from her throat. "There's a nice steak place a few blocks down. The line might take some time. The beef inside is so worth it."

"They haven't banned you?" You ask shakily, and perhaps a little hysterically.

Oguri digs into her jacket and pulls out her phone. It's an old flip model. A technological dinosaur. "I have contacts. American and New Zealand ones."

You're unsure how foreigners relate to this, but you understand. This is Oguri giving you an excuse to skedaddle, to back out. It's sweet of her to offer.

"I'll be fine." You say. "I want to catch up with Diamond too."

You give Oguri a reassuring smile. You hope she believes you.

And you hope you haven't jumped out of the frying pan and into an open furnace.

After FAITHFUL released its first enka album and began to take off in the underground idol scene, Suzuki and Kaede, the two leaders of the group, floated around the idea of preparing the team for whenever the Satonos came knocking. They'd never sell you out—the underground scene doesn't exactly mesh with the corporate and the wealthy—yet the moment your face was revealed on camera, pests gathered in the venues. Hecklers, troublemakers, nosy journalists who said they followed the trail of your mother's misdeeds, even a few who claimed to be Opal's former fans and had to deal with the second-hand disdain and disgust projected by her scandal. It wasn't a stretch to think once enough infamy built up, the proxies or the affiliates of the Satonos might come knocking.

In the end, preparing a counteroffensive PR scheme never took off. The team had gigs to perform. After Suzuki made some calls to his old friends in other undergrounds, while Hotaru began digging up on the Internet, the heckling and investigating ceased. Mostly. FAITHFUL was active in Kabukichō too, as part of Shinjuku's gigs. There are certain idol otaku who wear designer wear and spend their nights at cabaret clubs, who earn alternative sources of income the general public tend to disapprove of. Saya might have nudged a couple of those guys along.

And the Satonos never showed up on FAITHFUL's doorstep. They were just as willing to stay away from you as you were from them. An uneasy, dysfunctional truce.

Standing in the here and now, you're thinking the etiquette training of that PR scheme might've come in handy, because you're currently stuck in what can only be described as a 'coffee palace'.

Crystal chandeliers with dim lighting. Solemn piano music plays in the background. A stained glass window depicting the interior of an European palace stands at the back of the room, surrounded by wooden carvings and wallpapers in the shades of muted browns and beiges that spring to mind old castles in movies and FAITHFUL's original Alice in Evilland shooting sets. You squirm on a velvet-lined sofa that seems tailor-made to wrap around your buttocks and provide as much comfort as possible.

"What will you have, Ruby?" Diamond asks.

"Uh…" You smell coffee and sugar and your head spins.

"Order anything you like," Diamond says, pushing the menu forward. "My treat."

She swept into this miniature palace with you, Kitasan and Oguri in tow, as if she owned the place. That might not be too far from the truth. It'd explain why you weren't kicked out for violating whatever dress code surely exists. It was a shock to learn such a magnificent coffeehouse existed in Fuchu in the first place.

[Logic check: 62/40 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

Then again, the news did say more investment was flowing into the city.

The coffee palace is mostly deserted at this time of the day. Empty chairs, empty tables. The only other occupants are an old couple discussing the papers at the back. Diamond tucked everyone in the corner, as far away from the staircase leading to the second floor as possible. No-one will bother you. They'll have to squint to find you. It's a near-perfect space for a private conversation.

You would've preferred peak hours. Not just because you enjoy chatter over silence. Other customers means a frame of reference on what to order. The assortment of cakes and snacks displayed on the menu is demonic in its appeal. The money-conscious side of your psyche wails.

"I'll have the latte, then." You respond. "A-and maybe the lemon slice?"

Diamond takes the menu back. "Kita?" She asks.

"The carrot cake and the matcha tea." Kitasan replies, leaning over to look. She's in-between your discomfort and Diamond's assuredness. Seated well enough in her spot, she kept glancing around the place with interest. Maybe awe. This isn't her usual environment.

"And you, Miss Uma X?" Diamond continues.

Oguri takes the menu. She flips it open to the desserts page. She places one finger at the top, then runs it down to the bottom whilst looking Diamond dead in the eye.

Diamond doesn't recoil. She takes out a black credit card from her purse and deposits it on the table. Silver-bordered, its center imprinted with the Satono logo, it's a classic businesswoman move. Straight out of a movie. Coupled with the muted lighting, and the sheer confidence Diamond wields it, you can't help but imagine your sister in a business suit and a head taller, seated at the board of directors with a trusty-pen.

The desserts arrive quickly. They continue to arrive as Oguri devours cake after cake without dropping a single crumb. You sip your latte and immediately discover it's better than any you've ever tasted. The freshness of the beans, the silky smoothness of the milk froth…there's a dash of cocoa powder, too! And the lemon slice is baked just crisp enough without being crumbly, the icing giving a zesty tang to the tip of your tongue.

It's good. It's great. Objectively fantastic. Yet, you can't help but compare it with the sandwiches Rudolf gave you. The only extravagance was the miniature fridge Rudolf took them out of. They were fulfilling, despite—or perhaps due to—their simple, grocery-store-bought ingredients. You're just as hungry as you were back then, but this cake you're eating? The sugar cloys your taste buds. It burns as it shifts down your gullet. Will the number of calories disrupt your nutrition plan, too?

It's bad manners to turn down food, so you tuck more of the lemon slice in your mouth and pray you can burn the incoming fat off this afternoon.

[Mood has gone down to Bad.]

Diamond's comfortable. She has no hesitation in taking apart her apple crème brûlée piece by piece, spearing evenly-cut slices on her fork and giving them dainty nibbles.

"So, is there a reason why you chose this spot?" You ask, once everyone has had her fill—and Oguri has gone back for seconds.

"Not particularly. I've just wanted to visit this cafe for a while. Crown recommended it to me, along with a friend of Kita's dad," Diamond says.

"He's…" Kitasan hesitates for a moment. "A family friend of Dia's mom and dad. That's how we got to know each other."

"I'm not exactly swimming in money. I can't pay for this."

"I said it's on me. You don't need to worry about a thing, Ruby." Diamond says. "It's the least I can do for you as my guest."

She smiles as she says this, a demure expression that fits perfectly with her elegance. It's the first one you've seen from her today. You reluctantly tuck away your protests. They still squirm like caterpillars in your throat. Having someone pay for an entire meal when you're now well-fed and well-rested these days doesn't feel correct.

Diamond puts her knife and fork down on her plate. She clasps her hands together in front of her in a thoughtful manner. "How are you, anyway?"

"Fine?" You hazard.

"Just fine?" Diamond presses.

"You want to know more?"

"I'd be delighted to."

"Well…" You begin. "I'm super tired these days from a bunch of extra studying and training. I have to catch up somehow. It's been running me ragged, though it's been fun to learn these new ideas and theories. I'm looking forward to putting them into practice at the upcoming try-outs, as well as meeting my new trainer!"

Your burst of glee rings out. It's swallowed up by the piano playing in the background. Diamond listens, sipping her chamomile tea.

"I see." She says and leaves it at that.

You lean back, noticing you've lurched forward in your chairs, now feeling a flush across your cheeks. Maybe that was too much.

"You?"

"So-so." Diamond replies. "I've been very busy with my family duties."

"Charity, right?"

"Philanthropy." Diamond corrects you, tapping her finger against the tabletop. "We've been opening new schools across Tokyo. I've been out of Tracen for a time to bless some of them at their opening ceremonies. Alongside that, I've been attending formal dinners and business meetings with my parents and the elders of the family."

"Sounds…" You struggle to find the words to respond. "Busy."

"It's very complex. You should see our schedules someday." Diamond says.

"I can't imagine being there with all those stuffy adults."

"Stuffy? I suppose that does apply to their suits sometimes. They're important clientele of ours, and I found opportunity to cross paths with Mejiro McQueen a few times, so that's a plus."

"I've heard of McQueen." Oguri adds. "She's Tokai Teio's rival. She's not bad."

"A truly dignified and respectable racer with the Kikuka Sho under her belt." Diamond says, smiling softly. "She's someone I look up to a great deal."

Oguri shrugs. She bites into a chocolate mousse, speaking around the layers of sugar and fat, before licking up the icing with a slurp. "Like I said, not bad."

That wipes the smile off Diamond's face, and Kitasan shoots Oguri a scandalised look, but Oguri is too busy staring down at her plate, piling candied strawberry on a sort of sandwich-esque pile with some almond biscuits. What follows next can only be described as a mild unhinging of the jaw. Down the glutton's throat it goes. It's washed down with a deep drink of a lemon-lime bitter.

Diamond wrinkles her nose with what can only be disgust. You hurriedly change the topic.

"I guess that schedule doesn't offer much time to relax. Makes sense. Makes a lot of sense." You say to Diamond. "You're still going for the try-outs right?"

"Obviously. She'll be doing them with me," Kitasan says. "We'll be doing them as soon as possible."

"That's great! We might be competing together, then." You ball up a fist and pretend it doesn't feel floppy. "I'm—not going to hold back. I've been training real hard with my student mentor to make up for my shortcomings."

"Very well." Diamond responds.

Again with the disinterest. Has Diamond already found a Trainer?

"And…I'm just glad to see you." You try. "In general."

Diamond raises her eyebrows. She puts down her teacup. "You are?"

You feel the skin on your neck crawl. You suppress it and place your hands in your lap. "It's been a while."

"It has."

"I missed you and Crown back at the shrine." You chuckle awkwardly. "The last time you saw me, your guards sorta blew me off. I didn't know what to think."

This gives Diamond room for pause. Her ears stiffen. She pulls herself to the edge of her seat, examining you with a critical eye. "When was this?"

"A couple of years ago, in Shibuya. You were there for shopping in a limo—"

"No." Diamond says.

"But—"

"You must be mistaken." Diamond says firmly.

You sink back. "I was there."

"Yet I don't recall any of that. You must be misremembering."

Force in her tone. No room for counterarguments. You feel yourself deflate. Your head lowers.

"Okay…"

Two years isn't a negligible amount of time. What was a chance encounter for you must have been quickly forgotten by Diamond amidst the frantic rush of her heiress and umamusume training. The family dream rests on her back, after all. That's what you're telling yourself, even as your chest tightens, and your nose instinctively shivers at the scent of a lie.

[Subterfuge check: 49/40 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

Liar. Liar. My memory isn't terrible.

"Is Crown doing well?"

"She's busy, too. She assists in the management of the Hong Kong side of our family operations."

"From Japan?"

"She lived there for a time."

"That sounds cool! I'd love to hear more. Would she be willing to meet up with me in private?"

Diamond sips her tea. "Probably not. She doesn't have much time to spare, either."

Yet she's attending classes like the rest of us.

You nod. You mumble a sentence along the lines of 'I understand'. Your fork pokes at your cake, splitting the top half from the bottom, and you barely care. The sugar, the tinkling piano music, they fade into the background. A sensation pulses inside of you. It's the spike of a physical stitch with the antsy spider-crawling nerves of the minutes counting down before the curtain's rise at a concert. It's the edge of the cliff. It rumbles with the voice of Narita Brian.

Narita Brian, triple Crown winner and member of the student council, who got straight up in your face and put you on full blast. She exposed your inadequacy. Lashed your psyche with her tongue, wielding her indomitable, unavoidable fortitude. She tried to help you. She succeeded.

Diamond's different. This umamusume, who speaks so gently to the camera, posing like a wallflower in commercials and photographs, insists on blanking you out. She's evading your questions. The olive branch is plastic; its leaves prickling with tiny thorns. As your psyche stings and grits its teeth, a tiny niggling voice grows louder and louder at the back of your head. Rip off the band-aid. Break the faucet, cut the chaff. Enough games.

You perform the mental equivalent of plugging your fingers in your ears. Maybe Diamond's having a bad day, like Narita Brian was. Maybe this isn't her type of hangout. Maybe she's secretly the standoffish type who's cold to her family members but warm and gentle deep down, and this doesn't conflict with her public persona at all because it's something she's rehearsed while dealing specifically with you.

You're sentimental. You desire to return to the past. You want to see your sister smile like she used to.

A bitter giggle wraps itself around your throat, and squeezes tight. You bite down on your own teeth.

A fork slams down on a plate. A loud ringing sound. You jolt. It's Oguri. She's glaring straight at Diamond, icing and crumbs clinging to the corners of her mouth.

"Do you want some more?" Diamond asks. "Because—"

"Out with it." Oguri demands.

"Pardon?"

"You're doing the thing from My Big Body again. You're Folkqueen on a bad day, except a dozen times worse."

Diamond scowls. "Excuse me?"

"Don't pretend like you're innocent. Bringing us here to this fancy restaurant, deflecting Ruby's questions, acting like you're Rudolf behind her desk with this passive-aggressive game of charades—it's sickening. We all know you've got a bone to pick against Ruby, little Miss Satono, so do us a courtesy, quit beating around the bush, and spit it out!" Oguri snarls—snarls, a legit sound of passionate fury you never thought was possible from her.

"Hey!" Kitasan cries. "Don't talk to Dia like that!"

Diamond bolts up from her seat. "You are free to leave my hospitality anytime you want, Miss Cap." She growls.

Oguri mimics the action. She stands up, cracks her neck, and towers over Diamond. She bares her teeth.

"And you are no Mejiro Ramonu, nor Ardan, not even a McQueen. You're an open, transparent book with a cover written in pretension!" Oguri hisses.

Diamond's delicate hands curl up. Her teeth clench and she vibrates, a steam engine ready to blow. Kitasan reaches out, only to have her hand slapped away, and there it is—the ice cracks. The facade breaks, collapses into a heap. You perceive what was teeming and writhing within Diamond's psyche from the moment you met. Upon her visage, it is utterly grotesque, a bristling canvas of rage and hate that twists and warps like a mask crafted from stolen flesh and twine.

It is naked and unrestrained, and it is directed straight at you.

"Where are Opal's shoes, Ruby?"

"Huh?" You squeak.

Diamond whirls her head around. Her cheeks are an ugly shade of red. "Satono Opal's shoes were delivered to the shrine you were staying in. They were taken there to be purified by incineration. Yet, around the day you disappeared, they went missing!"

"I…what makes you think I have them?"

Diamond scoffs out loud. "Who else could desire such a vile object from such a horrid person?"

Something inside you breaks. It sounds like shattering glass.

Oguri rolls her eyes. "They're just a pair of shoes. They can't do anything."

"Don't speak about things you have no knowledge about, Miss Cap." Diamond seethes.

"Then explain, because we're not understanding!"

"They're a remnant from my family's greatest failure, and they're also our property. We would very much like them back!" Diamond roars.

You slump back in your seat, dazed. "You brought me here, all this way, to ask about my mom's pair of shoes?"

"Where are they?" Diamond demands.

"Dia, calm down!" Kitasan begs. "You're causing a scene."

"Where are they, Ruby?" Diamond repeats. She slams her palms on the table. "Answer me!"

Gazing up at your sister-cousin, feeling the full brunt of her fury, noxious and pulsating, you realise the deceit has been wiped clean. There was no chance of reconciliation, no means of returning to the past. Satono Diamond brought you here for an interrogation. She was fattening you up, trying to break your guard. And now that the curtain is torn down, she has switched tracks to be direct and unabashed with the truth.

She despises you with every fiber of her being.

Wetness gathers at the corners of your eyes.

[(Guts check: 8/11) && (Composure Check: 47/80) -> Failure.]

[Mood has dropped to Awful.]

[Total EXP gained: 20.]

2.5: Relinquish

>>Ask if Diamond even saw you as Ruby, or all she saw was the chance to erase another part of your mother's existence.

>>Leave, you are done enjoying Diamond's 'hospitality'.

>>Ask Oguri for more help.

>>Cry.

EXP: 95/130 (1 LEVEL UP pending...)

Mood: Awful

People are staring. The staff, the old couple on the other side of the room, the security personnel from the future when they play back the recordings via the nub-shaped camera in the corner behind the table. You detect them with an innate umadol instinct. And how can they not? This car crash of a tea break has broken past the railings and swerved onto a busy highway. Oguri Cap, Ashen Beast of Kasamatsu, is baring her fangs like a wolf, and not the starving kind. Kitasan Black, Tracen's favored rookie, fixates on her plate, her shoulders hunched and her mouth tight. There's Satono Diamond, up in arms and furious on her feet, so completely divorced from the elegant, demure heiress her conglomerate has curated for interviews and the big screen.

And then there's you seated closest to the corner, mind full of static, hearing and seeing little and instead replaying the channel of wrong, wrong, this is all wrong.

"Back away. Now."

"This has nothing to do with you, Oguri Cap!"

"You think just because you were raised with a silver spoon in your mouth, that means you can say whatever you want?"

"This is a family crisis. An outsider like you should stay in her lane."

"Dia, please…"

You risk a look at your estranged sister, an act as welcoming as shoving your face on a sewer grate in the middle of summer. Diamond is etched in rage, at Oguri; at this stupid coffee palace; at the people watching, a passive, secondhand ire; maybe even a tiny fraction at Kitasan, but mostly towards you. It is worse than open flame on your skin, worse than a storm whipping through the countryside. It is what you imagine what it would be like to wrap yourself in barbed wire, switch on an electric current, and force yourself to meld with the pain.

Diamond locks eyes with you again, and you tremble.

For a brief moment, you contemplate giving Diamond what she wants. Just hand over Satono Opal's shoes. Their model is probably outdated. You had to spend multiple paychecks on that steel-lined case to protect them instead of food and clothes that could have made you bigger and stronger. Tracen has the budget to buy you a new pair of running shoes, or at least fund half—the rest you'll figure out from a part-time job; there are sure to be endless across Fuchu.

Oguri was right. The shoes can't do anything. They are inanimate objects. Any impression you put upon them is derived from yourself. If relinquishing them could lessen Diamond's hate, make her or Crown smile even a fraction like they used to back at the manor…

But, as that thought reaches its tail, another clings on. You remember the ghost of your mother's hand cupping against your face; the hearty wooden scent of the comb she made in her old woodworks class she used to untangle your hair in the morning; the twinkle in her eye as she peeled the family orchard's apples in lieu of the maid and fed you piece by piece on the grass. Your heart squeezes painfully. You are struck by the sudden urge to check with Hishi Amazon that the steel-lined case remains in your room. You feel rancid for even beginning the prior thought…

[Logic check: 55/50 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

…and you realize, with a flash, that an inverse of Diamond's refusal to meet you applies here. She could have demanded a search of your room for stolen property, yet she didn't. She couldn't. The Satonos are not idle. There must be some kind of law or rule in place preventing the Satonos from doing so. You're not certain what it is, but it means you can question Diamond about the shoes without suffering consequences, to an extent.

It's small comfort. Your sister was trying to guilt-trip you into giving up the last memory of your mother. It's another stab in your wounded back.

"Why does it matter?"

"Excuse me?" Diamond snaps.

You incline your head, raising a napkin with a shaking hand to wipe away the tears. You speak past the lump growing in your throat. "Why do you want my mom's shoes so much?"

Diamond half-giggles, half-sneers. "Do I even have to ask?"

"They're just shoes. They didn't do anything, like Oguri said. They're the only thing I have left of her." You protest. "And you're telling me I was supposed to sit back and let them be burned to ashes?"

"The proper term is purification."

"They'd be gone, either way."

Diamond glowers at you some more. All of a sudden, her lips quiver. She chortles, a disbelieving, disdainful sound. "You're still clinging onto her."

"She's my mom." You exclaim.

"And she abandoned you." Diamond counters.

"She didn't have a choice. My mom loved me!"

"Opal—" Diamond seethes, "—was a cruel, selfish woman who abused the love and generosity of others. She dared to violate the sanctity of the sport our entire family has devoted its existence to supporting. Because of her crimes, one athlete crashed during a term and broke her leg, ending her career altogether. Another missed out on the prize money she needed to pay for her father's cancer treatments. She hurt Tracen, the URA, her countless fans and sponsors, and her own brothers, sisters, parents and ancestors! A sane person would have cast aside such a vile woman long ago!"

Your cheeks burn. Second-hand shame. There's nothing to say against this, because these are facts Diamond is speaking. Satono Opal sabotaged her competitors. She sniped a few careers before they flourished. Her crimes were well-reported and are still well-known these days. The motivation doesn't matter as much as the results.

"And she did those things, knowing she had a daughter!" Diamond crows, her eyes suddenly lighting up.

"Dia…" Kitasan finds her voice. It comes out as an uncertain quaver. Her knuckles are white, from gripping her fork. "Isn't this too much?"

Diamond ignores her friend. She presses on. "That's why we exiled her. That's why you were sent to the shrine. You were to become a shinme to rid yourself and the rest of our family from Opal's kegare."

"What the hell is that?" Oguri asks.

Impurity. Spiritual contamination. Defilement of the world's harmony. You could write a speech on the nature of kegare and its causes across wider society. Its definition was among the first you learned back at the shrine. The mere usage of that word in reference to your mother causes your gut to roil.

"Is that all you think I am, Dia?"

Diamond recoils, as if slapped in the face. "Don't you dare call me that again!" She hisses.

You persist. "Am I just my mother's evil to you? Her impurity?"

Diamond scoffs again. "You ran away. You threw our generosity back in our faces. And you sit there, having the gall to play the victim—"

You interrupt her with a shout. "I'm sorry, okay?"

Diamond closes her mouth, almost wide-eyed.

"I'm sorry to you that I stole my mom's shoes and ran away from the shrine. I know I did something wrong—multiple of them. I've regretted leaving behind my responsibilities and my duties even through the years in the Tokyo underground. But I can't give my mom's shoes up, no more than Oguri can give up her mom's hairband, nor you nor Kitasan nor Mejiro McQueen can give up their own family treasures!"

Diamond's cheeks turn redder at the last name. It's a low blow you've struck, bringing her own idol into this, surely a source of her own courage. It doesn't slow you down. You can't stop, won't stop, and you're on your feet, having shoved your chair aside with a mighty sweep. It rocks and almost tilts over—you don't care. Your ears are pinned flat against the flat of your head, and you grasp at air with your hands as if holding the collar of Diamond's dress.

You are finally at her level.

"I missed you, Dia. I missed Crown, too. And I was so confused, so frightened, when they separated me from you at the manor, then put me on a van to take me to the countryside. No-one told me where I was going. No-one told me what happened to my mom. I sent so many letters to the mansion and when they got no response I sat in my room and made up conversations with imaginary you and imaginary Crown where we played the same games of hide-and-seek and chocolate hunts and mock races because that's how much I wanted to go home!"

Diamond stares, jaw clenched. She's impenetrable. You taste the salt of your tears on your tongue. A sob leaks out of your mouth.

"Tracen's for all umamusume, isn't it?"

"What do you mean?" Kitasan asks. She sounds breathless. Tired.

You turn to her. "Dia's not the Satono heiress at Tracen, nor am I Opal's daughter. Under the watch of the Three Goddesses, we're just fellow students, aiming to be the best. We have the same goal. We seek the same dream. Can't we put our histories aside and get along?"

Can't we be friends again?

A shudder runs through Kitasan's frame. She averts her gaze, biting her lip. It's barely perceptible from this angle, but she's clutching the top of her shorts enough to crease the fabric.

[Persuasion check: 73/70 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

But Kitasan is not whom you're pleading towards.

A pregnant silence hangs. You break it by taking a nearby napkin and blowing your ruddy, running nose with it. The air tastes stale. Your chest aches with exertion. This is it, you think numbly. You've said your piece, and now it's time for the audience to enact its judgment.

"Easy for you to say."

When Diamond speaks, it is without the fervor she attacked you with. Her tone is soft, and almost dead.

"You never saw Papa bowing and scraping before the URA. I can't believe you have the audacity to talk about us getting along when you're still refusing to acknowledge what you've done wrong." Diamond inhales a shuddering breath. She points a trembling finger at you. "We can't help someone who doesn't want to be helped."

Her message is clear: I do not forgive you.

That's it, then.

[Persuasion check: 73/150 -> Failure.]

You have failed.

You slump back down in your chair, strength vanishing from your muscles. Somewhere deep inside of you, you feel the urges to laugh, to howl, to take the plate in front of you and smash it into itty-bitty tiny pieces, but mostly to sit there and let those fresh tears streak down your dirty cheeks.

"I still haven't gotten an answer out of you, Ruby. Where are your mother's shoes?" Diamond demands. "You're not leaving here until I get an answer!"

You don't react. Diamond slams her palm on the table. The cutlery rattles.

"Look at me, Ruby!"

Your gaze remains blank and distant. Diamond lets out a growl of frustration and lashes out with her free hand for your unmoving wrist lying limply on the table. Whether this is to force you back to reality, to drag you back up again, or perhaps to simply harm you, your instincts don't care. They recoil with the aftershock of your umadol self being pulled suddenly aside on the streets, pens and cameras shoved in your face. There's a nick, a faint brush of contact. Diamond's fingers snap forward again—and that's when it happens.

Sheer force explodes out of thin air. It bulldozes all others aside. It wrenches downwards and smashes the table into pieces.

…no.

Just the center. The force stabbed the table with a knife. A crack as ugly as a fault in the road lies there, splinters surrounding it like rubble raining down in the aftermath of a bomb's detonation. Some of the splinters rest on Diamond's manicured nails and porcelain-smooth fingers. She can't move them. She's gawking at the knife and the crack, smack-bang in the center of the arc drawn by the tip of her index and her middle finger; and the knife is gripped in the solid hand of one Oguri Cap.

"Sorry." Oguri grits out, her breaths snarling out through clenched teeth. "I kept hearing the buzzing of a disgusting insect, and I wanted it gone."

Diamond yanks back her hand. She winces as a splinter draws a cut, then a drop of blood. Any indignant splutter that would come evaporates into a mortified whimper as Oguri yanks the knife out and drops it on the tabletop with a clatter, revealing the curvature of her grip imprinted into the stainless steel metal. The side bulges like squeezed exercise putty. The intricate engravings are gone.

Oguri withdraws. She brushes strands of her fringe out of her face and catches your eye. She sees the desperate, silent plea.

I don't want to be here.

And she doesn't waste a second thinking about it.

"Where are you going?" Diamond splutters.

Oguri doesn't look at her. She's busy hoisting you up, allowing you to lean on her shoulder. She reaches into her jacket for her wallet. With a growl and a flourish, she pulls out a wad of bills and slams them on the table.

"Thanks for the meal." She snarls.

She grabs you by the wrist and hustles you away down the stairs, past the front reception, out into the streets drenched in the bright Fuchu sunshine. You do not protest.

Time passes by in a blur, the scenery of the city shunting from one realistic diorama to the next. A busy street, a crossroads where the little man turns red and green, a crowded bus where your head rests on the seat-rest with a hand guiding your shoulder and your vision filled with the poster of a warning to never forget your ticket in cheery corporate font and cartoon. The fare machine beeps and spits out a ticket. Hanging straps sway with the rhythm of leaves in the spring breeze. No loud talking on your phone, please, says the nice lady on the intercom, but whispering is fine.

"Belno. Belno—you there? You worked with Team Rigil before on that health survey thing, right? Can you call one of them up and get me Grass Wonder's number, please? I'll explain later. You will? You're a lifesaver. Thank you so much…"

An asphalt road. A sign that says Welcome to Fuchu No Mori Park. The road winds and twists past a fountain spurting with water, before going at a steady incline up through a grove of trees and to a hilly spot looking over a wide swathe of the park. The bench feels hard on your bottom. A kite with rainbow trails flies in the sky from below. A family of brown-eared bulbuls chirp. Your nose twitches with the presence of fresh flower pollen sailing on the breeze, and you take a mindless sip of the vending machine lemon tea handed to you several minutes ago.

It's quiet. Nothing here is noxious . Nothing will harm you. You can sit here and let time idle by.

"Ruby!"

A sharp cry. Footsteps. Umamusume footsteps. You tilt your head up. You see them jogging out of the path between two thick evergreen trees—Grass Wonder, and two others close behind. They stop just in front of the bench where you and Oguri are seated. The first of her friends bears faded green hair; her lithe form is dressed in a white blouse. The second wears a striped green-white dress, her shoulders covered in an expensive black-silk shawl. These are fellow members of Grass Wonder's Golden Generation: Seiun Sky and King Halo.

On any other occasion, you'd be leaping with excitement at the prospect of meeting Grass Wonder's friends. She's gushed about them before, how their mutual rivalries pushed each other to excel on the turf. She even suggested asking permission from Rudolf to bring some of them to your student-mentorship sessions. Regular Ruby would have pestered them with racing questions until her tongue grew swollen. The you of the present can only look and not perceive.

Grass Wonder is the first to approach. Her cheeks are flushed from the exertion of sprinting. Her hair is slightly disheveled, with a few irksome strands poking off in disparate directions. This is normally cause for a quick combing, because Grass Wonder is nothing if not meticulous even in casual appearances, yet she couldn't care less in this moment. A hundred different questions wage war across her face. Are you okay? Why are you like this? Did Oguri do this? I'm so sorry to have suggested this weekend for you.

"Are you hurt?" She asks.

You shake your head.

"Miss Oguri called me. She said you were in great distress and needed my help." There's a sureness present that points to her already having an inclination, if not full understanding. She takes a seat next to you and gently takes one of your slack hands, massaging its back with her fingers. They are smooth and feel cool against yours. "Would you like to talk about it?"

"I…"

"She looks shocked." King Halo mutters. Her tone is laden with a rich accent. "Should we take her to a hospital?"

"I thought about it." Oguri says. "She's not injured, though."

"Physically, you mean," Seiun comments. "Mentally…"

The combined attention, coupled with the sudden awareness that you must look awful, your mild makeup smeared and your top stained with tears and faint crumbs, jolts an ember of awareness back into your mind.

"I met Diamond, Grass." You utter.

Grass Wonder's eyes widen. So do Seiun and King Halo. The tension goes up a notch. Oguri just nods her head, miserably.

"Satono? As in that Satono Diamond, the heiress everyone's been making such a fuss?" Seiun questions.

King Halo pulls her friend aside, whispering in her ear. "Seiun, perhaps we should take a backseat to this…"

"Did she force you?" Grass Wonder asks.

You shake your head. "No. We ran into each other at a sports store. Kitasan Black was with her. We talked for a bit and then Diamond took me to a fancy cafe."

Grass Wonder flicks her gaze further to her right. "And Oguri…"

"It was my choice. Oguri gave me an out, and I didn't take it." You reply.

Grass Wonder stares. She's confused. It's not difficult to understand why, because who goes and meets up with a person who despises them for seemingly no good reason? What you did was a foregone conclusion long ago. The signs were there. Framed this way, you were foolish.

Exhaustion weighs down your back. You ponder whether to stay silent. None of these girls is forcing you to talk. But, you realise from Grass Wonder and her fellow Golden Generation's outfits and flushed cheeks that you interrupted their morning, made them run from one side of Fuchu to the other to see you. You owe it to them to explain what happened.

"Because…"

"Because?" Grass prompts.

"Because I wanted to see how Diamond was doing." You murmur. "Deep down, I knew she didn't appreciate me. Like, a month and a bit has passed since the start of the year? She could have come and met me anytime she wanted. It'd have been so easy."

"Miss Ruby…" King Halo clears her throat. "We would never blame you for trying to reconnect with a family member. That's something to be commended, not spurned."

"Sounds like you did all you could," Seiun comments.

Did you? You squirm at the self-accusation. If only you were smarter, more charismatic, had more friends…

"What happened in the cafe?" Grass Wonder asks softly, gently.

You hear Oguri clench her teeth again. That presence she bears upon you out of nowhere flares up again. It smoulders, unable to roar free again, this time with regret and sorrow.

"I hoped…" You say, and swallow again before continuing. "I hoped that deep down, despite our years apart and the fact she didn't come see me, it was because she was shy, or pretending to put distance between us because the Satono higher-ups ordered her to act that way. Once we got together in private, she'd drop the facade and we could hang out and giggle together like we did as kids. Her taking me to a coffee palace was just her being over budget."

You inhale a shaky breath. You make a weak chuckle. "I wanted to believe that."

Horror creeps over Grass's face. Her friends mimic the action. King Halo's hand has flown to her mouth. Seiun looks dazed.

"She bought me these extremely fancy cakes full of sugar and cream. We chatted—or at least I tried to chat, but she kept blanking me. Her friend didn't do anything do help. I knew Diamond was intentionally doing all that, but I was in full denial mode; and Miss Oguri got so mad, she accused Diamond on the spot. Diamond, she then…"

You jaw clenches shut. Your brain throbs. The nerves and chemicals binding your psyche and physique are pushing back, begging you not to unleash the flood of fresh memories.

"She…"

There's an invisible grip on your throat, choking you out.

"Ruby!" Grass Wonder cries. Her hold on your hand grows stronger. "You don't have to say anything if you don't want to."

'That's right." Oguri chimes in. "If it's too painful—"

"She was after m-m-my—"

Satono Diamond, running along the garden path, blowing raspberries and giggling. Satono Diamond, heiress of her conglomerate, taking her olive branch, stabbing you, and gouging the flesh until a chunk pops. You squeeze the bottle of lemon tea so hard the plastic contorts and the sickly sweet-sour fluid spurts out and floods the front of your jeans. A broken, strained sob escapes your throat. You lift your head up, bloodshot, wide-eyed, falling apart at the seams.

"Grass, I loved her. I loved Dia and Crown and I begged and I pleaded and told Dia that straight up, but all she saw was my mother's mistake. She said she couldn't forgive me. She thinks me as a parasite. She looked at me and she wished I was never born!"

And you place the heels of your palms upon your eyes and wail, as the park vibrates with foreign cheer and foreign laughter; as your world coalesces into runny tears and wracked sobs; as Oguri's firm arms wrap around you and she nuzzles her own forehead into your shoulder, because the miracle was never a miracle in the first place, it was an ephemeral longing from a decade and a million years ago. The nightmare of your sisters' hatred that you buried so deep is irrefutable reality, from which you will not, and cannot, ever wake up from.

2.6: Whispers II

"It's done. Those pesky eavesdroppers have deleted every last photo and recording."

"Good work."

"…it's the least I could do for the poor girl. My mother's name finally ended up being useful for something. How is she?"

"Still asleep. That much crying will make anyone exhausted. I don't think she's eaten lunch either. I'll ask the cafeteria to prepare an extra big meal for her when she wakes up."

"You'll take a taxi, then? I'll pay."

"King, I couldn't—"

"It's fine. Consider it payback for last week. Our shopping trip was done before we even got started, so I thought I might as well return to Tracen and get to work on a few other things."

"Like that Kawakami girl?"

"They're in the same year. Their ear ornaments are even similar. Goodness, I had heard the Satonos were mired in controversy, and there were unsavory rumors floating about Ruby's character here and there, but this—this is obscene. Even at my family's worst, we would never."

"You've got a real nasty look on your face right now."

"Describe it to me, then."

"Like a hannya crossed with the red oni."

"Sky."

"Yeah?"

"I will say this once, and only once, because you are a cherished friend of mine. Don't you dare get in my way."

"You think I'd disagree?"

"Does the phrase 'cut her teeth' mean anything to you?"

"Shoe's on the other foot, you mean? Well, jokes on you! I don't have an argument. I was wrong. Even I can't pull my usual tricks when I see a rookie cry her heart out. Just…don't go and do anything reckless, okay?"

"The heavens must be falling if you're telling me that."

"Yeah, normally it's the other way around. I'm serious. Those Satonos are the nouveau rich type, except they've actually got brains—endlessly crapping on a poor girl aside. They're rivals of the Mejiros for a reason. I heard they threatened to pull a chunk of their funding out of Tracen, which forced the Director to comply with some of their wishes."

"And yet Ruby is still here, alive and well. They have their limits."

"Just don't crash and burn by ramming yourself against their wall."

"A wall that is far from insurmountable. I have won multiple G1s where they haven't."

"…heh. True. Seriously, how have they not done that with so much money?"

"Perhaps they should spend less time haranguing my student and more on refining their techniques."

"You gonna talk to the Prez again?"

"Indeed. I think a good long chat with Rudolf is in order. She was proposing extending the student mentorship program a bit longer—what a good idea, wouldn't you say? As for our Satono Diamond herself, you of all umas should know that I am a very patient girl."

"Yeesh, don't tell me you're still upset over Spe…"

"Oguri."

"Hey, Grass."

"…"

"…"

"My sincere thanks to you for helping Ruby today."

"I should have dragged her away the moment I had the chance. Hell, I should have thrown those cakes in Diamond's face."

"I won't disagree with that. However, as callous as might seem, this tragedy may end up as somewhat of a positive. Better for Ruby to face this now instead of lingering in denial. She knows who her sister is for real now."

"I'm just so furious. Everyone knows the story of my own mom, and just imagining her in place of Opal made me—damn!"

"…I have never seen you like this."

"I don't enjoy feeling like this, either. And I was careless."

"How?"

"The knife. I almost wounded that girl and turned this mess into a legal battle."

"You didn't."

"I got lucky."

"I do agree it's better to err on the side of caution, though I can't help but wish I could've seen the look on her idiotic face."

"Belno looked up the restaurant for me. It's completely owned by the Satonos. There's not a single chance that any of our conversation will be leaked into the public. Diamond's getting away scot-free."

"It's fine."

"Is it?"

"It angers me, yes, but what's done is done. I doubt they'll be pursuing you, since they'll be so busy covering it up."

"I'll talk to Ardan. She deserves to know what kind of uma is hanging around her little sister. Whether she'll believe me without evidence is tricky."

"Wise idea. It's a start, if nothing else."

"…"

"…"

"…you keep staring at her. Still got our previous conversation on your mind?"

"Yeah. I do."

""Ruby's a good girl. She'd love to have you as a friend."

"I…I gotta take a walk. I need to think."

"She'll wait for you."

"Take care of her for the tryouts, Grass."

"You're the one who might have to initiate this time."

"I know, alright? Give...give me some time. Like I said, I've got things to think about."

"Very well. Don't be a stranger, Oguri. See you."

There's a new rumor floating around the school, and it goes like this: Satono Ruby is a thief. The origins? A total mystery? The evidence confirming this? Positively ethereal.

Anyway, who cares? A decent number of students entertain the idea, which means it must be true. The dominoes of Tracen's society fall.
