3.2: Daily Life IV

Mood: Normal

EXP: 75/140

>>[Event 1] Perform a distracting dance on the spot.

Your new bullies get a good workout going on their patch of gym floor. It's standard stuff: repeated squats for leg stability, lunges for stride power and balance, push-ups and planking for core strength, and so on. The four of them divide themselves into pairs. One girl in each pair performs their reps, then switches over with their spotters once a stopwatch counts down.

It's not just an agreement. It's a rhythm. The girls don't talk when they need to switch; they simply gesture with hand signals or nods of their heads. It's fast. It's efficiency designed to take as much advantage of the limited time as possible. And it'll be happening on the day that's not today, because these bullies are having an extremely hard time concentrating due to the school pariah hopping up and down and waving her arms about.

"Oooooh~Umadacchi!" You belt out at full volume, a soaring sensation swelling through your abdomen. "Oooooh~Umapyoi! Umapyoi! Oooooh~Sukidacchi!"

This isn't just any ordinary song you're singing. This is Umapyoi Legend, the umamusume racing song in Japan. Talking at length about its accolades would leave you here until midnight, so you'll give a sample. Number 1 on Oricon for months on end on release, a mainstay in any karaoke bar, a mandatory part of the lineup for any high-tier G1 winning live, and—of course—a song in your repertoire as an underground umamusume idol. It deserves that praise because it's good, it's great, it triggers those dopamine receptors, and is just about what you'd expect from a composer downing several bottles of wine and dancing in his underwear.

You can only hope to mimic a fraction of that energy as you dive into the next verse. There's no space to mimic the action where you're meant to run down the stage, hand-in-hand with the second and third place, so you extend your both your arms outwards, twist your torso half-way both times, and pretend you're an airplane instead.

"Oooooh~Umapyoi! Uma-uma umya-unya three, two, one, run!"

The bullies try to ignore you. They honestly, truly, do. Ribbon-Red on the left squeezes her eyes shut on her push-ups. Black-Ringlet bites down on her tongue and launches herself into a coughing fit. The ringleader, an Orange-Earring, along with her lackey-best-friend-whatever White-Cowlick, swing into their sit-ups with their full strength. They grunt and groan in an attempt to drown out your pro bono performance with their own exertion.

Sucks to be them. You were taught to magnify your tunes over the cheers of hundreds.

[Dancing check: 100/85 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

"One, two three, four, five Dandandandandebangachikazuki! Tension high, it's time to go! Stride was strong but didn't get first—Chaah!" You exclaim. The dance steps flow one after the other. Your future self is moving ahead, and you are slipping into the gap she left behind. Hands up, right hand down! Left hand up, swing that loop. Hands to ears, pump to fist, make a cross, penlights all around— "Don't stop!"

You clasp your hands, spread them out, and then top it off sideways while stretching your mouth into a goofy smile with half your tongue dangling out. The imaginary karaoke machine vomits out a PERFECT!

Somewhere in the slowly forming crowd of sweaty onlookers, someone giggles. Orange-Earring launches to her feet. She stomps up to you.

"What the hell are you doing?" She demands.

"Don't you cry! Wipe those eyes!" You respond, waving your hands up again. "Tough it out!"

"You've seen this is funny, don't you? Can't hack it for the tryouts, so you've got to act like a clown. Or are you the type of uma who bases her personality on getting her sick kicks by screwing over others, just like your horrid mom?" Orange-Earrings shouts.

There's genuine anger there. But you see it. That faint, smug smile beneath Orange-Earring's dimpled nose. It's a tactic.

[Subterfuge check: 52/50 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

It's called self-victimization. She's trying to paint herself as an innocent girl by leveraging the fact that most of the umas in this gym will treat you as less of a glass half-empty and more of a broken teacup with rotting dregs stinking up the bottom. They'll never believe that Orange-Earring fired the first shot and wronged you first.

The longer this goes on , the more likely it is that you will be kicked out of the gym on your pretty little behind. You're not sweating though. No, you are a disciple of one Hotaru of the FAITHFUL, goth enthusiast and enemy of Shibuya's department store middle-managers. Remember what I told you about malicious compliance?

You smile as if nothing is wrong. She grimaces—and before she can respond, you spin on your foot, twirl a single step forward, and look her dead in the eye.

"Victory smiles upon me today…"

Her nostrils flare. "No." She cries, scrambling back and almost stepping on Ribbon-Red's hand, "You bitch, don't you dare!"

"…She blows a kiss as I'm making my win!"

You lift your hands to your mouth and blow a kiss with as much fresh saliva as you can muster. The sheer force of the kiss's smack is material romcom directors would weep with joy at. Imaginary Saya and Hotaru throw their hands to their mouths. One uma behind you collapses into raucous laughter that involves much clutching of one's stomach.

As for the leader of your new bullies?

"Screw this!"

Orange-Earings storms off before you can finish the chain of doki-doki-doki, her minions shortly following behind you. They don't bother to bundle up their gym equipment. Two of them shoot you dirty glares over their shoulders—nothing you can't handle. You'll only feel frightened when they start brandishing notebooks and pens.

The moment they're out of sight, you relax. You smooth your tracksuit pants over, brush your hair out of your eyes and take a sip of water from your exercise bottle. According to the lyrics you managed to sing, you got through sixty percent of the short version of Umapyoi Legend, which totals to a little over a minute wasted dealing with those bullies. That leaves you with twenty-eight minutes of precious workout time. It's not ideal, but you're relieved your problems are over for the moment—

"Satono Ruby!"

Oh no, now what?

You turn around and find a fresh, new umamusume up in your face. She's slightly shorter than you, bearing almond-colored hair tied up into twintails by pink-purple checkered ribbons. She's also sporting puffed-up cheeks like a tomato grown wrong.

"Uh, can I help you—" you begin.

The new girl whips out a finger and slams it in your face.

"My name is Smart Falcon!" She declares.

You feel as if you should recognize her…

[(History check: 40/60 || Social Media check: 52/60) -> Failure.]

…but you don't.

"Okay…?"

"And I am Tracen's number one umadol! I don't care how much experience in the underground you have: I will never give up my position to you!"

She balls up her fists and stands there, glaring.

You fall silent. It is a dreadful, indignant lapse of time. Excuse you? Number one umadol in Tracen? By whose authority? The Director's? The masses'? The Three Goddesses? You're not seeing it. And what's with that attitude, too? You weren't shooting for an umadol position in a racing academy, but look at that arrogance? Is…she saying that your time in the Tokyo underground meant zilch? Is she one of those 'artists' who have nothing but scorn for the indie scene?

Your jaw clenches. You glare back. The feeling is mutual. Teeth grind, sparks fly and the imaginary audience weeps. There's only one thing you and Smart Falcon will agree on. This is no longer about confronting a random stranger. It's a contest to bear the reputation of your respective umadol groups on your backs. Losing is unacceptable.

Smart Falcon breaks the deadlock first. She breathes in, hand on her chest, then shoots it up straight into the air. The other hand is balled up as a fist to her mouth—an imitation of a microphone!

"Come on, everyone, let's get started!" She hollers, her previous anger blindsided in exchange for raw passionate cheer. "One, two, three, now!"

Smart Falcon hops up and down, pumping her fist. You watch how her legs flow, how she effortlessly switches between left and right towards her imaginary audience, as a chant of n-ma-ma-ma bounces out of her lungs with precise staccato. Horror strikes you. This girl is good.

"N-ma-a n-maa I'm running out of breath!" Smart Falcon cries, feigning a gasp. "Huh? There's no sound!"

She hurls her imaginary microphone up into the air, and the surrounding atmosphere seems to shimmer and twist. Festival lanterns high up in the sky, orange light beaming down. A stage constructed from steel girders and solid wood. The German-accented uma shaking her head and muttering to herself is up on the top portion, banging wooden sticks on a taiko drum as Smart Falcon is down on the ground, dancing in the centre and surrounded by legions of backup dancers and waving fans. The whole stage roars with Amaterasu's inferno.

"The sound of drums, full of joy and spirit, ooh let's go. Flowers and yukata are swaying and fluttering. Tie up your hair and fasten your obi tight tight tight~it's too tight!"

[Smart Falcon's Dancing check: 165/100 -> Success!]

No, you realise with a shudder. No, no, no, this can't be. This melody—it's enka! Smart Falcon is using your own weapon against you! You could never have predicted this; otherwise you'd have started off with one of FAITHFUL's own songs. It doesn't matter now. Your own stage is shrinking, the penlights swaying in her direction. An aura of pure power radiates from her in powerful waves, buckling your knees as it hits.

Is this…the power of an aboveground umadol?

Smart Falcon sees you. Triumph blossoms on her face. A wire snaps inside your head. You storm back to your feet, fury overtaking you. Claiming victory before the final note? Shame on her! And shame on you for even considering giving up before the curtain call. Puff up that chest. Face forward with dignity. You are not some half-dressed rookie snapping her first short on Umatok. You performed on cramped basement stages with four other moving girls. You pranced around Shibuya Crossing in your first year in the city, pumping your lungs like pistons in a steam engine to make your singing heard above the busy morning rush. You are a girl shaped and forged by Tokyo's streets; a proud, professional underground umadol with merch sales, streaming rights and solo stans to your name.

In the name of all that is FAITHFUL, you will rise to the challenge!

"Kimi no Aiba ga!" You launch back into Umapyoi Legend, limbs pumping with strength as if you had never stopped. "Zu-kyun! Do-kyun! Start running your way; ba-kyun! Bu-kyun! Heart's racing with you!"

Smart Falcon grinds her teeth for a fraction of a second and not a speck more. "...what did you say? Wha-wha-wha-what do we do? What do we do—let's go!"

You amp up the volume. "Emotions all brand new, jump through that gate—three, two, one fight! Zu-kyun! Do-kyun! I'm taking the lead—"

And Smart Falcon counters in turn. "Su~uuper duper su~uuper duper yo-isayoisa yo-isayoisa get dancing, go wild!"

"Today we hear your cheers; Come on, come on baby! Three, two, one go fight! Come on, come on honey! Three, two, one, ooh, fight!"

"Oooooh Umadacchi Oooooh Umapyoi! Umapyoi!"

"DOING THE TRACEN ONDO WITH A GREAT BIG YOI!!"

"OOOOOH SUKIDACCHI OOOOOH UMAPYOI—"

"SHUT THE HELL UPPPPPPP!"

You and Smart Falcon freeze on the spot, mouths hanging open in determined scowls. Hishi Amazon charges through the gathered crowd with the rage of a matador's bull, her megaphone brandished like a club.

"THIS IS A GYM, NOT A DANCE HALL!" She roars, smacking both of you on the shoulders. "GET BACK TO EXERCISING THIS INSTANT OR I'M SENDING BOTH YOUR ASSES TO AIR GROOVE!"

"Yes ma'am!"

You have never dropped faster on all-fours in your life.

Hishi Amazon continues glowering at you until you complete a set of push-ups, before waggling her finger and leaving. As you sigh with relief, you catch Smart Falcon off in the distance, being berated by that German-accented uma. The two of you lock eyes. The enmity returns. The fire of competition resumes smoldering. This is not over. Smart Falcon mouths with a sneer, and you couldn't agree more.

[Intimidate has increased by 5.]

You work on your core muscles in a routine, that's ironically similar to the four bullies'. Elsewhere in the gym, chatter resounds.

"Damn. Opal's kid sure has a screw loose…"

"Why did I keep seeing a certain grey-haired uma over her…"

"Falcon, you have wasted not one, not two, but eight point five-two minutes on that spectacle. I simply cannot believe you. You have genuinely offended me!"

"My, my. The cheater's daughter has no lack of audacity. She must have inherited it from her mother."

"Pft…gyahahaha! That was lowkey fire! That was givin' main character energy for real! Nice one, rookie!"

[+2 to Light Alignment.]

[+3 to Chaos Alignment.]

[Overall Alignment did not shift.]

Later on, you would find out an anonymous person had recorded the whole spectacle and uploaded it to Tracen-adjacent spaces on the Internet. A lot of the commenters took time to heckle you, as expected. However, some of them praised you!

[Prestige has increased by 1.]

And even further than that, you would hear a certain Mejiro Dober had gone petrified at her gym buddy Agnes Digital not freaking out and drooling as the entire academy expected. Instead, she wore a tight-lipped, focused expression, her gaze glued solely onto you.

Your new social link
NameLevelDescriptionEffectsSmart Falcon-1A dirt racer and rival umadol who claims to be superior than you. Like hell you're letting her say that. Crush her in an umadol battle or let Tomorrow is FAITHFUL's honor remain tarnished! May appear in encounters.

>>[Event 2] The peppy, pure-hearted champion of the Japanese Derby, Special Week! (+1 to Guts)

The friend Grass Wonder invites is Special Week, her fellow Golden Generation member. Any doubts about her being as menacing as her title of Supreme Commander of Japan might imply instantly crumble as she bounds up from further along the park to you, then grasps your hand in a firm, vigorous shake.

"You must be Ruby! It's so good to finally meet you!" Special Week exclaims.

"L-likewise." You say, chuckling nervously. Special Week's grip is deceptively strong for such a cheery girl. "I hope most of those were good things."

"More like great! Grass talks about you all the time." Special Week says. "We were getting fruit salads for snacks last time, and she kept going on and on about what an unbelievably good stroke of fortune it was to become a student mentor. It definitely sounded like bragging."

Given that Grass Wonder has been talked about as being the strongest of the Golden Generation whilst being compared to legends such as Maruzensky, to hear that from Special Week is no short praise. A fluffy, lightheaded sensation wraps itself around your head and you can't help but grin like a loon."

"Spe…" Grass Wonder begins, "We don't want to give Ruby too big a head before tryouts, okay? She still has quite a way to go."

Special Week giggles, her ears twitching. She backs off with a playful, "Okay, okay!" Grass Wonder's words are mostly good humor, because you are aware how merciless Grass Wonder can be when she tries. Which is right now. The two older umas flank you, their movements synchronized, and your stomach drops.

"Ready, Ruby?" Grass Wonder says.

"Yeah…?"

"Good. It's time for the fun part."

"Don't worry. We'll be with you all the way!" Special Week adds. She squeezes you on the shoulder. Diving into the river and swimming through the floodwater has suddenly become ten times more appealing.

The following thirty minutes are designed to bolster your inner fortitude. There are mental locks in your brain set upon by the lack of racing experience, and they must be destroyed. Welcome to long jogging around the parks followed by rope skipping, jumping jacks and continuous push-ups on a mat on the grass. Any admiration for the simplicity of the exercises quickly vanishes in favor of the lactic acid burning up your joints and the steady thump of your heartbeat pounding between your ears. No asking for breaks. Only movement now.

Grass Wonder and Special Week both encourage you. The former calmly orders you to keep going. The latter exercises alongside you and barely pauses for breath in between her cheers. You're not certain which is worse.

"You can do it, Ruby! Thirty more skips to go. Think of all the sweets you can eat afterwards!"

"She'll be drinking my special tea, you mean."

"What Grass said! But you totally deserve a batch of sweets after the tryouts."

"I like…" You wheeze, feeling the jump rope almost slip out of your grip. "I like carrot cake!"

Special Week beams at you. "Me too! Let's go get some together, the three of us. Oh, we should invite Halo and El and Seiun too!"

A Golden Generation reunion for the most hated girl in the URA's future lineup. It sounds like the beginning of a bad comedy routine, except Special Week is one hundred percent serious. Then again, if this Hokkaido girl saved Japan from being humiliated on their own turf by the French, then perhaps she possesses all the leeway in the world.

Somehow, you manage to push through the barrage of exercises and end up collaping head-first onto the ground, where the cool dew soothes your ruddy, sweating skin.

[Guts has increased by 1!]

"Good work, Ruby. Here…"

Grass Wonder produces three flasks of kombucha out of a backpack. You sit on the grass with your two mentors, sipping the drinks. The sweet-sour tang is heavenly for your poor throat. Grass Wonder and Special Week then begin swapping stories from the previous year, more for your benefit than anything else. The time Special Week got kidnapped in a sack by Gold Ship, the donut eating contest Grass Wonder and El Condor Pasa judged that ended in Oguri's victory after Super Creek cheated, the time Special Week had to lock away all her prized carrots in the school warehouse just so she could focus on training. Grass Wonder brings up the Takazakura Kinen, and Special Week looks aside while shivering in response.

You briefly recall a sideways comment about how she just loves pressing Special Week's buttons to make her react. The decision never to irritate your mentor is once again reaffirmed.

"Are you excited to get your trainer, Ruby?" Special Week asks, after she recovers.

"You think I will?" You reply.

"Well…" Special Week hesitates. The obvious elephant in the room blows its trumpet. She then nods her head firmly. "Yeah! I'm sure you will. You've got so much potential. Grass thinks so, and so does the Prez!"

Rudolf thinks you have potential? She did assign you to the mentorship program in the first place. You suppose. That wouldn't have happened if she had thought you were going to waste her teammate's time.

"You can always go to Miss Tazuna or Director Akikawa for assistance." Grass Wonder adds. "They'll never turn down a student in trouble."

"I get it, and I know you guys are talking about. It's just…" You shrug. "Are trainers that really effective?"

Grass Wonder and Special Week nod in sync.

"Yes."

"Definitely!"

They are slightly confused too. On the surface, this is a question with an obvious answer. But, your education was stunted, so Grass Wonder must understand. She adopts a lecturing tone.

"The Trainers that reach the national level are very experienced and capable in understanding an umamusume's body. They are not nobodies. Each one has passed URA's gruelling Trainer exam. The filtering is so strict that, in some years, only ten percent of applicants pass."

"It's like having an extra pair of eyes and ears and a completely new brain looking after your body," Special Week adds. "That way, you don't have to worry as much and can focus on training and studying."

"But Grass is already doing that." You object.

Grass Wonder shakes her head. "Oh no, I'm not."

"But—"

"I'm flattered you think that, Ruby, but there's a major difference between our training sessions and a Trainer's job. I'm merely catching you up to the level of your peers. Your Trainer will push you to excel amidst the URA circuit. They'll write your exercise routines, design nutrition plans, figure out what races are best suited for your abilities, help you find information about your rivals—"

You remember that one from your first session. It's a good point.

"—and they'll do it with far more frequency and opportunity than what I can offer. I'm still a student, after all." Grass Wonder says. She places a hand on her heart, smiling. "I could not have won my G1s if it weren't for the expertise of my own trainer, Hana."

"And my trainer is super understanding and hardworking too!" Special Week chimes in, smiling. "He helped me believe in myself after a losing streak, and he never gave up on helping my friend Suzuka recover from her leg injury, even when other Trainers said she should retire."

You know which Suzuka she's talking about.

[History check: 40/35 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

Silence Suzuka, the front runner whose body collapsed on the turf, unable to sustain her record-breaking speeds. Had Special Week not rushed out to save her immediately, Silence Suzuka surely would have perished. The incident raised quite the scandal in the mainstream news, with reporters and newscasters debating about how safe umamusume racing truly was. It proved Special Week's noble heart; her initiative turned Manager Suzuki into her fan.

"Think of your Trainer as a combination of a manager and a coach." Grass Wonder says.

"And a sort of therapist, too. You can go to them when you're feeling down, and they'll make time to care for you."

Grass Wonder and Special Week radiate enthusiasm. It should be infectious. Indeed, there's a part of you that wants to cling on. But what if a nasty voice at the back of your head sighs. These two girls are G1 champions. They naturally attract the best of the best. Their Trainers have a vested interest in keeping them satisfied. You? Your mother betrayed her Trainer by cheating. She dragged them into hell with her. That incident made you radioactive.

And suppose you, against all odds, did attract a Trainer—so what? Tracen is not impenetrable. Its staff is not omniscient. Who's to say the Trainer you attract will even be a decent one? There are so many adults who should have been capable and compassionate and reliable to you, the child, and instead proved themselves to be as lazy and terrible as tyrants. The staff back at the shrine, who fed you empty promises about your mother to keep you pacified. The head miko, who never once smiled despite your efforts to please her. The big city had no shortage of that type. You once had the displeasure of encountering a coffin hotel manager who promised you a good pod, yet sold out your location to a local rag the next morning.

You pull your knees up to your chest and frown. Your mind wanders. Will your new Trainer give you as much leeway as your old manager? Will they be as forgiving as that man? You still owe Suzuki for not exiling you the moment he discovered your true age. He could have done it. He should have, in order not to risk the entire group a lawsuit. Instead, he kept a blind eye and pretended the confrontation between you and him got lost amidst a late-night drinking party with his boss. That's a lifetime debt right there.

If only he could magically switch careers, or if you could be tutored by Grass Wonder forever…how wonderful that would be.

"It can't always be sunshine and rainbows." You mutter.

"Nothing is." Grass Wonder comments. "But Tracen sets the national standard for a reason."

"Don't you guys ever argue with your Trainers?"

"Not really." Grass Wonder says. "Hana usually knows what she's doing. Whenever we raise objections, she usually provides an answer."

"Sometimes." Special Week replies, simultaneously. She pouts, folding her arms. "Mine can be a real jerk when he wants to be."

"A jerk?" You repeat.

"I almost forgot you were part of Spica, Spe." Grass Wonder says, and sighs. "Ruby, please don't follow their example too much. Spica is somewhat of an anomaly, even amongst the more eccentric teams."

"Hey!" Special Week protests. "We're not that bad."

"You told me Gold Ship kidnapped you in a sack." Grass Wonder counters, sounding deadpan.

"W-water under the bridge!" Special Week protests.

"And last fortnight you kept complaining about how your Trainer never fails to point out whenever you gain weight—which is entirely your fault, I may add." Grass Wonder says.

"It's not my fault the cafeteria has so many good snacks! Stop bullying me, Grass!" Special Week whines. "You're just saying this because Spica's your rival. I could dig up as much dirt about your Trainer as I wanted!"

"Like?" Grass Wonder prompts.

Special Week hesitates. "Um…"

Grass Wonder smiles, tilting her chin up with pride. "I rest my case."

Special Weeks pouts. "I'm not done yet! I bet your Trainer has skeletons in her closet too, like mine when he—"

Grass Wonder's smile drops like an anchor. She shoots Special Week a glare, which on any other umamusume would be a profanity-ridden screaming fit. It works. Special Week pales. She hastily shoves to tip of her flask into her mouth and takes a deep, long gulp.

"Like?" You ask. "What did he do?"

"Nothing important." Grass Wonder says after a pause. There's a hint of dark disdain in her tone. "Nothing you should be concerned about, Ruby."

Special Week nods in agreement so fervently the ribbons begin to unravel out of her hair.

But you are concerned about it, since this is a red flag if you've ever seen one, and a Trainer is your future. That's why after bidding the two girls goodbye, you crash on your bed back in your dorm, pull out your phone and dig for information about Team Spica's Trainer.

[Social Media check: 52/30 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

It is on that comfortable afternoon that you discover two particular infamous highlights of Trainer Okino's career.

The first is that he was temporarily suspended for touching multiple umamusume's ankles without permission, a tendency that his psychological evaluation revealed these acts were somehow entirely non-sexual in intent and were actually done in pure appreciation for the beauty of the umamusume form. Director Akikawa still raked him over hot coals for acting like a complete moron, which he was.

The second is that the trainees of Team Spica frequently roughhouse the man in the form of…wrestling moves? And Trainer Okino never fails to climb back onto his feet with a smile, utterly unscathed by this endless conga line of umamusume assaults? Are you reading this right? Is his skeleton constructed from titanium?

Combined, these two wrongs…make a right? It's karma in motion, except it's rumored the Spica girls haven't stopped haranguing their Trainer after he stopped with highlight one. If Gold Ship, notorious troublemaker, and a bonafide Mejiro remain under Trainer Okino's tuition, it means he's an okay guy? Special Week thinks so. You are so confused.

Umastagram echoes your sentiments. There are as many fangirls of the man's handsome looks as proponents of his immediate expulsion from Tracen's faculty.

This leads you to researching the other trainers, and you find out that…

"Trainer Nase and Super Creek disappear behind closed doors whenever Creek wins a race…"

"Trainer Minamizaka is totally a hackerman."

"Trainer Hana doesn't sleep."

"Trainer Kuronuma was cursed by a one-eyed demon never to cover up his abs."

"Team IKZE is a secret government experiment to see how hard umas can psychologically torture a man before he breaks."

"Trainer Kitahara is secretly dating Oguri Cap's mom!"

Are you…going to be okay?

[History has increased by 5.]

You do spot something else of note amidst the rumors.

[Visual Mathematics check: 50/50 -> +10 EXP.]

It's Kitahara Jo—or rather, his famous cap. The Trainer who supervised your physical exam wore a cap of the same shape. The sun had set back then, casting the-then deserted empty stadium in a veil of shadow. The man stood in the darkness, watching you run laps across the turf with a stopwatch in hand. You weren't able to see much of the man's face, nor did he give you his name. When you tried to follow him, he apologised and said that an urgent matter demanded his return to the office. You never saw him again.

Maybe…

Nah.

There are probably thousands of those flat-rimmed caps out there. No way you were examined by the Kitahara Jo. Adding Oguri Cap on LANE was insane enough.

>>[Event 3] The Charm drink. (Must get 5 or above)

The beanie-wearing girl slugs down the rest of the canned drink. She does not fall to her knees and convulse on the spot; rather, the opposite happens: a deep, satisfied belch that sends her into a brief laughing fit. Does that mean the drinks are safe to consume? You squint at the vending machine's display and decide this is still suspicious. Any woman who slathers her clothes in red that gaudy is clearly compensating for her product; to say nothing of the stories surrounding her.

Then again, you suppose, it can't be that bad. No-one's placing toxic substances in a spot so easily accessible by the student populace. The alternative is earning the ire of the Symbolis, the Golds and Tracen's other wealthy sponsors. There are faster ways of committing financial suicide.

"Oh, you're getting in there." The beanie-wearing girl comments, flashing you a sardonic grin.

"I'm a little thirsty." You say. This is totally the reason and definitely not you wanting to act brave in front of a Gold.

You insert the coins. They fall with metallic clunks. Lights on the machine flash to life, a tinny, cheerful voice congratulating from a small speaker. It sounds like those jilted, middle-aged housewives who go to Shinjuku cabaret clubs and try too hard to sound young to the male hosts. You examine the lineup and settle on hitting the button labelled 'Charm'.

The can falls to the bottom. You take it out.

"Last chance to back out."

"I don't waste food."

"Respectable." The beanie-wearing girl flicks a smirk your way.

"Bottoms up." You comment and pop the lid. The girl crosses one leg over the other, watching you with interest.

The first mouthful almost elicits a gag. Take the chalkiness inherent in health drinks, thicken the texture, then boil foreign herbs and roots to add a bitter, sour aftertaste. Sprinkle in lumps reminiscent of boba tea seeds without the sweetness before running it through a dirt filter. Voila! One Charm drink, ready to serve.

Yet, the moment you let the drink settle, an invigorating sensation overtakes you. Your feet feel lighter, your skin shinier, your skin smoother. It's like stepping out of a perfume commercial.

[All PSY-scaling skills have increased by 3!]

[Mood has gone up to Good.]

"Not bad, right?"

"No, it tastes terrible. It's worse than medicine. I have friends who would take me to the hospital to get my stomach pumped. But it's working."

The beanie-wearing girl grins. "No shot?"

"My heart is fluttering. My tongue is freshening. There are ideas for speeches and debates and cool ways to snap Umastagram photos flowing through my head!" You press two fingers to your forehead, and exhale with a growing, maniacal grin. "I'm getting another."

The girl barks out a peal of laughter. "Hell yeah. Let's roll the slots again!"

A fire lights under you. Grinning like madwomen, you and the beanie-wearing girl pump in more coins, both of you selecting the option at the top of the listing. You clink your can with the new girl's own, pop the lid open, and tip your head back in preparation to drink.

The first drops never touch your tongue. This is due to Miss Tazuna screeching around the corner at the end of a furious sprint. She hurls a pair of office pens, smashing the cans straight out of you and the beanie-wearing girl's grips and completely obliterating the vending machine in the process. As you stand there, staring at the smoking piece of aluminum in your open palm, Miss Tazuna asks both you and the beanie-wearing girl whether or not you're alright, begins a lecture on what a terrible idea it is to drink from shady vending machines, and finally snaps her fingers. Two burly security guards pop out of the bushes and haul the shattered vending machine away.

That's the end of that.

"Well, that was anticlimactic. Shucks. I wanted to try the top one." The beanie-wearing girl grouses. She shifts her look down the path, and grins. "Hey. Wanna go and see what Tabaru's up to?"

"…sure?"

You end up strolling down to the Tracen racetrack with the girl by your side. That's how you learn the girl's name: Nakayama Festa, member of the Gold Clan, Tracen's reckless gambler, and the umamusume who came the closest to winning the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe for Japan. A formidable pedigree for such an easygoing outlook. Perhaps that's why the moment Tabaru catches sight of Festa, she screeches to a halt, and bows her head. Her elaborate twintails drape across her back.

"Sister."

Festa laughs and wraps her hand around Tabaru's shoulders. "C'mon. No need to act so stiff. I'm not here to pester you. In fact, I just stumbled across your roommate near some weird vending machine. We got to chatting. She's right here."

"I know." Tabaru replies. "I can see her."

"Hi, Tabaru." You say and wave.

"She's not bad. Not bad at all. We were worried about you, y'know? Coming here to nats after you cleaned up those messes back in Hokkaido. Drejour and the old man, especially." Festa continues. "Think they'll be coming around to check on you more often."

"I see you guys all the time."

"Yeah, but we need to catch up. Go out to the baseball cages, or something."

If Tabaru is frightened by this, she doesn't show it. You, however, feel your tail jerk itself at a perfect ninety-degree angle. This is not helped as Festa eyes you again, and winks.

What have I done?

"So, none of your lackeys today?"

"Remedial lessons." Tabaru replies.

"Thought you'd be with them."

"Pelte told me I didn't need to worry about it. So, I'm not."

Festa laughs again, and you detect a jovial satisfaction in her tone. She's pleased Tabaru is alone for her to enjoy, your existence notwithstanding. "Whatcha up to?"

Tabaru points to the structure positioned further down the turf. A network of iron bars and meshes with an inert light up top. "…gate training."

Because no uma ever wants to end up like Gold Ship and her twelve billion incident.

You decide to join in, too.

[+10 added to the next starting gate roll!]

[Meisho Tabaru's Social Link has updated. Dream Journey, Orfevre, Gold Ship, Nakayama Festa, Fenomeno and/or Stay Gold may now appear…]

3.3: Daily Life V

>>[Event 4 Part 1] Aston Machan.

>>[Event 4 Part 2] Lavender. (Honesty, devotion, and loyalty)

The newcomer will be a marshmallow: soft, fluffy, sweet, and not without a core of her own. The inexplicableness of this thought shall not be known until it flashes back a fortnight later. It is as natural in the present as your tongue tasting the faint tinge of paper fibre in the air.

"Good day, Miss Brian. Good day to you too, Satono Ruby."

The newcomer is an umamusume of average height, with short messy brown hair and an emperor's crown for a hair ornament. The latter is no indication of royalty, just another participant in a semi-common fashion trend involving crowns, tiaras, diadems and other emblems that symbolize conquest or victory—of which even you are a part . Orfevre, the Golden Tyrant, should spring to mind, yet you can only think back to that top-heavy, tiara-wearing girl: Daiwa Scarlet of Team Spica. She has never placed any lower than second in her official races.

The comparison between this newcomer and it feels fitting, like a key sliding in place amidst a lock.

"Hi. Nice to meet you." You say to the newcomer. "Guess I don't need to introduce myself."

"I wouldn't mind. I'd like to hear who you are in your own words." The newcomer says, her voice soft, yet clear in the spacious room. "Rumors only tell us so much."

It's a kind gesture. You won't hold back, then. You offer your hand. "Satono Ruby, then. Former underground umadol and another rookie who's aiming for the top."

The smile the newcomer delivers is the opposite of that arrogance. She takes your hand. Her palm is a delicate one with well-defined lines in the flesh. "My name is Aston Machan. It's nice to meet you too. My goal is to become a mascot."

A mascot?

[Wits check: 9/6 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

"Like Hachiko?" You ask.

"Yep. Hachiko, Kumamom, the WcDonalds arch, even. We have similar goals, but different destinations." Machan says. "I'd like my name to travel to all sorts of places, for myself to fall into hands of many shapes and sizes, for my races to be viewed across the world's screens."

"Ooh, big merch deal plans, then."

"Yes. I'd like a statue of mine to seen from space. I want to become a super mascot."

She emphasies the super in a dreamy, airy tone. You giggle. You can't help it. Machan's goal is…egostical. There's no other way you can phrase it. If that were all, you'd end it with more humor, but you can't—there's something else. The way she framed her ambition is peculiar. It sounded pure, the opening monologue to a fairy-tale dream. Her influence will be for the benefit of others as much as for herself.

You try to find any hint of irony and discover none. Machan's serious, too. Completely, one hundred percent, serious. This is not a class clown you're shaking hands with.

Few are beloved by a nation, less so by multiple countries, never mind the entire world. This girl will need fame, lots and lots of it. The two of you might end up clashing in the upcoming tryouts. Still, she seems friendly enough off the track.

You and Machan let go of the handshake. The moment you do, a memory flashes.

"Hey, you're in the class next to mine." You say.

Machan blinks. "I am?"

You snap your fingers. "Yeah, you're the one across the hall. I've seen you through the classroom window. You're always fiddling…" You think for a moment. "With that phone? No, not a phone…"

"A recorder." Machan reaches into her uniform pocket and withdraws the device. She holds the recorder up proudly. An old model with a black oblong body, reminiscent of the ones found in the Akibahara electronic stores.

"Yeah, that one. I've seen you a couple of times. What do you use it for?" You say.

"An audio diary. I enjoy recording my own thoughts." Machan replies.

"Oh, sweet! I used to record my own singing and play them back during practice. It used to be super embarrassing, and it still is, but one of my fellow idols told me all artists cringe a lot at their own work. It's part of the learning process."

"It is lovely to remember who you once were."

"Yeah, that's a way of looking at it. You gotta bring the past into the future to create real art." And now you're missing songwriting with the girls. Maybe you can join in on the old chat room via LANE and catch up with Kaede, if homework doesn't eat up your evening time first.

A sharp clap of hands.

"Oi. This isn't the cafeteria. Get to work, girls." Narita Brian grunts. "We don't have all day."

You look back at the laptop.

"Are you sure we're meant to be doing this?" You ask.

"Got a problem?" Narita Brian asks.

Yeah, are you loading us with jobs you don't want? You say, in a universe where you want to be thrown out of a nearby window.

"None of us are expert flower arrangers…I think." You say.

"My mother is a doctor." Machan says, raising her hand. "Sometimes, I helped with filling vases with flowers for the patients. A nice nurse helped me with a few basic tips."

"You were an assistant, Machan?" You ask.

Machan shakes her head. "No. The hospital was my playground. My mother was a very busy woman. She refused to leave me at home."

A hospital kid, then. Similar to the idol's kid, except those don't have to be hidden away as their moms and dads prance around on stage. How wanting to be a mascot relates to a childhood of often seeing sick people, you're uncertain. It must have been a tough upbringing, regardless.

"If the Prez needed a professional arranger, she'd hire one." Narita Brian says, taking on a slightly annoyed tone. "We're just asking for your opinion. That's all. Quit thinking too hard about it and hurry up."

You and Machan look at each other and shrug. Fair enough. You both crowd around the laptop, shoulders bumping for an instant. Her hair smells faintly of lilies, her skin bearing the shiny freshness of good cleaning. There are worse umas to partner with on group projects.

"Ooh, I like that one."

"Those wilt too fast."

"They do?"

"Indoors, they will. It'd be a shame if those poor plants were put on display, only to wither away in days. No-one would have time to appreciate them. It'd be a tragedy."

"I guess so. It'd look bad for the academy if there were a bunch of dead plants everywhere. How about jasmine?"

"Mmm…I'm not sure that fits the school motto."

[(Inspection check: 34/40 || Insight check: 10/7) -> Success! +5 EXP.]

After examining a few more pictures and doing a few online searches, you both land on lavender. The amount of time Narita Brian spends confirming it is pitifully small compared to the time you and Machan spent discussing it.

It works, though. A few days later, you're in the reception hall, awed at the sight of lavender flowers placed on the welcoming desk and in plant pots along windowsills. A fresh, woody yet sweet scent wafts between the furniture, easing a few rough edges brought about by your training.

Machan is here with you, too. She was here from the beginning, smiling from the entrance hall, as if you and her arranged a rendezvous. You caught her peeking out from behind the wall.

"Wonderful, isn't it?"

You turn around and gasp. "Prez!"

Rudolf approaches down the hall, waving a hand. It's such a casual greeting, yet her neatly groomed hair and the confident gait she carries herself with both grant the gesture a solid foundation of authority. You and Machan cannot help but bow slightly in its presence.

"Hello Ruby, Machan. Good to see both of you. No need to act so formal in my presence." Rudolf says. "I'm here to congratulate you both. Thanks for pitching in at such short notice."

"No, no, it was our honour. We didn't expect you to take our suggestions so seriously." You say, lifting your head.

"Air Groove liked them." Narita Brian says, popping out from behind Rudolf. In comparison, her walk is far more casual and carries the sluggishness of a sibling dragged along by her elder's antics. "I'm not disagreeing with her."

"She's very fussy about Tracen's flowers." Rudolf adds. "If she approves them, it's good enough for me."

It's a small contribution you've made. Nothing on par with organizing budget reports or dealing with troublemakers. Yet, you can't help but puff up with pride somewhat. Take that, Diamond, Crown. Those two may have money and connections and fancy beds, but you assisted the Symboli Rudolf herself.

Machan holds out her phone. "May I take some photos of us together? I'd like to commemorate the occasion."

Rudolf smiles. "Go ahead."

Machan gets to work. snaps a few photos, mostly selfies involving you, Rudolf, Narita Brian and the lavender flowers. You flash a peace sign, Narita Brian rolls her eyes at first but puts on a stoic grin anyway, and Rudolf displays her usual public image smile. Machan forwards the photos to your LANE account, along with the student council's official inbox, then tucks away her phone with a satisfied hum.

"I must say, the purple really does bring out the color of the wallpaper here." Rudolf comments.

"They could've looked like weeds instead." Narita Brian says.

"I must say, as a symbol, lavender is appropriate."

"You think?" You say.

"Why, yes. Its three primary meanings—loyalty, devotion and honesty—can be applied to Tracen itself. We should be loyal to our friends and to each other to foster strong bonds. We must be devoted to our craft to achieve excellence. And we should be honest and unabashed about not just what we have achieved, but what we are as individuals. Only then may we be able to truly understand each other as fellow competitors." Rudolf finishes. "That's the draft of the article I'm writing for the school newsletter. I could use some editing, of course. But they are wonderful flowers."

She then chuckles, lifting a hand beneath her chin. "I love'n'adore them."

You stand there, grinning in admiration of Rudolf's intellectual prowess. And then—

…huh?

The spite rolls off the girl, a dark, oily cloud like the thick smoke from a barrel fire. You cannot see her face, but you've faced this form of enmity before. Shinjuku, walking through the main lane at night after a long concert. Hotaru and Miki split up to take care of their businesses, so it was just you, Keade, Saya and Manager Suzuki heading towards a barbecue place for a late dinner. Manager Suzuki pointed out those unsavory fellows—distraught gamblers, the ruddy-faced alcoholics, hollow-faced salarymen retreating from their corporation enclaves. He spotted their trademarks like a detective on a case. He warned you not to go close, not when they were wallowing like that, because they might do terrible things to a lonesome young girl.

But this is not Shinjuku, nor an adult you're conversing with. It's a fellow Tracen student who vented, opened her heart to you, as thorny as it is. You are here. You are available to help, even for a fraction. Why should you leave?"

"Do you want to hear it?" You ask.

No response. It's not a 'no', either. You take a moment to gather your thoughts, then inhale.

"But?" The girl in the stump prompts.

The girl snorts. "After she abandoned you?"

"She was pregnant with me for her first year at the academy. There are old news articles of her carrying me as a baby around Tracen and showing me off to her old classmates." You sigh, feeling mist gathering in your eyes. You wrap one hand around the silver bullet and let its weight rest against your palm. "Mom loved me."

The girl snorts again. She spits out a mocking laugh. "So, you're clinging onto the memory of a woman who's probably dead?" The girl sneers.

"She's not dead." You say firmly.

"That's what I'm talking about. You're so naïve, it's sickening."

"I choose to believe she's alive. I believe she had a good reason for what she did." You say.

"Like the Satonos, right?" The girl counters. "Diamond and Crown, wishing they had mauled their auntie's kid in the womb. That's totally a good reason, right?"

"They were my friends before. Maybe they can be again." You reply.

"They hate you. You're doing nothing but running away from the problem!" The girl screeches. "You've done it before, and you will again!"

"It's not the first time. My friends in my old idol unit didn't like me when I first met." You say.

That shuts the girl up.

You smile wistfully, as the nostalgia creeps up.

"Two of them thought I was trying to style on them, because they were human and I was the young, exotic uma. They pestered me for a while, gave me the hard jobs. I didn't know how to handle myself in the face of their teasing; several times I was brought to tears, which usually ended in me running to the bathroom to cry—before the group leader taught me how to stand up for myself. It might sound like we shouldn't have gotten along at all, but after weeks of practice sessions and a lot of events, some successful and loads of them unsuccessful, the barriers between us thawed. You conclude with a shrug and a smile. "If it happened before, it could happen."

"It might not." The girl says.

"But it could."

"How reassuring." The girl mutters. "We're talking in circles."

"They weren't the only friends I made in the underground. There were also others: rival umadols, concert staff, even my manager, whose tact falls out of his brain when talking to us girls! "I think there's enough wonderful and plentiful and beautiful parts of this world that I shouldn't count out, just because my life was hard before."

You're sitting on the grass now, watching the girl's chest slowly rise and fall from the side. That's the trouble with these speeches. The anticipation is grueling. You can mean every word you said, but if the recipient is mired so hard in their own misery, then any lifeline you throw at them will unravel into twine. Maybe if you were older, possessed more life experience and connections like Kaede, or were as charming and popular as Curren Chan or Gold City, you could have filled the silence better, solidified this unsteady connection between you and this girl.

You still remember the first day you arrived in the big city. The escape from the shrine had tuckered you out completely; you slept through the ride straight to Tokyo. When the station announcement rang and bodies started shifting, you tottered to your feet and let yourself be swept along. You flitted nervously through the station halls, so afraid of being crushed by bodies like in those earthquake horror stories, that you clung to the wall the whole way through. It was more people than you had ever encountered in your entire life, and you hadn't reached the surface yet.

But, you did. Against the crowd, against the fear of having your mother's shoes stolen, against your complete ineptitude of knowing how a train pass even worked! You pushed past the morning rush, trod up the staircase and took your first step into Tokyo. Shibuya Crossing, 19XU. You stood in the shadow of the underpass, gazing forward and upward.

The tarmac gleamed brightly and hot in the sunshine. The department stores towered like giants. Humans and umamusume strolled around the crossing, each one dressed in slick tops and bottoms bearing colors and patterns you had only grasped at in your dreams. They ate gigantic, cheese-filled sandwiches and sipped drinks from oversized cups as music blared from the rooftops, so rapid in its beat and sounding so much like the lightning that it sent your tail swishing in tune from multiple blocks away. You pressed buttons on a strange machine near the statue of Hachiko and it spat out a chocolate ice-cream loaded with rainbow sprinkles. The big city was a fairytale kingdom constructed from concrete and steel, and you were free to run around it as much as you wanted.

You smiled. You giggled hysterically. You walked into a WcDonalds and bought the biggest burger on the menu. You thought that as long as you lived in Tokyo, you could do anything—including racing like the umamusume on the big billboard screen attached to the 109 building, an advertisement for Tracen itself. That was the honeymoon phase, of course. Tokyo proved to possess its own rules. You walked the line on more than a few occasions during your years in the underground. Yet, you cherish the memory of that first day. You wish you could serve the hope you felt on a platter to this forlorn girl.

Because that's what it was. Hope.

As long as a day like that existed, and the following days were comparable to it, then you held hope.

"You got lucky." The girl says, eventually.

"Yeah." You admit, "I was. I was very fortunate to have met Manager Suzuki near Hachiko."

The girl scoffs. "Just wait for the cosmic roll of the dice. Brilliant. Just pray and hope everything works out well. Don't do a damn thing!"

You shake your head. "I didn't just pray. I worked hard. I had to make my own luck. I chose to sing my lungs hoarse at Shibuya until someone noticed me. You need to grow your perseverance."

"Then what are we supposed to do when our Trainers are second-rate morons, and we can't catch up to Rudolf or El Condor Pasa or Orfevre because we weren't born right?"

You don't know. You're not a scientist. But…

"I wouldn't sit around doing nothing. I'd try."

The girl howls. A laugh that wails and ends in a coughing fit spitting with phlegm. She slams a fist against the ground. "This isn't some puppy-dog league where you can get a makeover, shake your ass for some filthy salarymen and get showered in money. Races don't award participation medals. You're either on the podium, or you're not!"

"There's not just one race."

"The body degrades. The muscles tear, the heart squeezes itself stop. At some point, you don't improve. You run and run and only get worse. Just ask Oguri Cap, or that mother of yours!"

You smile drops. "Excuse me?"

"Satono Opal! You think an uma can push past her limits and reach some kind of epic singularity? This isn't fantasyland. Opal faltered. She burned out, slid downhill too. Because she couldn't hack it, she ended up sticking her cunt in the wrong places and paid the price!"

It's come to this, then. The usual jeers. The old accusations. No matter. You've built up resistance to them. You stand up from the grass, brushing dirt and stray strands off your tracksuit.

"You'll end up just like her." The girl shouts. "You'll end up in the graveyard of broken dreams like the rest of us! Count on it, Ruby!"

You don't respond. You've said all you wanted to say to this girl, and you're reaffirmed your own values. Sometimes, that's enough.

"Ruby."

A familiar voice. You turn around and raise a hand in greeting. "Morning, Tabaru!"

Your roommate jogs over to you, dressed in the tracksuit. Her crisscrossing braids flail behind her, well-maintained as ever. She frowns. "You were screaming into the stump?"

"Nope. I was talking to this girl. She was the one screaming, not me." You say.

"What girl?" Tabaru asks.

"The one right there."

Tabaru's frown grows bigger. "The heck are you talking about?"

"She's right there, Tabaru. Look—"

But Tabaru only squints over your shoulder. Sighing, you turn around, ready to admonish your roommate. Instead, you can only blink. The area around the stump is empty. No girl, no fragments of bark, not even a single indent in the grass where the girl kneeled.

"Huh?" You say, dumbfounded. What's going on?

"You sure you were talking to someone there?" Tabaru asks.

"Positive!"

"Did she leave?"

"No. She can't have. She was right there, Tabaru. She was a student like us in her uniform!"

Tabaru stares at you for a few seconds. "Why?"

Her question slams the brakes on your thought processes. "Pardon?"

"Why would she be dressed in her uniform at this hour? It's cold. Everyone who comes out this early wears a tracksuit for their morning run."

"I…" You swallow a lump in your throat. "…you're right."

Tabaru peers at you. Her frown has deepened into one of concern. "Ruby, are you sleepwalking?"

Were this yesterday, you'd be affronted, maybe annoyed, and brushed it off. Today, you don't answer. Instead, you examine the stump. A hollow shape surrounded by dead wood, its cavity a pitch-black deeper than the night. It is a place where losers go to vent their frustrations in the shadow of the glorious winner. And it's empty. But it was full mere seconds ago. There was a conversation here, its memory crystal clear, and now it's a contradiction, which means…

You mouth goes dry. You clutch your silver bullet harder. The flesh in your palm digs painfully into the metallic shell.

Look. You know you aren't a normal girl. The longer you lived in the underground, the more you came to understand this. Normal people don't describe strangers with the colors and metaphors of artforms. They don't spin little trinkets or gaze at plants to decide where to go. They don't look down side streets and see the shadows creeping out before them, scrawling messages akin to cave paintings on the concrete that piece together into warning signs. Ever since you cracked your head on the shrine grounds, your mind has been attuned to a special frequency innate to sapient beings. It spits out information like a fuzzy radio station, the helpful portions manifesting as an abnormal intuition.

You never once sought out a fortune-teller or a mystic to check that intuition. You were afraid some of them might be linked back to the shrine at first. Then, you became too busy with your idol work to care. Your intuition faded into the background, a semi-conscious ability on the same level as breathing or hunger.

Now?

There's a tinny whining in your head, and it's transforming into a full-on scream.

"Tabaru?" You croak.

"Yeah?"

You step back from the stump, clammy sweat trickling down the sides of your cheeks. You barely resist the urge to clutch yourself.

"I…" I feel like my fingers were inches from brushing against a swarm of furious wasps, or a chalkboard stuffed with a dozen rusty nails teeming with tetanus. I feel like if I put my head down that stump, it will never come back out.

"I don't like the stump very much." You finish shakily.

Tabaru stares at you. She nods, and beckons with her hand. "Let's get jogging, then."

Together, you and Tabaru set off on your morning jog. You set a pace faster than usual, switching routes so you head into Fuchu earlier than usual. Tabaru doesn't comment. You are thankful for that, more so when Grass Wonder's sessions arrive and you can focus on tearing apart your own physique from the inside out.

Later that day, you would hear the news of a rusty switchblade hidden in the grass near the stump. It would be discovered by an up-and-coming runner for the Classics pricking her bare foot on it. She would contract an infection so horrendous it would penetrate the bone and retire her for the rest of the year.

Two months ago, you could never have imagined yourself not just enduring, but acclimatising to a G1 champion's almost-Spartanesque training regimen. There are theories of racing tactics and slipstreams and disruption counter-wars threatening to fall out of your brain!

And yet, your childhood was stunted. You were never granted resources other umamusume spoiled themselves with. Malnutrition in the big city left you stranded.

Are those two months really enough for you to close the gap between you and the top rookie of the year?

"Grass?"

"Yes?"

"Do you think I can beat her?"

"Kitasan?" Grass Wonder taps the side of her cheeks. "Well, what do you think?"

"I asked you."

"I know. I'm still asking you that question." Grass Wonder looks you straight in the eye, her smile dropping for her a steely determination. It causes you to do a double take. You fidget with your fingers, now put on the spot.

"What do you think, Ruby?" Grass Wonder asks.

You blink. You avert your gaze, tugging your knees up to the chest. You lift your head and seek the wisps of clouds floating through the clear blue sky for advice. Breakfast in the cafeteria rewinds and plays back in your head.

After you read the tryout listings, you placed your phone back in your pocket, grabbed your chopsticks and resumed eating. Tabaru and Pelte maybe glanced at each other, maybe tried to tug your sleeve and prompt further conversation, but you weren't in the mood. You were once again zoning out, focusing on grabbing pockets of rice to lift to your greedy mouth, as conversation floated through one ear and went out through the other.

"She's conked out of it, boss." Pelte said. "Looks like she just got punched. Let's come back later."

"The bottom seed against the top seed?" Jewel whispered to Tomoe. "That's rough."

"That's some cosmic or divine mockery right there. Poor Ruby. She's going to get her ass whooped." Tomoe replied.

"Finally, someone's going to put that bitch in her place." You overheard someone from the corner say.

"I almost feel sorry for her." Another girl added.

"Do you think the Prez rigged the listings? Maybe she wants that girl gone as much she will." A third girl chimed in.

From across the ferns: "The match is gonna be boring to watch. No-one can beat Kitasan. Not even Bourbon or Top Gun."

"What a snore."

"So? How many carrots on her late start? Two? Three? All five?"

"Ten! I'll take ten!"

"Hey, wasn't Satono Ruby? Wasn't she training with Grass Wonder?"

"That's just a rumor. No way the Grass is wasting a time with that bitch."

"I hope she trips on her shoelaces."

"I hope she just leaves the academy and finds another school elsewhere. It's not as if Tracen is the only school in Japan."

"What kind of style does she run with, anyway?"

"Immediate-surrender style, duh."

"Geez, maybe we should apologise on behalf of Kitasan. This isn't gonna pose a challenge at all."

"Maybe we should write her a card."

"Maybe we should invite her out to eat! And bring Diamond along with her."

"It's like a goldfish challenging a freakin' whale."

"D'you think Opal ever expected her kid to even get this far?"

"I bet she wants her to fail. Think about it!"

The voices ebb and flow. They echo and dissipate. In the present, you open and close your fists.

"She's in my way." You say.

Grass Wonder's ears twitch forward, and that's all. There's not even an anticipatory flare of her nostrils.

"The winner gets the best chance of getting a good Trainer. Everyone thinks she's going to beat me. The Trainers think she's going to beat me. They've going to use every trick in the book to find a reason not to accept me, because they think I'm my mother. That means I have to come in first, which means Kitasan is in my way."

You inhale a breath. Your hands shake. The body language you displayed back in the cafeteria repeats: Eyelids fluttering, lips curled, ears pointed forward; and your teeth gritted, your left hand's fingernails digging into the fabric covering your lower half. You wear a smile that is less of a smile and more of a detestable contortion via the malleable curvature of flesh.

[Guts check: 9/9 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

Grass Wonder isn't fazed. You keep going.

"I don't want to lose. I don't want to lose to Kitasan. She might've had a headstart and better equipment and maybe even trained with Dia together for years, but I don't care. I put in the effort. I have results too!" You say, voice growing louder. "If there's even a slightest bit of chance I can win, I'll seize it!"

You curl your fist and clench it, and you realise you are angry—yes, angry. Amidst the anticipatory excitement of the race and the fear of failure, you hold legitimate ire directed at Kitasan. It isn't a morning thing. It perhaps goes back to when the two of you met in that athletics shop. The reason is simple: she's Diamond's best friend. She's the uma who knows her best. She held a position that once was yours in a very happy moment of your life, and she sat like a mannequin in that coffee palace and lowered her head and did nothing.

Was that a silent affirmation? Does she believe your birth was wrong? Does she want your mother's shoes, too?

Why does Diamond like her, and not you?

Grass Wonder mulls over your words. She takes her time, so much so, you begin to wonder if you've said something wrong.

"I give that a seven out of ten." Grass Wonder says.

"Only seven?" You exclaim.

"You are still new. I'd give you the estimation in rookie numbers, but we are measuring you with a different stick. At least you didn't say, 'I'll do my best'."

"Um…"

"People like to attribute that to Spe, but the thing about Spe is that she eventually stopped saying that." Grass Wonder says, and claps her hands. "In any case, you're fired up now. Good. Stay that way."

"Thanks…?"

Is Grass Wonder teasing you? Is this how she lightens the mood—by critiquing others? It's working, you suppose. You're brimming with motivation whilst having left some of the tension behind.

"Keep Kitasan in mind as we go over your other opponents." Grass Wonder points to a section on her phone. "One of them is quite interesting. Hana was talking about them last weekend…"

(Who is that other interesting opponent? Note that the listed tags are not exhaustive for each uma)

[] [Opponent] Mihono Bourbon (Style: Front Runner; Tags: Speed, Breathing)

[] [Opponent] Kawakami Princess (Style: Late Surger; Tags: Power, Frenzy)

[] [Opponent] Happy Meek (Style: ?; Tags: Wits, Traversal)

[] [Opponent] Mayano Top Gun (Style: Pace Chaser; Tags: Insight, Racing Tactics)

[] [Opponent] Cheval Grand (Style: Pace Chaser; Tags: Stamina, Pain Threshold)

Morning, May 30th, 20XX

"Each of the umamusume is surging forward with all their might! We have no idea who'll pull ahead. Oh, but a racer just broke out of the pack. She's gaining, she's gaining, Vivlos is gaining, the front's trying to box her in, but she's not stopping—and she's done it!" The commentator screams, and you can imagine her on her feet in the booth overlooking the racetrack. "Vivlos has won her tryout race, the first one of the day!"

The girl, a bright-eyed gal with blue ribbons intertwined through her twintails, throws off her number patch and jumps on the spot past the finish line, waving to the cheering crowd. A couple of journalists rush down to the turf, small camera crews following. A bright sun shines down them all.

Welcome to the Tracen Academy tryouts. It's not even the maiden races, yet the fervor is palpable. The entire academy, and by extension a good portion of the Japanese racing world, has been looking forward to this date for a while.

You are no exception.

This is it. This is what the past two months have been leading up to. You'll perform in your second-ever race and either win a Trainer in the first step of a proper racing career, or crash straight to the ground before the first hurdle. It's one or the other. And it'll be viewed by a crowd of hundreds.

Butterflies flutter in your stomach, barely suppressed as you straighten your back and roll your shoulders.

Calm down, Ruby. Calm down. You've got this. Grass is backing you up. Goddesses sake, your race isn't even here yet.

It's true. You check your phone. According to the official schedule, there's a few hours before your race begins. There's still time to roam around and take in some sights in this all-day event. Alternatively, you can keep sitting here in this shade offered by a nearby tree, a good distance away from any prying eyes.

Please don't let my future Trainer be a creep...

3.5: Starting Line

Mood: Good

EXP: 40/150

"Salsa Step tries to catch up, but—Mayano! Mayano Top Gun maintains her lead. She dashes through the final stretch, and she crosses the finish line! Mayano Top Gun is our victor!"

The tryouts are a minnow, an elaborate dress rehearsal, compared to the main URA races, yet with every new victor, the bleachers roar. Claps. Cheers. The clicking of cameras with their pretty silver flashes. It's the usual in the biz, and it shouldn't tense your gut nor tempt you to paw the ground with your foot, but Tracen is different. It is powerful, so much so that a minor event like this swarms with the press, that the turf supercharges with energy to rival several late-night finales in the underground halls.

It's tempting to join in. Walk around, strike up conversation, snap a few pics and chomp a few snacks. It really is. You can't. The risk of bumping into a journalist is too high. They'll ask too many questions, maybe throw you off your game. Grass Wonder offered to accompany you—you declined, citing this reason, and she acquised. Your mentor is beloved, but she knows how bad the press can be.

So you stay where you are. You park your bottom further down on the hard white wood of the bleacher seats. You rest your hands on your knees. The more you sit, the more you realise this is a perfect spot. Shade to keep the heat from sapping your stamina, distance for you to avoid most of the crowd. The spot runs semi-parallel to the first bend of the racetrack, allowing a close-look of the action for any races at miles or above. When all else false, your phone has a zoom function.

The sun keeps climbing. The starting gates keep swinging. The lady commentator up in the booth keeps screaming, and you get yourself comfortable, and observe.

"Cheval Grand. Cheval Grand takes first, two lengths ahead. That's two for two for the V-sisters!"

"The photo finish was checked, and it's Aston Machan! Aston Machan won by a nose. An absolutely unexpected turn of events!"

"…but what's this? From behind—it's Kawakami Princess! Kawakami Princess surges—no, she explodes forth! She's powering through up the outer lane, tearing through the crowd, and she's done it! Kawakami Princess has won!"

Recording races without permission is forbidden by academy policy, so you make do with pen and paper. You mark the names of the winners and the runners-up and match their names with their forms, their running style, and whatever tricks they might have pulled off. Star marks for ones who look the strongest: Cheval Grand, Kawakami Princess, Mihono Bourbon, and more. These girls are the ones who were swarmed by Trainers the moment they tore off their numbers. They're the ones who will be trained the earliest. An eye on the competition is worth a dozen recitals. Grass Wonder gave this to you as homework, but you would've done it anyway, as per your umadol life.

[(Inspection check: 34/60 || Logic check: 74/50) -> Success! +5 EXP.]

Seems like the most popular styles are front-running and pace-chasing. You tuck that detail away for later.

In between races, you drink water. You do stretches. Lunch is a light ham sandwich you made in the dorm kitchen. You flip through social media, deliberately not looking at any of the comments.
