The last one makes you frown. It's nothing special. Whatever Satono Crown feels about you, she's smart enough not to air it to the world. Also, did Smart Falcon get permission from the academy to sing here? In a racing event? Ugh. Talk about ego.

...nice shots, though. You could learn from her techniques, not that you'll ever admit this to anybody.

[Social Media has increased by 2.]

That's not to say you remain in the same place for the entire day. The first time you leave happens shortly after lunch. Tabaru's race is up next, and you join her and her crew down on the turf in giving her some pre-race prep.

"You've got this, boss. You're gonna kick their asses." Pelte pats Tabaru on the back with a grin. "None of these girls got a fraction of the mettle we faced back in Hokkaido."

"You can do it, Tab!" Jewel cries.

"Get revenge for us!" Tomoe chimes in, nodding up and down.

"Good luck, Tabaru!" You say, pitching your voice slightly higher. Widened eyes, bright smile, positive words only. This is pure umadol handshake energy. "We're all rooting for you!"

Tabaru just nods, a rare smile coming to her usually stoic face. It's a beautiful sight. She should make it more, you feel. Pelte lifts her fist for a special handshake. Lock hands, twist thumbs, break apart for a fist bump and halfway through, Tabaru goes still. Not her usual still, when she's mulling over what she thinks. This is frozen as a statue. Carved from mountain limestone and displayed in a museum.

"Tabaru?" You say, getting worried. This isn't normal. "What's up?"

[Meisho Tabaru's Instinct check: 120/90 -> Success!]

Tabaru yanks her head to the side, rolls of flesh twisting in her neeck.

"Anego" Tabaru replies, hoarsely.

"Anego?" You say. "Your sister? Which one?"

"Stay Gold."

Stay Gold. Troublemaker, traveller, terrorist of the racetrack.

The name finally registers, and you follow Tabaru's sightline. There, in a gap within the bleachers' crowds some distance away, sits an uma with a stature so short it falls within the bounds of midget. She's slouched on the seat, her legs kicked up on the backrest of the empty seat below her. A hint of gold glints around her right ear. From first glance, nothing about this uma suggests she is another slacker with a slight interest in modern fashion trends, yet she's facing forward, observing the competition like you did (and maybe better), and surrounded around her like a ring of bodyguards—

"Orfevre is here." Tabaru mutters to herself. "Dream Journey, Golshi, Festa—"

A fleshy pop. The scent of iron. You yelp as blood dribbles down Tabaru's chin, the thick droplets splashing onto the grass.

"Boss, your lip!" Jewel cries.

Tabaru…she bit her lip so hard it bled on the spot. And she doesn't care. She just wipes the spill away, leaving a dark red smear on her right arm.

"I'm going." Tabaru says.

"Shouldn't you see a—"

"I'm going!" Tabaru shouts.

You stumble back. It's the first time you've heard Tabaru raise her voice. It's the equivalent of a regular uma screaming her throat until it cracks. Pressure cascades off Tabaru, practically flattening the surrounding grass. The sense is like Oguri's—obviously not as strong, yet sharper and denser. Rich with more blood. The scent snaps any lingering traces of sleepiness from your early morning jog.

Is…is this how Tabaru hyped herself up back in the regional? No, you think a second later. Pelte, Jewel and Tomoe are just as confused, even frightened. None of them did particularly well in their own tryouts, and to see their own leader this stressed has driven them quiet with shock.

"Boss—" Pelte tries.

Tabaru stalks off without a word. She goes to the reserve area and gets her number. When her race is called, she stomps to the starting line and vanishes behind the gate. The moment the pistol pops, Tabaru tears herself out of the gate so fast you imagine the iron bars flying through the air in her wake. The other contestants scramble to keep up. It's no use. Tabaru keeps gaining and gaining for one length, two lengths, three lengths in front, and the finish line soars to meet her.

"Goal!"

First place. Pure domination. No question about it.

Pelte pumps her fist and shouts with joy, and you clap. Trainers prepare to charge down the track. They're all interrupted as Stay Gold hops onto the turf and walks forward, whistling. Everyone puts their plans on hold to see what this infamous, recklessly-dressed uma will do. She just grins and pats Tabaru on the head. Tabaru bows, far lower than when she did to Nakayama Festa.

[(Foreign Languages check: 57/70 || Sneak check: 48/85) -> Failure.]

Damn it. It's too far to make out what they're saying. You're no lip-reader.

The rest of the Golds approach, starting with Gold Ship's energetic embrace and sealing with Nakayama Festa's noogie on Tabaru's head. They circle around them, leaving a gap that barely lest you catch a glimpse of her face.

Tabaru's clammed up again, composed herself. Mouth in a tight line, responding with short, quick responses. Still shaking.

That's not happiness.

[(Psyche check: 9/11 || Intimidation check: 39/60 || Subterfuge check: 54/65) -> Failure.]

You're not sure what it is, but it's not happiness, and it adds another notch to your nerves.

[-2 to the next starting gate roll.]

A sprint race concludes with a close finish. There's cheers, more of them, because the victor dared to run the sprint as an end closer.

"My Lord!" The victor bellows, "Your words guided me to victory. I couldn't have done it if it weren't for you!"

"Yeah, no problem. Great work, Durandal. Don't be so modest. I just gave you a few pointers before the race. The rest was all you."

A golden retriever in umamusume form and a middle-aged man with a baby-face. It'd be a heartwarning renuion, the start of a new legend, if it weren't for said golden retriever practically crushing the Trainer's fingers in her grip.

"No." The umamusume named Durandal says. She shakes her head and beams at the Trainer. "It was more than advice. It was the affirmation I was seeking. You saw my closer potential and did not scorn me. It was inspiration, as if you were there, our hearts beating as one. The one to whom I should offer my sword is you!"

Cameras click. Photos are snapped. There's more of a crowd, allowing you to blend in and take a peek withou an issue.

"You flatter me…" The baby-faced Trainer mutters. "You've got a lot of potential, Durandal. I'm sure your future Trainer will be pleased with you."

"You're wrong." Durandal says. "Because my future Trainer is already here."

Durandal drops to one knee. She places a hand over her heart. " Sir Keiichi of Team IKZE! I beseech you: allow me to serve as your vassal. I shall put my heart and soul and dedicate my victories on the field to you!"

The crowd gasps. You can't help but join them. This is one spicy proposal. It's the stuff newbie managers in the business dream of. Trainer Keiichi backs away. You suddenly put name to Umastagram posts, because if this is the infamous Team IKZE, then its star player is…

"How insolent."

From behind: a thunderous presence, stalking down the nearby steps towards the commotion. The crowd parts like the sea, bodies jostling around you. Orfevre, the Golden Tyrant, strides forward, her regal golden-orange hair flowing behind her like an emperor's cape. The contours of powerful, lean muscle shine from beneath the standard Tracen uniform. You instinctively slip back behind two umas who couldn't care less about you.

Trainer Keiichi gulps. "Orfevre…"

"For a mere vassal to act as if he is a lord; and for an interloper to dare covet a monarch's property," Orfevre stands between her Trainer and Durandal and shakes her head, disgust written on her sharp features. "This year's crop of newcomers possesses no shortage of audacity."

She walks up front of her, focusing the brunt of her ire on the newcomer. Durandal barely flinches, to her credit, and stands up, tilting her head upwards.

"Wait. Calm down, Orfevre." Trainer Keiichi says. He slides between the two of them, holding up one hand. "This isn't what it looks like."

Orfevre glares at him. "Do you think I lack eyes and ears?"

"No, your eyes and ears are right there where they are."

"Then do you believe me to be a witless fool?"

"Nothing was signed. Nothing was made official." Trainer Keiichi presses. "I helped Durandal, yes, but it was a side thing."

"He saw me struggling on the track and was kind and generous enough to help." Durandal adds. "He is a man worth several lordships."

Another shade of anger colors itself on Orfevre. "Five seconds."

"Pardon?" Durandal says.

Orfevre holds up her palm. Five fingers outstretched. "I will grant you five seconds to explain where in this matter did I ever grant you permission to speak to him.

"He is a free lord." Durandal says.

"He is my vassal." Orfevre counters.

"Isn't it the other way around? I heard that Trainer Keiichi shaped you, not the opposite."

You wonder for a moment if Durandal is trying to needle Orfevre up—a task as intelligent as shoving several razor blades between one's legs. She's not. Starry eyed, excited enough to wag her tail; she's genuinely asking, oblivious to the living storm cloud gathering before her.

"Trainer." Orfevre hisses, rounding on the human man. A twitch throbs around her forehead. "You have exceeded my expectations once again."

And they're not good ones, Trainer Keiichi knows. "Now, now, calm down, Orfevre."

"To think you would neglect your duties to us in favor of an outsider—"

"I had some free time, alright?"

"Free time, you say?" A soft voice pops up behind Trainer Keiichi. He, and a good portion of the crowd, freeze as an umamusume melts out of his shadow. Half-lidded eyes, spectacles and a stark white cowlick to match her long black hair. Dream Journey, Orfevre's elder blood sister, and a G1 champion herself. "I beg to differ."

If Trainer Keiichi was pale before, he's gone full on ghost-white now. "Dream Journey—"

Dream Journey tuts, waggling a finger.

"You had multiple sessions with this girl." Dream Journey grips her Trainer's shoulder. Hard. "Multiple sessions. I saw."

"I see. We have a philanderer in our amidst." Orfevre comments.

"She's an end-closer. An end-closer who does sprint, a race where runners normally try to set the pace from the start. And she managed to win. It's—amazing! We all know this." Trainer Keiichi splutters, waving his hands about. "Please be reasonable."

Dream Journey grin stretches. A hypothetical serial killer tosses down his hockey mask and runs for the hills. Trainer Keiichi shrinks into himself, only to be saved—

"Another sprinter?"

Never mind. He's not being saved. It's Curren Chan, Tracen's number one Umafluencer, approaches, dressed in a white top and a crimson skirt. The moment she gets into view, she tears up, a pout wobbling on her cute lips. Trainer Keiichi sees this, and whatever relief he instinctively found at the sight of his best sprinter crumbles into dust.

"Am I hearing things right? You're courting another sprinter, big bro? Is your cute Curren not good enough for you?"

Trainer Keiichi groaned. "No, Curren, that's not—"

"We were so busy packing up in the clubhouse, and you, y-you—" Curren Chan lifts her hands to her face and lets out an exaggerated sob. Wow, she's good. There's even real tears leaking out; you don't learn to cry on command unless you're good enough to star in actual movies. You also don't do this if you're not at least slightly pissed somewhere in your soul. About a hundred death glares from Curren Chan's retinue of fans slam into Trainer Keiichi. He lets out a long, suffering sigh, clearly thinking that things cannot get worse.

"No!"

Sweep Tosho, the last member of Team IKZE and the umamusume who threw a tantrum in front of the fucking Emperor of Japan, pushes through the crowd and stamps on the ground.

"No, no, no! We don't need a knight! We already have a mage—me!" Sweep Tosho wails. She grabs Trainer Keiichi by the side, the tip of her big purple hat jutting into the side of his face. She glares at Durandal. "Go away, you big dummy! You're not touching my familiar!"

In the face of a tyrant, a pseudo-yakuza, a girl whose Umastagram account is estimated to be worth millions, and Sweep Tosho, Durandal clears her throat and bows her head. "I understand your protests, everyone but I must have this man as my Trainer! We have forged an unbreakable bond through today's victory."

The retorts fire back like cannonballs.

"No is no!"

"Big bro, I can change. I swear I can. Give me a chance!"

"Sister, grab this fool's collar. We need to teach him some discipline."

"Wonderful idea, Orfy."

The four umamusume descend upon their Trainer in a manoeuvre so quick it feels coordinated. To give the man credit, he tries to sort his furious trainees out. Soak up a question, respond, grab another, repeat. You watch with burgeoning pity and are suddenly struck with a revelation. Is this how Manager Suzuki felt when you and the rest of the girls were squabbling over which restaurant to eat at?

Then again, Kaede and the others couldn't hurl him through the door with their bare hands—only you could. Phew. For a moment there, you almost thought it was wrong for cute girls to demand free desserts from their manager. Thank god you didn't change your mind.

Still, you think, as Durandal grabs Trainer Keiichi's left arm while Curren Chan grabs his right, Team IKZE sure is in for a bumpy ride…

[No changes were made.]

And then it's your turn.

Minutes before the race, you enter the changing rooms with your sports bag. You exchange your uniform for a shirt and a pair of shorts. You make your way down to the track from a set of steps, cutting through the center set of bleachers.

A hush falls over the crowd. It is taboo to heckle contestants in tryouts, especially when Director Akikawa and President Rudolf are attending, so whispers and an aura of silence fill the gap. Tracen's crowd have given you many titles—arrogant, a thief, the black sheep of the Satonos, the daughter of the worst umamusume to ever walk through Tracen's halls—but only now will they see your settle tested.

Your race is the main attraction. No-one wants to admit it, but it's true.

[(Composure: 65/80 && Guts: 9/10) -> Failure.]

The stares prickle. Some of them burn. Your own eyes can't help but wander, despite your best efforts to keep them forward where they belong. Forget the usual Friday crowd, because you're surrounded by umas who are regional runners-up at the absolute worst. Some of them are curious, a lot of them despise you, and overall the audience here is bigger, more prestigious, more powerful. Mejiro McQueen, Stay Gold, Nice Nature, Agnes Digital, the rest of Team Spica, Team Rigil and her Trainer, the V Sisters, the aforementioned Team IKZE—you pass by these big names whom you've only seen in press releases and online articles, who have all somehow decided to take up the best seats, whose attentions are now focused on you. Needles without blind spots.

Should you feel flattered? You'll settle for the pressure weighing down your shoulders.

Luckily, you spot some friendly faces. Aston Machan gives you a smile. Meisho Tabaru nods her head. Makitanefukukitaru is groping the air around her crystal ball in what you think is a fortune-bringing chant. Grass Wonder sits with the rest of the Golden Generation, who wave and mouth good luck as you pass by, and then there's Oguri Cap at the bottom, munching away at a towering bucket of fried chicken. Guess she finished the rescue efforts in Kasamatsu—you recall hearing snippets of news over the radio. She gives you a thumbs up, still chewing on a drumstick.

You smile and hope it's not too forced. If the Oguri Cap thinks you're good enough, then you definitely stand a chance. Grass Wonder, too.

You step onto the turf. Green grass, tasting fresh. You walk towards the gates. Towering hunks of metal and grate, checked up and down by harried-looking staff. An assistant trainer hands you a paper sign with the number five on it. A generic one—in an official URA race, it'd have your name. The other girls stare, but you refuse to look at them. You focus on checking your shoes and doing your stretches. The caster rattles off the names, including yours.

"Number four: Satono Ruby. Number five: Rice Shower…"

As you twist your body, you spot her: Happy Meek. White-haired, dopey-eyed, staring off at an invisible butterfly in the distance as she too stretches. She's number three, and the girl whose Trainer put her here to show her strength, not for her to get scouted. You remember feeling put off at this exploitation of rules. Right now, you only feel a tight numbness, anticipation for dealing with her. There's nothing in her posture that signals her running stance. Her movements are fluid, almost as robotic as Mihono Bourbon's. You wonder if that means she's excellent at keeping a steady pace, or if she's playing mind games.

"Number seven: Kitasan Black."

The favorite is here. Cheers rise up. Somewhere among them are Diamond and Crown, probably already assured that their longtime family friend will defeat you. You try not to think about your estranged sisters. You try not to remember how Kitasan refused to stop her best friend from verbally abusing you back in the city.

Focus.

She's another opponent. The strongest one, perhaps, but nothing more, nothing less. Don't look at her as she passes by.

The race is what matters.

Past the gates, across the turf. Four corners, and then wrapping back to the start. The finish line. Two whole kilometers—thereupon lies the culmination of your efforts for the past few months. Practice has made you as perfect as you can be. It's now time to seize victory with your bare hands.

>>All participants, please make way towards the starting gates…

[Rice Shower has performed gate training. +20 to starting gate roll.]

[Happy Meek has performed gate training. +15 to starting gate roll.]

[Kitasan Black has performed gate training. +25 to starting gate roll.]

3.6: Tiny Rapport

>>[Opening] I'll ease myself behind the front runners. & I'll latch onto the favorite.

>>[Middle] I'll dive inside the pack for the rail to save ground. & I'll keep shadowing the favorite.

>>[End] I'll try and slip through the traffic. & I'll shadow the leader, then try to move around them!

>>[Interference] I'll project my spirit to throw them off.

>>[Pray] For your friends and mentors to see.

>>[Kitasan] Wish her good luck.

"Good luck, Kitasan."

The girl crosses paths with you as the time to enter the starting gate draws, and those words cause her to flinch.

She goes silent, drops the hand she was waving to the bleachers. A complicated web of emotions scatters across those normally bright features. Surprise at your sudden words, suspicion at any of your ulterior motives, a dash of anger at being addressed by you of all umas—these are nothing new. No different from how she treated you back at the shopping mall. Her loyalty to Diamond holds firm.

It hurts to see. It hurts once again to know this girl still treats you with scorn, when she possesses the same love of enka and racing as you. There exists a universe where you, Diamond and Kitasan are the best of friends, and it is not here; instead, she is another proxy of the Satono's persistent animosity towards your very existence. You won't, cannot, say it doesn't matter. The small ache in your heart is proof enough.

But Kitasan won't stop you from acting with good sportsmanship. Better to act respectable to avoid making further enemies. Better to extend the olive branch, because there's a chance, always a chance, that the person on the other hand will take it. Hotaru, Manager Suzuki, Machan, and even Oguri.

The last thing you want for Kitasan or anyone here is to be hurt.

[+1 to Light Alignment.]

With that, you resume walking to your allocated gate. Just as you are about to enter, you hear a mild grunt, followed by a brief pause, and then:

"G...good luck to you, too, Ruby."

You blink, then slowly turn around. Did she just—yes, Kitasan did just say that. She's staring back, her posture stiff, her glance askew in a manner that speaks of regret. Beneath the usual aversion, hidden by her grimace, you catch a glimpse of something soft, something that maybe sings of reciprocation, of sympathy. You can't confirm, because Kitasan marches forward and vanishes behind her gate.

You blink. You stand there, perplexed, yet with a slightly lightened heart. That—you'll dwell on it after the race. You have to. For now, you proceed towards your own gate. The staff close the doors behind you.

"Thank you all for being so patient! The final race of today's tryouts is ready to begin. To begin, introducing the favorite: Kitasan Black running in bracket number seven. The second-most favorite: Happy Meek at…"

The gate is a confined but not cramped space. You twist your elbows as far as you can for a last-second spot of limbering up. You look ahead to the turf. Enough time has passed for the hues of afternoon to wash across the sky. The green grass is awash with a faint tint of orange. The first corner is visible, the metallic bend diverting to a sharp right. It is exactly as you expected. Plans and procedures you rehearsed with Grass Wonder press themselves at the forefront of your mind, as your heart hammers harder against your ribcage.

[The sun is setting…]

You slip your right hand down your shirt, wrapping its fingers around your silver bullet. You run your skin over the trinket's notch, let its comfort wash over you once again until your mind is empty aside from thoughts of the race. Then, you pray to it, the images of your friends and your mentor filling your head. Grass Wonder, Oguri Cap, Tabaru, Aston Machan, and everyone else you met and appreciated and who were so compassionate as to help you over these two months.

Watch me, everyone. I swear I won't let you down.

This race is already a dream, and you will use its victory to ensnare more.

Finally, you drop into a kneeling start: one leg bent, one hand out, head and neck relaxed. You are ready.

The staff retreat back from the turf. The commentator confirms the beginning of the race; hundreds of spectators hold their breath. Behind the gates, the starter lifts the remote control to a buzzer. He presses a button.

A loud shrill buzz sweeps across the turf.

>>ON YOUR MARKS, GET SET…GO!

3.7: ORDEAL ~Tryouts~

Mood: Good

EXP: 45/150

The gates slam open with a loud bang. You and nine other runners rush out across the turf, feet thundering, arms swinging, grass stalks trampled and flying beneath the howl of the rushing air. It's everything you ever dreamed of. You should be smiling so wide your face threatens to burst, yet there's only a pained grimace stretching those sweet cheeks.

"A clean start from all the runners…except Satono Ruby and Happy Meek! They're both trailing behind the pack!"

That's why.

God damn it! You scream in your head.

(Holy shit—)

(Serves the bitch right.)

(This is gonna be easy!)

A hundred curses to the caster. A hundred curses to the owner of those gates. And a thousand curses more to you, because it was you, you who misjudged the timing, was set on edge by the cramped confines, thought too hard about tactics, and now embarrassed yourself in front of the entire academy as well as burning chunks of precious stamina in needing to catch up. Your heart is squeezing blood like paste from a tube, so stop panicking Ruby! An imaginary Grass Wonder shouts.

Yeah. Imaginary Nakayama Festa chimes in. Weren't you listening? The first thing you should do in a late start is accept it's happened. Ain't got no time left for regrets.

The first corner's rushing up!

In front of you: dual railings swinging left. The distant form of Kitasan Black and the rest of the front runners are already leaning in to finish the turn. A nearby signpost reflects the afternoon sun like the glare of a violent stop sign.

[Composure check: 64/55 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

You snap awake, connecting your eyes back to their brain. Quick, it screams back. Stop thinking. Pump those legs faster. You've half-caught back up; any more lollygagging and the gap in the pack will seal up. You've got the power and the acceleration, so rush through and swing around the corner like you practiced already!

You grit your teeth and charge forward.

[(Nutrition check: 47/80) || (Stamina check: 11/9) -> Success! +5 EXP.]

Someone tries to cut you off—

[Dodge check: 82/50 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

—but you zip around them, then return to your lane. You finish the charge and settle in the middle of the pack.

[(Speed check: 11/9) || (Acceleration check: 72/60) -> Success! +5 EXP.]

(Tch. She made it after all.)

(Meh. She'll burn out fast.)

(…hm. Ruby—)

"Now entering the corner: Arcade Champ sets the pace with a minor lead over Kitasan Black. Grand Chamard is third on the inside, Rice Shower right behind her in the middle. Satono Ruby has caught up at fifth—let's hope she's not burned too much stamina. Going Noble's pursuing her, and behind them are Faster Than Ray, Happy Meek, Slaine and Farm Volume—all at the back! And here comes the backstretch!"

The crowd cheers. An appetizer for the finale, ringing across the turf.

You run down the backstretch with the others. Sweat trickles down behind your shirt. Your lungs simmer with heat. These sensations are faded, distant, barred by a mind taut as stretched iron wire. This isn't calm you're feeling. Calm doesn't involve your heart beating this fast. Calm doesn't shriek distantly with bodily electricity. No, this is the immersion of the performance, where you take every ounce of what you have learned and practiced, shove it down the root of your physique and force your body to obey.

You dive further into this sensation. Submerge yourself. You wrap it around your swinging legs and arms. It is tense inside yet smooth on the outside. It helps you steady your pace.

[Breathing check: 67/50 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

And it keeps your feet planted on the ground without slipping.

[Traversal check: 37/35 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

So much longer do you have to go? Imaginary Grass Wonder asks, as her real counterpart had done in so many practice runs over the past few months.

[Racing Tactics: 82/60 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

Fifteen hundred! You choke back, trying to keep your stride. The first two turns cost three hundred meters, and you're now a third of the way down the backstretch. The racetrack you're on is an imitation of the Tokyo Racecourse, which means two more turns and the homestretch remain.

To the average spectator, you're still in the opening stages of the race. That assumption couldn't be any further from the truth. A race is not divided into individual stages, but a flowing stream of decisions that cascade into each other like a stream of dominoes. The endgame, therefore, is already being decided on this backstretch in a test of control and positioning. Front runners can't burn out. Pace chasers can't get themselves boxed in or stuck on the outside. Late surgers and end closers can't slip behind too far. Then are the other contestants to worry about, followed by the lane scramble. Going wide gives you a clear path, yet the inner railing shaves approximately a whole hundred meters off the remaining distance.

You want that inner lane. You need it to compensate for your late start. But everyone's searching for that avenue. Trying to switch lanes always runs the risk of bumping into someone and ending up disqualified. Do you have enough finesse to pull this tactic off?

Yes. You can.

You will.

"Arcade Champ is still leading, but Kitasan Black is closing in. Kitasan overtakes Arcade who drops into second. Rice Shower gains onto third, Grand Chamard falls back into fourth and Satono Ruby is still at fifth! Which of these umas will make the first move?"

You relax your pace, but not so much you slip back down into sixth place, then quickly scan the surrounding crowd. Grass Wonder told you she learned the fundamentals of her opponents' physiques through the turf and the air. She felt the ground vibrate beneath her feet, tasted the sting of the air slowing down the slipstream. You are an apprentice unable to comprehend this heightened, enlightened perception of your mentor's. You can only catch your opponents' forms out of the corner of her eyes and try to sift through the thumping of the horde.

Four in front, five behind. Sixth place comes up rushing alongside you on your right. Kitasan is blazingly fast, as expected. She's marked by the uma with the tilted hat and the blue rose—Rice Shower. No-one talked about her before the race, not even your mentor, yet this girl has marked Kitasan with no signs of slowing down. Her lithe form has allowed her to dive into the slipstream. Happy Meek is somewhere behind you. No clue what she's doing. The rest of the pack is running steadily. These are all formidable opponents.

Yet, you can tell: no-one here is as swift and graceful as Grass Wonder. No-one wields the gut-punching force of a merely retired Oguri Cap. You are zero for two on these fronts a swell, but you spent the past two months trained by these multiple-G1 winning behemoths. Compared to them, the pack is nothing!

There—

[(Wits check: 9/9) || (Visual Mathematics: 52/45) -> Success! +10 EXP.]

—a gap in the crowd. Third-place moved up too fast. She's giving you an opening. Vigour fills your muscles. A grin leaks onto your face. You stomp the ground and pump power into your legs.

"What's this? Satono Ruby is making a move. She's angling to the left. She's going towards the inner rail. But—"

The other runners aren't about to make it easy. Fourth-place and sixth-place exchange immediate glances and close in on you. Heightened footsteps from behind—either seventh or eighth. They're coming to the left. They're all trying to box you in. Maybe one of them is hoping you'll crash and tumble out of the race. Their animosity towards you gathers like a storm cloud, invisible needles stabbing down at you.

(Piss off.)

(You think we're gonna make this easy!)

(You should've quit when you had the chance!)

(We're not going to lose to you of all umas!)

The gap shrinks. You could stop. You could risk the squeeze, or try to find an alternate path.

No. Just—no. None of these options sings to you. Instead, you have a much better idea.

Gulp that breath. Glare back at your opponents in the eye without faltering your pace. Oh, mighty komainu of the shrine, lend this humble soul divine fervor. Coat her in your stone pelt. Lend her the roar that shook the dragon, vowed the underground halls of modern-day Shibuya amidst a ballad of thunderous strings and thoughts of fire. May these opponents be cowed by this outpouring of raw, FAITHFUL spirit!

[Frenzy check: 75/50 -> Success! The enemy Frenzy was reflected back! +5 EXP.]

A roar bursts out from your throat. Uncouth, unabated, and your presence surges forward like a tidal wave alongside it.

(Wha—)

(What the hell is this?)

(She's…she's not backing down?)

The wave of animosity crumbles. Fourth-place and sixth-place startle. Their strides waver, their bodies instinctively angling away from your barreling form. Third-place tries to accelerate, but she flinches at the last second, tearing off a chunk of stamina as she recovers. Burnout settles in. She falters, and you seize the opportunity to squeeze through the gap.

[Dodge check: 82/70 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

It's a tight fit, but you made it. You're close to the inner rail now.

"And Satono Ruby overtakes Grand Chamard and Going Noble. She's clinging close to the rail. She's caught up to third place. The back turn is here!"

The ground curves. You tilt your body, letting its center of gravity gradually drop. A hundred swings around this same corner guide your feet; at the halfway point, you plant your right foot on the ground and kick off as you had on that fateful, first mock-race—only stronger, swifter and with no pressure at all. Third-place tries one last time to check you, but you're too nimble, and too fast.

[(Acceleration check: 72/80 && Power check: 10/10) || (Dancing check: 100/90) -> Success! +10 EXP.]

"Into the homestretch—Kitasan Black at first, Rice Shower at second, and Satono Ruby closing in! Will Satono Ruby make a miracle comeback, or will she falter at the final stretch?"

The turn ends. Kitasan and Rice Shower see you.

(This is—)

(Ruby, you—)

And you lock eye with them.

Get back here! Your twisted face howls.

[Frenzy check: 75/70 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

Eyes widening, mouth agape, Kitasan flinches. Rice Shower turns away, stiffly facing forward through her run. You grin wider. You've knocked them off guard. All that's left is to shadow Kitasan through these last four hundred meters, maintain your pace, and then zoom past her once she shows signs of slipping!

You're gaining on her, preparing for the last spurt, when you hear the commentator gasp.

"What's this?"

A presence behind you. A taste of stark, composed white.

(Hm. I promised Aoi—)

"It's Happy Meek! Happy Meek is breaking out of the back line! She's rushing up to the front."

(—that I'd run a lot, and win.)

The comment rattles off the places. Eighth, seventh, sixth—fourth. A pit falls in your stomach. An end closer. Happy Meek played as an end closer. She watched you and the others battle it out, conserving her energy for the entire race until this final, fateful moment. Don't tell you—she factored her late start into this plan? She's even coming around the left, clinging to the railing as you did, but she's completely brushing up against the thing. She has the shortest distance to cover!

(Aaaaaaah, I don't believe this!)

(Rice…Rice won't lose! Watch me, Miss Bourbon!)

Kitasan clenches her teeth. The sight of Happy Meek re-bolsters her resolve, undoing the damage you did to her. She ups her face, Rice Shower not long behind her. The gap widens, and you want to scream again. Curse this Happy Meek for throwing a wrench in your plans!

[Racing Tactics check: 82/70 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

No. It's not over yet. Third place is more than enough to catch up. Rice Shower is busy shadowing Kitasan. Happy Meek is near you, but she won't try lane switching this late. Nor can you try to encroach on her lane; the moment you do, she'll slip past you and accelerate forward. No, in this case, the simplest solution is the best: charge forward with all your might. Let the pieces fall where they may!

"What's this? First through fourth places are bunching up. They're all charging forward together in a pack—Kitasan Black, Rice Shower, Satono Ruby, Happy Meek! The rest of the competition is several lengths behind. The homestretch is a battle of four!"

Three hundred meters. Two fifty, two hundred, one-ninety—the distance is all you are aware of. Rice Shower broke out from behind Kitasan to overtake, but Kitasan summoned strength out of nowhere and sped up forward. You contest Happy Meek while pursuing Kitasan and Diamond, the gap seemingly stretching and shrinking with every passing second. Limbs swing, feet kick up clumps of dirt, and nothing but raw, animalistic fury bleeds from your and your fellow contestants' faces.

(Go away. Now.)

(Make way for Rice, please! Rice…is strong too!)

(I won't lose. I promised Dia and Teio I wouldn't lose. You hear me, everyone? I'm going to get into Team Spica and there's nothing any of you can do about it!)

To hell with Team Spica, you want to scream. That victory is mine!

"Kitasan Black, then Rice Shower—no, it's Satono Ruby. No, it's Rice Shower in second. Happy Meek is gaining alongside them. Kitasan breaks away yet again. Goodness, they're all neck-to-neck!"

[Stamina check: 11/11 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

[Speed check: 11/11 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

You accelerate further. Momentum from the past pushes you on, sending you faster and faster. Speed, stamina and raw strength combine to thrust you to the apex of your spurt. Kitasan's eyes are widened. They're getting bigger in your field of vision. You're gaining. Catching up to her for real. Overtaking her is possible!

Yet, your mind tells another story.

[Pain Threshold check: 42/65 -> Failure.]

It hurts. Oh, goddesses, it hurts.

[Guts check: 9/10 -> Failure.]

Agony deeps into your joints. Kneecaps beg for mercy. Your throat is aflame. Your physical prowess wars with your mental failings, and to your horror the latter turns the tide, instinctively slowing you down.

Please. A little more. You've all done so well now. We can finish the last stretch.

One-ten, one hundred. The finish line squirms into existence. Tunnel vision wipes away the bleachers and the turf beneath you until the line and your opponents fill the void. Kitasan and Happy Meek's forms move in slow motion, their own screams drowning into long, hollow groans. Rice Shower has fallen back, or she's switching lanes in a last desperate effort to overtake. You feel your right leg extending first, left leg supporting it back, and then the opposite again. That too is soon drowned out.

The shadows created by the afternoon sun stretch and linger. Your own footsteps fade into soft thumps like stones cast on a vast, snowy field. A languid silence reigns…

[(Micro Cosmos: Exists && Insight check: 10/10) -> Success! +10 EXP.]

(Ugh, she's still there.)

…where voices break through your dull footsteps.

(She's still going? I'd thought she'd give up already.)

You're running, yet you can hear them. It's the crowd. So close, yet so far away. Frowns upon faces, fists clenched with sneers, heads turning away from the sight of you.

(Hurry up and fall behind already!)

(This is so lame…)

(Go, Kitasan! Don't let that cheater's brat win!)

No. Please. Not now.

(We're all counting on you, Kitasan!)

Don't do this, not right now.

(She's nothing! You hear me, you bitch? Nothing!)

(Like she's impressing anyone with that running form…)

The voices keep ringing. Insults, jeers, the familiar one, but from an audience of almost a thousand, so close to the turf you dreamed of running on. They are swords stabbing into your psyche. Acid burning in addition to the physical agony.

It's not fair. It's so not fair.

You worked hard to get into Tracen. You broke your limits under the tutelage of a G1 winner. You've tried your best in the race, like Kitasan and the rest. So, why…

(Go Kitasan! Go Rice! Anyone but her!)

(Hey, refs! Check her shoes for signs of tampering! It's what Opal did, after all.)

(No Trainer's gonna want to sign with her. No-one wants to deal with the Satonos, or a potential PR disaster. It's just common sense.)

(Does she think this is a game? Why is she wasting everyone's time?)

…why do you have to suffer these insults? Why do they hate you so much when you've never said a mean word to them?

You're not the monster everyone thinks you are.

You have hope. You have dreams. You're a perfectly nice girl who could be friends with all of these hecklers if they just gave you a damn chance!

You're just…

(A thief and a liar.)

(A runaway and a whore's bastard.)

(You stole the places of more worthy girls.)

…a girl who wants to see her mom again.

Is that so wrong?

(Just stop.)

(Just give up.)

(Leave Tracen.)

(Leave this life.)

(You already did well.)

(Hurry up and accept the participation trophy already!)

You squeeze your eyes shut. Your head lowers. Your hands reach for your ears, and in doing so, you slow down.

"RUBY!"

Grass Wonder. Standing tall, her hands cupped over her mouth. Utterly uncaring of the shocked looks flung her way, nor the fact she just revealed her association to you in front of the entire academy.

"YOU'RE ALMOST THERE! YOU CAN DO IT! I BELIEVE IN YOU!"

She's still here. She was watching the whole time, and she believes in you.

Her encouragement rings in your ears. The pain blanks out. You lurch forward, forcing the last remnants of your strength upwards, begging your legs to return to the stride, to close that final damned gap between you and Kitasan.

Senpai believes in you. Both of them. You can't let them down now.

Both of them?

Who—

A force grabs you. Tugs you back.

(Stupid, insolent girl, starry-eyed girl. We warned you. We said as much back at the stump.)

(Remember, this is all your fault.)

The shadows that crept around your vision rise, surround, and swallow you whole.

[World Resonance check: 74/100 -> Failure.]

[No-one else was sucked in…]

[Total EXP gained: 120.]

3.8: Begin the Nightmare

The sky is an ugly bruise, pulsating with the spillage of a ruptured vein.

"Get your hands off me right now!"

Your scream rings through the cold air. It goes ignored by the human manhandling you, just as he did ever since you were forced through the rusted gates of this decrepit stadium.

You're being guided along, handcuffs behind your back, a boot to the knee every time you stumble. By all accounts, you should have shattered his ribs and broken away long from this man minutes ago. And you've tried, then failed. This man, wearing the dark jacketed uniform of cops and security guards and so many faceless adults, grips your shoulders with the strength of an industrial vice.

You are nothing more than a doll in his arms. An animal trotting down the straight line.You can only squirm and struggle and accomplish nothing, as you are led to a looming, bulky shadow in the distance.

Swathes of weeds. Broken glass shards. Sticks of mold sticking out of wilted dandelions. In the distance, blurry figures plod along, their own men wrassling them with ropes, or even chains around their faces.

You squint, but you can't discern any of them.

"What is that?" You ask. "Who are those people? What are you—"

The shadow is here. A mess of towering steel, many spikes lining the outside. You skid to a halt, shivering at the imminent skewering, a lump in your throat. It does not stop the man. Far from it. There, from a view created by your twisted, bent ncek: a garbled hiss instead of speech. Fleshy protrusions twitch where a normal sneer should wrap. His uniform patch is melted and deformed.

The man-thing rips the handcuffs off your wrists. You have no time to dwell on this freedom; he kicks your back forward, and you go flying headfirst through a gate locked by a padlock.

The padlock shatters.

You black out.

And you wake up.

You totter upright, back hurting, shoulders bruising, blood trickling out your delicate nose. A moan from parched lips.

"Where am I?"

The gate, you realise. The starting gate. The implement that locks and loads each participant to ensure a fair start.

But you were loaded into a gate. You were in a race at Tracen under the afternoon sun, running alongside Kitasan Black, Rice Shower, Happy Meek and others. You entered the homestretch and were charging neck-to-neck with the other girls, before…

Before…what?

You won?

No, you couldn't have. You don't remember crossing the finish line. That means you lost, then? That doesn't sound right either. The results weren't called. Which means…

Means…

Means I'm still in the race.

The thought is a ray of light breaking through a thick haze of clouds. They were there. They have always been there—right? Oh, it doesn't matter. Again, that thought of yours doesn't make sense. It's a contradiction. You can't be in the middle of a race while being loaded into a gate, and yet here you are standing, shivering.

"Kitasan? Rice? Happy Meek?" You call out. "Anyone? Hello?"

No response.

"Can I be let out here? I…I don't think I'm meant to be here. I think I might be dreaming?"

You make an uneasy chuckle, which peters out. The wind howls. It bites against your skin. It feels so real. It's as if the air itself is spiting you. You shift around, wondering if you've been made the victim of a super-elaborate prank by the academy staff, and bump your elbow on the mesh to your right.

A low moan. It catches your attention. You peer further, and see a shadowy figure lurks in the subsequent position. An umamusume like you.

"Are you here to race too?" You ask, cautiously.

The figure lifts her head, slowly, arches her back upright with a crack. She clings to the thick mesh separating you and her, fingers interlocking through the holes. Her eyes are empty white pores atop a pitch-black visage that stare at you, before there's a dull glint that causes you jerk back.

A rusty switchblade, sticking through a hole in the mesh. She pokes it forward. Hisses when it doesn't reach. The blade is flecked with inky black splatters.

Rust means tetanus. Tetanus means pain and death.

No!

You slam your body back. You jump again when the figure to the left snarls and slams her fist on the mesh, the metal wrapping around your fist. The front is barred shut, so you back away and hit the door you entered. You expect to fall to your behind onto a pile of jagged glass or mold. Instead, your back slams against hardness, and you are flung off painfully.

Metal chains. The door is locked again, this time from the inside with a single padlock.

But—

That's—

"Hey! Hey!" You shout out, scrambling to the front and poking your head out. "Something is wrong here! I'm not supposed to be here! Let me out already!"

The turf doesn't answer.

You rattle the bars. You shout some more. Red lights blare across the stadium. They blind and sear. Metallic-smelling fluid seeps through the cracks in the meshes. A loud, slurping out pours out of the left figure's mouth, and she smiles.

High above you, a rain-doll, once so pure and sweet, droops its face, melts it right off, and crumbles, all by the way of a hideous, purple flame.

[Rain is falling…]

>>All sacrifices, please proceed to the execution gates…

Name: N/A.

Location: Nowhere.

Victims: Satono Ruby, nine others.

Length: Unknown.

Gate Status: Meaningless.

Goal: Give in. Or, you can run and never look back.

[Vile shudders rock your body. Mood has dropped to Awful.]

[There is no respite. Your LEVEL UPing has been sealed.]

[The air tastes sickening. Your tagged Skills are gradually losing their power…]

(Darkness clouds your head. Terror. This is terror. And beneath its judgment, you…)

[] Cry.

[] Scream.

[] Plead.

[] Collapse.

[] Pray.

[] Stare.

[] Giggle.

3.9: Nightmare Race

Mood: Awful

EXP: 170/150 (LEVEL UP SEALED)

>>Pray to your silver bullet

>>Run and don't look back

[Guts check: 9/16 -> Failure.]

A siren blares, shrill and loud. The surrounding stalls quieten, the shadowy figures within seeming to listen to the harsh snarls coming from a distant intercom system. Your hands slide down from a patch of rusted mesh.

You stare at them dully. They're bleeding. They're the product of your rampage around in your stall. Umamusume were not designed to be confined in such a small space, and you proved this trick of biology; limbs flailing, body thrashing, fists and forehead slamming against the metal, the nerves rendered insensible by the white noise swirling around inside your head. It was futile. The metal construction was as immovable as Mt. Fuji. yet the idea of being confined to do nothing stressed you on a primal level.

You can't do nothing. A can collector, a street sweeper, a waitress and an umadol—opportunities failed more than they succeeded, but at least they were something.

And now, that something has returned. It's written in a single word, and it's obvious.

This is a race. It has to be with these gates. You'll have to run. You don't know how far, but you will. This stall is a cage. A prison. It's just like the broom closet you hid from a horde of journalists, or that terrible coffin pod you got swindled into at your first fortnight. Hurry up. Hurry, hurry, hurry the hell up. ANother second longer, and you'll go insane!

The siren shrieks again. The metal gates vibrate with energy. A gunshot rings across the turf, and the gates fly open with a bang.

Your body tears a whole length across the turf before your mind catches up.

Fifty meters. Your legs pump up and down, feet splashing wetly against the muddy earth. The action is familiarity, clarity. The white noise shrinks, barely. One hundred metres. Two hundred meters. Flailing arms, posture too stiff, too much force in your strides. Your posture is pathetic. Three hundred meters. Grass Wonder would be so disappointed. Four hundred meters. Because you're devouring energy. Five hundred meters. Because you're not running according to your training, so terrified of what bubbles and sizzles beyond the inner railing. Six hundred meters. A piece of broken glass pierces through your thin soles; it hurts and bleeds. Seven hundred meters.

The commentator mocks you, harsh growls and screeches fit for tangled machinery, dangled in front of the microphone.

Eight hundred meters.

Where's the furlong posts?

Nine hundred meters.

And run—

How come the curve has barely gotten started? Why is it so wide? You need to swing around it!

One thousand meters.

You're burning up, with a stitch in your chest. Sweat mingling with the rain and filth. Shoes that should be pristine are wearing thin. Where is the finish line?

One kilometer and one hundred.

Where the hell is it?

[Acceleration check: 63/150 -> Failure.]

[Breathing check: 58/150 -> Failure.]

[Traversal check: 28/150 -> Failure.]

A screech reverberates through the air around you.

You whip your head around. Your stomach drops. The other contestants. A mockery of a race deserves a mockery of umamusume. The shadowy figures have the outlines of your fellow sapient kind, ears and tails and feminine physiques alike, but forget the lilac of Tracen's uniform or the chestnut palette of Grass Wonder's hair. These are hollow-eyed monsters, drenched in so much inky darkness they almost blend in with the rain. Their forms are only visible by strobing red lights, and the aura surrounding their forms, smoke radiating off a non-existent fire. Their footsteps boom in tune with the thunder rolling across the ugly sky.

And they want to catch you. They want to destroy you. They're destroying each other right now. You hear them through the rain. There's a guttural cry of pain, followed by a smash of hard flesh on soft flesh. The crunch of broken teeth rings, then is overridden by the thump of a body thrown to the ground. It's trampled on by several pairs of feet speeding faster than a car in the city.

"Stop!" You cry out. "They're hurting each other. This is against the rules!"

But no-one lifts a finger. These creatures are so persistent, so dogged, they're tearing themselves apart to reach you. The commentator blares out harsh static, and the red light keeps strobing.

[Frenzy check: 66/150 -> Failure.]

So, you run. You can only run. The walls surrounding the turf belong in a stadium, and the inside of the railing only twists your stomach when you look at it. Running is that something of yours. And eventually it reaches its logical conclusion.

[Stamina check: 11/16 -> Failure.]

Exhaustion seeps into your muscles. You slow down, allowing one of the shadowy pursuers to catch up. She runs alongside you, a rattling laugh erupting from her throat. She reaches into her chest and pulls out her rusted switchblade. A banned implement. A common implement if you know which numbers to dial. The girls of FAITHFUL carried their own knives discreetly, proudly, in case of creeps, starting with Hotaru; Manager Suzuki always turned a blind eye. That means you are aware of its range, and so you switch lanes to evade it.

Unfortunately, all knives possess a secondary range, one that you remember when it whistles through the air and pierces your left shoulder.

[Dodge check: 73/150 -> Failure.]

[Pain Threshold check: 37/150 -> Failure.]

You crash. You roll. Momentum somersaults you, the mud kissing you several times before you hit a post in the railing and stop there. This time, you don't black out. You spin around, drenching yourself further in the wet filth, because the knife—it's there. You need to pull it out before it infects you further. You reach around with right hand and grasp the handle.

There's no blood. No skin torn. The knife did not sever flesh. It merely slid into it like paper through a slot, an aberration of physics. Instead of pain, an icy sensation spreads from within. The moment you focus on it, your head goes fuzzy. Little needles in your head, akin to a fever. A whimper slips from your mouth.

The race you were in previously—why are you thinking of that now? You were running so fast, learning through execution, especially with how you slipped out of being boxed. Now, you can't remember.

Something was taken from you. Something very important.

[5 EXP was destroyed!]

There it is again: that primal fear.

Forget the knife. Forget it! You're screaming again, frantically pulling yourself up with the railing as a support, but it's coated in foul-smelling fluid, and combined with the unsteady ground results in you falling again with a soft splash.

Your pursuer grabs you by the scruff of your shirt. She flings you through the air and slams you back down on the ground. Then, she pulls the knife out and stabs you

[5 EXP was destroyed!]

Again

[10 EXP was destroyed!]

And again

[15 EXP was destroyed!]

And yet again.

[25 EXP was destroyed!]

And you're left cold and hollow, the fire of your resistance sputtering until not even embers remain.

[All your tagged skills have dropped by 2!]

"Please…" You moan. "No more. I can't…"

Your pursuer hisses in your face. Her fellows catch up. They surround you, then exchange glances, speaking in a gnashing of teeth and tongue. They are not as faceless as you initially thought. Noses, eye shapes, the ways their sneers are stitched together—there are subtleties. They look at the first pursuer, who nods her head, and looms over you to brush your water-slick fringe out of your hair.

She crouches down and lays you flat. She grabs your leg. Angles it. Tugs it. Pulls it until the tendons strain, then begin to scream.

"No. No!" You cry out, instantly alert. "Not my legs! Don't touch my legs! I can't run without them!"

Your pursuer's smirk grows wider than ever.

"Why are you doing this?" You howl.

They glance at each other, then answer. Not with speech, but with information. Your mind floors with a slurry of visions, multiple Tracen students overlaid atop you in this same position. Like you, they were ambushed. Forced to race. Hounded, brutalized, stabbed over and over before they woke up and found their legs leaden, their bodies struck sick, and their motivation shriveled and dried. There was no other choice but to leave their dreams behind at Tracen. Pieces of their souls were irrecoverably lost.

And these pursuers, denizens of this horrid world, they didn't do it to eliminate the competition. They didn't attack out of a twisted sense of justice. They show you more: flashes of sweaty, fatigued girls at Nakayama and Tokyo, glaring at a winner showered in confetti at the end of the turf. There are visions of teeth grinding, nails bitten, necks shoved into the Tracen stump to weep and scream. The shadowy figures suck up the envy, the hate and the spite, and they return to this place to indulge in their sick games simply because they can.

A bolt of anger pierces through your despair.

You flail again, straining against your restraints, all the while howling insults that'd get you booted out of FAITHFUL. One hand slaps away a pursuer that attempts to grab your ear. Your free leg tries kicking you backwards against the crowd. Multiple pursuers pile atop you, pinning down one arm, as the other squirms around and tries to find something to grab in return.

Your free hand squeezes around your silver bullet.

Time slows down. You feel the notch in its body, taste the old, familiar comfort. The silver bullet. Your lucky trinket. Your first act of rebellion against the shrine, your personal amidst in the big city. Across the heat, through the cold, into the depths of the best racing academy in the nation, it has served you with comfort, with stability, and as a symbol representing your own will to seek your future with a smile on your face, no matter how hard the universe tried to press you down.

[World Resonance check: 65/25 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

It must have popped out for a reason. You think with startled lucidity.

A pursuer yanks on the chain. She tries to pull it to pieces. You tighten your grip in response and pull in the opposite direction.

Please. You pray, squeezing your eyes shut. Someone, anyone, grant me strength. Grant me hope. I want to run a thousand races. I want to make a million friends. I want my mom to see me on stage, and most of all—

A sudden surge of vigor flows through your chest. Your eyes flash open, blazing with a new ferocity.

I don't want anyone else to be hurt by them!

The fabric of your being thrums with energy, and your silver bullet bursts forth a brilliant, white light.

It's as if the moon just punched your assailants in the eyes. Each one reels back, yelping, their hands covering their faces, their sneers no longer in sight. The pursuer holding your leg receives the brunt of it, collapsing onto the mud and rolling there like a dazed mutt. Yet, you are not blinded. You are not immune. The bullet invites you, and you witness it elongating, extending, sharpening itself with additional notches, grooves, springs and screws, and finally coalescing into the shape of a…

Gun?

A pistol with a thin barrel, a wooden grip, and an oversized trigger. The name of the model eludes you. It falls into your hands, your fingers instinctively wrapping around the frame.

You stare at it. Your assailants stare at it. The rain slathers the barrel with moisture. The scene is a tableau of pure confusion.

Then, your brain kicks itself back into gear. You squeeze the trigger.

A bullet explodes from the barrel. It flies through the rainy air and crashes into the head of the first pursuer. Blood and bone chunks do not fly, only clumps of dark mist that dissipate into the rain. The sound, so fantastically loud, causes a wire to snap in your head. You squeeze the trigger over and over, your shocked cries drowned out by the repeated gunfire.

[Hand-Eye Coordination check: 25/25 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

Your aim is terrible. The bullets fly wide. Their silvery trails clip shoulders, arms and do not pop anymore heads. But, it's enough. Your pursuers scatter further back. They recoil and hiss whenever the bullets whizz past them, clearly afraid of what's stored inside. It's a split-second chance, but that's enough. You scramble to your feet. You flee down the turf once again.

The rain falls. More mud splashes up your bare legs. The pursuers give chase, screeching louder than ever. You awkwardly aim your new gun behind you and fire again. Oh goddesses, are you using this thing right? Does it need reloading? Maybe not, considering you fired, what, nine or ten bullets without hearing a click? Why didn't you go with Saya to the arcade to play the shooting games? So many questions, and you've only just finished the first bend in this horrendous mockery of a race!

The red light strobes in your direction. Rings of them overlap and follow you. Another seizure of fear down your fine. Just as you're wondering if you can shoot down the lights themselves, a crackle of electricity sizzles through the intercom. There's a sharp cry of pain, and the lights switch off.

"Ruby."

A woman's voice floats out from the intercom, crystal-clear.

"Ruby, can you hear me?"

It's familiar. Very, very familiar.

Your lips tremble. Salty moisture gathers in your eyes.

"I'm so incredibly sorry that I took so long to reach you. I suspected the Nightmare had grown, but to strike you this quickly—never mind. I am here now. I am here to help you."

You lift your head and wail to the heavens.

"SENPAI!"

You're blubbering now, tears and snot rolling down your nose and cheeks in waterworks no Tracen student, Satono or umadol should be caught dead with. You don't care. A dam has burst in your head. The memories are flowing back: the meeting, the tour, her head bobbing along to that awful debut song of FAITHFUL's, the softness of her palm brushing your ears and the promise she'd always be your ally. Plain Jane is here. She's real. She was always real, and she was always around. You heard her whispers in the Prez's office. Your gut hunches were not wrong!

"For you to have manifested the soul of that silver bullet at such a nascent stage…you are truly one exceptional umamusume." Plain Jane muses.

"Help me, Senpai!" You wail, even though she is so far away. "I was in a race and then I woke up here where I was chased by monsters and I-I don't know what to do!"

You imagine her nodding, speaking through the microphone tersely. "This is a race, Ruby. A nightmarish one, but a race nonetheless. The Goddess of Victory holds dominion over this portion of the Nightmare. She has bound much chaos into stability, ensuring the only rule that has disappeared is that which prevents violence. Her will now dictates two paths to victory: reaching the finish line first, or eliminating the other participants. It's not too dissimilar to the Coliseum games from Ancient Rome."

You nod fervently, too overwhelmed to argue.

"Ruby, if you wish to survive, you cannot stay idle. You must win through either means. And for that, you will need power. Here!"

A loud booming soul. Twin beams of light soar through the sky from behind the turf walls. They crash land onto the ground a short distance ahead of you. Two duffel bags burst open, revealing their glowing contents: a uniform and another weapon.

"These are the gifts I was saving for you since the day we met. The uniform is protection. The weapon is strength. Take both and wield them against the forces of the Nightmare. Win, and we'll go back to Tracen together. I believe in you, Ruby!"

Your pursuers howl like starving wolves. They sprint forward with their hands outstretched, but it's too late. Plain Jane's words lit a fire in you. You sprinted faster. You grabbed both the uniform and the weapon out of the duffel bags, hauling them around and over you, and now you're ready to fight back...

[Your mood has become Normal.]

[Your Hand-Eye Coordination has increased by 10!]

[2000m remains in the race…]

The Nightmare twists and churns. A realm born from the shadow of hopes and dreams, it bears host to entire grimoires of gruesome creatures, hostile locales, dangerous traps and mystifying artifacts. Now, it has infested Tracen Academy, luring its students from the shadows to be hunted and ruined, eventually resulting in the downfall of the academy…unless you can somehow halt it.

Expeditions into the Nightmare are different to regular encounters. Your Health and Morale will be tracked.

Health: Equivalent to 1 + (Highest Physical Attribute / 3) Morale: Equivalent to 1 + (Highest Mental Attribute / 3) Your current Health is: 1 + (11/3) => 1 + 3 = 4

Your current Morale is: 1 + (10/3) => 1 + 3 = 4

Should your Health run out, you will be Downed. In this state, you are incapacitated, unable to act. You will eventually recover to 1 Health, as long as you are not damaged further.

Should your Morale run out, you will be Panicked. You will act erratically in this state for a time, almost certainly damaging yourself and/or your allies in the process, after which you will recover to 1 Morale. This is your current Panicked state:

Loses sight of herself and runs around frantically. May cause friendly fire if holding a weapon.

Different characters have different Panicked states. Catch them all!

The Nightmare is ruthless. It does not just inflict physical damage, it also damages its targets mentally and spiritually, resulting in the loss of their aptitude and the degradation of their soul. To combat the Nightmare, you and your future allies must wear regalia—uniforms infused with a trifecta of magical protection:

Byerley's Strength: Lowers the difficulty of stat checks to the extent where fighting against the Nightmare is realistically achievable. Darley's Courage: Ensures Mood remains the same when entering the Nightmare. Godolphin's Grace: Prevents the loss of EXP and other stats whilst neither Downed nor Panicked. By default, regalia takes the form of an umamusume's G1 racewear. This applies even if the uma has not entered a G1 race. The design of your regalia can be customized later.

Note: Your current regalia has no other effects beside the trifecta.

You must also wield weapons. These are tools that capable of harming the threats of the Nightmare. For example:

NameOwnerRankDescriptionAffected bySilver TracerSatono Ruby1A pistol formed from the soul of your lucky silver bullet. It is capable of firing bullets infused with colorless magic, which are capable of inflicting damage to a wide range of threats. A mild homing effect applies to each shot.Hand-Eye Coordination, Speed, Insight

Now, your regalia and weapons are clearly magical in nature, but explaining that requires a separate update with Plain Jane involved, so I'll say it basically involves drawing power from souls, both internal and external, and leave it at that. Also, your Health, Morale, regalia and weapons will receive their own unique upgrading opportunities in the future.
