EXP: 125/150

Mood: Normal

Health: 4/4

Morale: 4/4

You don't so much grab Plain Jane's gifts as they grab you. The purple-lined Starting Future outfit designed for backup dancers, along with a Western-style sword as fake as a cardboard prop in some photoshoot—and then they envelop you with their silvery aura.

The regalia is first. It loses its colors. It unravels its form. Streams of thread and ribbon fly forward and wrap around you like wind currents in a typhoon. Your muddy clothes are ripped away, devoured into sparkles of light that feed the ethereal thread, and before you have any time to comprehend that you are soaring and stark naked, the regalia reaches deep into the recesses of your soul and pulls.

A great swell of energy bursts out. It dyes the threads, weaves them right. It transforms the regalia into an embodiment of yourself.

A tight-fitting vest and long skirt beneath a regal jacket for your desire to be dignified and brave. Golden epaulettes in the style of your admiration of Symboli Rudolf and her many compatriots of her era. A sharp tie for a sharp mind, sturdy boots that hit the ground with perseverance, a cape for the girl who can and will run like the wind. And of course, the scarlet hues, the overpowering reds, hot and fiery and full of passion and love, for the companionship you always wish to seek, and for the love of your mother who gave you this pair of matching eyes.

The regalia forms its fronts and backs, tails and sleeves. It attaches itself to the curves and dips of your physique in a miracle of wardrobing. As you fall, it summons the final touches. Three hands grip you at once: a steady grip on your shoulders, a firm pat on the back, a nurturing caress beneath your chin.

Yellow, red and blue.

Each one wishes you great fortune in this gruesome world. They are familiar, achingly so.

The lights cease. You fall. You land on the grass. Your back foot sinks towards the earth, and the broken bottle lying there smashes into a thousand pieces.

"Go, Ruby!" Plain Jane shouts.

You kick off and tear down the turf, trails of silvery stardust flying behind your cape's wake.

The wind streaks past your face. It's cold. It tastes bitter from whatever rotting mass lies in the center of the railings, but that distaste bounces off your psyche. You are back to normal—no, you're better than that. Ears peeled, intuition sharp, muscles floating on thin air. Every ounce of fatigue has been replaced with pure sizzling vitality. It's as if you were never hounded by those monsters in the first place!

And your pursuers are not fans.

"Incoming, Ruby!" Plain Jane shouts.

One of them breaks out the pack and rushes up beside you, her ghastly features contorted with rage. She whips out her switchblade and slashes as she encroaches on your lane…

[Dodge check: 80/50 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

…which you dodge with as much effort as bobbing your head.

The pistol is in your left. Somewhere amidst the lights and sounds, it dropped to your inferior hand. You could switch it back and shoot your pursuer. You have a better idea. The second weapon from Plain Jane is tucked on your regalia's black belt. Your right hand flies down to your side, wraps itself around the hilt, and obliges.

A flash. A glint of sharp steel, shining from the spotlights that Plain Jane rigged.

You and your pursuer briefly stare at this short, sleek saber with a curved edge, this instrument of limb severing and blood spilling, and you panic, because umadols aren't trained to assault, only defend themselves and run. Will you accidentally cut yourself with this? Do you possess the upper body strength to swing it properly?

Who cares? Pointy tip goes in soft end! Imaginary Hotaru yells in your brain. And then she waves her own pocket knife around.

You swing your new saber. Oh, this is crap. You're no kendo genius, but you've tangled with your physique long enough to intimately understand you put in too much force, worked the wrong muscles. At least you know that swords aren't meant to be swung like baseball bats. And against all odds, it's effective.

[Swordplay check: 35/35 -> Success! + 10 EXP.]

The saber cuts through your pursuer in the chest.

Black ichor spills out of the wound. The shadow girl screams and topples headfirst onto the broken ground. She doesn't get back up.

"Well done!" Plain Jane calls. "One down, eight to go! You've got a good lead now!"

A cry of raw exhilaration, and you speed around the corner into the backstretch.

Action movies are your only frame of reference for shooting guns, so you copy them. Left hand outstretched, the pistol angled to the side, bang-bang-bang. Half the shots miss, which you determine by the lack of any cries of pain. The ones that do aren't enough to down them immediately. Quantity wins over quality. Around the start of the next corner, the pack's footsteps are dampened. Two or three more pursuers were downed, by your estimation.

Into the homestretch you go.

The remaining pursuers shriek, a keening sound like several wounded wild animals jumbled together. It means Plain Jane was right when she said winning the race would result in the banishment of this gruesome exercise. Nothing but pure desperation lives in that sound. The stampede hurries, and your pursuers surround you.

Two on each side, with the rest trailing behind.

One of them leaps off the ground and latches onto you before you can accelerate. Your center of balance immediately tips.

"Get off me!" You scream.

This new pursuer hisses back. Her sharp fingers clamber onto your own in an attempt to prise your new pistol off your grip. You squeeze the trigger and shoot her in the chest.

The blow pierces her, causing more of that black ichor to splash out. She doesn't let go. She digs in her heels, dragging her feet hard against the dirt, slowing you down as a loathsome dead weight. More hisses explode from her open mouth.

"Are you kidding me? You think I'm in the wrong?" You shout.

These creatures don't speak Japanese or any normal language. Their emotions, however, are plain as day. The hate. The rage. The indignation that you managed to pull yourself out of your lynching and are now mere moments from victory.

"You hurt me. You hurt others. You hunted them down and attacked them while they were vulnerable and confused. You are nothing but a pack of big, stupid bullies!" You scream. "I won't never lose to you!"

You swing your left hand and elbow this parasite in the bullet wound. Her hollow eyes bulge out of their sockets, and then she's falling, rolling and slamming into the rusted rail.

The rest of the pursuers make their last-ditch attempt. Five heavy bodies slam you from all sides except the front. You're tackled to the ground. This time, you don't lie there and take it. You thrash about, waving your gun and your new saber as dual clubs. You are a beast being frantically held down by the struggling hunters. The pursuers have to continuously press you down, barely able to fumble for their switchblades, and you are still so very enraged.

The surge you felt amidst your regalia rolls up your right hand. It latches onto your saber. It tastes the air and fire bursts free. An entire wave slashing up and behind you, full of that vicious, purifying power. Shadow flesh bubbles and burns. The pursuers scream louder than ever. You don't bother to check; you're already sprinting back towards the finish line.

[Soul Affinity with Fire was acquired.]

And you cross it alone.

The air ripples in your wake. A shift in the atmosphere as subtle as more cannon fire. You whirl around to see your pursuers scorched by the flames, writhing around on their spots. They clutch their heads. Their eyes and mouth bulge obscenely. They shake back and forth once, twice, and then they each explode into a mess of black particles that quickly disintegrate into nothingness.

"I won." You say.

"You won," Plain Jane says from the intercom.

"I won. I won, I won, I won!" You bounce up and down, still holding your two new weapons. You point your saber, still smouldering with embers, at the empty field. "Take that, you monsters! You stupid bullies! Don't you ever come near me or anyone else ever again, or I'll set you on fire and send you down to…to get hugged by Izanami!"

Lame. Imaginary Hotaru murmurs.

Shut up, you tell her. Just shut up. You barely escaped with your life. You deserve this.

The spotlights switch off. The stadium goes dark. Neither the oversized gates nor those hideous guards reappear. You stand there sweating, a cold wind kissing the back and sides of your ruddy cheeks.

"Senpai?" You call, cupping your hand to your mouth. "Are you there? Is it over?"

"I'm here."

Your tail goes rigid. You whirl around, and there Plain Jane stands, chestnut-haired, freckle-cheeked, looking exactly the same as the day you met her.

"Well done, Ruby. Very well done. That was a magnificent race you ran."

"Senpai!" You look down at yourself, dressed in this strange yet powerful uniform, twin pieces of weaponry in your hands. "I…"

She chuckles. "You have a lot of questions, I bet."

"That's an understatement. I mean, I'm so hot!"

"Yes, you are quite fetching in that outfit."

"No, I mean I'm literally hot. Burning up hot." You laugh and flex a bicep. "It's like a fever, but it doesn't hurt my forehead as much. Is it because I summoned fire out of this sword?"

"That might have something to do with it." Plain Jane says, cheekily. She points at your right hand. "By the way, you should sheath those weapons before you accidentally hurt yourself. Friendly fire is a real thing."

You blink. "Oops. Sorry."

Plain Jane chuckles again as you obey. She looks proud. It's the type of face that broke Manager Suzuki's stony facade whenever you and the girls pulled off a concert of a lifetime. It should give you a fuzzy feeling, and it does. Yet, your instincts do not abate. There's still apprehension.

"This isn't a dream, is it?" You ask.

"In the traditional sense, no. In what has been present throughout history since ancient times, yes," Plain Jane says. She glances to her left. "And this part of it is dissipating."

You follow her gaze. The stadium walls are crumbling, wisps of earth, concrete and plastic trailing up to a hole in the sky like swarms of tiny insects.

"The Nightmare is a world that overlaps across baseline reality, akin to a set of islands within a vast churning sea. When the core of an island is destroyed, it sinks back into the sea, joining the bedrock at the ocean to be reborn again. Though, instead of the islanders drowning, they are just catapulted back to your world, which will happen to you soon."

[(Wits check: 9/7 ) || (Logic check: 72/50 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

"So I'll wake up back at the tryouts?" You say.

Plain Jane nods. "Time flows a bit differently in the Nightmare, so you'll actually return immediately after the point of entry to here. Rest assured, it will be as if nothing had happened."

You smile. Your head throbs. You pinch your forehead and grimace. "Senpai, I think the opposite might be happening."

"What do you mean?"

"I mean, I don't exactly feel assured. Look at me. Look at what just happened." You turn side by side, showing off your new clothes. Your hands drift across your new equipment. "A gun? A sword? Monsters that held switchblades and stabbed me but I didn't bleed? That's not normal. That's a bit crazy."

"A bit crazy?"

"Insane. It's plain insane, no pun intended."

"I understand." Plain Jane says. She reaches out and places a hand on your shoulder. She gives you a squeeze. "The Nightmare is nothing like you've ever faced—"

The words blurt out of your mouth before you can stop it. "And then there's you!"

"Pardon?"

You point a finger at Plain Jane. "You were there. You were always there. The hint I got out of nowhere in the Prez's office when she asked me about what the academy motto meant—that was you."

Plain Jane's eyes widen a fraction. "You remember."

"It's like a blindfold was ripped from my eyes the moment you came back to save me." You say. Your head stings again. "You watched Narita Brian run a train over me! You're Tracen's friendly neighbourhood ghost!"

Plain Jane taps a finger to her forehead in exasperation. "That's…not what Miss Brian did. Ghost, however, is not a terrible comparison."

"Does this count as a reunion? Or are we meeting again because you erased yourself from my life for several months? Gosh, this is so confusing!" The blood rushes to your head. It's the memories. They're surging back, forging new connections in your neurons. It's a strain akin to a concussion. A hysterical giggle leaks from your lips. Your hands quaver, torn between throwing a hug or the biggest punch of your life. "Are you sure you're real, Senpai? Am I dreaming? A coma? Another concussion? Tell me, what am I supposed to do!"

"Nothing."

The glibness of Plain Jane's response stops your rant dead in its tracks. You stare at her.

"Nothing?" You repeat.

Plain Jane nods.

"Nothing." She clarifies.

Another swift answer. It's as if she was prepared for this response all along.

"Why?" You exclaim.

"Because explaining the Nightmare and its facets, including the existence of magic—" Your ears twitch at the latter's mention, "—will take an entire sitdown and a discussion. You don't deserve to have your ear lectured off by me at the moment."

"I…" You swallow. There's a lump in your throat. You want to be angry, or at least think you should be accelerating towards that point, but her words are like a cold bucket of water. A parry in a fencing contest. They send you crashing back down to reality. "I guess so?"

"And you have full right to be upset with me."

"I'm not." You protest, and then think. "Much."

"Were you from the Gold Clan, I'd have prepared to dodge some hands."

"I take it back. I'm definitely not that mad at you."

"Well, I wouldn't blame you if you were. I was avoiding you. Partially to prevent the Nightmare from accelerating, but also because I thought it'd come across as strange to your peers if you talked to a person you could not perceive." Plain Jane says, and then sighs. One foot of hers scratches against the ground. "That's just an excuse. I could have made it work. It was a decision that I made for you."

"I don't think I like those a lot." You say.

"And I'm sorry for that." Plain Jane replies.

She's sincere. Working as an umadol means wearing a mask, and wearing a mask properly means learning when one isn't worn at all.

There's a rant bubbling inside of you, born from the girls who lost their will to race, the apparition at the stump, the sudden downpour, the whispers of your hecklers growing louder and louder, and Aston Machan, the girl whose actions you can predict milliseconds before they happen. You are aware of these oddities. You tried to suppress them, perhaps by some instinctive, long-forgotten protective mechanism in your brain, but you can clearly focus on them now. Alongside the existence of this realm, they paint a truly horrendous picture.

You could get mad, you suppose. Shout at Plain Jane. Grab her shoulders and demand the truth. Accuse her of all sorts of emotional crimes. The energy that summoned your pistol and your fire rises up again, ready to lash out with glee once again. But…

[Light Alignment > Dark Alignment.]

…you remember the hand she put on your head. She said she was your first ally in Tracen. She comforted you and said that you were not responsible for the sins of your mother. Very few older figures have ever bothered giving you that courtesy. Plus, Plain Jane did save you. She gave you the weapons on your belt and the regalia on your back. If she wanted to harm you, she could have simply abandoned you on the turf.

[Psyche check: 9/9 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

From how apologetic she acted right before she hurled you the equipment, she must've misjudged or been unable to predict the arrival of this 'Nightmare'. Maybe she was as frightened as you were. It's a sobering thought.

You don't want to be mad at Plain Jane. You want to believe she won't be like those adults back at the shrine, who evaded your questions and took perverse glee at lording their so-called superiority. So, to check, you ask more questions.

"Do I still have a chance at a normal academy life?"

"Once the Nightmare is acknowledged, it cannot be forgotten. But it ebbs and flows, so there will be times of respite."

That's a yes, then.

"Will I still be able to make friends? Run the Twinkle Series? Win a G1?"

Plain Jane nods at each other. "We'll work together to ensure you can."

Once again, you can tell she means what she says. It'll have to do for now. Life has never not thrown a curveball; this will just be another.

Your ears return to their neutral position. The fire in you smoulders.

"Buy me some super special dream ice-cream and I'll forgive you." You mumble.

Plain Jane bursts out laughing. It's as melodic as the time in the dream infirmary room. She sweeps you into a big hug. Her soft hand rubs a circle on your back.

"Oh, Ruby. You must have been so terrified." Plain Jane coos. "And yet, you were so, so brave. You wielded your regalia and your weapon so well. Such a natural and accomplished kouhai I have."

Plain Jane isn't as old as an adult, at least not on the surface, so the hug feels sisterly. Strong, firm and warm. She smells of sweet dandelions and fresh grass. It's a nostalgic scent. You relax into her embrace, resting your head on her shoulder and wonder if this is how Diamond feels whenever she's with Crown.

"Thanks, Senpai."

A ghost and a cosplayer who can set her somehow real sword on fire. What a pair the two of you make.

"You were a true hero." Plain Jane continues.

"I am wearing a cape."

"And by defeating this portion of the Nightmare. It was tormenting other girls, too. By destroying those Nightmare Horrors, you saved their souls. They'll keep on running thanks to you."

The ground shakes. You look over Plain Jane's shoulder and see the stadium crumble faster. Chunks of concrete and steel slough off its roofs and crash to the ground, sending large dust clouds billowing. The inner railing begins to flake into a rusty heap. The grass withers and dies.

Plain Jane digs into the pocket of her uniform. She pulls out a small crystalline substance and crushes it in a single blow. Another wave of silver light envelops you, and then you're both gone.

[YOU ESCAPED THE NIGHTMARE.]

[Plain Jane sacrifices something important. The prior decrease to your tagged skills was nullified.]

Warm afternoon sunshine high above. Real and fresh and not trash-littered turf beneath your feet. Behind you: a white line painted across the grass, and beyond that are the bleachers chock-full of living human and umamusume bodies.

Tracen.

This is the racecourse at Tracen Academy. You're back at Tracen Academy, just as Plain Jane said you would!

With shaky hands, you cup the air. With burning lungs, you suck it down. It's tinged with hints of oil from fried snacks and the aftertaste of petrol via the maintenance machines, but oh goddesses, if it had lips, you'd kiss it. You want to shout and scream and cheer in these perfectly ordinary and completely satisfactory borrowed shirts and shorts. Except, you're exhausted in mind and body, so you settle for basking in your glory, hands on your hips, before taking a good look around.

The bleachers are quiet. Near silent. Wide eyes, pointed fingers, whispers behind the hands, the whole shebang. The notion is not unheard of in concept, considering that was the general reaction to FAITHFUL before you all switched to enka, but from several hundred people at once?

Scary, scary.

[Composure check: 62/25 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

But you endure, because at least the crowd here are merely staring and pointing, not attacking you with knives.

Then, you notice the trail of sweaty bodies behind you. There's a lot of them. Happy Meek, Rice Shower…everyone except Kitasan Black. Did you miscount? Nope. She's not here.

Wait.

That could only mean…

"…what a finish. What a finale!"

The warble of the commentator breaks through your consciousness. If everyone but Kitasan is behind you, then that means…

"I can't believe it, folks. We just saw an insanely close battle for the last stretch of the last race of the day! Every one of these girls gave it their all, yet one winner stands alone, and only by little over a nose: Kitasan Black!"

The jubilant voice rings across the track. Behind you, the scoreboard reveals the rest of the top results. Fourth place: Rice Shower; third place: Happy Meek, and second place: Satono Ruby.

That's you. You, the malnourished idol. The no-racer, the academy joke, the runaway and a thief, the scorned daughter of Satono Opal who robbed others of their rightful place, who flunked her early classes, who had zero proper training unlike her estranged sisters before arriving at Tracen...only lost to the rookie of the year by barely under a second.

A second, for reference, is about as much time as is lost from a late start.

A coughing sound catches your attention from behind. You turn around. Kitasan Black heaves loud gasps further down the track, bent over with her hands on her knees. Unlike what the crowd expected, she's not triumphant at the thought of securing her place inside Team Spica. She's not even waving at the crowd. She's looking straight at you, and her eyes are full of fear.

[An alignment shift brews…]

[Total EXP Gained: 35. EXP threshold met. 1 LEVEL UP achieved!]

3.11: Minor Prestige

>>[ResultFeelings] Second place, it's proof that you belong here. Next time 1st place will be yours.

>>[Crown] Look for Grass and smile and bow towards her.

>>[KitasanReaction] Offer a friendly handshake AND challenge her for next time.

Mood: Normal.

EXP: 10/160 (2 LEVEL UPs pending...)

The Tracen racetrack scoreboard, that hunk of black plastic and metal, flashes the results for the entire racetrack to see. For once, first place is nowhere near the top of everyone's attention. That honor belongs to second place, the silver medal, the big 'II' in LED yellow.

You.

That's right, you realise again and again with each ragged breath. The name up on the penultimate slot is not Happy Meek. It is not Rice Shower, nor Cheval Grand, nor Mayano Top Gun or the many other hopeful umas who attempted the Medium-long race today. It's your name. The air does not wobble. The scene does not melt. That 'II' up high is your result. The fruit of your labors. You made that late start. You caught up regardless. You weaved through the encroaching pack with quick footwork and a sturdy sense of balance. You charged down the homestretch to the finish line against three others who were supposed to be as insurmountable to you as Mt. Fuji is to a mere kappa. You, you, you.

They'll have to measure the gap between you and Kitasan in centimeters. This was a finale fit more for Tokyo or Nakayama than a mere school zone, and the crowd knows it. Adjacent to Kitasan's fearful stare, shock frames itself across hundreds of faces. Hushed lungs, mouths pushed shut, shaking held phones.

Amidst them, veterans such as Mejiro McQueen and that Nice Nature uma (who almost became your student mentor) contemplate. They push their bewilderment for contemplation. They taste that tantalizing, sweet yet bitter taste of the what-ifs.What if you hadn't had a late start? What if these tryouts had been delayed by another week? What if Kitasan Black had started one post more inwards?

You don't know. You want to know. How the tongue of your mind drools for more. It's not the only emotion swirling there. The adrenaline's wearing off; the reality of five minutes ago smacks you in the face. Shivers crawl up your spine alongside the shudders of raw physical exertion. A shadow world exists alongside Tracen. It was responsible for hurting students behind everyone's backs. It probably created the girl who was groaning into the stump on that one pre-dawn morning. There was a desolate stadium playing gruesome war games littered with shadowy figures and broken bottles leaked their noxious smelling fumes and they were banished by surges of mysterious flame and billowing threads of ethereal silk wrapping around your form by a ghost. Magic is real.

[(World Resonance check: 72/20) || (Insight check: 10/4) -> Success! +5 EXP.]

It circles around your silver bullet via invisible wisps, whispering the feeling of your hands upon that gun.

Nothing has felt more late-night anime binge in your life. The sweat soaking through the back of your shirt begs to differ. It's slick as a rainwater puddle. You're lucid. The Nightmare was real. And with this comes indignation—no, scratch that. Frustration. A fist curled. Fingernails digging in. Add another what-if to the list. You're not sure how the Nightmare works precisely, but it definitely interrupted you as you were running the last hundred meters. Without its nasty invasive comments, you totally would have won.

No, you are not in denail. There was momentum in your body. Momentum!

But, tunneling through the anger, the shock and awe; grander than the Shibuya skyline, sweeter than any vending machine ice-cream, and purer than a young child's heart: joy. Raw, precious joy. You want to leap about, waving your hands and leaping straight into a winning live's dance, because this race was not just a means of attracting a Trainer. It is proof of your place, forever immutable by virtue of the past, and untouchable by even your estranged family.

[Composure check: 62/50 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

This is only a tryout, so you break into a wide, wide smile instead, as a mechanical grunt echoes over the microphone.

"And that's the last race of Tracen's first tryouts for 20xx! C'mon folks, make some noise for our brave umas! Everyone did a fantastic job!"

The claps start up as a tiny smattering, a few hesitant brave ones leading the charge. Heads turn to the upper echelons of the bleachers, where Symboli Rudolf sits. Rudolf, along with her student council and a few notable veterans in Maruzensky, Mr. C.B. and more, gives the crowd the approval they want by clapping wtih gusto. The floodgates open. Mass applause rains out from the crowd, along with whistles, brief cheers and flashes from professional and phone cameras alike.

[Social Media check: 57/40 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

You pose with V-for-victory hand signs and hope some of those cameras snap a good look of your fatigued yet triumphant form. Hard work and results—that's what makes the real headlines in the racing world. This is the umadol brain in motion.

Behind and around you, the rest of the contestants totter to their feet. Happy Meek's gone back to staring off into the distance. She might be running through her own script of post-race retrospective; there's a noticeable frown there. Rice Shower is having her own regrets, judging by her hung head and her clenched hands. The other six girls, who failed to reach up to the pack of four, are wiping the seat off their brows and shooting you the usual nasty looks. The venom's gone out of them. These girls are furious with themselves, since they thought they had a swift ride, then lost to the worst-seeded girl in front of the entire school.

You stare at one of them. Faster—Faster than—the girl who led the charge in trying to box you in. Her name eludes you. There's a second of eye contact before she averts her gaze. It's tempting to stick your tongue out and mess with her. Thumb your nose. Cement your superiority in naked public. But hold on, that's already happened. The scoreboard's proof, and besides, you've only got so much energy left in your tank. Faster than whatever is let off the hook for now.

You stride a length down the field. You ignore the dark little voice that tells you to look at Diamond or Crown. You face the spot in the bleachers where your friends are.

Meisho Tabaru and her new Trainer—Fumino Nase if you remember correctly. They're clapping politely, and Tabaru is smiling honestly again. Makitanefukukitaru is slamming her palms together with that heavy crystal ball on her lap. Aston Machan rests a miniature doll of herself on her lap. When she catches your eye, she winks and her demure smile widens. Even the Nakayama gambler girl is there. Seated alongside her cousins, she grants you the honor of a cocky, casual smirk.

Finally: Grass Wonder. Your student mentor, the elegant, strong senpai who was there for you since your very first day at Tracen. She does not weep, because this is merely the beginning of your journey. Yet, her applause ring louder than anyone else's, and her visage beams with vast pride.

Relief.

For a moment, you were worried she'd be upset at your second place, given her competitive streak.

A lump forms in your throat. You swallow it. If Grass Wonder won't shed tears, neither will her umadol protégé. But that umadol will demonstrate her utmost gratitude. You straighten up your posture and bow from your waist with a hand swept across your side. A perfect, FAITHFUL motion.

Your wonderful friends deserve nothing less.

[Prestige has increased by 3.]

[+3 to Light Alignment.]

[+2 to Lawful Alignment.]

[+1 to Chaos Alignment.]

[Overall Alignment did not shift.]

"Dude. Dude!"

"Let go of me."

"Are you crazy? Do you even know who you're snorting like a bull at? You're gonna piss off—"

"Who gives a single sh—anything about that! Don't tell me you didn't see her strides or her recovery or finesse—Satono Ruby!"

"Y-yes?" You yelp, standing at attention.

This human man in the black jacket and grey tracksuit pants, looking like any ordinary citygoer obsessed with minimalism if it weren't for his official Tracen badge; he sprints from halfway down one set o bleacher stairs and across the grass towards you. He seizes your hand—or would have, if you hadn't reacted with a quick backstep.

"Fantastic performance out there!" The Trainer exclaims in a mild, scratchy voice. A possible sign of too much late-night caffience. "You sure showed them!"

"Thanks?" You say.

"You've got serious potential. Champion-level, even. Please! Allow me the honor of pulling it all out by becoming your Trainer." The man babbles. He smiles, holding up his finger to list options off. "We can start by building your core strengths, then covering your weaknesses through rigorous study, before taking on a graded race at the end of the year. If all goes well, that G1 victory will be ours!"

"Don't listen to him! He barely made it through his entrance exams." Another Trainer, this one a woman, runs up and damn-near shoves the man aside. A piece of paper held bewteen her index and middle flaps in the gentle breeze. She holds the bottom of it down, showing its contents to you. "Miss Ruby, I've got the contract filled out right here. I have experience managing over half a dozen trainees who have all surpassed the G3 level and I possess sponsorship connections with sports stores ready to supply you with the best tracksuits, shoes and cleats in Fuchu. Will you take on the Twinkle Series with me?"

You take another step back, flicking your gaze back and forth between two sets of eager eyes, and then some more. Oh goddesses above. This is it. The logical conclusion of excelling at the tryouts: the part where Trainers crowd the standout rookie and beg her for contracts. It's a scene you've witnessed multiple times in movies and documentaries and only fantasized about due to your less than stellar entrance exam results, and now it's happening in your face.

Secretariat. Danzig. Haiseiko. The heroines in those movies made their decisions on the spot. You're not ready for that. You are so not ready. Sweat beads down your forehead as more Trainers clamor with their own proposals, and you feel the inner railing inching closer and closer. Um. Uh. Kaede? Manager Suzuki? That one underground arena janitor who always managed to break up fights between rival girls? Are you meant to dress well for these affairs? Your head is spinning from the noise. This would be an excellent time for your mother to materialize out of nowhere and give you advice!

"Fools. All fools." An older woman approaches, clad in a dark grey suit. Spice-laden perfume sold in designer boutiques wafts from her neck. She smirks at her competition. "You are not understanding the crux of the matter."

"Who cares about the Satonos?" The first Trainer shouts. "Tracen ain't their backyard!"

You'd burst out laughing, if you weren't so preoccupied with your nerves.

The suited Trainer clicks her tongue. "Diamond and Crown both attend. A conglomerate heiress and a very well-respected manager in the family's business management division, despite her young age. Who do you think helped schedule today's event? And do any of you fully comprehend the burden this uma holds? Will you be able to shake off the Satonos' lawyers? Negotiate with sponsorships to give Ruby a chance? Do you people have the faintest hint of an idea of how to distance her from her mother's sins.""

Your ears prickle back at that. The nervous smile you were growing constricts into a tight line.

The woman doesn't notice. She basks in the rest of the Trainers falling silent. Calmly, assuredly, she approaches you and extends a hand, her eyebrows lifting slightly.

"Rest assured, Satono Ruby. With my half a dozen years of experience—more than the rest of these Trainers, I must point out—alongside my repertoire in law and business, we'll be able to navigate those turbulent waters with ease. All I ask is your full cooperation."

You don't doubt her expertise. Her getup is the same as the other salarymen you saw bustling around Tokyo. Still, you do not take her hand.

[Orphaned: Exists.]

Because she certainly feels entitled to your attention. The rest of these Trainers: did one of these adults send a single kind glance your way before that race? How many of them took pleasure in mocking your mother behind your back? The rest of your glee drains, and a mix of dread and annoyance coil around your center. One of Kaede's old stories floats back up, in which a sleazy manager signs up a decent rookie, uses it to advance further in the business, then abandons her to rot for some fresh new talent.

[History check: 45/60 -> Failure.]

You don't know any examples from the URA, but they must exist. Human and uma psychology doesn't change that much between industries.

Just as you're wondering if hightailing it out of here sounds like a good idea, a man's drawl cuts through the crowd.

"C'mon guys, don't hound the poor girl at once…"

Fluffy-brown hair with an undercut on the left; a black vest and a yellow dress shirt on a lean posture. He tsk-tsks around the lollipop in his mouth.

"You saw that final heat. Poor girl's probably exhausted from running her legs raw, so why don't we give her some breathing room. She's not going to have an answer for all your proposals at once anyway."

"Ah, shove off Okino!" One of the trainers shouts. "You just want her first!"

Trainer Okino chuckles, an easy-going drawl. "I won't pretend Ruby here is easily one of the most attractive prospects. She's got the talent, the hard work ethic and, most of all, the initiative to put both into good use. But…"

His eyes fall on you for a moment before departing.

"As much as I'd love to have her, I already made a prior agreement with another uma." He turns his head and calls, "Right, Kitasan?"

Some distance away, Kitasan's tail yanks up. You realise she's suffered the same fate as you. She's quick to scurry over after stammering out an apology to her crowd of hopeful Trainers.

"Yes. Kitasan Black right here!" She cries.

"So, are you in?" Okino says.

"In…?" Kitasan blinks once before her brows lift and a big smile slowly forms. "You mean...?"

"Don't tell me you forgot about our deal already?" Trainer Okino says, grinning. "Teio was super excited to see you come in first, you know. She almost fell out of her chair. The other girls were happy, too. One open slot in Team Spica, all yours for the price of a handshake."

"Yes!" Kitasan almost shouts. "Yes, yes, yes, of course I will!"

Kitasan latches onto the man's open hand, shaking it up and down as if it could dissipate into mist at any second. Her new Trainer gives her the thumbs-up and claps her on the back, then guides her towards the bleachers where the rest of his team no doubt are. Some of the nearby Trainers groan. No doubt some of them were hoping for the minuscule chance of Kitasan being open to offers. Alas, you can't beat an uma's team of her dreams.

Watching their retreating forms, you get an idea. You face the assembly of Trainers and give them a short bow.

"Thanks for your kind offers, everyone, but I'm afraid I must agree with Trainer Okino. This is not a decision I can make hastily. A Trainer is the second half of an umamusume's career, as the saying goes, which means I must take sufficient time and effort to contemplate my decision. It'd do Tracen a great injustice if I didn't. I hope you can understand these thoughts and feelings of mine and, again, thank you, and I hope you all have a lovely day!"

You flash them a trademark charming umadol smile, then sprint over to Kitasan.

"Kitasan!"

She flinches at your call. "Y-yes?"

You stop in front of her. At first, you're not certain what to say. To the rest of Tracen, she's a top rookie, best friend of Diamond, and daughter of an enka singer, in that order. To you, she is an arbiter, perhaps even an enabler of the Satono's antipathy towards your very soul. For that, you have been upset at Kitasan. In a dark corner beneath the pounding rain, you might have hated her. These feelings could very well be mutual.

Yet, she put whatever reservations she inherited to run her hardest against you. No shunning. No uncalled taunts. Just respectable competition.

And honestly, that's all you've ever wanted.

You put out your own hand for a shake. Kitasan eyes it, then glances up at her new Trainer. He nods. She tentatively grasps your hand. Her fingers are callused-kissed but not truly roughed.

"That was a great race!" You declare, then point your thumb at your own temple. "But don't get too cocky. The next time we meet, I'm taking first!"

The nearby crowd of Trainers gasps. A camera clicks. Kitasan looks thunderstruck, stuttering a response. You ignore them all, give them a wink and another grin, and finally dash off to the sides of the grounds for your quick escape.

Yes, you think. Nightmarish alternate dimensions aside, today was a good day.

[Prestige has increased by 1.]

[Total EXP Gained: 15.]

3.12: Ripples

1.

As you wave and bow and then become mobbed by starving Trainers, Cheval Grand sucks in air. It tastes of snack sugar and sweaty palms that twitch her nose. She realises her palms were digging into the sides of her seat and yanks them off, hoping the surrounding people didn't see while she adjusts their gap. The answer's no. They're too busy discussing the last race with gusto, and that makes Cheval grimace all the more.

"The rumors lied to us!" Her sister, Vivlos, groans.

"They always do." Cheval says.

"But we got suckered in, Chevacchi!" Vivlos cries, rounding onto her sister. She fidgets with the ribbons intertwined in her twintails. "Everyone said Satono Ruby was like, the bottom tier. Instantly cooked the moment she stepped out of the frying pan. Not you or me or even Verx put her on our radar, and now she's like, super super good all of a sudden. She almost beat Kitasan! What are we supposed to do now?"

"Calm down, for starters." Cheval mutters, knowing it's never that easy when Vivlos is in a mood. "Then find ourselves a Trainer who'll provide us with the real facts."

She's equally as perturbed as her Dubai-loving sister. She just has a better time concealing it.

And she watches you more, replaying the trajectory and velocity of your mad dash through the gap of the pack. Had the race allotments been switched around, could she have beaten Kitasan? Could she have beaten you? In a fully optimized landscape where her condition was at the tippest of tops, maybe. That never happens, and Cheval can't recall anything else about you besides this race. The real answer squirms out amidst a foundation of track times and gym class results. She doesn't like it.

"We might have to ask mom and dad for help." Cheval Grand muses.

Vivlos makes a whine and pouts. "Do we have to?"

"I won't tell her about your last shopping trip, I promise," Cheval says. "It's more about screening advice. How to spot experts from amateurs, and stuff. I'm not siding with anyone who hates Satono Ruby so much that they develop a blind spot for her."

That, and she remembers her mother, Halwa Sweet, raising her voice about Satono Opal at the dinner table once. The two of them might've had some history.

2.

"That was magnificent!"

"I don't get what all the hype is about."

Two rookies, one exuberant and headstrong, the other a petite firecracker wrapped in a flight jacket, find themselves at an impasse.

"What? Don't look at me like that. Ruby wasn't that good." Mayano Top Gun harrumphs, a pout between her angelic cheeks. "I could've totally made that last turn. I wouldn't have late started in the first place, because I do gate training."

"No, no, no, with all due respect, you are totally wrong." Kawakami Princess retorts.

Mayano narrows her eyes at Kawakami. "Are you challenging me?"

"As in the fact that Ruby isn't good. She is! We can see it!"

"I could've totally made that last turn. I wouldn't have made a late start in the first place. I didn't! But I don't see the whole school making a big fuss about it."

Kawakami chortles, hand to her chin. "You and Ruby are different. Apples and oranges! Ruby suffered a late start, almost got boxed in, faced down the champion of our year, all the while shouldering the burden of everyone's shared disappointment, yet she didn't give up and kept on pursuing the gold medal. It's a classic underdog story, burning brilliantly with the flames of passion!"

She sighs, dreamingly. "She must be a princess like me!"

"Maybe an evil princess from the evil Dark Lord." Mayano grumbles, sticking her tongue out in disgust.

Kawakami ignores the petulant girl. She clenches her fist. The flesh curls, unbothered by the extreme pressure sent down from the girl's mighty muscles. "I won't let our shared princessness stop us when we meet. When our paths cross, I'll do her the honor of bulldozing her into the dirt!"

"Do speak with a little more decorum. This is a racetrack, not a sumo ring." King Halo chides. She's seated next to her unofficial protégé, having paid the faintest bit of attention during a brief skim of her text messages. Clearing her throat, she adopts a stern, lecturing tone despite having almost crushed her soda can an hour earlier during Kawakami's race. "And it'll do for you to not underestimate that girl. I'll have you know that she's good friends with Grass now. Don't believe their involvement will stop after today."

3.

"Talk about a sleeper pick."

"You think she's a fluke?"

"If she is, Grass won't let her stay that way."

"Touche. But still…"

"Look." Daiwa Scarlet interrupts. "No-one goes limping through the Tracen's gates to almost beating the best rookie of the year. Zero chance the Director or any teacher is letting her get away with doping. Grass set Satono Ruby some insane Spartan training, and she passed."

Vodka sucks air through her teeth. She shakes her head. "I'm still mad about losing."

"But I'm right." Daiwa Scarlet says.

"As rare as that is—"

"Excuse me?"

"—you're right. That was a damn good turn she made."

Daiwa Scarlet looks back towards the turf. "The second one, right? Yep. That's a girl who optimized her own body."

"Hell, I have trouble making those kinds of turns on my ride, and that's backed up by steel and a real engine." Vodka says.

"And her stamina and speed's only going to improve from here on. Halfway there to her maiden race, I'd say. Trainer definitely would've picked her up if our team weren't full." Daiwa Scarlet remarks.

"Shit, maybe you should pay more attention in dance practice."

"Huh? Who was the one who tripped over her own tongue while singing Ms. VICTORIA?"

"Dancing, not singing, you dolt. Don't think I forgot you falling over on your fat ass. You should go on a diet."

"You shut your mouth. It's not my fault my family's pedigree is like this!"

The two girls squabble, as they often do. Halfway, they run out of steam and return to speculating about you. The fire of their competitive spirit has been kindled. It won't relinquish its warmth so easily.

"Kinda feels weird, hyping up this girl who's supposed to be our team's future opponent." Daiwa Scarlet says.

"I think Kitasan has received enough praise." A dreamy voice sings from the row of seats behind them. "Don't you think?"

Daiwa Scarlet and Vodka turn around to look at Aston Machan.

"These cinnamon buns are delicious, by the way." Machan says, holding up the sugar-stained cardboard box. The scent of strawberries and chocolate assaults the two girls' noses. "Are you sure you two don't want one?"

"Nah…"

"Just enjoy yourself, Machan…"

The two rivals sigh and grumble as Machan polishes off her bun, then goes for a donut. The age-old adage is true: a tie is always worse than losing.

4.

"You good there, El?"

"No, I am not good, Seiun!" El Condor Pasa wails, her hands to her head, an act suited more for fillies who just lost their favorite doll instead of arguably the strongest member of the Golden Generation. "I am horrorizada! How could Grass hog such an awesome kid from us for months?"

Seiun shrugs, munching on a piece of pocky. "It wasn't a secret. Half the school knew already."

"She invited Spe to train. Spe. Not you, not me, not even King. Spe!"

"Grass probably didn't want you corrupting her baby girl."

"I'm her roommate!" El wails.

Seiun kicks back and relaxes as her friend goes off on another rant. Secretly, she's happy for you. The kid who cried her heart out on that sunny day found her feet again.

The rest is in her hands.

5.

Mihono Bourbon closes her eyes. Afterimages from the beginning, middle and end of the race flash in the darkness.

"Processing complete. Accuracy of recording at approximately seventy percent. New threat of Satono Ruby registered."

The tall human man next to her grunts. The wind tickles his exposed abdominal muscles. Several women and Tracen students stare with intentions beyond passing interest, but he cares little. He looks at his new trainee through sunglasses as impenetrable as the bottom of a whiskey tumbler on a rainy Friday night.

"Good. You're not underestimating the competition."

"Proposal." Mihono Bourbon raises her hand. "Satono Ruby will be busy sorting through those Trainers' offers to find a suitable one. Her training will be comparatively inefficient during that time. I'd like to begin my new training regime immediately to take advantage of that gap."

"We can." Trainer Kuronuma says. "But it will only be a minor advantage, if she's anything like her mother."

Mihono Bourbon furrows her brow. "She is beatable. I will ensure it so."

Behind a pillar, two long uma ears tuck themselves away. Rice Shower presses her back against the concrete and nods in silent agreement.

A new target has been acquired.

6.

"You're not going to go down there?"

Oguri shakes her head. "It's too busy."

Kitahara Jo tussles her hair, chuckling softly as she bats his hand off. Older, smarter and stronger in heart, he is no longer the same man who quivered in his boots at the mere sight of Symboli Rudolf. The only new additions to his image are a few extra lines and the beginnings of some grey hairs. His cap and his jacket remain the same.

"You wrote the speech, talked it over with me, rehearsed it with Major of all girls, and the gift is right there in your hands." He notices you shaking hands with Kitasan, a faintly nostalgic smile crossing his weathered features. "Good wrapping paper doesn't last forever."

"It's not that." Oguri replies.

"What is?"

Oguri leans in to whisper into her Trainer's ear. Understanding dawns on him.

"Oh."

"Yeah."

Kitahara rests a hand on his chin, thinking. "You're right. You should definitely hold off on that gift."

"The Prez is weird, sometimes."

7.

"Everyone! Thank you so, so much for coming today. Don't forget: practice is the road to success, so don't be afraid to get out there and Umapyoi Legend in front of the mirror!"

Glowsticks wave, chants roar, and Smart Falcon takes her final bow atop the small portable stage. There were only two hundred attendees at a time due to the exclusive nature of the tryouts, but if her Umatube stats are to believed, she raked in almost a hundred thousand worldwide views! This impromptu dance lesson was a massive success, and she got to confirm that you're not a dirt racer.

Today was a good day for Tracen's true number one umadol.

[Smart Falcon's Dancing has increased by 5!]

8.

"Damn it! Fucking damn it!"

Behind the bleachers, Duo Pelte slams her fist against a brick wall. She only succeeds in sending spikes of pain up her own knuckles. Tears bead at the corner of her eyes as she clutches her injured fist. A movie plays in her head, of Tabaru's race, of your race, the other rookies' races, the sight of Stay Gold chatting with a tense Tabaru in the lunch queue, and finally her race. Sixth place. Not even close to the podium. Trainer Nase provides the credits commentary.

"While I'm pleased you have a good relationship with my new trainee, I'm not accepting any further applicants at this time."

Pelte shakes her head, trying to dissipate the woman's dispassionate, yet scrutinizing eye.

"I came third in Hidaka." She snarls to herself. "It should mean something! It should…"

"It'll be okay, Pelte. Different teams doesn't mean we're not friends."

But Pelte didn't get a team. Not a single Trainer so much as glanced at her. They cast her aside into the dustbin of gate fillers. A divide now stands between her and Tabaru, one that you have already crossed. Long ago, even.

Time will not reverse. Power will not suddenly flow itself into Pelte's legs. She curls up on the sun-kissed grass and hides her face, the shadows of the nearby wall obscuring her shaking form.

9.

"I take it you're not apologetic."

"I do not believe my actions crossed any line."

Trainer Hana pushes her glasses up. The walls of her office feel tighter. "Even if it means associating our team with Satono Opal, of all umas?"

"I would be more concerned if our team were not one that already possesses a stellar reputation." Grass Wonder replies, her tone equally as cool as her Trainer's. Hana's gaze sharpens, grows stern and angry. Grass just lifts her chin upward with pride, and Hana understands her star trainee already knows. She was, on some level, well aware of the PR disaster that follows when associating with an uma who permanently ruined several promising careers, yet sailed forth with that public show of support anyway.

She didn't even ask Hana or the rest of Team Rigil for their opinion. She just assumed it would work out, regardless.

"I will accept any form of punishment or distance from the rest of the team. I will even provide an official statement of apology, if necessary. The press may slander me all my want; my feelings on the matter have not changed. Satono Opal is a distant memory, while Ruby is one of the most dedicated, hard-working and all-around lovely umas I have ever had the pleasure of meeting. My family did not teach me to suffer injustice."

It is easy to forget, Hana thinks, that for all her grace, success and maturity, Grass Wonder is still a teenager. A stubborn teenger. A young girl not even in the prime of her life, who thinks she can handle the entire weight of the world on her shoulders. It is also ironic that a girl who tries so hard to act the perfect Japanese woman would inadvertently let that a spark of that independent, American spirit slip out.

There are ideals, and then there exists reality which grinds those ideals into compromises or dust.

Hana does not want to lose Grass Wonder. She does not believe that striking a friendship with you is inherently wrong. Yet, allowing Grass Wonder to remain ignorant would be a terrible mistake.

This talk will last a while.

"Congratulations on getting into Team Spica, Kitasan!"

"There's still time for you to switch—I'm just kidding. Congratulations!"

In the face of Diamond and Trainer Akiko's excited praise and passionate applauase, Kitasan knows she should smile back. Bless her young heart, she tries. The umas passing by are likely fooled, but not these two, who have known Kitasan ever since she was introduced to the Satonos at the age of seven.

"Kitasan." Diamond says, "Are you alright?"

"I'm fine? Question mark?"

"Question mark? Is that also a question?"

"I guess so?"

"My, you are in distress," Diamond remarks.

"Did something happen with Okino? I bet it was him. First, he lets Gold Ship run amok, then he dumps his entire paycheck while flubbing his chances with Hana…" Akiko shakes her head. "He can be a real handful sometimes."

"What? No! Definitely not!" Kitasan exclaims, perking up and waving her hands about. "My new Trainer was nice to me. He was just as enthusiastic as I was. It's just…"

The amount of immediate concern her two friends are displaying is overwhelming. She falls silent again, one hand gripping her arm in a sign of reluctance. Diamond and Akiko share a glance and agree to move this conversation elsewhere. They find a secluded part in Tracen's gardens, guaranteed to be deserted with most students returning to their dorms at this time of the evening. There, they guide Kitasan over, before they all take a seat on a public bench and wait for Kitasan to work up the courage.

"Aren't you guys upset with me?" Kitasan eventually asks, after a minute or so.

Crows caw in the distance. A cool breeze flows. Diamond thinks, her delicate ears twitching. "Did you accidentally leave your dirty socks about?"

"Nope."

"Thank goodness! The last you did it, it raised a stink and we both so mad at each other!" Diamond says. "But if it's not that, I can't think of any reason why we'd be upset with you."

"Because I almost lost to…" The name tastes acidic on Kitasan's tongue. She gulps it down. "You know."

The effect is immediate. A shadow crosses Diamond's face. Her smile strians at her edges, while Akiko purses her lips. Kitasan shrinks back in her seat. The sight before is a mimicry from not just that disastrous encounter with you and Oguri Cap in the coffee house, but from a long line of other instances at family dinners, karaoke sessions, and public events, all of which Kitasan either ignored or followed along, because it seemed like the right thing to do. Her eyes are open further. She detects, feels the repugnance these two have toward you slithering around her neck and temple, and shivers.

"Kitasan."

Akiko speaks first. Her tone is flat.

"Yeah?" Kitasan dreads the response.

You're right. That race was a very close shave. Had that girl exited out of the gate competently, it would have been a fifty-fifty toss-up whether you won or loss. There are many aspects of your performance that Okino will undoubtedly seek to improve with you on."

Kitasan nods. "I did sorta mess up near the end. Part of me was dragging myself across the finish line."

"It'll do you good not to forget those mistakes. But…" And this is where Akiko smiles again. "That doesn't mean you should deny your results either."

Kitasan hesitates. "That's a good thing, right?"

"Most certainly, it is!" Akiko exclaims. "You won your tryouts, silly. You signed up with the team of your dreams nigh immediately. Both these are major victories that any other uma would sell their best cleats for. You should feel proud of yourself."

"I still almost lost, though!"

"And you'll keep improving and improving, because that's the kind of hard-working, diligent girl you are. This isn't flattery, by the way." Akiko says. "These are the facts."

"You're so right, Akiko!" Diamond chimes in, all traces of her anger vanishing in a flash. She claps her hands again. "Why are we sitting around here moping? We should be celebrating!"

Akiko grins. She pulls out her phone. "Who wants Haagen-Umaz?"

"I do, I do!"

Kitasan watches Diamond and her Trainer pour over ice-cream deliveries like siblings. She can't help but smile at the sight. Hadn't Diamond said something about cutting back on sweets like McQueen? Oh, who cares at this point. Akiko has the correct idea, Kitasan decides. What's done is done. The results are set in stone, and they say she beat you fair and square. She can do it again. She will do it again. In the maiden race if that happens, in a G3, a G1, definitely, absolutely, now that Team Spica has her back!

So, she lets herself relax. She allows herself to scoot over on the bench, bumping shoulders with Diamond as she leans over, and offer her opinion on excellent chocolate desserts, thereby banishing the rest of the thoughts about you, including that handshake, from her head. Her best friend is smiling again. Life is good.

Elsewhere, Satono Crown picks up the phone, and prepares to offer her sincerest apologies.

And for the coup de grâce: Symboli Rudolf behind her desk in her office, reading through a report on her trusty laptop. She's tired from the managing the tryouts, yet she couldn't be more pleased.

"I think we can declare the vertical slice of the student mentorship program a success."

"You're not afraid that Satono Ruby might be too peculiar?" Air Groove asks.

"She's not that different from the kids who actually try." Narita Brian remarks from next to the water cooler. "Her family couldn't be assed to take care of her, is all."

"Second place is more than enough of an indication of success." Rudolf adds.

"I suppose we are planning on introducing tiers. And the project is still in its alpha phase." Air Groove mutters. She takes a paper off her own pile and places it in front of her. "Are we planning on making any last changes?"

"For now, no. Any more and we risk rocking the boat. This is a good selection." Rudolf spins her laptop screen around on its swivel axis, proudly revealing an array of mugshots. These are the potential student mentors, initially picked from a pool of almost fifty excellent students, then filtered down to less than a dozen. A student mentor cannot merely run well. They must express diligence, patience, prudence and flexibility in their efforts to uplist those who have lost their way, or were refused a chance in the first place. The finalists are therefore students who struggled through significant difficulties through their careers. Super Creek, Special Week, King Halo, Yaeno Muteki and more. Any umas possessing abnormal mentalities, even by Tracen's standards, such as Eishin Flash or Stay Gold, were eliminated.

Narita Brian idly reads the list again. She then notices more lines of text further down that Rudolf must have added in private. Upon reading those, she pulls a face.

"Rudolf, are you an actual psycho?"

"Brian!" Air Groove scolds.

Narita Brian rolls her eyes. She points to the screen. "C'mon Groove, look at that name and tell me the fallout isn't going to be obscene. And here I thought Rudolf telling Grass to train that squirt by faux-G1 standards was bad enough."

Rudolf lets out an awkward chuckle. "You're right. It was extreme."

"Self-admitted idiocy is still idiocy, Prez."

"I will defend myself and object to that. This is not idiocy, Brian. It is the correct course of action. I did look for a softer-hearted uma, but upon reflection there is simply no other student in this academy who will teach Ruby her next lessons with such enthusiasm." Rudolf retrieves her laptop. She stares at the final mugshot at the bottom of her hand and steeples her hands near her uniform's buckler. A slow smile grows on her regal features. "In fact, she and Ruby should have already made contact by now."

"That's definitely not ominous."

"It's for the good of Tracen, Brian."

It bothers Narita Brian. Normally, she'd write it off as Rudolf acting melodramatic while running high with joy at finalizing the first stage of her new project. Pencil-pushers aren't bathing themselves in what regular people refer to as fun. But, as Narita Brian pops a fresh grass stalk in her mouth, she examines her boss's emerging smile. A ferocious anticipation lurks at the edges, steepled in the slow thirst a wolf salivates with as it stalks its prey through the cold snowy night. It blazed in its full glory when Rudolf marked her targets upon the racetrack in the Twinkle Series long ago, then smouldered over the years as she took her current administrative position. Narita Brian has only seen it rekindle during Dream Trophy leagues, or whever her old friends come around and badger her for a chess game.

Now, it's back because of you. And it's not the first time today, either. A flash of remembrance, and Narita Brian recalls that a hint of that same, expectant edge cutting into Rudolf's look, high up in her personal spot atop the racetrack bleachers, shortly after you crossed the finish line.

Huh.

Someone's busy tracking their investments.

Narita Brian pours herself another drink of water and gulps it in a single go. She heads for door, changes her mind, pulls up her seat, sighs internally, and finally prepares to do some actual paperwork tonight. It's not the first time Rudolf has spawned a new, innovative scheme, and it won't be the last. And since it involves Satono Ruby and her 'wonderful' family, it means this student mentorship program has transformed into a long, troublesome ordeal-serpent that'll chew through and strangle their free time.

Whatever. She signed up for this. It's her duty to support the Prez. She'll wait and observe, and if Rudolf ends up being wrong...well, that's what a hard-headed, blunt-tongued uma like her is for.

Maybe they should actually try to get Ramonu on board. The hag would be thrilled to see her old childhood friend like this.

3.13: The heroine chooses

Mood: Normal.

EXP: 25/160 (2 LEVEL UPs pending...)

"Satono Ruby."

You've dealt with strangers for long enough to know when someone calls you with purpose.

A lonely side path to the Miho dorms, your hair dripping with lukewarm shower water; this is the state and location you find yourself and this new girl in. An indignant retort balances on the tip of your tongue, because you've had a day with more up and downs than a rocking cruise liner and it's just concluded with the best victory you've ever had, so there's no way you're letting any of the usual heckles ruin it.

The girl steps out of the shadow cast by a nearby lamp, and you go still.

"Hey." She says, shrugging one shoulder awkwardly. "Nice to see you."

"You…"

She's cast in the afternoon sun, this girl with the hair the hue of strawberry yoghurt, adorned with a large ribbon in the center and a cluster of fake pearls off to the side. A mild blush stains her cheek, the type from physical exertion and too much caffeine at once. The handbag slung across over shoulder is kitted with a jewellery bag's worth of pins. Opening your mouth to ask was not necessary. There is no mistaking who this uma is.
