???, June 1st, 20XX

A television sits in front of you, blaring out a variety of Tracen's greatest hits.

"Has it become a one-on-one battle between these two? Grass Wonder and Special Week! Here they go!"

Takarazuka Kinen. The final stretch. Your mentor clashes with her bumpkin rival from faraway Hokkaido, overtaking and slipping again and again in a loop on a distance that felt like an eternity for them. Darkness shrouds the surrounding air, drowning out the rest of the competition and the shouts of the commentator. Just as Special Week makes her final push, Grass Wonder clenches her teeth. Blue fire envelops her flowing form and she charges forth. Unburdened, victorious, and not collapsing to the ground, screaming in agony from the burns and blisters that should have covered her skin.

You obviously don't want that to happen, but it is odd. Your thumb, meanwhile, couldn't care less. It hits the forward button on the remote. The screen fizzles. A wall full of green-white URA logos greets you.

"Tenno-Sho, Japan Cup, Arima Kinen—I'm going to win all three of those autumn G1 races!"

Lightning blasts out of Tamamo Cross's diminutive form. The cameras snap their pictures unharmed.

The channel changes again.

"Gentildonna trying to get into the clear. She's switching lanes. She side-stepped out. Third place, here she comes, here she comes!"

The ground splinters apart on the Dubai turf, chunks of earth soaring and landing like falling meteors. No-one is crushed, least of all the Triple Tiara champion, who tears down the last fifty meters with a vengeance and wins just exactly like the results stated she did.

"To move horizontally while everyone else is moving forward is a near-impossible manoeuvre, yet that girl was mad enough to pull it off. They will talk about her audacity for decades."

Plain Jane approaches, wearing a coy smile. She pulls up a seat beside you.

"You know how if you listen to a song long enough, you'll eventually pay attention to the backing track, which then overrides the lead, and the song starts to sound like something else?" You say, not looking away from the television. "That's what I'm feeling now."

Japan Cup. That Folkqueen uma Oguri is enamoured with takes the finish line, a cloud of smoke and glass shards petering out behind her racewear.

You hit the remote and switch the TV off. A beat of stillness. You slowly turn to look at Plain Jane. There. Behind your forehead: a tensile wire of awareness. You lift your hands and slap yourself on the cheeks. The sting rings. You are lucid.

"I've seen it." You say. "Felt it, too."

"How so?"

"Oguri. The first day you met when she walked up to me from behind, there was still pressure crushing my back. It wasn't colorless, though. It was immense and burning, like a volcano had erupted out of the ground and was spewing everything out. Aston Machan—she feels like a fluffy cloud mixed with a marshmallow in my coffee. I'd say that even if you plucked out my eyes and put me in front of her. These…images? Auras? I'm not sure what to call them, but they've always been there."

"And you're only noticing them now." Plain Jane finishes for you. "It's a consequence of you entering the Nightmare. Think of it as a third eye opening."

"So what is it, this phenomena?" You ask.

Plain Jane pauses. She hums. "A manifestation of their individuality. You'd call it a soul. You seem to possess an unique aptitude to sense them."

You take this definition in. You roll it over your tongue and compare it to every other instance of the word you've heard: Miko training, anime, bemoaning in the music industry, URA reports. A combination of identity and consciousness. A crowd might share many different similarities, each person seemingly almost indistinguishable from one another, but dig right down to the core and view their backgrounds, habits, personalities and biases and you'll see they are technically, truly distinct.

The soul exists. It's a thing. A real thing, not mere theory. You've always been perceptive to a certain tendency of others ever since the day you fell and hit your head on the shrine grounds. Now you know what the origin of it is.

Alright then.

This is merely the beginning of a long lecture. Plain Jane will surely dump more earthshattering revelations upon you, so there's no use in getting your panties in a twist yet.

"Can my soul shoot lightning like Tamamo Cross?" You ask. "I want to charge my phone for free."

Plain Jane chuckles. She then raises a pair of fingers. "Two problems. The first is that the soul tends to manifest itself in your reality only during situations of high stress or emotion, such as competition. Secondly, you'd probably set that poor phone on fire because lightning is a volatile little beast."

Your dreams of saving money on portable battery chargers goes up in smoke.

"The first problem, however, becomes trivial when standing in a location with foundations in the ethereal and the mystical."

Plain Jane stands up. She lifts her arms upward and stretches with a soft grunt. A leaf detaches from high above and lands on your ear ornament, tickling the flesh around it. You're sitting on a plastic classroom seat facing a TV on a wooden classroom desk, but the walls around you have flattened down like the sides of an abandoned cardboard box. A tree rests next to you, its foliage of long, slender leaves casting a mild shadow across you. A wooden, earthly sweet scent wafts down, brushing against your nose, then it is swallowed up by rolls of manicured paddock grass, stretching endlessly in all directions.

"Behold." Plain Jane says, spreading her arms wide. "The Nightmare!"

The clouds are frozen. The sky is still. A serene stillness dampens the area, flattening any wind from disturbing the nearby flowerbed of chrysanthemums. You walk around and notice a pool of still water in a dip off to the side. A finger to the surface, and a ring of ripples casts outwards, shimmering with a swaying image of Tracen's main building. There are distinct lack of evil shadow umas wielding switchblades.

"It doesn't seem that dangerous." You remark, returning to your seat.

"Because it isn't. Or wasn't, to be more accurate." Plain Jane says. "This small corner of the Nightmare is how it has remained for most of its long existence: a distant, docile realm that only collected and transmitted bad dreams. Terrifying, yes, and responsible for a range of psychological conditions such as anxiety amongst the more afflicted, but very rarely anything permanent. At worst, the Nightmare would synchronize the souls of the supernaturally-inclined and frighten them for a while. That's what's happening to you, by the way."

She points at you. You look down towards your hands. Where the pink flesh should exist, it now fades away into a murky translucence. A white outline covers your digits and the outsides of your wrists. You do not panic. It could be worse, you think. This place could have shown you the inside of your skin.

"You stand here in Soul Form. Your physical body is currently asleep in bed dreaming, synchronizing your soul to this place. Imagine an invisible stream of water flowing out of your existence to this side, then manifesting a duplicate of your form. Different instances of yourselves, yet connected by a thread."

You raise your hand.

"Is it like streaming? Like with online concerts and vtubers and stuff?"

Plain Jane gives you a look. "From what basics I understand of the concept, yes."

"I get it, then."

The look continues. It's mild disappointment, of dusty librarians and random grannies at convenience stores when you tell them you'd rather watch Umatok instead of reading books. Plain Jane, thankfully, spares you the rant. She hops off her seat and withdraws a large black marker from her uniform pockets. She takes it to a portable whiteboard.

"All objects possess a soul." She states. She draws an umamusume, a dog, and a tree. "Sapient, sentient, inanimate. Doesn't matter how old the human, how small the insect, or how gigantic the mountain—no exceptions. They all have a soul. The magnitude of the soul varies, however, biased towards sentience or sapience, since it's easier to demonstrate individuality if intelligence is present. Competition also helps. Souls develop faster and greater when their holders are pushed to their limits. To give an extreme example, famous umas like Kincsem, Secretariat or Man o' War were said to radiate overwhelming presences. Their souls were too large for their cages. Inanimate objects, however, need significance placed upon them to distinguish themselves from their peers."

She picks a stray dandelion from the grass. "This is yet another flower, destined to be ignored as an individual. Its soul is less than a speck of a speck. However, if this dandelion were to be cared for by me—the soil tilled, the compost applied and the water poured—it would become my personal flower. The care and emotion I put into the flower would bolster its soul."

Ah. You understand. You reach down your collar, pull out your trusty silver bullet. This is the perfect example of what Plain Jane is talking about.

As you smile, a thrumming flows down your fingers and detaches where your skin meets silver. A flash of light erupts. You yelp, and the pistol you wielded in the Nightmare pops into your hand. You fumble with it, almost dropping it on the grass, and Plain Jane giggles.

"That's one use of an inanimate object's soul: a vessel for magic. But that's a topic we'll cover later."

"Excuse me?" You say, picking up your pistol and placing it in your lap. "But I want to learn about magic. That was the only fun part about that evil race."

"I know, I know. Magic is very exciting," Plain Jane says. She taps her marker on the board. "But there's no use learning it if you don't know what you'll be wielding it against."

Her smile vanishes. She regards you with a serious eye. You gulp and sit up straighter.

Fun time is over.

You're about to receive the answers you asked for.

"What do you think happens when the soul is damaged?" Plain Jane asks.

"You said it's based on individuality. Obviously, they lose it." You reply.

"Indeed. Now, soul damage is not easily recovered. It is a primary component of your existence, alongside your mind and body. Losing a chunk is comparable to losing a limb. What does that mean for a girl pursuing a championship in the Twinkle Series?"

If they lose part of their individuality permanently, they won't think about standing out as much. And if they give in to that mentality—

"They won't try as hard for first place?" You guess, "They'll stop pursuing their hopes and dreams for a long time?"

"Precisely."

Plain Jane doesn't elaborate further. She stands there with her arms folded, letting the thoughts sink in. It works. A dawning horror drapes itself across you the more you contemplate, month-old whispers and rumors flowing back to the forefront. Matikanefukukitaru's friend. Tabaru's old roommate. Both girls who dropped out of Tracen for inexplicable reasons. No-one knew why, since they were both physically and mentally sound and acting fine beforehand, but if the soul exists, and it truly is responsible for sustaining their motivation, then it makes sense those girls would give up without anybody understanding them.

"There were other victims the Nightmare sought." Plain Jane continues. "It lured them in through their Soul Forms, then set its Horrors upon them. They will never shoot for greatness again. That is one of the main dangers of the Nightmare: the destruction of the soul."

You sit there, stunned. Are you sure you should be listening to this? The soul existing is one thing. Plain Jane describing a hidden natural disaster is enough. Shouldn't the adults get involved? The police, the government, Director Akikawa? This is a national emergency! You quickly rationalize that won't happen, since you can't exactly bring a ghost to court. It doesn't make you feel any better.

A thought occurs to you. Your stomach churns. You're now feeling worse. "The stump."

"You saw something."

"A girl. She wouldn't show me her face. She kept asking me why I wasn't giving up. I chatted with her for a bit, trying to explain why, then Tabaru came along for our morning run, and when I looked back, she wasn't there!"

"A Horror. She almost got you."

You can't deny it. You made a move to pat that fake girl on the shoulder!

"It's a consequence of the Nightmare encroaching upon your world—let's call it standard reality to differentiate the two. Both realms are beginning to overlap in spots."

Plain Jane returns to the billboard. She draws two circles, one normal, and the other filled with squiggly lines. She redraws the two circles, now intersecting at a tiny fraction as a Venn Diagram.

"Technically, this has always been the case, since before only scarce special individuals could be summoned into the Nightmare, Its encroachment has now reached the extent to present an active danger towards the Tracen. The manifestation of Horrors in standard reality is one symptom. An increase in frequency of 'bad luck' events, such as sudden accidents or weather spikes, is another. With the interruption in your tryouts race, we can assume it's now possible to physically enter the Nightmare too. It's safe to assume that's limited to the supernaturally-inclined. It's still unacceptable, since their physical form and minds will be harmed alongside their souls."

"And this is happening all across the world too?" You exclaim.

Plain Jane shakes her head. "Not yet. The Nightmare's encroachment is currently only present upon Tracen. As the encroachment develops, every terrible fate that could befall upon the school will occur. The aftershocks may cause heavy, if not irreparable, damage to umamusume racing in Japan. Ultimately, the entire soul of Tracen will be consumed by the Nightmare. Legacy, students, faculty, Director Akikawa herself...either corrupted, exiled or gone. That's when the Nightmare will set its sights on Tokyo, I suppose."

Plain Jane doesn't sound excited or frightened or even furious when she concludes speaking. Just sad.

Your ears are pricked back, your tail dead still. A grinding sound. Your teeth. It's kegare again. You hate you jumped to this comparison so quickly, but there's nothing else. The Nightmare is very similar to what you learned about kegare: spiritual pollution that manifests sickness, accidents and harm by simply existing. And it's real. It's not scripture or prayer or invisible faith to keep peace at heart. It's real, and it's happening and it's already hurt innocent umas in your academy who could have been your friends.

You could have been one of those victims, too. A girl with a soul mauled to shreds, never to sing your heart out on stage with the FAITHFUL, never to savor the delicious exhaustion shuddering through your physique as you break yet another lap time. Never to dream about showing your mother's shoes to the whole world at a G1's winning live, because that part of you would have been amputated off, and it'd be as if you were back in the countryside as a small child. A steady life. A placid life. A grey, featureless blob in the shape of an umamusume.

Slimy nausea dredges up your throat. You cover your mouth with your hands and wait for the sensation to pass.

"How…" You swallow. "How do we stop this?"

"There are entities in the Nightmare, akin to power generators. Destroy them, and the Nightmare will lose its power. Given time, it will regress to its original form."

"And who's going to do that?"

Plain Jane stares at you. You blink. She keeps staring. The one-yen coin drops.

You point a trembling finger to yourself. "Me? You want me to fight the Nightmare?"

"I can travel to any location whose soul possesses a strong affinity for umamusume racing. I never would have imagined that the daughter of Satono Opal, of all umas, would have her eyes almost fully open." Plain Jane says.

"B-but I'm not strong! I was a miko-in-training and then an umadol and I've only just learned to feed myself properly." You protest.

"You've already defeated a group of Horrors, haven't you?"

Your ears droop. That's a fair point.

"You wielded your equipment like a natural. I was frankly a little astounded. I'd thought you struggle more with the regalia." Plain Jane says. "Anyway, that makes you more qualified than anyone in Tracen, no?"

Also true. Those evil shadow umas don't seem so scary after cutting several and setting them on fire. You were desperate back then, sure, but the fight after you got your new equipment wasn't what you'd call difficult.

The more you fight, the better you'll get. It doesn't mean you want to dedicate the rest of your school life to that, though!

"What about you? You're older than me, right? You're been around Tracen for longer." You say. "Don't know you know how to fight the Nightmare?"

Plain Jane doesn't respond. Her lips purse in contemplation. You think she's about to spurn you, before she walks around and takes her seat on the front desk again. She kicks off her shoes, a pair of black Mary-Janes from Europe. Then, she gently pulls down her stockings, exposing what's below.

A second of sight, and then the nausea rears itself back up in full force.

There, beneath Plain Jane's kneecaps, lies a pair of swollen and blackened lumps in the shape of legs. A moist sheen glistens the surface, oozed out by the ever-flowing pus from clumps of blisters that dot the flesh like miniscule mushroom clusters. The putrid odor of rotting meat wafts outwards, causing your eyes to water. It's horrible. You can't turn away. A sick fascination has gripped you, and with informs you with nasty glee that the flesh is neither dried nor leathery unlike that preserved mummy you saw in a museum trip once, which means nerve endings are still active. Forget running. The mere act of walking must be excruciating. Oguri and Mejiro Ardan and the many umamusume who suffered leg fractures would rather amputate their lower halves and spend their lives in wheelchairs.

Yet, it is how Plain Jane has lived and will live, forever.

"As you can see, I'm not what I used to be." Plain Jane says.

Your breath chokes in your throat.

Plain Jane lets the sight linger for a moment longer, then slips her stockings back on. She digs into her pocket and hands you a tissue. You only notice you're weeping after you've wiped half the tears away.

"There's a long story behind this injury. I'll tell you some day, but it's not relevant right now." Plain Jane says. She takes a soft breath, as if not enduring hellfire at her feet. "For the victims before you, I was able to catch up and withdraw them before the worst damage could be done, but I could not save them fully, nor could I avoid sacrificing part of myself."

A memory hits you. "The time we left the Nightmare…"

She crushed an object in her palms, then. A rainbow-colored light enveloped you, and the emptiness from the shadow umas' stabbing vanished. You thought it was the relief of returning to the real world, back then.

"You did it for me, too." You finish, hoarsely. "Senpai, oh goddesses, you…"

"And I'd do it a thousand times more, if it meant you would live to see another sunrise, unscathed. Same for the other girls. Same for this entire endeavor. Sadly, my reserves aren't infinite."

You lower your head, a big lump lodged in your throat. It's not fair, you want to protest. How are you meant to come up with a counterargument to that?

"It doesn't have to be you."

You look up. Plain Jane has seated herself at the desk in front of you, facing backwards in her chair. Her thighs wrap around the sides of her seat.

"There are other girls who possess an affinity for magic. That Aston Machan friend of yours is one of them. As the Nightmare approaches and intersects with standard reality more, more mystical phenomena will occur around the school, speeding up their awakening. Eventually, they'll reach the same state as you by encountering a Horror or accidentally falling into the Nightmare. They'll be ready to talk to me. I'll offer them the same thing."

"But, Senpai, you said the Nightmare will keep advancing. That means it'll eat more uma souls!" You say.

"Correct."

"And since I have the best chance out of everyone," You continue. "I could prevent that from happening if I started fighting it now?"

"Also correct. Others will awaken as the baseline reality around Tracen and the Nightmare intersect. That's sort of an inevitability. For the first juncture, it will only be you and me." Plain Jane says.

"Do…" You stumble over the words. "Do you think I can fight the Nightmare, Senpai?"

"I know that forcing someone to fight a war will only breed deep resentment in their heart." Plain Jane replies.

That's not a denial. If you do nothing, innocents will be hurt. If you move forward, you will be hurt. She knows this. You know this. And you are both at an impasse for words.

Plain Jane leans her head against her shoulder, tucking a strand of her hair back. She lets out a soft sigh.

"You are but a single girl. You suffered unjustly from the discrimination wrought by your family. You persisted through hardship after hardship, arrived at the academy of your dreams and are a single agreement away from taking on the Twinkle Series to take on the Twinkle Series, only to run headfirst into a vast realm beyond your control or comprehension. To say nothing of how more unfair the duty I'm imposing is. To act the watchful vanguard, always watching, always throwing herself into the maw of the Nightmare's endless labyrinths to fight its endless Horrors, unappreciated by most who cannot perceive the supernatural. It is a duty that must be prioritized over friendships and races and the dreams of an ordinary life; and it shall hound and punish and torment…"

"But someone has to do it, otherwise innocents will be hurt." You finish.

Plain Jane nods. Her mouth tightens. It's the first time she's looked so anxious, so uncertain.

"Will you do it, Ruby?"

(Will you fight the Nightmare? Top 2 wins.)

[] [DutyCalls] Yes. It's a necessary task to ensure everyone's safety.

[] [DutyCalls] Yes. My own soul is at risk too.

[] [DutyCalls] Yes. I fought the Horrors and won. I'll punish them good!

[] [DutyCalls] Yes. I want to explore the Nightmare and learn its secrets.

[] [DutyCalls] Yes. I'll save my friends from evil!

[] [DutyCalls] Yes. I can give it a good try.

[] [DutyCalls] Yes. It'll be a chance to earn more glory.

[] [DutyCalls] Yes. Because every uma has the right to freely run to their heart's content.

[] [DutyCalls] No. I don't want anything to do with this!

[] [DutyCalls] Write-in.

Magic is a manifestation of the soul's energy that creates miracles. Currently, it has the most effect within realms with higher supernatural tendency, such as the Nightmare.

Magic derives its resources from the user's overall energy pool akin to exercise, study and other intense activities. This pool is represented mechanically by the sum of all your Attributes, henceforth known as Soul Power. The more Soul Power you have, the more energy will be available for magic.

Here is how each Attribute affects magic:

Speed: Improves casting time. Stamina: Reduces magical damage, including self-damage. Power: Improves magic's forcefulness and explosivity. Guts: Reduces mental fatigue and degradation from magic. Wits: Makes magic more innovative. Psyche: Improves communication with magical entities, including your allies. Insight: Improves aim with magic. Increases overall sense of magic. The application of magic involves your Soul Affinities combining with Disciplines (i.e. specific schools of thought) to produce results. You currently possess the following Soul Affinities:

Basic: The most generic form of magic, usable by all. Fire: Heat, light and combustion. Destructive yet easily quenchable. Both Affinities start at Rank 1 and can only be upgraded through special means. Different characters will possess different Affinities. You may also acquire more Affinities as you delve deeper into the Nightmare.

Any disciplines can form a combination with any Affinity, including ones that seem contradictory. There are also special applications of magic unique to each user…but you're not at that level yet.

Your current application of magic is conducted through your weapon and regalia. You have already demonstrated the ability to coat your blade in flame, hence you will receive the following discipline:

NameDescriptionValueEnchantmentImbue your tools with power. Alter their physical properties.25

Magical Disciplines are treated as skills with special scaling: +1 for every +1 to any Attribute.

You will now gain two more Disciplines based on your primary weapon (the cavalry saber) and regalia, one offensive and one defensive respectively. Both will also start at 25. Assume that neither of them are wholly specific to your weapons or regalia. As an aside, your pistol is a little underpowered at the moment and can only resonate with the Basic Soul Affinity.

(What is your sword to you? Select only one.)

[] [OffenseDiscipline] A conduit for projecting and hurling energy. (Invocation).

[] [OffenseDiscipline] A tool to spread confusion and obfuscation. (Illusion)

[] [OffenseDiscipline] An implement of conquest to force others to my will. (Domination)

[] [OffenseDiscipline] A gateway to bring forth my dangerous friends. (Summoning)

[] [OffenseDiscipline] A means of turning my foes against their own allies and minds. (Derangement)

[] [OffenseDiscipline] Write-in. (Must have offensive properties.)

(What is your regalia to you? Select only one.)

[] [DefenseDiscipline] A shield to protect me from harm. (Warding)

[] [DefenseDiscipline] A conduit to draw energy from the environment. (Replenishment)

[] [DefenseDiscipline] A source of threads to restrain my foes. (Binding)

[] [DefenseDiscipline] An engine to strengthen my physical prowess. (Potency)

[] [DefenseDiscipline] Write-in. (Must have defensive or supportive properties)

You'll get to tag one of these Disciplines later.

Bear in mind that magic will not carry you alone through the Nightmare. You must also sharpen your other skills.

3.14: Sleepless Crown (Bonus)

It's twenty past ten and Satono Crown misses the taste of pineapple tart.

She's being foolish. A blockhead, as Duramente would put it. There is absolutely no reason for her to be craving sweets when an open laptop rests on Crown's lap, the half-finished draft of an email staring up at her.

She knows exactly what her aloof-minded, currently slumbering roommate would say. Is she a moron? Just do it. Slap your cheeks, knuckle down and get that work done. An uma only deserves treats after she's accomplished enough to treat—there! It's right there in the name, for crying out loud.

But Crown can't help herself. Tonight, Umasoft Word is cursed.

Because there was a delay at our partner factories, the delivery of silver thread did not make it in time. We apologize for the inconvenience—

No. This sounds like a justification instead of proper contrition. The apology is an afterthought. It's too offensive.

The silver thread was delivered later than expected; hence, the schedule for the upcoming line was affected. We are—

No. The usage of 'hence' suggests a cause, which implies it could have been remedied. That's untrue. The delay was caused by an accident on the road.

We are sorry for the delay and will proceed with adjustments.

This sounds as neutral as plain white paper.

Just accept the delayed thread the wedding's not for another three days you absolute asshole

And now her own thoughts are bleeding onto the text.

Frustration pulses against her forehead. It's one email. One apology. She's written them a hundred times before. For whatever reason, the words aren't coming. The characters on the screen morph into the glitzy text emblazoned on plastic wrappers. The more she stares, the deeper she tastes the treat on her tongue. That warm and rich butter crust shell, the spurt of hot and sweet jam seeping out from the first bite, the magnificence of how the mixture goes tangy and sticky-sweet and crisp as it grinds between her teeth before finally falling down her waiting gullet…

Oh no. Saliva bubbles on her tongue. She's drooling.

She sucks the saliva down with the insides of her cheeks. A near-silent motion; a product from years of etiquette training ingrained to become an instinctual habit. They flew a tutor over from Japan to her internship at Hong Kong, and sure, why not? She's already distracted—her Umatube tab is filled with scrolling cat videos—so what's another trip down memory lane to her home city?

She misses the nightly rush muffled behind her curtains in her father's second apartment. She misses strolling down Temple Street with her older cousin, flitting between trinket stalls and listening to the sizzle of street food oil amidst the night air. Most of all, she misses the Hong Kong offices, where she and her seniors would gather at the break room between hours, where they'd sip their coffees and eat their snacks, discussing everything from the goofy hairstyle of their latest client to the new kung fu flicks on at the downtown theater. The most wonderful corner shop stocked with snacks stood only a street crossing down, and the clients they bargained with were never some nouveau riche middle-aged woman who inherited her Papa's trust fund along with the entitlement to demand the world from complete strangers in her path.

She'll suffocate in that damn wedding dress, and the whole procession will cheer.

Crown sighs.

Damn it.

And to think her day started off so well. Diamond won her tryouts. Same for Kitasan. Crown had been so ready to celebrate with the two younger umas with ice-cream before her phone buzzed and buzzed and buzzed.

She notices how other umas stare at her. The jealousy. They see the family name Satono and assume life as a conglomerate daughter is smooth. Fast cars and luxurious carrot banquets. They don't comprehend the weight of an elite family's responsibility. Crown was trained in business education at the age most of her peers began struggling with high school mathematics. Designer brand clothes and sprawling mansions cost their own taxes in time and effort spent helping her father's tailoring company.

Don't get her wrong. Crown chose this life. She's proud to be a sales consultant while running in the URA. She lives for watching a deal locked and sealed. She relishes the crinkle of paper and the smell of printer ink from a fresh report filled with positive sales figures. The Satono Group gave her sufficient outs to pursue a normal racing career, and she turned down all of them. In fact, she's already secured a deal with the student council to show off a formal wear exhibit within Tracen's grounds. That's an amazing achievement for a high schooler!

But three goddesses, she'd be lying if her job wasn't exhausting. There's just enough time during the off-season months for her to relax before peak season arrives and the company's battered with potential deals left and right.

She gives the email one more stab. A single character is typed. Nope. Nope, nope, nope. This isn't working. She desperately needs a change of scenery. Not more electronic screens, but a proper stretch of her legs.

Exiting Miho is out of the question. Hishi Amazon will break her kneecaps if she does. The break room, then. She'll walk down there, brew some tea and take five or ten to unwind. She'll return by ten-thirty and spend another half-hour finishing that email. Whatever she'll write is what she'll send to her superior for review. Then she'll slam her eyes shut and try to optimize her REM sleep.

Morning training will bring another heaping of headaches, but Trainer Akiko has never taken Crown's auxiliary duties as an excuse to slack. The woman dresses as a maid and is as far from submissive as Mt. Fuji is tall.

Crown closes her laptop. She tucks it under the blankets and tiptoes onto the floor. She slides on her uniform and slips out the door.

Goosebumps creep over her exposed skin. The dorm hallways are chilly tonight, a high contrast to the warm energy earlier that day. Faint green emergency lights dot the floorboards. Crown treads carefully, her slippers making soft shuffling sounds as they hit the solid floorboards. She accelerates when she makes it to the staircase. A couple of flights of stairs downwards, a left turn and she arrives at the Miho dorm's break room.

The door creaks open. The room is deserted. No-one else is stuck up late at night dealing with their business. How fortunate for them.

Crown's gaze sweeps across the furniture. Microwaves, pantry cabinets, three sound tables with chairs. A spot where the gas stoves used to be. They were once allowed, but after a series of disastrous cooking endeavors, they were removed from both dorms. It's a pity. Crown would've loved to whip up a stir-fry.

Finally, the kettle.

Crown fills the kettle up. She grins a little at the gentle slosh of running water pouring out of the tap. She sets the kettle to boil, then rummages around in nearby cupboards. Tracen's food budget is not infinite, but its high standards for food extend towards the snacks. Crown withdraws a stock of carrot-lemon teabags with rye flavor attached. Next is a jar of honey, then a spoon from the cutlery drawer, and places both on a table before sinking down on a nearby chair for a breather.

She rolls her neck, then her shoulders. She closes her eyes. She orders herself not to fall asleep. With the laptop screen out of her vicinity, her mind is allowed to relax. It wanders and strays, conjuring up thoughts of Diamond and upcoming races and the situation back home, but at least those are either stuck in the past or in the far future and do not demand any attention now. An uma could have far worse problems to deal with. Real poverty. Lack of opportunities. Living on cup noodles her whole life. Meanwhile, Crown is struggling to write five hundred letters. A mild sense of guilt washes over her.

One thought squeezes out another.

A grain of sand from a crack in the earth. A bubble rising from a pungent bog. The foreboding rolls across Crown's psyche. It's the true reason for her unsettledness, and it's floating there, taunting her with its glistening reflection, a balloon filled with hives waiting to be popped. She can't. She blanked it out when she sat down for her nightly work, knowing that the moment she dwells on it she won't stop.

She should've brought her cards. A quick game of solitaire could've distracted her. Party games and tricks bolster the imagination—the present and the future.

A quick solitaire round would've let her mind linger elsewhere. Instead, she takes a breath. She straightens her back and tightens in her chest. Inhale, hold, exhale. Four counts for each step, four repetitions. Simple thoughts for a turbulent heart. Her nerves settle. The unsettling bubble sinks back down into its swamp.

The kettle whistles. A shrill sound.

Excellent. She can finally brew that tea. With a smile, Crown opens her eyes to a yawning darkness. The entire break room is pitch black.

She stares into the center, bewildered. Hold on. Did she open her eyes properly? A few blinks, she concludes that she must have. This is real. She leans forward in her seat, squints and manages to discern the murky outlines of the sink and the kettle rattling in its socket from her chair.

Only one conclusion. The power's out.

But that's weird. She was just marveling at how well-maintained Tracen was five minutes ago. Neither Hishi Amazon nor Fuji Kiseki are tolerant of a single stain on their respectively dorm's windows, so for them to have overlooked a fault in the power lines is…odd, putting it lightly. Was Fuchu struck by a mass blackout? Probably not. She can see the windows of the distant city blocks twinkle through the window. The electronic billboards, late-night apartment dwellers and department stores.

Wait. The mass downpour from last month. So much rain crashed down it caved in the roofs of some particularly geriatric buildings. Water damage might have persisted over the weeks and sunken into the fuse, the transformer or whatever doohickey controls the power in Tracen. It sounds mildly incorrect, but it's the best Crown's got. She is not an expert with electronics.

The kettle blares again. Crown winces at the noise. Wow, that's sharp. Guess it's only the lights that were affected. Trust her luck for her water to finish boiling now, of all times, and for the kettle to go bust, seeing it's not switching off by itself. She'll have to deal with it herself. Grunting, she stands up, pushes her chair aside, takes a step forward and catches herself.

Hang on a moment. Is she seriously going to inspect that whistling kettle in pure darkness? Isn't that dangerous?

Yes. It is. They don't teach kids to handle stoves while blindfolded.

So why isn't she waiting for the power to turn back on? She'd get a better view of the room.

Her mind stalls. Because…

A throb pulses in her forehead. She lifts a hand there, stroking the skin with her slender fingers.

Because…

The answer pops into her head. The kettle must be bust, too. If she leaves hissing and steaming, the water will all evaporate, leaving the kettle empty but the power running. The continuous heat will sear the plastic bottom of the kettle black, combusting it. A fire hazard. The break room will burn down, the entire Miho Dorm will need to be evacuated, and Hishi Amazon and Air Groove will chase after her with pitchforks and very pointed questions. The last thing the Satono Group needs is more reputation distress.

Crown has to switch that kettle off. It's not difficult. She just has to grab the handle and lift it away. She's no stranger to darkness. She's walked through Hong Kong's streets at the dead of night. She used to love wandering down the halls at night as a child, pretending she was a lone magician on a quest to strike down the terrible demon lord. She was the oldest and the boss, and she always strung along Diamond and the other Satono girls for the ride.

Crown clenches and unclenches her hand. She can do this.

She pushes back the chair further, ignoring how her neck hair bristles at how loudly the implement grinds across the enamel flooring. One step forward. Two steps forward. The walk to the kettle stretches and stretches, as the appliance puffs and hisses. The wailing fills her eardrums, a dissonant, continuous note from a steam train off its rails.

A shiver runs down her back. Sweat beaded on her forehead. Her uniform clings to her like a prisoner's garb. The room's soaking in warmth.

She moves forward. Her fingers brush against the water vapor. They burn. She's there now, right arm snaking around the back to where the handle is. The first grasp from her fingers misses. The second touch glimpses the edges, but the kettle jerks leftward before she can tighten her grip. It hisses another bout of steam that clings to her cheeks, stings her skin further, and obscures the silhouette in her already dimmed vision. Annoyance hits her. She's so close. She can't back down now. The damn appliance is moving so much for an object stored with that much water. She estimates the position of where the handle should be after its next rattle, extends her fingers for the third and final touch atop this fiery beast—

"Don't."

Crown lurches back. The lights flash back on. A sucker-punch to the eyes; Crown stumbles, then finds herself pulled straight back by a firm hand grabbing her shoulder. Her ears and tail shoot up, and she almost whirls around to shove this mysterious intruder off, only to see a jet of boiling hot water arc from the kettle's spout and splatter on the ground where she'd been standing.

Oh. Crown thinks. Oh, goddesses, she realises. She'd been standing in front of the kettle in the darkness. Her face had hovered in front of the spout. Had she kept standing there, groping for the button, that jet of water would've splattered straight into the top of her face her seared her eyes shut.

Shudders rock her frame. She clings to the fridge for support, trembling. Her voice comes out shakily.

"Thank you so much, Miss…?"

Long jet-black hair, golden eyes, and bangs so long they reach down to the base of her neck. Crown's savior. She yanks the kettle away, dumps it in the sink, then tears the base's plug straight out of the power socket.

"Manhattan Cafe. Are you all right?"

Manhattan Cafe sits Crown down. She asks questions. Are you injured? What happened? Does she have to break out the nearby first-aid kit? Her eyes peer into Crown's soul. Crown answers no, the kettle and no again in turn. Her heart won't stop hammering in her chest. Her mind replays the boiling hot water arching in the air over and over in some kind of relief-delivering horror show. A few seconds in the darkness, and her career would've ended. So much of umamusume racing relies on a contestant's vision to analyze and predict her opponents.

Stupid. Stupid, stupid, stupid. What had she been thinking?

A clink on the table. Crown snaps out of her stupor.

"I couldn't."

Manhattan Cafe presses the mug of tea forward. She brewed it while Crown sat there, shocked silent. The hot water comes from the microwave; the kettle water was dumped and drained.

"You saved me. You saved me from dropping out. This is too much—"

"You were set up to brew yourself some tea—" Manhattan Cafe's expression shifts beneath her bangs in what can only be a mild frown, "And it seems like you desperately need it. We all have our dismal moments. A good cup is a great way to wind your nerves down. Don't worry about the caffeine either. It's pure decaf."

Manhattan Cafe gives the cup a nudge. It steams gently. It's a gift. Crown takes it and drinks a sip.

A strong earthy flavor hits her tongue, akin to the fresh smell of the paddock at dawn. The droplets roll across her tongue, and she's captured back into her childhood, where the adults took her and Diamond and the other girls of the estate on camping trips. They sat her down in front of a campfire with a pot above and taught her which roots and mushrooms were good to eat and which ones would give her the mother of all tummy-aches. The days passed leisurely back then, so tranquil compared to the frenetic nature of business and the URA. She finds herself core settling.

The pleasure must show on her face. A hint of smugness latches onto Manhattan Cafe's smile.

"It's lovely, isn't it?"

"It is." Crown admits. "Dandelion?"

"Correct. Soak in the aroma. Let the duality of bitterness and the natural sweetness naturally mingle together. The drink will stimulate your bile and stabilize your blood sugar. Drink it to the last drop, and if you want more, there's plenty where it comes from." Manhattan Cafe pats a tin she pulled out of her uniform. "Everyone thinks it's silly to carry coffee ingredients on person until the need strikes."

Her tone is soft and demure, yet she sounds so proud. Crown can't help but smile back too.

"Thank you so much for saving me, senpai. If you hadn't come in time…"

"Think nothing of it. I only did what was natural." Manhattan Cafe says. "I don't think we've met before."

"No, we haven't. But I've heard of you."

"Oh?"

"We studied our Kikuka Sho back at the estate. Some of my younger cousins are in love with your action figure."

Manhattan Cafe's cheeks tinge the faintest bit of pink. "Give them my kind regards."

"I need to buy you lunch sometime."

"That's not necessary."

"You saved my career. I need to emphasise that. One second later, and goodbye to my hopes of breaking the Satono curse. That at least deserves a trip to this awesome Chinese restaurant in Fuchu's central."

"…I'll consider it."

That's how Crown and Manhattan Cafe begin chatting. It's unbelievable, especially given the circumstances, but it's happening and Crown's not complaining. They start with Manhattan Cafe's coffee blog, her quest to restock the beverage section of Tracen's cafeteria, a proposed occult club, the afternoon's tryouts—Crown brings up her little cousin with pride—and about how crazy it was for a kettle to puff that much steam. Crown suggests Hishi Amazon overlooked it. Manhattan Cafe shakes her head.

"Don't use it for a while."

"Is it getting replaced?" Crown asks.

Manhattan Cafe looks behind Crown towards the inert appliance. "It will."

Crown shrugs inside her head. Trust the coffee aficionado to be so into kitchen appliances. Crown's not one to talk, however. She's still got her baton from her tenth birthday. That tool is her ride or die for every stage performance she'll run until the whims of the universe inevitably snap it in half.

Time passes. The two girls whittle down their drinks and chat some more. Out of all the umas to stumble upon for an impromptu coffee break, Crown could do a lot worse than Manhattan Cafe. Sure, she seems mysteriously downcast from first glance. Sure, anyone who's good friends with Tracen's number one mad scientist, Agnes Tachyon, has at least a sprinkling of unhinged weirdo in her. Rumors of Manhattan Cafe gazing off into the distance or stringing along actual ghosts—whatever. Crown, in this moment, finds the girl pleasant, saving her aside.

It helps Crown doesn't have to rehearse an entire routine like she has when anticipating a walk-up to Symboli Rudolf. Manhattan Cafe is down-to-earth. Conversing with her is like talking to Duramente. Patience and perseverance help.

"Were you also taking a break?" Crown asks.

"A break from…?" Manhattan Cafe trails off.

"Work. Recreation."

That gives her pause. "You're working at this hour?"

"Business for the Satono group. I'm a sales associate for the Satono Group's tailoring enterprise."

"In high school?" Manhattan Cafe raises her eyebrows, which are barely visible beneath her fringe.

"I mean, most of us who reach the G3 level have to deal with sponsors and negotiate brand deals. It's not too different."

"We're not the ones talking to clients. That's normally our Trainers' jobs. An ocean with no end in sight, the land of finance and economics." Manhattan Cafe gently partakes in her coffee. It's a controlled movement. "You must be commended for daring to cross that space with nary a lighthouse in sight."

Crown giggles. "It's not that dramatic."

"I couldn't do it. My constitution is unfit for extended desk work unless it's at a kitchen. It must be difficult."

"I can't deny that."

"Red flags?"

"Oh, you have no idea. This client of ours has been…I'd rather not put any insults to names, but she has been fidgeting back and forth between the designs for this wedding dress she thinks will look in her head and what won't trip her over her own heels down the aisle. We had to order five different outfits for her perusal. Just when we thought we had it at her sixth, a shipment of the materials came late, and now she's put us on blast. I'm in charge of writing the apology, and it's…" Crown catches herself. She peters out and gives an awkward shrug. "It's not going great."

Manhattan Cafe hums. She taps the tabletop as she thinks. "I tend to find apologizing from the heart is best."

"I wish, but we have this protocol when it comes to writing letters." Crown says.

"Another oul exists on the other side of the screen. If I shared their perspective, I'd like at least to know that the words written are genuine. Enough obfuscation drapes over our daily lives." Manhattan Cafe says. "Tachyon and I agree on that."

"Oh no, did something happen between you?"

"Happened." Manhattan Cafe corrects. "She's capricious. I'm more morose. We clash sometimes. But we've always made up."

That's no small feat. Agnes Tachyon is said to be as prideful as she is fanatical about analyzing the umamusume body. It might not be a bad tip, then. Crown will take anything at this point.

"I couldn't do your job. My constitution wasn't meant for long desk work. That, in combination with France…a truly bad omen."

"But late-night coffee isn't a problem?" Crown teases.

"Only because my friend demanded we go for a late-night walk. She's a picky soul."

Manhattan Cafe flinches. She rubs a spot on her head, shooting a dissatisfied look towards thin air on her right. Oh, Crown realises. This is that famous imaginary friend of hers. The ghost of Tracen, who is with one hundred percent certainty not real and most likely a coping mechanism of sorts. Whatever motivates her to win those G1s, Crown supposes. It'd also be hypocritical of her to sneer, given her own fondness for stage magic.

Then again, with stage magic, the audience plays into the act. They know magic isn't real. It's the execution of the illusion by the performer that keeps the audience on their toes.

"You know, Cafe…"

"Yes?"

Crown smiles. "You'd look great in a designer suit."

"You mean my racewear?" Manhattan Cafe asks.

"That too, but also in general. I'm talking about the fits stitched in the best ateliers in Hong Kong. Suits that come with luxury cravats, lapels and other high-class accessories. You've got the sophistication of an A-lister movie star."

"You think so?"

"I also think you'd kill in an evening dress, too."

Manhattan Cafe tilts her head. It's not an observation she's accustomed to hearing. She sinks into thought as Crown's mind fills of the girl before clad in the various luxury outfits from the Satono Group's new catalogue. Yep. She's not wrong. The girl seated before her moves with a languid elegance, apparent in her footage. She just has to stand up straighter and tuck in her stomach, and she'd blaze a trail down the red carpet.

"I heard through the grapevine your family is putting on a fashion exhibition at Tracen." Manhattan Cafe states.

It's Crown's turn to look surprised. "How did you know about that?"

"I know Jungle Pocket, who knows Fuji, who's already signed up to apply…" Manhattan Cafe pauses. "Sorry, was I not meant to investigate?"

"No, no, it's already been announced on socmed. But it's in the early stages, and it's gotten drowned out by the tryouts. And the rain. It's not happening for at least a month." Crown replies. "I didn't expect anyone to know about it."

Manhattan Cafe drifts her gaze to the side. She mouths a few words, nods twice and twists her lips. It's a serious commitment to the imaginary friend act.

"Can I join?"

"The fashion show? You want tickets? It's free for Tracen students."

Manhattan Cafe shakes her head. "I wish to a halt."

Crown blinks. Her brain grinds to a halt, then restarts with a jolt. "Wait, you mean—"

"I want to model. You said I'd look decent after all. Is that allowed?"

"No. I mean yes. I mean, yes, yes, definitely!" Crown splutters out. "I'll have to clear some things up with my boss, but you're an established champion already. It shouldn't be a problem!"

There must be sparkles twinkling in her eyes. Ladylike restraint prevents her from rubbing her hands in glee. To recruit the Manhattan Cafe for a Satono Group event—is she dreaming?

"Hold on." Manhattan Cafe raises her palm. "I have a single request."

"What is it?"

Manhattan Cafe fixes her with a serious look. "Don't go out at night."

"I…wasn't intending to?" After tonight, Crown is giving the new kettle a wide, wide berth.

"It's not safe."

"That sounds extreme."

"Did you hear about the girl who stepped on the rusty switchblade?"

Crown shivers. The answer is yes. The whole academy had. The poor soul still lives in the hospital—an almost career-ruining setback. It's an eerie reminder of her own close shave.

"That's why," Manhattan Cafe says.

Crown startles. "Are there saboteurs out on the grounds?"

"In a sense, yes."

"Oh no!" Crown exclaims. "Is the Director doing anything about it?"

Manhattan Cafe pauses. "The right people are taking care of it."

Vague and mysterious, and not how Crown enjoys it. She nods regardless. Any trace of good humor has vanished from Manhattan Cafe's demeanor. She's not messing around.

"Okay. I won't," Crown replies.

It's a small price to pay for securing Manhattan Cafe's assistance.

"That should be—" Manhattan Cafe jerks her head to the side. Her ears twitch. She mouths in silence some more, and this time Crown lip-reads the words Are you sure? As the black-haired uma's eyes widen a fraction.

"What's up?"

"Sorry. One more thing." Manhattan Cafe says, turning her head back. "My friend wants to tell you something."

"And that is…?"

Hesitation. Longer and heavier than before. "You should patch up any broken relationships with former friends before their foundations sour further and rot forever."

"Excuse me?"

"My friend says life is fleeting. Life is relentless. Life can be cruel. The end of the stories between ourselves and our friends and family can strike at a moment's notice. She had a friend in America. The kindest, sweetest uma, yet a fierce rival with whom they clashed and pushed each other to the greatest of heights. But fate was not kind to my friend. She had to depart before she could say a proper goodbye, and now the clock has turned and they will never meet again."

The story ends solemnly. Manhattan Cafe looks into her own mug for a moment.

"She's not without reason. I've seen it happen to the younger souls. It's never pleasant to imagine the what-ifs, the what-could-have-beens." Manhattan Cafe adds.

Crown sits there, a loss for words.

This is becoming too personal. She'd feel offended if Manhattan Cafe didn't look so grave. Does she have associates inside the Satonos? Surely not, otherwise Crown would've heard about it by now. Then, who on earth in Crown's life fits that imaginary friend's bill? She sifts through her internal photo album: her parents, Diamond, Diamond's parents, Akiko, Grandmother, her colleagues and friends back in Hong Kong, Kitasan Black, even Duramente. No-one in her current life has a relationship so fragmented it could break. However, if she reaches into the past, extending her hand back to her childhood, then there's—

She clamps down on that thought before it forms. Forbidden. That name is forbidden.

"I'll keep it in mind."

A prickle on the side of her left cheeks. It feels like someone is staring at her. No-one's present; it's just the two of them in the room. And yet, the colors of the fridge and the sink behind that portion of air shimmers. Crown blinks spots out of her eyes. Wow. She is growing tired. How much time has passed…twenty whole minutes?

She downs the rest of the dregs dandelion coffee in a single gulp. "Thanks for the chat, senpai. I should be getting back to bed."

Manhattan Cafe stands up. "I'll walk you back."

The words fly off Crown's fingertips. She raps at the keys so swiftly they sound off in droves. It's possible Duramente will hear this rattling, wake up and start a row, but Crown couldn't care less. Manhattan Cafe's advice sharpened her inspiration and dumped a heaping of gasoline on top. Crown's on fire. Like, duh. Obviously, she needs to write her apology using the client's perspective. Why hadn't she thought of that thirty minutes ago? The tryouts, her brain answers. Kitasan Black, Grandmother, and—Crown cuts the thoughts off again.

The delay has caused you great distress and concern for what is undeniably the most important day of your life, and we deeply regret to have failed to meet your expectations…

She runs the grammar and spelling checking program, rapidly clicks through the corrections, and finally, finally attaches it to an email straight to her boss.

Done.

She breathes in.

Done and dusted.

Crown saves the final draft twice. She slaps her laptop's lid down, shoves it to the side and plops her head onto the pillow, slamming her eyelids shut before the fabric hits her hair. She doesn't want to see that damn machine for another twenty-four hours. It won't happen, since she needs to use it for her accounting class tomorrow, but a girl can dream.

Flush with success, she pulls the blankets further up over her and presses her back against the soft mattress.

No more electronic humming. No more burning her retinas. The only sounds she can hear are the quiet rising and falling of Duramente's chest. Peace and quiet, how Crown has missed thee.

She settles in a rhythm. Counting numbers down. Basking the triumph of finishing that email at long last, the fresh aftertaste of the dandelion coffee lingering on her tongue. She reviews her day. Breakfast. Tryouts. Watching Diamond win with great relief. Watching Kitasan Black win by a single nose, feeling even more relief and then immediately getting battered in the head with dread, because of you.

It's you again.

Satono Ruby.

You're the thought-worm squirming and wriggling at the back of Crown's head. You are the bleeding wound that shall not clot. A proper lady of the Satono household must not seethe and glare in public; Crown and Diamond have been taught a number of techniques to conceal their intrusive thoughts, to let them linger at the back before they dissipate for a time. Even now, Crown pushes back, as she has done multiple times tonight. She hopes sleep will claim her. It doesn't. There's nothing to distract her, and so your image retakes its throne at the forefront of her mind.

She hears the peals of the commentary caster's enthusiastic cheer. She sees the haze imprint of your bow towards your mentor in the audience. The smile you gave off towards Kitasan, so bright, so pure with happiness and respect—so distasteful. It is utterly out of place for an omen of disaster, of which you truly are.

It was supposed to a good day for the Satonos. A new beginning. An exhibition from their heiress and her best friend and you ruined that.

What media coverage that paid attention to the tryouts has conveniently slipped you by the wayside. Journalists who have covered your performance imply it's a fluke. They wonder what black magic you summoned to cheat your way towards beating the best rookie of the year. Fans of the Satono group are buying into that narrative, calling for an investigation, an expulsion. Crown knows the Director will not budge. Nor will Symboli Rudolf. They understand fairness. They know hard work paid off when they see it.

The same goes for Crown, and Trainer Akiko, and Grandmother.

Grandmother was livid, when Crown called after the tryouts. Every word, the strike of a poison-soaked dagger, and it wasn't even aimed in Crown's direction. Denial is fruitless. You are competition. A contestant who will find her Trainer and most likely win her maiden race. You are a future threat to Diamond and Kitasan on their runs across the Twinkle Series. A universe exists where you seize the title of first G1 from Diamond in yours and hers first year and the thought horrifies Crown beyond a doubt.

Noxious enmity floods her. How dare you, she thinks. Everything was going so well. The tryouts were meant to be swept by Kitasan, close friend and associate of the Satono Group. Then you showed up and ruined the entire script. How dare you poison the winds of her family's fortune?

This is your mother's doing, she thinks. The interloper. The false champion. The bitch that gave hope and tore it down for no reason whatsoever. Did you know employees of the Satono conglomerate dare not mention her name, for fear of being accused of sympathy? That mothers within the family estate teach her a nightmare to frighten their children. And are you so naïve as to think the Satonos and those two poor competitors were the only ones she hurt?

Set aside the fact that your mother's actions prevented the Satonos from rising to the same echelons as the Symbolis and the Mejiros—their rightful place, for your information. Look further.

The government investigated the URA once that disastrous Tenno Sho passed. They questioned the security measures, the legality and moral ethics of umamusume racing as a whole. Two healthy umas had their lives shattered to pieces by your mother's work. Should the public just rollover and accept these risks because those souls were a minority?

No, the public said. And it showed. Trust in the URA waned. Attendance at racecourses diminished. Sponsors withdrew themselves from other aspiring stars, as stocks fell and droves of employees from racing-adjacent industries were let go. Even Tracen's enrollment for the year stalled. The sabotage conducted by your mother knocked down lines of dominos that hurt the lives of tens, if not hundreds, of thousands. Divorces. Drunken ex-salarymen at late-night bars. Mountains of tickets abandoned in the trash.

And who took the brunt of this blame from racers, fans and onlookers alike? Why, the Satono Group for birthing your mother in the first place, of course! If it weren't for the immediate following generation, of Symboli Rudolf, Mejiro Ramonu, Mr. C.B. and the rest, Japanese umamusume racing might have suffered an irrecoverable wound.

At least your mother conducted one good deed. She saw how much society despised her, took the hint and vanished into the darkness. You, however, possess the audacity to seek her mantle. To grant the Satonos an ever-present target for the world to mock and sneer at. Don't deny it. You stole her shoes, for goddesses' sake!

Okay, you missed her a lot. So much your heart threatened to break. Crown can understand that. But they're just shoes. Tracen could fund you another pair. Do you really want to tie yourself to someone so destructive and horrid?

You could have stayed at the shrine. You could have been reintroduced as a servant. Crown and Diamond would've loved to have you back.

Well, so much for that!

But it's fine.

You hear that? It's fine.

The Satono Group failed in blocking you from Tracen. They kicked and screamed and couldn't convince the Director, so they'll commit to the rational move and adapt. They'll just beat you fair and square on turf by way of Diamond, Kitasan, Akiko and, last but not least, Crown.

It doesn't matter that you and her once lived under the same roof; that Crown used to sneak pineapple tarts from the pantry to feed you and Diamond, or that she caught you from always burning yourself on the campfire; or that in the hazy early minutes of post-slumber she still remembers throwing a massive tantrum—running across the mansion, pestering every maid and butler, desperately trying to figure out where the adults had abducted you—and still feels traces of guilt.

That time has withered and frayed. Satono Crown has grown up. She...

The enmity cools. A more languid emotion settles in. Facing the wall, deep in the darkness, the echo of a child's laughter muffled as her ear presses against the pillow. Manhattan Cafe's words float back. They embed themselves into the bedrock and take root.

Crown...

She feels pity for you. Yes, that's what it is. For your poverty, your starvation of opportunities. Not sympathy. Just pity, like praying for the sake of a lost, flea-infested puppy.

It's unknown how much a mother's blood transfers onto her child's personality. That woman never contacted you once before she left, so Crown supposes it's possible you are unblemished by your mother's twisted psyche. She'll never say this out loud, of course. And she cannot cling to mere chances. Her family is at the cusp of developing some significant breakthroughs. They'll contribute to the Satono Group's grand philanthropic dreams. They'll set everyone up to reach the position they deserved so many years ago. To pave the path forward, she must adhere to her duties and put the entire Satono Group, its countless employees and associates, ahead of your hopes and dreams.

Her resolve solidifies. You are the enemy. Crown will fight to rid Tracen of you, as long as she remains the diligent, familial daughter of the Satonos.

How comfortable that sounds.

[Satono Crown's Insight has increased by 1.]

>>[DutyCalls] Yes. You don't want to be the type of person who'd run from this.

"I'll do it."

Plain Jane's ears perk up. Her head remains rested on the chair's backrest, as if she hadn't heard anything at all. Around her, the air of the paddock hangs still, the clouds.

You clench your fists as if you could grip the air and haul it away. "I won't lie, Senpai. This talk of souls and a nightmare world full of monsters and traps and magic on top of that—it's overwhelming. It's scary. I don't think I've ever felt more terrified than when those shadow umas chased and hunted me down. And it's off the back of the most ping-pong day of my life, which has also felt super long, too, like an entire month! Part of me wants to accept the offer to give up. But…"

"But?" Plain Jane prompts.

"You said that these 'Horrors' will keep harming Tracen's girls. That they'll find worse and worse ways to destroy their souls of everyone here. And if the Director or the government can't do anything about it…" You gulp. Speaking this feels like treading the edge before a vast, vast pit, but you've already brought yourself this far. No backing down now. "Then I'll do it in their place. I'll fight the Nightmare as…I don't know what the term is, but I'll do it."

Plain Jane looks at you, silent. You pump your fists again and stand up, eyes focused, shoulders square.

"It will be difficult." Plain Jane says.

"I beat those Horrors. I can do it again." You reply.

"Very, very difficult." Plain Jane adds.

"Pandora Box's opened." You counter. "If I gave up knowing that I ran away from this, I'd never be able to look myself in the mirror again."

Plain Jane still doesn't relent. She angles her hand, lazily flipping it upside down with the roll of her wrist. She opens her fingers, revealing a cluster of swirling lights around. Your attention is hooked, the faint whine of television static whistling from the core of the lights.

"I can wipe your memories, should you choose to reject my proposal. No more knowledge of magic. No more fighting Horrors. No more communication with me."

In other words, you will be free.

Your mind spins. A conqueror of that horrid stadium you may be, but repeat that a dozen, a hundred times? Constantly rolling in the mud, conjuring real flames and tearing apart shadow flesh, before heading back down to normal reality and pretending you're hyped for races like the rest of your peers? Now, that's chilling.

You are tempted to take the offer. The safe option. The coward's option. Putrid after your last sentence—but only for a few seconds.

You shake your head.

"It probably won't work. You said I've got a natural affinity to detect souls. I'd end up stumbling across the Nightmare again, and then we'd have to begin talking all over again. My life was never like the other girls, anyway." You say, and flash a half-grin. "And it wouldn't be a normal life, even if I was. The Nightmare would keep existing. It'd wreak havoc, and my new self wouldn't have any idea why."

You then clutch a hand to your chest. "And I've made friends."

You think of them. Meisho Tabaru, Grass Wonder, Aston Machan, Matikanefukukitaru, Special Week and more. The thought of them in the position you were in, without magic clothes—intolerable.

"I don't want them to be hurt."

Plain Jane presses on. "Most of them are not supernaturally attuned. They won't ever know what you've done for them."

"And that's okay with me, Senpai! I don't want to help them for a reward. I'll do it because I think it's the right thing to do." You say. "So, please help me. I'll do my best to fight off this evil Nightmare!"

You belt out the last lines, summoning power from your lungs, as if this is the stage and you're reaching the finale. You let your words ring out and float over the vast fields of grass. There. You've said it. You told the first girl to treat you well at Tracen your resolve. The coward in you waits for the pin to drop again, for the tremors to wrack across your frame and for the protests to squeak out. But it doesn't happen. You're frightened and astonished and a little excited and, most of all, you meant what you said.

Tracen is a place for all umamusume to run freely to their heart's content. They don't need a second alternate world full of evil barging in and ruining their souls because of their twisted games. Not your bullies, not Diamond nor Crown. No-one.

Plain Jane stares you dead in the eye. You stare back. At the back of your neck, you begin to sweat.

There's a perfection to your esteemed senpai's face. The type of girl who's overlooked in a movie before the big reveal occurs and it shows that she was the prettiest all along. Clusters of freckles that aren't too scattered. Hair that is neatly groomed with not a single tangled strand. Almond-shaped eyes with open schlera. A vision of calm, collected prestige, upon which expressionlessness is hung.

It's almost uncanny. Definitely eerie when she's not smiling amicably. You wonder if this is how ghosts are in general.

Then, Plain Jane lowers her head. There's a pressing of her lips, a tightening of her jaw. She runs her arm across her face as a muffled sound close to a sniffle pours out.

"You truly have a noble soul, Ruby," Plain Jane says. "I am so fortunate to have met you. Tracen is so fortunate to have enrolled you. Thank you so much."

You nod, feeling both a weight lift your shoulders and a new one fall in. The final test from Plain Jane, and you've passed. That's it then. Your life has irrevocably charted course to fighting off the Nightmare for the sake of those who cannot perceive it.

There's no going back.

Plain Jane guides you to her lake. This is the portal where she enters Tracen for a visit. It is also a source of a refreshing drink, which you confirm when you scoop water from within and taste. The Soul Form can wield all major senses, including that of taste. Since it's detached from the main body, it won't have any nutritional effects, though special foods like Plain Jane's water can repair the Soul Form from any immediate danger, she explains.

She then teaches you magic. You have a natural talent for a technique she calls Invocation, the ability to conjure and summon energy.

"Whoa!" You gasp at the newborn flame smouldering between your palms. "This is just like…"

"Like?"

An anime. You think. "A…light novel?" You reply.

Plain Jane gives you a milder version of her previous disapproving look. "I suppose we'll make a proper bookworm out of you someday."

"It's not my fault books are so boring! This is the twenty-first century, Senpai! Umatok and Umastagram exist!" You protest.

"Goodness, the literacy rate of your generation. The President should honestly do more about it…" Plain Jane mutters. She then points downwards. "Also, your regalia is on fire."

"Huh?" You look down at the sleeve, which is red and also greying and blackening from a lick of fire that detached from your palm. "Oh no!"

In hindsight, you could have just stuck your sleeve into the water instead of jumping straight in.

Plain Jane hands you a towel she produced out of thin air, chuckling. She teaches you a second Discipline called Replenishment, which you wield to collect soul energy from the surrounding grass. It coalesces into a green, almost-gooey substance and tingles pleasantly against your skin. It'll be able to heal any wounds on both Soul Form and your regular body. At your current level, it's not much. You'll get better through experience the more you exercise it, like any other skill.
