Plain Jane leaves the lesson there. More of a crash course, honestly. She then sits beside you for a rest, during which she plucks fresh dandelions off the ground and pops them straight into her mouth. You follow. They're surprisingly tasty once you get past the traces of dirt.

"How was your talk with Agnes Digital today?"

"You know about that?"

Plain Jane smiles. "I do enjoy a good stroll across Tracen's grounds. It so happened that after rescuing you from those Horrors, I lingered at the back of the academy for some fresh air and overheard a girl saying Miss Digital had muttered your name rapidly after your tryouts race. She's not the stealthiest uma, given the number of times myself and others have found her engaging in impromptu self-roleplay in the school cafeteria."

You pull a face.

"It didn't go well?"

"Not badly, but I kinda get where her reputation comes from…"

You inform Plain Jane about your meeting with the infamous uma-obsessed girl, including what happened after you agreed. Digital reared up, hands outstretched for what might've been a hug, before collecting herself and settling for muttering about how awesome you were and how this plan of Rudolf's was amazing with what might've been a trickle of drool leaking out of the side of her mouth. She then whipped out her phone for the two of you to exchange numbers.

"You seem conflicted." Plain Jane comments.

"Yeah, I am." You say. "On one hand, I'm glad she doesn't hate me, and she does have a point in how my reputation totally sucks. She's also part of Rudolf's new mentorship program."

"Clever move, that one," Plain Jane remarks. "Many aspiring racers don't fully understand the necessity of good PR until a controversy whacks them in the face."

"Rudolf sent me Grass, and she saved me from complete failure on the track. So logically, I should trust her and get on board with what Digital wants. On the other hand, did she have to say all those things about my mother?"

"It's much like Digital to be upfront. Passionate, obsessive, fanatical—but rarely ever not honest about her feelings." Plain Jane says. "At least she gave you the courtesy of that."

"Yeah, it'd be super awkward if I got all buddy-buddy and then realised she was hating my mom behind my back." You say. "She said she wouldn't bring the topic up unless she needed to during our projects."

"That's good of her."

You let out a sigh. "Wouldn't be the first time I've worked with someone like this. There were others in the underground. Other idols, staff members—those guys at least saw me as me, not Opal's daughter. I'll cope."

Even so, hearing another blip of vitriol towards your mother—it always stings. You won't deny that what your mother did was very wrong. Nor are you super thrilled about vanishing into thin air. It's simply that you sometimes wonder why society finds so much pleasure in bringing up the same sins over and over. A hundred more articles about that disastrous Tenno Sho won't turn back the clock and undo the injuries of Cotton Sphere and Semi Sonic. You've heard of corrupt politicians who were treated more nicely by the press than your mother.

Plain Jane reaches out and squeezes you on the shoulder.

"Agnes Digital is a sweet girl." Plain Jane says. "I've been around the block for a very long time. Few others, past and present, are more committed than she is when it comes to uplifting their fellow uma. She is no fool, either. Her mind is keen and diligent. I'd say you're in good hands."

"Can she beat the Satonos?"

"They don't dominate the press."

"But, I heard they have lots of connections.

"That is true, yet you underestimate the number of connections Digital herself has. You'll have to hear about those from their end; Digital still thinks of herself as undeserving, even after all those championships. She's not as bad as she used to be, though."

That's reassuring to hear. If you can't trust Tracen's friendly neighbourhood ghost senpai, who speaks as if she knows the famous champions of Tracen like a teacher surveying her graduates, then who else can you to?

You think for a moment and

Maybe you can make friends with Digital for real. No friendships are born within a day. That speech of hers was a slightly awkward way of breaking the ice. Remember how scary Grass Wonder seemed on your first meeting?

NameLevelDescriptionEffectsAgnes Digital1A super versatile uma-otaku and the heroine who has conquered a wide variety of battlefields! She's teaching you PR skills as part of Tracen's new student mentorship program.Will appear in encounters.

"How long is 'around the block' anyway?" You ask.

Plain Jane hums as you think. "I remember when Saint Lite was a cocky young hotshot, boasting how she'd claim all three crowns with ease."

"Oh God, that is old. No wonder you hate smartphones."

"I do not hate smartphones. I merely prefer paperback books and detest how said smartphones have rotted the brains of you youths. Ask Haiseiko. She was Oguri Cap before Oguri Cap was born. And before her was Kurifuji! Such a tragically beautiful love story that girl shared with her Trainer." Plain Jane then winks, a wry smile growing. "But those are stories I'll reserve for another time."

"What? No fair!" You whine. "You can't leave me hanging! You were around when the Prez was my age and super competitive and stuff. Tell me stories about that!"

"A young lady such as yourself deserves her proper rest. Especially after winning a bout against the Nightmare."

Oh, that's right. Plain Jane summoned you here in the middle of your slumber, which would put this anywhere from the dead of night to an hour before dawn. You can't waste any more sleep. Once dawn slips out from behind the horizon, there's morning exercises to complete, classes to attend, a Trainer to find…your schedule is packed.

Plain Jane stands up. You copy her, and then follow her over to the open classroom.

"Thanks to your efforts, the Nightmare has stalled somewhat. It is far, far from ceasing its influencing, but by suppressing a group of its Horrors, you have forced it to regenerate. It will be unable to lure students in via Soul Form or open fractures to its depths as traps. The worst it can do is spread additional misfortune and create accidents."

"That's still not great." You say.

"It's not ideal, but physical or mental damage is far preferable to soul damage. The Director is more than willing to fly injured students via her private helicopter to the best umamusume hospitals in the nation, if need be," Plain Jane says. "Use this break to rest up, study, find your Trainer, and so on. I will not be telling you how to use your time outside of anything directly fighting the Nightmare."

"I appreciate that."

"Once the Nightmare shifts again, I'll contact you. We'll figure things out then." Plain Jane says.

She pats you on the chest. A tug on your core. A fishhook in your existence. The wire begins reeling back, pulling your Soul Form back to your body. Your translucent self fades in and out, yet there's no panic. This is a natural reaction, as smooth and natural as climbing out of your bed in the morning. A gentle languidness washes over you, and you smile dozily.

A thought then strikes. "Wait!"

"What is it?"

"Will I see you at school?"

"I dare say we'll be running into each other at unexpected places and times." Plain Jane says. "Try not to stare too hard. Your classmates might think you strange."

As if they don't already, if they're not ignoring you outright.

"And you'll tell me everything about the Nightmare?" You correct yourself in haste. "Everything that you know, I mean."

"Yes. Yes I will. It won't be all at once, because I don't want your poor brain to explode. But I will tell you as much as I know."

You laugh and understand. Rookies in the idol business aren't taught the ins and outs of how management works. That's knowledge they pick up over their careers. If they're smart, they'll take the initiative to figure out it works by themselves.

Now that you think about it, taking a peek inside Tracen's library might prove fruitful.

Your Soul Form shimmers in and out. Sleepiness latches harder onto your mind.

"I'm going now, Senpai. Thanks for everything! And please keep on supporting me!"

"The pleasure is all mine. Have a good rest, you hear?"

As slumber latches on and drags you back to reality, a sense of uncertainty strikes you. It asks if you should feel happy, sad or angry, and you find that you're either none of them or all three. But, as Plain Jane waves her hand in farewell, pure gratitude shining in her eyes, you decide that your decision was at the very least not wrong.

>>END OF ENCOUNTER.

[Mood has reverted to Normal.]

"Literal translations of an ancient language or rooted in unusual brain patterns? What's in Uma's Name—a documentary on the etymology of umamusume names, coming soon to theatres near you!"

"Tokyo police have raided an Ikebukuro underground poker den and seized custom equipment, cash and chips, as well as several servers running an illegal umamusume-racing gambling website. The den, reputed to be yakuza-run, was unfortunately deserted upon forceful entry, but the police are already hard at work investigating the traces left behind. It is suspected the den was run by the notorious Suetomi family…

"Tazuna Hayakawa, chief secretary at the prestigious Tracen Academy, has pledged to provide half her salary this year to support medical funding and infrastructure related to umamusume racing. Critics of the sport have questioned why these funds were not directed to less supported endeavours, such as domestic violence…"

"Spokespeople Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism has petitioned for the installation of anti-flooding mechanisms across all towns and villages across Japan. The initiative shall be put up for a vote the following morning…"

"The Aiguille fashion brand, subsidiary of the prestigious Mejiro conglomerate, has announced a new line of formal evening wear inspired and contributed to by the Crown Jewel—Mejiro Ramonu—herself. The announcement is set to spark an all-out fashion war…"

"Man, I hope this doesn't take too long. I have to finish my training for the Kikka Sho…eh? A fracture? The hospital? No way, no way, no way, no way—wait, what's that ggyyyAAAAAHAHHHHHH!"

>>END OF ACT 1.

[THE NIGHTMARE HAS PROGRESSED.]

Intensity: ACT 1 -> ACT 2

Active Effects:

Horrors will invade Tracen's grounds late at night. Fractures to the Nightmare's depths will open. More traps akin to the rusty switchblade will spread. Innocents will be lured into the Nightmare via Soul Form at night. ??? Passive Effects:

More misfortune will spread across Tracen. More accidents will happen across Tracen. ??? Current State: Lulled (for a short time…)

4.0: Shibuya Sunday

Morning, June 7th, 20XX

[World Resonance check: 100/85 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

Magnetism radiates from the bronze statue.

"I get you. No, I totally do. It must be tough standing here every day. In the sun, in the rain, tourist season with the cameras…really tough."

There's no nudge. Your phone doesn't detach from your hand.

"The scenery's nice here, though. A nice, sunny spot."

Nor are your fingers torn apart in a bloody mess, like in that one spy movie with the teenage uma and the giant MRI machine Miki insisted was good for a year straight. You weren't expecting it here. The statue does not radiate physical magnetism. The attraction was directed to you, not the metal on your person, and it resonated deeper, thicker, closer in nature from an intrusive thought beamed from some high-off conspiracy antenna. Come, it said, and you went, past the waves of bustling pedestrians, the line at the burger cart, and a cheery sign warning kids to look twice before crossing the road.

You're here. Statues don't hold conversations. They stand there in silence. You talk to it anyway.

The obvious notion isn't at the back of your head; it's at the forefront, and it's begging you to understand how stupid you must seem. The city's busy on the weekend, sure, but a single stray camera from a heckler and Umatok will be plastered with clips of SATONO RUBY IS A LOBOTOMITE AS WELL AS A CHEATER???

Bad. Very bad. This isn't the underground, where no-recording signs popped up like mushrooms in the arenas and gachikoi enforced the rules with mob rule alone. You received enough hate comments on that one hot clip showing off your tryouts race's finish. Turns out almost beating the number one favorite isn't enough to quell an online mob.

You chew your lip. Not too much—you don't want to ruin the balm. You shoot a quick glance over your shoulder: a warm midsummer city day, the sky speckled with white clouds. Asphalt, trees, dirt. The usual weekend crowd wanders in the square outside the train station: tourists holding fat crepes, a group of four older girls hoisting band equipment on their backs, a harried intern in a suit stumbling with half a dozen full coffees. A schoolboy takes a photo of his old superhero figure, some handsome masked guy wearing a red scarf. None of these folks have so much as shot a glance at Satono Ruby, daughter of the worst umamusume to ever run in the URA. They don't care what she says, or why she's here. Yet, there's two-seven hundred degrees worth of reality out of sight, out of mind.

What if? The question echoes. What, where, why if?

[Composure check: 70/40 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

They don't care. Therefore, neither should you. Back to talking.

"That's the life of a public figure. We gotta do what we gotta do to bring smiles. All the more reason to give it our best." You face the statue again, brush a hand across its bronze leg and rub away a speck of dirt. "I used to be an umadol. I know."

High up: an advertisement billboard. The scene shifts into a hot and fiery advertisement about sports equipment. Sneakers by a company that's just hopped onto the market, and also a subsidiary of the Satono Conglomerate. A prickle on your ears—the same, minute yet consistently uncomfortable itch whenever you hear of your estranged family's businesses. But beneath that, the statue pulses. The magnetism flares, sending off waves that coalesce into the sound of a dog's bark. It sounds like satisfied. Affirmation.

"A friend told me that audiences place symbols on us entertainers. Their own identities. That friend, she's an aspiring actress and a voice actor for doujin games, says we should lean into it, giving the audience what they want but also putting our own spin on it. Like, some round pegs don't fit into square holes, but we can always sand those pegs and find better holes for them to slot in?"

The bark reasserts itself, more questioningly.

"Anyway, this might be a weird question, but can you drink rainwater with that mouth of yours?"

[(World Resonance check: 100/150 || Insight check: 10/12) -> Failure.]

The dog statue falls silent.

You tap it on the side of the ear. Nope. It's not responding. That line of yours was a failure. You have offended the puppy. You silly girl. Oh, you silly girl, how could you? Your hands fly to your head, and a shiver runs through your shoulders. Only the fear of public humiliation prevents you from crying out loud.

A thought suddenly occurs to you: the first round of barks was purely your imagination. Stupid. Then, the a second thought: the barks were real as part of a sequence you failed to understand at the outset, which means you've been blabbering by yourself, anyway. Stupid-er.

Aaaaah—

Can you swear now? Are you allowed to? You're not an umadol anymore. You have agency. Or will Air Groove write you up for saying a word Kaede told you to forget about? You decide your shoulders shall slump as compensation. Maybe not the best idea, since you're wearing your nice outfit today, but the fabric should withstand it.

You uncork your water bottle, a portable one in your handbag, and take a sip of lukewarm freshness. The day has barely started, yet you're already in tumult. It's all because of your childhood…ability.

Framing it with that term sounds weird, like an entry in your growing umamusume racing arsenal.. But 'competency' sounded too long, 'power' was too extreme, and the other terms were copyrighted by the creators of certain anime and manga, so 'ability' it was.

A metal detector, a security radar, a second nervous system, compressed somewhere that isn't your flesh or mind. That which lets you detect the presence of souls.

Once Plain Jane broke this ability down for you, it was as if blinders tore from your eyes. Souls are now everywhere. Their 'radiation' is everywhere. The fern in the school cafeteria whistles and quivers its leaves in greeting whenever you sit down near it. A starry-eyed uma shone with Christmas-tree sparkles as she ran after that Mayano girl. A second layer of water vapor gushes off the Three Goddesses' water fountain in the main courtyard, the moisture tending to your tired skin after a run. You once brushed past a girl leaving the school library, and when it came your turn to head back, you noticed a long, dark trail on the ground, like a giant calligraphy brush had gone haywire, and the ink, for a lack of a better word, smelled faintly of roast coffee beans.

Ominous. And gone the next day. The same afternoon, you encountered Rudolf scolding some girl for bringing in a form of unmentioned contraband. The pressure the Prez emanated almost pinned your feet to the ground, hammer and nails constructed from thin air, and you only caught a glimpse of her from behind two other umas.

Rudolf didn't notice. Nor did her victim. You did, and you fought to keep your face still as the crowd dispersed. That was only from the last two days. The amount of examples you've caught in Tracen alone could fill an entire chapter of your literature textbooks.

The subconscious is now the conscious; fantasy encroaches upon reality. You think you remember English lyrics along those lines in Suzuki's vintage song collection. There was a bit about a new color, too.

That's why you're chatting up this old statue. It's experimentation. Preparation for when that awful Nightmare strikes again. You promised Plain Jane you'd give it your best shot, and that means seizing the initiative. She won't let you delve into the Nightmare yourself, so investigating your childhood ability is the next best subject. There's probably no harm. The soul's radiation doesn't physically affect anything in baseline reality, no matter how hard the adrenaline surges through the umas scrapping for the lead. They're nothing more than magical holograms, for now.

You pat the dog statue's head. Now, how to get this good boy to resonate with you again? The radiation of sapient and sentient souls leaks out in periods of intense emotion. At Tracen, that's midway through a race. What's the equivalent for an entity that neither talks nor moves? What emotions are born without a brain? Do you need to ask the dog more questions? Organize a campaign to prevent birds from pooping on its metallic hide? Crush it with a hydraulic press inside the Nightmare to force it to a breaking point, like your trusty silver bullet moments from being stolen by a Horror?

On second thoughts, the last one might get you arrested. The reason: damage and being super-duper awful to national property. Change of gears. The Tracen stump instead. The less said about that…thing, the better.

[Instinct check: 40/50 -> Failure.]

"Geez, never took you for a Hachi fan."

A cheery voice from behind. The accompanying presence, a mix of a songbird's chirp and the sting of salt staining a microphone's grip. Your tail goes rigid. Then you smile. You break into a wide, wide smile and spin around, tail swishing with delight.

"Morning, Ruby."

"Kaede!"

Because the dog statue is Hachiko, and Hachiko belongs to Shibuya. If there's any reason to return here, it's to meet with a few specific important people to you. Kaede Mitsuyama, de facto leader of Tomorrow is FAITHFUL, fits the bill.

"I missed you!"

Kaede laughs and rubs you on the shoulder. You leaped into her arms for a hug. She spread them out half-way in anticipation. "We spoke three days ago."

Your tail swishes back and forth. It catches on a nearby branch, courtesy of the greenery planted around Hachiko, and you couldn't care less. "But that was on LANE. Voice calls don't count. It's been ages since that final concert. It's so awesome to finally hang out with you again!"

"Are you sure?" Kaede taps the sides of her cheeks, her grin widening. "It sounded like you were having a date with good old Hachi over there."

You respond in an instant. "Nope."

"Nope? You don't want to make more conversation with the puppy? You want to spend a day with some boring maid cafe attendant than the goodest little boy in all of Tokyo."

You pull out of the hug, then make a firm X-shape with your hands. "Nope, nope, nope! I was just admiring how well Hachiko was sculpted. I took an art class, and now my inspiration for statues has magnified tenfold. It's a mental infection. Only you can save me!"

Kaede shoves a hand over her mouth and chortles through her fingers. A melodic, sunny sound. You break the cross and giggle too. It's so wonderful to see your friend again.

"Train take long?"

"Nah. The line was fine. Only took forty or so minutes. I forgot how stacked the malls at the center are, though. So much stuff on display, I had to drag myself away before the plushies trapped me in their web."

"Oh yeah, you have actual pocket money now."

"I'm still saving heaps. The school funds me enough."

"So no new cute, plush friends in your room?"

"They need to renovate the Fuchu train station to be less boring, Kaede! The mall has a duty to give us window shoppers eye candy. It's the principle of the thing!"

And speaking of eye candy, it's right in front of you. Oh gosh, Kaede is cool.

[Artistry check: 55/40 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

So cool, so pretty, and most importantly: so classy. There's a misconception that underground idols are dumb and talentless because they couldn't hack it into the aboveground leagues; and to those morons, you spit. You tear out your own ear snot and flick it at them. Could a stupid person construct Kaede's fit? Look at it. A soft coral cropped cardigan and high-waisted, pleated mini-skirt on top. Her toned legs lead down to chunky white sneakers, while a casual, pastel-pink hoodie is thrown open on her shoulders. Her blonde hair hangs in waves, with mild sweetheart red highlights at the ends.

It's a getup that screams friendly confidence and dominance, perfect for a sunny Shibuya day. And it looks so modern, despite being picked out and reworked from a bargain sale—you know, because you stayed at Kaede's apartment for a few nights, where you watched her perform the needlework herself.

It isn't a new outfit, save for the clef-shaped hairpin attached to her hair. You don't care. It's better than a lot of amateur work online. How seamlessly Kaede slips into it—more so.

"You look good, Ruby."

"Aw, you think?" You glance down at your own fit. A long-sleeved blue coat, a red ribbon around the neck, black stockings on your legs. No patterns like the graffiti-esque logo on Kaede's top. "It's the usual."

"Change of words. You still look good."

A blush stains your cheeks. "I thought about wearing my uniform today."

"Mmm, I prefer what you have. You're letting that second layer pull its weight. I think it's because you're filling in the space better. You've grown taller."

"Hey, don't lie about that."

"Fuller, then. More defined. Your ears are fluffier now."

"Are they?"

You tilt your neck, letting Kaede brush her hands over your ears. It's ticklish. You giggle as the fur shifts.

"Tracen's feeding you good."

You puff out your chest. "I haven't eaten cup ramen in weeks."

"Now that's a sentence I never expected to hear." Kaede's thin eyebrows rise. "I'm going to call Suzuki and ask him to buy a lottery ticket on the way home."

"It's not my fault Tracen's cafeteria is so good. They have everything. Steaks, rices, breads…Kaede, I swear on my heart, the lunchlady makes vegan food taste good."

"You're joking."

"I'm not. I'm not!"

Your ex-leader stares. You do not relent. Your words were spoken with utmost seriousness. The next time Miki switches your hot dog for an ersatz sausage is the day she lands in the hospital. Umamusume are not grass-munchers. You love a fine piece of meat like any ordinary man, woman, or uma. Sizzling hot pork and beef on the grill, stained with soy sauce and served with fries—the perfect meal after a long, sweaty underground show.

She scoffs. "And next you're going to tell me they have an infinite carrot field or something—" She sees the twinkle in your eyes. "Oh my God."

"I'm so getting the raffle tickets next Feb. Grass won last time, and she shared an entire crate of fresh carrots with her class."

"Jesus…" Kaede places a hand on her nose. "Ruby, you're drooling."

"Oh no!" You gasp and swat at your chest.

"Ha! Got you. But seriously…" Kaede pulls out her phone, flicks it on, checks something, and then places it back in her handbag. "You better not be too full."

You place your hands by your sides. "Why?"

"Because I plan to stuff you silly with treats." Kaede points across Scramble Crossing. "They opened a new ice-cream chain from Ireland. The butterscotch almost knocked my ex to the floor with glee. Want to start there?"

Saliva gathers in your mouth. You practically squeal with joy. "Do umas grow tails, or what?"

Kaede extends her hand, and you follow her across Scramble Crossing and into the depths of Shibuya.

Celebration. That's the crux of your arrival in Shibuya. FAITHFUL was so impressed by your tryouts they offered you to hang out with the entire group on the weekend. Yes, even with Manager Suzuki tagging along, like in the good old days. You had no major commitments; your grades had gone up, the tryouts were done, Plain Jane told you to get some rest, and Agnes Digital said she needed more time to prepare for the next stage of the student mentorship. There was a certain elephant in the room you were wrangling into line, but it wasn't a task completable through a good study session, so you decided a break was needed.

Sadly, life got in the way. Hotaru was called in for her part-time job; Saya had to rerecord lines for doujin game; Suzuki's daughter fell ill; and Miki is trapped in maid cosplay as part of a cafe collaboration. The apologies poured in down LANE, and you pinged the girls back with care and understanding. It's a cutthroat industry down in the underground. FAITHFUL needs as many advantage as they can collect, now that they're down a member.

Not all your fans went to the other girls. Some only supported you and, despite your best efforts to present Kaede and the other girls are cool and beautiful and worthy idols, left soon after.

You clamp down on that thought before it infects your mood. The last concert sold out. The door you closed won't reopen. Kaede is here with you in the present, and you have her all to yourself today, so there!

You and Kaede run a tour of the ward. Strawberry Crepes at Dogenzaka, free dress tryouts at 109, crane games at Adores, selfies with the British phone booths outside Parco. You sample new hits at Tower Records with those massive demo headphones and find yourself torn between loving and critiquing the latest pop single from the States. Kaede picks up some charms she thinks Grass Wonder might like in the corner shops along at Tokyu, then hands you your tail at a DDR game on the ground floor of Marui City. Umas run fast, but the superiority in your species's physical strength shrinks in the field of twitch reflexes. It's why human and uma dances are segregated by ability instead of strength. You get her back when you dig through a basket and find an acryllic stand of Kaede's old group from her rookie days; she covers her face at the sight of her teenage self in the frilly pink dress. There's slightly less URA content than before; not that you're complaining, suprisingly enough. It's nice to take a break from the Twinkle Series.

The day is peppered with soul radiation sightings. A burning dragon wrapped around a man in a long coat. A golden crown perched atop a young, brunette uma, fading in and out. Balls of light swirling around a small streetside shrine in Cat Street. Each instance of the phenomenon is indistinct from a distance, living heat hazes that cease refracting once you approach. You're uncertain if this is their inherent nature, or if your ability lacks an extra chunk of oomph. Whatever the case, you're pleased they're not too distracting.

Time flies. You trace roads of long-trodden steps, immersing yourself in this intertwined, ever-shifting garden of commerce, business, and culture. Every corner, a new scene or curiosity. Every month, a new subculture breaks through the waves and embeds itself into Japan's artistry. It's tempting to stand on the street corner, put on a tune from your phone, and sing to the flowing crowd. The world inside you is rooted in Japan, barely a speck of speck of habitable land, but if a beam were to shoot down from the sky, or if a truck were you crash into your body and transport you to another world, you wouldn't mind if Shibuya was the last city you saw.

Lunch happens on Center Street. Ramen and a light beer for Kaede, a katsudon and a lemonade for you. Kaede is possibly breaking some law here, but she and the other girls have broken out alcohol in front of you, and Manager Suzuki stopped protesting after a few tries. Personally, you'd rather sample the soft drinks.

Juicy chicken. Delectable curry source. A portable billboard across the road flashes a trailer for a movie: a grand wooden ship soaring through a wide sky.

Kaede leans forward. She whistles. "Siete's dreamy now."

You follow her gaze. There's an animation of a blonde man in summer gear on the billboard. His abs could shred an entire ham.

"Is he? I thought he was super mean when he stole all his friends' wounds."

"Yeah, he's a pathetic loser sometimes. Most of the time, actually. But that's part of his charm. It's a feature, not a conflict. No matter how many swords he slays, or how many stupid trials he puts on the ground, he's still the dork who's touched metal more than he's held hands with a woman."

"What are you trying to be, his girlfriend?"

"Siete?" Kaede slugs down a mouthful of beer. "Not a chance in hell. Now, Six…that's a different story."

"I gotta watch that movie. It's out in two weeks, right?"

"Didn't Hotaru give you that site full of…"

"But those are illegal movies! What if the Director finds out and kicks me out of Tracen?"

Kaede lets out a soft snort. "They're not monitoring the Internet."

"It feels wrong! The company's losing money if I stream movies without their permission."

Kaede puts down her beer, opens her mouth to say something, then decides against it and resumes eating her ramen.

"We can watch it together once you win your debut."

"Deal. Either this or the latest Peco Adventures."

"Eh…"

"What? Peco is just as good as Prifight. The last movie was peak!"

"It…" Kaede sniffs and tilts her chin up. "It can't stop stroking itself and thinking it's some kind of unique masterpiece."

"It's a well-told story about AI, Kaede!"

Kids these days, her face says. Adults these days too, bleh! Your tongue sticking out counters. The lemonade is quickly drained. The billboard shifts to a romantic scene, which is only watchable in how corny it is.

"Gotta say, Siete's hair reminds me of that one Trainer at Tracen, the one with the yellow jacket…"

"Trainer Okino?"

"That's the one."

"I can't see it."

"It's the feel I get. The…what word did my friend overseas use? Bleh. I forget. Did that guy touch your ankles, by the way?"

"Nope. He was actually nice to me. Went up and said I was as good as Kitasan once the tryouts finished. Spe likes him, so does McQueen and Teio allegedly, and the Director already yelled at him enough, so…" You shrug. Kaede shrugs back. Most of what can be said about Trainer Okino's controversy has already happened.

"A lot of hubbub about him snatching up Kitasan."

"Snatching?"

"That's what the guy on the podcast said. A lot about how that many star trainees is unfair on the rest. Sounded like kvetching to me."

You count on his fingers. "He's got Golshi the six-time G1 winner, two Tiara champions, a Mejiro, the Supreme Commander Spe, Silence Suzuka, Tokai Teio…"

Kaede winces. "Not that one anymore."

"Oh yeah." Your tail droops. "Poor Teio."

"Saw it right on the stage. Absolutely awful."

"You girls were watching?"

"I was in the office break room. Miki was there in person. She instantly noticed what was up; texted me and all."

You noticed, too. The angle at which Teio's bent sent a cringe up your spine. The news of her fracture shook the entire academy. The Internet swam with denial so wide it could drown a beach. Tracen itself was barraged with questions about their health protocols. Your sympathy is reserved for Teio herself. You can't imagine how it must feel, for your most valuable tool in the sport, a best friend even, to give way beneath you. The amount of momentum Teio was riding on, too. It's like hurtling straight from heaven to hell.

Poor Kitasan, too. She was so excited to join her idol's team. They won't be allowed to run together for a long, long time.

"Spica's got it rough."

"That reminds me. How's your search for a Trainer going?"

Your smile dims. An awkward cough follows. You cover it by scooping up rice and sauce into your mouth and down your gullet. But, Kaede notices. She has to. Part of being the centerpiece means leading the other members, and that in turn means checking up on them. An emergency button exists inside Kaede's psyche labeled BREAK IN CASE OF SATONO RUBY BREAKDOWN. The glass is half-cracked; knowing Kaede, she must've detected the few moments where your thoughts returned to Tracen, and your smile grew strained around the edges.

"Ruby."

Your ears slink back. "I shouldn't…"

It's been a lovely day so far. You feel ill at the idea of ruining it with business. Shibuya was meant to be a break from that mess.

Kaede places down her chopsticks. She brushes her hair aside and tosses her empty beer can into a nearby bin. A three-point shot. "You won't ruin my day with a chat. Just because we're on different paths now doesn't mean we can't help each other."

"It's my responsibility."

"Dogged persistence works in shonen. This is real life. You won't gain anything by spinning your wheels. But, in the end, it's up to you."

Kaede can't hold your hand, is what goes unsaid. You stare at the dregs bubbling in your bowl. It's a fitting depiction of your chances back at Tracen. "Okay. It's like this…"

The problem isn't that you're not receiving Trainer offers. It'd be impossible, given your performance. No, the problem is that a few days ago, you were sought out. Trainers badgered you in the corridors exactly like the histories of known champions. Speeches were spoken, and resumes were handed out. Many offers were presented from rookie Trainers, but a couple of experienced Trainers threw their lot at you, too. You ducked away to the academy computer room to do some research, compile a list of pros and cons, and the very next day after narrowing down your shortlist, the offers dried up faster than a mirage in a desert.

The Trainers that waited up to half an hour ghosted you. Those you tracked down fed you excuse after excuse. They weren't up to the task. They found other trainees. Or they just plain blanked you until you stormed off in confusion.

Tabaru showed you an article one night. A smear piece that made it to mainstream journalism. Remembering Satono Opal, the true monster of the turf.

A tragedy for all involved…

Previously unforeseen amounts of damage…

Sickened, saddened, deeply disappointed…

The article wasn't a coincidence. It couldn't be. That was far as you got. You're not privy to whatever goes on in Trainers' Lounge.

Your fist clenches on the tabletop, where it rests. Disappointing. You liked some of those Trainers. The blonde one was good at chatting you up. So disappointing. Worse is the loss of momentum. Your rivals are gaining ground through their own training, while you're floundering in shallow waters. Tracen does run group programs for Trainer-less girls, but the content is bulk, merely competent. You don't want to be just competent. You want to stand within the top 0.5%, win a G1 and fulfill your childhood dream.

"Forget those morons. If they're folding at the thought of the Satonos, we can't expect them to treat you well when the Twinkle Series really heats up."

"That's obvious." You mutter.

"Did Grass Wonder do anything?"

"She said she couldn't help me with this because her role in the mentorship was over. I think they were orders from her Trainer. Not sure."

Anger and self-loathing had melded in your now-former mentor's eyes. Grass, too, was disappointed, most of all at herself. You patted her on the shoulder and reassured her, for a change.

"You do anything else?"

Yes. You tried asking Plain Jane for advice. She declined. She said using her vast repertoire of knowledge would be cheating.

You don't tell Kaede this, because Kaede can't see ghosts.

"Being proactive. Sending resumes, asking Trainers myself, showing them videos of my running online and in person…" You slide your phone over the table. Kaede looks at the screen. It shows a clip of you running alone across Tracen's turf, without commentary or backing music. "So far, no news."

You let the statement hang.

Kaede doesn't respond. She leans back in her seat slightly, places her hands atop the napkin on her lap, and gazes off into the distant buildings. Your tail rises. You know this behavior. It's a shifting of the gears. Gone is the mask of Kaede the cool big sister, and in its place is Kaede the strategist, the leader. The woman who teamed with Manager Suzuki and refined Tomorrow is FAITHFUL's dances, costumes and choreography down to the wire for the sake of an underground idol battle. The result: two rival groups with similar appeals and twice as good odds, crushed under FAITHFUL's heels.

You zip your mouth shut and tuck the key in your pocket. Kaede's thinking time is the group's hidden treasure, rooted from a strict childhood in a finance strategist's household. Growing up in the big city, she's accustomed to filtering through background noise. She's not listening to anything beyond her own thoughts. You're nevertheless afraid a single stray comment will scatter her plans like leaflets in the wind.

A minute passes. Kaede blinks. She picks at a few strands of her ramen, then clears her throat.

Kaede clears her throat. You straighten up in your seat. Kaede gestures to your phone.

"Is that all?"

A pointed question. It's not an aggressive one. "I've contacted some Trainers' social media accounts. They haven't responded, either."

"They're not going to."

"I see…"

"Because what you're doing isn't enough."

"How so?"

"This stuff? The running, the basic results? The Trainers know, Ruby. They already have access to this level of data. I'm willing to bet my deposit that most of them attended the race where you almost beat Kitasan. You're repeating the same trick, expecting a new outcome." Kaede then raises her index finger. "That's it. You only almost beast Kitasan Black. You didn't win against her."

"I mean, I would've liked to win against her. But I beat Happy Meek and other girls who thought they were faster."

"And only that."

"I don't get you."

"I'm saying, when taken uncharitably, it's a fluke."

You blink. You clench your jaw. "It wasn't!"

Kaede's looks you in the eye. Twin points of hard obsidian. Her soft features, so accustomed to shifting between a young gal's happiness and full-on rage screaming mode on stage, have sharpened themselves. "You can't prove that."

You stiffen, ears pinning back against the side of your head. And you understand your ex-leader. Some prospects are genuine flukes. They blaze through the first round, try the stage, realize they can't take the heat and whiff out in a flash, unremembered save for a small article in some dusty deleted newsletter. Kaede's talking sense. She rarely messes around when her mood is this hard.

"On one scale, there are your results. A good one, but it stands alone." Kaede lifts her other hand and lowers her first. "On the other scale, there's a massive sack called…"

"I get it now." You say, quietly.

Kaede nods. If you're a fluke, then your baggage, your mother's past, along with the endless harassment and scorn via association, is not worth dealing with.

"Signups are risks. A manager can prep the interview as meticulously as they want. There's always the chance new girl or guy unleashes their hidden malice and tanks the entire project. Your malice is plain obvious. It's not your fault. I'm not saying that. It is, however, a risk to training schedules, personal lives, sponsorships and the rest, because those dumbasses Satonos and their yellow journalism friends will make a big fuss about anything you and your Trainer do. Every little mistake, every little failure raked over the coals. Controversy brings in the clicks. A lot aren't signing up for that."

"And I now have to finish the job for them." You grumble.

"Yep. You gotta reduce the chance of that screw-up to as miniscule as possible in their eyes. Show that you're worth the trouble." Kaede says, running her fingers along the edge of her table in a tiny dance. "Compensation."

Advertising. That's what this is.

"Lame…"

Kaede isn't fazed. "The other girls put in one hundred percent? You put in one hundred and twenty. They run a lap in X time? You run it in X times two-thirds. You record your efforts, your commitment; blog it, ask your friends, put a bunch of posters, whatever you can to make those results public, and then you pretty up those second batch of results and thrust them in the hands of those waiting Trainers. All they need is an excuse."

To take the plunge. To act when they shouldn't hesitate in the first place. It's a test, in a sense. You, versus the public's persistent perception that you'll lose your any day now, when Triple Crowns like Narita Brian have acknowledged you as a proper Tracen student. This isn't doing impressions of adults any favors. So much for the world-class title Tracen has.

Yet, as you stew in your seat, you are reminded of a time two years ago. Back when Tomorrow is FAITHFUL had just wrapped up the failed Alice-in-Eviland narrative. The group was trying on so many costumes, hours spent in Seamstress's Sugar's workshop. You liked a style, a yami kawaii obscenity, and whined about how the group was stupid and dumb for being unable to afford it. Hotaru, sick of what she thought was a legal adult, griping, stormed over to give you a piece of her mind. Kaede moved to intercept, but it was Miki, the chill and sleepy Miki, who brushed past, took you aside and told you in a soft voice that it is what it is, so let's build what we can.

You quietened down. Kaede sighed with relief. Months later, Hotaru discovered you were actually thirteen years old and took you out to a big dinner with some friends. You learned life wasn't fair. You had three choices: adjust, compromise or get out. Someday, you'll buy a gift for Miki as repayment.

Kaede watches you. You don't throw a tantrum. You sit in silence and mull over her words. The truth is rarely pleasant to hear. It also doesn't swing around as much as it should.

[(Logic check: 85/50) || (Social Media check: 60/50) -> Success! + 10 EXP.]

"I guess I could run some scrimmages…" You mutter. Those are undeniable results. Your imagination puts on its apron and strikes its hammer against the anvil. And then you record your scrimmages, clip them into bite-sized chunks, layering a speech analyzing the race or how you might improve on each one. Finally, you drop a link that explains your journey from a poor city basement to Tracen itself, or an ad about how you've already surpassed regional champions by enrolling from the exams alone, or a demonstration of your dancing and singing, so that you new Trainer won't have to organize as much winning live practices!

Yeah. That might work. You might have thought this up in one week? Two weeks? Thank goodness Kaede gave you her push. Your smile grows and grows until another realization taps you on the shoulder and smacks you upside in the forehead.

"I'm turning into a salarywoman!"

Kaede stares, then bursts out laughing. "If it works, it works!"

She waves over a server for another can of beer, as you clutch your head in your hands and groan. Whenever you asked about Manager Suzuki his early twenties, his big frame seemed to shrink in its suit and a faraway look never failed to deaden his eyes. A bevy of soul-crushing anecdotes squirms in your head. Midnight trains. Convenience store dinners. Drinking parties with terrible bosses that leave them drunk on a bench to be arrested by the police. You already can't stand the smell of alcohol. How is your poor soul going to down all that sake? Now wonder those poor protagonists welcome being reamed by a truck!

"It might not be that bad, though."

You squint at her. "You made it sound intimidating."

"Yeah, but you're already accustomed to giving over a hundred percent. Effort's not the problem—experience is. I was afraid Manager Suzuki picking you up immediately might've given you the wrong impression, but I'm glad that's not the case. You've got this. You're a smart girl, Ruby."

Kaede cracks open the fresh beer, smiles, and you preen at her praise. The mask slips, and the tension across the table relaxes. The casual Kaede is back. You order an orange juice, and Kaede flips through a dessert menu, poring over the snacks.

"There's…not sure I should tell you this."

"You can't say that and not elaborate."

"Fine. It's only a guess. A hypothesis. That's why I'm debating it, because it may or may not be real, but oh well. Here goes! It's the type of Trainer you're most likely to attract."

"And those are…?"

Kaede puts down the menu. She forms a triangle with her hands. "Mavericks."

You frown. "Like the American movie?"

Kaede waves her hand. "Mavericks. Loose cannons. The underground to the aboveground." When you don't get it, she finally elaborates. "The guys and girls who buck the trends and give everyone else headaches."

"Those types exist?"

Kaede raises you an eyebrow. This is a look. A look that writes 'are you serious' on calligraphy paper and hangs it up in the Tokyo National Art Center. The phrase 'unhinged weirdo' rears its combobulated head, and you remember the time you broke ranks in the gym to fight Smart Falcon on the battlefield.

"That Okino used to only train Gold Ship, if I remember correctly, but his team's stacked with top tier talent, so let's use another example." Kaede takes a gulp of her drink. "Ever heard of Director Akikawa's personal army?"

This is a sentence you never expected to hear in your life.

"Like the police?"

Kaede gives a wry grin. "This was from Oguri Cap's era."

Now, your attention is hooked. Oguri doesn't talk much about her Twinkle Series days. They're already well-documented enough, you think.

Kaede continues. "It was around the time Oguri had come down from her high. She struggled with her races. She wasn't placing on the board, totally bombed the Japan Cup. Washed was the big word floating around. Everyone thought she was on the way out. Suzuki's wife was one of her fans, and she was one of the girls who wrote letters begging Tracen to let Oguri retire. She was one of the more restrained ones. You had people sending in bomb threats or even stating stuff about how they'd attack Oguri Trainer's because he was forcing her to run, or something."

Trainer Kitahara pressuring Oguri? Judging by what you've heard from him in interviews, he'd rather slice open his own stomach.

"No way."

"The journalists were the worst of all." Kaede's grin fades here. "They wouldn't stop. Banging on the gates, demanding an interview. Four mobs surrounded Tracen, stretching the security forces at their limits. I'd call them vultures, but vultures are important to a desert ecosystem. Those guys were just parasites."

Amen to that.

"So, Tracen's under siege. The noise is overwhelming. The girls in the school buildings are terrified out of their skins. The gates buckle. Just when all hope seems lost…" Kaede points to the sky. "Helicopters."

"Helicopters?"

"Helicopters and parachutes, each one -bearing a man in full-on khaki military gear. The Director herself strides to the front gates, waves her fan, belts a war declaration and her personal army rushes forward to beat the crap out of the mob."

Mental images sound in your head. A cacophony of flying fists, pig-like squeals and hard pavement crunches. Oh my goodness. It's beautiful.

"But isn't that assault?"

"It's a story."

"A true one?"

Kaede flashes you a cheeky grin straight out of a perfume ad. "You should look it up."

"Kaede…"

"They didn't carry any guns. Probably. The Director's a loaded woman. She's a queen who will do anything for her uma racing kingdom. Who knows what weirdos she employs as Trainers? The best of the best don't rise to the top by being normal people. You might find ex-military or an ex-anarchist. A PhDer who had a mental break. switched gears. Someone who oversaw a Mongolian Derby uma. A survivor from that botched West Coast to Manhattan marathon from a while back."

"Or I could join another team like a normal uma." You say.

"You could." Kaede admits. "The mavericks are the least likely to care about what your mom did. They've already got enough skeletons in their closets already. And they're usually relish a challenge, so you might get more offers from them, instead of the mainstream folks. Won't that be something?"

Kaede chuckles. You chew your lip. A crazy Trainer for a shunned girl. That's an underdog narrative in the making. You guess you're already at rock bottom, so it can't get any worse.

"Say, do you want a guy or girl Trainer?"

"Does it matter?"

"Well, if she's a woman, you might relate to her more. The species barrier won't matter when it's just talking. Or she reminds you of some horrid teacher from your past, and you end up hissing and clawing at each other. Fifty-fifty odds."

"And a guy isn't going to do that?"

"They like to keep us girls at a distance at first. That's a benefit and a detriment, in that they won't pry, but they can also be brick walls you have to punch over and over until you make headway. Sometimes, you do need a wall to complain to and cry on—it's cathartic. But not all of them are as solid as Suzuki. You're got wimps, blockheads, creeps, dunderheads; and if it's not that, you should see the state of of their apartment. Like, c'mon guys, would it kill for you to put a spot of wallpaper here and there? Honestly."

Didn't Kaede break up with guys twice? One she liked, the other she almost hurled into a bin. Normally, she keeps such details hush-hush, but she's ranting more, so it must be the alcohol in action. Never fails to turn her giggly. It's a good thing none of her fans are swanning about, because the contrast between Kaede's casual mannerisms and her loud, domineering stage persona is like night and day.

She's not actually drunk. Two light drinks is her limit when you're around. You suck down on your juice and think any arguments between you and this hypothetical male Trainer will solely be emotional, because as an umamusume, you can break his ribs in half with a single kick.

The topic drops. A new one surfaces.

"So, what's the boss up to?"

Kaede's grin almost stretches past her face. "Oh, you would not believe what he said to Sugar's face the other day…"

Mint tarts for dessert. A tale about FAITHFUL's new project, destined to hit the stage next months. A walk around Yoyogi Park. Candied carrots, big apples and other snacks to give to your friends from Hikarie, courtesy of Kaede. Another round of selfies taken outside Shibuya Station in the dusky afternoon breeze.

Down at the platform, the announcement rings across the intercom. The gates open. A train rushes down its tracks, buffeting the nearby air with a cold whoosh. Kaede pats you on the shoulder, then gives in and hugs you, tighter and longer.

"You've got this, Ruby. Ride safely."

You bury your head in the shoulder of your ex-leader, your pseudo-older sister. This is warmth you wish you could bask in forever.

"I will. See you around, Kaede!"

One day, in the far future, when those G1 sashes drape like a second skin across your shoulder and chest, you will return to Tokyo and reward FAITHFUL with as good of help as they granted you. It's the least they deserve.

Kaede waves you off, smiling at you until your train passes into the underground tunnel and you vanish from her sight.

Yes, you think to yourself, clutching the plastic bags of gifts with a head of burgeoning plans and smiling, today was a good day.

There might not be one like this for a long while.

>>ACT 2.

>>ENCOUNTER #4: BEGIN.

[Mood has raised to Great.]

[Total EXP Gained: 25.]

You are umamusume. You are fast, strong, and tough. The instinct to run is ingrained in your brain from millennia of evolution, hence you are the species that lives on the turf. Humans do not. Humans are squishy, slow and fragile. Their minds, however, are as good if not better, which is why they stand behind-the-scenes, advising you as Trainers.

Here's what a Trainer can do for you:

Manage your time (increased AP) Create training plans and schedules (increased stat gains) Organize scrimmages and joint training sessions with other umas or teams (increased socialization chances) Protect you from the media or harassment (goodbye paparazzi) Deal with paperwork and administration on your behalf (Thanks for setting an example, Oguri) Care for your mental state (Morale gains) Help you rehabilitate from injuries (Health gains) Be a second mind to bounce ideas off (increased Perk options)

Here's what they ask in exchange.

You have to communicate with them. You have to be careful around them. You must be punctual to training sessions. You must be willing to listen to them. A very unfair deal, I know.

Since Trainers take on a supporting role, their Attributes are modified to fit. Here are the four main ones:

Intellect (INT)

Raw brainpower. Determines conventional intelligence.

Intellect is the Attribute of thinkers, lawyers and scholars; who take the science in sports science and emphasize it to a tee. It'll put that IQ score dotted on your exam results to use: calculate the trajectory of a trainee's run down with physical to the last digit, then outline a regime with flawless logic behind it. Or recall trivia that sets off a breakthrough. Or whip up a counterargument with insufferable smugness to a rival Trainer trying to butt in on your turf slot. The inner layers of umamusume racing are yours to parse, one rule at a time. Wield your other sciences too. You never know when a spot of trivia might come in handy.

High Intellect might warp your worldview around numbers and figures, distancing you from the softer parts of life, but that's a fair trade for Low Intellect, in which you'll struggle to come up with more than basic plans…right?

(Disclaimer: Intellect is the not a equivalent to wisdom. No Trainer at Tracen is truly stupid by the average person's standards.)

Psyche (PSY)

Emotional prowess. Influence, manipulate and charm others.

Umamusume are not machines. That's why it's called umamusume racing, not uma-shaped-robotics racing. As a Trainer, you must deal with the emotional highs and lows of your trainee; their joys, sorrows, and lowest pitfalls. Psyche is the Attribute that bridges this emotional gap. Convince her to keep on track with the passion in your heart instead of cold logic. Rally the team together with a burst of authority. Shove on the brakes when she acts petulant, then embrace her and resonate with her woes as she cries into your shoulder about how far the Triple Crown seems. Alternatively, wield Psyche as a weapon, planting seeds of doubt and treachery in rivals' minds, perhaps going as far as to seduce and bend them to your will…

(Disclaimer: Do not seduce your trainees unless they have already graduated.)

High Psyche will make you likeable. So likeable, you'll attract types and entities you'd rather prefer tucked away. Tending to the others' emotions means less time to care for yourself. It's better than burning bridges because you failed to understand your trainee—just ask Old Man Roppei from his early days.

Physique (FYS)

Power of the body. Determines physical strength and athletic understanding.

Why exercise when the umamusume are already doing that for you? Because, despite what the tabloids think, a passive role is not a zero-activity role. Enduring a sudden downpour at practice, slogging through consecutive all-nighters for a breakthrough, shoving aside a pushy paparazzo in lieu of your trainee, and fending off sabotage—Physique is the engine by which these strength and endurance-based feats run. In addition, it encompasses the body's knowledge. Umamusume and human biology aren't too dissimilar. Intellect and its scientific theory may fail for your trainee's injuries, allowing Physique with its instinctual understanding of murky bodily systems to finish the job. Acupuncture, hot spring therapy, training regimes you personally test…

At the end of the day, it's your trainee running, not you. Effort spent on raising Physique may be better placed elsewhere. Then again, you don't want to end up like Trainer Kashimoto, who bowls over whenever she tries to lift anything heavier than a water bottle.

Guile (GUI)

Mental flexibility and innate perception. Scheme and strategize on the fly.

Umamusume may not fight with swords or bows any longer, but make no mistake: competition is warfare. The best tactics go unnoticed until after the fact, and that's where Guile comes in. It's street-smarts and perception rolled into one. Read your rivals' cues. Adjust to those cues. Feint with your own cues, and watch as your trainee storms past the competition because those suckers are too busy mired in your carefully laid misdirection. Then, slap on a poker face to the post-game accusations of foul play. You can teach your trainee all this too. Anything's fair in love and war, right?

Guile also excels at reading the environment: the flow of a room, the eyes laid on your trainees' backs, the twitch that signals life's about to get ugly. Invest too high in this Attribute and you might end up too smart, too cynical and manipulative for these young umamusume. It's no substitute for Intellect or Psyche, either. But lack Guile, and you'll view the world straightforwardly, predictably—a fatal mistake in any battle.

We will now proceed to begin the Trainer Search. This is NOT Character Creation. You are not building this Trainer, because this person already exists in-universe;—you're simply looking for them. To accomplish that, you will release a series of advertisements that will attract a variety of prospective Trainers based on their preferred Tendencies. Each Tendency selected will improve the chances of a related Attribute, skill or information appearing more or at higher values in the upcoming Trainer profiles.

Example: a total of +3 to Intellect Tendency means your potential Trainers will all have high amounts of Intellect. It does not mean they receive a hard bonus of +3 to the Intellect Attribute. You will also not find a prefect Trainer embodying all the chosen Tendencies (but I will spread the Tedencies out so that every Trainer has some worth to them).

Other Tendencies available at this stage include:

Age: High Age Tendency means more life experience and wisdom, but less chance of relating to the young (like you). Conversely, Trainers with low Age Tendency are easier to get along with, but may struggle to put their theories into practice. Note that the minimum age to enter Tracen as a Trainer is eighteen. Foreigner: Foreigner Tendency determines whether the Trainer originates from overseas or not. High Foreigner Tendency means less chance of being affected by Opal's actions, but may relate less to Japan and its customs. A lack of Foreigner Tendency means the Trainer is a long-term Japanese native with the opposite effects. Racing Skills: Determines which Racing Skills the Trainer is best at teaching.

Here's an template of a Trainer Profile.

Codename: Lorem Ipsum (Names are not given out until after a Profile is selected)

Age: Young (Low Age Tendency)

Nationality: Japanese citizen (0 Foreigner Tendency)

Background: Insert a description of the Trainer's background here>

Attributes: X INT, Y PSY, Z + 2 FYS, A + 1 GUI*. (Exact numbers will be provided in the actual profiles. Each Trainer has a tagged Attribute, which provides them with an innate +1 bonus)

Teachable Skills: Racing Tactics (and maybe more…)

Other: Insert any trivia here.

Did you get all that? If not, feel free to ask as many questions as you want. Now then…
