4.1: Trainers Six

Mood: Great.

EXP: 80/200.

The train grinds across its magnetic track: smooth, principled, unable to deviate from its course. It's a reflection of your efforts so far. Alright, you think to yourself, with a firm slapping against your cheeks, enough is enough. Systematic inequality—that's the word Hotaru loves to let slip out, whenever she's had a cocktail and a chicken skewer and thinks the others won't gripe too much if she bangs on about her personal blog. You can gripe about it until the sun explodes, and it won't advance your search efforts by a single millimeter. Tonight is the night when you sit down and have a good hard think about your mindset.

So that's what you do. After a dinner of tender carrots and beef stew, you lie down on your bed with a playlist of calming tunes in your ears, your inner self squeezing those brain muscles taut. This is how you finished lyrics for FAITHFUL's group projects. It works some of the time, which is better than none of the time. On this occasion, the answer…

[Wits check: 10/6 -> Success! Trivial: +0 EXP.]

…arrives easily, mostly because Kaede spelled it out for you. It's not that your efforts were too passive. It's that they're too normal. The thought of this jabs you with self-inflicted spite, but you shake your head against the pillow and continue on. All that resume handling and cold emailing? That's bog-standard. The tactic of the everyuma. The innate backup dancer, and many more beige-colored titles that send a shudder through your artistically minded soul. Here's the big fat reminder: you are not mainstream. You are notorious. A former shinme, underground umadol and runaway. Your past two years were immersed in the less than reputable side of Tokyo, a great economic machine built on the vivid, the raucous, and, above all else, the assertive.

Yes, now you're getting it. Forget about sitting back and hoping for the best. It's time for you to bring the fight to the Trainers themselves. Manager Suzuki once taught you no interviewer truly delights in rejecting applicants. They want to find the right man, woman or uma for the job, if only to get their job over and done with. You are more than happy to grant Tracen's Trainers an excuse.

You sketch down ideas in a spare notebook. You review them and cross out the ones that are too long. A double-check, a refinement of certain strategies, and you smile and get to work.

You create the plan. You double-check it. And then you smile and get to work.

>>[AdvertisingEffort] Launch an impromptu idol concert somewhere trainers are bound to see.

Agnes Digital's LANE icon is a photograph of herself waving glowsticks at a winning live, a mote of drool trickling down the side of her mouth and her eyes framed as giant hearts. It's pure gachizei energy and not what the public thinks of a multi-G1 champion on turf and dirt—at least not anymore. You press the call button with no small apprehension.

She picks up after two rings.

"Ruby!"

Yup. That's a squeal of delight blaring out of the speakers.

"Hi, Digital. Did I call at the wrong time?"

"No, not at all! I was proofreading an essay, checking for SPAG and all that, but I can finish the rest of a jiffy. You're so much more important." No doubt she's beaming so hard it's giving her roommate a case of first-degree burns. "You're sounding lovely, by the way. How may this humble Digitan help you?"

"I need a favor."

"A favor? What for?"

She's quick to agree, but then again you are her mentee now. A couple of days ago, Agnes Digital sat you down and grilled you on basic PR tactics. As a former underground umadol, you passed with flying colors, skipping what was intended to be the first batch of basic lessons. You could have begun the second batch, but it'd be of limited effectiveness without a Trainer, since their reputation and image will influence yours, and vice versa.

"To be honest, I've stumbled into something of a roadblock. It's not great. Yesterday, I was hanging out with an old friend who gave me some advice, so now I'm thinking about switching up my tactics. What I've got in mind is this…"

You give the rundown, and Digital squeals again at the end, gushing at how smart and proactive you are.

"Leave it to me!"

Dear readers of this hypothetical autobiography, let it be known that five years ago, a poll was conducted across Japan's regional and national umamusume racing academies to gauge reactions and opinions to how races were run. According to the results, approximately fifteen percent of Trainers believe the winning live is a waste of time.

Shock. Gasp! Blood rushing to the forehead, office implements wielded as torches and pitchforks! Now, you'd like to ask these readers to put down their impromptu weapons, because you empathize with them. You can emphasize. You, too, almost popped an artery upon reading this horrendous slander against your precious artform. If you were shunted into a world where dancing was never held after a jaw-dropping G1 finale, you'd fall to your knees and beg the kami to send you back. You'd even sacrifice your unborn child. And you have no doubt many girls in Tracen agree with you.

But in the present, where your head is clearer, you'd rather examine the reasoning behind this antipathy. The poll itself wasn't as comprehensive as you'd liked. No names were published, possibly to avoid social lynching, and the selectable options were limited to three: like, neutral, or dislike. You don't know if most of these Trainers held mild annoyance, or long-suffering antipathy, or active hatred for dancing itself. Only the fact they'd prefer the winning lives to be dismissed entirely.

[Logic check: 86/65 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

That doesn't preclude you from making an educated guess. These Trainers are not in charge of the champions. The winners are more than happy to cap off their achievements with a song and a dance. These mentees of these Trainers are likely the runners-up, the no-placers. They and their Trainers must have cursed the dance lessons for siphoning their time, cutting off those last few training sessions where the big breakthrough sat right around the corner. It's a flawed mentality, since the winning lives are good avenues for PR stardom; and if the dance lessons did indeed cease to exist, then it'd free up lesson slots for the gold medalists, resulting in the gap between them and the rest of the competition remaining the same.

But it's a mentality that exists. It's accessible to those who like or feel neutral about the winning lives. Individuals who work in the same field inevitably influence each other, even through disagreements. It's possible Trainers as established as Hana or Kitahara have glanced down at their schedule and flirted with the idea of cutting off dance lessons for more stamina training, or whatnot. Which means there's a market for an umamusume who saves time by handling the dancing, and the rest of the strategy practically writes itself. Get in front of those Trainers and show your moves!

Except not in Tracen. Air Groove will yell at you.

That's where Agnes Digital came in. She doesn't think your plan idiotic. She calls up Nice Nature, who slips in a good word to the shopkeepers across a certain lane within Fuchu's center-east. The process takes less than a day. Digital messages you at lunch to inform you of your news, at which your sandwich slips out of your fingers. Any lingering doubts about her competency shatter like glass amidst the blades of a combine harvester.

Four in the afternoon. Fuchu is hanging up her tie and picking out what konbini dish to eat. The orange of an encroaching dusk peeks out from lumps of grey clouds, casting muted shades across the concrete like streaks of loose fabric. Across the sidewalks, pedestrians flow like minnows: schoolkids in their uniforms, salarymen rushing out for late-night coffee supplies, mothers and aunties picking up groceries. The buildings create a valley; signs atop shops flash with adverts for groceries and night cuisine, and beneath them wafts the oh-so-comfortable smell of concrete and faint cigarette smoke, drowned beneath phone bleeps and earbuds.

Go towards the shopping lane that's all but sponsored by Nice Nature. An urban sandwich between a late-night beef place and a closed-down convenience store. On any other day, it's ignored. Years in the future, it'll be memory-holed when renovations finish and the new ramen bar opens up. But in the here and now, it's occupied, alive, all thanks to the most infamous student in all of Tracen.

"The big race is about to begin, ha ha! Colorful race outfits from beginning to end! The stands are roaring out loud, today's the Derby, so let's raise a cheer!"

You sing your heart out, dressed in your Tracen uniform, atop a wooden stage slightly better than a spare fruit crate.

"Run, run, oh umamusume! Champions and underdogs in the fray!"

It's plain. The awning above you will barely shield you from the rain. There's no roof nor sturdy walls to enclose the sound and project it into an audience. You don't care. Music in your ears, a finger on the microphone button—it's greater than slipping on a comfortable cloak, more akin to a cocoon metamorphosing into the butterfly it was destined to be. As long as you have the sound and a pair of functioning legs, then you're here and about, and your exhaustion is liquid ethereal future you's problem.

[Dancing check: 116/70 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

The city tries to swallow you up. It defends its peace with the asphalt, the shadows of the looming apartment blocks, the sheer permanence of its evening flow, and yet the boombox never ceases playing, your feet never not shifting and skittering. Hashire Hashire flows into Make Debut and then UNLIMITED IMPACT and soon enough a crowd gathers, because your notoriety is an attraction of itself. The flashy Tracen advertising cardboard stands, a condition set by the academy administration, are the hooks that reel in Fuchu's URA-brained population.

"Hey, is that…"

"The heck is she doing now? Here, of all places?"

"Damn. She's not too shabby…"

Had you tried this two months ago, an entire camera crew would've waved their lenses in your face. But, not even Satono Opal's daughter can dominate the headlines forever. The crowd you receive comprises the regular folk. Half of them stop to properly watch. Even less hang around for half a song. From those, some heckle, others glare, yet more often than not, the audience remains quiet and pays attention. You ensure to flash these folks an extra-wide smile, then strike a cool pose at each song's climax.

As for the trainers, they don't come on the first day. One does on the second.

"Yo."

It's a man, recognisable as a Trainer by the ID card on a lanyard around his neck. You noticed him watching from the back for a while. Middle-aged, dressed in a orange Hawaiian shirt and jeans, his hair slicked back into spikes at the top. His hands rest in his pockets, and he's chewing on something that's too squelchy sounding to be candy. Combined, you think of a shady Ikebukuro cabaret son, drinks at his beck and call and a heart full of greed for some poor, bored housewife's wallet.

Except, he pays attention to you, tapping his feet in tune to the last chorus of Girls LEGEND U. He approachers after the song dies down. You notice while he wears his shirt casually, the sleeves wide to let the air circulate, his shoulders are broad. The property of a professional athlete.

"Cute setup you've got there." Mr. Orange-Shirt awards you a polite round of applause. "The dancing's not bad too."

"Thank you!" You grant him a short bow. "Want an encore?"

"I'll take a request if you're offering."

"Only URA-approved songs, please. Usually, I'm not picky, but they're the only ones on the playlist."

"Hmmm…" Mr. Orange-Shirt thinks, glancing off to the side. A sign above a shop apparently gives him inspiration. He snaps his fingers. "How about Daitaku Helios's special?"

[Foreign Languages check: 64/100 -> Failure.]

There's a musical lilt to his drawl that you can't put your finger on. It distracts you, blanking the song's name from your mind. A quick check of your phone saves you, and so you hit the play button. The first part's easy: you swinging back and forth, spinning and improvising to an upbeat-big band's tune. The first section break demands that you deepen your voice and lean into the microphone. The single word is spicier than an entire bucket of chilli. Then arrives the part where your partner is supposed to exist in this amped-up waltz. You pretend Hotaru's there. You grab her invisible hands and count the steps. She's the shortest member of FAITHFUL, so it works.

Mr. Orange-Shirt claps again. "First try?" He asks.

"Third. I practiced a bit beforehand."

"That's good enough. Not bad, young miss. Not bad at all."

"I'm a professional." You reply and wink. Sweat trickles down your forehead; you do not wipe it. It is evidence of your prowess. "This is what I'm obliged to do."

Mr. Orange-Shirt grins. It's sharp on one side. "No sweat for the winning live, eh?"

"There are still better dancers in Tracen. I wouldn't mind if someone signed me up for more classes. It's just that…" Your feet criss-cross butter-smooth, and you twirl around, ending in a pose with a beckoning hand shot out. "They better sign me up for the advanced course, otherwise they'd be wasting my time and their money!"

Mr. Orange-Shirt lets out a bark of laughter. It's short and breathy, like a happy, well-trained hound.

"That footwork." He nods to your feet. You switched your uniform shoes for a proper dance pair out of Tracen's gym storage. "We saw that at the tryouts."

"Oh?"

"Hard not to. Entire lounge talked about it for a while, going over the footage on the TV over our coffee breaks. Some of the older guys—the ones with established teams and all—were pretty jealous. I'm gonna take a stab in the dark and say that's now your specialty. It's a decent card to have up your sleeve."

You blink. That's confirmation that the Trainers are observing you. A good snippet of information to have. Why is he telling you this? You decide to slip back into an umadol persona for the time being.

"Thank you!" You flash him a wide grin. "Tell them if they want more, they'll have to come over, sign me up and find out!"

"Ah, c'mon, you're not going to give those poor saps a hint?"

"Sorry, that's my umadol pride." You cross your arms in an X shape. "All in or nothing to win!"

You and he laugh together. Those jealous, quietly seething types won't have the guts to choose you, anyway.

"You chose a good spot, by the way." He says, suddenly. "Thanks for not distracting us after-hours."

Your laughter peters out , and you freeze, caught-off guard. Did he—yes, he did. He figured out your strategy. A night bar lies at the end of the shopping lane, honored with being the favorite hole-in-the-wall of many a Tracen Trainer. Your stage wasn't erected in front of it. It's located a few blocks down, close enough for the Trainers to hear your singing, but far enough as to not distract and agitate them with your singing. It's a detail that took no less than five seconds to request, but it's one of the most important of them all, and this guy figured it out by just observing you.

Are you grimacing or grinning? You can't tell. On the surface, it's like he's pulled one over you…

[World Resonance check: 106/50 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

…yet a warm touch of camaraderie lies in his mannerisms, peeking out from beneath his casual attitude. He is, at least, not poking fun at you.

Mr. Orange Shirt nods once, then steps away, raising his hand in farewell.

"Also, your left side is slightly less coordinated. Try doing some one-sided deadlifts."

"What, you're giving me a freebie?" You call back.

He cackles back. "We saw your footage. Fair's fair. And it helped my old girl beat Air Groove!"

Another wave, and he walks away, a thin ponytail swishing and a whistle on his lips.

[Traversal has increased by 2.]

Mr. Orange Shirt doesn't contact you the next day. So, you continue to dance. You're out Tracen's gate as soon as the final bell rings, stretching your time on the lane as much as the dorm curfew allows. One night, you're performing Tracen Ondo, getting back into a sorely-missed enka rock groove, a real microphone in hand (take that, Smart Falcon!) when you spy a murmur in the crowd out of the corner of your vision. Two men in hoodies, slipping their hands into their jackets. Their stares are anything but entertained. The usual suspects flash their mugshots through your head. A phone, a rotten egg, a milkshake filled with stones, or worst of all: a knife.

You don't stop twirling on the spot. Fear breeds initiative from an assailant. You do prepare a call-out, and are on the verge of enacting it, when a large shadow steps out from the back of the crowd.

Two meaty hands crash down on the two interlopers' shoulders, buckling their knees.

"I would advise you to keep those implements tucked away."

You hit the pause button on your microphone to stop the music. It'd be irresponsible to dance in this situation. It's a Trainer, you notice. Another middle-aged man. His head is shiny as a cueball, save for a single blonde cowlick protruding from the front. He pushes the two interlopers forward, where they stumble, almost crashing into the bottom of your stage. The Trainer's in full view under the late-night streetlights now. Your breath catches in your throat. What you mistook for corpulence was in reality a wall of bulging muscle, barely restrained by a snazzy black work suit.

[World Resonance check: 106/50 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

He's a walking mountain, a living boulder. Nothing but a titan's force shall tear him down.

The two interlopers spin around. They rear up on their feet in a display of masculine protest. They realise the obvious: any fist or kick launched at this Trainer has as much effectiveness as attacking a tank with a stick. But, they've committed to pestering you, so try to rebuke him, bless their foolish hearts.

"We're doing nothing, man!" Hoodie #1 says. His speech is slow, drawn-out. "Why'd you gotta push us like that?"

Hoodie #2 chimes in with a whine. "Yeah! You're getting up all in our personal space. That's a violation of our personal rights."

"An interesting proposition." Mr. Muscles responds. Pure bass covers his voice. "I'd say the same applies to recording a lady without her permission."

He gestures to one of the signs near your stage. It possesses a camera icon with a red cross slapped across it. It's there because you'd rather not give your antis any more ammunition, since it could spill over to your Tracen friends and FAITHFUL. It's Japan. Most will respect this rule, which in return gives you an inkling as to where these interlopers come from.

"Why do you care, man?"

"You going to stop us? This is a free country!"

"Yeah, do you have any idea whose daughter she is?"

"That woman hurt, like, hundreds."

"Thousands, even!"

"She's a public figure. She put herself out there. You expect us to turn away from this gold mine?"

The two interlopers wave their cameras about. Pinpricks of red and white dash across Mr. Muscles's form. Being taller, they have to strain their arms upwards to obtain a good angle. Clearly, the two men are attempting to rouse Mr. Muscles into controversy. But, he doesn't fall for the bait. He doesn't encroach over the two men, or shake his mighty fist in their noses. He simply stands there, arms folded, letting his gaze fall where it may. A quiet disappointment is engraved on his features, of father figures and stalwart next-door neighbours.

Whispers arise from the surrounding crowd, none of them positive. Bit by bit, the two interlopers realise their wind is buffeting out of their sails. Their shoulders slack, and they're unable to look anywhere else but each other. The cameras are aimed at the floor.

"You should reconsider your lives." Mr. Muscles's says, his words almost gentle. "Think about what led you to profit off an innocent girl's suffering."

"But our sponsors—"

Hoodie #2 yanks his friend back, dragging him through their side of the crowd. They vanish into the night.

Mr. Muscles's relaxes his stance. He shakes his head. You decide this is as good a time as any to pack up.

"Everyone! Thanks for coming tonight! Don't forget to take a brochure if you haven't already!"

The crowd disperses, salarymen and tourists shaking their heads and gossiping about the state of the streets these days. Mr. Muscles approaches as you pull out the wires on the boombox.

"Are you alright, young miss?"

You look up. Gosh, he is massive when up-close. His shadow is smothering yours. If you weren't convinced he's a nice man, you'd be terrified out of your tail.

"I'm fine. Thanks for helping me." You reply. "Those nasty streamer types come around to my concerts now and then. They try to get me to say something stupid. In the past, I've had my manager or groupmates scare them off, but tonight I had you."

You giggle a little. Mr. Muscles just looks concerned.

"Should we put in a word with the Director?"

"Oh, no, no, no!" You exclaim, waving your hands. "It's okay. Fuchu's been kind to me recently. Let's not make a big fuss over this, yeah?"

He nods reluctantly.

"It's late. At least let me escort you back."

You protest again, but he's already packing up your equipment for you. Shrugging, you let him. He then gives you another reason not to doubt his strength by balancing the boombox, the stage and the stands on a stack and lifting them with a single palm above his head. The amount of raw physical strength this requires is troubling for an umamusume, never mind a human. People stare, but they dare not interfere, especially the terribly disguised paparazza lurking at the doorstep of a coffee house.

Mr. Muscles helps you pack the equipment in the gym's storage and grants you a short bow once you meet him on the pavement outside.

"Take care, Miss Ruby."

"Wait. One request." You raise a finger. "Can you do a flex for me?"

Childish joy beams in his eyes. His handlebar mustache vibrates with joy. He lifts his arms, concentrates, and then drops them by my side.

"I shouldn't. It'll tear my suit."

"Ah."

"Which would be inappropriate towards you."

Fair enough.

"Forget I asked, then. Have a good night!"

[Composure has increased by 2.]

>>[AdvertisingEffort] Challenge your rivals to a scrimmage.

That's easy enough. Tracen has set up an automated system via its online portal to organize scrimmages. All you need to do is mail in a request, and the administration will take care of the rest. Of course, it helps if you ask your future opponents in person.

"Kawakami Princess, please run with me!"

The wide-foreheaded uma breaks into a fierce smile. She smacks her fist into her palm. "Absolutely! Let us engage in a showdown of good and evil!"

Judging from the colorful Prifight merch on her school textbook, it's clear who she considers the 'good' uma is. You'll let it slide because you agree. Season III of Prifight annihilates any other anime on air.

The race is a miler, a distance you're less accustomed to. The instant you run around the first corner, the dissonance in your rhythm manifests itself. The finish line pokes in the corner of your vision, throwing you off by how close it's getting. Your instincts buckle against the will to accelerate early.

[Acceleration check: 76/70 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

Still, you adjust and manage to put up a good fight. The two of you are neck and neck at the homestretch, but Kawakami's renowned as the physically strongest of your generation for that reason. Her right leg crushes the earth in a single mighty slam, and she blitzes past, winning by half a length.

"King! King! Did you see that? I won!"

You brush fragments of fresh grass off your cheeks and decide on your next opponent.

"Happy Meek!"

The white-haired uma blinks and gazes off into the distance before answering with a soft. "Hmm...okay."

You burst out of the borrowed gates at a far more acceptable time. So does Happy Meek. She tries front-running this time, which soon proves to be a mistake. The result's a win in your favor, much to the chagrin of Trainer Kiryuin.

"Tabaru!"

Your roommate fiddles with her hair ornaments, then glances up from her literature homework. "Sure."

Unlike practice runs, scrimmages are semi-official bouts. The academy creates official schedules, their attendees consider of other students, Trainers and sometimes the press, and the results are recorded, then displayed for public use. The participants, therefore, take scrimmages more seriously than standard training, though not to the extent of the Twinkle Series.

That's not why you're nervous at the prospect of facing Tabaru. In fact, you're not afraid of racing in front of a Tracen crowd at all. Bullies and journalists pale in comparison to real shadowy monsters capable of disintegrating the fabric of your soul. No, the reason for your apprehension lies in your morning jogs. You've seen how fast Tabaru sprints in a casual setting. Plus, she won her tryout race by several lengths.

Your fears are well-founded. Tabaru's expression locks itself into rigor mortis as she vanishes behind her gate slot. When the signal blares, she's barges ahead before the metal walls have fully opened. She tears and tears her way down the turf, moving with such recklessness it's as if Yomi itself hounds her back.

[Speed check: 11/12 -> Failure.]

. You barely pursue her for three-quarters of the two thousand meter track, then can only watch as she closes the last stretch in a flash.

The small crowd roars. They're all there: her fellow Gold Clan, her posse, and members of her new team. Trainer Nase claps her hands, smiling. Hoots or jeers aimed in your direction drown out as your attention directs to the statuesque uma sprinting to meet Tabaru. That was not an incorrect adjective. Auburn-haired, a long braid trailing down the back of her head—this new uma is quite attractive. Her arms are outstretched in a fashion that sends an ache through your heart.

"Great job on the scrimmage, Tabaru. You did so well! We're all super proud of you."

Super Creek, the uma who could have replaced Grass Wonder, embraces Tabaru. She pats Tabaru on the head. You can't decide if the squiggle on Tabaru's face is one of embarrassment or resignation. The crowd titters. Trainer Nase, over in the background, rubs her forehead. It's a display that has occurred far too much and far too often for what should be Nase's liking, yet nothing short of divine intervention will curb Creek's habit. Nase might enjoy it, you ponder.

You feel a hand on your shoulder. "You'll get them next time."

"Oguri—"

The Ashen Beast of Kasamatsu grips your shoulder tighter. "We'll get them next time."

She locks eyes with Super Creek. The reaction is instantaneous. Creek's smile grows testy at its edges. A glare shoots out, compounded with a wave of barely restrained fury. [Nook and Cranny: Exists.]

"Rice Shower!"

The long-eared girl squeaks. This is because you have cornered her in the library.

The gates fly open, and you and Rice charge out along with several others. Your new rival demonstrates her marking skills were no fluke. "Congratulations, Satono Ruby."

"Thanks!"

It's yet another Trainer speaking to you, this one a woman whom you estimate tobe eighteen at the youngest and twenty-five at the oldest. She's acting as the scrimmage's supervisor today. This new Trainer deserves to be on the cover of a fashion magazine rather than clad in a tracksuit and supervising a bunch of sweaty umas. Her face is pretty, the head small and elegant, a heart-shaped contour rounding out the bottom. Then again, this is the same academy that enrolls bombshells like Gold City and Tosen Jordan. Ms. Gold over here makes her fair complexion. It's the attitude. You can dress up in an oversized trash bag and remain cool if you carry yourself proudly enough.

Ms. Gold writes on her clipboard. "So, how do you feel about your result today?"

"Good. Winning's always nice."

She peers up at you. "Even if Rice Shower almost beat you?"

"I'm not afraid of her. She's a nice girl." You crick your neck. "Am I being graded?"

"Then I'd have upped the pace and dashed forward to shake her off, disrupting her stamina management. Or I could have slowed down and made her try to commit first in the other half. That trick is too cheap unless I can worm my way into her head, which I'm not sure I can do yet."

It's a half-lie. You think you can dominate Rice Shower with the force of your presence. You'd rather not give too much information to someone who might train one of your rivals in the future.

"So I'll content myself with my victory and ensure it won't get to my head." You tilt your neck. "Are you offering something, miss?"

Ms. Gold smiles. It's the metaphorical pull of the trigger. She whips out her clipboard, flipping to a new sheet and raising her pen. In seconds, she's sketched a breakdown of the race at the start, each participant represented by a wide polygon and a number. She draws arrows. Lots and lots of arrows. She replicates the breakdown in the other three stages: middle, middle-end and homestretch, and talks you through the places where you were strong, where you faltered, and where you just scraped by but could have improved.

It helps her voice is like crystal. Smooth, not too distracting, and not brimming with the superiority of talking down to a child. Maths homework is a most illogical torture devised by the government to oppress the student populace, yet you find yourself swept up in a comfortable, audible embrace.

"So if I measure my energy levels down to exact units, I can optimize my bursts against stayers?"

Ms. Gold nods. "Yes, because then you'll have another objective measurement than sprint times. There's a spark in her eyes, one that speaks of how immersed she is in assisting the most infamous uma of her generation. A complete stranger. You guess this is her way of proving her own worth to you, or it's how she practices her teaching skills. You're not complaining. You're learning.

A loud buzz interrupts her speech. Ms. Gold delivers you an apologetic look and turns away to pick up her phone.

"My apologies." Ms. Gold says. "I shouldn't trouble you with my personal life."

This is a woman born to a prestigious family, who willingly left its gilded halls to forge a life of her own. It's an admirable endeavour, and you can't help but ruminate on those what-ifs. "No? You're not proud of yourself, after all?" Ms. Red raises her eyebrow. "You're having second thoughts?"

"It was a joke, teach. A-a joke…"

Umamusume can shatter a human bone with a single kick. The physical discrepancy is the cause of many divides in respect in certain fields, including dealing with stubborn trainees. Why should the powerful uma listen to the human teacher, when the latter can't restrain them in any meaningful way? Yet…

[World Resonance check: 106/50 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

Smoke clogs the air. Invisible barbed wire creaks and grinds, its filaments reeking of fresh bloody iron. The dual sensations warn you that if you and her took Ms. Red in a fight, she'd eviscerate both of you, nine times out of ten. Power lies beneath that crimson suit. Lean, dense, and coiled like a wolf baring its fangs, ready to devour its prey.

The cheeky girl flinches as Ms. Red leans forward. "You did this to harass Satono Ruby. Own up to yourself."

The cheeky girl gulps.

Ms. Red scowl deepens. She side-eyes the steadily growing crowd, then pulls back and paces back and forth. "I know why you did this. I know why thought you it was a good idea. You thought it wouldn't do anything, that you'd earn your laughs and maybe disrupt Ruby in the gates. Setting aside how that's a violation of the sportsmanship conduct, did you know that since the incident you thought you understood so well, the URA enforced strict equipment checks across all races? Zero tolerance applied until much recently, and I still wouldn't push my luck. They rake over your shoes and cleats with a fine comb. They conduct these checks before the race as to not slow down the already-packed race schedule."

Ms. Red stops in front of her victim, arms folded. "Guess what happens when a participant raises their hand at the last second and goes foul."

"That's…"

He tone goes hard. "Guess."

"They waste time?"

"They waste everyone's time. You waste everyone's time. At least a dozen of your fellow contestants, who must be subjected to the emergency check to ensure fairness. The staff, who toil through the night ensuring those gates and banners are setup and now are saddled with an extra job out of nowhere. The commentators, the fans, the sponsors and the thousands of spectators, who have lives and plans and must now reallocate themselves due to the delay. And that's not getting into how gleefully the press will tear into you and your Trainer. Do now you understand how imbecilic your idea was?"

Hands slam into their sides as the back pulls itself into position. A salute flies forth.

"Y-yes ma'am. I understand one hundred percent, ma'am!" The now not-so-cheeky girl wails.

Ms. Red jerks her thumb towards the starting gates. "Get yourselves prepared for the scrimmage. And don't make a mistake like this ever again."

You take the race. It's not even close. Your bleeding heart pities your mollified opponent and you ask for a rematch. She declines, preferring to wobble off to the change rooms to presumably slide into the shower and rethink her life choices. You catch up to Ms. Red instead. She's leaning against the fence, viewing the turf's landscape with a lazy eye.

"How was my running?"

Ms. Red scoffs. Her breath smells of mint. "Nothing I haven't seen before."

You break out into a grin. "So that I'm running like my senpais and therefore on the right track?"

She glares at you, then snorts with amusement.

"Touché."

[Intimidation has increased by 2.]

>>[AdvertisingEffort] Teach Tabaru's posse how to do better in their next tryouts.

One night, you're scrolling through Umatok on your bed, the algorithm finds fit to bestow you with a human boxing match. A man with white gloves slugs his beefy opponent twice, once in the cheeks and once in the forehead. The beefy man stumbles, and that's when the white glove's man soul explodes with radiation. A fiery aura in a color you think is cyan surrounds him. He launches a flurry of punches straight into his opponent's chest, finishing in an uppercut that knocks the man down and earning him the match.

Cool, you think, and swipe to the next clip…or you would have if you hadn't paused the video to stare at the pompadour sweeping up from the boxer's head. Do people still wear those these days? You didn't see much of those in Tokyo, aside from strays at cosplay gatherings. Did the boxer style it himself, or is he friends with the best stylist in town? How should you compose yourself, if a man with such a distracting fit walked up in front of you and started a conversation? These questions swirl around in your head, before your finger takes action and closes Umatok, because the maths homework on your bed is glaring a hole through your stomach.

You don't think about Mr. Pompadour for a good long while. Then, one morning, you're eating breakfast in the cafeteria with Tabaru and her posse. They're the group you eat with the most, despite Pelte persisting in hating your guts and openly stating as such at regular intervals. Perhaps it's routine. Or, perhaps, you no longer find their antics as irritating, now that you've obtained a few small achievements under your belt. Meanwhile, Pelte bombed in her tryouts.

Why yes, being superior does feel lovely.

Jewel pops the question right as you're about to tuck into your omelette. "Hey Ruby, can you teach us not to suck?"

She's raised her hand, like a naughty student in class. The reason is obvious. Pelte hisses, shooting daggers over her fried chicken.

"Pelte…" Jewel groans.

"We talked about this."

"Don't you start. Don't be like that for a change."

Pelte slams her glass on the table. "We don't need help from her."

You pick at a cherry tomato, inspecting the fresh sheen on its surface. You mix it with a small smear of runny egg.

"She almost beat Kitasan."

"She didn't win."

"She almost beat the best rookie in the grade. And before you say it's a fluke for the millionth time, she's won other scrimmages too. Us? Fourth, sixth, fifth place! We're backup dancers. No-placers. Umas that'll settle for the group training instead of earning a Trainer of our own. That's all we'll ever amount to, if we keep acting the way we are, and you, Tomoe and I didn't work our butts off to come to Tracen and end up like that!"

Jewel doesn't fly to her feet. Her ears do pin back, and a snort suffixes her rant. Your eyes have gone slightly wide. Jewel normally goes along with whatever Pelte or Tabaru decide, so to see her this fired up is unusual. You don't dislike it, though.

Pelte's glare intensifies. She can't find her tongue. She doesn't have an argument here.

"If it's stupid, and it works, it's not stupid." Tomoe breaks the deadlock with a wet slurp of her morning ramen. She winks and mimics a gun with her free hand. "That's what the TV said last night."

Pelte glances at Tabaru—her last resort.

"I want you guys to do well, too." Tabaru says.

Game, set, match. Jewel relaxes, triumphant Pelte crashes down in her seat and simmers in silence for the rest of breakfast.

To her credit, she doesn't give in. Five in the morning, when the air's chilly and the crows caw from their nests. You and Tabaru lead the posse on a jog out of Tracen and into the city, Pelte sticking close to her boss's side. The other two girls trail behind. You lead the group through the usual haunts: main lane, park road, waterside and through the mini forest. The posse holds on through the run; they gulp down water from the public fountain as if Fuchu suddenly transformed into a desert. After a cooldown, you inform them it's time to run back in the same direction, and that's when the protesting happens.

"This is too much!"

"I can't!"

You, the organizer, receive the pleasure of laughing in their sweaty faces. "C'mon! Step it up, girls. Tabaru and I do this every day!"

"You're both monsters!" Jewel wails.

"How? It's so hard!" Tomoe whines.

Tabaru shakes her head. "Second time's the hardest."

"And then the third time's the hardest!" You add, with a thumbs up.

Tomoe and Jewel let out another groan, You pat them both on the shoulder, applying a gentle nudge in the Tracen's direction. Sorry girls, this motion says, but your bodies need that microtearing to grow up healthy and strong! By the time the group returns to the academy gates, the posse's cheeks run ruddy red, their feet tottering from the fatigue. Pelte doesn't complain. She grits her teeth and heads to the changing room without a word, shooting you a defiant glare, as if this run proved something to you. It did. The fact she's more of a fighter than you initially. You doubt telling her this would cause anything but more insults, so you keep mum and plan the next morning run.

A few more sessions, and you and Tabaru decide it's time for these girls to experience the turf. A practice run should do.

This is when Mr. Pompadour strikes.

Your ears prick up at their ends. A muffled grinding sound, that of boots sliding down across the turf. Lo-and-behold, the boxer you saw on Umatok. The shock that he's a full-fledged Trainer is overshadowed by his pompadour in living, breathing three-dimensional vision. It's so…big! And pitch black! It's a puffy alien wedge jutting out from a perfectly normal scalp. Sunshine gleams off its outer layer, life itself granting its approval—or is it a mockery? You won't call his hairdo ugly—you possess manners, after all—but you can understand why this style of hair disappeared from the fashion industry!

"Can I help you?" You ask, cautiously?

"You? You're fine. Great, even." Mr. Pompadour says. "It's your friend. I'm worried about. Hey, you!"

Pelte freezes in place. She turns her head, annoyed. "What?"

Mr. Pompadour beckons with his hand. "Get over here and show me your feet."

The immediate connotation instantly pops into everyone's head. except for Mr. Pompadour. He doesn't skip a beat.

"I'm serious. I saw you: your gait's off. Right heel. You were dragging it along the ground when you finished that last lap."

[Insight: 10/10 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

You too had noticed Pelte struggling. In fact, you were seconds from asking her yourself. You had debated passing it along to Tabaru, since Pelte doesn't appreciate you, but there was a chance Pelte would've feigned strength in front of the girl she adores. It might be better if a real authority figures takes up the mantle today.

"You can pry them from my cold dead hands, you freakin' weirdo!" Pelte exclaims

Okay then, Mr. Pompadour's frown seems to state. It was the easy way or the hard way. Guess we're doing the hard way. His eyes roll upwards in introspection. He takes a breath and his voice goes serious.

"Section six, article four of Tracen's official rules and regulations. Staff members may request a student to undergo a medical examination at any time, should that student be detected with a sufficient level of injury. Should the student have attempted to conceal said injury, disciplinary action may be taken."

"Bullcrap!" Pelte cries.

Mr. Pompadour pats his pocket. "That's a rule Tazuna herself wrote. And let me tell you, you will not appreciate blocking her path when she smells that particular blood in the water. Every Trainer in Tracen has her number. The phone's right here."

The sight before you is an adult bearing down on a child to force her to do what the adult wants—never a pleasant memory. On the other hand, Mr. Pompadour is so serious, pleading even, that your objections are quelled.

And for Pelte: that's definitely guilt worming its way through her inept composure. She can't look him or Tabaru in the eye,

"Pelte. Please." Tabaru asks.

Pelte lets out a strangled snarl. She sits down on the ground, grabs the tip of her shoe, twists her mouth, then finally pulls it off. The sock is next. Mr. Pompadour approaches. He takes her foot and gently inspects it. He brushes his index against Pelte's calf, and she winces.

"Achilles tendonitis." Mr. Pompadous states. You crowd around with the rest of the girl and notice a swollen strip of flesh across the heel and the tibia. The intersecting lines bulge obscenely. "How long have you had this?"

Pelte doesn't respond.

"How. Long." Tabaru interjects.

"Boss—"

"You said—you promised. You promised! We both know what happened to Traffic back home!" Tabaru's voice goes strained. It rises in volume. "How long, Pelte? Answer me!"

"It's nothing, damn it!" Pelte leaps to her feet, stumbling as the swollen flesh compresses. She tilts to the side and barely regains her balance. "I'll push through it like I've always done!"

"No." Mr. Pompadour advances, waving his finger. "You are going to the infirmary, right now, if you want any hope of running this year."

Pelte turns around to flee. Mr. Pompadour kicks off his feet, closing the gap and landing in front of her. She side-steps, he follows. He encroaches in your space, using the watching group and the rule of physical harm against staff to box Pelte in, where she can't escape. That technique doesn't count for Pelte's patience, or lackthereof. She shoves her palms forward—a move that causes you to flare with shock, since that alone can fracture a human spine on impact, or at the very least deliver nasty bruising.

Mr. Pompadour raises his hands. He doesn't catch Pelte's shove. He strikes with his palms at Pelte's wrist, redirecting the blow and dissipating its energy away from him. No sign of panic flashes across him. Pelte, shocked at first, snarls and pulls back her fist, only for someone to rush behind her and haul her by the shoulders.

"You can't do that."

The first thing you see of this new human is her wide, black and white skirt. A maid's dress, you think with utter confusion.

"You can't do that, miss. You'll get expelled if you hurt a Trainer!"

It's yet another Trainer. Petite, twintails the color of swamps and marshes, and…nail-shaped ornaments holding her hair up in lieu of bows? Yet, raw strength flows through these seemingly fragile musculature. Her hands and arms restrain Pelte, her lithe frame twisting back and forth below to avoid her kicks. This is a feat comparable to Mr. Muscles, yet she's pulling it off without injury. It's unnerving.

"Let go of me!"

"I heard everything from up here. Achilles tendonitis. Tendonitis. It'll cause tearing. A rupture. The back of your foot will practically collapse. And then you won't be able to walk without a cane!" Maid Green screeches out a pained wail. She shakes her head back and forth.

[World Resonance check: 106/50 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

Mania, orchestrated by a violin and a network of screeching, serrated blades, pours out of her. They are ceaseless. Her eyes are wide with terror. The hairs on your tail stiffen.

"W-we have to take you to the hospital!"

"Wait!" Mr. Pompadour raises his hands, waving them. Clearly, these two are acquainted each other. "Don't—"

It's too late. Maid Green has scooped Pelte up in her arms, bridal style, and is now a rapidly shrinking dust cloud vanishing into the horizon. Pelte's screams fade into the distance. Mr. Pompadour gawps, then runs a hand down his face.

"Uh. Um." He stutters. "Let's follow her."

The staff on duty, one Dr. Junko, puts Pelte on full blast for leaving such an important injury uncared for this long. The diagnosis is as Mr. Pompadour and Maid Green feared: achilles tendonitis. Dr. Junko assigns her with two months worth of rest with weekly checkups, then writes her passes for her to take it easy at gym class.

Somewhere inside your head, you feel as if you should be relishing in schadenfreude. You're not. There's a painful squeeze in your chest, as if your heart is smothered beneath a thick blanket.

"You did all you could."

It's Mr. Pompadour speaking to you, from his place leaning against the wall. His chest looks far more broad, when he's posing with his legs crossed like this. This is outside the infirmary. You and the rest are here and to give Pelte, Tabaru and the doctor privacy. Tabaru insisted on staying. Jewel and Tomoe are lost in their own conversation; both looked crushed by Pelte's injury.

"How do you know?" You ask.

"Nase wouldn't let one of her trainees wander around without a rigorous lesson on common injuries. Word on the street is that you're a more responsible girl than first impressions mentioned, too." Mr. Pompadour gestures towards the infirmary door. "You told that Pelte girl the usual checks, right?"

To not exercise under injury, and to report any injury that does occur. "Yeah. I did."

"Might sound harsh, but it's her fault for neglecting herself. Some girls are stubborn like that. They believe training is a video game, where more they train, the more results they'll earn, ignorant of how the body can break down through overuse. I ran into those types when I boxed in uni, too." Mr. Pompadour claps you on the shoulder. "So, it's not your fault. Chin up."

You nod, glumly. "I still wish I could've done more."

He examines you for a moment. "Want to check out the library, then? I'll show you some good books on sport injuries."

You look up at him…

[World Resonance check: 106/50 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

And detect a core overflowing with light, its foundations more solid than steel. The cords and arteries that wrap around it are ripe with vitality.

"I'd like that."

[Brawl has increased by 2.]

The final Trainer you encounter, as a result of your redoubled search efforts, arrives out of nowhere. A notification is pinged to your phone, requesting your attendance at the pool on the day after Pelte is sent to the infirmary. Instead of a swimming instructor to patch up what must be your poor swimming skills, you instead receive another maid.

"My partner gave you trouble yesterday." Black-haired, the hue of a classic Japanese human beauty, with a pierced tongue. She chews on a gummy bear and swallows it with a gulp. "Sorry about that."

"Partner?"

"Apologies, apologies, my sincerest apologies!" Maid Green bows her head rapidly, reminding you of those drinking bird toys from an antique toy boutique deep in Shibuya. She and Maid Black are the youngest-presenting Trainers you've met. They seem like they're barely over the minimum age requirement.

"We're a tag team. Two brains in one. As for this…" Maid Black gestures to the swimming pool. A few lanes are unoccupied. "It's a freebie. Orders came down from above. You girls go into the pool much?"

She means Tabaru, Jewel and Tomoe, who were also invited.

"No?" Jewel says.

"Figures. Well, that's why I'm here. Let's get changed."

You switch out of your Tracen uniform and slip into the standard blue Tracen swimsuit, still confused as to purpose of this swimming lesson. This becomes clear as soon as you touch the water. Hesitation. The old enemy. You're not afraid of swimming, but it'd be a lie to say you're good at it. The shrine didn't let you, FAITHFUl either lacked time or the resources to organized a swimming trip, and you only used the public pool for a week to train yourself in order to pass Tracen's entrance exam.

The water surrounds you, cold licks lapping at your naked skin. A shiver courses through your body. At the far end of the lane, surrounded by bobbing plastic chains, the deep end awaits, its mass absorbing the luminescence of the overhead lights…

[Composure check: 76/50: +5 EXP.]

But you manage to bear with it and grin. The staff won't stand by and let you drown.

You dive forward into the water and perform a few freestyle laps. Small plumes of whitish water splash up as your arms lift up and down. Your legs kick wet splashes. Water resistance grips you at every pull, forcing you to strain your chest, shoulder and core. Right. You forgot how tiring this is.

A hand rests gently on your head, guiding you to a halt. You bob your head out of the water, gasping, to see Maid Black, clad in a matching swimsuit, floating beside you.

"How often have you swam?" She asks.

"Not often." You reply. "Never had the chance on the holidays."

Something soft flickers through her gaze. She beckons you over to the adjacent lane, passing beneath the plastic chains. You follow. Together, the two of you are alone.

"I'll give you a crash course on the three main styles. Freestyle, breaststroke and butterfly. They'll train your stamina and your strength. How's that sound?"

You cannot detect any dissatisfaction nor mockery. You nod.

Maid Black demonstrates the three swimming styles. Replicating them, however, is far from easy. A crooked arm here, a wrong angle there. It is the learning pains of translating theory into motion, a task that would be so much easier if you possess a bird's-eye view of yourself. The butterfly stroke is the worst. Synchronizing the kick and the arm the recovery threatens to twist your submerged head into knots. Maid Black swims by your side, never losing her temper, offering encouragement…

"You've got this…yeah, lift your hands just liiike that—fantastic. Brilliant of you. You totally rocked this, Ruby."

…beyond what she intended to do, even.

"T-time's up."

"Tell them I'm not done here. Five more minutes, alright? Ruby's almost got the breaststroke correct."

Maid Green bows and retreats without complaint.

"Fantastic job." Maid Black says, as you lift your head out of the water. "You've got the basics down. The rest's up to you."

She's not an excitable person. A woman of few words, half of them probably snarky and scathing, if your experience with Hotaru is any indication. Yet, the look she's wearing fills you with a warm swell in your chest. It's pride. She's genuinely pleased you succeeded.

"Thanks." You mean that too. Your cheeks also go warm, though that might be your body compensating for the cold air.

"No problemo. You've got talent." Maid Black shakes her head, water droplets flying from her hair. Elegant strands cling to her immaculate skin. "Too bad the URA doesn't offer swimming championships."

The words blurt from your mouth before you can stop them. "Wanna race?"

She stares at you, then breaks out into a wider, toothier grin. You both line up at opposite ends and kick off when Maid Green blows the whistle. Immediately, Maid Black launches into a vigorous butterfly, her finesse practically melting her legs and arms into the water. You follow with freestyle. You possess your innate natural umamusume strength, but Maid Black's got the finesse and optimization. You catch a flash of her face as you cross paths, and she's smiling wide, elation coursing through her…

[World Resonance check: 106/50 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

…her soul soaring, flying, lively and free as a dolphin in the wide, wide sea.

"You're so fast!"

"Eh, you'll get better. You are just a beginner." Outside the pool, shortly after changing back into regular clothes, Maid Black hands you a box of jellybeans. You take it. Lemon flavored.

"Give it a year and I'll be lagging behind your tail."

It's a fun picture to imagine. "Should I invest in swimming more?"

Maid Black shrugs. "If it fits you. It's great for training your core. Not so much for your glutes or feet. You're running on ground, not through water—remember that. But if you want to bolster your endurance, hop into the pool."

She chews through another jelly bean. "Gotta say, I'm grateful you didn't freak out like some of the other kids."

You smirk. "Like Oguri?"

"Like her. I'm called in as a consultant whenever trainees don't behave in the pool. When they begrudgingly get in, they drag their feet. Sometimes literally. You behaving yourself puts you in my good books."

"So…" You look down at your dress. "You're wearing that…"

"I've got nothing to do with Akiko." Maid Black says.

Straight and to the point.

"I see…"

She shrugs. "We get asked that a lot. Understandable, but you gotta understand: she doesn't have a monopoly on our uniform. We originate from two completely different households."

Your tail swishes and halts. "Households?"

"Not the Symbolis, nor the Mejiros; my buddy and I do work for our own master. He's the affluent kind. And in the interest of fairness and good sportsmanship…" Maid Black grabs the last handful and tosses the jellybean box into a nearby bin. "He used to be pals with your ex-family."

The key word being used.

[Breathing has increased by 2.]

[Total EXP Gained: 70.]

4.2: A Damn Daring Decision

Morning, June 22st, 20XX

"Feeling pensive today?"

A normal Tracen student would have fallen out of their skin in fright at the presence of a living ghost hovering less than a meter in front of her. For you, it's another Monday.

"That's a word, alright, Senpai. Melancholy is another."

"My, you are perturbed."

The usage of that word sounds familiar. You're not certain why.

It's the afternoon again. The horizon intersects the sun's rays, draping a swathe of fiery red and glowing orange gradients across the path leading through Tracen's grounds. Around you are students fidgeting with their schoolbags, distant chatters of gossip, the smell of fried carrot treats and soda—you couldn't care less. You wouldn't care if some random uma poked her nose in your voice and asked why you're mumbling to the patch of air beside you. Something else occupies your mind.

"Want to talk about it? Or shall we reserve it for our nightly 'direct messaging'?" Your illustrious and mysterious senpai walks alongside you. She flashes you a coquettish grin.

You snort in response. DMs. With Plain Jane's beat-up typewriter. Sure. Plain Jane once described the implement, and you felt your skin flaking and drying from the first internal image of its antique gears and keys. Neither autocorrect nor auto-annotations function exists on that device—you don't understand how she copes with it.

The thought of Plain Jane hunched over in her desk, tapping away, inspires a small wisp of a grin, but only for a second. The clouds of gloom coat the sky once more. You resume walking, staring at nothing in particular.

"Well," You mumble, as a flock of pigeons soars off in the distance. "I did the best I could."

"With the Trainer Hunt?" Plain Jane asks,

"Ee-yup."

"You sound sure about it." Plain Jane responds.

"I'm not sure if you're sure that I'm sure about it."

"My predictions are usually eighty percent accurate. For you, ninety or more."

"Wow, stalking much?"

"More akin to the observation of common behaviors. You are not the only troubled girl to walk through Tracen's gardens on a lonely afternoon, Ruby. And you won't be the last. Though, from what I've seen during my morning walks, you've made a fine effort."

You give a noncommittal bump with your shoulder. A shrug and a sign of muted annoyance. Plain Jane's ghostly form cannot be harmed—you saw a stray baseball go through her face once—but she dodges out of the way, smiling.

The garden opens onto tarmac. A vending machine thrums at the bend. Evil diet soda, orange juice, a new drink that promises heavy electrolytes, and plain old water. Your hands flirt with one of the buttons, then drift off.

"The stage's packed up. The scrimmages were tallied. Pelte's in temporary rest, Tabaru's gone quiet in our room, and Jewel and Tomoe are exercising better by themselves. They're twice as confident now." You state. "That's a good thing, but it means I'm no longer needed as much. And the Trainers…"

"They haven't contacted you."

"Not yet."

"It's only been a couple of days since the end of your recruitment drive, if I remember correctly."

"Three of them. Yeah."

"And not a peep?"

"No."

"I see…"

Now that's a pensive statement from your senpai. There's a dip in her lip, which would be a frown on any normal uma.

Mr. Orange-Shirt, Mr. Muscles, Ms. Gold, Ms. Red, Mr. Pompadour and Maid Black & Maid Green. None of these so-called interested Trainers followed up on you. You saw them around campus, some of them waving or nodding at you in polite greeting, but nothing else. No paperwork was placed in your lap; no pens were offered for you to sign. For intents and purposes, you have returned to where you started.

Okay, that's not accurate. You learned a few extra dance moves. You honed your racing skills through scrimmages while also learning how your rivals ticked. You even built rapport with some. Kawakami Princess, the other day, had a fun chat with you about Prifight Season III vs IV. These accomplishments aren't nothing, but you wish you had spent some of those two weeks under the tutelage of a professional.

Meanwhile, your rivals: Mihono Bourbon, Kawakami Princess, Kitasan Black, Satono Diamond and more; they've reaped the benefits of having their own Trainers. They accelerated while you jogged. The last pair of names stings your heart something loathsome. Is it any wonder that you're feeling down?

Still, it could be worse. The example presents itself as you amble towards the training grounds. You spy the Special Week and the other girls, their visages tiny in your view like little dolls. Their heads bob up and down as they perform their laps. Trainer Okino yells commands from the starting line, his firm voice echoing across the grass. Beyond him, a lone figure sits on a wooden bench. Tokai Teio. It can't be any other uma else. Crutches lay by the side of her bench, and you notice she's lifting a dumbbell in her arms.

You can't see her face from up near the bleachers, but you suspect it's as subdued as yours. The eyes see, the mouth speaks, and the brain registers little except for the absolute necessities.

"Okino's telling her to visualise the races in her head. Image training. It's best executed alongside the flow of an uma's body for maximum effectiveness. In her state, it's better than nothing."

"Isn't that giving her false hope?" You ask.

"Perhaps. But it could lead to something greater." You shoot her a surprised look, so she elaborates. "Trainers of his caliber didn't reach his place by not taking risks. At the very least, it's a task to take her mind off her injury."

She sounds vaguely fond of Trainer Okino, as if he were her trainee from long ago. It's a sentiment you should agree with. You've held similar feelings when you were struggling through early mornings and late nights, squeezing every last drop of training time between your underground umadol duties. The passion that fed and drove you through those times feels distant. Hollow, even. Your brain isn't secreting the chemicals you wish it was, and Teio's predicament now seems cruel.

You walk away. It's rude to observe another team's training without permission. Instead, you head towards another section of the grounds, where you sit down, lie back, and let your ears drink in the greenery.

Plain Jane's head pops into view.

You wave your hands languidly. "Yeah, yeah, I know I'm being a grouch. Give me a day and a bottle of carrot juice and I'll be back to peppy, life-loving Ruby."

"I forgive you." Plain Jane states.

"I forgive you for being cryptic as always, too, senpai. Anything happen with the Nightmare recently?"

"No. And thank goodness for that."

"Okay. That's good to hear." You pluck a blade of grass and sniff it. You used to fiddle with the fields back at the shrine, in a small clearing in the nearby forest, where the adults had a hard time reaching—for a while, at least. The memory dips your mood further, and you bask in those ugly feelings, frowning harder.

"Can I ask a question?"

Plain Jane sits cross-legged down next to you. "You may."

"I know…" You inhale the cool air. "I know the adults don't like having me around because of Mom. But sometimes I still think about the Trainers who initially wanted to sign me up, but chickened out. Can you tell me what exactly goes through their heads when they think about me? What's the step by step?"

She hums as she thinks. "The laconic verison is that those men and women are afraid of how you might transform their comfortable, stable lives."

"Like, because of the Satonos?"

"Their fingers in finance, their arms manipulating the laws. Journalists, endless questions, harassment from riled-up fans of Semi Sonic and Cotton Sphere, and finally those who will attack because their own lives are sliding downhill; so, for no important reason at all. You're already aware of this, I assume. Yet, life is a snowstorm for the adults, Ruby. A harsh, bitter gust of wind through cold fields of grey. The adults erect their cabins, storing their heaters, cooking pots, a pantry of fine meats and cheeses, warm beds and blankets. All of these were accumulated through personal trial and suffering. They're not perfect—none of their neigbours' tools are, either—and sometimes insects burrow through and need to be squished, but they provide enough comfort for them to weather out the storm. Should a stranger be invited in, possessing the chance of disrupting that balance—" Plain Jane gazes towards Tracen's main building. Her smile has vanished. "They will shake their heads and gently, politely, bid them farewell. They will pull out their shotguns if the stranger does not comply.

"That violent?"

"It's a metaphor."

"Am I that intrusive?"

"Those Trainers have family members and friends to think about."

[Persuasion check: 111/90-> Success! +5 EXP.]

"That doesn't make sense." You say.

Plain Jane blinks. "What doesn't?"

"You say it like they're moaning and groaning inside their little houses while the rest of society is messed up. But that's not the case at all. Tracen is nationals. The Trainers who make it in are the best in Japan, probably the world as well! They gotta study for years and years, and some of them come from alright families. Even the ones like Trainer Kitahara back when he was just starting with Oguri Cap weren't bad off, either. I didn't grow up in those kinds of environments. I was kidnapped from my family, raised in the boonies, then lived below the poverty line when I fled to Shibuya. I was wiping dishes at midnight for food and bunk while those Trainers were watching TV back home, drinking sake and eating fresh rice every evening! Practically paradise compared to me!"

A weight swells in your chest. It is utterly unpleasant. You're upright again, clenching your fists. "So what if the paparazzi annoy them? News flies fast. Everyone cried about Tokai Teio and now they've moved on. And so what if the Satonos pick a fight with us? They have to obey the URA and Director Akikawa or whatever. They're not unstoppable—look at how they failed to stop me from entering. Fact is, those Trainers have more than enough room to share my burden. It's the moral thing for them to do!"

Your rant soars forth, like a great aerial machine taking flight. It rings out, fades, echoes and you suddenly jolt up, glancing left and right to check if anyone caught you.

No-one's present. It's only the wind, the grass, and your mysterious senpai. Relief. You slump back down, sighing. A tingle pulses on your index and middle fingers. Plain Jane is brushing her fingers beneath yours. They interlock, in the wake of your lack of resistance.

"The burden of one ends up as the burden upon many, more often than not. Those Trainers are frightened for their friends and family." She says.

You don't answer. You don't wish to acknowledge her point.

"Imagine if your idol group picked up a member who threatened to bring scandal towards your office's doorstep every week. Would your manager not hesitate?"

"That's where you're wrong, senpai. The underground is different. The girls who were ostracized from the aboveground come down and find shelter with us. That new member would have to be truly toxic to be pushed out." You pull your knees up to your chest, shaking your head. "I'm not that girl. I know I'm not. They're the ones who missed out, not me."

"Those who only capture the bottom of a well cannot comprehend the depths of the ocean. We are all afraid of losing what we have." Plain Jane says, softly. Her grip toughens. There's a quiet despondency lurking in the touch, a sympathy and a pity for you. "It is their own folly. You need not accept it, only understand it."

You curl up harder, unable to stop your teeth gritting. This isn't like you, you know. This isn't the fresh-faced, eager-minded prospective trainee who presented herself so fervently toward those six Trainers. You get it: signing on any trainee is hard work. It involves enough paperwork and red tape to choke an elephant to death. You were never going to be that mythical uma who meets her Trainer on a fateful encounter. That's simply not how real life works. You still wish they'd move a tad faster. At least they should send you a letter if they're disinterested in boarding you on.

Frustration. That's what these emotions are. And illogical; here arrive the brigade of standard platitudes—it is what it is, and what happens falls, et cetera, et cetera. Shut up, you bite back in your head. Listen to my cawing heart for once. Look at yourself. You struggled so hard to reach the same level as your peers, and now they're gaining ahead again. Entering Tracen was but the first step of your lifelong dream. You don't want to wake up before dawn breaks. And so you slipped back into your umadol persona and thrusting hope, love, and optimism forward with the zeal of a Triple Crowner whilst keeping your reservations in the backline. And it's over. The curtain has fallen; the props are packed up, and those bastards have crawled out from the shadows to whisper their hate-filled filth into your virgin ears. It sucks. So, terribly awfully. Why can't this side of your brain leave you the hell alone?

[Mood has fallen to Normal.]

Plain Jane approaches closer. She hugs you from behind, rubbing gentle circles on your back, then kneading your shoulders. A note of tension eases off your chest.

"You won't be waiting long, Ruby. Efforts like yours don't go unnoticed." Plain Jane says from behind you. "Call it a hunch."

You look over your shoulder. "I thought you said you weren't allowed to give me hints?"

"From my vast repertoire of racing history knowledge and acumen, correct. I maintain my previous statement. The day I sign up as a Trainer is the day I pull out the stopgaps from beneath the URA and send it tumbling into the pits of oblivion. But, tips to guide my kouhai on the right track…" Plain Jane lifts a finger to her mouth in imitation of a shush. "Those are perfectly acceptable."

You snort.

"And…"

"And?"

"I simply believe in you."

You look at her. She smiles back. Seconds pass, and something wet gathers in your eyes. You rub it before it trickles out.

"That's not fair, senpai…"

[Total EXP Gained: 5.]

EXP: 155/200.

"Good evenin', Your Grace. You're sounding sprightly tonight—what's that? That old codger picked up on my plans? Ha! He's still hovering over us. Tell him that if I couldn't handle of a girl that infamous—yeah, even after a break—I wouldn't be much of a Trainer, would I?"

"Ooooh….uuurgghhhh…my heart is aflame. My soul roars with triumph. This is the moment of inspiration I've been waiting for. I must go posthaste!"

"Please step aside. There is a young lady out there I must meet. Oh, very well, since you insist—here: my CV. As you'll note from my several reputable career choices, I am more than qualified to take her on."

"…Tch, that cheek on her…she's just like her damn mother. Not that it's a dealbreaker...I'm off, then."

"Mmm…yeah. This is great. G-R-E-A-T! Yosh, I've totally got this in the bag!"

"… Understood, sir. Have a wonderful night… Give our kindest regards to the young mistress too…oi. Partner. Partner! You hear that? Master has granted us his blessing. Let's get moving."

"O-okay!"

Notes:

All Trainers are at least eighteen years of age. The minimum Attribute value a Tracen Trainer is allowed to possess: 9. Most will enter Tracen with an total of 40 across all their Attributes. Established trainers have at least 55. Training Specialties boost the rate at which the mentioned Attributes/skills increase. Assume this is the same for all listed Trainers. Proximity Bonuses activate when you are nearby your Trainer (and deactivate if you're not). They can be upgraded later on. Assume both male and female Trainers will treat you with equal amounts of respect. Trainers that are not chosen may reappear elsewhere in the story. An umamusume's Psyche can be compared to a Trainer's Psyche.

The Bloodhound

This Trainer is the proud protégé of another Trainer, who was so prideful and nefarious, her wrath rivalled the war goddesses of yore. Her attitude has rubbed off on this man; you may discover him parrying insinuations with a sharp tongue, or engaging in unexpected close-quarters confrontations (at your benefit, of course). He also tends to open up in the company of a good drink. Don't think for a second he is neither diligent nor resilient, however. This is a man who has travelled the world seeking out the best international circuits, and has won and lost in equal, glorious measures.

Age Bracket: Middle-aged

Nationality: Foreigner

Photo: Angled to the side somewhat; he's flashing a smirk and a wink.

Attributes: 12 INT, 13 PSY, 15 FYS, 16 GUI

Training Specialties:

Attributes: Speed, Stamina, Power Skills: Frenzy, Pain Threshold, Traversal, Subterfuge, Swordplay, Foreign Languages Proximity Bonus: +1 to Wits and Insight.

The Modern Strongman

You'd be forgiven for assuming this Trainer was a Greek sculpture that animated itself to life. Unlike cold, hard marble, this Trainer possesses no shortage of gusto. Indeed, you may stumble across him declaring statements such as 'muscles are an ode from God himself', followed by him tearing off his shirt and engaging his peers in a flexing competition. Such acts may be cause for second-hand embarrassment, but at least he means well. You should not underestimate his keen insight into the human, or umamusume, physique, either.

Age Bracket: Middle-aged

Nationality: Japanese (well-traveled)

Photo: Sparkles radiate off his eyebrows. Somehow.

Attributes: 11 INT, 14 PSY, 19 FYS, 12 GUI

Training Specialties:

Attributes: Stamina, Power, Guts Skills: Nutrition, Pain Threshold, Breathing, Composure, Persuasion, History Proximity Bonus: If Mood is negative, +1 to Mood (only once per meeting.)

The Honored Daughter

A refined lady from an affluent family. You'd think she'd delve into economics, politics, or at the very least arrange a marriage with some oil baron's son. But, we suppose escaping death by a hair will bolster anyone's drive for life. Polite, assertive and generous; what she lacks in experience, she compensates with a powerful, analytical mind—just ask the trail of bodies she's left behind in airsoft. Don't expect her to lean on her family's assets unless a terrible crisis falls into her lap.

Age Bracket: Young

Nationality: Japanese

Photo: A composed smile to the camera. The only piece of jewelry is the brooch in her hair. No makeup.

Attributes: 16 INT, 15 PSY, 13 FYS, 12 GUI

Training Specialties:

Attributes: Speed, Psyche, Wits Skills: Racing Tactics, Nutrition, Frenzy, Logic, Visual Mathematics, Hand-Eye Coordination Proximity Bonus: Bonus EXP range for Intellectual & Social skill checks increases from 0-10 to 0-20.

The Lady Scourge

Director Akikawa's madness manifests yet again with her recruitment of this Trainer, a former war hero from the frontlines of ████████ and ███████████████. She will serve as an excellent disciplinarian and advisor for your racing career, as long as you can tolerate a fierce, no-nonsense attitude. Indeed, slacking off or talking back without a sufficient reason may prove to be the worst mistake of your life. On the flipside, this Trainer will not tolerate bullshit from your opposition either; for pack is pack, and the pack will be protected.

Age Bracket: Middle-Aged

Nationality: Japanese (well-traveled)

Photo: A neutral expression.

Attributes: 12 INT, 13 PSY, 17 FYS, 14 GUI

Training Specialties:

Attributes: Speed, Power, Insight Skills: Racing Tactics, Pain Threshold, Frenzy, Acceleration, Intimidation, Swordplay Proximity Bonus: x1.5 to Intimidate (Max 100 from this effect).

The Ex-Delinquent

This Trainer and his punkish sense of fashion are indeed outwardly alarming. Fear not: with his compassionate heart, bevy of stories from his boxing career, and a humble countryside background, he's among the easiest to strike a chord with. He also left a top-class medical school to join Tracen, so feel free to take advantage of his medical expertise too. Do note his emotional core isn't as mature as his peers. There exist rumors about sudden explosions of wrath during his youth—though we're unsure as to their triggers at present.

Age Bracket: Young

Nationality: Japanese

Photo: He's combing his pompadour with one hand while cupping his chin with the other.

Attributes: 13 INT, 16 PSY, 14 FYS, 13 GUI

Training Specialties:

Attributes: Speed, Power, Wits Skills: Pain Threshold, Frenzy, Dodge, Brawl, Artistry, Instinct Proximity Bonus: +6 to all Esoteric skills.

The Dual Maids

"So…we're maidservants. We work for our Master. Full details are private, but his family tree's available for public viewing, if that's what you care about. And don't worry—Director Akikawa is okay with us here."

"W-we passed the entrance exams with flying colors. And we're conscientious and attentive, too!"

"If we couldn't do that much, we'd be out on our butts. As for our strengths, my partner here's the brawn. I'm the brains. For a given definition of that, anyway."

"You shouldn't talk down to yourself…"

"Hey, I'm keeping it real. I'm not the smartest, nor are you the sturdiest. But, as the old saying goes, two heads are better than one. When one of us falters in an area, the other substitutes in to pick up the slack, and that means we're worth it."

"S-sometimes one of us might be called back to estate for domestic duties, which can last for a few days or weeks..."

"Or a month, if it's a major pain in the ass..."

"But we do leave notes for each other! And I'm good at finding extra help. We sincerely apologise in advance for any trouble our absences cause!"
