4.3: Grit & Void

EXP: 155/200.

Mood: Normal.

Morning, June 23rd, 20XX

An umadol is a shining, stellar supernova dressed in fancy ribbons and colorful, make-believe silks on stage, and a bundle of nerves a manager's slack awareness from biting her fingernails and ruining the next handshake setup when off. It happens in competition's twilight, that razor-wire taut counting of the seconds leading up to the announcement of the results; where the group sits in the chairs in their little VIP area and thinks with sweaty palms and trembling knees about the what-ifs and what-could've-beans. They anticipate the screech of victory, of despair, in the pit behind the curtains.

You are not a fingernail biter. More of a tail swisher mixed with an ear retreater, yet life at Tracen has yet to detach you from that identity, so you gladly mire yourself in what can only be described as a mood. After your rant towards Senpai, the consternation shows. Mild frowns. Pointed glares. The teacher calls you up to the front, where you proceed to grab the marker and attack it with a memorized math equation. Aston Machan pops in front of you during the break and asks if you are okay—of course you are. Your lungs are breathing and your belly is full, so why wouldn't you be?

This does not convince your friend, who offers to buy you ice-cream. You don't turn it down. It helps. But only a little.

There's a spiteful pleasure in swimming in your own bad mood, splashing droplets into passersby's faces. Deeper still, when you understand the circumstances behind the opposition's logic. Adults looking out for themselves and their immediate circle: what an unambiguous truth! Did Manager Suzuki not ditch nights out with the girls to take care of his kids? Are most world politicians not repugnant because they cannot bear the thought of parting with their tenth luxury mansion? You can't say you'd risk your mother's shoes for a stranger on the street, at least not without buying each other boba tea and listening to their sob story first.

On the other tail, please kindly shut the expletive up, dear ego. You are the victim here. Children are born to be assisted by adults. You will not budge on the theory that most Tracen Trainers have more than enough financial cushion and brainpower to support you. They're just being cowards. They're fighting against the laws of nature. It is wrong, right, wrong, and so you are so pissed off!

"Excuse me. Miss Ruby? Apologies for interrupting you from…what it is that you are doing, but may I have a moment of your time?"

You unfold your arms and take Ms. Gold's laminated print-out, your cheeks burning as hot as home ec's hot plate in contrast to her bright smile.

It's only after exchanging a few pleasantries and after she leaves that you glance down at the print-out. Name, address, phone number, and title. Beneath it: work experience, licenses, skills, certifications. It's a resume. And attached to the back is a letter addressed to you. You read halfway through it, idly admiring how neat and curvy Ms. Gold writes her Japanese, then go about your lunch in the school courtyard, before the truth batters you in the face so hard you see dots.

It's an offer. From a Trainer. Addressed to you.

What?

What the?

What in the…something?

Is this real? Is this happening? Yes, the resume lodged under your hand says, this is real. Look, there are fellow umas gazing jealously at the resume. That's evidence. This is your life now.

[Mood has increased to Good.]

"…huh, so Mifune beat us to the punch. Well, nothing we can do about that. Here's our lot. They'll speak for themselves. Meeting date's on there too—you got that? Alright, peace."

"Yo. Hey, nice reflexes. Seems like you're getting popular. There room on that stack for one more?"

"Your mom was a reckless weirdo whose antics drove my old squad into a laughing fit. One of them tipped his head back and avoided a bullet aimed at his neck. This isn't me repaying her on whatever. Get on board with me. I'll train you into a champion."

"Your Miss Ruby. I—please don't turn tail and run. Please listen to me. I was simply so moved by the display of pure effort and courage you displayed when you put yourself out there after school hours. Your song reached us as far as the entrance to our favorite haunt, and it made this old heart of mine beat faster again. It's exactly the type of resoluteness any aspiring champion needs. Please take this and consider my assistance for your journey through the Twinkle Series!"

"Ah, geez, I knew I should've printed these earlier. Better late than never. Good luck with choosing one of us!"

One by one, they approach you in broad daylight.

[Sneak check: 53/100 -> Failure.]

One by one, you are left stunned at the papers they leave behind in your hands.

Once the last bell rings, you wander back to your dorm room, whereupon you slump face-up onto your nice, comfortable bed.

Six. Six resumes and cover letters from the Trainers Six. It sounds like the bad first draft of an uma-cosplaying band, or a terrible romantic historical comedy where six handsome guys fight over some inexplicably pretty girl who possesses an attention span shorter than a flea's. Except, you're not that dumb, there are women in this mix, resumes aren't within the same solar system as the idea of romance, and the mere fact you're comparing your predicament to those rolling Korean comics is yet another sign of your mental inaptitude!

You muffle your ears in your pillow. So much for adults not giving you chances, eh? It's a good thing Tabaru isn't around in your room, because she might have mistaken you for a clown.

Punch the pillow. Let your adolescent indignity take control.

When Kaede talked about mavericks, you imagined some eternally-grinning loon in a lab coat or a bulletproof vest. An entirely unreasonable image, since Tracen does enforce a dress code for its Trainers, but Kaede was the one who started the conversations about movies. And, at the very least, you expected those mavericks as never having won a good race due to their eccentricities, but they retained their tough guts and spirits, and all that lovely underdog spirit. Not established Trainers with at least one G1 champion in their care!

[Logic check: 88/30 -> Success! Trivial: +0 EXP.]

No, wait. It makes total sense. Only G1-level Trainers have the gall to thumb their noses at the entire URA by training the daughter of the worst uma in the business. There's a cute notoriety in raising the worst to be the best, and you know full well with your level of perseverance and innate talent (one hundred percent true and you will take no arguments), you'd easily snowball an avalanche through the URA, burying hecklers and reporters in your path. That must be it! The Six are hiding their true madness behind their polite words and copyprinted essays. They want a challenge, a chance to prove themselves, and a needle to prick those prisses in the casting booths together at once!

Thinking of them like that, it's comfortable to slot them into the mold of yet another manipulative grown-up, and yet…

[(Psyche check: 10/6) || (Subterfuge: 75/35 -> Trivial: +0 EXP.]

You couldn't detect any ill intention from them. They were trying to recruit you, sure, but their help was sincere. Not many producers or scouts in the underground go to that lengths.

They truly do want you.

A lump falls in your throat. It doesn't go away despite a gulp of air.

You're stuck again. The billion-yen question keeps ringing the hotline. Who's on the up? Who's the lucky soul privileged enough to take Satono Ruby to the Triple Crown and beyond?

You don't know.

You ask yourself the question again, hoping the answer will spring out of thin air. It doesn't.

You don't know.

You don't know. Seriously, you don't know, and it's so irritating! Mr. Orange Shirt trained the weirdass princess that defeated Air Groove. Mr. Muscles looks to be a barrel of laughs and warm hugs who'd come running any time you felt down, and he's strong enough to mimic his own trainees' exercises. Ms. Gold and her five friends destroyed their local airsoft scene; she then took the tactics from those victories and helped a complete dropout take a crown. Ms. Red is a war machine in human form who you assume could tussle with Hishi Akebono herself and win. Mr. Pompadour is the youngest, whom you could quickly build rapport, and he's super knowledgeable about how to treat injury and stress. And the two Maids come as two Trainers in one! So what if Maid Black said she and her friend needed to go back home to scrub the floors every once in a while? There's two of them! That's, like, a super broken secret tech that lets you play two mahjong tiles at once!

…maybe the Director will take pity on your soul and allow you to contract with all of the Six?

[Logic check: 88/5 -> Success! Trivial: +0 EXP.]

No? Okay…

You stare at the ceiling. You count the idly floating dust particles and feel jealous of how carefree and brainless they are in the air, while you're down on the ground trapped against the daytime equivalent of sleep paralysis. A thought occurs to you as three particles clump together. Should you ask your friends? Get Grass or Digital on board? You get as far as picking up your phone and tapping LANE before giving an internal shake of the head. None of your friends have met the Six. Any advice they might provide will be superficial and thus useless.

You suddenly feel an additional heaping of sympathy for your old manager. This must be what he felt when he decided during auditions.

You know what he'd say if he were here with you.

"Get up, Ruby. The city lights dim without you."

Rising from your bed, you slap your cheeks and feel the nerves sting. You climb out of bed and head over to your desk. Pen, paper, a quick twirl to warm up your fingers. You grab the resumes and copy a summary of Ms. Gold's. Forget your natural apprehension towards anything adult—you'll imagine them as a series of lines, numbers, and charts first. You then scribble your immediate imagining of how she'll take you past your debut to the first graded race, using your knowledge of standard URA trends and your own evaluation of yourself. It's imperfect and messy…

[(Wits check: 10/8) || (Artistry check: 58/75) -> Success! +5 EXP.]

Yet you manage to string a thread of understanding through it. This theoretical Ms. Gold does ensure a satisfactory Twinkle Series career.

You repeat the process for the other Trainers. You read what you've written. Eat dinner. Do homework. Double-check their meeting times, then slip under your covers and dwell on the selections well until your brain clocks out and you go to sleep.

Dawn breaks. Your eyelids flutter open. Brush, brush goes the toothbrush. You gargle toothpaste and water and spit it into the sink's hole, and as you prepare the hot water for your facial wash, you find your answer.

Morning, June 25th, 20XX

The call comes late in the morning, when your bottom is parked on the benches in the school bathrooms, a bottle of shampoo clutched in one hand and a wooden comb perched in the other. Your mind is preoccupied with doubts of Ms. Gold's generosity, a plan of how to push her patience to her limits (without angering her, obviously) brewing in your head, causing you to take the call later than you should have.

"Hello?"

"Ruby."

What flows out of your phone's speaker is a sword's hiss en route out of its scabbard. Your ears perk up, and your tail goes rigid.

"Grass? Good morning—I mean, what's up? Is everything all right?"

"It's Trainer Mifune." Grass says. "I'm watching her from a distance over at the main turf, where the two of you arranged to meet. She's in a predicament."

You almost blurt out the moniker of 'Ms. Gold', before catching yourself. Grass doesn't live in your head. She has zero clue about your internal stranger naming conventions, which sound stupid and are the embodiment of impolite in their mere existence. Also, you learned her real name a while ago. Why are you even still referring to her like that?

"What kind of predicament?"

Grass hesitates. "It may be a deliberate attempt to sabotage either of you."

"Are you serious?" You fling the shampoo and comb aside. "Are there reporters down there?"

"There's a small crowd, indeed. It's composed of other students; some of the other notable faces from the previous tryouts are there. They're surrounding Trainer Mifune and refusing to leave."

Poaching. The act of luring an individual player away from another offer. Restricted by rules, technically not illegal in its current foundations, yet scummier than a scum pond on the surface of a bubbling bog. You found yourself on the receiving end of one such attempt, courtesy of some suit trying to skim new talent off Shibuya's scene. That day, you learned Manager Suzuki used to run track. The man couldn't cross the dance hall fast enough.

You're on his end now, in a sense. The thought of some random faceless 'mob' uma taking Kaori's free spot, your rightful spot, makes your stomach somersault.

"I'm coming right now. See you there."

You wrench open your dorm room's door, slam it, then storm over to your closet. A thought occurs to you, and you refrain from hovering on the hangup icon.

You switch to speaker-phone instead. "Wait, Grass."

"Yes?"

"Why are you with Trainer Mifune?"

"I'm not with her. I'm seeing her."

"Same thing."

A tiny pause. "Oh. I forgot to mention this. I've been chatting with her lately."

"Seriously?"

"Why, yes." There's a soft, faintly amused sound, which signals the uptick of Grass's lips, though not a smile in this context. "I've had the pleasure of speaking to Trainer Mifune recently. She came to me bearing a gift of tea leaves and fruit, and asked if she could trouble me for a slice of my time. We ended up spending the afternoon together, chatting about you. She simply wished to learn more about you before she made her offer."

"But…" Shoes, tracksuit, sports-bag and cleats. You tear off your blanket for your water bottle, then remember it's in your schoolbag. "She's not my Trainer yet."

"I suppose she's meticulous. If you rejected her, then at least she'd know about you as a competitor."

That's no small compliment, coming from Tracen's embodiment of the traditional Japanese woman. Trainer Mifune took the extra step to understand you, too. You'd be impressed, and a little flattered, if you weren't in a massive rush.

"Hey, you didn't tell her my secret strategies, did you?"

The door creaks open. You whirl around.

"Oh, Ruby, can I borrow your—"

"Take whatever you want Tabby I gotta go!"

A muffled "I'm not a cat…" peters out in your wake.

Fast-walk through the dorms. Burst out the door and fast-job across the designated running lanes. The breeze whips at your hair. A slight humid tinge hangs in the air; rain must approach on the horizon. The absence is a blessing, since you're not accustomed to running across wet turf yet. Circling around the main building, dashing between the trees, the turf opens up, the rings of green and dirt swaddled beneath fresh morning sunshine.

You race towards the bleachers. A hop over the railing and a quick zip down, there she is: Trainer Mifune, standing on the edge of the turf surrounded by around a dozen umas gathered in a semi-circle. Her long, golden-blonde curls gleam in the bright light. Add the fact that Trainer Mifune arranged a meeting beforehand, and a far more insidious thought bubbles up, reeking of spilled juice boxes and huddles of faceless shrine workers.

Grass waits at the bottom of the bleachers. She waves in greeting. You wave back and head for the stairs down near the railing, then screech to a halt on the penultimate step.

"You took your sweet time."

A figure steps out of the shadows cast by the overhang and blocks your path.

An uma that hasn't been a friend, nor an acquaintance, nor an enemy. Pressurized fury seeps out from Grass; a blade wreathed in flame, slicing through pounds of naked flesh and bringing troublemakers to their knees. [Grass Wonder's Social Link > 1.]

Tosen Jordan

It's too hands-off. It's too risky. It's a contradiction.

So, what's actually happening?

Is this work of a Mifune executive? No. Lady Mifune called Kaori directly. Alright, what about the work of an executive attempting to move against Lord and Lady Mifune to seize power, or disrupt their operations? Doesn't work, either. It'd result in an intelligent, capable daughter beloved by the household heads returning to the fold, the equivalent of this hypothetical executive shooting themselves in the kneecap.

One possibility remains. Kaori isn't the target here. You are. Lord and Lady have discovered your scouting and are now testing whether you'll buckle or not under their pressure. Like Jordan. Like Narita Brian. Like—oh goddesses, why can't anyone in this academy be honest for a change?

"As you can see, young mistress, Satono Ruby seems to lack an attention span…"

"Call me Ruby." You snap at the suit. "And I'd appreciate if you lay off the insults, thanks."

You'd like to rescind your earlier statement. This suit does contain a smidgen of personality—a disgusting one. You will now take that adjective and fling it upon the actions of Lord and Lady Mifune, too. It doesn't matter how much they love their daughter. Sending their toadies to interfere with her private business, knowing full well the boundaries she's set, is revolting.

The question of how they mobilized the suits so quickly remains up in the air. Maybe that Satono Trainer told them. Maybe someone else in the academy faculty still holding a chip on their shoulder for you told them. Maybe they installed spy cameras in Kaori's bathroom—you'll figure it out later. For now, someone has to speak to the Lord and Lady. Someone has to grasp their collars from beyond the veil of corporate red tape and teach them a lesson about setting boundaries.

Kaede told you this a long time ago: to live in the entertainment industry means to be constantly judged. To have the last frill on your dress, your most minute breaths and angle of your legs put under a microscope. Accept this as your fate, and you'll reflect those judging gazes into ticket sales, fans and etched memories.

You agree with her.

Sure.

Why not?

You'll put yourself on stage. You'll hold a special Satono Ruby show on this track for the Mifunes via their meathead of a proxy; a big shining, starry banner screaming your partnership with Kaori and her parents can piss off from your shared careers together! It'll need to be explosive. Powerful. A demonstration of who Satono Ruby is, scorching as hot as the flame conjured in the Nightmare. And it'll be a pain in the rear, since it'll be spontaneous and you're not the greatest at improv.

But, you must do it, lest the suit return to bother Kaori with more empty words in the future.

You smirk.

In a roundabout way, the suit's an opportunity, too, because the Satonos also employ his lot. He can be your training dummy for when you'll inevitably take them on.

That said…

You sneak a glance at Kaori. She's wearing a very special expression, the kind in the process of sending tremors rippling through the crowd. Sweat trickles, teeth chatter, and the lisping girl hides behind blondie with her head buried in the other girl's shoulder. Only the paper sack girl stands unaffected.

You remember Kaede telling you another thing. An umamusume's wrath is a speeding bus, a human man is a sledgehammer to the knees, and a human woman is a collection of knives, stabbing in and out of the target's chest, over and over.

Seems like Kaori has a plan too.

(How will you assert dominance as Kaori's new trainee? Top 2 will be used.)

[] [AssertDominance] Challenge everyone here to a race.

[] [AssertDominance] Call campus security.

[] [AssertDominance] Trust in Kaori and let her handle this.

[] [AssertDominance] Call up Lord and/or Lady Mifune directly via Kaori's phone.

[] [AssertDominance] Grab Kaori and run.

[] [AssertDominance] Begin umadol dancing on the spot.

[] [AssertDominance] Pull the paper sack off the paper sack girl and see what happens.

[] [AssertDominance] Convince the crowd they're being hoodwinked by the suit.

[] [AssertDominance] Assert Tosen Jordan to film a clip about the Mifunes' deception.

[] [AssertDominance] Write-in.

[Total EXP Gained: 40.]

EXP: 195/200.

We will now discuss Training Time—the recurring event where you spend time with your Trainer & teammates and learn from them. But first, we need to talk about how Encounters will be structured from now on.

Encounters will now use the following gameplay loop:

Training Time. Daily Life Planning. You'll spend TP (Time Points) on specific Events to decide what Ruby does. (More about this will be revealed later.) QM rolls for a few random Events (less than 4). Daily Life Beginnings. Voting for Event choices happens here. Daily Life Resolution. Plot stuff happens. (May be optional; will almost certainly take longer than Daily Life.) Repeat until End of Encounter. There is no strict in-universe time limit for any of these items.

The exception to this loop will occur when a race happens. Points 2-5 will be replaced by the buildup, climax and aftermath of the Race itself. No TP will be spent, and no voting will occur except for matters pertaining to the race itself, and all random events will be replaced with random mini-events. Training Time and plot stuff will remain consistent.

Now, let's talk about Training Time. During it, you will…

Meet with your team and discuss your coming goals. You will most likely receive some training recommendations and intelligence on the competition here. Your Trainer will also perform a checkup on you. QM rolls for a training event (uses 2d12 system). All kinds of things might happen depending on the dice. Your Trainer organizes inter-team training. A scrimmage is set up. You and your teammate get into a fight. Reporters come, the Director herself visits, someone steals your equipment, and so on! This is where your Trainer's Attributes are checked the hardest. Will they be able to resolve disputes properly or take advantage of fortunate opportunities? Positive outcomes will lead to bonuses such as improved gains for the Training Time or general stats increases. Negative outcomes will lead to the reverse. General skill training happens. All racing skills increase. Tagged racing skills increase further. General Attribute training happens. All Attribute meters increase. Tagged Attribute meters increase further. Personal training happens. Your Trainer teaches you in what they know best. All racing skills and Attribute (meters) they specialize in increase. QM rolls for a teammate training event (also uses 2d12). Depending on the outcome, some skills or Attribute (meters) your teammate(s) specialize in increase. If your Trainer has organized joint team training, trainees from other teams might appear instead. Training vote happens. A list of training plans will be presented for you to vote on. Attribute meters are a new mini-system that tracks the progression of your Attributes. Each one starts at 0% and progresses up to 100%, upon which the respective Attribute gains a +1. Any overflow (e.g. you have 90% and you get a +20%) is then halved (from 10% to 5% in this instance). A meter's progression is not limited to Training Time and may happen in other scenarios, such as scrimmages, Daily Life segments or running a race.

All your Attribute meters are currently at 0%. Due to their addition, the +1 to any Attribute option in the AP shop will have its once per LEVEL UP restriction added back. They will be treated as if you gained a 100% boost to the Attribute meter, meaning the overflow halving will also apply.

Let's look at an example, abbreviated Training Time, using Kaori and Tosen Jordan.

Example training time (this is not real)
Kaori teaches you about your upcoming debut race. You get some info on potential competition.

QM rolls a 11 for a Training Event. A journalist visits the training site to take some pictures. He asks Kaori about her family.

[Trainer Kaori's Guile check: 12/11 -> Success!]

Thanks to Kaori's quick thinking in front of the camera, she's able to avoid a PR slipup.

[Mood has increased to Great.]

Kaori teaches you racing theory.

[All racing skills have increased by 2.]

[Your tagged racing skills have increased by 1.]

You perform core training with the team.

[All Attribute meters have increased by 5%.]

[All tagged Attribute meters have increased by 5%.]

Kaori tutors you on what she knows best.

[Racing Tactics, Frenzy and Nutrition have increased by 5.]

[Your Speed, Psyche and Wits meters have increased by 10%.]

QM rolls a 15 for teammate training event. Tosen Jordan grudgingly teaches you how to improve your spurts.

[Acceleration has increased by 2.]

Voting for a training plan begins.

(Example options)

[O] I want to work on speed. (+10 to Dodge, +5 to Traversal, +20% to Speed meter.)

[O] I want to work on strength. (+10 to Acceleration, +5 to Brawl, +20% to Power meter.)

[O] I want to work on endurance. (+10 to Pain Threshold, +5 to Breathing, +20% to Stamina meter.)

[O] I want to work on disruptive tactics. (+10 to Frenzy, +5 to Racing Tactics +10% to Psyche and Wits meters)

You might notice that the gains in this example Training Time are small. Tosen Jordan only helped you out in one skill, for example. Kaori's non-racing skill specializations weren't mentioned at all! This is because you're a fresh trainee who hasn't gotten that close to your team, your Trainer or your teammates. Improve your relationship with these three factors to increase their bonuses and unlock more of them! Your Trainer has her own Social Link, but the other two are dependent on a stat called Team Power…which will explained in detail after you've voted on your team name in the future. For now, understand that the greater the Team Power, the better your team will run and grow (the opposite is true).

(Values within the example are close to the real thing but may be subject to change.)

Lastly, after acquiring your Trainer, you will gain a permanent +1 AP and 5 extra LEVEL UP skill points. But you'll be busy training with her instead, so the +10 Racing skill points option in the AP shop will be granted the once per LEVEL UP restriction from now on.

So, that's that. I hope that was a sufficient breakdown of how Training Time works. Please do not hesitate to ask any questions.

Now, it's time for your compensation. That's right—it's another freebie. I did not properly explain how training works, which was a failure on my part as it should have factored into the Trainer vote. Since Kaori has been locked in, this is the compromise I hope is sufficient. You will now receive 1000000 carats the ability to refactor some Kaori's stats. First, select one of her four Attributes to increase. Here's a reminder of what each one can do:

Attribute use cases
Intellect:

Designing training regimes. Parsing and writing legal documents. Analyzing biomechanics and physiology (stride mechanics, asymmetries etc.) Collating data and making predictions (industry trends, weather patterns etc.) Debating philosophy or politics. Psyche:

Resolving disputes between Trainer and/or trainee. Requesting external assistance. (Other Trainers, team collaborations, private tutors) Enforcing team or self authority. Negotiating with sponsors. Planting insinuations in opponents Physique:

Improving efficiency of Nutrition plans. Detecting and preventing injuries. Pull all-nighters without losing focus. Determing effectiveness of experimental therapies, such as acupuncture. Self-defense and intimidation from malicious parties. Guile:

Responding to unexpected press questions. Taunting and mocking others (while deflecting external attempts). Creating underhanded tactics. Studying opponents' strengths and weaknesses. Picking up useful rumors.

Kaori figuring out Ruby's flaws through observation and giving her the breakdown in 4.1 is her passing an Intellect check (difficulty: 12).

(Choose only 1.)

[] [TrainerRefactor1] Increase (insert Attribute name here) by 1.

Secondly, you may replace her Nutrition skill specialization with any other racing skill (that's not already present).

(Choose only 1.)

[] [TrainerRefactor2] Do not replace any skills.

Lastly, you may replace her Wits Attribute specialization with any other Attribute (that's not already present).

[] [TrainerRefactor3] Do not replace Wits.

These are her stats, for reference:

But, we suppose escaping death by a hair will bolster anyone's drive for life. Polite, assertive and generous; what she lacks in experience, she compensates with a powerful, analytical mind—just ask the trail of bodies she's left behind in airsoft. Don't expect her to lean on her family's assets unless a terrible crisis falls into her lap.

Mood: Good

EXP: 195/200

Here's a history lesson from your non-existent autobiography.

Kaede and Manager Suzuki figured out you lied about your age within the first month. In hindsight, you shouldn't have bothered at all. A poker face worth a million yen debt, an accent straight from the boonies, and constant rolling of shoulders and the awkward, continuous stretching of back muscles to stand taller than your bones allowed—a half-blind dumpster diver could've sniffed out you weren't telling the truth about your age. It was a miracle FAITHFUL's two seniors didn't drag you to the nearest police station by the ear and dump you there.

You like to think the dogeza you made in front of them helped. You know the other girls didn't speak up, trusting their leaders' judgment. You understand together that you will pay the debt you owe those two over the rest of your life, and then the next one.

Since FAITHFUL let you stay, they set conditions. Assignments. Read this. Write about that. Take this book, fill out the questions in the sheet stuck between the middle, and return it to Kaede. No cheating, because she copied these exercises from her high school textbooks and has access to the answers. It was a slapdash form of homeschooling, of scattered maths and literature, and while you diligently tried in between practice as to not the rock the boat, you didn't understand the full point of learning this stuff until the group fully left that awful gothic mess behind and entered the real enka rock stardom FAITHFUL was always destined to be.

Suddenly, you found yourself attending meetings. Mildly comfortable chairs under dull lights, complementary water on the table, the prettiest clothes in your meager wardrobe on your back—an almost double negative—and Kaede called you up to introduce yourself, present your strengths, and talk like a proper sapient being.

Oh, you realised, that was why you got homeschooled. Your new friends hoped you wouldn't embarrass the group in front of clients.

Underground stardom is an onslaught of exploiting niches. Groups built a house from back-to-back lives, photoshoots and handshakes; so many grains of time and space contested by hundreds of rivals, scraping the beach with metal detectors around the clock. The big wards only contain so many theatres to perform in. The end result is that everyone pitches in. Anafabula Offices doesn't care if you have two part-time jobs, an awful breakup over the weekend, or a college course, or if you're a runaway desperately hiding from the arm of an estranged conglomerate family—everyone means everyone.

A prop, your antis might call, and you'd be legit insulted at that. Those were serious tactics the group employed. An umadol's presence is rare enough! Any advantage is non-negligible. Gimmicks aren't worthless. Only their application is. Secondly, the two seniors (or Hotaru if she was in an bad mood that day) always asked for at least one thing you learned afterwards. Those meetings comprised the second part of your education, and honestly, you found them more interesting and useful to your daily life than boring old algebra.

Now, back to the present.

Lesson number sixteen, from the afternoon where Kaede went silent for ten seconds straight before unleashing a response on a sponsor so tailored, it deserved to be in a museum. Negotiations aren't constant flows of back-and-forth speech. You are allowed to cut the brakes, stand on the spot and think up a proper response. When that happens, time stretches. It doesn't hang in the silence, like some dull blanket on a washerwoman's line. It crawls, drags, shimmies an invisible sieve that squeezes seconds into minutes.

That's a good thing, because your brain instinctively speeds up to make use of that time. That's bad, because that allowance of time isn't as long as everyone thinks it is, including you. The length is primarily dependent on patience. Kaede's almost twice as old as you, to say nothing of Madame Sugar, and neither of them were able to provide a solid answer The ballpark: ten to twenty at the maximum, depending on how the other parties' tick, and only if you keep yourself composed like a stone-cold strategist.

This standoff is a negotiation. It is an attempt to wrangle something away from the Mifune family's desire to manhandle their daughter's daily routine. Your disposition might be a problem.

You're not composed right now. Far from it, with those hands balled into fists, while the burns the back of your neck and turns up the heat in your brain. It is a still from some bottom-barrel manga in Mandarake's discount bin. You breathe in and tuck your chest in, straightening your back, so those in your local radar—Kaori, the suit, that blondie you've pinpointed as Fusaichi Pandora—are surely filtering through their sieved time, hearing your silence, and are thinking your brains have leaked out of your ears.

Is that an exaggeration? Maybe. Maybe, maybe, maybe, but what is not a 'maybe' is the fact you are so done with these back-and-forths and your Trainer hunt, you think you will place the outcome of next few minutes slightly below your mother's prized shoes.

Yell at the suit. Call Tracen campus security. Possible actions flit through your head behind a furrowed brow. Take an incriminating photo, perform a dance as if Smart Falcon were here, go for a run. Trust Kaori. That sounds pleasant, the next thought comes. Surely, an adult thorough enough to hunt down Grass Wonder for your recruitment possesses a contingency plan for her stupid parents. Except, judging from her reaction, it's the first time her parents have gone to such lengths to convince her to return. Except except you immediately counter that sniveling doubt, she was born and bred in that politics-ridden gilded cage, then escaped to roost beneath Director Akikawa's wings. Her stature, from the stitch of her uniform to the firmness of her feet, speaks of poise. So much so, a couple of the girls look confused instead of frightened.

Yet, her wrath seeps out of her fleshy smell, faint sugar-sweetness oscillating and clashing with a metallic sharpness in waves. Your moods are synchronized, then. It's a comforting thought.

You should trust Kaori.

You think that again.

You should trust Kaori. For this, at least. Common enemies are actually friends, and so on and so forth. It doesn't taste foul as the thought of going back to the academy tachers for more homework. Okay. Alright! That's a decision. A good, great, idea. Your brain continues walking down those tracks of thought, and the rest swiftly follows.

Kaori is a Trainer. Trainer helps umas run races. Races are what's important. The suit can roll up, warble his nonsense and gas up the girls until his hearts stop beating. It doesn't matter. This is Tracen Academy, kingpin of the entire Japanese umamsusume racing industry. Pretty faces, aced paper exams, rich families imitating the Mejiros with their silver spoons—no matter how glitzy they shine beyond the academy walls, this is inside. All those traits fall short in the face of the one supreme metric: results.

Thus, the plan clicks into place. It's so obvious you want to laugh. Why didn't you think of it immediately?

[Logic check: 87/40 -> Success! Trivial: +0 EXP.]

You lift your hands, grip them, and crack your knuckles. Kaori blinks. Jordan raises an eyebrow. You give them a knowing nod, hoping that it communicates that you're on their side. The words are already crawling out of your noggin and into your voice box. Once a boulder starts rolling, it will not stop.

You clear your throat.

"Excuse me. Excuse me, everyone. Hey! I'm talking to you, Matikanetannhauser!"

You've never spoken to the girl in question before in your life, nor are you facing in her general direction. The mere dropping of the lisping girl's name, an act of the personal, causes her to jolt and swing around. Her hands fumble with her dollar-store notepad, as her hat dangles further down from where it's hooked around her ear. An almost-hurt look flashes on her face.

You snatch the attention of the rest of the girls as well. This is another idol trick. According to their subconscious, if you know one person's name, then clearly there's the possibility you might know the others too.

"Uh, what do you want?" Fusaichi Pandora emerges from the crowd, one hand on a tip. Her tone drips with gal energy: upbeat, smooth, and tinged with a hint of condescension.

"News. The topic is news." You reply. "Hello, everyone. I have interrupted whatever it is you were doing for important news!"

You spread your arms wide. Then you say nothing else. Pandora blinks. Matikanetannhauser raises her hand. You ignore both. Five seconds pass, and Pandora scowls.

"Earth to Satono Ruby? Earth to Satono Ruby? You lose your tongue—"

You flash her a humorless smile and jog over to the starting line of the nearby track. Pandora yelps, indignant. You ignore again. This would be social suicide for any other uma, as audiences don't have as wide attention spans as they think; immediately ditching them is a fast ticket to lost interest. Unfortunately for them, you are Satono Ruby, a target and therefore a curiosity. Your infamy smiles in your favor, for once. The crowd watches you crouch into position at the track's starting line.

The wind whips up. It tousles your long dark locks and flies grass scent up your nose. You inhale deeply, thankful to be away from that crappy meeting for a change. You clutch your lucky charm in a quick grip, contract the muscles in your lower half, fire the imaginary whistle in your head and launch off.

[(Stamina check: 11/10) && (Speed check: 11/10) -> Success! +10 EXP.]

You surroundings rocket and stretch into a blur. The headache from dealing with the suit snaps off and vanishes into the dust for raw, physical exhilaration. You smash the lap. You ace it—pace, stride, energy, and the rest of which Kaori taught you. The victory reverberates deep in your skeleton before the naked proof reveals to you: a gobsmacked crowd. Open mouths and still ears. Jealously seeps out next, the slime of a snakeskin shed.

"Show-off." One of the girls, a freckled-face, sneers. "We get it, Satono Ruby. We see the fit. You're soooo cool."

"Thank you!" You respond. The girl flinches, rolling her eyes to try to hide it.

"I-I could totally do that!" Matikanetannhauser cries, her cheeks puffed up. "I've been training my glutes too, you know."

That's a statement more aimed at herself than you.

Pandora shrugs. "I'm totally not impressed, Satono. Feels like your head's full of it just 'cause you almost beat Kitasan. Like, excuse me? You still didn't win. Your time wasn't great. You're down at ground zero with the rest of us."

There's an undercurrent of hesitation present, the type where you're trying to turn a lie into a truth. You will admit she's got a grain of a point. Out of the entire crowd, Pandora acted the most proactive and looks and smells the least sweaty. The rest of the girls shift to cluster around her, minnows selecting their de facto leader. More murmurs of agreement. More green eyes. It's exactly how FAITHFUL acted when a singer from the aboveground returned 'home' to pay her respects.

You raise a hand to your mouth in mock surprise. "Wow. Wow! I can't believe it. Someone finally gets it!"

"Gets what?"

"Ground zero. You're so right, Pandora."

"Yeah. I'm a real genius." Pandora says carefully. "What's your deal?"

You tilt your head slightly, feigning surprise. "We're athletes, aren't we? We run."

"Yeah. We run."

"We totally run."

"Thanks, captain obvious—

You cut her off once again. "Run, run, run umamusume, champions and underdogs in the fray—it's in the song. The damn song, with the banjos that are so American it hurts. Funny story: that song's special to me now, 'cause I sang it on the streets to attract that Orange-Shirted Trainer and the one that's a wall of muscles."

Pandora splutters out indignation. You keep going. You raise your volume over her pretty little face hole. The trick to impromptu speeches is to never hit the brakes.

You place your hands behind your back, idly nudging your foot against the grass. "I came down here to run. To show and strut my stuff in front of Trainer Mifune. Only to see that she was being hogged by half a dozen other girls. Begging and pleading and causing her all sorts of trouble! And I was thinking real hard, jogging my brain, really, really trying to figure out how to stop this sudden clench in my chest."

Pandora frowns. "Nobody said we couldn't ask Trainer Mifune directly."

"Yeah, I get you. It's tough out there. Tracen only employs so many staff of her caliber. You gotta do what you gotta do…" You give her an exaggerated shrug. "Even if it's totally rude."

"Excuse me?"

"Like I said, I attracted those Trainers. Trainer Mifune among them. She scouted me personally. Two meetings together. Not you, Pandora, not Tannhauser, not that girl with the freckles or the one next to her with the orange scrunchie—" You whip out your finger and jab at the crowd, smiling wider and higher before slamming it down into a cold, dark scowl. "Me. Satono Ruby."

[Intimidation check: 42/40 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

You are not a ferocious uma. You tried to act scary towards a journalist once, and it backfired enough that the other FAITHFUL girls had to step in. Yet, that sudden jump from smiles to scowl, a glimpse of your bottled up anger, slides over the edge and throws the girls off balance. They flinch. A couple step back. You sweep over them all, then revert.

"But, that's in the past." You say, clapping your hands. "It's totally my fault. I should've accounted for this. Can't do anything about it now, whoopsie me!"

"What do you want?" Pandora asks.

"Eh? We're getting to that now?"

"I seriously can't handle umas who can't say crap straight." That's rich, you internally scoff, coming from her. Pandora's frown turns aggressive. "Get to the finish line already!"

You stare at her, batting your eyelashes.

Another five whole seconds.

The color on Pandora's cheeks morphs from a tangerine to a fresh tomato dangling on its stalk. She whirls around. "Someone call this chick's mom, because she's lost her own head!"

"But, I don't want to be picked up. My mom can't pick me up, anyway. She's gone, remember? I want to run. Run, run, run—that's why I showed off a minute ago. Couldn't you figure that out?" You fake-whine. You sweep your arms out and stomp your feet a few times. Then, you go still, calm and composed, and raise a finger. It is more whiplash. "Because we are well and truly are getting nowhere. Let's skip to the obvious. A race. You, Tannhauser, that girl in the paper sack, all of you! Whoever wins gets to be Trainer Mifune's new trainee!"

You round your beaming face across the apprehensive girls, eyebrows wiggling. They don't know it yet, but they're inched a step or two throughout your miniature turf performance. Hook, line, and now, with a half-twirl and a brushing of your long hair aside, the sinker.

"Unless…"

"Unless?" Pandora echoes.

She clamps her mouth shut , her eyes widened. It's too late. The bait's already been swallowed. The shogi pieces has been sent out to die. You spin around, tilting your head up and behind whilst forming the edges of a small yet hard grin. Deep inside your head, further metal locks break. A glossy CD imprinted with cherry blossoms in the night, a moon high up, is retrieved. Tomorrow is FAITHFUL project #3, subsection A, character #2. Beneath the full moon and atop a battlefield, her dress, soaked in rainwater, her sword speckled with fresh crimson, she glances idly at the band behind her, those pathetic human soldiers and their trembling spears, and her heart pulses with vigor.

"Unless—" The umamusume onnamusha, caged and transparent behind the shell of your psyche, smirks, viciously, bloodily, "You're all too chicken to face me on the turf?"

You tip your hand, which is arched enough to reveal the dents of your knuckles, and emit a high-pitched giggle—a perfect replication of the arrogant, the glamorous, and the profoundly irritating rich girl you once dreamed of being.

[(Psyche check: 10/12) || (Subterfuge check: 73/70 && Artistry check: 55/50)) -> Success! +10 EXP.]

[+1 to Chaos Alignment.]

[+1 to Dark Alignment.]

Fireworks explode.

"Huh? What the heck did you just say?"

"Chicken? I'm not chicken! I'm…I'm…M-m-m…I'm super mad now!"

"She thinks she's Opera O…"

"Was that meant to piss me off? Because it's working!"

You cackle and spread your arms out. "Going once, going twice, do I have three, four, five, eight participants? Ten? Friends, are we making this happen?"

"Daughter of a cheating whore thinks she's all high and mighty…fine. Fine, fine, fine! get over here! We're going to beat you into the dirt!"

"But this is the turf…" Someone next to her points out.

"Shut up!"

Pandora clenches her fists. Her nostrils flare. "You're gonna eat those words."

"No." You reply, thinking of the six resumes on your desk. "I don't think I will."

If looks could kill, you'd be less uma and more raw hamburger mince splattered across the turf. Pandora, sadly for her, can't manifest a chainsaw in her bare hands, and so she settles for giving you the stink eye and storming off.

You chuckle. You gaze upon your handiwork. It's already in motion. The crowd of umas is getting ready: jogging, stretching, checking their feet, huddling together in small groups. Their shared desire to beat the snot out of your nose is as apparent as smoke is from a raging bushfire. It is an atmosphere full of vigor, and from an outsider's perspective, including Jordan's gawping mouth and palmed face, you have now stacked the deck against yourself. You have made a blunder so terrible, so obviously avoidable, you deserve nothing less than an ambulance straight to the ER ward.

Ah, but, but, but—you'd waggle your finger to this outsider with a smug, teenage-knows-better-than-the-adults grin—you have succeeded.

[Psyche check: 10/10 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

Look at the suit. Look at how he's feeling. He is so not pleased. "I…" Mr. Takashi averts his gaze. "I erred at work and was assigned this task soon afterwards."

A fool's errand. A sliver of a chance for redemption, via the Mifune's greatest treasure. A web of plans and foibles that entrapped you in its shadows. Suddenly, you can't stand the sight of the man.

Kaori falls silent. She lets out a long, suffering sigh. She reaches up to her hair and plucks the hairpin out from it. A tuft of peachy blonde dangles loose, a blemish on an otherwise perfect hairdo.

Kaori holds the citrus-colored hairpin between her index and her thumb. She gazes into it, unblinking, then drops it towards the ground. It falls without sound, bouncing off a tuft of grass and landing still. It glints its golden-orange one moment, then perishes the next. Kaori slams her boot on it once, twice and thrice with the heel of her boot, before grinding the finishing touch in.

[Trainer Kaori's Physique check: 14/12 -> Success!]

Mr. Takashi breaks into an expression of pure horror. You steal a glance at Jordan. She's gaping.

Kaori crouches down and picks up the shards tinged with earth and grass. Her slender fingers sift through the shards, lingering on the center of the flower for a second longer. Then, she holds them out in her palm.

Mr. Takashi sputters. "The Lord and Lady gave those—"

"For my eighteenth birthday. As a present for when I set out into the world as an adult." Kaori forms a bitter smile. She dumps the shards into Mr. Takashi's shaking hands. "They and I know I have been very, very patient with their requests. So much so, the child in me buckles at the thought of what I am about to do. But a charade must end; and enough must one day become enough. Record this if you must: should my parents refuse to cease their interference with my and my trainees' education or personal lives, I will take the stacks of gifts, presents and clothes they have graciously gifted to me, pile them together, set alight, photograph it and personally deliver them to their office inbox. Any money they have lent me will be personally donated to Tracen."

Mr. Takashi chokes. He stares at the shards as if they are a nest of spiders. "You will live as a pauper!"

"They're luxury products. The streets are clogged with enough already." Kaori says. "Besides, Grandfather lived as a pauper until he was twenty. He kicked the bucket at a hundred."

[History check: 53/80 -> Failure.]

You don't know who Kaori's grandfather is. Probably a founder, the rare kind who did pull himself out of destitution, though it's no indication he was a good person. He must still be a respected figure in the conglomerate for his name alone to shut the man up. The leverage Kaori has—it will work. Old families like the Mifunes place great importance on their prestige, their honor. It must not be tarnished, including within its own offices. No cost is too high. Why else would the Satonos be so desperate to destroy your mother's shoes?

"Go."

And Mr. Takashi and the other suits do exactly that. You will never see them again.

It's the end of this whole mess. Or, it should be. Jordan runs up to Kaori, grinning wide, asking if her Trainer is alright. The two of them exchange quick affirmations, the tension in Jordan's shoulders relaxing. It comes rushing back as she notices Kaori staring at the sullen girls loping off. Jordan immediately shakes her head, those twin-tails swaying like tree branches in the wind, and Kaori herself is looking hesitant too. Too late. The words have already left her mouth.

"Hold on."

The crowd turns around, questioning.

Is she doing this? She is. Kaori waves her hand towards her. "Come back, all of you. You took the time and effort to come here and deserve at least a tip for that."

Once the still-confused girls have lined up in semi-neat rows, Kaori rattles off names. "Fusaichi Pandora!"

"Y-yes?"

"You tried to overtake too quickly and early. Exercise patience. Matikanetannhauser!"

"Here!"

"Speak to Trainer Minamizuka. He manages Team Canopus, of whom their star trainee is Nice Nature. Well-connected and well-rounded, she'll serve as a good senpai."

Tannhauser blushes. She rubs the back of her head. "I…am already in them?"

Kaori narrows her eyes. "Then why are you here?"

Tannhauser holds up her notebook. A shield. "Research?"

She squirms under Kaori's mounting disapproval.

"Do not do this again, unless you want to be disqualified and barred for espionage."

"I'm so sorry!"

"Gold—don't make me say it."

"Hey! I ran too." The paper sack girl faux-whines. "I deserve equal rights."

"This is a privilege, not a right. Go home this instant, or the deal is off. And stay away from Jordan, too!"

Kaori repeats the process for the other girls. There's no struggle. The girls listen, thank her, and leave. Disappointment paints them, but they swallow it down. At least they have the sense to realise Kaori is doing them a favor. She was there; she's an official Trainer, and what she says has legitimacy, as opposed for another random student or an online video. From a utilitarian standpoint, she's kneecapping you by helping your rivals.

You appreciate it. It's nice to see your future Trainer having compassion.

One girl sticks around.

"I mean it."

"Miss Pandora…"

"I'm serious, Trainer. I swear!" Pandora cries. "Everyone's heard about you. Tosen Jordan was a total moron and you took her straight to stardom. Like, I'm super smart, but I admit: I lack EXP. There are parts where I'm totally braindead. I can't run without you!"

Kaori breathes in. "Please don't insult my trainee."

"Oh, um…" Pandora blusters. "I'm sorry. She called herself that on Umatok."

"And I do understand your frustrations, Miss Pandora. But it must not arise due to the machinations of others."

Pandora looks at where the suit once stood. "Is there seriously no chance?"

There isn't.

Pandora slinks off, her shoulders hunched and her footsteps soft. You watch her go with burgeoning pity. There are always backup dancers at the winning live. There will only be a few who pass an audition. And there is no godly metric that can objectively categorize a candidate's aptitude and compatibility. This is an unfortunate truth entertainers have been forced to face since the first stage was erected, and now it's Pandora's turn.

Such is life in the business.

Next time you meet her, you'll buy her a cheesecake.

"Oi! Satono Ruby! You better be ready to explode my tastebuds, otherwise I'm gonna call Fuku to curse ya!"

"I'll be off, Trainer Mifune. As we agreed, I'll send the materials over to your office. Please take care of Ruby in my stead."

Grass and the paper sack girl depart. You jerk your head back and forth across the turf in case another pack of weirdos shows up. It doesn't. It's time. Goddesses-blessed, the trials have concluded, the past put behind you, which means it is finally, finally time to sign Kaori's contract. You are so flooded with relief, the notion feels surreal even after stepping into her office.

"Apologies…" Kaori flits through a folder and deposits a stack of papers on a sturdy table. "For the inconvenience!"

The next step of your dream sits on the oak wood. It's oddly quiet.

You pick up the papers and read them one by one. It's a standard contract. Detailed within are the scope of Kaori's services, the duration of her work—initial period included, performance expectations, exclusivity deals and whatnot; stuff you sat down with Miss Tazuna to work out. Grass was quite afraid your literacy rates weren't good enough and suggested that. Notably, the contract includes several clauses set by Tracen itself in case any of the Trainers try to scam trainees over. Tracen itself will interfere on behalf.

[Logic check: 88/85 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

The contract is safe.

You reach for the pen sign, only to hear a grunt.

"Oi. Trainer." It's Jordan.

"Jordan, please." Kaori says, her voice strained.

"Trainer, I hella respect you a great deal, but please. Let me have this."

"We've been through this a…I've stopped counting. You don't need to like Ruby. You only need to tolerate her. Chiwa and I told you how we used to feel about each other back in the day."

Jordan grinds her teeth, emitting a muffled screech of frustration. "What if I, like, want to more than tolerate her? I don't enjoy being pissed off every day."

"And you think this will solve that?"

"My chest's gonna explode if I don't."

Kaori gives her star trainee a long, hard look.

[Trainer Kaori's Psyche check: 15/11 -> Success!]

She relents.

"Say it here. Anything you say to Ruby, you should be comfortable saying to me."

Jordan nods. She waits for you to pull up out of your seat and stand in front of her. Cast under the bright noon light, the songs of birds floating through the half-open window, you sense a peculiar vulnerability in Jordan, divorced from her haughtiness.

"You saw what happened back there. Dumbasses and slickers trying to mess with us. Take it from me, rookie, as a girl who's been in too many scraps online and offline to count. It won't stop. The press can gonna latch onto you being here like roaches and drain every drop of 'Net money they can from us."

"That was my life, yeah." You say.

"Kaori thinks she can take that. Says she's used to dealing with PR crap." Jordan grimaces. "I dunno. I think it's a long shot. None of the other rookies would've been this much of a pain. None of them had bigwig corpo families staring down at them with laser pointers."

"You don't trust your Trainer?"

Something intense flashes in Jordan's eyes. She reaches out and yanks you by the shoulders, pulling you forward, nose-to-nose.

"I'll admit it. You did good work chasing that suited asshole off. I'll admit that, rookie. So…" She takes a breath. "You gotta keep those smarts juiced up."

Jordan's head droops. She lifts it, and there's a tremble in her lips and something watery in her eyes.

"Kaori's stubborn as hell. Super duper smart, yeah, but once she's got her mind set on winning something, she's planned it like a textbook and written three separate backup plans. She's not perfect. She and I…almost hated each other at first. Her fancy maths and degrees, and I couldn't read a centimeter of them due to my dummy dum-dum brain. She kept trying. Kept persisting when I was ready to throw in the towel. Nothing about what I've achieved—my races, my gal pals, my Tenno Sho—would be in a whole other reality if Kaori wasn't around, picking me up and encouraging me and standing there when I threw food in her face! I should be serving fries at some dinky food stall back on the streets, not here!"

Jordan's breathing goes ragged. A dark flame burns in her eyes.

"I. I have zero clue how she's gonna weather the PR hell that is you. I trust her. Got no choice but to trust my Trainer. You better put in your end of the deal, Ruby. Damage control, sleep in the same room as Digitan forever, beg Rudolf or throw a bomb at your old home, I don't care. Do what you gotta do. Anything but breaking Kaori's trust. If you do, I'll kill you. I swear I'll kill you. I'll throw you down, rake my nails over your cute cheeks and pluck your eyeballs myself, you hear me?"

Her speech ends in a strangled cry. She whips the back of her hand to her eyes, her jaw shaking.

You don't answer at first. You allow Jordan the privilege of letting her words sink in. You gently pull away from her face and cast a glance around this office, with its modern & chic furniture, its portable whiteboard, its small couch with a pillow and blanket, a lovingly tended display case of sashes and medals, and posters on the wall near a second desk stocked with school textbooks and a box of cosmetics. #0: SIMPLEST IS THE BEST, #9: GENTLE STRENGTH, FAITH IN YOUR JUSTICE, NEVER SAY NEVER.

A narrative exists here: a mountainous climb from the pits to the top. A heartwrenching yet heartwarming underdog story. Reading it from reports and Umastagram posts convinced you of Kaori's expertise, yet reading alone doesn't compare to witnessing Tosen Jordan in person. This is a girl who isn't used to rage and hatred. Perhaps, she's made that expression before, tucked away in her bed with nothing but the night's silence pressing down on her, as her worst fears in regard to Kaori's well-being manifest in the gloom above her skin. Then, during daytime, she laughs and dallies about, hiding her agony from her friends, as best as she can.

You won't apologise for seeking Kaori. You refuse to be ashamed of being yourself. You will acknowledge that in spite of her threats and prickly attitude, Tosen Jordan is a Tracen uma who genuinely loves her Trainer.

Kaori's gone silent. Her mouth is set in a firm line. Disapproving, yet patient. She's not a saint. Jordan will be punished after this. It won't be too harsh, and probably will involve tutoring you to fruther team bonding; the mere realisation that you're allocating such leeway to an adult sets your mind wandering. If only, you think. If only Kaori had existed back in the countryside. If only she'd worked as a shrine maiden, or if she'd been the principle of your first public school. If only someone of her nobility and integrity had been employed in the Satono household from the beginning.

Then, maybe, just maybe, your childhood wouldn't have been left to rot.

"I promise."

"Promise what?"

"That I won't let you or Kaori down."

Jordan heaves a shudder. "Words are cheap, rookie." She points two fingers in the air close to your head. "I'll be watching you.

Kaori sighs. "Oh, Jordan, 'killing'…really? There's no reason to be so dramatic."

"Hey, you said I could get this stuff off my chest."

"Ruby, if Jordan physically assaults you, please see me after you leave the infirmary. I will be sure to discipline her well."

"It was a…metaphor. Yeah, that's what it was. I remember my lit classes, Trainer!"

You and Jordan shake hands. Then, you pick up the contract, sign your name with a flourish, and Team Rasalhague is born.

Plain Jane smiles from her spot in the corner.

[Kaori Mifune is now your official trainer. Her Proximity Bonus is now active.]

--[X] Pain Threshold: 45 > 45 + 16 = 61
