>>ENCOUNTER #5: BEGIN.

Early Afternoon, June 25th, 20XX

Once the contract is signed and tucked away, Kaori shows you around her office. She points out the table for where you can study, the sofa where you are allowed to nap (but not too often, hopefully), the trophy cabinet where your future cups are sure to stand, and the vast bookshelf of racing-related material she's bought and rescued from library bins over the years. The fuzzy feeling inside you keeps growing and growing as you realise that every piece of material and furniture in the office belongs to you. It's so clean. So shiny—relatively. FAITHFUL's outfits are top-notch, in your humble opinion, but you can't say the same about Anafabula's offices. But you're the uma who lived in coffin motels; this office is more than sanitary to take out a sleeping mat and crash for a night.

"Uh, no, you can't. Because sometimes Kaori's here." Jordan interjects.

You stare at the couch and shrug. Makes sense. You can imagine Kaori radiating that overworked salarywoman energy. Flecks of darkness radiate from a spot on the couch, where a human form must have slouched with empty cans of energy drinks nested on the tea table nearby. The woes of trying to wrangle the dummy called Tosen Jordan.

[World Resonance: 113/50 -> Success! Trivial: +0 EXP.]

The rest of the office is subsumed in this nigh-tangible light, glowing and soothing and radiating orange and gold, as if liquid gold and orange juice were mixed together, cooled to a pleasant temperature, and rolled across your skin with the hands of a professional masseur. It's such a refreshing shift from that suit's nastiness.

Goddesses, get his memory out of here. You're basking in how awesome this office is.

[Mood has increased to Great!]

"Yeah, yeah, let's see how happy you are when your first G3 comes up…" Jordan mutters.

Kaori then pops out to take a phone call, while you fill a plastic cup of cold water from the Tracen-mandated water cooler. You take a sip. It's delicious. Music to your tongue. Security and safety really do make a drink taste better.

"Girls."

Kaori closes the door behind her. She's wearing a smile. Your ears perk up. It's happening. A lot of happenings happened over the past few hours, and oh goddesses, this is one happening you've waited for so, so long, and it's now finally due to arrive. Your Trainer, a person verified and trusted by Director Akikawa herself, is going to perform her duty and open her mouth and speak the truths that will let you annihilate Kitasan, Diamond, Rice Shower, Happy Meek or whoever the heck is challenging you on your debut.

"The future is bright. It is also going to be very busy." Kaori says. "Jordan, you have your upcoming graded races. Ruby, you are set for your debut. And I will be coordinating the two of you in-between additional duties as a substitute teacher. Sad as it is, there won't be much time for leisure unrelated to the sport. So…"

Kaori claps her hands and grins.

"Before the weight of the future threatens to ram headfirst into us, why don't we get some fresh air and have some fun?"

Jordan raises a hand. "Is this happening today?"

"Tomorrow." Kaori looks at a round clock on the wall. "Are you free?"

"I've got zilch. Totes down for fun times. What about you, Rubes?"

You'd object to Jordan's new moniker if it weren't for a deflating sensation permeating through the bulk of your stomach. Oh, you mind says. Relaxation. Yes, yes, that does sound…nice? No. Change of opinion time. Relaxation sounds so quaint. It's the exact opposite of gaining back the ground you've lost against your rivals. The names float again: Kitasan, Bourbon, even that Vivlos girl you've never raced before. None of them have debuted, according to the public race records, but those girls are not idle souls. Bourbon was said to conquer three slopes in a single day, every day…

"Ruby?" Kaori asks.

"Uh…"

"You good there?"

You rub your thighs. There's a bit of weariness in there. You did just run a race. It might be worth resting your legs and feet. Plus, this is your team now, which means team bonding is part of your duties. The more you connect with them, the easier future training sessions will go. There's nothing stopping you from night training if you're super desperate.

"I'm down for it!"

"Let's get going." Kaori says.

A drop-off of your bag, a quick change into your casual fit, and you're out the gate with Kaori and Jordan. Sunglasses and fancy hats are perched atop your heads. Yes, this is something you must do now. It is extraneous effort, correct. The girl known as Satono Ruby was adept at maneuvering as a nobody through crowds and brushing your journalists through quick words and fast dashes through city lanes. But that was yesterday in Tokyo, a bastion of fashion and cooking and convenience stores, and a hundred other subcultures beyond racing. Now is Fuchu, URA's home turf, where momentum from the recent Takarazuka Kinen has staked more tension into the collective crowds and displays. Look, beside the bus stop: a poster for Tosen Jordan herself. Now that's an uma at the height of her career, worth an article or two!

No fear. The press leaves you alone. They don't notice you in those cheap disguises. The plastic-smiled receptionist at the karaoke den barely gives you a second glance as Team Rasalhague brushes through their assigned room. Laminated key pass, a menu of fried chicken and drinks in hand. The seats are plush. The walls wash themselves in sparkling, rotating starry lights. And the TV shows a swirling tableau of love hearts and dolphins that have only a sliver of relation to the song you're singing.

"Let's go! Start!! Gallop into this current era. Come, let's shine, forever more..."

The microphone weighs as much as a bouquet of roses. Your heart soars with the chorus. This is perfect.

"Hello! How are you? "I've got this in the bag♪"!? You're just spouting nonsense—you're not at the top yet. We're the ones busting our tails. Say it from the dumbest and strongest—that's me, Tosen Jordan!"

"Hey, wait a minute!" You exclaim. "You're singing your own solo!"

Jordan shrugs, raising a smirk engineered in a lab to piss you off. A younger version of her waves her fingers towards a crowd of swinging penlights on the TV screen. "Better get to winning that G1, rookie!"

If you were in a truly awful mood, you'd tell Jordan that nobody actually likes her solo for her singing. They only bothered listening because it was Tosen Jordan singing. You will not do this because you are a professional umadol with industry-level standards, and secondly, Jordan wasn't bad. She's not as good as Smart Falcon, or Kaede at her best. However, the buildup, the intermingling sound effects that blast her carefree attitude like fireworks…your teeth grind as you swallow this in your head. That solo of hers is fire.

So what?

"I'm next!"

You've got your own fire burning up inside you!

"All the riff-raff on a Saturday night! Lambada dancing is so uncool, ain't that right? Flirting with dudes isn't my style; I'm running with the guys owning this town!"

The songs come and go. Pictures and graphics of cities, golden halls, dancing sheep and silhouettes of uma and man and man and woman and woman and woman shifting on the TV screen. Fried chicken arrives in boxes, the complementary drinks slugged down. Carrot juice stains your lips. Sweat pours down into your nice clothes, as your voice box flexes its muscles.

"Take my hand now, stay close to me. Be my lover, won't you let me go…"

[Foreign Languages check: 63/50 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

"人之初, 性本善…性相近, 习相远…"

"Lord, give me one more chance…"

"I-C-B-M!"

The karaoke scoreboard has long since been forgotten. Now, it's a competition of who can sing the best and the hardest without dropping out of tune.

"Wanna give up, Ruby?" Jordan heaves a breath.

You smirk back. "Not on your life. I was a professional, y'know?"

"Oh yeah, that enka stuff. Golshi played it over the PR system."

"I won't charge you for the sample! Fragrant cherry blossoms bloom…"

Kaori giggles over at the seat. "Girls. It's not a competition. I brought you here to relax."

"This is relaxing for us!" You shoot back. Jordan nods fervently. Kaori holds her hands up in mock surrender. She then takes another bite out of her pre-ordered strawberry shortcake.

Looking at her, she's pleased. Happy. Relieved that there's no real animosity between you and Jordan. You won't call Jordan a friend, but you won't deny the ice between you two has cracked. Hanging out with her is sorta fun. Far, far from the terror of running into Crown or Diamond on a random street corner. This is because you understand where Jordan came from. Hazing sucks, yeah, and you're pretty sure FAITHFUL's other girls are above such dirty tactics, but you can't deny that if you were the one sizing up a new girl on Manager Suzuki's behalf, you'd feel protective of him, too.

Even if he is an ass who refuses to buy you the good ice-cream.

"Hey, Kaori. You sing too." Jordan says, tossing Kaori the microphone.

"Oh, I'm not that great." Kaori says. "I'm happy with just watching. This is more entertaining than playing the game, actually."

"C'mon, someone has to prepare Rubes for her first winning lives."

Kaori raises her eyebrows. "You want me to coach the professional idol? Jordan, you and I both know she's got that down pat. You mentioned the PA system, after all. But since you insist…"

Kaori stands up and takes the remote. The usual punchline to this joke is that the offender puts you and Jordan to shame or sings so terribly that the plaster in the walls threatens to crack. It's neither. Kaori is above-average. Some notes are off-key, and she slips on a few words. The rest is a crystal in the rough. The bones of a decent soprano lie within. It's the song that's the issue.

"They have the Mejiro anthem here?" You say, staring at the TV. McQueen, Ryan, Bright, Dober…guess that explains who owns this chain of karaoke dens. How egoistical.

A thought then occurs to you. Your ex-family isn't attempting to replicate this, are they? Please no.

Kaori puts down the microphone. She stares at the result on the TV, a decent score, and smiles. "One of the perks of attending a private ladies' academy."

The karaoke session wraps up once the allocated two hours are over. By the time you're leaving on the short train ride back to Fuchu proper, the sun's setting. Jordan bids you and Kaori goodbye near the dorms, having plans with her buddies. Her smile is slightly mean around the edges, though not in spirit. The pair of you has built some manner of respect for the other. Dragging her to that point felt like an eternity, despite you only knowing her for a little over a full day.

"Well, Ruby, I'll see you tomorrow morning at eight for our morning training session. You know what to bring, yes?"

"Uniform, shoes, cleats, water bottle, notepad and pen, and med supplies. All cleaned and ready to go."

Kaori beams at you. "Fantastic. Have a wonderful night then. I'll see you tomorrow."

She moves to leave. She gets as far as a whole concrete square tail before you clear your throat.

"Actually…"

Kaori turns around. "Something the matter?"

You hesitate at first, sweeping your gaze across the courtyard. Class has ended and the bulk of the student body is diverted between heading back to their dorm, the city, or whatever after-school activities Tracen provides, of which are many and scattered across a variety of buildings. A few might see you close to Kaori and deduce she's either your Trainer or a friendly teacher, but it's nothing special. It happens all the time. What's important is that No-one's close enough to overhear you, much less bother to shadow you.

Good.

You cough into a fist and hope it's enough to squash the caterpillars hatching in your stomach.

You grunt and hope that clears the caterpillars hatching in your stomach. "Sorry to bother you, Trainer. But, uh, could you spare fifteen minutes at my room at Miho? There's something I have to tell you in private."

Kaori blinks. "Something you couldn't say around Jordan?"

"It's kinda personal, yeah."

Kaori gestures to the main building. "We can head to my office. No-one will hear us there."

"That's, uh…" A perfectly reasonable plan. Drat. You scramble for an excuse "It's related to a thing."

"A thing." Kaori repeats.

[(Persuasion check: 116/50 || Psyche check: 10/7) -> Success! Trivial: +0 EXP.]

"A thing that's in my room that you've gotta see. It's nothing harmful. Nothing against the law. Definitely nothing that will waste your time, I promise." You make a cross with your arms, nodding. "In fact, you could say it's the cornerstone to my entire racing career."

Pure surprise washes across Kaori, before it's suppressed into a mild look of interest. By now, she knows you're not the type of girl to play pranks, which makes this blurt you're springing out of nowhere more enticing and much more confusing. What could this cornerstone be if it's not your physique, your ambition, your perseverance, nor the path you took to enter Tracen itself?

"I can spare fifteen minutes." Kaori says. "Lead the way."

You nod and step in the direction of the Miho dorm without a second's hesitation. When occupying someone's time, it's best not to muck around.

Kaori is stopped at the Miho dorm by one of the assistant dorm managers. Trainers are prohibited to enter the student dorms without explicit permission; a rule you supposed is rooted either in the basic idea to protect the students' privacy, or a forbidden romance between uma trainee and human Trainer you have no business imagining or indulging in right now. You swipe Kaori through and lead her up the staircase towards the hall containing your dorm room.

Footsteps weigh in heavy thumps. Your hand trembles on the doorknob.

"Ruby?" Kaori says from behind you. Her posture shifts. "Is something the matter?"

The fact that you are currently struck with the urge to psyche Kaori out and say this entire trip was just a prank is what's the matter. As the person who initiated said trip, it's a big problem.

You can easily predict how Kaori would react if you were to indulge yourself. She'd become annoyed. A fracture would be set into this blossoming relationship, though you're clever enough to play your change of heart as a joke, courtesy of a certain paper sack girl. An awkward smile and a stammered apology. Stage exit.

It's doable. It's not polite. It's the sort of act that'd make Grass disappointed in you. She did not teach you to cower in fear from your own decision, nor did she go to the effort of cultivating Kaori's goodwill for you to spit in it. Yet, you cannot deny how that narrative you've churned up is tempting, whispering; the shadows across the edges of the walls and floors lengthening into long, sticky tendrils…

[Composure check: 85/80 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

It's fine. It will be fine. A Trainer exists to support their trainee's hopes and dreams. A trainee must therefore be willing to trust that their Trainer will act in good faith.

Kaori is not biased against you for being your mother's daughter. She was from a reputable, wealthy family who worked in industries tangentially related to umamusume racing at best. She is also younger than most of the veteran Trainers and wouldn't have been impacted much when that disastrous Autumn Tenno Sho kicked off.

These are facts. Hard, solid reality. That contract you signed was based on them. It must mean something.

You exhale. You grip the doorknob tighter. Goodbye, stick figures drawn in your head.

The door swings open.

The curtains are drawn. The room is silent. Tabaru is elsewhere—a relief. You don't waste time, dropping to beside your bed and withdrawing the metal case. You input the combination, fingers working deftly at the slots, a new arrangement you created via a random number generator two days ago. The quartet of latches detach with harsh metallic clicks. The lid flies open.

"Oh." Kaori says.

She falls silent. You stare at her, then back at your mother's shoes, which in turn stare up at Kaori's face.

The room's low light dulls the oranges, turquoise and pink across the stripes. The outer shell contains nary a speck of grime. It is cleaned, dusted, maintained—an artifact that could rival the trophies in the Director's own office. The shoelaces are tied in a neat bow with near-perfect geometrical symmetry. The padding inside lacks wear and tear beyond what your mother originally caused.

You cannot help these thoughts. It is your habit to obsess over your mother's shoes.

You turn to Kaori. You see her rigid posture, the way her mouth is tucked into a thin line. She's the third human to see these shoes in their case. Does she understand the gravity of this privilege? The sacrosanct nature of their presence in relation to yours? Kaori gives off no verbal indication. She reacts with faint bodily movements. The surprise fading away for quiet introspection. How fast those gears inside her head must be turning. That cranial lightning spinning, conjuring up blocks of fleshy data and pieceing them together to form photographs, news articles, case studies for paper and pen exams. Then, Lady Justice holding her scales, weighing that formulating opinion on the brass disks, in the name of determining whether you are guilty or not…

The seconds tick down. Your head spins at the fifth. You plead in a quiet voice inside you for Kaori to say something by the tenth.

"I understand why you wanted a private meeting." Kaori says.

You flinch. Then, you give an awkward chuckle and shrug with tense, rigid shoulders. "So, were you expecting this?"

"Honestly. No. Not even when you brought out the steel case." Kaori replies. She adopts a pensive look, one hand under her chin. "The mystery of Satono Opal's equipment has circulated around Trainer circles and the Internet for a long time."

"You heard the rumors, huh?"

"The Satono family recall program for Satono Opal's merch. Posters, plushies, patterned glowsticks, the rest—very successful, but not completely. You have American pawn shop and shoe factory hunters flying to Japan and scrambling around countryside villages for the crème de la crème of her lost equipment. It's never been successful. The consensus amongst my circles is that her shoes were rotting in a dump somewhere or destroyed long ago by the Satonos."

You try not to wince at the last sentence.

"Until now." Kaori's hand reaches out to the shoes. She stills it, notices how you tense up, and lets that hand fall by her side. "Better you than a glass case in some private gallery, I suppose."

Savagery. It flares in your gut, a sharp, rancid lash that satisfies instead of sickening. You couldn't agree more with your new Trainer. A drunkard tried to snatch them off you and you retaliated with your foot to his skull. You don't care if the blow cracked the bone, putting him in the ER, or a wheelchair, or a bed forever. It's your mother's shoes. You'd fight a hundred of those drunkards and beat the crap out of them and win every single time.

Kaori gazes at the shoes some more. Her expression grows seriousness. The tension inside you rises again.

Kaori rubs a hand of her chest, composing herself. Then, she puts the shoes out of sight and fully turns to you.

"Ruby."

You hold your own gaze and voice steady. "Yeah?"

"Is there anything else you want to show me?"

"No. Just my mom's shoes."

"I have a few questions, then. Firstly, do these shoes belong to you?"

You answer immediately. "They indeed belong to me."

"Is that your final answer?"

"Yeah."

Kaori regards you for a heavy moment.

"Okay." She says. "I won't ask you again."

Implication and curiosity are loaded in that final sentence. Kaori's not stupid. Her family has surely dealt with the Satonos before; she must have picked up on a rumor or two while attending their parties and joint conferences as a young heiress in training, prior to her flight. She understands full well that a story exists behind the procurement of your mother's shoes and it's dubiously legal at best. Yet, she won't pry. It's not her story, it's yours, and most importantly of all, she trusts that you will prepare a sufficient reason to tide any critics over.

This is the same woman who chided that Tannhauser girl for spying immediately. If Kaori thought you committed a crime, she'd be dragging you to Director Akikawa's office to bow and scrape.

A knot of tension undoes itself inside your stomach. The big elephant in the room walks out the door and dissipates into the ether.

"Secondly, since you have presented these shoes to me in the context of your career, do tell me if you are planning on wearing them for your official races."

You're grateful Kaori's not angry or hateful of you, as your worst fears said she would be, but now she sounds…suspicious? Like an annoyed teacher, which she technically is? The melancholic tension you were bearing vanishes in exchange for an armful of creeping shame.

"Uh…"

"An adult uma's foot size is, on average, larger than a teenager's. You can predict where my train of thought is heading, yes?"

Heat rises to your cheeks. Your tail begins to swish. "They fit."

"Do they now?" Kaori asks.

"Sort of?" You say.

"Sort of?" Kaori repeats.

"Like, eighty percent."

"And not one-hundred percent."

You shrink under this slowly forming glare. "I'm guessing that's a no to you?"

"It sounds like a half-measure." Kaori clicks her tongue. "And half-measures are unacceptable for you when running at over fifty kilometers per hour on turf."

Oh no. That's the lecturing voice. Manager Suzuki's disapproval overlays Kaori's face. They are one and the same.

"I understand this pair is undoubtedly extremely precious to you, but I must object to their function. Have you considered how your feet will chafe against the internal walls as it slips and grinds around, resulting in blisters? Or how you might trip over your own toes and collapse on the turf?"

"They're not that bad. I can fill the gaps with cloth." You protest. "I actually had thought about wearing them to my tryouts…"

Kaori scoffs. Scoffs! "I'm glad you hadn't. You would've lost to Rice Shower and Happy Meek."

So blunt. A mental dagger to your poor, frail heart. Your knees buckle.

"No-one wins a war with shabby tools."

Wasn't this supposed to be a harrowing meeting? Why are you on the receiving end of such…discipline?

"I mean, I didn't run with them at the end. And I'm not going to wear them at my debut, obviously!" You say, quickly picking myself up. "It was a suggestion. I've researched the risks. The shoes are for my future. Think about it this way. It might take me a while to win a G1 and my feet will grow larger in that time. The shoes will probably fit me, then."

"Or, you know, they could not grow at all."

"That's true…"

"Because you might win a G1 this year. Asahi Hai and Hopeful Stakes are available."

You perk up. "Is that a compliment? You think I can do it?"

Kaori smirks. "You've got the potential."

"Kaori, you're so—"

Kaori holds her palm up. "It's also a reaffirmation that these lovingly cared-for shoes should stay in their box if you want to win those two races in any universe in the multiverse."

Your shoulders slump. "I can…dance in them?"

"Ruby…"

"That's real. That's not me joking. It's not as intensive as running, and it only lasts like five minutes max at the winning live. Trust me!"

Kaori narrows her eyes. She scans the room for a chair, finds the one at your desk and sits down on it. You plonk down on your bed to match.

"Who are those shoes for?" Kaori asks.

"They're fine pieces of technology for their era, which means they haven't exactly aged the best. You can find pairs of their quality in the discount section of most sports stores. Despite this, you are adamant in wearing them. Therefore, if it's not for gaining an edge over the competition, it must be for attracting attention." Kaori says. "If I didn't know you, I'd say you were motivated to wave the middle finger in front of the Satonos."

"I'd be lying if the thought hadn't crossed my mind." You say. "Poetic irony and all that."

"And I'm sensing a 'but' here." Kaori replies.

And you think, from how her expression has softened, she already has a better guess in mind.

Diamond and Crown's smiling, young faces pop into your head, blurred and cracked.

You don't answer immediately. You gaze at your mother's shoes again, then slam the lid shut and redo the latches. You shove the case beneath the bed before retaking your position. "Trainer, how much have you heard about my mother?"

"Only what's present secondhand from news articles. I didn't know her personally on account of having recently started middle school at the time of the incident." Kaori says. "I had met a new friend, and we were concerned with sneaking out of class to eat apple pie at a corner cafe near a church than listening to adult news."

So Kaori was rebelling against her parents at the age of thirteen or fourteen? It's hard to imagine someone so straight-laced playing truant. Then again, she did delve into airsoft instead of the traditionally feminine recreations of poetry or flower arranging. The mental image that pops in your head tastes red, in both the crispness of the apple and the hair of Kaori's old friend. It's charming.

"Yeah. Figures. You didn't give me the stink eye like some of the other older Trainers. Some of those guys took what my mother did hard."

"Their loss." Kaori says. "And it's not all of them. Hana, Okino, Kitahara and many others bear no grudge against you."

"That's good to hear." Not that you'll be interacting with them much, at least not in your current state.

"Your mother also popped up as a case study in my study materials for my Trainer's license exam. Only in a hypothetical context, though." Kaori continues. "It's assumed your mother destroyed her own body via overexertion and resorted to cheating with the justification of levelling the playing field, but that's only speculation. The circumstances surrounding her disappearance are puzzling. Your former family is keeping their lips tight. Her Trainer, that stern old man, has gone missing. Private investigations into her whereabouts have been conducted, some from angry ex-fans, some from her remaining devoted fans, but the trail has always gone cold."

"It's as if she's dropped off the face of the planet." You say quietly.

The obvious answer hangs in the silence between the two of you. You refuse to acknowledge it and clench your fists shut, scowling into the floorboards until it picks itself up and dissipates.

"I said the shoes were a cornerstone. They're more a lighthouse."

"An adept metaphor." Kaori says.

"G1s attract a lot of attention."

"Jordan won a lot of prize money from her Tenno Sho Autumn. Combined with donations on those who had counted on her, the sheer volume of wealth bowled her over and I had to fetch my friend Chiwa to introduce her to a financial planner who excelled in teaching young prodigies, before she invested in the wrong stocks, or some other mistake. It also earned us an endless conga line of calls from the press and multiple reputable high-fashion brands. My parents reached out if I needed a secretary and I legitimately thought about accepting their offer." Kaori shakes her head. "But, if we had to include searching for someone as part of their deals…"

You stretch your fingers into the shape of a gun. "Bingo."

"They'd even search overseas if it had meant securing Jordan to advertise their nail polish. The revenue from one line of ads would greatly outweigh the private detective fees. It'd be an easy method of maintaining a healthy relationship," Kaori says. Her gaze softens further. "This is no folly. You truly have given this a lot of thought."

"My mom…" Something thick grows in your throat. Your voice cracks. "My name's been plastered over news articles before. It's not hard to find them. Put my name into the search bar and away you go. The idol office I worked for wasn't a secret, either. Assuming she's not bedridden somewhere, my mom has had thousands of chances to find me. She's never turned up."

"I see." Kaori says.

Do you resent her? Goes the unspoken question.

You do. You cannot help it, as any abandoned child would. The nature of the resentment does not burn with active hate like your disdain towards horrendous adults a la the Mifune's lackeys. It does not prickle and bind, like the jealousy directed towards Kitasan Black for becoming best friends with Diamond in your place. It is an object of sorrow, kin of the tears you shed on that dreadful afternoon; born from love scorned, the wounds muted and half-scarred and engraved within the bedrock of your heart. You hide it behind a facade of acceptance, and that's an easy enough accomplishment, as the memories of your mother's love are crisp in your mind by virtue of your constant acknowledgment. In times of introspection, when you are alone in the middle of the night, when sleep refuses to claim you, you dwell on those memories. Beyond their sepia-washed backdrops lies the nothingness of possibility, and within it you ask 'why'.

You take a shuddering breath. "Maybe she's overseas in Australia, or she doesn't recognise me after I've grown up, or she's found another family and is trying to forget me, or there's a sword dangling over her head from the Satonos or some other evil organization and she can't meet me, even if she yearns it with all her heart. I don't know. I simply don't know. If I win that big G1, if I create a big enough ruckus and emerge from the other side untouchable and superior to the press and the Satono Group, then I won't have to scurry in their shadow. I'll be the uma who can look them in the eye and order them to move aside instead of the other way around, and I won't need to rely on Tracen to shelter me. I'll do it at a press conference or on the street or at a high-class boutique where I'm buying the clothes I wrote in my imaginary shopping spree wishlist, and once word of that gets around…" You shrug weakly. "My mom will see how powerful her little girl is and won't be so afraid to reunite with her."

A vision of yourself: tall, strong, clad in a glitzy high-class dress that shows off your gorgeous older self's figure while remaining classy, as a true athlete turned celebrity should be. The golden-trailed sash of the Arima Kinen or the Triple Crown is wrapped in a blaze down the diagonal of your chest to abdomen. It's a pleasant autumn day, the ground beneath your feet firm as a sidewalk in Shibuya or the plaza outside a skyscraper in Ginza. The taste of your favorite honeyed yam drips across your tongue, as your ears pick up the click and the calls of flashing cameras wielded by rabid fans and pleading journalists. They have no choice but to part like the sea because your ring of uma bodyguards are here.

In the center, huddled up next to you is your mother. She's afraid. She's recoiling from the accusations thrown at her. But, as your hand wraps around hers, she is filled with awe, and so much pride for how her come.

Her touch is featherlight. Emptiness. No matter what angle you look in this tableau, her features are obscured by sunshine that blinds them into a pure, stark white.

"And if that fails, I'll have a lot of money to search for her, regardless." You conclude.

The words hang in the gap between chair and bed. That's it. That's the core of your desire: a child's wish to see her mother again. That's not so much, isn't it? Not something so grand or ludicrous that the world would spit in your face and call it a sin. Oh, but, if that were the case, you wouldn't be here with merely your mother's shoes. You'd be digging your shoes onto your feet, mumbling out an excuse to her voice floating down from the kitchen, like every other young lady in Tokyo. Your fingers dig into the side of the sheet covering the mattress; a great exhaustion wraps itself around you. One weight has been lifted off, and another one has piled on, it's name a dreadful anticipation. You can't muster much strength to be afraid of what Kaori might say next.

"How badly do you want this to happen?"

When you raise your head again again, Kaori's hands are placed in her lap. A faint trace of mistiness wavers in Kaori's golden eyes. A soft grimace without disdain. Pity and sympathy melding together.

"With every fiber of my being." You say.

Kaori slowly nods and reaches over, patting you on the shoulder. She squeezes the flesh there.

"Then, as your Trainer, it is my duty to make your wish come true."

If Kaori spots your own mistiness gathering at the corner of your eyes, she's tactful enough not to mention it.

Morning, June 27th, 20XX

Kaori puts on her best, which in essence is the same smart blouse and uniform skirt she wore to your recruitment. Stern-faced, she cracks open her whiteboard pointer like a whip and smacks it against the center of a pie chart.

"Listen up! Your debut will be a two thousand meter medium-length race. Do not believe for a second that your familiarity with this distance alone will provide you with a sufficient advantage. Many of your rivals—Cheval Grand, Kitasan Black, Satono Diamond, Mayano Top Gun—are just as familiar with the medium race, and for good reason. Out of all the distances, it is the most common within the Twinkle Series. It is present throughout graded races from G3 to G1. It possesses the most amount of data by virtue of its proliferation. And it lies between the relentlessness of sprints and the endurance war of longs. Go too fast, and you'll burn out. Depend on your stamina, and you'll fail to close the gap at the end. The medium is a nigh-perfect blend of speed and stamina; a crucible that demands awareness, acceleration, pacing, and tactics!

"Conversely, this makes it perfect for evaluating the strengths and weaknesses of aspiring races. Even girls who became sprinters and milers have attempted mediums, like the renowned Taiki Shuttle. They sometimes slot mediums in as their B option when they need a different type of graded race under their belts. The competition for this length, even at the debut level, is far and wide, and so we must not take it lightly!"

You sit there, tail swishing, wearing that big dumb smile you dreamed up yesterday on your showered and eager face.

"Something funny, Ruby?" Kaori demands.

"No." You shake your head. "Not at all! I'm just excited. You're just so…professional!"

A mild flicker of concern zips across Kaori's refined features. No doubt she's questioning what forms of authority figures you encountered in your life. It's nothing sinister—you simply think most teachers suck. Having one that cuts to the point and teaches you what you're interested in is not a breath of fresh air…it's a gulpful of springwater from the fountain of youth. You were never the problem. Your brain simply wasn't being fed enough meals. Eat dog crap, countryside teachers!

"Then please take that excitement towards my next question. Did you research the four racetracks like I asked you to?"

You did. The gist is that Twinkle Series debuts do not have their own special events. They'd clog the calendar beyond repair if they did. Instead, debuts share schedules with pre-open, open and graded race days, typically earlier up in the schedule as appetizers for the main event later down the line. According to the upcoming fortnightly schedule, there are four racetracks available to apply for.

The first is Chukyo Racecourse, located in Toyoake, Aichi. It is home to the Takamatsunomiya Kinen and the Champions Cup. Its track, measuring approximately 1706 meters, runs leftward instead of rightward. It is notable for 1. a second curve that is significantly longer than the first, giving the track an uneven oval shape, and 2. A gradual downhill in the backstretch, followed by a sharp uphill in the homestretch. Patience to conserve stamina is a must for the medium distance race.

The second racecourse is Hakodate Racecourse, located in Hokkaido. Unlike Chukyo, Hakodate is a right-facing course. Its track is a nearly perfect oval, possessing almost claustrophobically tight corners. While its slopes aren't as jutting as Chukyo's, the turf's elevation on average is hilly, resulting in heightened stamina requirements than on average. It is also located near the sea, resulting in lowered temperatures year around. Racing here is a test of positioning and stamina optimization.

Due to its distance, Hakodate Racecourse pulls less numbers than its contemporaries. It also doesn't run any G1 races currently.

The third option is Hanshin Racecourse, located in Takarazuka, Hyogo; home of the Takarazuka Kinen, Osaka Hai, Oka Sho, Hanshin Juvenile Fillies, and last but not least: the Asahi Hai Futurity Stakes. It is also a right-facing course, with a track shaped like a bulged oval, similar to Chukyo. Its elevation, however, is even more brutal, consisting of a mostly flat distance before thrusting a ferocious downhill-uphill combo that threatens to burn out the most seasoned of runners. Additionally, thanks to its turf shape, inner gate runners have tighter corners and shorter straights, whereas outer gate runners have longer and broader stretches. The two are not equal. Excellent judgment to deal with the gate drawing's curse and stamina conversation take the crown home at Hanshin.

The final racecourse is Tokyo Racecourse, home of the February Stakes, NHK Mile Cup, Victoria Mile, Japanese Oaks, Japanese Derby, Yasuda Kinen, the Tenno Sho (Autumn), and the Japan Cup. This normally wouldn't be up for signup if it weren't for the downpour that pushed a bunch of races back towards later dates. Tokyo is considered the 'fair' racecourse, for its long straights, wide turns, a semi-balanced elevation compared to the other three racecourses (a single uphill section before levelling out, starting from the third corner). But that itself is a danger. There are no tricks; everyone has room to breathe. The strongest uma with the fastest legs wins—end of story. As an aside, Tokyo Racecourse is the closest in execution to Tracen's own racecourses. It is also one of the most popular racecourses.

By the time you've finished reciting this information in your head, Kaori has sketched diagrams on the whiteboard in red marker and is now staring you down.

"I am more than capable of training you in any of these racecourses." Kaori says. "I'd also like you to ace your debut so that we can carry that momentum into the rest of the Twinkle Series."

The more a racer wins, the more she's hyped up to get back into the fight, thereby increasing her motivation during training and thus the chances of winning again.

"Have a good think about the course that suits you best. Think about what you'll learn from the race as well, not just the easiest racetrack to run on. An official race is still a practice run in the grand scheme of your career!"

(QM's Note: Running official Twinkle Series races will boost your stats, just like in the mobile game. Boost is dependent on the nature of the competition, the course chosen and whether you win or lose. Heavy competition might teach you Racing Tactics, long straights might teach you Acceleration, inclines might teach you Traversal and so on. These boosts will not be as effective as Training Time.)

Kaori sets the two of you off with some light jogging as she calculates equations in her brain with her finger on her pen. Then, said training session comes to a halt, as another team of three umas comes by and demands your turf slot.

Kaori is having none of it.

"You are mistaken."

"But—"

[Trainer Kaori's FYS check: 14/10 -> Success!]

Kaori plants her feet in front of the other trainer, folds her arms across her chest, and stares him down. "The scheduling is here. See? I arranged this three days in advance. It is immutable, ironclad. You must be mistaken."

"That…" The other Trainer swallows. "…seems to be the case."

"May I request that your trainee over there stop giving Ruby the stink-eye?"

Mollified, the other team backs off. But not before they request partner running, since they've already packed their equipment and brought it here. Kaori acquises. She allows a few laps.

"Twelve hundred meters at the backstretch! You're pace chasing. Tell me how you know your position isn't a liability!"

These are not difficult questions. Any half-competent Tracen student would ace them on a written exam. The difficulty, however, lies in solving them out amidst heavy physical exertion.

"Go, Rubes! Go, go, go!"

Jordan has never been happier to sit on an oversized tire in her life.

[All Attribute progress meters have increased by 5%.]

No rest for the Tracen uma. Your body rests as Kaori takes you to the grass on the side, hands you her laptop and runs you through old debut races. She quizzes you afterwards.

Finally, Jordan teaches you some of her racing expertise. By herself.

"Alright, Rubes. Listen up. I'm not going to repeat this twice."

That's a grammatically accurate but somewhat nonsensical sentence, you think from your standing spot in front of Jordan's proud, punchable face.

"Right. So, like, the medium-long race is a game of endurance too, capiche? You gotta mold your form and your stride to compensate for that. If you bend your knees like this, and squish your body like that, and then when you run you go…" She runs forward. "Woosh! Like this."

She tilts her head back, grinning.

"Pardon?"

"What?"

You raise your head. "What do you mean by 'wooosh'?"

"You didn't explain it that well."

Jordan gives you a frank look. It is exact one you gave Hotaru when you thought she had suddenly developed a brain aneurysm. "Didn't you see what I did?"

"I did."

"So do that."

"I don't know what 'that' is!" You exclaim.

Jordan runs back up to you. She mimes with her hands. "Y'know, the rush. The explosion. It happens when you charge out of the gate but less gas on the pedal. You can also eat a spicy hot burger and feel the hot sauce in your lungs."

Absolute heresy. Spicy food is hell for a singer. A couple of the girls in the underground learned that the hard way.

"You're not making a lick of sense!"

Jordan drags you for a run, which is also fruitless, as it's difficult to determine the intricacies of her stride when she's speeding past you.

Kaori has realised what you already knew at the beginning of the conversation. This was an incredibly terrible idea.

We shall now discuss the new and improved Daily Life system. Here's how it works:

You receive a limited amount of Time Points (TP) at the start of Daily Life Segments. You read the selection of events available. Certain times of the year may provide special events. You vote on how to spend your TP. Rules:

All events cost 1 TP unless specified otherwise. No stat checks are required to initiate any Daily Life event. No dice rolls are required to initiate any Daily Life event, unless specified otherwise. Any events that mention randomness involve rolling the standard 2d12. You may select as many instances of a Daily Life event as your TP limit allows. The QM will decide the time of where events take place unless you explicitly state your preference. Assume every event has an additional 'at <Time>' tag bolted on. 5.1: Daily Life VI

>>[CourseSelect] Hanshin Racecourse

>>[TrainingTime] I want to work on my stamina. (+20% to Stamina progress; +6 to Breathing and +4 to Pain Threshold.)

>>[x] [DailyLife] Plan: Bonds Old And Nooks New

-[x] Spend time with Meisho Tabaru at an ice cream shop

-[x] Attempt to find Oguri Cap

-[x] Spend Time with Aston Machan at the Academy Shrine

-[x] Investigate Tracen rumors

Mood: Great

EXP: 125/220

"Hanshin."

Kaori raises her eyebrows at your answer, a sign that you answering her was beyond her expectations. You were supposed to let the question of the track choice mull over in your head with the time and respect such a pivotal part of your career deserves. She's not too surprised, not saying a word, before she crosses the small distance between the whiteboard and the table to pull up a chair and sit down. Her hands rest in her lap.

Go on, the combo of her posture and expression seems to say. Present your case.

Pressure weighs down on your shoulders. Did Kaori ever try for a law degree like her friend?

"Hanshin. I t—" You catch yourself before the tremors escape from your mouth. It's tricky talking to a brand-new authority figure with candor. Kaori sitting there has a line straight to the squiggly, vibrating bits in your brain. She has the power to veto your plans as your Trainer and set you on a different course, so that edge constricting your chest isn't present for no reason. Convince your Trainer, or fail in getting what you want.

You are certain in this instance that what you want is best. Adults are notoriously stingy in that regard.

"Hanshin's the best fit for me." You say with more confidence.

"Thinking of following in Grass's footsteps, I see," Kaori notes.

You chuckle. "Can't help it, Trainer."

"You're got ambition and spunk in spades, Ruby. An uma like you wouldn't stop with a single graded victory in her first year. You'd go straight for the highest echelons of the sport. It's either the Hopeful Stakes or the Asahi Hai, and given whose protégé you are of, it was barely a decision to peg you for the latter." Kaori folds her arms, puffing out her chest. "I will note that Asahi Hai is a mile race, compared to the Hopeful's medium."

"I understand that." You say. "I'm more edging towards Hanshin for learning the track first."

Which requires you to possess a fighting chance on said track, thereby shifting you and Kaori to the next item on your agenda. You lean down and retrieve a mauve-colored textbook from your bag. You deposit the book on the table, flip it open with a riffle to the desired page, and push it over the flat surface. Kaori takes it by the bottom of its spine and drags it over to her side. What she sees lying in the center is a diagram of a bulged oval, a replication of Hanshin's two thousand meter track in thin black ink. Annotations dot the sides: elevations, starting lines, difficult turning spots marked with icons of slopes, checkerboard flags and blue arrows.

Kaori lets out a soft hum. Nascent approval. The first step. You clear your throat, a gentle grunt, and rip out a rehearsal from your cranial archives.

"We've established my strengths lie around speed, stamina and flexibility, relatively speaking. That's evidenced from my tryouts and the couple of scrimmages I did—we've seen the times. Jordan has acknowledged it, and the other girls are taking me seriously. Hanshin's the best fit for my arsenal. The wide turns won't be much of a problem for me; I'll hook my feet on the ground and swing around like I've always done, plus I don't get as dizzy as the others. The flat, long stretches afterwards are coded for my pace and stamina, and they're chock-full of breathing room for me to plan any corner cases on the fly. That'll compensate for the gate-drawing issue."

Kaori swallows your argument. She shoots out a counter, nary a millisecond later.

"And they place you in the outermost lane?"

[Racing Tactics check: 113/70 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

You snipe back. "I sus out the early speed drawing and angle inwards once everyone's sorted themselves out." You say.

"Innermost lane?" Kaori fires again.

You blast back. "That's not a bad spot. But it means I might get blocked."

"Indeed you might. But if you're blocked…"

"Then I'll adapt before that." You tap your finger on your chin. "I hold my position just behind the front runners before trying to peel inwards when the homestretch is in view. There's a crap ton of distance there waiting for me to run across. Of course, if I can find a placement by catching my opponents off guard with my centrifugal tech, I will."

No response from Kaori. No barely concealed disdain, or a growing smirk—so not a denial either. You've surpassed the bare minimum of repeating an article straight from Umapedia. It's not enough, nowhere near the homestretch, and you wouldn't be sitting in this office if you were satisfied with that.

Her silence is a swing of momentum; roll with it or end up a plodder.

You turn the textbook's page. Hanshin's replica waves goodbye in exchange for three of its brethren.

"Chukyo's okay, but it can't train me for the G1s I like more, while Hakodate's too irregular. Now, I thought about Tokyo a lot."

"It's popular for a good reason." Kaori says.

The Japan Cup, the Derby, the Autumn Tenno Sho, a bevy of Triple Tiara races, and so on. The G2s and G3s on Tokyo Racecourse aren't too shabby, either. The place is steeped in prestige, dating all the way back to the beginning of umamusume racing in Japan. When kid umas think about the race of their dreams, it's usually at Tokyo Racecourse.

"It's the most similar to Tracen's turf." You remark. The flat and stable type. "That's sort of the reason I didn't pick it."

Kaori glances up. "Most would call that an oxymoron."

You raise a palm. "Hear me out, Trainer. Hear me out. I'm used to running on odd forms of terrain. I spent most of my Tokyo life running in whatever parks and alleys were available to me before the morning rush before arriving at Tracen. Most of my trodden ground was uneven because why would the groundskeepers give a damn for how a struggling uma racer wannabe thought about standardization and well-maintained turf, right? Turns out it's a blessing in disguise, as those bumps and grooves fit more in line with Hanshin and Tokyo. Grass and a few of the other Golden Gen girls dropped hints telling me that Tracen's turf can actually trick racers if they practice too much on it. They get too comfortable and slip up on the real deal."

You lift your hand and sweep it outwards. "Plus, I lean more towards right-handed than left-handed. Forget about compensating for the motor asymmetry. And I've got a good balance of speed and stamina, which is another aspect that's more Hanshin and Tokyo. Once I put learn the track…"

"Those advantages of yours will chain together and intensify." Kaori finishes for you.

"Exactly!"

You beam at Kaori and hope it doesn't come across as insincere.

Kaori leans back in her seat, humming. She closes her eyes, disinterested, rolls her neck for a second, then leans forward to inspect your notebook again. She flips back to the Hanshin diagram, where she runs a finger across the edge of the replicated track, stopping at a set of triangular marks near the finish line.

"Slopes. You're lacking in those. Before you protest, Ruby, I do have plans for them, inspired by a certain 'cyborg' among your year level."

Forewarning strikes you, a great heaving motion swelling from upwards, that you register right after Kaori pulls the pin on her grenade and flings it at your head. "A cyborg, who excelled in her tryouts, taking first place where you didn't. Who might end up facing against you in debut through her pursuit for the Asahi Hai."

The ethereal smoke wipes the joy from your big, stupid face. "Bourbon's challenging the Asahi Hai, too?"

"Kuronuma. Another Trainer colleague of mine. He mentioned it in the lounge a few days ago." Kaori says, with a slight sting of distaste to her tone. "The man is built like a Greek sculpture and, more often than not, behaves like one. He won't open his mouth if he doesn't believe there's anything worth speaking."

Your mouth is frozen shut. This is a curveball and a half.

Mihono Bourbon. Her face grows in your mind's eye. Voluminous, desaturated pinkish-brown bangs. A futuristic headband in front of long, thin ears. Her speech is robotic. Her facial muscles don't twitch. And her strides are so practiced and consistent, there's no other uma in your generation who can ever compete.

You can't count her as her friend. That's more Rice Shower's forte, apparently. What you are aware of is her results. During her tryout race, she swam through air while the rest of the competition crawled through quicksand—an absolute blowout that put Tabaru's lead to shame. Hush settled over the crowd. Love hearts and yen signs bloomed in the eyes of the press watching. Some went as far and said she was a Crown champion in the making. Weeks later, word around the grape vine is that Bourbon undertakes slope training suited for graded racers as much as three times per day, no doubt sweating up a storm yet with no hint or rumor of any complaints or corralling by that Trainer Kuronuma of hers.

Kitasan, Happy Meek and Rice Shower were tough enough opponents in your tryout race. Had Bourbon joined in, you probably wouldn't have grabbed a podium placement at all.

As for her Trainer you faintly remember him baring his abs on the track. A couple of the girls nearby swooned; you wondered who this strange man was and why none of the security was asking him to cover those gains up. After learning he was an accomplished Tracen Trainer, it all made sense, and admittedly, they were pretty solid abs you could grate cheese on.

Rumor has it that Trainer Kuronuma learned how to handle umas from backstreet brawls of Tokyo's bubble crash. Any human intimate with an uma's fighting spirit will pass that down onto any trainee.

You suck in air through your teeth. It's visible. It's audible.

"That's bad. Really, really bad, if true."

But it's not breaking news. Most of the rookie generation is lining up to debut around the same period. Conflicts with your rivals are almost guaranteed.

"If Bourbon or Kitasan or someone else appears, then she appears. Nothing I can do about it. I'll just deal."

"And what will that entail?" Kaori asks.

"More training. Figuring out her strengths and weaknesses? Figuring out mine? I will admit, I super wanted to scrim against her, but she turned my offers down. Her glutes and calves must be as thick as sandbags by now. But I think I can beat her." You shake your head, hands and thighs clasping tighter. "Nah. Sorry. Those are the wrong words. She's not impossible. Kitasan wasn't, so she's not either. I will defeat her."

"Bold words." Kaori murmurs. She rests a hand under her delicate chin.

But can you back them up? Goes the unsaid phrase.

[Artistry Check: 61/35 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

What's with the questions? That's what you're here for, isn't it? Imaginary Hotaru says in her haughty rich villainess cosplay, with gothic frills and ribbons and all that.

No sweat. I can take Bourbon on any day! Imaginary Saya slams a fist into her palm.

Imaginary Chiwa, the old friend of Kaori that Jordan described as having the face of a serial killer, just folds her arms and glares at your Trainer. She's fifteen years old here. Look me in the eye, Kaori, truly do so for once in the life, and conceptualize the magnificent absurdity of asking that question.

You don't put on either of these masks, despite a tiny part of you that's tempted to act the third. A mysterious solidarity ties you and this Chiwa together.

"Gotta learn slopes somewhere." You say with a shrug, "Going from debut to maiden is not the end of the world."

Even if the prospect burns caustic and thick on your tongue. Kaori's of a mutual mind, judging from her frown.

Silence.

You breathe in. Your throat goes parched. The glee you concluded the first portion of your speech seems far away. That's it. That's your case. You've said as much as you can. Time to watch where the sword falls.

Kaori looks down at your textbook again. She flips through the last pages in silence. Occasionally, she mouths a word or taps the page with her ballpoint pen. Her posture doesn't relax; she refuses to move her lips, just a pure stretch of reading, thinking, and planning. Around you, the air seems to still, thickening like rice pudding. The office clock ticks in the background; a football soars and lands with a soft thump in the courtyard below. Your fingers play with the hem of your skirt, and you force yourself not to roll your tongue and play with the inside of your cheek.

You've done a good job. Grass and Digital said so, both offering to help you practice. Both drew from their own G1 expertise. Both reassured you, which is why you spoke up today with confidence. Sitting in this chair and feeling the seconds crawl by in your bones—you're spotlighted. Grilled like a hamburger patty in the back of a smoky diner kitchen. These nerves, these reactions, were born from your butt and tail smooshed in the plastic chair as the producers behind the audition table whispered and gossiped and shot prying eyes from behind their paper sheets.

You can dodge, deflect, or endure a punch. Words are softer, squishier. They drag on when dissipated behind the receiver's mask.

Kaori, you realise, doesn't abhor the businesswoman spirit her family so lavishly furnished her with. Her issue lay in being unable to channel that spirit to her own volition. Otherwise, she's more than willing to draw it as a tool in her arsenal. Those smiles and gentle words she attracted you with are reserved for off the clock. On the job, it's full speed ahead, gears set to at least six point something on the perfectionism scale, no mercy required.

This is one of those scenarios where you should feel offended. Interrogations suck. But at least Kaori raised valid counterarguments. At least she presented herself as genuine in contemplating what you said, instead of stalling for time.

Is…is she preparing you for an actual sponsorship interview? You wouldn't put it past her attitude. She must've brought Jordan to tears back in their old days.

At long last, Kaori pushes the notebook over. "Any further objections?"

You can't help but flinch a little. "Pardon?"

"This is your last chance to switch to another track if you're uncertain. Otherwise, I'm going to make the call to the URA and mark you down for Hanshin." Kaori says.

A blink. The gradual echo of a trumpet rises. "You agree?"

"I'd be a fool not to, after this much homework from your end. You've exceeded my expectations, Ruby." Kaori replies, unblinking. She then smiles. A true, light-hearted one. "I see no reason to turn you down."

Your shoulders slump and you let out a sharp exhale, struggling to resist the urge to throw up your hands and screech. "Thank you very much!"

Kaori waves it off. "No need to be so dramatic."

"Hey, you're the one who started it."

"Perhaps. But I did say we had to ace your debut. This is the bare minimum." And she smirks.

You will be pissed off in the future. You will bemoan this to Tabaru over the dinner table. For now, you are too relieved to care.

And that's the end of the track selection. After training that day, Kaori logs an application for the debut race happening at the Shirasagi Stakes. She shows you the confirmation printout the next morning.

"You know what to do now, yes?"

Train hard, rest well, and spend what free time you have as best you can. The usual.

You pump your fist and grin, causing a nearby Tosen Jordan to gag. Yep, you've totally got this!

>>DAILY LIFE: BEGIN.

"Further investment is to be placed into Japan's rice production, following the torrential rains earlier in the previous quarter. Critics from the agricultural industry warn that too large a surplus may cause too low prices…"

"Tired of four walls and a ceiling, yet afraid of going outside? Spinning your head with the crushing reality of a wasted life? Hire an uma temp sister now! Guaranteed to turn your introvert into an immaculate extrovert!"

"Convenience store restrooms—a liability, or a public service in disguise?"

"Satono Diamond, heiress of the Satono Group, revealed the nitty-gritty details of her training through a series of clips across Umastagram. Commenters and prominent figures in the racing scene have praised her tenacity in the face of looming adversity. The young heiress is speculated to hold her debut at…"

"I tell ya, it's hidden radio signals on the airwaves. They're primed at a frequency uma ears can't hear. They're beaming the same toxic crap that causes apartments in Taiwan to randomly collapse. Game over, man. Game over!"

Noon, June 27th, 20XX

Life resumes as normal, more or less. There are more burdens, of course. The ramped-up homework. The additional training. The debut race at Yonago, a sword dangling over your head, the blade gleaming with the promise of public failure and embarrassment. Instances of umas tripping or falling or doing worse are well documented in Umatok and Pakatube; you may or may not have had a bad dream about a video starring you, the title along the lines of SHE HAD ONE JOB AND STILL…😭, complete with harsh bass booms and that rapid-fire editing style where words flash on the screen like musket shots. Adjacent to that, there's the case of Team IKZE and the incredibly bratty end closer.

At some point of your life, you were terrified of embarrassing yourself on stage. Then you got over it because, honestly, what good is stage fright when you've food bills to pay. Putting in your hardest and falling short? That is the real terror. Battle of Shibuya Maidens 20XV; a hundred groups attended, FAITHFUL practiced until legs ran raw and voice boxes threatened to scrape like sandpaper, and it culminated in FAITHFUL's best display of enka rock that ended up with the fantastic result of eighth place.

Anticlimactic. A cause for a trembling lip and some tears trickling down, smudging makeup. Hotaru punched a wall and instantly regretted it. Sponsors still ended up seeking Anafabula for deals, so it more or less recuperated the lesson bills. Didn't remove much of the sting. The entire group looked at the participation ribbon and decided as a collective that you could all have done more. Much much, more.

In retrospect, you are far more equipped and prepared for your racing debut than the Battle, so why are you complaining?

You endure the new stresses. You knead the growing tension in your stomach into fulfilling emotional bread. You eat actual bread. Sandwiches, croissants, healthy barley treats for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. The cycle crawls with the sun and sleeps with the moon. Wake up, brush your teeth, brush your tail, eat a healthy breakfast of porridge or miso soup and rice and fish, then attend whatever classes you have and train your soles off with Kaori and Jordan in the afternoon. Homework at night, then plop under the covers in your still-soft dorm bed and crash. Morning runs in the stinging cold air later, brushed off with a hot shower.

Rinse and repeat.

Time flows.

The skies around Tracen grow warmer, muggier. Flowers across the lawns and the gardens bloom bright. The odd drizzle splashes down from occasional dark clouds, softening the turf and giving it that fresh grass smell. Kaori instantly puts the softened turf to good use. She whips up a soft-ground training exercise and slots it into your training regimen. A test of maintaining balance against your wet feet while dealing with the extra friction from the squelching and the sticky mud strands—it's hell on cleats, honestly.

Near the tail of one training session, you catch yourself sweating and stumbling towards the bench, strands of hair clinging to the sides of your face slick with humidity. A quick glance into the water bottle as you put out-down; it reflects your stretched out, red-cheeked visage. This is your life, your harrowed smile says. The duty you have decided upon for yourself. The new niche, that which defines Satono Ruby as the uma reflected in your view. It's a road of thorns and pools of smouldering lactic acid, where you must run, listen and study in such close parallel that it's almost synonymous, a dozen other upstarts clamouring for the finish line, and you couldn't find the whole skedaddle any less marvelous.

Kids, adults, old men and women. So many live their lives without living out their best lives. Forget the Tokyo Dome, that half-baked 'dream' of yours; this heat, this rancor of the physique is what you wish to bathe in for the rest of your mortal life.

You throw yourself into your routine. You are so immersed, in fact, that you exit the shower some other day, laughing at how outstanding it is that there are no other commitments worth paying attention to. Like, imagine if you had to eat sweets with your friends and ruin your calorie intake. How awful would that be!

Wait.

"Ruby?" Tabaru says from across the table. "Are you going to eat that?"

You stare down at your chicken udon, full of intertwined nutrient goodness, then at Tabaru, then at the rubix cube she's holding.

"Ruby? Tabaru echoes.

The next thing you know, you're sitting in a stall in the girls' bathroom, your head in your hands.

You forgot.

Try as you might to deny it, the fact remains the same. You forgot. You utter imbecile, you forgot. Your promise with paper s—Gold Ship.

She's Gold Ship. The paper sack girl was, is, Gold Ship. That race has passed and gone. You can stop pretending now…or can you? Team Spica's got eyes and ears. There aren't any Tiara champions holding ropes and sacks heading your way, right? Just to be extra careful, you stand up and peek above the stall doors. Nothing. The bathroom is deserted, the lone silver lining above this swelling typhoon cloud, because you forgot the promise you made with the Gold Ship.

For a brief, brief moment, you consider the possibility of letting it be. There are reasons. Reasons your traitorous brain generate with the speed of rheumatic hands banging on a typewriter. Gold Ship's a busy uma with lots on her plate. She's got better things to do than mess with a rookie. Tabaru's dealt with her mounting pressure for the past couple of weeks; can't she keep internalizing that until after your debut concludes? Look at how packed your schedule is.

Your ego then backhands you across the cheeks and tells you to forget the sack. Forget being yelled at like a normal uma. Who the heck do you think you are, acting so cheeky and smug? Gold Ship doesn't have to get physical, or call her friends, or look you in the eye at all, in fact. She merely has to play that stupid Alice in Eviland trash on the school PA system to reduce you to a quivering mess.

The last dregs of saliva in your mouth dry up. Past assumptions combust into smoke. The air reeks of old uma piss. The violins—no. No, no, no, a thousand million billion times NO.

You also realise you considered ditching Tabaru to stew in your own misery, which makes you feel like a total jackass.

The question is popped that very afternoon.

"Tabaru!"

Class is over, the bell has rung, and students vacate the classroom. Your roommate looks up from her desk. So do a couple of students, midway through packing their bags with their books.

"What's up?" Tabaru asks.

"Wanna get ice-cream?"

"Ice-cream?" Tabaru repeats. "As in, now?"

"Nah, tomorrow." You reply. "There's a parlor in Fuchu I've been eyeing. Grass told me Spe, as in Special Week, couldn't stop yapping about it when they visited. According to her, the chocolate and caramel mix is to die for; and I got my monthly cut from my idol group's streaming services, so it'll be my treat."

Tabaru closes her mouth shut. She mull over the idea, then lifts her uniform skirt to knead a roll of flesh on her belly. That familiar, tense-lipped grimace returns. It's a sight you've seen too often for your liking in your shared dorm room.

"I dunno about my weight." She mutters.

You can't help but scoff. You transform it into a chuckle half-way through.

"Tabby. Tabaru. I was an umadol."

She lifts her head. "Yeah?"

"As an actual professional who used to work in the music industry and used to hang around human girls with bodily issues and gym habits and crap, trust me when I say you are nowhere near fat."

Tabaru ponders this, squeezing a roll of abdominal flesh through her uniform.

"You're leaner than me. But we can get the yoghurt if you wish. I promise we'll only get small servings."

"Creek did say I need more on my bones." Tabaru mutters.

"Also, I promised Gold Ship we'd go together."

Tabaru tilts her head. "Oh, that was a thing."

"You forgot?"

"She told me with a surprise hug that my roommate had done something super grand and amazing—think I was trying to work on homework so I only paid half attention. Trainer's been running me ragged too. I wouldn't have remembered it if you hadn't reminded me."

When you fail to respond for several seconds, Tabaru leans in closer. "Are you okay, Ruby? You look tense."

A blood vessel in above your eyelid almost throbs. Almost. There are not enough windows in this room to throw stones at.

Okay, but bad Ruby. Very bad Ruby. Compose yourself, you. You're not here to seethe over Tabaru's obliviousness. You're here to help her, a task that sounds unnecessary to the outside uma at first glance. From their perspective, Tabaru's decent. Ruffled and worn down from a maths class, but who isn't? Oh, you shall laugh at that. You will cackle and wheeze while clutching your stomach to hide the pain. It's a ploy from Tabaru, a true facade. She'll put up a brave front in public, smiling, nudging her head, rolling her eyes, a bevy of normal reactions that fooled you for a time, but once she thinks you're not looking, or when she's immersed in a documentary or a practice run, the symptoms seep out from the cracks. Furrowed brows, ears pressed back, conversations reduced to grunts and single-sentences through gritted teeth!

It's a lock. A heart under strain. The behavior of a machine made of flesh, more akin to aging middle managers under stress than a teenage uma living in the best racing academy within Japan.

And no, before this hypothetical uma gets funny ideas, what Tabaru displays isn't standard umamusume adolescent nerves. You did your homework. Aston Machan, Rice Shower, Happy Meek and Kawakami Princess. All four girls bemoaned their debut in their own ways; Rice Shower acted the most nervous with that hunched posture and mild stutter. None of them were ready to crack like your roommate does acts every other night. The most relaxed you've seen her these days is when she's buried her nose in a textbook during morning classes, which should be ironic but now sounds more like sense, and is just plain sad.

You wish you could sit Tabaru down. You wish you could confess to her how you've lived in that dreadful space. How thoughts that churn too much will rot and devour a healthy mind from the inside out. You don't want a potential rival to fall prey to her own nerves, nor do you wish for your friend to suffer in silence.

If only.

If only!

As if the above wasn't enough, you're adding another factor into this mix. Tabaru's too proud to listen. Again, this sounds ridiculous on the surface, but no—Tabaru's got more in common with her cousin Orfevre than you or the rest of society thinks. They're both strong-willed and think they're always right. You've breached this topic of nerves with Tabaru multiple times, only to be stonewalled with a "I'm fine" or a "I've got this, alright?". Being the respectful girl you are, you always backed down, not wanting to stoke unwanted fires within your dorm room, a decision which has snowballed out of control into a huge mistake, if Gold Ship of all umas can see it. Damn it, Tabaru! Is this a Hidaka cultural thing?

[History check: 56/100 -> Failure.]

Heck if you know. You're in Tracen, not Azabu High. You could ask Jewel or Tomoe, but no offence to them, they're not intimate with Tabaru, either.

So. The symptoms. What's the damage?

You arrive at a mental block around this point. It's tall. It's mighty. It's sneering from the upper reach of its mountainous girth. Stubborn, you refuse to leave it unscaled and take to the Fuchu streets to stroll and ponder. The tactic worked for dance routines, so it'll work for this. You walk a few blocks, go window shopping inside a convenience store, pluck up a stray dandelion from between a crack in the road for a sniff, before coming up with three candidates. The first is Pelte's injury.

You shake your head.

Nah. It doesn't fit. Tabaru's already moved past that incident. She tolerated a joke from Jewel a couple of days ago. A friend gets injured, everyone cries and offers support, and healing takes its due course. Such is life.

Her team, then? Her Trainer?

Doesn't fit, either. A few days ago, you pestered Tabaru about the juicy details because it's Trainer Nase! The Fumino Nase! Kaori's better, obviously, but c'mon, how many friends in your life tutored under URA's biggest human celebrities? Tabaru rolled her eyes. She ended up spilling the juicy details, such as the fact Nase and Kaori are cut from the same, white-collar cloth; that the press sometimes swings by to watch and irritate everyone; that her team consists of a Symboli exchange student from America, that aloof rival from the Overlord Generation with the deceased sister, a rich young lady that Daitaku Helios simps for, and Smart Falcon.

You're not thinking about that last one. You refuse to.

Anyway, nowhere in that conversation was abuse or harassment from Tabaru's team.

Is it her debut race, then?

The answer is yes, via process of elimination. The answer feels too simple, too incomplete, a gut hunch that intensifies once you scroll through socmed that night and eye a couple of clips from Orfevre's Japan Cup. The last time Tabaru raced in public was technically at the tryouts. She'd acted enthusiastic before the race, accepting yours and her crew's kind words and promising to do the best. She caught wind of Stay Gold and the rest of her cousins. Her lip split with blood; she burst out of the gate and stormed across the turf as if a Horror itself was hounding her.

After the race, Stay Gold congratulated her, and Tabaru bowed like a yakuza underling towards her boss. It wasn't a bit.

Are the Golds…bullying Tabaru behind your back?

You scowl at the thought. It morphs into a mild frown. No, probably not. The Golds possess vivid personalities, but none of them are what you'd call malicious. More rumors would've circulated, if true. Special Week, or the rest of Team Spica, wouldn't be okay with running alongside a bully.

Tabaru's simply super nervous around the de facto youth head, then.

Why?

The thought hammers your skull. It makes you wish you could rip it out and plaster it on a piece of paper for a mind map. Why, why, why? Because this is how Tabaru's underlings behaved and she's mirroring them? Because it's in her nature to fret? Because something happened in the past to urge Tabaru to be nervous?

Hold on.

[Logic check: 96/90 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

The last thread. That something happening in the past…or at least, Tabaru believes it did? An imaginary event, conjured from a game of verbal telephone, that implanted a specific fear in Tabaru? It tells her to demonstrate respect to her senpais whenever they meet, wherever they exist in the same space, lest she suffer dire consequences. The Golds are not just a collection of friends; they are a family, and since they exist in the world of umamusume racing, they want victory.

A victory that exists only in Tabaru's mind.

[(Psyche check: 10/11 || Intimidation check: 45/60 || Subterfuge check: 76/65) -> Success! +10 EXP.]

Tabaru believes she's not living up to the Golds' standards. She is, in a sense, lying to herself.

Suddenly, you're wide awake. Your head is clear, the neurons burning and whizzing with electricity. You don't want to jump to a conclusion this early without evidence; this is a hypothesis after all, yet you can't deny these thought patterns slot nice and clean into the surrounding situation like none prior have. It explains why Tabaru acts on guard around her cousins, yet doesn't run from them. It's why stories regarding her times with them are scant around the cafeteria table. She trembled in front of Stay Gold, not out of terror, but in apology. A healthy, decent relationship between her and the Golds lies buried beneath Tabaru's inferiority complex!

And none of them have brought it up because the Golds don't wish to pry or respect Tabaru's discretion, while Tabaru views herself as an ant compared to their titanic prowess, refusing to speak up because it's the more respectful course of action. She's super wrong! You've witnessed how talks between girls can spiral out of control when misunderstandings arise—thanks, Hotaru and Kaede on that one Christmas. So much truth is kept silent because both parties assume and assume and get worse and worse. If left unchecked, nothing will be left but hate and wrath!

The wind blows. The bitter, sun-setting coldness stings against your bare skin. You rise, face turned towards Tracen, mouth set in a firm line.

You could be wrong. This is your hypothesis, after all. But it's a start, a real course of action: to invite Gold Ship, sit her down over ice-cream and give a good, stern talk to Tabaru about the misunderstandings. She'll have to do it from a position of authority, but if she mixes in a dose of compassion, it'll work.

The relationship between you and Manager Suzuki is evidence of that.
