Early Morning, June 29th, 20XX

A thought strikes you in the middle of lunch. Have you drifted away from Oguri Cap?

At first glance, the question sounds silly. Silly and audacious. Friends with Oguri Cap—who do you think you are? Tamamo Cross? Belno Light? Pathetic. You're just some random, pitiful straggler she raced with once. The first real race of your life, in fact. She shared a table with you at lunch, stalked you to a department store, comforted you on the worst day of the year…alright, perhaps you do have reason to feel lonesome over here.

The curious part is after almost severing Diamond's fingers and loaning her lovely casual jacket for you to cry your eyeballs out in, she ran back to Kasamatsu to deal with the torrential rain, returned, and practically vanished off the face of your radar. It wasn't as if there were no opportunities for you and her to connect. She spectated your tryouts and you've waved to her a few times in passing.

A nasty voice, a remnant from your disenfranchised childhood, says Oguri got bored of you. She doesn't enjoy your company. You should be grateful Oguri spent any amount of her precious free time with you at all.

You shove a dirty sock into that voice's mouth. Next, you head out to search for Oguri herself. The job's over sooner than you expected. She's sitting on a bench on the side of the main path cutting through the school courtyard.

"Oguri!"

"Ruby." She lifts her head up from where she was reading a newspaper. A paper one with solid black ink, earthy scent and all. Gosh, how old-fashioned. Oguri squints at you. You notice you're standing directly under the sun and move to the side before the glare burns her eyeballs. "Long time no see. What's up?"

"Nothing much. Wanna hang out today?" You say.

"Sure," Oguri replies.

She folds her newspaper, tucks it under her arm, and stands up.

"Let's go."

You don't answer, due to your mouth hanging open as your brain short-circuits. Eh? Eh, eh, eh? Are your ears deceiving you? Did you hear Oguri agree to hang out with you? You aren't required to chase Oguri through the halls whilst Air Groove chases you from behind?

"Ruby? You good?"

"I'm good!" You squeak.

Oguri doesn't believe you. You wouldn't believe yourself. Clearly, nothing needs to be done, since Oguri is standing up and surveying you with concern. Why did you even buy tickets to that train of thought, you dolt? It wasn't rational. It wasn't plausible. Oguri's not flighty, she's as blunt as a hammer; you must've had a bad dream last night, and you should discard the brain virus of its Tracen and Tracen is the home of multiple unhinged weirdos who kick fences or drink martinis that aren't alcoholic and now Oguri tilts her head, as if asking a silent question, and you barely refrain from shuddering out of your bones and melting into a pile of goo.

[Composure check: 86/50 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

"Apologies." You cough into your fist. "I thought you were busier."

"Not much these days. Events have calmed down a lot since the downpour. There's my degree, but I'm on top of that thanks to Belno's coaching." Oguri says. She folds her newspaper, then glances towards the front gate. "You got any particular plans?"

"For the most part, yeah! I've got training in the afternoon." You pause. "I super have to get on track of that. My Trainer will kill me if I don't, and then I will."

"Gotcha. They set a date for the debut?"

"Yonago Stakes. Fourteenth of July."

Oguri whistles. "That's a fortnight away. You've got your work cut out for you. I'm rooting for you. Do better than mine, yeah?"

Well then. Forget one hundred and twenty percent, a la Kaede. You're putting in one hundred and fifty percent the next training session. The Ashen Beast is cheering for you. Hotaru is so not going to believe this on LANE tonight.

[+10 to the next starting gate roll!]

"Otherwise…" Oguri lifts her legs, twisting her individual feet in a stretch. She hops up and down, then lifts her arms. "Hang with me, Ruby. I'll take you someplace nice, my treat."

"Oh no, I couldn't."

"I insist. Seriously."

"I've got money."

Oguri grins. "Senpai privileges. You gotta listen. No backsies, alright?"

You gasp in mock-offense, hands flying to your chest. "You wound me, Senpai!"

"It's what you deserve, Ruby. Call it a surprise!" Oguri walks off, beckoning you to follow with a tug of her hand. You do so with glee.

You reach Oguri. You walk side-by-side with her. The two of you chat nonsense: decaf versus real coffee, new shoes on the market, the new dishes at the cafeteria. Absolute paper-thin garbage that distracts you from your duties and is fun to indulge in. You once again affirm that Oguri is more transparent than opaque, an uma who wears her heart on her sleeve.

That's when you notice.

[Psyche check: 10/10 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

Wistfulness on her lips. The smile she's wearing doesn't quite reach her eyes. They're aching, in fact. It's not malice. It's…apologetic? You're uncertain if that's the right term. You're puzzled as to why. It's not as if Oguri has done anything to hurt or offend you. The opposite, more like.

"Ruby?"

You blink. "Uh…"

"Don't want a drink?" Oguri says, pointing to the nearby vending machine.

"No, I mean, yes, I do. I'll have what you're having. That's a decaf, right?"

Must be a trick of the light. The sun's been blinding. It's compensating for the dark, stormy skies last month.

Anyway, where is Oguri taking you?

Morning, July 2nd, 20XX

Shocking news! That shrine you thought belonged to Tracen? It doesn't. The shrine is a separate entity overseen by the Association of Shinto Shrines, as is the case of most Japanese shrines. That means, yep, that you are wrong. You fell for the colloquial trick, the verbal telephone fallacy, and deep down your own stupid superego is pointing and laughing up a storm. You are also climbing the thick stone stairs to its summit, much to your chagrin.

The story began centuries ago. The 'Tracen shrine' was constructed first anywhere between Jomon and Heian. It enjoyed a prosperous, if slow, existence, only increasing in activity during holidays and special ceremonies, as is the case with many shrines around the country. In 19XX, Tracen Academy was built, and the shrine abruptly faced the problem of students running up and down the steep, hundred-plus steps or so to train their glutes and quadriceps.

The training happened so frequently that the regular shrine-goers became blocked from access. The stone steps also wore and crumbled at the edges, thanks to the very real cleats the students were wearing. The Association raised a fuss, Tracen enacted a ban, and it succeeded as well as frying takoyaki in the middle of a snowstorm. Nothing else nearby competed with the shrine's stairs. Students sneaked in at the dead of night to train, rules be damned. At the worst, or best, depending on the diaries donated by alumni, up to half a dozen kids raced on the stairs at a time. Each one of them wore mufflers, fancy fur-lined shoes closer to slippers, on their feet to quash the noise. The group was only caught when one of the faculty installed hidden cameras in a great oak tree up top.

Director Akikawa's predecessor threw up his or her hands and decided clashing against the desires of several hundred umas was too much trouble. A new agreement was drawn up between the shrine and Tracen. Students were permitted to train on the steps, at the expense of following a strict schedule and contributing to the shrine's maintenance at regular intervals.

This is where you were. You were one of the unlucky saps picked according to the random draw. Most umas groan or accept their fate with resignation. You, upon receiving the slip of paper, felt your heart squeeze out a dollop of spite. Such was your antipathy, to the prospect of anything that cage in the countryside, motivated by neither payment, nor the quest for inspiration, nor the joy of helping your friends; you seriously contemplated explaining your circumstances to President Rudolf under the excuse of emotional hardship.

No dice.

Rudolf wouldn't have allowed it. You're no favorite of hers. And you are nothing if not grateful for your enrolment at Tracen. Thus, on this quiet, sleepy day, where families enjoy picnics in parks, you are here, standing atop the shrine's summit.

The torii gate swings into view, tall and proud and its red paint chipped. A sizeable crack rests on the right post, located on the section of the curvature that faces the left. The shape resembles a crushed walnut. Cause: damage by throwing. Not the wind nor the rain. Beyond that, patches of stray weeds and moss line the cracks of the concrete-bricked path leading to the front. At the back: donation box, wooden supports, balcony and sloped roofs; holes and nicks in each. A gentle gust blows southeastward from where the small wooden fence meets the city skyline, drifting pungent, heavy incense and that old and dry, foresty cedar smell from the walls. Rows of white zig-zagging paper strips, the shide, dangle from above the shrine awning.

The wind picks up, and they sway. Like a small child's kite. Like a lost tissue stained with tomato sauce and mustard, scattering across a park pavement. Like your old clothes on the line, your small hands reaching for the pegs and the wicker basket.

A hand reaches for your forehead. Sweat beads. The sun glares down on your exposed back. Dragging your eyes from the…pretty much everything, you lower your head and plod along to the shade offered by a nearby oak tree. You lean against it, then bounce off as the thick rope wrapped around the trunk digs into the side. More shide are there. One of the komainu glares at you from his position. His tooth is chipped.

To fix that, you can't. You have to call a stonemason and have the fella carted away. Replaced, even. The damage is too minute to be smoothed over with concrete paste.

You grimace.

The past is leaking. Thick, slimy fluids slithering from cracks in the dam. It hasn't even been a minute since you arrived here. You close your eyes, try to squeeze it out, and fail. The scents, the whistles and the creaks clump on your nostrils and ears in a smorgasbord of cloying, pasty nostalgia.

[Mood has decreased to Good.]

Back in the underground, when you pulled up your legit miko experiences for concept sessions and lyric writing, you at least contented yourself with how opposed the underground scene was to your old duties. They didn't find out about your childhood until the half-way through the second year. Following that, the first time you arrived at Tracen, Makitanefukukitaru was here. She distracted you from the past by being Makitanefukukitaru. Amusing, then concerning. Especially when the story of the missing friend was brought up.

(You hope that friend is recovering from her soul damage. Royalty treatment in a good hospital somewhere.)

Right now, you have—

[World Resonance check: 108/50 -> Success! Trivial: +0 EXP.]

The other uma accompanying you on this duty. A silver lining. She's arriving soon, as in almost right this instant. Her dainty figure climbs up the steps, her bag jostling on her back. Her steps tread light. Her fingers cluster around an object thin and hard. The torii gate welcomes her shadows. There. The scent of marshmallows tinges you, softness overlapping the sugar, and she's raising her hand in three, two, one—

"Ruby."

You raise a hand back. "Heya, Machan."

Machan strolls up, joining you in the shade. Her forehead is also damp with sweat. "Rough night?"

"To an extent. More of a rough morning, honestly. Not even Grass's matcha helped." You reply. That's saying something, given how expensive those little packets are. Machan understands. You shared one packet with her a week ago.

"Not too keen about this, then. I'm in the same boat. This allotment of our time leaves much to be desired." Machan hums a soft note, gazing across the yard. "There's a non-insignificant part of me that wishes I under the stern watch of my Trainer."

"I know, right?" You exclaim. "Why can't they get retired runners on this? Why are they siphoning our valuable energy and time doing crap that isn't going to train or help us study?"

"It's reminiscent of the unfair randomness of wider society. Or, as my Trainer put it, 'shit happens. Suck it up, kiddo'."

Machan says it so softly, so within her usual sweetness, you can't help but chortle.

"Did they give you the jury duty excuse, too?" Machan asks, leaning back against the tree.

"They did." You say.

"It's inaccurate. Jury duty is informed in advance. They only gave us a couple of days."

"It's the kind of stuff that's there because the grown-ups can't be bothered to fix it."

Machan nods in response.

"Couldn't they, like, hire actual staff? Is Tracen that desperate for money?" You continue.

Machan breathes in. "Big institutions like Tracen are often in debt. They own a lot of assets, true, but the money is illiquid, unlike coins or cash. The banks let them get away because they technically have enough resources to repay the debt. At least, this is the laconic version I heard from my mother when she worked in private."

Right. You remember. Machan's mom was a doctor. A risky, high-paying job that involves long hours away from home. Machan spent a great deal of childhood as a hospital girl, and not for any real illness of hers. She must've picked up grown-up concepts from the patients she ran across.

"God, Machan, you are just so correct and smart and cool today. You should run for the Student Council and fix this stupid process once and for all."

Machan smiles. "Paperwork isn't my thing."

"Is it anyone's?" You say. Maybe Kaori…no, Jordan told you Kaori conceals her frustration.

"You should come to my mom's hospital one day."

"I'm down. I'd take you anywhere to get out of this." You say, yawning. "You, me, the movie theater, two tubs of popcorn. We'll burn the calories off running to and fro. Or do ten push-ups for every cringe scene in the movie."

Machan titters. "Goodness, what kind of movies do you watch?"

"The kinds left behind in coffin motels. Bad, bad comedies, along with anime no-one bothered to pay as collectibles."

The concern on Machan's face is real. "We must fix that. What about Gloriana III?"

"Nah. Tabaru watched that and said the queen mom in that one would piss me off to high heaven. I'll borrow a DVD from the dorm lounge."

You laugh again. It rings hollow. It's stalling, that's what this conversation is. It's not like you. Thousands upon thousands of gals and guys parading through Shibuya, Ikebukuro or Shinjuku are the types to flag off the toil now to indulge in the present, consequences be damned. They're the ones with apartments or daddy's money in their pockets. You learned very early on that the streets do not appreciate their level of work ethic.

Machan catches your surliness, neither frowning nor smiling. She's caught between offering help or stretching out the procrastination. She doesn't ask for the sake of your pride. You're grateful for that.

"C'mon, let's get this done before we sweat all our salt out."

You expect the worst when the groundskeeper, a hunched-over man in a loose wrap jacket and brown trousers, walks out from his shed. The pepper-white tinge to his thinning cut is a dead ringer for the head miko's. Always asking why you didn't do more, why did you overstep your bounds, why this sweeping and tidying was a gift from the kami themselves, because just look at how indolent and wasteful city girls are. How dare you ask what said city girls are like—you'll catch their mind disease, can't you see?

Luck is on your side, however. The resemblance between head miko and the groundskeeper is only skin-deep. The man's not ornery. On the contrary, he's one of those jovial grandpas, happy to see you and Machan standing in front of him. He goes as far as offering you some tea, which you and Machan decline. He doesn't bark orders, nor does he reprimand you for sitting around and chatting. He shows you the tools, gives you the rundown, and lets you and Machan be on your way.

You examine the tools. They're standard fare. Broom, hoe, rake and gloves for sweeping and raking. Water, soap and rags for the decks and the walls. Bleach and other equipment rest in the back of the storage room. Your hands will suffice for the weeds.

As you begin with the sweeping, you tour the shrine.

[(Inspection check: 38/45 || Insight check: 10/8) -> Success! +5 EXP.]

For as much of a relationship as the shrine has with Tracen, the place is flaking apart. Someone should drag the bins down the hill for the trucks. The ofuda ink's worn out; better to draw up new ones. The water in the purification basin shouldn't be that hue of brown; there's moss creeping up one of the back walls; one of the vending machines has gone bust; the damage you noticed earlier, and you're writing a list at that point.

Damn it. You can't help it. It's diligence, but born from fear and distrust. You'd rather lop off your tail than admit anything originated from that misanthrope's teachings.

She's a thousand kilometers away, so the question becomes as follows. Should you lend Tracen's shrine an extra hand?

Night, July 3rd, 20XX

Sometimes, you forget you're an uma with real magic, who swore to fight the Nightmare threatening to destroy Tracen. Sometimes. You've only glimpsed its bowels once, yet its imprint upon you is undeniable. That silver bullet pendant whizzes and thrums with purpose, not luck. Walking through crowds, your fingers twitch in the curl of a sword. Invisible smoke flows up your nostrils when chowing down on spicy noodles, cats on walls seem to stare straight at you, and of course, scratches and howls resound in the dead of night. They are sounds that cannot come from a stray animal.

You are also drawn to Plain Jane's home—the Shadow Paddock—in Soul Form. Time doesn't flow the same as Earth here. You discover this after a chat with Plain Jane for what felt like a couple of hours, only for her to tap a slender finger on your forehead and order you back to sleep. A loss of thirty minutes of sleep can and will cause ambitious racers to trip and fall.

The exact temporal ratio is unclear. You tried timing it, receiving varied results each time. There was the problem of you unable to fall asleep on self-command, too. It's definitely extended on Plain Jane's end.

[(Logic check: 93/35 || Insight check: 10/7) -> Success! Trivial: +0 EXP.]

It's also 'worse' in the actual Nightmare. You ran in that trash-strewn arena for what felt like hours. Yet, it happened in the span of mere seconds at the finish line, back in the real world.

You take advantage of this time anomaly after listening to a podcast Grass sent you. An old episode, hosted by some former racers from overseas. One of them brought up a series of ancient military treatises to assist in creating new strategies. It sounded violent for your tastes until one guest, some retired New Zealander, noted that brain psychology on the battlefield translates well to the sport.

An idea sparked in your head. You and Plain Jane are fighting a war against the Horrors, correct? What if you took a page out of those ancient treatises and got the jump on the Horrors before they did?

"The Horrors aren't pervasive around the school grounds yet," Plain Jane says when you ask her that night. "I've checked myself."

"That stump is giving off foul vibes." You counter.

Plain Jane scoffs. Scoffs! You didn't know that was possible for an uma-ghost so unruffled. "The stump always radiates its accursed energy. It's the natural consequence of acting as a recipient for the myriad sorrows of this academy's students. Not even Tracen paying for world-class therapists has stymied it, for you children think yelling into its depths is faster, more convenient, more effective, and more trendy-worthy than talking to an actual, reasonable adult."

"But, Senpai, adults can be stupid."

Plain Jane ignores you. "I'd ask you to mail in a request to Miss Rudolf to get rid of the damned object, if it weren't for such a public declaration inevitably sparking a riot."

"Oh, is that why you haven't burned it down?"

"I'd love to. It'd make a most beloved Valentine's Day gift. Sadly, that hunk of wood serves our purposes. We'll talk about them once the Nightmare ceases lulling."

Ominous, but whatever. If Plain Jane doesn't want to tell you, she won't tell you. She doesn't strike you as the pushover type, and you're not in any hurry to return to the Nightmare.

"Back to your original question, I have noticed a few new Horrors wandering the eerie hours. The best they can do is gripe and moan in their tongue before vanishing." Plain Jane lifts a hand, forming a circle with her index and thumb. She smirks. "The atmosphere on our end is currently a tad too thin for their liking."

"Is that normal?"

"What do you mean?"

"Shouldn't there be more Horrors crawling around Tracen's grounds? I don't want them to, obviously, but a bunch of races are cropping up and tempers are soaring."

"Horrors lose a portion of their power when the Nightmare lulls. Simple as that." Plain Jane says. "Most of them won't bother. The ones that do find their sphere of influence is limited."

"And they're not the cause of the other weird stuff happening around Tracen?" You ask.

"You were part of the entertainment industry, weren't you? You should know the higher you climb, the more eccentric the competition becomes. Knowledge of fundamentals more or less equalizes, and the law of competition demands you discover your own breed of helpful idiosyncrasy." Plain Jane says. "But I'll humor you. What is peculiar about Tracen this year?"

You fold your arms and crick your neck. Good question. Where to even begin?

"I think Curren Chan brainwashed a group of bullies last week." You say. "They showed up chanting her name in a reel."

"Nothing I haven't seen from the subcultures surrounding Elvis Presley, Michael Jackson, and the like." Plain Jane responds. "Celebrity worship."

"Someone found tiny steel balls in a box that should've contained dumbbells."

"Miss Gentildonna ran out of her favorite equipment and had to compensate."

"Kitasan said monsters lurked in the trees."

"Sakura Bakushin O."

"Muffled shouts of 'MARVELOUS' in the distance!"

Plain Jane falls silent.

You advance forward. "Senpai."

"That one is harmless."

"Senpai!"

"Pay no attention to that girl."

"You totally think she's weird, don't you?"

Plain Jane turns, gazing into the nearby pool. Her reflection shimmers. She shakes her head, sighing. "Sometimes I forget how young you are, Ruby."

"Wha—what is that supposed to mean?" You holler. "Just tell me if you've noticed anything weird and-or Horror-esque too!"

"Should your duties bear no relation to the defence against the Nightmare—"

"Then you're not helping me, yeah, yeah. I heard it the first time. I'm not asking you to hand me the exam answers. Feed me gossip. Your favorite hobby is taking long walks around Tracen. You listen to the happenings and goings-on as much as the rest of us flesh and blood umas."

Plain Jane huffs. "Who do you take me for, some perverted voyeur?"

You decline to comment.

"Ruby."

You stride up to her. The two of you are almost nose to nose. You bow your head and clasps your hands. "Senpai, please."

"You should return to bed."

"Please."

"You have a race to practice for."

You fall to your knees. "Please, Senpai. Please."

"This is not appropriate behavior for a young lady your age."

"Please, please, please, please, please—"

"You devouring your own tongue will not—"

"—pleasepleasepleasepleasepleasepleasepleasepleasepleasepleasepleasepleasepleasepleasepleasepleasepleasepleaseohprettypleasewithacherryontop!"

[Persuasion check: 114/70 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

A palm flies to Plain Jane's face. She inhales. She exhales. She looks very weary indeed.

"I refuse to entertain you in this matter again."

You receive your leads.

(Select a lead. Choose only 1. None of these are related to the Nightmare…yet.)

[] [DailyLife4] A string of unfortunate incidents that'd frighten a black cat.

[] [DailyLife4] Matikanefukukitaru's Kokkuri board.

Noon, July 5th, 20XX

You desire snacks. You go to the academy shop to sate your hunger. As you peruse the colorful packets and bottles on the shelves, you're hit with a premonition. The hair stands up on the back of your neck. Kaori caught wind of your ice-cream date and has forbidden snacks. Jordan laughed at you, prompting Kaori to file a case against her tummy as well.

Jaw trembling, stomach rumbling, you tear your gaze away from the poster of frozen snacks on the wall and go for a simple ice carrot. As in, a carrot that's wrapped in ice and sprinkled with a bit of artificial sweetener. It's the healthy version of an ice lolly and it tastes of pure humiliation.

But what's this? Etched across the wooden stick are the words…

"Winner?" You utter, holding the wooden stick up to the light.

"Congratulations!" The shop's clerk chimes in from behind the counter. "You've just won the first place prize."

"Woah, seriously?"

"Serious seriously! Come up and get it!"

Right. These ice-creams companies hold competitions with these sticks. You remember a couple of kids blowing out their tiny allowance trying to pull winning ones back in the countryside. Not that you were allowed such luxuries back then. This victory is all the more sweeter now that it's an opportunity to try something denied to you, you suppose.

Your prize is a free piece of equipment from the academy shop. What is it?

5.2: Daily Life VII

QM's Note: You may have noticed Spacebattles has gone through a UI overhaul. If you are as displeased with this as I was, you can return to the old UI by clicking the 'Load Old Spacebattles' option at the very bottom of the page.

>>[DailyLife1] No-one. Gold Ship is enough.

>>[DailyLife2] To meet her friends.

>>[DailyLife3Part1] Fix as much as you can.

>>[DailyLife3Part2] Karaoke.

>>[DailyLife4] The coffee-stained crawling shadows.

>>[DailyLife5] A good-luck charm. (+5 to all Magical Disciplines.)

EXP: 180/220

Mood: Good

Afternoon, June 27th, 20XX

The answer of whom among the Gold clan you shall invite to the ice-cream date is…nobody. That's right. Nobody! Not the Tyrant, nor the gambler, nor even the head honcho whom the rest of the URA racing scene grants a wide, respectful berth. None of them! It's sacrilege to the armies of fans the Golds have, yet you remain unrepentant in your judgment, because it is not without reason.

On your trek back to the academy, you stopped for purchase a bottle of orange juice. The blast of nature's sugar greased the gears of imagination spinning inside your head. You visualised, through an exotic marriage of semi-real 198X manga and smooth synthetic modern animation, the scenes of inviting each of the Golds to hang out with Tabaru. There was Orfevre, who took one look at Tabaru's ice-cream serving, back-handed the dessert glass and demanded the store manager bow at her feet. Dream Journey, comforting a quivering Tabaru in soft nothings, saying that her sweet little cousin deserved better, before striding into the back with a cake knife. Nakayama Festa, ordering half a dozen soda cans and shaking them into Russian Roulette on the spot.

The one with Fenomeno proceeded swimmingly at first, and then Gold Ship made too many random remarks, causing Fenomeno to lunge over the table and strangle Gold Ship until her face turned blue. They crashed over the table, pummeled the chairs into a scrap of plastic; Gold Ship tossed Fenomeno into a bucket of lollies and strawberry yoghurt, and it was, by the goddesses, just plain awful. You'd have a more peaceful time if you tried to put out a cafeteria fire with a canister of gasoline.

As for Stay Gold…Tabaru didn't even get as far as the parlor with Stay Gold. She dropped into a dogeza and lay there for five straight minutes.

Are you exaggerating? Did you spend too many late nights in coffin motels, binging the free manga and anime to cope with the hunger? It's fifty-fifty. Unhinged weirdo doesn't begin to describe the shenanigans you've heard about the Golds. You'd have to invite Curren Chan or another uma with a steel backbone, otherwise you're playing roulette in a casino where half the pins are pitfalls and the others fling the balls up into the ceiling to smash against the chandelier. Mejiro McQueen, by the way, sadly, does not qualify.

And, setting those jokers aside, this is Tabaru's show, not her cousins'. You will invite whoever will serve her worries best, and for now that is only you and Gold Ship.

You hope to the Three Goddesses that the rumours of Gold Ship mellowing out in Team Spica are true.

The days swim by. You do not ask Tabaru for her cousins' contact details. You don't bring them up during conversations at all. Time between classes and training sessions is partially consumed through rubbing your head in attempts to recall Manager Suzuki's old PR training, scribbling down conversation hooks, and stalking Gold Ship on her Umastagram to suss out her personality. The fateful afternoon slams into you, apathetic, and the moment the bell rings, you're out the door with Tabaru lingering behind. Destination: academy gates.

"Ruby." Tabaru speaks up when you and her near one of the benches. "Step back."

"Huh?"

Tabaru rolls her eyes and shoves you on the shoulders.

You sprawl back, yelping in astonishment. Any annoyance about to splutter off your tongue is silenced, as your ears and tail jolt up, and you witness a blur leaping out from the bushes. The blur vaults out at a perfect forty-five degrees angle, somersaults in mid-air, a grinding whirling sound accompanies the motion, and then slams touchdown on the pavement.

Concrete cracks. Dust particles fly up. Two strong, beefy arms outstretch, and Tabaru closes her eyes and leans into the incoming embrace that glomps and devours her in equal measure.

You back off.

"Ta-ba-ru~!"

The figure's bellow erupts through your eardrums. Ruffled Tracen uniform, fake tree cardboard props discarded on the pavement behind her, a long silver mane cascading from behind a round, strapped copper hat, the strands matted with leaves and dirt—it's Gold Ship.

"Tabaru! Tabaru, Tabaru, Tabaru!" Gold Ship squeals, in an accent parodic of a lonely, old uma granny, "I missed you so, so, so much!"

She then crushes Tabaru into her chest.

"Big sister…" Tabaru wheezes, "Can't breathe…my oxygen…"

"Oh, Tabaru, you're still on that grindset. Listen to me. Listen. You, yes, you, don't need anything as useless as oxygen."

"I object to that. Yes, I do need oxygen! I have…lungs!"

"Your lungs are machines on their own. Flesh and blood, hard work and grit. They can sustain themselves on raw life force inside your soul and my undying sisterly love!" Gold Ship chirped. "Now get further in here!"

Tabaru goes down further into Gold Ship's bosom, an act whose sensations are akin to shoving your face into a bucket of marshmallows. She's then lifted off the ground, her legs and arms flailing back and forth. The sight of it catches you off guard. Neither you nor Tabaru are short—middle of the road, if you had to put an estimation to reality. In contrast, Gold Ship towers over the competition. The paper sack she doffed atop her head, the last time you met, concealed the fact she is simply that tall. You'd go as far as to brand her as statuesque, with her square, broad shoulders, balanced proportions from hip to head, long legs and natural poise, immune to the stares and recording lenses flocking around you, Tabaru and her.

Put Gold Ship in a Mejiro coat and heels and remove that silly hat, and she'd easily earn a place on a fashion magazine cover, or the centerpiece of a runway for Yohji Yamamoto. You'd have to remove that dopey grin and tape her mouth shut, though; so probably impossible.

Gold Ship releases Tabaru before the latter's cheeks turn blue.

"You could've greeted me like a normal uma…" Tabaru mutters, dropping to ground level.

"But how else would I rehearse?" Gold Ship says.

"Rehearse?"

"C'mon, Tabaru, you know what I'm talking about. The show. The Tale of Umataro Genji, rewritten and starring me, myself and I! I gotta earn my reps for the second-to-last line of the penultimate act."

"There you go again, big sister. I don't know what that is."

"I dropped the hints in the group chat, duh. Orfy said it was awesome!"

Tabaru peeks off to the side. "Oh. Oh that one." She says in a flat tone.

"You get it?"

"Totally." That's a lie so obvious you could view it off the moon. "I totally get what you're talking about, big sister

"Hooray! We can make you the supporting girl that dies." Gold Ship clicks her tongue and fires finger guns at Tabaru. "I'm going to quiz you on it on the train later! Say, where's your lackeys?"

"Pelte's still injured. Tomoe and Jewel are practising. So, you just have me…"

Tabaru nods. She then bows her head, the manner a salaryman would towards his ornery boss. Gold Ship immediately acts. She lifts her hand, raises her index and thumb, and flicks a solid blow atop Tabaru's forehead. Tabaru reels back, a peeved expression forming, and her head lifts. There's no real offense involved. The hurt melts into a small, relaxed grin, half-embarrassed, and precious and rare these days.

"Thanks for coming, Goldshi" Tabaru says.

"Hm? No problemo. You're you, and I'm me, and also someone's buying us ice-cream, after all. Speaking of which…" Gold Ship swivels your head. You flinch. "Is that her?"

You raise your hand. "Hi?"

"You! You, you…" Gold Ship approaches you. She pulls a frown, then rubs her hand under her chin. She stares off into the wide-open sky. "Eh? Who are you again?"

You are starting to think there is a problem.

Gold ship looks back. "Tabaru, darling. Step over here and whisper into my ear for a tad. Did you ever tell me who your other friend was again?"

"Ruby. Her name is Ruby, big sister."

"Ruby, huh?. Ruby, ruby, Rupert, rubes…"

The problem being…

"…that's totally something a dummy obsessed with basketball would say!"

…that Gold Ship is far too dazzling.

This is a literal statement, by the way. The reason that you didn't rush over and attempt to wrench Tabaru away from Gold Ship's bear hug, besides being dubious if this was a bit between the two cousins, was you were busy blinking the spots out of your eyes?

[World Resonance check: 108/30 -> Success! Trivial: +0 EXP.]

Take the streaks across a fallen meteorite, dip the grooves and notches in luminescent paint from a rainbow's bucket that spent an eternity rolling on the back of a lost van, then carve it up into the shapes of a cosmic flare processed in parallel. Sprinkle in the aftertaste of the voltage between G1 championship and a loss worth an entire modern-day apartment, and that is what radiates out of the core lodged in Gold Ship's chest. An angel's halo, a mesh of runic script, a corona of light that is not real light, you cannot help but be entranced and walloped in the senses by its radiance.

It's her soul's force in action. You can tell by how no-one else in the near vicinity is paying attention to it, and by how the silver bullet is vibrating and threatening to pierce your uniform's front with the velocity of its rotation. You're clutching it now, forcing it to calm down while squinting past the corona.

The glow is blinding. The source, bottomless. Vast and turbulent and fathomless, a property of the farthest reaches of space, where the stars fade and other existences creep out from the masses of nebulae. Did Plain Jane ever warn you about her? Does she know Gold Ship is like this? Seems like a massive oversight not to inform that you'd have your magical eyeballs seared shut!

You have to force past it, lest you spend the rest of the ice-cream date unable to meet Gold Ship's eyes. Frantically, you think back to Plain Jane's lessons. Forget about magic. The phenomenon in front of you isn't that. It's baser, more fundamental.

The soul is individuality manifested. The force of its power corresponds with how confident, how assured you are of your distinct you are amongst the crowd, and Gold Ship is a candidate for the most unique uma to ever enrol in Tracen's storied history. But you can certainly compete, at least. Your own history has a decent lineup: infamous mother, turbulent childhood, rookie underground idol career and propensity to attract G1 champions to your side, which very, very few other rookie umas can boast. And that plants an idea into your head.

Where else have you heard your soul roar with the cry for victory? The track. What followed in its wake? The echo of your desperation, bulldozing the umas who dared try to box you in. A lightbulb flashes above your head. Are you not desperate here? Pissed off deep down at this curveball you had zero chance of anticipation? Like, hell yes, you are! How dare it bar you from fixing up your roommate!

Puffing your cheeks, you step forward and stand in front of Gold Ship. She cocks her head. You stare back.

You reach deep inside yourself and summon up your outrage on this invisible stage.

[(Frenzy check: 87/85) || (Intimidation check: 42/110) -> Success! +10 EXP.]

You withstand the radiance…

[(Frenzy check: 87/200) || (Intimidation check: 42/220-> Failure.]

…but are unable to neutralize it. That's acceptable. As long as Gold Ship doesn't appear like she's attached the universe's brighest torch to her lapel.

"She's pretty pretty, I gotta admit. Handsome if we put her in a school festival suit. Kinda intense, though." Gold Ship squints at you. "Hey, girlie! You sure you're not McQueen's cousin from the Ramonu lineage?"

"No, no, I'm Satono Ruby." You say, releasing a held breath. Good. Her face is visible now. "Nice to see you again, Gold Ship?"

"Again? But we haven't met before?"

"You're sure."

"Absolutely, positively sure! You and I are complete strangers."

"Well." You say, and pause, "That's interesting. I did meet a very interesting uma wearing a paper sack on her head. She almost beat my teammate Jordan. She sounded a lot like you."

"Ah, her. Paper sack woman. Sounds super attractive, delivish, and generous, even. But losing to Jordan? You kidding me? There's no way I'd ever be her." Gold Ship shrugs. "Guess the box factories aren't what they used to be these days. A shame!"

"I'll be sure to pass on my regards the next time we meet on the turf. Maybe she won't have to run with a handicap this time." You say and clap your hands. "Shall we get going? If we don't hurry, the parlor's gonna get stuffed."

Tabaru nods her head. Gold Ship prances off with Tabaru in tow, thankfully giving you a respite from imminently encroaching blindness. You follow and think about buying an extra pair of sunglasses.

"Say, don't you have training?"

"That, Tabaru, is what we call shifting priorities. I'd never miss hanging out with you for the world. Not even the fastest, most groundbreaking space shuttle launches to Jupiter could stop that. You should try it, too."

"Super Creek will get mad."

"I changed my mind. Don't listen to me. Do not ever piss off your Mommy, Tabaru."

You lead Tabaru and Gold Ship to a bus station, where it's a quick hop-on and a ride down Fuchu's main roads to a cinema located on the opposite side of the city. The ice-cream parlor is located to the side. Marble white flooring, cute, round tables lining glass windows, their tops stocked with covered menus. Lo-fi jazz pours out from overhead speakers. Colorful posters wink at the walls, a showcase of ANNE AND GREA III: THE REVENGEANCE and ATTACK OF THE ENCROACHERS 2. The scent of buttered popcorn wafts from the cinema next door.

At this time of day, the clientèle consists of schoolboys and schoolgirls and the odd parent-child pair or couple, thankfully spaced out as to give your group enough space for a semi-private conversation. You find a seat with a good view overlooking the nearby overpass and hog it there. When Tabaru and Gold Ship join without issue, you internally grin with relief. Step one is down.

The ordering is swift. When the parfaits arrive, they are explosions to your color palette sensibilities; full of vanilla and cream and fruit and candy that sends the saliva generators moistening. Kaori would be extremely disappointed if she saw you indulging in this. The woman's a stickler for calorie graphs and diet plans, despite owning several awards for baked goods competitions. She'd understand, you hope, cope. It's for your friend's mental health. Sugar flood the brain juices with that sweet, sweet dopamine. This is the universal bad mood cure shared by human women and uma. You can file it as a something something tax break or whatever!

You dig into your parfait and light up with ecstasy.

"It's so good!"

"It is. I love the mint." Tabaru says, smiling. "What about you, big sister?"

"It's fab. I think I've found my new favorite place." Gold Ship says. She places her spoon into her exorbitant parfait, which is about thrice as large as yours and stocked with bananas and apple slices. She lifts her smartphone and snaps the pics from all angles, smirking. "One for the road, and that for…I better not spoil."

"Is it for McQueen?" Tabaru asks.

"Tabaru! I'd never dare offend the illustrious Mejiro heiress like that." Gold Ship says. "This is for showing off the whole team."

"Wow, Spica's mellowed you out," Tabaru remarks.

"I was always mellow. I'm the big bad older sister now. Anyway, Mac's not on a diet anymore. I'll drag her and Kitasan once her debut's over."

"Oh. You finally feel guilty about her." Tabaru mumbles.

"You think Kitasan will win?" You say.

"Oh yeah, she's a monster. Lifting weights and running with weights on her legs. Trainer's whipping her into shape after she almost lost to you in the tryouts. We gotta haul her on a stretcher after every training session." Gold Ship taps her glass with her spoon, then grins. "You better watch out, Satono Ruby! Rasalhauge might be the brightest in its region, but Spica is number fifteen in the whole wide universe! Kitasan's going to blow you away the next time you meet."

That is likely not how astronomy works. You chuckle, regardless.

The smile has slipped off Tabaru's face. She stares into her ordered diet coke. "Debut…"

That was fast. Too fast for your liking. You'd hoped Tabaru would've eaten at least half of her parfait and gotten more of that lovely sugar into her brain before breaching the topic. Since you and she are already here, you might as well rip the band-aid off in one go.

"Hey, Tabaru…"

"So, Tabaru, how are you gonna take your debut?" Gold Ship asks.

Tabaru goes rigid. Her gaze flits between you and Gold Ship. She stumbles over her own tongue. She goes quiet.

"As best I can."

"That so? Welp, we're rooting for you."

"That's right, Tabaru." You say, nudging your seat over. "Me, your big sister here, Pelte, Tomoe, Jewel…

"And the rest of the clan, too!"

"…eh?" Tabaru squeaks.

"What?" You say.

"Orfy, Drejour, Nakayama, the old man, Mamechin…" Gold Ship counts on her fingers. "We're all gonna gather at wherever your debut is and cheer you on! We're even gonna see if we can get the kiddos—you remember Lala and Marche from New Years', right? I'll tell Nakayama to think an excuse for them to play hooky and ride in from Tokyo!"

You stare at Gold Ship, mouth hanging open. Tabaru's spoon shakes in her hand. A vast shadow seems to flatten itself across her visage. She's five seconds from sinking into the floor and never coming back out.

"We'll get yakisoba and hot dogs and smoothies with cream on top…" Gold Ship spreads her arms wide and exclaims, "It'll be great!"

(What will you do? Choose only one.)

[] [DailyLife1] Let Gold Ship handle this.

[] [DailyLife1] Interrupt and ease Tabaru into facing her fears.

[] [DailyLife1] Interrupt and bluntly state Tabaru's problem.

[] [DailyLife1] Tell Gold Ship off.

[] [DailyLife1] Agree with Gold Ship, but in a gentler, more convincing way.

[] [DailyLife1] Call Oguri, who will call Super Creek.

[] [DailyLife1] Write-in.

Noon, June 29th, 20XX

Wistful. Relating that mood onto Oguri cap feels surreal. Pleased, full-bellied, upset, burning high with adrenaline on the track, even upset in rare circumstances, those masks fit nice and tight in your impression of her, but wistful? As if she's regretting a past mistake or longs for the old days? It doesn't feel right. It's a jigsaw puzzle with a couple of pieces colored monochrome and with the nubs aligned wrong.

Then you realise, what the heck are you thinking, of course Oguri has her nostalgic days. All professionals do. It's in anyone's nature to dwell on the past times when they were the most successful. You yourself still are sometimes tugged by the urge to break out of dance practice and whip out a new routine you talked with the rest of the FAITHFUL girls, only for your ego to seize control and hit you with a reminder that this isn't the indie stage anymore, you silly little uma. Oguri's nostalgic daydreams are probably filled with stadiums loud enough to burst eardrums and thunderstorms of confetti and donuts.

Shows how little you know about her if you're thinking like that.

"What's up?"

"Nothing much. Just my mind wandering a little."

"Something you're thinking about in particular?"

No, not really. You're not answering that, because admitting you spaced out in the middle of a hangout session is a fast ticket to awkwardsville. One recovery strategy Kaede taught you is to focus on one topic in the past that's connected to the circumstances of the now. And the one person in your life whom you thought always wasn't listening was…

"Just remembering a funny tale from my old boss. Big, strong, silent, blockheaded type in a suit. He'd be a salaryman if he didn't fly down to the underground and soak up all our girly idol energy radiation. We turned him into a real man instead of a walking zombie." You say, giggling, "Did I tell you how he met his wife?"

It works. Oguri chuckles heartily at the story. The laughter wipes the question of why Oguri is feeling wistful out of your mind. She's allowed to be reminded of random stuff in her life at random hours of the day. It's nothing you should be concerned about, nor your place to pry.

The real surprise is soon to arrive. The lunch bell dings. The switch happens immediately; Oguri's ears prick up, and her head jerks in the exact direction of the canteen, so perfectly charted it must go beyond muscle memory and enter the realm of an inscription on the fabric of her soul. She wipes her mouth; the angle's away from you, but you know there's a hint of drool on her fingers. She grabs your hand, gestures silently, and away you go.

Minutes later, you stand in line with her, trays in hand, and the sweet scent of meats and fluffy rices and carrots massaging your nostrils. Your stomach rumbles. The snapshots of the meals on the billboard menus seem so real, so fresh. The luxury foods are off the menu for you, much to your chagrin (and Kaori's delight), though you do pile yourself with enough several dishes in the healthy section. As a perk, no-one tries to cut in or bump you on the shoulder. Oguri's presence is as powerful a deterrent as ever.

"She's with Oguri again?"

"I thought it was a rumor…didn't they have a falling out?"

"Ugh, she has to look so smug…"

Stacked plates of rice, tofu and vegetable-meat stew in your tray; Mount Fuji sculpted in fried rice and steamed fish in Oguri's. The two of you move to a table. It's occupied. Oguri sets down her plate and raises a hand in greeting.

"Hi, guys."

"Hello, Oguri!"

"Yo. Still not on that diet, eh? And who's this?"

You do not respond, tongue frozen to the roof of your mouth and hands trembling so hard you think the cutlery is rattling, because the table Oguri has picked is occupied by Super Creek and Tamamo Cross.

The White Lightning. The heel of the Heisei Big Three. Tracen is home to the best umas on the URA racing scene, yes, and you've lived here for a few months and trained under a couple of them, also yes. There's one standing beside you right now, yes, yes, yes. None of these changes the fact that meeting two more up close, who are so accomplished, their techniques so definitive in how the sport is practiced nowadays—Super Creek rewrote the book on long stride running—that you cannot help but find yourself stunned.

"It's alright." Oguri gently nudges you on the shoulder, almost causing your miso soup to float above the rim. "They won't bite. Much."

That last word comes out as a whisper.

[Composure check: 83/50 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

You manage not to sputter out anything stupid.

"Hey! I heard that." Tamamo Cross yanks out a finger and points it at Oguri over her udon. "You better not give the new kid the wrong idea! I'm not some rabid hamster, you hear?"

"Oh, Tamamo, you've long since graduated past that." Super Creek pipes up. "You're more of a bunny these days."

"Huh? Excuse me? A bunny?"

"A fluffy, adorable snow bunny from the Alps, in fact."

"I was a wolf and now I'm a bunny? Hell no, Creek! At least call me a rabbit, for crying out loud!"

A snort pops up your throat, grinds through your clenched teeth and emerges as some sort of amused whine. You quickly plonk yourself down and shove a mouthful of rice and cabbage into your gob before your mouth slips open and something embarrassing falls out. Oguri notices; she pats you again on the shoulder, a quick burst of stability you are ever so grateful for. Across the other end of the table, Tamamo Cross huffs, Super Creek smiles in response; you notice both their meals are mostly untouched, and suddenly their postures shift from annoyed and cheeky to relaxed as they examine you.

"Satono Ruby, right?" Tamamo Cross says.

"That's me." You stammer.

Super Creek clasps her hands together and beams at you. "I knew it. It's so wonderful to finally meet you! We saw you at the tryouts, but we've never had a chance to see you in person. Tabaru has told me so much about you."

Tamamo Cross reaches across the table for a quick handshake. She's got a firm grip, despite her small fingers and the overall shape of her hand. The rabbit comparison was apt—those creatures can be vicious little buggers when pressed. "Guess Oguri finally screwed her head on straight and broke you outta her prison."

"Her prison?" She echoed.

"She told us she was hanging out with you months ago. It's only now she's been kind enough to bring you here," Super Creek says.

Oguri shrugs. "I had some searching to do."

"Yeah, that's called being tardy, Oguri." Tamamo says, not missing a beat. She lets go of your hand. "Glad to meet you too, Ruby. The scary demon next to me is Super Creek, and Oguri—you've already met her, no need for introductions there, probs. Happy to have you here."

"Same, same! And come now, sit down and eat. Your food will get cold. A growing young lady like you must intake all the nutrients you can get for your debut!"

The space between you and Super Creek vibrates. It's a paint bucket of liquid sunshine splashed onto your ear and hair, so incandescent you find yourself moving on the spot, obeying the commands, and smiling lopsidedly with a mixture of embarrassment and comfort. You cannot help but think you are some short measure of time away from a cheek-pinching and a head-patting. That is not a joke you made up in your head. Super Creek does that to the girls on her team whenever they accomplish a daunting task. She's done it to Tabaru. You saw it in person.

The conversation stills as stomaches rumble and food takes priority. Super Creek and Tamamo resume picking at their sandwiches and udon, respectively. Oguri takes out a spoon the size of a ladle and reaches to the tip of her rice mountain to carve out a mound. With the seniors occupied, you take it as the go-ahead to eat as well.

"So, what's the occasion?" Tamamo asks.

"Um…I'm not sure." You reply, lifting your head from your soup. "There isn't one. Oguri didn't tell me she was bringing you here.

"She sprang that surprise out of nowhere? Yeah, that's Oguri for ya. She goes where her wind blows." Tamamo shrugs. "Eh, you'll get used to that, kiddo. We did."

"She's always been the free-spirited type." Super Creek says. "It's what makes her, well, her."

"That's a compliment, Ruby. These two are saying how awesome I am," Oguri remarks, giving you the thumbs up.

"Most of the time." Super Creek says.

"No, it's totally all the time."

"Nuh-uh, don't you start! We ain't forgetting every time you ran off and had to get someone pounding after you," Tamamo says.

"But that's how I met Ruby. I wandered around and found her on the racetrack."

Super Creek and Tamamo stare at you. You sip your drink.

"She, uh, crashed my race." You reply.

You give a quick recap about your first race in Tracen. The two older umas listen, enraptured, and do get fired up at the mention of Grass, though they're not exactly blown away by their friend's behavior.

"See? See?" Tamamo says. "Rudolf had a nice, comfy plan lined up, and Oguri threw a wrench in it."

"It was for a good cause, and Rudolf gave me the okay." Oguri protests. "It worked out fine, right, Ruby? We got to know each other, which means good came out of it. It's like that, um, donut-eating competition."

Super Creek thinks, tapping the tabletop. "To an extent…"

"Donuts? When was this?" You ask.

"Last year at the school festival. Oguri took one whiff of the sign and made a beeline, dragging us along because we had her shopping in hand." Super Creek says, and smiles. "And, I admit we had a lovely time stuffing ourselves silly on the grand stage in front of everyone."

A mountain of free donuts for the sake of prizes—that sounds like heaven to your pre-Tracen self, assuming you ran a million kilometers to tear your umadol kimono into shreds. Maybe if you intentionally lost and scooped the leftovers into plastic containers for storage? It could substitute an entire month's worth of calories.

"I won that one, by the way." Oguri says.

"Also, Super Creek cheated."

Super Creek's neck swivels towards Tamamo's. Her expression grows strained. "Tam-tam, did you have to mention that in front of our adorable new friend?"

"I'm setting the record straight. It totally happened. And itw as kinda funny, because it was the exact same thing that happened at Arima Kinen! You've gotta admit that!"

"The prize was a big donut…" Oguri's shoulders slump. "But it wasn't even real. Just a fake…I had to sell it off to charity."

"Well…" You trail off. "You made a lot of hungry kids very happy."

"Yeah. I had a lot of snacks afterwards, too."

"Hey, Ruby…" Tamamo leans in to whisper inside your ear. "Keep a tab on her when she's at a restaurant. You take one eye off her and you'll walk out there with a bill longer than a phone book."

A memory of Oguri's finger running down a list of expensive desserts floats into your head, and you can't help but giggle a little.

The conversation continues through a departure from the donut-eating contest to the three senior umas' heydays. You sit there, eating and nodding and listening, invisible wires wrapped tense and tight around your upper and mid-section. The rich flavors jostling on your tongue threaten to degrade into blandness, a porridge-tofu substance that's the result of the mind paying too much attention as to not screw up, instead of proper digestion. It's only after the bell has rung and everyone has bid each other goodbye that you realise you're no longer so wound up.

You held a conversation with Super Creek and Tamamo Cross and enjoyed yourself. They're normal umas, not distant legends. It was a good lesson to learn.

"Thanks, Oguri." You say, smiling. "That was great. Super."

Oguri smiles back. "No worries."

The day passes in a relaxed haze.

And that's the end of Oguri's surprise—so you think. The next morning arrives. Oguri finds you again. This time, she leads you towards the edge of the academy. Through a gap in the trees, away from the big school buildings; your nose sniffs pungent fertilizer before you step into the main fields. Beyond a fence, rows and rows of dirt-patches line up under the sun, bulbs and cheery green stalks popping out in neat sequence. A sign stands nearby, portraying a petite human woman with a fan and a cat on her head—Director Akikawa.

These are the carrot patches. Akikawa's pet projects. You recall hearing a story where it rained too much, and she was driven to tears? Or was the one where a Trainer yanked a massive carrot from the patches and gobbled it on the spot?

You hear a rustle. The soft, weighty thumps of fertilizer heaped across the earth. An uma looked up from her works, then walks toward you two, a wicker-basket held in firm hands. Her cheeks are flushed pink from the sun.

"Morning, Oguri! You here to help with the carrots, too?" The girl notices you. "Hey, who's that?"

You recognise the fox mask angled off on her head. This is Inari One. Another of the Heisei Big Three, alongside Super Creek and Oguri.

"Satono Ruby." You say.

"Woah!" Inari One walks up close. Her nostrils twitch as she examines you. "You're that new girl everyone's been talking about. Pleasure to meet ya. I'd shake your hand, but…"

"I don't mind." You say, extending your hand. The heady soil scent is giving you nostalgic vibes.

"Wanna lend a hand?" Oguri says to you. "Anyone who works on the Director's patches earns free carrots in the next harvest. You and Inari can talk about that enka rock bands you guys like."

Inari One's eyes light up like fireworks. "Hey! You better not be lyin' about that, Oguri! The only kid who likes my type of beats is that Kitasan girl!"

That's how you end up weeding and watering the carrot patches with Inari One, discussing and then bagging each other over the merits of Kiyoshi Hikawa and Dohatsuten.

What follows can be described as Oguri's daily Introduce-Friends/Acquaintances-to-Ruby scheme. You swing swords with Yaeno Mutuki in her dojo. You sit down with Mejiro Ardan, who has flown in from Hong Kong a few weeks ago, for tea and cakes and attempt to dig up any shred of formal etiquette from your birthplace, as Ardan chuckles and reassures you there's nothing to be worried about. Sakura Chiyono O is delighted to hear about your umadol days. The obscure classic literature Hotaru loaned you is of great interest, so you entertain her by going behind the scenes of one of the group's more successful albums. Jordan is hanging out with Gold City when you meet. Your new teammate grudgingly introduces you to her friend and warns you with her focused glare not to embarrass her in front of Tracen's top model, or else, so you sit still as the two fashionistas poke and prod at your complexion.

[Swordplay has increased by 2!]

[Social Media has increased by 2!]

[Foreign Languages has increased by 2!]

[Inspection has increased by 2!]

On the fifth day, Oguri brings you down to the turf.

"Belno."

A short uma in a suit glances up from her clipboard. She wakes up in a wide smile. "Oguri! Hi! That's the famous Satono Ruby, I presume?"

"Pleasure to meet you, ma'am." The nerves are returning. Belno Light is the famous umamusume Trainer in Japan, and not by virtue of simply being a rare case.

"Thanks for putting up with Oguri's whims."

You chuckle, a tad awkwardly. "I've been receiving that a lot these days…not that I mind. It's a welcome relief from debut practice."

"I'll be sure to tell Kaori that."

You flinch, then realise from her cheeky grin that she's only joking.

"Do her proud, Ruby," Belno Light says softly. "She's a headstrong woman beneath that elegance, our Kaori is. I should know. She apprenticed under me for a while."

"Woah…"

More juicy history. It's like a reversal of the usual Trainer-trainee relationship. You'll have to ask Kaori for the deets, once events come down.

Oguri looks around the area. "Is Kitahara here?"

"You just missed him. He took the whole team to Tokyo racecourse for observation."

Oguri mutters a curse under her breath. "Damn. I was banking on him being here. Was hoping he and Ruby could meet."

Belno Light gives a wry, knowing smile at that. You can't determine why.

"I can go and find him myself." You offer.

Oguri shakes her head. "It'll be better if I'm there. Trust me."

Emphasis on her words. This isn't a throwaway decision, you can tell, and since she's known the man since her early days, you don't protest. You do ponder why Oguri is pulling this ploy, running around the school introducing to your friends. It's a calculated, deliberate move, as if some higher power has its finger on Oguri's button and demands she tick off the rest of her friendship quota, or else she'll suffer divine wrath.

On the flipside, Oguri's treating you to an experience most URA fans would sell their left kidneys for, so why should you decline? She could've done a lot worse, like treating you to frozen yoghurt. Or buying you a cookie.

Other umas, however, are less than pleased. They notice you hanging out with the Ashen Beast. They notice more than a couple of times, an indication that your involvement with Oguri is not a coincidence. The usual behaviors crop up: the staring, glaring, whispering, and jeering, stuff you've begun to learn let slide off your shoulders; rain on an umbrella. It's not as if these hecklers will do anything to offend these old legends when they're still well respected.

Then, after gym class, you find your locker door busted open, your spare running shoes drenched in aged yoghurt and mud, and a note scrawled in jagged black ink shoved on the heap. You read the note and heave a sigh.

"For crying out loud…"

They couldn't even get the vandalism part right. Academy policy states that the repair of damaged equipment is free if said damage was the result of unwanted harassment, and a note with a message telling you to neck yourself counts.

You're tempted to ride out the wave; a good deal of your hecklers quietened down once tryouts ended. Cockroaches will multiply if left unabated, which leads you to meet three stooges at the back of one of the academy buildings, where the brick walls cast tall shades and a lovely row of evergreen bushes lines opposite the back door. Somehow, this trio is less distinct than Pelte and friends. You don't bother to assign them nicknames.

The ringleader opens her mouth. "Satono Ruby—"

[(Prestige > 5 && Guts check: 10/10) -> Success! +10 EXP.]

You wave a hand. "Just get to the point."

"Huh?"

"Insult me, call my mom a sick freak or whatever, tell me I should throw myself in the river, which none of you have the guts to do yourself—get it over and done with, already, thanks?" You huff out another sigh. "I have my debut race coming up, and the more time I entertain your stupidity is less time I have focused on prepping my debut."

One of the lackies smirks. "As if you could ever ace your debut."

It almost happened for the tryouts. You won't give these morons the pleasure of an argument. Instead, you raise your eyebrows. "Wanna go?"

The girl is taken off guard. "Huh?"

"You heard me, Miss Huh. Wanna go? Come on, let's race. You and me on the two thousand meter turf, five thousand yen on the line. Let's do it."

You slap your arms on your thighs, raising your eyebrows again. You take a step, and the girl who challenged you retreats in turn. It's your turn to smirk. You mouth something, a hidden sound that's barely a word. It's enough to make the girl flinch again. The key to dealing with these sneering bullies is to whack them off balance and watch them stumble.

"Just kidding." You say. "I wouldn't waste my time on a you or anyone who thinks this sort of backdoor crap is a replacement for hard work."

That sets the ringleader off. She marches up to you. You catch a whiff of lemon shampoo, the first identifying trait you bother to identify. The other two lackies huddle around her.

"Do you know what you've done?"

"Enlighten me."

"I'm giving you one final warning, Satono Ruby. Stay away from Oguri! Who gave you permission to cling near her like some sort of parasite?"

"Oh, now the truth comes out." You roll your eyes. "Personally Oguri and me hanging out together is awesome, thank you very much. And, in regard to what you said, who the heck gave you permission to act like you can read her mind?"

"Shut up! You have no idea how Oguri is. She's too kind. Too generous to any random bum lying on the street. There's no way she would've spent any amount of time with someone as radioactive and poisonous as you unless you cheated your way into her circle, filthy skank!"

Oh. Oh, now you understand. Setting aside the American insult hurled in your direction, you recognise this behavior. This ringleader is one of those parasocial, armchair psychological obsessive fans. The type to create an image of their idol in their own head, which they project their own thoughts and opinions upon. These fans spread misinformation, act as if they possess the authority to speak on their idol's behalf, harass less obsessive fans, stalk their idol's every move on socmed and behind-the-scenes, and, most pressing and relatable to this situation, become enraged when the real idol acts in manners that are inconsistent with the parasocial fan's imaginary version.

Your opinion of the ringleader suddenly crashes below the earth and tunnels into the mantle. FAITHFUL had the displeasure of dealing with these disgusting freaks. You were never targeted; your fans basically summoned a wall at events to protect you, the 'little sister', but poor Hotaru—Manager Suzuki had to call a few old buddies from his corporate days. It's the only time you've seen Hotaru bow her head towards him and thank him with such vulnerability.

You angle your gaze upward. This ringleader has an Oguri hairpin in her crown. Fantastic. Absolutely fantastic. And nothing out of the ordinary. A lot of umas try to enrol into Tracen for a chance of glimpsing their favorite runners.

"I don't care." You state.

"You—"

"I honestly, truly, seriously do not give one iota for whatever stupid problem you have with me being with Oguri. Go back to your dorm and cry to her old tapes or something. I have training this afternoon."

This is the point where the old you would have turned on her heel and walked off. You aren't doing this, because you suffered through fighting magical shadow monsters bent on ripping your soul to shreds. Your innate instincts have sharpened, and throughout the ringleader's ranting, you've noticed how the two lackies approached closer, almost forming a semi-circle of bodies around you. The passage between bushes and the building seems to press in from the sides. This meeting has devolved from verbal abuse into the realm of physical confrontation. The risks fly through your head: Cracked skulls, fractured limbs, broken bones, and concussions that hit the brain and more are possible when taking into account an uma's natural strength. Any one of them would wreak havoc on your debut. And they will happen. The ringleader's stare is laden of that same callousness that pushed a drunk to steal your shoes. Dealing with her won't be as simple as planting a foot on someone's head and scarpering off.

You're not completely boxed in, though. As long as you apply the proper footwork, you should have a chance.

The ringleader lunges forward, hands held out in a shove. You leap back at the same time, your momentum falling in the same vector as the shove. In theory, the force should be reduced…

[Brawl check: 40/65 -> Failure.]

…but you are not as adept as you think you are. You sprawl onto the grass, your head hitting the ground. Panic surges through you.

"Stay down, you bitch!"

A kick lashes out.

[Dodge check: 105/65 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

You scramble to your feet in time and evade it.

Suddenly, you're grabbed by the back of your uniform. A strong pair of arms lifts you up. You whirl around, teeth bared for another aggressor, then smile in relief when you see Oguri's rough features.

The feeling isn't mutual.

Oguri plants you down. She gently brushes past you. She faces down the bullies. "What's happening?"

Her tone is as cold as winter's earth.

The ringleader goes pale. For a while, she cannot speak, only stutter. She regains her voice, and it's more high-pitched and far less aggressive. "Miss Oguri, didn't notice you there. We were…"

Oguri raises one foot and slams it on the ground. The dirt beneath crumbles, clumps of debris and glass flying out like shrapnel from a bomb. "Were you bullying Ruby?"

"Um."

"Were you bullying Ruby?" Oguri repeats herself, each word enunciated. "Don't lie to me!"

The two lackies tremble. They sneak glances at each other, silently asking if they should ditch their friend and run away. They don't and can't, paralyzed by the sheer slab that is Oguri's mounting fury. Only the leader manages to stand her ground. She gulps down air, then steps forward, fists balled tight enough to crack bone.

"She was…" The ringleader gulps. "She was tricking you. We saw you talking together. It wasn't right. You know that. You've heard the rumors about her and her mom. She was leaking her shitty aura into your…"

Oguri cuts her off. "Who asked you?"

The ringleader recoils. "I-I…"

"Answer me. Who asked you? Who said you could think for me?"

"I was just trying t-to…"

Oguri storms up into the ringleader's face. "Who the HELL asked for your help?" She roars.

A pillar of blue flame explodes from Oguri's core. The overwhelming pressure you felt on the first day crashes down on the trio of bullies, snapping their wills into twigs and glass. The two lackies slam their necks up and down and sob out tear-stained apologies. The ringleader stands there. Her mouth mimes words, but they do not vocalize. Her eyelids blink, but the lens behind them does not see. She is a living, breathing, frozen statue.

[(Inspection check: 40/50) || Insight check: 10/8 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

It's as if she expected a different reaction. One, in which Oguri flipped her mind around and joined in with the ringleader in harassing you. That sheer scale of unwarranted faith is on par for these delusional superfans, and yet the ringleader acted so assured, so cocksure, as if she believed her plan had a one hundred success rate, that you cannot help but stall your thoughts and ask yourself: why?

Is she just that stupid? Or is there some other context you are missing?

Oguri's soul spurts out another wave of force, snapping you out of your thoughts. Thick veins bulge out from the exposed neck skin. Her muscles coil, stretching her posture, seemingly sprawling her flesh through this confined passage so that she towers over her three victims, a behemoth in ashen gray. A slab of darkness seems to envelops her face; the lone star that struck fear in her turf opponents blazes its terrific light onto the ringleader.

You are the defendant here, yet a nasty chills runs down your spine. Oguri isn't going to assault these three…right?

[] [DailyLife2] Attempt to calm Oguri down.
