Satono Opal, bending so low as to enter a dogeza in a press conference, a corrupted reflection of Oguri's own, muttering out a recited apology, as Cotton Sphere covered in plaster and bandages tortuously wheels herself towards the front stage, takes the microphone, and asks, breaks down, why did you do this, why did you have to cheat and ruin the spirit of the sport, why was Cotton Sphere chosen to never run again weren't they classmates and friends why to the heavens and the earth and the demons of Avici Narka why why why—

"I did what I…" Satono Opal sniffles back in time. She's crying openly. This part is off script, judging from the panicked look of the man that everyone assumes is her Trainer. "I did what I had to do. I did what I had to do! I did what I had to do!" The rest is incoherent.

The phone falls from Oguri's grip. She gazes into the darkness, exhausted in body yet burning high in her head. The sickness spreads and rises bile in her throat.

She was never born with good legs. Everyone knows that. Had her mother not bothered to massage her legs every day or sacrifice her own meals to ensure Oguri's stomach was sated, she might've never walked properly at all. Her mere entrance into the regional racing scene was nothing short of a miracle, never mind the Twinkle Series. For her to witness this Satono Opal, who was fed and clothed and sheltered in luxury; whom acted on nothing but her own selfishness to so ruthlessly destroy not one, but two careers of her own compatriots for her own selfish gain; and violate the one principle that unites all umamusume past and future: that they were born to run.

It is an offense beyond comparison.

Dawn peeks through slits in the curtains. Oguri rolls over in her bed. Beneath the insomnia and the headache, an understanding lodges in her belly, curdling like rotten milk.

She finally understands.

Hate.

————

The memory of Satono Opal's misdeeds attack Oguri in the waking world. Like bacteria in sinuses, like metastasizing cancer in her brain, they swell and swell until the rage and the pity for the two poor souls expels from her mouth and nostrils in torrents.

"I told you not to look her up," Musaka grouses, hand to face. "I knew this would happen."

"My one wish is that I never be compared to her again," Super Creek says, glaring down into her udon.

"The nerve of that rookie!" Tamamo Cross huffs. "And that stupid Sensuke bastard for letting things escalate to that point!"

"I'm suddenly more grateful I stayed behind in Kasamatsu," Fujisawa March mutters over the phone.

"Try not to think about her too much?" Belno Light suggests, and then tries not to wince at the fury in Oguri's eyes.

The one silver lining is Oguri's lap times. She channels her ire into her legs and feet, rocketing down the tracks past the other umas on her team. But even that proves her downfall; she burns out too much stamina and ends up walking more cooldown laps to compensate. She's sweaty, exhausted, and still stewing like an unwatched pot on the boil.

The wind bats her in the face, freezing her sweat. It's not right. She shouldn't be this irritated. Satono Opal is history from years back? What the hell is she supposed to do, she asks herself, build a time machine like that one meme Norn sent her and bash Opal over the head before she took out her hammer? That's unreasonable.

But it's the first time Oguri has witnessed such depravity. Such callousness, from the sport she loves, no less. The fact that a creature like Satono Opal was born, wreaked havoc, was let off with an apology at a press release and the world kept spinning on its axis—there's no justice in that. It doesn't feel right that her fellow Tracen students can grin and carry on through life when two perfectly healthy umas had their futures ripped straight from their grasps?

She needs to talk to someone. Get this off her chest. Musaka is too blunt, and Rudolf probably doesn't want to talk about Opal, judging from her expression post Arima Kinen, so Oguri calls one of the last few adult figures left in her life.

"Sheesh, Satono Opal?"

Oguri frowns at the flippant response. "Is this some kind of open secret everyone's been hiding from me?"

Kitahara Jo, still stuck in Kasamatsu, detects his ex-trainee's ire. He softens his tone. "Not particularly. Closer to ancient history no-one wants to touch with a ten-foot pole."

"Yeah. That's what Roppei said. He also left out a lot of detail. He made it sound like something out of an emergency first-aid manual."

"Look, you can't blame the old man. One of his old trainees was friends with Semi Sonic, if I remember correctly. The emotional harm from Opal's incident floated down to the rest of the URA, the Trainers and trainees especially. Opal used to be well-liked, believe it or not. They called her a pushy, if respected, big sister to the young ones. Finding out that she had planned to betray two classmates and the idea of uma sportsmanship was…" Kitahara sucks air in through his teeth. "It was a rough time to be enjoying uma racing, I tell you what. Huge cuts to funding, along with the investigation. And then there was the overseas response."

"I heard that from the documentary."

"Oh, you saw that one too?"

"For the first time. Belno sent it to me beforehand. No-one showed it to me before. It's just…" Oguri shakes her head. "How come no-one told me about this? Did they think I was too dumb or soft to hear about it?"

"No? No, no, no!" Kitahara says quickly. "It was just bad luck. It's not yours or anybody's fault. She wasn't relevant to our training back in Kasamatsu, so I didn't bring it up. Maybe your classes mentioned her—"

The classes that Oguri basically dozed off in.

"—but apart from that…nothing. No-one's heard hair nor tail of her since the incident."

Oguri scowls. "I hope she's in prison."

"Either that or house arrest. I dunno, maybe she's working as a maid in the Satono holiday home, or something."

"It's weird how the Satonos raised an uma that horrible. I thought it was their big dream to win a G1. One of them came up to me for a sponsorship deal before, and it was like they worshipped the Goddess of Victory herself."

"Nike?"

"No, our one."

"Well, they're certainly regretful," Kitahara says.

"Are they?" Oguri exclaims.

She can hear Kitahara wince over the line. Looking back, this was rude of her. In the present, she can only roll her eyes and immerse herself in the full swirling force of her ire.

For all Kitahara's faults, patience is not one of them. He listens to Oguri rant. He interjects at the end of each angry sentence, pointing out that no, the URA did not suffer Opal's injustice without responding in turn. They tightened restrictions regarding equipment checks. They station security guards near changing rooms. All post-debut racers are offered psychological counseling at the URA's expense. The injury of Semi Sonic and Cotton Sphere inspired a wave of research into spinal, leg and bone injuries for humans and umamusume.

A good chunk of the red tape was cut by the Satonos themselves, who were desperate to distance themselves from Opal and her crimes. They compensated Opal's two victims by paying for expensive rehabilitation plans, as well as granting them massive discounts on Satono-brand movie theatres, casinos, hotels and the works.

"Cotton Sphere's doing okay, last time I heard. Think she was training to become a physiologist."

Satono Opal's achievements were scrubbed. Her merch was recalled and burned. She exists primarily within URA documentation as a lesson for Trainers, aspiring and veteran, to study and contribute to the praxis of never allowing an uma like her to appear ever again.

Slowly, Oguri vomits her anger out.

Slowly, she realizes she's interrupting Kitahara during his coursework and feels a flush creep up her neck.

"I guess there's nothing we can do about her?" she admits.

"Pretty much, yeah," Kitahara says.

Oguri breathes in. "I think I knew that yesterday, but…"

"It stung you too hard?"

"Yeah," It's such an obvious conclusion that she blushes. The embarrassment bleeds. "I'm really sorry for unloading that on you."

"Hey, no worries. It was a pretty massive shock for us back then, and we were the humans. Can't imagine how you must've felt as a uma," Kitahara says. She can hear her grin. "It's always good to get something off your chest, right? I'm here if you need me. We're gonna be Trainer and trainee in the future, so I might as well get a head-start on counseling you."

Oguri laughs at that.

It's not an end to the Satono Opal problem, nor does it exactly restore Oguri's faith in the URA. But at the very least, she understands that the world didn't stay idle.

————

Oguri tries to forget about Satono Opal after that. It's easy. Very easy. Tamamo Cross may have retired, but the rest of the scene hasn't. For every rival that bows out of the Twinkle Series, two more take their place. Inari One from Ooi. Bamboo Memory from the other Fumino Trainer. Just as Oguri's finished polishing herself back up to speed against them, Super Creek returns with a vengeance and steals the Tenno Sho.

Winter's ready to pour in, so here comes Japan Cup round two starring Obey Your Master in her original racewear. Oguri stumbles around the city square and finds this cool and gorgeous uma well versed in recuperation tech. She's Folkqueen, New Zealand's final hope.

She's so magnificent that Oguri is struck dumb at a party, her platter of food forgotten, as she realizes she has no idea how to talk to someone so classy. Folkqueen then obliterates Obey Your Master and Oguri and Eve Binti and everyone else in the final stretch to win the Japan Cup. The press doesn't miss either incident.

Arima Kinen II. Oguri fails to stand on the podium for the first time in her life. She goes into a slump. But Kitahara passed his exams and is now a fully minted national-level Trainer, which is awesome. They go on to win the Yasuda Kinen together. Oguri's so happy she could almost burst. This is everything she's dreamed of. Where's the room to think about some failed has-been when the pieces of her life are finally, once again, falling back into place?

Then, everything collapses.

Super Creek retires. Inari One's not far behind. Oguri's the last of the Heisei Big Three, a so-called unstoppable force who will shine forever. Biology herself is tapping a watch and cashing in those debts. Oguri refuses, so matters are taken into Biology's own hands.

First are her legs, which lag behind on the turf. Then it is her heart, which no longer explodes her muscles with strength. Her stamina drops. Her breathing falls shallow. Belno, Kitahara and Musaka search for an answer, but to no avail. Nothing can stop the cold, hard reality that no star shines forever.

Sixth place, then eleventh place. Wipeout. Journalists crowd outside Tracen gates. Someone mails in a pipe bomb in a vain attempt to change the URA's minds.

On a cold riverside at the dead of night, within the deep black pit Oguri digs herself into, she's struck with remembrance and and wonders if this is what Satono Opal felt, kneeling to the flashing cameras. It only gouges the wound harder.

————

"I can't even run properly anymore."

"Yeah. I know."

"Even if I run the Arima, there's no way I can win."

"Maybe not."

"I'll just keep letting everyone down. Musaka said so. Everyone says so. You know that!"

"And I'm asking you, Oguri!"

She can't breathe. City lights shine behind Kitahara's tall, stalwart form.

"We're not talking about if you 'can'. We're talking about what you want. Good or bad shape, the expectations of your fans or the press, hell, even what Musaka said—none of it matters. Your decision does. If you want to call it quits, that's up to you. I'll gladly respect that and keep my mouth shut. But if you say you want to run, and you truly mean that, then as your Trainer, I'll do possibly everything in my power to help you achieve that."

He holds up those shoes, stained with dirt and mud.

"I'll ask you one last time, Oguri. Do you want to run?"

Arima Kinen III. There are no fancy techniques, no plans on whiteboards. One line of advice: just run. That's exactly what Oguri does. The midnight clock stalls for the final second, allowing her to surge past Mejiro Ryan in the homestretch and win her last G1. She etches herself in Japanese umamusume racing history as a legend amongst legends.

The gap between her and Satono Opal is wider than night and day.

PART 2

Retirement is easy after that.

The process, that is.

Contrary to what Oguri assumed, the aftermath becomes something of an existential crisis. Stuck in a limbo born from infinite possibilities and fueled by zero direction, Oguri only becomes cognizant of the fact she might have slipped up, after purchasing half a department store's worth of clothes she can't wear and finding receipts on a down payment on a car she doesn't know how to drive. There's still ninety-five percent of prize money left.

Her friends quickly stage an intervention, then send her to a financial planner.

It's a common problem with retired athletes in most sports, it turns out, and it's a problem that Tracen is aware of. Rudolf hops off her throne to personally sit Oguri down and discuss a special educational program for retirees. The gist is that as long as said retiree contributes to umamusume racing in their own way, whether that be through advertising, teaching, sciences or whatnot, then Tracen will gladly remain their home. The program is flexible enough that Maruzensky, who ran at an era earlier than Rudolf's, is still considered a Tracen student.

Oguri need not jump into the program straight away, though. She's just finished a career of a lifetime. Why not vacation for a bit?

So, Oguri departs from Tracen. She visits the hallmarks of Kyoto and Osaka. She runs a circuit of Tokyo's wards with a disguise cooked up by Gold City and Belno. She dives into the most remote villages to taste the most exquisite Japanese delicacies, careful not to overeat and destroy the region's crop yields for the year. She returns home to Kasamatsu during the summer, where she meets up with her mother, then March, Norn and the rest of the hometown gang. Together, they spend a grand old time mucking around the place. Festivals, mock races, stories comparing Tracen and the regional circuit.

Oguri picks up some casual work when harvesting season approaches. It's fun, she finds, in a sweaty way, picking up pumpkins and pulling leeks and learning the crop cycles and placements from the old-timers. It settles the heart. Agriculture could be her second calling, now that racing is off the table.

Convinced, she returns to Tracen, where she picks up an Agricultural and Life Sciences degree sponsored by Tokyo University. It's a mixed bag. A mild shock to everyone who knows her, because who expected Oguri Cap, of all umas, to walk down the path of a scholar? Certainly not her, and for a good reason. The fieldwork where she gets to observe plant growth cycles or manage her own plots of land is interesting. The homework and the exams, less so. Figures and graphs and politics, of all bloody things, combine into a lethal cocktail that leaves her head flat on her desk wishing she was a couple of years younger. Worse, she has to sit through a preliminary exam, as the professors are unsure about whether her secondary education was up to snuff, the jerks.

It's fortunate that Oguri still has access to her dorm room, because it'd be super embarrassing if all the starry-eyed newbies at Tracen saw their idol, whom some enrolled specifically to see, banging her head against her desk and wishing she was three years younger.

Vacation's over. Welcome to the school of hard knocks, idiot.

But Oguri persists. The rest of her generation has moved on: Mejiro Ardan managing the Mejiro business in Hong Kong, Super Creek acting as an assistant to her Trainer, Folkqueen running her own enterprise under her own name. Belno's off in America learning to become a fully fledged Trainer herself. What reason does Oguri, arguably the most successful of her generation, have to complain?

She grinds out a bachelor's degree. The fanfare is mellow. It's not enough to earn a specialized job in the field, so onto her master's degree.

Around her, the scene changes, as it always does. Belno Light becomes a proper trainer. Kitahara picks up his own team, his reputation massively boosted by Oguri's successes. Oguri follows in Creek's footsteps and pitches in with the training here and there, then lessens her activity after too many trainees get distracted. Biology strikes again on her latest victim, Musaka, after decades of drinking, smoking and dealing with teenage umas without end. He retires, too. New umas flock to Tracen and new champions take the stage.

The legend of Ashen Beast becomes simply that: a legend, no longer in the spotlight. One of Kitahara's new girls doubts she existed at all. She'd be laughed out of the team back in Oguri's day; instead her comment dissipates into the air, like any other. It's a cocktail of mixed feelings, one of which tastes like longing.

She still runs, in casual races with other Tracen girls, Dream Trophy affairs, sponsored company deals and the like. She cannot bear to let the physique and talents she developed during her prime degrade into nothingness. Belno's parents are ecstatic their daughter formed such a long-lasting friendship with Oguri and offer Oguri exorbitant deals if she wears their sporting equipment. It's a good 'side hustle', as Folkqueen called it, but she warns Oguri that sort of cash doesn't last forever.

The do-or-die, win-or-lose zeal that drove Oguri forward in her prime has hung up its coat and taken off its shoes. It is simply how the world flows.

Still, if Ashen Beast is a memory, then Satono Opal is a half-exorcised ghost. Satono Opal is a long-forgotten ghost. Oguri rarely thinks about her at all, and when she does, it's most often when she's distracted during part-time work or during lapses amidst her studying. She cringes at her younger self's rant towards Kitahara.

The scene is on the cusp of banishing her from existence; it feels like, and that's the best everyone can hope for.

20XX rolls around.

————

"What did you say?"

The two umas whom Oguri overheard in the hallway flinch. They clam up, then glance aside to see if there are any cameras recording their incoming faux pas. Oguri waves her hands gently to gesture that they're cool. It's a common problem former legends often have when communicating with their juniors. Oguri vaguely remembers Rudolf discussing a new policy to remedy that. "Could you repeat what you said, please?" Oguri asks.

"About, um, what exactly?" The first uma, a red-ribboned girl, squeaks out.

"The rumor you guys were discussing."

The two umas exchange another nervous glance. "That…the daughter of Satono Opal apparently signed up for Tracen?"

Oguri can't see her own face. Judging from how the two umas inch up against the nearby wall, it's nothing good.

————

The two young umas show Oguri the evidence. An Umastagram selfie of a young, lanky uma with the same rich black hair as Satono Opal. Minute differences exist in the shape of her nose, the thickness of her eyebrows, and the fool's gold crown ornament, but the rest—the bangs, the posture—are dead ringers for her mother.

The photo is taken on the sidewalk outside the entrance to some underground arena. The walls are plastered with peeling, neon-vivid posters. Swaddled in early morning daylight, the uma gives the peace sign and a nervous smile, then says in a cheerful voice she's graduating from the idol business to enrol at Tracen. Wish her luck!

This is a complete joke, is Oguri's first, instantaneous thought.

The second: is this real? Satono Ruby actually exists?

Why, of course, Umapedia says cheerily, after it finishes dragging its feet to pull up Satono Opal's page. The information is all here. Satono Ruby was born to the Satono family as the product of a teenaged Satono Opal and a yet-to-be-identified father. The affair created a scandal, as teenage pregnancies tend to do, that the Satonos smoothed over by telling Opal to keep her mouth shut while they fed the press the appropriate legalese. The scandal was then forgotten in the wake of Opal's second major, and more popular, scandal. Satono Ruby, at five years of age, became little more than a footnote.

The last time the world heard about Ruby's infant (or was it toddler?) self, it was from a Satono press release stating Opal's poor daughter—a sympathetic party, though less so than the two victims—would be taken away from Tokyo proper and raised elsewhere, so that she could grow up free of controversy. They'd send her to some nice and quiet country town, where she'd have her name changed and live under the care of a foster family. She'd live a quiet, peaceful life out of the limelight.

Bollocks to that, Satono Ruby's cheery peace-sign seems to say.

Oguri doesn't understand her. Neither does the rest of the academy. The rumor mill brews up a storm, tongues flapping and tails wagging with the fever of locusts towards wheat.

"Oi. You sure this isn't a prank? That uma in there an actress?"

"Doesn't look like it. The Umastagram profile leads to a legit account. Doesn't seem like a social experiment…"

"Checked out her band and—ugh. She's not that great at singing. Hardly Winning Live material. They'll boo her off the stage."

"Regional girls already struggle like mad trying to fit in here. Her? This random umadol from the underground—not even the aboveground? She's no Smart Falcon. No way. She'll flop before the tryouts, bet."

"Hear me out. I just saw Crown walking around in an awful mood. Bet the Satonos are super-duper pissed."

Her friends eventually join in the action.

"I'm not sure if Tracen is the place for her. The little ones are becoming antsy," Super Creek says, worried, glancing around the cafeteria one lunchtime.

"Yeah, I totally get you. She should've kept up with her music career. Her fans liked her. Some of them were crying at her retirement ceremony," Inari One comments, "Feels like a lost opportunity, you get me?"

"One of my little brothers got addicted to one of them underground idols and ended up spending more cash on merch than his textbooks. Ma said the idol seduced him. She's not gonna come here and bring that sort of attitude, is she?" Tamamo Cross exclaims.

"If she is enrolling with the intent to cause trouble, then I'll show her the true meaning of discipline!" Bamboo Memory then pulls out her bamboo sword and waves it around at the table, prompting the other girls to tell her to calm the heck down.

In the end, the decision isn't up to Oguri, her old friends, or any of the other students. Forces shift behind the scenes; a parade of shouting behind doors, phone calls, and filed forms. It culminates in a van pulling up in front of Tracen's gates on a pleasant spring day. Men, women and umas in matte black suits pour out, before filing into a congregation led by a sharply dressed woman with the kind of spectacles that slice and dice when she glares. The Satono Conglomerate has come to bargain. The sight of them sends onlookers ramrod-stiff.

Endgame, the Satono team's marching footsteps drum out. It's been fun, but Director Akikawa needs to see reason. She cannot allow the walking plague known as Satono Ruby to infect Tracen while two Satono heiresses are attending. They will talk sense into the Director. They will convince her to see reason. Satono Ruby's enrollment papers will be shredded by sundown.

They are incredibly incorrect.

An hour later, the suits leave with their tails between their legs and their leader looking frazzled whilst gnashing her teeth. Later reports will claim that the Director watched them go with hollow, cold eyes. Regardless of whether that's true or not, the Satono operation ended in a total, abject failure.

Akikawa will not budge.

Satono Ruby is here to stay.

————

Not.

Director Akikawa granted Satono Ruby, her blessing. Director Akikawa is also the woman who almost broke her bank account on strange and cumbersome farming equipment that Secretary Tazuna had to return with many apologies. The students put two and minus one together and decide Akikawa was struck with a bad case of ideals over reality. They still respect her, obviously! But nobody's perfect.

Back to the old question, then.

Why? Why is Satono Ruby doing this? She could've been a clerk. A writer. A scientist. A journalist, a doctor, a professional singer, a basketball player, a hostess, a thousand other respectable career paths—and she chose to join the sport her mother defiled so much? She…this…this is insanity! Are the lights on behind those thin eyelashes of hers?

Well, the girl's not responding. Immediately after making that announcement, she locked off her DMs and switched commenting to followers-only mode on both Umastagram and Umatok. The rest of Tomorrow is FAITHFUL followed suit, manager included. Any followers who spewed out hate comments were swiftly banned as per her moderators' last hurrah. A total stonewall strategy from beginning to end.

The academy rumor mill is left to speculate. The umas looking forward to mailing Ruby hate mail are especially frustrated. Coward, they decry. Afraid of everyone learning the truth, you stupid bitch?

None of these girls are Oguri Cap. Instead, she's off to the side eating her mountains of rice and meat while cocking an ear, listening to the academy chatter, as usual. What she hears sets her on edge. Sure, Satono Opal was a horrid, horrid uma, and her daughter might be insane or idiotic for throwing herself into the scene that vilified her mother, but to hear so many threats casually thrown around…is a bit much, isn't it?

A couple of the younger umas go as so far walk up to Oguri with concerns.

"Miss Oguri Cap, you're like a big shot, aren't you? Could you, um, maybe tell those girls in the corner to calm down? They're creeping us out."

When Oguri points at herself, the gaggle of umas nod. She's the authority figure they desire.

It's tempting to decline them, despite her agreeing with them.

This shouldn't be her fight. She's retired, for starters. She's better at hyping others up than at ordering them around, like Air Groove, or charming them like Symboli Sirius. This sort of disciplining puts her at odds with who Oguri is these days. The fire that stoked her through her career has smouldered into charcoal. She's developed a new reputation: the academy glutton, the chill, approachable ex-star, who is always ready to share a tidbit about uma cuisine or offer a smidgen of advice without acting all high or mighty.

She's hesitant to launch into a speech about adhering to standards she's unsure she could even draft. This should be a teacher's job.

Still, these young umas do look afraid, so Oguri sighs, gets up and goes to chide the offending Satono Ruby hecklers. This pattern repeats a few times. Sometimes, they lope off ashamed. Sometimes, she can see the lack of regret in their eyes. Those are the ones who will continue mocking Satono Ruby behind not-so-closed doors.

"I'm sure the Prez will sort it out," Oguri always says, afterwards.

"Will she?" The umas that sought her often ask.

"If not her, then Groove or Brian or…" Oguri shrugs. Someone with more charisma than her, like Sirius. A real heartthrobber. Oguri's the opposite of that. "Scandals don't last forever. France once singled out one of our girls for taking this lung medication that was banned overseas, which ended in disqualification and a lot of fines. It raised a big ruckus, since this is Japan and all, but that didn't last forever. This Satono Ruby hate train will burn out at some point."

Then, she finishes her lunch, returns to her room, and drowns herself in her master's work. The professors attending Tracen don't give a crap if she was the Ashen Beast or not. They expect her to behave like the tertiary student society expects her to be.

————

The thing is, a siren won't stop blaring just because a single uma plugs her ears.

The rumormongers and hecklers decide that since Ruby closed the door, they might as well open a window themselves. The following week, day after day, post after post, information about Ruby drip-feeds down the Internet pipeline, sourced from archived blog posts, candid photographs from creeps and sickos, and the few brave enough to take to the dirtiest corners of Shibuya, Shinjuku and Ikebukuro. Wannabe bloggers record entire reels detailing her life from scraps.

Satono Ruby is homeless. Satono Ruby is theorized to be a runaway. She flipped burgers in WcDonalds, stole thrown-out bread from behind bakeries, and sneaked into coffin motels by crawling under the desks. The Satonos hate her guts for running away. According to Tomorrow is FAITHFUL, she is thirteen, eighteen, a lady's secret, non-existent! Of course, they were forced to do this to secure the sheer advantage of possessing an umadol in the underground when most umadols seek the aboveground path, but their fans often say they'd be better off without Ruby; some state they enjoyed the group's albums more when she wasn't there. How innocent are they in this matter, really?

Kaede. Darling fearless leader-queen Kaede. Didn't her ex mention she was a complete menhera? Hotaru wrote some edgy blog posts about blowing up the Diet Building when she was thirteen, too. They seem like the type of loose women to engage in relationships with fans behind everyone else's backs.

Oh? What's this? FAITHFUL's manager has threatened to lawyer up in case his girls are harassed online and offline? My god, the audacity! The independent press was merely asking questions. That's bōryokudan crap. Yakuza-coded. The man's hiding skeletons in his closet, an entire catalog of calcium. Following a link from his bio into another account and then once and another: a hidden camera captured some random idol girl telling Ruby it was a bad idea to disrupt Tracen's atmosphere with her enrollment. Ruby dismissed her. Brushed past her.

Rude! Rude of her! From that angle: was that a sneer on her lips?

She's concealing something—

She's deliberately stirring up a ruckus—

She's poison—

She's a fake miko who doesn't know—

Idols are liars in pretty dresses, according to this week's hit manga. When has manga ever led umas astray? That smile of hers is a deceit; her kimono'd form a marionette on a malevolent puppeteer's strings! She's the spawn of Uma Satan. She's here to wreak havoc and smash up all our cleats. Stalk her, jump her, hurl mud at her from the track; hide her pens and watch her snap. We gotta do something about her!

To Oguri, this is rancid. Rancid, awful, revolting talk, verbal smog from factory pipes streaming across a pristine country field. Aim it at someone else, say Nishino Flower and—she can't finish it. The consequences are too much to bear contemplating. And yet, despite possessing otherwise rational minds, none of Satono Ruby's hecklers seem burdened with guilt. They're having the time of their lives, in fact!

What Oguri, and many others, have forgotten or didn't notice, was that Satono Opal's second scandal was as popular as it was horrible. Her actions set the media ablaze. People couldn't stop talking, blogging, writing essays, profiting off the destruction and the devastation, reveling in their own self-righteousness for weeks, months, and now years.

It's fun to talk trash down at someone, to let the spite inside your heart squirm out and offload the curses dwelling inside your heart onto another. The only requirement is to brand them as an acceptable target to relieve yourself of your own moral burden.

Oguri could speak up about this. She could complain to the open air about how this spite is ruining her food. She doesn't, because, again, it's not her job, because she's not great at constructing a convincing argument, because she thinks she might be a hypocrite.

Umastagram snares her during her downtime through its curated, endlessly scrolling interface. Soon, the downtime becomes study break time, and then eats into her study time. Her mind screams at her to stop as it taps the phone and drags a finger down. It's like watching a car crash, stretched frame-by-frame into a daily updating serial. It's her sociological immune system lacking a vaccine to the Internet brainrot virus, feeding on the lack of progress towards her mid-year Master's thesis.

She has no right to chastise others about feeding upon controversy when she's engaging with it as her own guilty pleasure.

————

The press catches wind. They do what they always do to controversy and dump a canister of gasoline onto the flames. Satono Opal's daughter isn't a hoax. Take to the high seas, boys; there are entire war chests to be made!

The first time Oguri catches wind of this is when she's passing by the student council room. The door is opened slightly ajar, from which an angry wind pours out.

"This is the last goddamn time I will say this. The decision made by the Director is final. The statement she wrote is on the academy's website. You and your yellow journalist toadies harassing me, Air Groove, the rest of the student council or any of my friends, for that matter, isn't going to change that. Accept the fact that Tracen is open to all umas and stop wasting our precious time!"

Narita Brian slams the phone down, almost cracking the plastic casing. She heaves a labored sigh, then whips her head around, glaring at Oguri through the crack in the doorway.

"Are you alright?" Oguri asks.

"Not a single word," Brian hisses.

"But—"

A vein throbs, ugly and purple on Brian's forehead. Bags cling to her eyes, evidence of a complete lack of sleep recently. Before Oguri can respond, Brian stomps forward, grabs the doorknob, and slams the door shut.

The second time happens on the turf.

"No, I'm not related to—never mind. You already know!" Belno clicks off her phone, tips her head, and stares at the sky for several moments. Her back vibrates with a shudder. It's the equivalent of a regular uma gripping the sides of her head and screaming to the heavens.

"Belno, are you okay?" Oguri asks.

"Yes," She mumbles out. She walks a few feet away from where her team is running laps, then confesses, "No. No, I am not. I have had five calls asking for scraps about Satono Ruby, after the Director put out a statement asking for empathy; after I wrote an essay on our team Umastagram; after I contacted several offices and told them to stop bothering us when we have training to do!"

She tucks her phone back into her pocket, her face scrunching up with raw frustration.

"Why did that Satono girl have to exist?" she grouses.

Fear shatters the anger, followed by remorse. Belno glances aside. Too far. Director Akikawa would've murdered her, had she noticed a Trainer in her employ wished failure on a new student. For Belno to say that, it's no small deal, Oguri thinks to herself with a hollowness in her gut.

A mob gathers outside Tracen's front gate. This meatball of writhing, wriggling suit-clad limbs pounds on the heavy iron, then spots her and bleats out requests for interviews. For Oguri Cap to make a statement on Satono Ruby. Like what? Oguri thinks, half-hysterically, as flashbacks to her own downward spiral slam through her nerves, what the heck is she supposed to say about a girl she's never met?

"Also, is Rudolf in her right mind?"

Tracen, thankfully, has learned from the past. She arms herself with security guards and threats of legal action, and the mob disperses with shouts and waved fists. Oguri watches from afar, clutching the side of her uniform skirt and agape at the fact that a single uma could be this influential, this destructive before arriving.

————

The mob is the last straw for many.

"They seriously sent a mob to our gates? That's so lame."

"How long are we gonna talk about some random girl? Ugh, let's go back to chatting about Gentil's thighs already."

"That's only you, perv."

"She's gonna enter, do nothing because she's too shy to speak up, and then this whole mess is gonna end up as a nothingburger."

But, Ruby's hecklers point out we still haven't answered the why of her arrival. But, no-one's there to provide a convincing argument against her. Look, see, there's this latest video in their defense is a full exposé on the girl named Satono Ruby from a vlogger with a whole ten thousand subscribers on Western Umatube. An artist's mentality bleeds into their work, and while Tomorrow is FAITHFUL is a team effort, clear patterns of rebellion exist in their discography, as exposed by Verse A of Song B…

Hands slam on the table. A red-faced uma stands up and roars. "Oh, shut up! It's all celebrity magazine bullcrap. No-one actually cares about your stupid vendetta!"

Her opponent responds by insulting her mom. The uma hurls a toast slice, which is answered by a catapulting of hot porridge spoonful, which in turn is then countered by the dumping of an entire plate of eggs and bacon, and soon that section of the cafeteria delves into a vicious food fight. Oguri dies a little inside at the wasted carbs.

"You know I'm right!" a heckler yells as she's dragged off by Bamboo Memory, "Everyone's against that rotten bitch. You say you want us to shut up, but not once have you ever agreed on her sticking around! When the whole world calls you an asshole, maybe it's time you start looking inside yourself!"

"You're the asshole!" someone yells back.

"Why do you think that journalist asked Oguri Cap? She agrees with us!" The heckler cackles.

Oguri freezes as practically every single head in the cafeteria turns to stare at her. Déjà vu strikes her. Mad, terrible déjà vu.

"Is that true, Oguri?" someone calls out.

"Um…" Bread falls from her lips. She was browsing her phone for a repeat lecture she half-slept through on its first iteration. "Um, uh…"

"Wait, do you hate Satono Ruby too?"

"I never said—"

A scoff from the crowd. "She was a legend. Of course she hates Ruby, because everyone from that time hated her mom!"

"Are you…" A fourth uma presses closer. She sounds hopeful. "Gonna do something to sus Ruby out?"

Oguri's mind goes blank.

What?

What, what, what—how, when, why—where did that become a possibility?

"Because if the Director's not doing anything about it, the teachers or the student council won't, then only you guys can…"

Who is 'you guys' in the first bloody place?

Press release training. What did her press release training say about unexpected questions? It's been years. She can't remember. Everyone's growing dissatisfied. Oh goodness, where's Gold City when you need her?

"Shut the hell up, the lot of you! Too much talking and not enough running," Tamamo Cross slams her hands on the tabletop and bolts from her seat. "Quit using that girl as an excuse to slack off!"

Super Creek joins in the fray. "It's bad manners to pressure someone in the middle of a meal. Wait until Oguri's finished eating, please."

They stand in front of Oguri and block her sight from a good half of the crowd.

The heckler's laugh floats down the hallway.

"They…they tell us to shut up," she giggles. "But they never tell us that Satono Ruby is anybody good!"

————

Then, is Satono Ruby evil?

The more the majority discusses the question, the more an idea forms. Less tenuous, because the Satonos did separate Ruby from Opal. Ah, but she had five years with her. That's more than enough time for a mother's ideals to implant themselves into a young daughter's brain. That age is old enough for a daughter to see her mother being forcefully taken away and curse the circumstances that led to that. The URA, that is, not the mother's own sins. No-one said children were always intelligent.

Also, who's saying Opal didn't perform her own dirty work in exile? Her body was fine. She could've earned an income. What if she hired a private detective to locate Ruby, then brainwashed her behind the Satonos' backs? There's no evidence Opal didn't do any of that.

What everyone does agree on is that Ruby is guilty of disrupting Tracen herself. The media frenzy, the mob, the negative atmosphere—all generated by her announcement. And she damn well knew she'd cause chaos, evidenced by how she locked down her account and went radio silent? What kind of uma is she, wreaking havoc across her desired academy and not offering a single post of remorse?

The threats against her are too far, yeah, but it's hard to feel sympathy for someone when they are deliberately making your life more difficult. But, oh, Director Akikawa put her foot down, so the Tracen populace has no reason but to suffer in silence.

Or do they?

It is Seiun Sky, lazy sleepyhead Seiun Sky, who crystallizes the sentiments into concrete form.

"She's a first-year. We're second-years," she reportedly says, "Isn't it our job to help her cut her teeth on something?"

Gasps ripple through the crowd. Wait, it's that simple? A moment's thought, and then: yes, yes, of course it is! Why go through the speculation, the hypothesizing, when Satono Ruby herself can prove her own innocence?

Let her come in, they say. Let her run, sleep, eat, and hang out with the rest of the student body. She'll be treated like any other uma, with a single catch: she must prove that she's not from the same cloth as her mother to at least fifty, sixty…maybe eighty percent of the student body before they pardon her for her crimes. She might have to carry some books, or fetch her seniors yakisoba piles at lunch. Cheap, volunteer work to demonstrate her sincerity. Oh, and she'll be walking on eggshells the entire time. The moment she steps out line and commits a single offense, it's petitions and student protests all the way up towards Akikawa's office.

No, this isn't hazing. That's such a filthy word. It's behavioral assessment. Or gatekeeping. Either way, Satono Ruby better prove she's a good person if she's going to hang with the rest of the Tracen girls.

Ah, Seiun Sky. Now there's an uma with a sharp mind! Unlike a certain grey-coat.

Oguri overhears these plans and think they sound cheesy and kind of lame. Half the girls involved are merely nodding along. It's fun and games until the Twinkle Series looms over the horizon and these girls realise they need to win their maiden or a find a Trainer, stat. They won't actually put their words into practice when Ruby arrives.

Still.

Discerning Satono Ruby's real intentions…it doesn't sound that terrible. She can't not contemplate the idea when so much buzz swarms around her.

She mulls the topic over while lying on the grass, a thin book balanced on her head as a makeshift shade.

————

"I mean, she's still throwing herself into the alligator's maw," Inari One says.

"My thoughts haven't changed since. Maybe she should reconsider if this is the reception she's receiving," Super Creek says.

"Perhaps she should return to the Satonos? Reconciliation might not be impossible. I am not privy to her circumstances, mind," Mejiro Ardan offers.

"Rudolf's clammed up. I've never heard her this silent. Think she's playing the long game?" Tamamo Cross asks.

"When did this place get so lame…" Dicta Striker bemoans.

That's one.

"You gotta be careful around those bastard children, Oguri. Spite's a huge motivator. And those Satonos—they're the old money types. Any possible child of theirs, even from an exiled mother, is potentially big on honor and tradition and ties that bind. Look at England and its imbecilic royal family."

"Isn't New Zealand part of that royalty, though?" Oguri asks.

Folkqueen, half-way across the world, scoffs and flips her gorgeous silvery hair over her morning cornflakes. "We're a constitutional monarchy. That means the royal family means zip. Unless we're talking about Ireland, but they're nowhere near as good as us."

"So…"

"You want a problem solved? Do it yourself," Folkqueen rolls her eyes. "Personally, it's a miracle you guys are inviting her in."

Folkqueen is smart and gorgeous and fluent in Japanese (another point to how awesome she is).

That's two.

"Miss Oguri! What do you think of Satono Ruby?" A random girl asks when passing Oguri by at the lunch table.

"What about her?" Oguri asks.

"Have you, um, heard much about her?"

"A couple of things, yeah," Which is an understatement.

The girl folds her arms in front of her, trying not to smirk. "Do you think she might be a pest, if she comes to Tracen?"

"Is she?"

"A pest."

"Yep, is she a pest or not? I've heard conflicting things."

"Well…hypothetically speaking? Like, she comes over with her head full of dreams about breaking kneecaps. Y'know, like her mom?"

Oguri glances between the group. "I guess she'd be a pest, yeah."

The girl smiles. She has a pin of Oguri herself. A super, super rare rainbow-shaded piece of merchandise.

That's three.

Kitahara and Oguri drink coffee together in his office. It's almost twice as large as some of the other teams', a privilege for Kitahara's excellence amongst Trainers. She asks him if that really was Satono Ruby he evaluated. He answers with a yes, then asks her how her courses are going.

"Oh, I'm doing alright for myself," She responds.

If okay is the definition of barely missing a pass on her last midterm exams.

She could ask him for assistance, but he's already swamped with his own trainees. An uma named Win Variation is experiencing another mental breakdown because of a certain tyrant from Team IKZE. Kitahara has his hands full with finding her a suitable therapist.

That's four.

Against her better judgmenet, Oguri rewatches the documentary about Satono Opal. The video has only gotten more popular since she viewed it all those years ago. The content warning is apt; the injuries of Opal's two compatriots sicken Oguri to the bone now that she's more educated in uma biology, and the sight of Opal waving and blowing kisses to her fans pre-race leaves a seriously bitter taste in her mouth.

Oguri goes to bed hearing the echoes of Semi Sonic's wails. She wakes up, unable to recall her dreams, and tainted with a bad case of bedhead and a curdling, sour sting in her dry mouth.

————

The pile of papers on her desk. The new textbooks in their fresh plastic wrappings.

A note on the calendar wall, circled in red. Exams. Behind them: a cabinet of dusty, old trophies and ribbons.

Five becomes six.

————

X number of days before Satono Ruby's arrival—no-one truly can land on a concrete number—Oguri finds herself convinced. It's taken a good week or so of mulling in private and listening to the surrounding chatter, but she done it. Not the hazing the others attempt to pass off as 'surveillance'. She won't stand for that. The idea where someone trails behind Satono Ruby and examines her—that has merit.

The girl is legitimately radioactive. She did cause panic at Tracen, deliberate or otherwise. A sizable amount of concerning reels and footage snippets are passed around Umastagram. Concerning lyrics, vociferous shouts, and allegations of bad behavior from first-time viewers. Oguri is no expert in the idol industry, but how different can it be compared to Winning Lives?

But, those are secondary reasons. When she boils it down, Tracen is Oguri's second home. More than the place where she eats, rests and studies, it is the academy where her legend was born, where she built herself into the uma she is today. So many priceless connections, friendships and memories were formed here that it moistens the eyes thinking about the weight of it all.

There exists a Tracen where Satono Ruby is normal and plain and harms no-one when she settles in. There also exists a Tracen where Satono Ruby is fuming with hatred for what the URA does to her mother and enacts a mass sabotage campaign against innocent Tracen students. Both exist in limbo, interdeminate. Oguri cannot risk the second reality ending up true.

It's better she does it than the mass group of self-appointed hall monitors. A single mind has focus, direction. It also has a line to Rudolf. Once Oguri observes Satono Ruby enough and maybe after talking to her a bit, she can declare to the student body that Satono Ruby is harmless and then there's nothing to worry about. She'll have evidence and proof and Satono Ruby can plead her case, and everything will be safe and normal again.

People called her a hero in her glory days. They saw her as a beacon of hope, an individual with the responsibility to exert a positive influence upon the world.

May she step into those shoes for real this time.

May she stamp out a potential evil before it manifests.

May she give back to her beloved Tracen, as much as it has provided her.

It sounds corny, but it also has a nice ring to it.

She smiles.

————

Imagine her bewilderment when Narita Brian asks her to join in on a practice race. Imagine her surprise when she approaches a wispy, lanky girl with cascading black hair and spots the dented faux-gold crown ornament on her ear. Satono Ruby, in the flesh.

Prime Oguri would've glared right off the bat. The Oguri of the present is more mature, more malleable. Drawing upon a multi-day revision of her PR training, she manages to force her facial expression still, restraining her curiosity, her eagerness—

"So where's the chibi?"

—and successfully pretend she's never seen Ruby before.

Admittedly, her footsteps might've gotten a little intense when approaching. The rest, however, should be easy. Opaqueness in transparency—Folkqueen mentioned Oguri had that aura around her, a backhanded compliment at the time, but as long Oguri she takes refuge in it, pretends that she's single-minded like she was in the past, as opposed to the more complex, thoughtful uma she is now, she can hide from Ruby that she's sussing the other girl out.

Oh, and Grass Wonder is there too.

They chat, the three of them. Oguri and Grass introduce themselves to each other. Satono Ruby gazes at them, seemingly awestruck. Rudolf calls for the race, the real reason they're all gathered here today.

Oguri's heart thumps. This is it, then. The beginning of Oguri's quest to do Tracen a solid. Something other than writing essays and helping starstruck umas re-evaluate the basics. She'll run this race, peek into Satono Ruby's soul and rip out a sliver of what she's truly like. The moment she reveals that she follows her mother in any way, shape or form—

PART 3

"What are you doing?"

It's been a long while since an uma sneaked up behind Oguri and spoke this close into her ear. Back stiffening, tail going rigid, Oguri turns around to see who it is. It's Grass Wonder, standing a few steps away where the yard's grass meets the veranda pavement. She's cradling a pile of textbooks, much like any other student between classes. The gentle breeze whips up the tail ends of her elegant, chestnut-brown hair.

They stare at each other for a moment before Oguri clears her throat.

"Hi, Grass."

"Hello to you, too, Miss Oguri. Could you answer my question, please?" Grass says. She's wearing a cautious frown.

"I was looking at Ruby."

"And why were you doing that?"

"Who's asking?" Oguri asks.

"Her new student mentor, that's who," Grass responds.

Ah. Right. The new program Rudolf set up to help struggling students. It's a bit obscure, as only two umas—Ruby and Grass herself—are currently involved in it as a test run. Very few individuals outside of those two know the program exists. Oguri's only counted because Rudolf told her about it in a DM after Ruby's first race.

The thought of that causes Oguri's own frown to grow.

"Is something the matter?" Grass asks.

"No, just thinking back to Ruby's first race. Y'know, from a few days ago."

"Is that the reason for your behavior? Did I interrupt you from speaking to her," Grass says. She bows her head slightly. "You can ask her for a rematch someday, if you'd like. She'd be more than happy to agree."

"Would she?"

"It'd be her second real race with a fellow uma. It's not as if there are many others willing to share a track with her at the moment, so I'd assume you'd be delighted," Grass says. Her ears flick. She suddenly tilts her head sideways, locking eyes with a trio of eavesdroppers elsewhere across the grass and causing them to freeze on the spot. A mild nod of her head, and the trio scatters. "You'd have to do it outside our training sessions, though. Those are meant for us and us alone. Again, my apologies."

Oguri falls silent for longer than is considered acceptable in a conversation, and long enough for Grass to make that puzzled frown of hers again. It's not that she dislikes the idea of a handicapped race, Oguri thinks about saying. She's done it dozens of times whenever she helps out Kitahara or Belno's team during training. It's more the fact that Ruby mentioned her race with Grass and Oguri was her first-ever casual case. As in, before she arrived at Tracen, she never ran a single stretch of distance with another umamusume in her entire life.

Were Oguri Folkqueen, she would've rolled her eyes so hard they'd threaten to bounce out of their sockets. Come on, Ruby. You lived in Tokyo, one of the largest modern metropolises in the modern world. Oguri wasn't born yesterday.

That incident was the first point in her report, placed within the 'insincere' bucket. Grass doesn't need to know that.

"Nah," Oguri says.

"No?" Grass prompts.

"I mean, I do sort of want to, but I can't. Got the rest of my master's degree to catch up on. It's on a delayed schedule, which helps, but the professors are lighting fires beneath my ass. And I signed up to help out my old Trainer and sub in for a few other teachers, too."

"I see," Grass says. "Is that related to why your eyes lingered on Ruby's back for several seconds after she left?" Grass says.

A small blip of annoyance pulses through Oguri's forehead. She forces it aside.

"Ruby was saying hi to me and left. I guess…" Oguri shrugs. "I was spacing out a bit, I guess."

"Immediately after the conversation ended?"

"It happens sometimes. My friends tell me I daydream a lot when I shouldn't. That's also something I'm working on," Oguri says. "What about you?"

Grass narrows her eyes, a movement that suggests she's now studying Oguri's body language, instead of merely deciphering it. Tension turns Oguri's ears rigid and her nostrils flare. Neither of them receives the chance to talk further. The morning bell rings, a shrill, repetitive clanging of several seconds. The small cluster of girls spectating from afar hurry off, joining the trickles of crowds towards the next classroom.

"Please don't distract Ruby. We've got a lot of work to do before she's up to scratch."

Grass bows once, stiffly, and leaves.

Oguri watches her go for a moment, then turns around and walks away in the other direction.

————

The farmer did not know the viper would bite him until the fangs sank into his chest. The frog and the scorpion promised mutual cooperation, yet the scorpion stung the frog while they crossed the river, for that was in its nature. The similarity between both folk tales is that both deaths could've been avoided, had the farmer or the toad bothered to open their eyes from the very beginning.

Comparing Ruby to either venomous creature sounds mean on the surface, but the girl did lie to Oguri, after all.

Like the viper or the scorpion, Oguri doesn't need to look far to get a grasp on how Ruby operates. She eats breakfast near the outer rim of the cafeteria tables. She attends her morning classes. Her afternoon is eaten up by her personal training, after which she returns to the academy for dinner or heads straight back to the Miho dorm, where she doesn't emerge until the following day. Sometimes she eats with her roommate, Meisho Tabaru, but otherwise, she's alone.

Rinse and repeat.

It's a routine that's—

—milquetoast.

That's the appropriate term. Milquetoast. Ordinary. It's the sign of a girl who knows she's many stretches behind her peers and is knuckling down to cram as much as she can before tryouts begin. It's nothing suspicious.

On the contrary, it's beneficial. If Ruby's routine is predictable, then so are her movements, which means it's easy to anticipate and meet up with her for a chat, a quick run, an opportunity to peel behind that surface-level smile and uncover the real her. That's what Oguri, along with Ruby's collection of hecklers and self-appointed hall monitors, agree on.

Reality isn't so simple. A single obstacle blocks their efforts, and her name is Grass Wonder.

The yamato nadeshiko of Team Rigil. The Chestnut Monster. The second coming of Maruzensky. An impressive pedigree, one which Oguri would've loved to race against during her prime days, but since Rudolf slotted Grass into the trialing student mentorship program, Oguri didn't think much of her beyond understanding her placement made sense. Yeah, okay. Whatever. Have the most sensible and least lazy member of the Golden Generation teach a struggling student. The idea prints money and publicity. It was strange that Rudolf chose Satono Opal's kid as the trial student, but Ruby was the weakest in her year level. It's not as if the program was intended to be public.

What Oguri didn't expect was Grass to act as Ruby's unofficial Trainer. Grass apparently took her newfound duties with great seriousness and conducted a threefold plan to polish Ruby up to perfection. Step one: hone Ruby's body by destroying and reconstructing her musculature by way of basics amped up to eleven every afternoon. Step two: add racing theory on top of her existing catch-up homework. Step three: constantly check up with her during gaps between classes to evaluate her mental state.

"Ruby, how are you today?"

"Grass! Eh, um, I kinda almost passed out while doing my homework yesterday…"

"You've got a spot of ketchup on your cheek, by the way."

"I do? I do! Oh no…and I call myself an umadol…"

There's no time for Ruby to wander around Tracen. There's no energy for her to respond to the hecklers who try to get up in her face. Grass acts like a shield when Ruby speaks to, her reputation as the epitome of gentle, yet frightening strength, baulking most hecklers or prospects. Anyone who protests her involvement is immediately shut down.

"My involvement with Ruby is part of a special program created by President Rudolf. The full details are classified. I hope you can understand," Grass says in these situations.

She's a thorn in these hecklers' sides, this Grass Wonder. It stings more, knowing that she's so accomplished, so respected. No-one is brave enough to suggest she is persona non grata, like her new apprentice, so they speculate instead. She is Seiun's friend. Is Grass on secretly board with Seiun here? Is she pretending to play nice with Ruby, waiting like everyone else is for Ruby to snap and thus seize a chance for justice? Oguri disagrees. Grass's attitude lacks the belligerence Oguri would assume from someone with those motives. She's pleasant, professional, and never insults Ruby once.

People become jealous of Ruby for spending time with Grass alone.

It gets so bad, Oguri picks up those threats of violence from before Ruby arrived. Slapping her, giving her noogies out of nowhere, hitting her with filled water bottles. Oguri saw the last one on a show about a youth internment center; the water bottles are less likely to leave bruises. Fury fills her. She notifies the student council in secret. She cannot abide by violence in her Tracen, even towards Opal's own daughter.

————

As for Oguri's own pursuit, she isn't so foolish as to crash Grass's training sessions, especially not after that awkward meeting in the yard. The good news is that Grass doesn't occupy Ruby's time forever. She has her own races to train for. Lapses in her attention exist: gaps in which Ruby sits alone with a table and her ears twitch because her instincts can tell others are staring. These are times when Oguri meets up with Ruby. Where the real observation happens.

Ruby's got instincts. Her ears prick up like fresh dandelions when she's sitting alone. They twitch with the practice of someone used to discerning individual streams of sounds, from concerts, presumably. She's keen enough to anticipate when someone is creeping up behind her. If it's someone she recognises, she gives a gentle smile and a wave.

She doesn't hesitate when Oguri is the uma pulling up the chair. Nor does she comment on Oguri's sunglasses.

"Hi, Miss, um…"

"Oguri is fine."

"Okay, then. Hi, Oguri! How's your week been? Lot of books you've got there in your hands."

"Ah, these? They're for my degree."

"University?"

"Master of Agriculture. Tokyo University. They're letting me study here as part of a special program. I've got two papers to write and an online interview to get through. They're doing alright."

"Wow, sounds tough. My old manager used to tell me horror stories about his business and communications degree. A quarter of it involved drinking with his senpais…"

Did you deliberately call the mob on Tracen, Ruby? Did you know half the academy would end up working in a tizzy? How often do you contact your mother, if at all? Oguri asks none of these questions and zero of the others. Ruby would not answer them, whether she's an average uma or a secretly malicious uma. No, what Oguri wants to find are the subtleties, the slip-ups of the true self behind society's politeness. Behavior akin to Obey Your Master and her attempts to act friendly while eyeing the competition with a hawk inside. The more amicably Oguri acts to Ruby, the easier it is to detects these hidden aspects of her.

On it goes.

Over the first two weeks, Oguri manages to nab a few talks with Ruby. None go over the allotted lunch break, and the majority are less than five minutes long. No-one bothers them, at least from what Oguri can see, which means the sunglasses are working, she guesses.

Ruby beams like Opal did when she won her first G2. She giggles like Opal during that interview when Opal asked if she could ever beat Maruzensky. She totters around, swinging one foot across another while hunched over, like Opal post exercise therapy from that recovered Satono public archives' footage.

Oguri tries not to let that influence her. Tries.

Opal's victorious visage bleeds upon her daughter, amidst the shadowy outlines of her mangled two victims. She destroyed those two innocents. Defiled the uma's sacrosanct right to run, with a punishment that ended up a slap on the wrist on society's widespread scale.

Writing unbiased notes about Ruby's behavior is difficult when Oguri is battered with flashes of that same curdling sourness in her gut.

She implied she downloaded movies from 'alternate' means. Is that illegal? Connected to Opal stealing that toolbox from the supply cabinet?

————

"We meet again, Oguri."

"Hey, Grass."

"Looking for Ruby again?"

"Not particularly. I was just passing by the turf."

"I don't see Trainer Kitahara's team today. Perhaps you got the time wrong?"

"Nah, I'm not here for him. I was on a walk and there're such a thing as looking for a bathroom."

"…go and use it. And be prompt. Ruby might end up too starstruck and want your autograph."

Grass giggles at that, but it's the polite, not-so-sincere type of giggle.

————

One week becomes two, then three. Results from the unofficial scrims and classes pop up. The wider scene begins sorting the crop from the chaff: Kitasan Black, Mihono Bourbon, Satono Diamond, and more. It's early speculation and is thus no substitute for reality following the next set of debuts—a sudden heroine like Oguri Cap herself could manifest out of nowhere—but it serves as a decent enough approximation for the tipsters to get their juices salivating.

Ruby, however, lies firmly in the chaff. Her form is sloppy; her acceleration wanes when it should surge forth. Her stance needs a chiropractor or whatever kind of doctor fixes bones and ligament structures. There's very little guarantee Rudolf's program will be able to shape her up in time. Grass is an adequate teacher, but is she a great one?

What's interesting, and also concerning, is how the hecklers and self-appointed hall monitors have taken it upon themselves to warn the best rookies about Ruby. Vivlos dear, don't approach her, she's not interested in Dubai, probably. Mayano, your father would kill her if she knew you were fraternizing with an uma so dangerous. Mihono Bourbon…you don't care about anything; you're good. Satono Diamond, you need no explanation. Please beat her ass into the dirt. Kitasan Black…I know she's pitiful, but a rabid dog doesn't stop drooling just because you learned its name.

The pin is poised to drop. The mask's wiry bands are fraying. Soon, the facade of cordiality Ruby has grasped so desperately will detach, revealing the hive of plague-ridden pests born from her mother's madness. The evidence? The fact that Ruby is looking brighter, for whatever reason. Guess Grass must've accidentally felt sorry for her. But that's good, because it means Ruby can't avoid the comments, the rightful questions.

She'll snap any moment now. When she does, they, and Oguri, will primed to bring down the hammer.

Any day now.

Any fortnight now.

Any…

…

————

"Where is it?"

Oguri overhears that line while waiting in line with her XXXL-sized food tray in the cafeteria.

"Where's the goddamn breaking point, damn it?" One of Ruby's hecklers barks at her friend, "You said she was as loony as her mom and hiding her seething and plotting to break the top rookies' cleats during the tryouts? Where's the proof, huh? She was supposed to have gone delulu by now!"

Through the cafeteria and amidst the LANE chatrooms, the same message echoes in lividness at the single phenomenon, or lack thereof on Ruby's part.

No snide insults. No letters made out of disparate newspaper chunks. No evidence of a plot to ruin her classmates' shoes or cleats. She eats, she runs, she trains with Grass, she sings alone on the empty practice stage. She lives like a normal uma in her circumstances.

Another girl vocalizes the burgeoning opinion.

"This is so lame!"

For the hecklers and hall monitors, Ruby's inaction is a death blow. Impossible, they say. This can't be happening. Something must, should definitely be happening. Ramp up the efforts. Pressure her. Mock her about her mom—

Except Ruby seems used to such taunts and simply blanks them out.

Make her buy yakisoba—

Except Ruby always manages to slip past, her footsteps swift as a swan's flight. Or she doesn't come back and it's revealed she devoured the yakisoba by herself.

Fine, the hecklers say, red-faced, let's invite her to run and haze her there—

Except Grass Wonder pops out of nowhere, including during strategy meetings, and brandishes a waiver signed by Rudolf and Director Akikawa themselves. Anyone who interrupts Rudolf's special trial program—a critical piece of Tracen infrastructure, by the way—will be penalized with suspension, with repeat offenders threatened with expulsion.

"The President decided that she will not tolerate nonsense during our training sessions," Grass says, "I happen to agree."

The waiver also bears a confidential policy. Do not speak a word to anyone about this. If you do, Grass will find out.

Grass is also seen involving herself more with Ruby. The cafeteria catches Ruby eating with Special Week, with Grass mediating between them. Team Spica behavior, what else can you do? But didn't Special Week cry over the thought of Ruby joining, or were those onlookers hallucinating?

Seiun Sky just shrugs when questioned.

"Huh? Why are you coming to me? All I did was make a suggestion that you guys ran away with. Me? I've got my own races to worry about."

She's useless.

Grass Wonder is a wall. A fortress. And like archers against a fortress, umas give up battering against it.

Oguri supposes it's a good thing that Ruby isn't causing trouble? She doesn't usually have to ask herself those questions. The more she thinks about it, the more she finds she cannot bring herself to believe it. Opal hid intentions for years. Why should her daughter be let off with a tiny fraction of that time?

She doesn't want to distrust Ruby, obviously. For fairness's sake, Ruby needs another chunk of time under the magnifying glass.

More meetings in the hallway. More waved hands when she's waiting in line at the classrooms. More excuses to inch near her during morning breaks and in the lunch lines.

————

"You should stop."

"Pardon?"

"I said, you should stop. Stop following Ruby around, Oguri Cap. You clearly have ill intentions regarding her, and as her student mentor, I refuse to abide by that."

"Excuse me?"

A day approaching dusk. A deserted hallway cast in half shadow, half muted light. Grass Wonder stands beneath a hanging lamp, her hands clasped in front of her, her posture forward and straight. The politeness she wore in front of her friends and requesters is wiped from her elegant features, replaced with a restrained unpleasantness that sets Oguri's ears at full-mast.

This is not the delicate wallflower of a magazine cover. This is an uma prepared for conflict.

Oguri tucks her phone back into her pocket. She folds her arms. "Excuse me?"

Grass exhales. "For the last time—"

"No, I heard that," Oguri says. "I was asking, because I was confused, and I was confused because it sounded like you were accusing me."

"It is always a pleasure when my conversation partner re-discovers her ears," Grass replies.

"Yeah," Oguri says, darkly. "They never stopped working in the first place."

Grass tilts her head. "Do you deny it, then?"

Is this girl for real?

"Yes?" Oguri takes a step forward. She widens her eyes to boggle at Grass. Her arms hug her chest, tighter. "Yes, like hell yes, I deny it. I'm the one wondering if your head is screwed on straight. Are you listening to yourself? Ill intentions—what have I ever said or done to Ruby that warrants that kind of talk?"

She's snarling now. Grass does not flinch. She lets out a very small sigh through her nose. "I can think of multiple examples."

"Lay it on me, then. Tell me what I'm doing wrong."

"I want you to understand, Miss Oguri, that from face value, you state that your repeated meetings with Ruby are merely coincidences and casual meetings that contain no unspoken intentions whatsoever."

Tightness in her chest. Oguri brushes it aside and does not let it show—she hopes. "Don't put me on the same level as the girls who feel it's okay to pick on Ruby all the time?"

"That's another thing. I've also noticed you haven't been telling those girls to apologize," Grass says.

"Last time I checked, that's your job, isn't it?" Oguri points out.

"A one-uma operation can't cover everything. I would've appreciated the assistance, particularly from a source as magnificent as the Ashen Beast."

"It's not like I haven't been doing nothing. There were girls who hyped themselves up about physically assaulting Ruby. I reported them to Air Groove. They got thrown into detention for two weeks," Oguri says.

And this, she speaks with confidence. A couple of girls huddled in a group, giggling about pokes, slaps, tickles, filled water bottles. Oguri recognised that tactic from a true crime TV show she watched once. Apparently, they're a substitute for batons or sticks that will hurt but not bruise.

That gives Grass pause. For a second, a glimmer of positivity seems to cross those features, scraping away the disdain. Then, it's squeezed to dust. The lines grow harder, meaner, on Grass's face.

"Is that all?" she says.

Oguri rolls her eyes. "For the love of—"

"It's wonderful that you stopped Ruby from being hurt—I will acknowledge that. It does nothing to remove the root cause of the program."

"That's not my job."

Grass titters. "Again! The legendary Ashen Beast says she has no sway over the rest of the class."

Oguri focuses on her. "Stars fade out and vanish. You might not know this, but people take me less seriously than they did in the past. It'll happen to you, too."

"But it is still not nothing," Grass says, "Fine. A different avenue, then. I caught you staring into Ruby's classroom."

"That's a…" Not normal, but since Ruby was there, what was the harm? "I was passing by and was curious what classes she attended."

"Normal umas don't stop and watch a girl like a hawk, Miss Oguri."

"And you're trying to take everything I say in the worst light possible!" Oguri counters.

Grass pauses again. "No."

"No?" Oguri exclaims.

"No, as in, I do not wish to listen to whatever excuses you've written regarding your behavior. I did not come here to bargain or debate with you, Miss Oguri. I came here to tell you," Grass advances until she and Oguri are within tail's reach. She speaks quietly, so steely that Oguri imagines a razor blade jutting onto her lips, "Here are the facts of the matter, Miss Oguri Cap. You are watching Ruby. You have gone out of your way to cross paths with Ruby whenever she has a moment of spare time between appointments. To her, it seems nothing out of the ordinary. The two of you chat normally and leave. What she doesn't know, and what I hope she never finds out, is that the moment her back faces yours, Oguri, your smile drops and you pierce her flesh with your eyes as if you want to rip her heart out and read it like a book. Those are not the interactions of a concerned senpai. They are those of an amateur, make-believe detective who has already painted a perfectly normal uma as a ticking time bomb."

Oguri lurches back. Rage flashes onto her. "You—"

"Honestly, I should be sending you towards Air Groove for stalking. It'd kill Ruby to learn one of the superstars she ran her first ever race with had approached her with such malicious intent, so I won't."

"That's only your opinion, damn it. Sophistry. I was—" A third thump in her heart. The organ strains against its ribcage. Her breathing starts to go shallow. "—just checking up on her."

Grass smiles sweetly. "I apologize, Miss Oguri Cap. I don't believe you."

Her venom glues Oguri's tongue to the tip of her mouth. Silence lapses. Within it, Grass backs off. She smooths the wrinkles in her skirt. She brushes off her smile and returns to the same contempt she began this conversation .

"Ruby is an ordinary girl, and I'd appreciate it if you and the rest of the girls would consider that line of thought for a change. Now, please do not go near her again, or I will contact Rudolf and have you removed."

She sweeps past Oguri and vanishes down the hall.

————

The next morning, Grass treats the entire academy to the sight of her walking Ruby to her morning classes.

————

At first, Oguri is peeved. Grass Wonder—the audacity of this uma! How dare she compare Oguri to some perverted, invasive stalker? It wasn't as if Oguri sneaked into Ruby's room, or took candid photos of her, or tried to steal her clothes for private and frankly repulsive sniffing sessions. All she did was get close to Ruby on multiple occasions in order to better understand Ruby's personality. Since when did it become a crime to mingle in the same general vicinity as another person?

Besides, Tracen umas trail each other constantly for the sake of gaining an edge over their opponents. Mihono Bourbon's got a follower, apparently. There's Daitaku Helios and Daiichi Ruby, though admittedly Helios's pursuits possess reasons beyond racing. Obey Your Master collected photos and recordings to plaster her room with, and while that wasn't right, it wasn't wrong either, and it let her win the Japan Cup, so who cares?

Oguri goes about the next few days fuming inside. When Tamamo asks, she just pretends she lost out on a box of carrots or whatever.

She was close. So close. A few more months and Oguri would've made a breakthrough—surely! She can't risk offending Rudolf, and reluctantly obeys Grass's request to leave Ruby alone.

She sees Grass in the halls on occasion, and the two of them fix each other with glares. That's it, though. With no Ruby in Oguri's line of sight, Oguri loses focus on her. She stops pondering Ruby. When she is reminded, in the middle of a shower no less, she finds a vacuum is carved out in place of her ire. Her head feels cool and unstuck for the first time in a blue moon.

After she dries herself off, she returns to her room. She picks up her old notes from beneath a forgotten nature study textbook and grimaces. Were they always this long?

She re-reads them.

Uma A called Ruby names. Ruby ignored them. Uma B said the girls in her class messed with her pens. Ruby pulled spare ones out of her uniform and picked them up after class anyway. Uma C said what an evil uma Opal was behind Ruby's back, when she was within earshot, and Ruby said nothing.

Day in and day out, Ruby does not escalate back, even when her hecklers are mocking her, even when they're doing it in front of the teachers, even when they should've been reported a long time ago.

Thirty records exist in these notes regarding Ruby's confrontations with umas who aren't Grass, Special Week or Meisho Tabaru or Oguri herself, and zero of them portray Ruby as anything but a victim. The rest are informative, journalistic—

—invasive.

All of this, in Oguri's own handwriting.

She imagines Opal. The notes are vindictive. She imagines Ruby. She feels perturbed, as if someone is poking her in the wrong places. Finally, she imagines Tamamo or Super Creek in Ruby's place. The resulting visions send up a spurt of nausea. In its wake, a realization settles in Oguri's gut like a rock. Her fingers shake. She cannot vocalize it. The fire that pushed her forward wavers with a mounting horror.

————

No-one wishes to acknowledge they are wrong, Oguri Cap included. She throws herself into denial. She shoves the oversized mess of words and phrases that constitute the report's true implications into a rickety wooden door in the back of her head. The moment she arranges those fragments, she will fall over the edge, never to return.

The world spits in her face. Ruby's self-appointed hall monitors lose their fervor. What's the point in waiting for a drop that'll never arrive? They experience enough anticlimaxes in their races themselves.

"She's not doing anything…this is boring."

"Heard her textbook got ruined after a scrap in the locker—isn't that a bit much?"

"Fenomeno dragged a girl who boasted about punching Ruby by her ears to the Director's office. That's scary. Maybe we should stop. I kinda don't wanna get in trouble with the teachers."

Their chatter floats around like a hive of wasps. Other accomplished umas weigh in.

"Why did you all waste time on this stuff…what a bother."

"Rice…I mean, I'm glad I don't have to walk on tiptoes anymore…"

"Disgusting peasants and their awful spending of their time."

"Fuku said Ruby helped her out, so she can't be that bad, right?"

"Don't be too upset at those girls who changed their ways. Slowly, steadily, we all grow up~"

Her own friends chime in.

"I'm so relieved nothing serious has happened to that poor girl. She shouldn't have been blamed for what her mother did," Super Creek says.

"Oh yeah, you were compared to Opal once," Inari One says.

"It was so long ago I almost forgot about the incident until news of Ruby arrived. I do recall being quite furious at the time. I'd hate for Ruby to have met that more immature version of myself."

These were the same girls who spun the rumor mill when Ruby wasn't around. Oguri's grip tightens on her chopsticks.

"Told y'all it was a big nothingburger. I swear, these kids these days. Too much gossip and not enough legwork," Tamamo says, "What about you, Oguri?"

Oguri glances up from her steak. Her throat seizes, and she chokes out tiny shreds of meat into a napkin.

"Uh, you good?" Tamamo asks.
