"Ladies! First item on our agenda. Let's get into it." Hands slam on the table. Pens rattle. "We must create a brand-new public persona for Ruby."

Agnes Digital is famous for two things. The first is fangirling over her fellow Tracen umas to the point where drool trickles out of the side of her mouth; and the second is stealing G1 trophies from the turf and dirt with such ferocity, such consistency, that it paints the first point's behavior as a nigh-on split personality. Both of these versions are ghosts in the present.

"Ideas. Names. Even intrusive thoughts!" Kaori's pointer raps on the whiteboard, held in Digital's hand. "List them, and I'll jot them down. Once we've got a dozen or so, we'll mindmap the daylights out of them!"

It shouldn't be possible for an uma whose hair is so bubblegum saccharine-pink to order around you and Jordan with such authority, but that's Agnes Digital for you. The same applies to that huge red ribbon. Team Rasalhauge, you realize, is being blessed with the honor of witnessing the third version of Tracen's most accomplished deviant.

"Come on, ladies! Anything will do." Digital raps the whiteboard again, creating a faint knocking sound. It wouldn't sound out of place from a corporate boardroom. When no one answers, Digital doesn't kick up a fuss. She picks up a blue pen from the whiteboard's rack. "I'll start. The Tracen uniform. Simple and recognizable."

"That's, like, so vanilla," Jordan says. "It's not going to be enough."

"And how so, my darling Tosen Jordan?" Digital asks.

"The elephant in the room, Digitan. Do I need to say it out loud?"

"Yes," Digital responds.

Jordan blinks. "…why?"

"To get the brain juices flowing. So that we can think harder about it," Digital says. "Mind-mapping."

"Y'know, I'm totally zoned out in that area."

"A one-in-a-million chance of something happening is not zero at all. Sometimes, the obvious solution is the best."

"It so is not here!" Jordan cries out.

"It's okay, Jordan. You don't need to explain," you say, reaching over and patting Jordan on the shoulder. "We all have our bad days."

Jordan's twintails flail and cross over as she turns around and shoots you an offended look. Were this the Nightmare, you think your brain would've exploded like a beach watermelon.

She knows it's a cheap shot. She knows that you know you said that on purpose, but she can't help taking the bait. A gal's pride must be defended. Crossing her arms, she lets out an annoyed, unladylike snort. "It's because of her damn mom, duh."

"Satono Opal," Digital says.

"Satono-freaking-Opal. The worst uma to have ever lived. As long as she exists, no one's ever gonna see Rubes for Rubes when Opal's sword of Damo-whatever is hanging over her head. They'll just see her as a repeat of an uma who sent two girls to the hospital, including what she's about to do in the debut. We walk into Hanshin's courtyard and there'll be a hundred dumbass paparazzi swarming over us like flies, asking if we need to show them our cleats or some stupid crap. I've already got trolls on my Umasta DMing me with slurs or asking if they need a private detective to check Rubes' behavior in the academy."

She slouches back in her seat and folds her arms. "There. I said it."

You hum, contemplative. She sort of insulted your mother again, but at least she didn't give Kaori a pleading look. Jordan earns three and a half stars out of five for this one.

"Jordan," Digital begins.

"Yeah, Digitan?"

"You are so right. The soldier simping for her faves recoils at the thought of saying this, but we cannot ignore the Satono Opal problem!" Digital exclaims, clapping her hands. "Ruby requires her own pizazz. The spark of a star inside her, unique and shining imminently, brilliantly, for her future stans to salivate and lavish attention with all their love in their hearts. Opal stigma will hold for some time, but as long as Ruby succeeds in her career in a steady fashion, it'll fade. The audience hungers for glory over spite, nine times out of ten guaranteed!"

"…yeah, that's why I said it was obvious," Jordan says. She tips her head back as she rolls her eyes. "Again, duh. Why did we even talk about this?"

"Well, it gave me food for thought. Think of it as a massage for the brain." Kaori raises her hand, speaking up. Jordan glances behind her, to which Kaori gives a small smile, then resumes speaking. "If we're attempting to give Ruby the best possible first impression, I do have some old outfits from my early days in my apartment closet."

Jordan sticks out her tongue. "Too high society. We're not copying the Satonos or your mom."

"Hmm. Good point. And the silk is out of style this month, if my friend is to be believed."

"Umas in the past have worn their tracksuits to prove their commitment to their personal regime until the last second before their race. I think Oguri did that. That's a regional thing, though," Digital muses.

Ideas float around and are scribbled down on the whiteboard's mind map. None of them are solidified as the 'one'. No one has detected that you are forming an idea that might be the 'one'. You're staying silent on it for now, because there are a few internal checks you need to run first.

"What if I ask Gold City for help?"

"Added to the list!"

"She might kvetch at helping Opal's kid…nah, she's too mature to get mad at that. Sorry, City."

Eventually, attention turns to you.

"What do you think, Ruby? You've been quiet this whole time," Kaori says. "This is about you, after all."

"Yeah, I got something," you reply. "Was thinking about it."

"Out with it, then," Jordan says.

[Underground Umadol: Exists.]

You raise your hand and grunt to clear your throat. "I'm wearing my old umadol outfit to Hanshin."

Then you fold your arms and look the other three occupants in the eye. The trick to launching a request over the finish line is to first frame it as a statement, not a question.

The reactions are immediate. Kaori stares. Jordan snorts, smirking with disbelief. That, too, morphs into a stare, when you fold your arms and stand your ground, metaphorically speaking. Only Digital doesn't react with scorn or surprise.

Your eyes meet, and there it is, striking like an arc of lightning between transformers. Rapport. The mutual synchronization of minds between two umas separated by time yet whose souls were forged in the same blazing hot furnaces of the oshi and the wotagei. Agnes Digital, praise the three goddesses, understands not only that being an umadol is amazing and spiritually exciting and a whole list of adjectives you wrote in a blog post once, but also that it's one of the few stages where Satono Ruby separated herself from Satono Opal. And the narratives! There's much to be said about how the umadol stage saved you from starvation, transformed you from a false bumpkin of a miko into a modern city girl and earned you your first measure of success! That's more good press divorced from your mother's scandal.

You can't help but smile, smugly. Yep, yep, no question about it. Your umadol costume must be brought to your debut. It's too great of a chance to miss out on.

A tear almost falls from your eye. Man, Rudolf is so intelligent and awesome, handing Digital to you as your mentor.

You pluck out your phone and flip open the Gallery app. Tomorrow is FAITHFUL earned a moderate amount of success in the underground leagues, enough for your old manager to afford multiple outfits instead of sticking to the same ones for multiple years, as is the case for the less fortunate groups. Flowing, black-and-crimson kimonos layered with gold paired with ofudas and mock paper umbrellas; alternate shrine maiden outfits that were deliberately frilly and lacy to contrast the traditional getup; punkish half-kimonos that took over neon cyberpunk hues and Harajuku-style maximalism. All of this was made possible by the amazing and insane Seamstress Sugar, whose connections to factory wholesale outlets are as aged and interminable as the needlework in her home-made crimson scarf.

"Ooh, me likey!" Digital says, as you pull up one of the looser, summer punk kimonos from your Umastagram. "Do you have this on you?"

"No. I could ask around, though. Pretty sure my old group will let me," you say.

"They do look lovely. Very spirited, very personable. If we enter at a regular time, without disguising ourselves or avoiding the crowd—yes, it'll certainly make for a remarkable, if astonishing appearances. Nothing we can't handle, though. And yet…" Kaori steps around the sofa to you. "Ruby. Are you sure you can borrow that outfit without encountering legal issues?"

You grin, raising the V-sign with two fingers. "Fanservice."

Kaori blinks. "I'm not seeing it."

"Anything goes in the underground scene, as long as fanservice is on the line."

"Is that meant to convince me?"

"It's the reason why my old manager won't cut the call the instant I tell him my idea," you say. "That, and the prospect of advertising."

Underground idols already flourish in audacity, and FAITHFUL needs every edge they can scramble for, now that you're out of the picture.

Your answer gets to Kaori. She pauses for another second.

"And you'll fit that costume?"

"Totally, totally! It's not like a full year has passed, or anything." You slap your chest for emphasis.

[Nutrition check: 65/50 -> Success! +5 EXP]

Tracen might've given you more to eat, but you've been careful to maintain your weight and waist circumference since you entered. Not that there was time to indulge in sweets, given Grass's training and the tryouts and all.

"I'll wear one of my old outfits, strut around the place, take a few selfies for my socmed and say hi to my old fans," you say. "Word on Umastagram is that they're preparing a meetup at the racecourse."

"Seriously?" Jordan pulls a face. "We're bringing that sort of energy into Hanshin? Bunch of sweaty salarymen with headbands around their heads."

Your mood instantly flips a one eighty. "Excuse me?"

"What?"

"What did you just say?"

"It's not my fault some of those guys are creeps."

"My fans are not creeps, thank you very much!" Now it's your turn to exclaim, "True, some of them have their oddities, but at the end of the day they're all upstanding, respectable members of society who just needed a bit of sparkle in their lives, is all."

"They radiate stink lines, Rubes."

Oh, now she's done it. With a surge of energy, you leap onto your feet. Jordan tries to scramble off the couch, but she's too late. You've blocked her path, hands on your hips with your shadow looming over her own form. All attempts for this dummy to beg Kaori for help are futile. Futile! The speech is tearing its way across your tongue. It's time for some good, old-fashioned umadol noblesse oblige!

"Mister Hideki stopped drinking so much after I told him Miss Liver would be sad and he wouldn't get to visit our concerts too much. Mister Taka said my cheki gave him the boost to ace the internal corporate interview that gave him a promotion. Mister Janai said I was one of the few sources of happiness in his miserable dead-end convenience store job while his father drowned in debt!"

"Hold on, those guys are…all guys."

She's pulling the gender card. A classic move. But you possess the counter.

"Miss Atsuko used our songs as motivation to curb her belly fat," you say, and then whip out your phone, showing a picture of a nervous, bookish girl holding a signed bookmark. "And Miss Sakurai here got so inspired she started her own vtubing career and is pulling in triple digits on Umatube!"

"Alright, I get it, I get it!" Jordan shouts, flinging herself off the sofa and through the gap in your side. She scoots back against the wall, breathing raggedly, where she jabs a finger in your direction. "They're not creeps. They're average dudes and girls. Are you happy now, you absolute psycho?"

"Reasonably," you say with a smirk, hands on your hips, and Digital bursts out laughing.

Kaori is a different matter. She's never been too impressed by your umadol career, mostly because she's not interested into pop music and thus doesn't get the idol subculture. You half-expect her to protest again. The blow never arrives. She fishes her phone from her pocket and taps on its screen. Her nail polish glints a faint pink shade. "Send me your ex-manager's contact details, Ruby. I will not have my newest star suffer a courtroom battle after her debut."

She says this, yet she doesn't bring up the topic in the following days. Case closed, then!

Afternoon, July 11th, 20XX

>>TRAINING TIME (SPECIAL)!

Upon arriving at Kaori's office, you discover she has printed copies of Tabaru and Diamond's mugshots and clipped them to her whiteboard, as if they were bounty posters from an old samurai movie. It'd be amusing, if the characters on display weren't your own roommate alongside the same estranged sister who almost destroyed your spirit in a coffee house months ago.

That, and the fact Kaori seems to be radiating a gravitational well from her stance's core. It sucks up every last drop of playfulness and forces you to sit down in the plastic chair behind the table like a good little girl.

Who was it that said blondes were dumb back at Ten Spices? Was it an American? The idiot has no idea what he's talking about.

"Meisho Tabaru." Kaori flips a button on a remote. A replay of Tabaru's mad dash during tryouts stretches across the whiteboard screen. "A front runner, and only that, according to her regional records, yet she was adept enough to attract the eye of Trainer Nase herself."

The replay slows down, capturing Tabaru mid-stride amidst her frantic break-out run that shot her three lengths ahead. The desperation on her face seems deeper, heavier, amidst this altered time.

"By now, you may have heard of Nase's lineup. You might have watched some of her races live, or in person. Don't believe for a second that Nase's propensity for training chasers and surgers above all else means Tabaru's training will have diminished for it. That idol rival of yours, Smart Falcon, is tucked tight and snug beneath Nase's wings, and Smart Falcon's records as a front runner atop dirt are so absolutely, almost flawless in form, focus and speed, they refer to her as the Silence Suzuka of dirt! No uma ever achieves such a title without years of back-breaking effort on their Trainer's part. Dirt and turf may be two separate battlefields, but they share commonalities in their basics, and someone as intelligent as Nase will have figured how to translate some of Falcon's prowess onto Tabaru. There's a reason why your roommate is tied with Mihono Bourbon and Kitasan Black for the best in your generation, raw-speed-wise!"

Kaori's nostrils flare. Flare! You wouldn't have caught it, if you were human. As you feel a nub of tension in your ears, you wonder. Did one of Trainer Nase's girls steal a win from Jordan at the last moment?

"Next, Satono Diamond." Kaori frowns here, before she wipes the expression off her face. "Brush aside any ire you have with her, Ruby. You're not the first uma to enter the gates with a grudge, and I won't let you be among those who have faltered because of it. No, let me amend that—it is a requirement you keep calm when facing Diamond. We have no room for grudges when clashing against an opponent with Diamond's level of ability."

"No promises," you mutter.

Kaori clicks her tongue. "Excuse me?"

You find yourself pinned beneath her glare. "I, um…"

"I hope that was a joke, Ruby, because you promised me the opposite exactly a week ago. I should also mention that opposite is the attitude I'm aiming to teach you about your opponents in this very important debut of yours."

You raise your hands and quickly say, "It was a figure of speech. My bad, my bad. Please, continue!"

Kaori sniffs and returns to the whiteboard. You press your knees together and arch your back straighter. Alright. No more jokes. You're having a war council here, apparently.

"Gate one is poison for a late surger such as her, which means a boon for us. It's not an inescapable trap, however. Late surgers are perfectly capable of pushing off a gate one slot into their strategy proper, as long as they exercise good timing and patience, which Diamond showed throughout her tryouts, and is reported to have consistently demonstrated through scrimmages and her publicly advertised training sessions. That's before I mention Diamond has also shown signs of pace chaser aptitude. No doubt she is whipping up remedial lessons on that style through that connection she shares with Team Spica via Kitasan Black. Her times were worse than her best friend's, but they were no slouch either. Nor is she an idle soul. This is an uma who will do everything she can to crush you ahead of Tabaru or the others. You must remain vigilant against her!"

Kaori's words boom out, linger, and fade. The ticking of a nearby analog clock sounds almost deafening.

She switches off the projector.

"So. Hearing all that, what will you do now?" Kaori asks.

"Win," you say in a quiet voice.

Kaori raises her eyebrows. "You believe you can win?"

"I can," you reply.

"Is that so? Because I'm not hearing anything."

"I can," you repeat.

"I can't hear you, Ruby!"

"I can!" you shout. "I can win and I will!"

"And how exactly will you accomplish that?" Kaori demands.

You rise to the challenge.

[Racing Tactics check: 118/80 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

"Tabaru is skittish! She's not good under pressure. She's scared of the pack behind her even though she tries so badly to hide it. I'll approach her and pressure her until she snaps! And Diamond! Diamond!" You leap to your feet, slamming a foot on the ground. "My gate picking is so much better than hers. I'm not the one who has to worry about getting cornered against the railing. I have the room to act patient and react to what's going on, whereas she has to spend so much mental energy figuring out how to burst through the others. She's downhill while I'm uphill. You say it's not impossible for her, but she's not impossible for me to conquer, either!"

You stand there, fists clenched, your throat stinging with aridness. Kaori grins. The jilted angle and the sheen of her perfect white molar drip the expression with a thirsty delight.

She's satisfied. You passed this tiny exam of hers.

"Sit down, now. We have the rest of the girls to cover."

It's a hard ask. Your heart keeps pounding. You are burning up with energy. So much so, you want to leap out the window, jump onto the turf and run laps until your cleats crumble into dust now.

[Frenzy has increased by 1.]

But, you obey, since that would involve smashing your perfect facial skin with glass shards, and Kaori obviously has more to say. You also realize Kaori may be deliberately acting the hardass to pump you up faster. She's still the amicable ex-heiress to the rest of the Tracen faculty…you assume.

[Trainer Kaori's Guile check: 12/11 -> Success!]

Kaori gives you a rundown of the rest of the competition. These girls share a couple of slides. They aren't anything to write home about, when compared to Tabaru or Diamond, but they're still umas who cleared their tryouts, attracted their Trainers and polished themselves enough to step onto URA's first stage. Treating them as mere cannon fodder would be a big mistake.

"According to the data, front running and pace chasing remain in vogue. Expect fewer late surgers and end closers, though of course we won't be counting them out."

[Your Trainer provides you with information about the race.]

Name: Your debut

Location: Hanshin Racecourse

Participants: Satono Ruby, Satono Diamond (Pace Chaser/Late Surger), Meisho Tabaru (Front Runner), 8 others (mostly Front Runner and Pace Chaser).

Length: Medium (2000m)

Ground Condition: Firm

Weather: Sunny

Goal: Achieve first place and progress towards Pre-Open races.

Kaori then takes you to a corner of the office, where a set of scales rests next to a cabinet full of personalized medical equipment. She gives you a quick checkup.

[Nutrition check: 65/50 -> Success! +5 EXP.]

Weight, balance, blood sugar levels—all systems are go. You are spared your Trainer's wrath for another day. She does make minor adjustments to your dietary plans—and yes, your sweets ban still holds!

"That is all for the briefing. Let's go to the turf."

[Rolled a 19. It's a Good Trainer event!]

[Trainer Kaori's Psyche check: 15/13 -> Success!]

Kaori breaks some more news when you return from the changing rooms. "I've invited a special guest for today's training. You'll meet her once your warm-ups are complete."

"Cool. How did you do that?"

"I'm friends with her Trainer. You'll see."

Curious, you keep an eye and ear out for movement at the turf's edges. Then, the warm-ups begin and you lose yourself in the flow of your own physique. Ten minutes later, sweaty and warmed up, you lift your head up from your push-ups and notice another uma striding across the grass towards you. Her brilliant form is partially obscured by the bright sunlight. It takes until she's standing a meter away before you're able to tug on memory's string and connect the dots. Once you do, you feel like an idiot.

That wavy brown hair, green ribbon and the confident aura of a modern noble young lady, it can only be…

"King Halo?"

"Correct! Fear not, Satono Ruby! Your expert on the late surger running style has arrived!" King Halo raises her hand to her chin and belts out a haughty, high-pitched laugh ripped straight from her official records.

"We're here too!" A group of umas you vaguely recall as King Halo's fan club comes sprinting across the horizon. "King! Wait for us~!"

This is the gift Kaori has granted you: a private lesson on how to combat late surgers, taught by the uma who wielded that style to conquer the Takamatsunomiya Kinen. At first, you're pensive. Will King Halo's fan club cooperate? The answer is they will. If King Halo accepts you, then so will they. Some of them even apologize when introducing themselves, explaining they fell for the same nasty rumors before King Halo swung by one late afternoon and lectured them into their right minds again.

The practice races that follow are set up in imitation of your debut. King Halo takes the spot closest to the railing, her fan club takes the middle, and you're positioned on the very outside. When Kaori blows her whistle and the races take off, it quickly becomes apparent the admiration from King Halo's fan club doesn't extend towards giving her an easy time on the turf. It also becomes apparent, far more rapidly, that King Halo doesn't need the assistance at all.

Two thousand meters isn't her best distance, she said. These cleats your Trainer made you wear are awfully heavy, she said. Then how is she pursuing you through the pack's center before overtaking you around the final corner every single damn time? You attempt to employ the tactics you said back to Kaori against this new foe, but forcing your body to obey them against your muscle memory leads to a familiar dimension of grindingly slow-progressing mental strain and pain.

After a few races, King Halo sits down with you on the grass. She's unfazed, while you gulp down water.

"What did you notice, Ruby?" she asks, her tone neutral.

"There's…" You wipe your mouth with your sleeve. Golden Generation girl, you remind yourself. She's exchanged time she could be spending teaching her own juniors—Kawakami in particular—to train you. No messing around here, either. "I didn't realize just how much interference there was teeming between gate one and gate ten. Or how fast a late surger could be? You zipped it like a dragonfly on steroids!"

King Halo ignores the compliment, at least on the surface. "And what did I do to beat you?"

"You predicted me. You predicted your fan club too. They weren't holding back—I could tell. Because you sussed all of us out, it probably gave you the confidence to take your time edging your way forward instead of rushing yourself and accelerating in a massive burst," you say, and then pause. Your memory niggles you. "Though, hang on, one time in the last run you did the latter instead…"

"Because?" King Halo prompts.

[(Wits check: 10/7) || (Psyche check: 10/7) -> Success! +5 EXP.]

"…because you knew we were responding to that and played some kind of reverse psychology game! You weren't mimicking us at all."

This elicits a smile of satisfaction from King Halo. "Exactly right! You're a hard worker after all. The essence of a late surger lies in acceleration and timing, yes, but also prediction and restraint. A roundabout path of clear air is worth more than pinching a hundred meters into an insurmountable blockage halfway through the track. The former leads into a place where I can run; the latter means I lose immediately. Mispredicting or overconfidence is the downfall of a rookie late surger."

"My opponent isn't a rookie anymore," you say.

"Perhaps. But this sort of know-how takes years to accumulate. Satono Diamond will be an open box compared to me," King Halo says, puffing her chest up with pride. "And she'll do herself a disservice to underestimate you."

It's acknowledgment from another Golden Generation member. You smile, warm and fuzzy, at that.

King Halo then takes a stick and begins drawing patterns in the dirt. The first is a slice of curved racetrack. "We shouldn't get ahead of ourselves too much. Now, there are some common tactics we employ. The first is to let pace chasers such as you and front runners run first. And the shortened distance by sticking to the rail is an advantage…"

You follow along, taking notes in a notebook.

In the distance, you spot Kaori chatting with that muscle-bound Trainer who helped you scare off those nasty men. Kawakami's is there by that other Trainer's side, peering through binoculars at King Halo.

Eh, checks out.

[You've gained insight in combatting the Late Surger aptitude! -10 threshold to checks regarding Late Surgers in the next race only!]

After King Halo and her fan club bid you goodbye, Kaori then puts you through the usual training. It's more of the same.

[All racing skills have increased by 1.]

[You remembered Grass Wonder's teachings! Acceleration has increased by 1.]

[Your Speed and Stamina progress meters have increased by 5%.]

More answering questions while you perform exercises. More quizzing on your tactics.

[All racing skills have increased by 2.]

[Your tagged racing skills have increased by 1.]

[You remembered Grass Wonder's teachings! Acceleration has increased by 1.]

She's not so harsh as to attempt to push you past your limits…

[All Attribute progress meters have increased by 5%.]

[All tagged Attribute progress meters have increased by 5%.]

…but neither does she grant you any mercy. She brings up shogi positions. You want to cry.

[Racing Tactics, Frenzy and Nutrition have increased by 5.]

[Your Speed, Psyche and Wits meters have increased by 10%.]

And Kaori's idea of rest?

[Rolled a 12. It's an Average teammate event.]

Public relations training for you and Jordan, starring Agnes Digital. There's a certain irony about how sunnily she beams at the two of you while your knees are about ready to buckle.

"Pick a card, Ruby. Any card." Digital presents a full deck of cards in her open palms.

You take the topmost one and reveal it. The words ANNOYING JOURNALIST are written in a clean, neat font atop a Jack of Hearts. Digital takes it, reads it and nods. She drops the deck of cards in her pocket and hunches herself over.

You blanch. This is the usual Digitan pose, clasped hands and all, but that usual manic glint in her eye—a lechery lurks there, tinged with acidic, soul-devouring greed.

"Hey. Hey! Satono Ruby! Satono Ruby! I'm from the Jane Doe URA Times. I'd like to ask a few questions. Yes, questions!" A shiver runs through her frame. "Wanna make a statement about the controversy surrounding your mom?"

Goddesses, she puts Kaori's early persona shift to shame. The shadow of numerous oily-nosed, acne-ridden older human men, plus a few women, twitches before you. There's no arena security to throw them out, nor a fellow idol to tell these paparazzi to piss off.

[(Composure check: 86/70 && Persuasion check: 122/80) || (Psyche check: 10/12) -> Success! +10 EXP.]

Luckily, you remember your old training and quell your instinctual reaction.

"I'm aware of the controversy. And I don't have anything to add right now," you say, turning aside and walking away from Digital.

"Same with her," Jordan adds, waving with a hazy hand. "Talk to our media team, 'kay?"

Agnes Digital straightens herself up. She flashes you both with a double thumbs-up. "Ding-ding-ding! Good deflection, and excellent withholding of aggression and defensiveness. Full marks here!"

Digital pulls out the cards again. The next card off the top is OVERLY ENTHUSIASTIC STAN. Digital immediately drops into her roleplay mode.

"Oh my gosh. Oh my golly gosh gosh! S-s-Satono Ruby in the flesh!" she squeals. A frantic, half-grinding, half-slurping noise escapes from the corners of her wide, wide smile. "Nothing could make me happier than this…oh goddesses…I have no more needs. Take me to nirvana now!"

You step back. On second thoughts, Digital might not be acting here.

"If it's not too much trouble for your magnificent self, could I get your autograph?" Digital holds up the card she drew with trembling fingers.

[Underground Umadol: Exists.]

"Sure!" You mimic reaching into your tracksuit for a pen.

Digital breaks out of the act. "Bzzt! Wrong!" she shouts.

"What?" you yelp.

Digital crosses her arms together, shaking her head with a reluctant frown. "Remember the pamphlets? You're not the one holding the pen. They're meant to hand it to you! Secondly, this is not the time or place for autographs. We're in the racecourse's pavilion, remember? Autographs are only allowed in specific areas, such as the signing booths post-race!"

"That's a thing?" you ask.

"The URA is strict about these policies. They don't want more incidents like Air Groove and the random camera flash. And they'll especially be keeping a close eye on you, Ruby!"

It hurts your professional pride to hear that. Digital does have a point. Seems like you need more than just a mere refresher…

[Your Psyche progress meter has increased by 10%.]

Finally, Kaori provides her own special training lesson. What is it?

5.7: Your impending day (again)

>>[TrainingTime1] I want to work on my agility (+20% to Speed progress; +5 to Dodge and +3 to Dancing.)

>>[TrainingTime2] Perform extra gate training. (Gain a temporary Advantage die.)

EXP: 60/240 (1 LEVEL UP PENDING…)

Mood: Great

Hell is an unending, horrendous, and abstract concept too advanced for your modern socmed-infused brainrotted mind to consume. Kaori, on the contrary, is a human adult woman and very well aware of it, as evidenced by the sliver of it she's thrust you into without mercy.

"Go, Ruby, go! Just a few more seconds. A few more seconds!" She stands on the balls of her feet at the edge of the practice track, her clipboard and pen thrown on the ground so she can cup her hands around her mouth. Her excitement glimmers through a semi-palpable golden thread, slicing through the blurry reality that is you sprinting your tail off down the practice turf's homestretch. Her voice tears through the rushing wind. "Two hundred meters more at the same pace, and your time record's broken. You can do it—go, go, go!"

Behind you, Jordan beelines for your tail, as if she caught you raiding her nail cabinet.

If, say hypothetically, there was an alternate version of you on a segway riding at the same velocity, who is unfazed and well-rested and not inflaming her own brain with mass amounts of adrenaline and cortisol, you believe she'd have words for Kaori. Specifically, that alternate would acknowledge Kaori may be reusing parts of the same methodology she once trained Jordan to win her Autumn Tenno Sho. That alternate would then drop into a cynical bent, stating Kaori was starstruck by the complete and utter dominance her insanely unfavored trainee demolished the rest of the competition with and has been chasing the same high ever since. Don't forget that she's former corporate. She was born and bred to seek victory at all costs. The training was so effective Kaori successfully rebelled against them and sought glory on her own terms.

She doesn't see the immense social and journalistic pressure upon you as a negative. Rather, a challenge she will overcome—with your help of course. Being marked for death by Tracen's biggest nail-polish fanatic is but a small sacrifice for future rewards, obviously.

As this reflection passes through your head, a second alternate version of yourself raises her hand and rebuts the first alternate, saying the first alternate's words were harmful, rude, and, most importantly, nonsensical. Did she see the competition? Something must be done to counteract Tabaru's great escape. A third alternate nods her head, sagely, and reminds everyone an uma only utilizes thirty percent of her maximum potential in her everyday life. There is much potential inside of you to be excavated. The first alternate says that's a load of bullcrap; the second alternate chastises; the third shrugs her shoulders, and this is when a fourth alternate, who has freckles and a baggy sweater and sounds suspiciously like the very real ghost you've been chatting with in your dreams, kicks down the door and politely requests we all take a gander at these boring lines and circles she's drawn on Kaori's whiteboard.

Everyone oohs and aahs and the first alternate is stuck in the corner where no one can see or notice her because she's cynical and actually quite, sort of, very much so rude, disparaging your Trainer like this.

You don't mention any of this to Kaori, by the way. There is no answer you can give that doesn't involve your lungs screaming themselves raw.

"You did it, Ruby! You did it!"

Kaori bounds over as you kiss the dirt. She grabs one floppy arm and hauls you up without an ounce of effort. She thrusts her stopwatch into your face. "Look at this!"

Half a second under your previous time for the record. It occurs to you that you've crossed the finish line.

"Sixth favorite, my behind. Tabaru and Diamond won't know what'll hit them!"

A thump hits your shoulder. Jordan, most likely. You smile weakly, flash Kaori the thumbs-up, then stagger over to the benches circling the turf to grab your water bottle and collapse again on the spot.

[Your Speed progress meter has increased by 20%.]

[Speed meter has reached 100%. Speed has increased by 1. All Speed-scaling skills have increased appropriately.]

[Your Speed progress meter has reset back down to 0%.]

[Dodge has increased by 5.]

[Dancing has increased by 3.]

[Gate training was performed. Gained a temporary Advantage die for the next race!]

The rest of the events regarding your debut follow at a rapid pace, once Kaori has let you off her hand-sewn torture-training roller-coaster ride.

The first item on Kaori's itinerary is enacting a full socmed ban on your humble self until the debut is concluded. She's no tyrant; she lets you put out a single tweet on your Umastagram, followed by a confirmation of when and where you will be meeting up with your old fans. She informs you through Jordan's socmed skills of the general opinion regarding your debut: disbelief, the usual hate, predictions on your imminent collapse the moment you leave the gates, and scatterings of genuine curiosity, like diamonds in the pig's pen. Other than that, it's goodbye doomscrolling for the next week.

The same applies to any phone calls. If it's not from a number you recognize, you block it. If it is, you forward it to Kaori. The only person who should be answering the phone about you is her, and her alone. She does note that she cannot physically enforce this ban upon you, since she always despised when her phone was confiscated at her old private school and refuses to pass on that trauma onto her own students—a principle you heavily respect. You end up agreeing with her, on both the socmed and phone bans. You'd say losing Umatok would hurt, if not for the fact your headspace is nowhere near doomscrolling at present.

Hanshin Racecourse, gate exercises, Kaori's war plans and velocity calculations. These are the ideas that dominate your head, cast under Hanshin Racecourse's wide, wide green grass fields. You are so absorbed in thinking about your debut you begin to neglect your daily academy life. Homework scrapes by with half-finished worksheets. Classes become opportunities to sneak peeks at racing VODs from overseas umas. At mealtimes, you shovel your food into your mouth with almost mechanical precision, the cloying porridge and sizzling chicken meshing into one mess through a temporal, culinary tapestry.

As the days fly by, the rest of your peers prepare for their own debuts. They succeed. Kawakami Princess, Rice Shower, Cheval Grand, Vivlos, Happy Meek—they're a row of dominos falling down, the sides labeled with a golden wreath and a fat number one. Most of them run with the gaggle of Trainers you rejected, ironically enough.

In the face of these rival victories, Tabaru goes dead silent. You're not much for words either. Put aside the envy those girls didn't have to face each other, and what remains are cowboy standoffs between you and her over the lunch table. She runs a simulated version of you in her head. You run her honored self in yours.

The sole consolation for both of you is that Diamond must be dealing with an even worse time, being the Satono heiress and all.

Throughout the chaos, Kaori grinds away at her desk. She calls Manager Suzuki and goes to meet him at a Tokyo cafe to receive permission for your old umadol outfit. She tells off journalists on the phone. She hires a reputable security expert to perform another check on your health and equipment, then write a statement to show to the URA officials. She organizes disguises for Team Rasalhauge, secures a deal for URA-sponsored motels and purchases transport in the form of a hired van and green car Shinkansen tickets.

You learn about all of this on said Shinkansen ride. Kaori might be divorced from the Mifune family coffer, but her own past corporate salary combined with a general frugality outside of clothing luxuries has earned her a steady financial cushion. Her cut of the first-place prize money will more or less equalize these expenditures, she explains. And you will claim first place, yes?

Takarazuka greets you through the train windows. Kaori stands up first to fetch the luggage, as the train grinds to a halt. Disguises on, girls, because some influencers are mad enough to camp outside stations. Not to fear, though. Team Rasalhauge still has their brain cells intact. You all successfully leave the train station and make it to the motel, unscathed.

Unscathed, and early. The race isn't actually for two days.

This isn't a schedule mixup, however! Kaori brought you here a few days in advance on purpose. You have a few important tasks to complete. The first is a set of reps through a park, then an outdoor running track, to acclimatize your respiratory system to the region's atmosphere. Sounds overkill to the average spectator, but to your lungs, the Takarazuka air tastes warmer, moister, heavier. The shift is more than enough to unsettle a pebble inside of you, tripping you over by a fraction of a second in the middle of a run. You walk it back and figure out how to adjust, Hanshin Racecourse standing a dozen kilometers away.

Jordan, meanwhile, waves the rest of the Team Rasalhauge goodbye and goes shopping, karaoke dancing and gallivanting about the city with her Takarazuka friends. She never fails to send you selfies of 'her and the besties!!!'. Blegh. Talk about overload. You don't need more temptation to open Umastagram, damn it. It's already bad enough Machan hinted at a couple of girls growing legit interested in your debut back at Tracen.

At least you get to make those faces in the privacy of your own motel room. Kaori chose to sleep in a separate room, trusting you could tuck yourself into bed without breaking an ankle, which you are grateful for, as it means more room to practice a few quick dances for the future fan meet-and-greet. She does request you to visit hers for her self-cooked breakfasts, though.

The days tick down, then the hours.

Finally, the long-awaited morning arrives.

17th of July, 20XX. Life awakens you with a ray of sunshine tickling your nose through the gap in the thick motel curtains.

You pull the covers off and stand up. You head to the bathroom, yawning and still wearing your pajamas. The toothpaste tastes of frothy mint.

It's funny. Back when you were living in coffin motels, you often fantasized about the morning before your debut. You were producer, director, and scriptwriter, rattling away at your mental keyboard about a nerve-wracking, tail-sweltering rush to the finish, like prepping for an end-of-year concert hopped up on steroids. Racing is a complicated business, after all. Surely, during the onset of this third act, you'd tear your mind in half trying to attach all the bells and whistles of your craft together. You'd miss a shoe, forget a cleat, anything to stretch out the tension as tense strings played themselves in the background. In the end, you'd find the equipment, including the miraculous trinket sent by your long-lost mother, and ultimately muster up the courage to dash out of the hotel and charge straight to the racecourse—fashionably late, as any good protagonist is, obviously.

Reality is a plain slice of white bread, in a metaphorical and literal sense. Kaori's breakfast for you is oatmeal, bananas and yogurt. A bevy of stable, helpful proteins and carbohydrates. Not exciting. Definitely not movie material, unless it's some boring documentary. You prefer it, regardless, now knowing how a race's preparation actually starts. Once you reach the open level, you'll qualify as a true authenticity consultant. Saya's about to get serious competition!

Smiling to yourself, you finish the meal. You get dressed back in your room, check your equipment one last time, and head down to the motel parking lot with Kaori and Jordan for the van.

The ride to Hanshin is swift. One moment, you're staring out the van window to the park opposite the motel. The next, you're spying the silver half-domed roof of Hanshin's main building. The van slides to a stop inside the special parking spaces allocated for competitors. The door clicks softly as you open it.

You stand on the concrete. You inhale the fresh morning air. It's a clear, sunny day, with wisps of white clouds dotting the sky. Hubbub sounds off in the distance, punctuated with announcements for racers or special attractions. The time is seven in the morning.

"I can't believe you changed in the car," Jordan says. "You underground gals are nuts."

There's no real meanness in her tone. On the contrary, she's wearing a grin, despite her 'better' judgment. The whole of Team Rasalhauge is brimming with excitement. And it only gets better once you leave the car park and stride up towards the gates.

The burgeoning crowd doesn't notice at first. Eventually, someone squints close, puts face to memory, and the peace is shattered. There's staring, there's pointing, there's narrowing of eyes and scowling and cameras flashing. Click-click-snap-click.

You almost chortle out loud. Instead, you stand straight, legs shoulder-width apart. You slap on a serious gaze, befitting of an uma on a mission, then outstretch your arm and hand and raise them both as if you're en route to a crescendo. The silent song escapes your lips.

[Dancing check: 137/50 -> Success! Trivial: +0 EXP.]

Behold, ye followers and fellow competitors of the URA! The daughter of the worst uma to ever live approaches from the horizon, clad in the battle garb of Tomorrow is FAITHFUL's third album: Nogitsune! Gaze upon this kimono, its thread woven from the silks of fallen comrade umadols, its hues drenched in the deep, bright crimsons of the accursed lover's pulsation. Cuts to the ohashori have merged the kimono into the realm of dress, granting dexterity and free-flowing fervor to the rebellious spirit. Purple breaks up the monotony; its cravat is a display of chosen vanity, and a combo of a golden obi and dark cloud patterns promises fortune for the audience—just not in a fashion an actual miko would approve of.

But opulence and pretty colors aren't what this uma is about, oh no. With fingerless gloves on her hands, and solid geta sandals to cause noise and slam down your territory, she's strutting around with the grace and expertise of a true professional.

You mimic drawing a katana...

[(Swordplay check: 58/50) || (Frenzy check: 99/60) -> Success! +10 EXP.]

...which causes an elderly grandpa to shiver, his hands grasping for a non-existent bayonet. A wide smile breaks free. Behold, again and yet again, O Hanshin Racecourse. An umadol and a racer—this is who Satono Ruby truly is!

Now capture her in those flashing lenses, if you must. The more she is framed, the more permanent her legacy shall become.

[+4 to Chaos Alignment.]

[+3 to Dark Alignment.]

Kaori strides up to you. She's a vision of handsome beauty, with that impeccably coiffed blonde hair and that smart, knee-length shirt dress. She grants the crowd a polite smile, catching the eye (and hearts) of several young men. Then, she meets yours.

For the past month, you and this Trainer have prepared yourselves to the best of your respective abilities, using the best of your shared knowledge. The only thing left on your plan is to run your best on the track. Despite the increased thumping of your heart, it is a wonderful, liberating feeling.

"Ready?" Kaori says.

You grin back. "You betcha."

Full of confidence, you step through Hanshin's gates.

5.8: never before frigid flows

[(World Resonance check: 116/150) || (Insight check: 10/12) -> Failure.]

The moment you step across the thin line dividing pavement from courtyard proper, a spell breaks.

You don't notice it at first. So flushed with nostalgic adulation, you carry yourself forward through the crowd's edge with a joyous, mind-numbing momentum. It is only after you've walked more than a dozen steps into the crowd's rim that the spell's effects finish clawing their way down your back neckline, turning what once tickled into a foul, squirming queasiness.

The courtyard before you is wrong.

The thought strikes you through pure instinct, a steel bar slamming against your synapses' shared spine. Bewildered, you shake your tail back and forth, then suck down a breath. It ends up as a lurching gasp, the same kind you made when you woke up at midnight while suffering a cold, trapped in a coffin motel pod with nothing but your phone and cheap konbini paracetamol to keep you company. You clutch the spot above your heart, and feel it rattle against its sinewy prison.

[Mood has dropped to Normal.]

[(Composure check: 80/110) || (Guts check: 10/11) -> Failure.]

Nothing changes. The courtyard before you is wrong.

No, the unpanicked fragment of your mind objects, what are you talking about? The courtyard is normal. Look at it. Crowd in front, blue-tinted windows high up, a signpost guiding newcomers and bulbous trees amidst the greenery. They're all present. They're exactly as you saw them in photographs and during the trip before today, to boot. Nothing has changed.

But no amount of rationalizing will avert your senses from reality. The instincts that made you an entertainer and a scavenger are shrieking at you to look closer. To perceive harder. The atmosphere. That's risen several degrees, raising the air from warm to a muggy, moist, cloying heat that shimmies down your exposed sleeves and sweats the skin down below, as if it were raw meat left to wither in the sun. The wind whips up, its undercurrent bearing an oily tinge. Logos of past uma stars glower at you from posters and T-shirts, and the nearby trees rustle, their leaves devoid of their luster, their sounds not a whistle, but a hissing, scraping grinding, like television static stretched to breaking point.

"Ruby."

Kaori. Her voice seems drowned, echoed. You're hearing her from the end of a long corridor that's not here.

"Ruby. Are you alright?"

"Yeah," Jordan adds, several seconds later. "Say something. Everyone's staring."

"I…"

You look at them. Their faces are plastic, their eyes made out of glass.

"I was just…"

You trail off, a faint slickness leaking out of the side of your mouth. Jordan scrunches up her nose; it must be drool, but you're not paying attention, instead listening to your guts convulse through your lower abdomen.

The courtyard is wrong. From top to bottom, from grayscale to color, it is a diorama of reprehensibility, superficially whole from afar, yet its angles and facets teem with loose hives of vermin when examined close. Except, that itself is a falsehood. No one around you seems affected. The nearby mom and dad with their squealing daughter push through the crowd whilst apologizing, unaware that they have been tarred with a rancid coat of paint. The same applies to the security guard nearby, and the woman with the notepad, camera and barking dog. Kaori and Jordan, too.

Ergo, the observation folds inwards. You are what is wrong, not the courtyard.

Why?

What explains this sickness that has enveloped you, squeezing liquid fortitude out from the fabric of your existence? You've lived through your fair share of hardships on the streets, so you understand from experience what you are sensing is neither hunger, nor thirst, nor heartbreak.

An answer soon arrives. The most inordinate for Kaori, yet the most obvious for you. The mere outline sinks your stomach down a pit. Your knees shake, your weight sliding down a slope. Your face must have gone stark and pale. Kaori has rushed forward; Jordan too, both blocking you away from the cameras. They must be speaking to the crowd as their hands reach down into their bags for phones, water bottles, or calming oils. Kaori's mouth moves in the shape of a question.

What's wrong?

You want to answer. You cannot. You don't want to entertain the thought of saying anything, because how—this—where would you—

Nerves flare up, snapping your neck eastwards.

There.

[World Resonance check: 110/40 -> Success! Trivial: +0 EXP.]

Like an introverted newbie in the concert hall, a gaze exudes from a figure lurking in the crowd. The silhouette is that of a regular uma. Its hair is long and parted to the sides; a bandage is attached to one cheek below. It is clad in a nondescript charity set of a top and jeans. Its entire form is wreathed in a tar-black darkness, her existence a blot on the landscape, as if someone had cut her out from a swamp and pasted her here with old tape. Tendrils rise up and writhe from its hair and clothes, soot-covered dandelions, and it locks eyes with you and mouths something, the eye sockets hollow white, the lips stretching far too wide.

"Ruby?" Kaori asks again. "Are you alright?"

Razor blades at the edges of the molars.

You tear away from Kaori and run.

Running, as it turns out, proves impossible.

The crowd has grown closer and denser these past few minutes, whether by its own natural flow or leering fascination at you. Bodies jam the path back to the front gate. Stuttering to a halt, you glance around for direction, and notice the statue of the Three Goddesses standing off to the side in the distance. It's blurry, yet you are compelled towards it, and start in its direction. Another mass of hard shoulders and flabby limbs blocks your path. Pure reflex seizes control, lifting your own hands up, but it's mindlessness turning what should have been gentle taps into hard shoves; footsteps into primal, frantic breakaways. Your new sandals emit loud clip-clopping sounds on the movement. It's the exact opposite of how a proper umadol should behave, yet you couldn't care less.

The aberration pursues you. Its gaze resumes leering at the crook of your neck. It gains two steps every one of yours. The gaze transforms from a pinprick, to a doctor's needle, to a railway spike, a vise's grip, a silk noose, your neck tightening and shrinking and your breaths choking.

Just as it's ready to merge with your flesh, the gaze vanishes.

You stagger to a halt and glance back over your shoulder, sweat trailing down your front, dread beating your heart. No one's there. There's nothing except the slice of pavement, a group of curious passersby glancing in your direction, and a teen pounding at a faulty vending machine. You wait, a hand clutching the silk covering your chest area, and the scene stays the same. Seconds pass.

It's gone. You must have outrun it with your newly minted agility.

"Ruby!" Jordan screams from down the road. "Get the heck back here!"

The sight of her, pissed off and screeching like normal, lets you relax. You open your mouth to breathe a sigh of relief.

An ear-splitting sound explodes from behind you. An amalgamation of a broken femur and metallic screeching. You scream and whirl and almost leap out of your skin at the aberration hanging off the fence before you. Its body contorts around the chain-links, elbows and arms squeezing through holes that should have chafed its skin raw. The divider up its back, its abdomen and chest arced towards you, gravity tugs its hair downwards in a ghastly curtain. Eyeballs swivel like cue balls in pockets, the bloodshot veins visible at this distance, but they're nothing compared to its bodily matter. The flesh—slimy, pulpy-soft flesh tearing and hanging from shreds like rotten party streamers.

Your nose catches the whiff of rotten pus, and the scream you emitted dies into a nauseated gag.

You know what this is. It's a—

Don't say it.

This is a—

Don't say it. Don't say it, you stupid girl, you scream at yourself. Those—those things shouldn't be around in daylight!

The aberration gulps down its own breath, and lets out another screech, loud enough to make your eardrums bleed. You stagger against the back of an old tree, where your head rams against the hard bark. Pain. It forces you down into a cowering, curled position, the heavy kimono sleeves held up as a flimsy barrier between you and the monstrosity.

This is a—this is a—

It can't happen. Not today. Not at your debut, of all places. Please, just oh please, not now!

You go down your kimono's front, searching for the sole object that has always brought you solace. What is excavated is only half. A lump of silver, consisting of a bullet at one end, a misshapen chunk of frozen, liquid ore with a pistol barrel jutting out the top. The silver chunk prickles your fingers through its vibrations, wisps of light coalescing around it.

Despair grips you. The chunks fall from your fingers, and tears gather in your eyes. The Nightmare's Horror twists its neck, sees the droplets' reflections, and smirks.

[Mood has dropped to Bad.]

"Ruby!"

You look up. Kaori. She runs down the pavement towards you in her heels. Her hair whips behind her, a mask of pure concern on those powdered and prettied adult features. She waves a hand in greeting. A pang of sheer relief falls through you, before you realize what's obstructing the path between you and her.

The Horror looks at you. It licks its lips, its rotten body trembling.

"No," You vocalize.

It trembles further, then climbs up the fence towards Kaori, its limbs contorting and shifting up and down like a long, spindly spider's. It flexes its right hand and juts out claws from its pitch-black fingertips.

"Don't!" you cry out. "I'm over here! I'm the one you want!"

The Horror ignores you. It raises its arm, reaching back for full momentum. The claws glint in the bright sunlight. Kaori runs closer, closer, within range, and the Horror swings back and you leap off, almost stumbling across your own outfit, to charge forward at it and scream—

"Stop."

A singular woman's voice, cutting through the din. Gentle footsteps approach, of solid loafers atop hard concrete. The Horror freezes in place, then whips its head around, hissing.

"I said, stop. I believe that's enough out of you, you foolish rapscallion."

That voice. You know that voice. Its presence, the waxy scent of olive flowers and rustling grass—it's exactly like that terrible afternoon from the tryouts.

Plain Jane approaches through the gap in the surrounding crowd, clad in her Tracen uniform. Her arrival is so sudden that you almost mistake her for having popped out of thin air. She doesn't come to you first, instead walking straight up to the Horror and gazing at it, in the same way a vacation-goer would at a zoo exhibit.

"It is considered bad manners by most to interrupt a young lady as she's en route to the ball, where she will become the season's cherished diamond. You would not be such an existence if you recognized that, so I shall state it plainly: damaging my dear protege or anyone living within the baseline reality at this stage, is impossible, and you are well aware of that."

The Horror gnashes its teeth at Plain Jane.

"So please, do us a favor, and give up," she finishes.

Heart pounding, you review Plain Jane's words. The Horror can't hurt anyone? That's nonsense, you want to shout at your senpai. Just look at the damn thing. Plain Jane spoke her statement with such confidence that your panic stops in its tracks to let the rest of your mental faculties catch up. Come to think of it, if the Horror wanted to hurt someone, assuming you, why didn't it ambush you from behind? Why didn't it rip you to shreds when it had you cornered against the tree, or in the middle of the courtyard where the entire crowd was watching? That's the course of action congruent with its hatred of you. Unless, of course, it was physically unable to.

You shoot a look at the Horror, then at Plain Jane, who nods her head, now wearing a calm smile. "Walk towards the statue of the Three Goddesses, Ruby. Then, you shall understand."

The questions explode down the base of your throat, yet you are so relieved, so gobsmacked by the rise and fall that you obey without hesitation. Kaori and Jordan call out again. The Horror screeches a warbling, corrupted raven's cry. You ignore them all.

It's a short walk, cutting through another busy throng of spectators and winding down a small incline surrounded by more manicured trees. It's a quick trip, made more so by your insistence to fast-walk and numb your senses to your surroundings. You plod and you push and soon the statue rises into view.

The detailed history of the Three Goddesses…

[History check: 47/80 -> Failure.]

…escapes you at present. They're old and divine and possess a heavy relation to umamusume racing, enough for the URA to erect statues at all of their racecourses. Hanshin's iteration of the trio is especially elegant, with it carved from high-quality limestone and erected on a podium above the ring of cooled water splashing below. Like Tracen's own statue, water feeds up from a mechanism inside the statue, then dispenses from an amphora held in each of the Goddesses' hands.

As you approach, you notice umamusume and fans flicking yen coins into the fountain waters for good fortune towards themselves or their favorite racers. That's normal. The statue is also surrounded by a gigantic bubble that brightens the scenery inside and around its surrounding areas, the outer rim shimmering with trails of stardust-esque sparkles. You feel an urge inside of you at the statue, akin to a magnet's pull. That's not normal.

Hesitant, you stop in your tracks. You glance over your shoulder once more.

"Go on," Plain Jane prompts. "They are waiting for you."

You close your eyes. You grip the front of your kimono tight enough to almost tear the fine silk. The garment suffocates instead of liberating, its corners pooling with cooling frantic sweat. You order yourself to bid yourself goodbye. A little longer, you offer yourself. A little longer, and Senpai will drop the answers you desire. She will not lead you astray. Swallowing your trepidation, you enter the bubble of light surrounding the Three Goddesses' statue. The effects hit you immediately. The sickness that captured you back at the courtyard is wiped away. A gentle, calming sensation embraces you. It is all the hugs, all the massages, all the gulps of water from a strenuous workout.

The lighting, the hues here, they're all normal. Reality is normal. You crouch down, back bent over, and heave.

"Ruby!" Kaori runs through the bubble's edges, oblivious.

"Damn it, Rubes! You're on camera, you know that?" Jordan is close behind. She too passes through the bubble, unaware of its existence.

The Horror is a different story. Through your brief walk, it has crawled around and across the various trees, signposts and vending machines lining the pavement, frothing and howling at deafening volumes in an attempt to throw you off. Never once has it succeeded. Never once did those claws rend your tissue asunder. The best it could do was send a hand through your shoulder, leaving behind a cold, slimy tingle through your shoulder. Nothing was grabbed. Nothing was torn out.

The Horror lunges towards the bubble. Its fingers slice through the thin filament, which shimmers, then radiates a pale white light. A high-pitched whine fills the air, followed by a sharp white flash, and suddenly the Horror is flung back, red-hot burns blotching its chest with steam trailing out the ends.

Plain Jane approaches the edge. She stands there, hands clasped in front.

"The Goddesses cherish the wishes of their mortal kin. From the primordial ages up to the modern day, through war, through myriad strife, they have blessed the fields and the tracks where competition raises her flag, encouraging all who set out to run, run and run," Plain Jane says. "They are far less merciful to abhorrent creatures who attempt to harm their kin before the starting gates fly open."

She stares down the Horror, dragging out a pause, before speaking again. "Are you literate, my ungainly friend? Do I need to repeat myself again? You shall not be harming my dear protege today."

The Horror spits on the ground, then limps off. You watch it squeeze down a crack in the ground and vanish from sight. The way its body contorts to fit will appear in your intrusive thoughts. Then, it vanishes from sight.

Safe. The area around the statue is safe. No Horror can enter here without harming themselves.

[Mood has increased to Normal.]

Plain Jane didn't let you down.

You walk up to her, smiling. "Sen—"

She whirls around and raises a finger to her lips. "Don't speak to me."

"But—"

"I am intangible, like the Nightmare's spawn. I do not exist in the boundary between the fantastical and the mundane, just as your Team Rasalhauge, except on opposite ends of a spectrum. You, however, are different. You should pretend that what you just did was a normal occurrence, lest they view you as mad and ship you off to an asylum."

In other words, dangle an excuse that will explain why you broke away from your team and sprinted off in a random direction. That's a bit much, isn't it, Senpai?

"Ruby!"

But there's no time to gripe. Your team has finally caught up to you. Kaori is the first to reach your side, whereupon she gives you a quick check-over from head to toe, paying special attention to your ankles, thighs and feet. When she's convinced you haven't injured yourself, she marches you over to a bench and sits you down.

"What the hell was that?" Jordan asks, when she arrives.

"Yes. Please explain why you ran off without permission," Kaori adds.

You gulp. Now that they're standing before you, with zero threat of death by evil monsters from another dimension, the situation is…awkward, to put it politely.

Somehow, by embracing the miraculous clarity that has enveloped your mind, you manage to eke out an excuse.

[Persuasion check: 116/100 -> Success! +10 EXP.]

"Sorry, Kaori, Jordan. I thought I saw an old rival in the crowd," you say.

It takes a moment for your words to register.

"Are you serious?" Jordan exclaims.

"Yep."

"For real? For real, real?"

You nod again. "Yep, yep."

Jordan's hands open and close. She's ready to strangle you.

"Rival? You never mentioned this in our planning meetings," Kaori says.

"It was from a long time ago. Relatively, I mean. I was a sprout from the countryside, who couldn't tell a guitar from a bass, and I did a lot of stupid crap as a rookie idol. One of these older girls from an up-and-coming group took pity on me and gave me advice. Well, she called it advice; half of it was venting. And a quarter of it was sorta uncalled for. But it was legit useful and it helped me get to a position where I earned money semi-consistently, so I'm super grateful to her and I just wanted to say my thanks."

"And that involved tearing away from us like a maniac?" Jordan asks.

"It was…" You pause. "A unique greeting of ours."

"Huh?"

"We re-enacted a scene from the first video we made together. I'm the terrified falsely accused prisoner in it, and she's the kitsune wearing a mask."

Jordan boggles at you, jaw slack. "Are you girls insane?"

"We're underground idols." you reply. "So, kinda?"

Kaori taps her forehead with her index and her middle fingers. She sighs.

"Ruby, while I won't say it's wrong to meet up with a long-cherished friend from the past, I would have greatly appreciated it if you informed us of this before we arrived. It's no coincidence this happened, from the sounds of it. We could have prepared an excuse for the surrounding crowd, instead of hastily blowing out PR talk around the lines of being slightly overwhelmed and hesitant and then chasing out to you. People have taken photos, you realize? Photos of your panicking that we lack the resources to deal with," Kaori says. Her hands are folded. "And that is without getting into how your behavior has reflected on the rest of Team Rasalhauge, and Tracen for that matter. Do not mistake the institution's adoration for utter and complete worship."

A maiden's fury leaks out from the contours of that strained smile.

It's unfair. How were you supposed to know the Nightmare would invade and send you into a flurry? You don't feel like getting into an argument with Kaori, nor is this the time and place for such an event, so you swallow your pride and bow your head.

"I'm sorry, Trainer!" you say, "I hadn't seen her in so long, and I missed her so much, so I guess I lost control of myself. It won't happen again and I'll think of something to cover it up, I promise!"

It wasn't as if Kaori could predict the Nightmare, either. She can't comprehend it.

Kaori shakes her head, huffing.

"Thank goodness this incident was at least before your race, and not afterwards. Once we win, it'll easily be overshadowed. I'm more relieved you're unharmed, anyhow."

She relents. She's taking your words at face value. To be fair, they are genuine. Hotaru was your rival. Hotaru did sit you down and rant into your face, under the impression you were eighteen and not a secretly terrified thirteen-year-old. She was in an up-and-coming group…the exact same one you signed for, actually. Lying is wrapping the truth in a peculiar context. Thank you, you miserable, awful adults of Japan!

Plain Jane winks at you, grinning. She nods towards the Three Goddesses' statue. You hop up from your seat, all smiles again.

"Anyway! Now that we're here, let's take some photos of our own. Right? Right?"

Item number four on the list has shot up the stack. Kaori and Jordan glance at each other, at you, and give up.

"The Nightmare has roused from its slumber."

Plain Jane opens as such after you have moved yourself into position behind the Three Goddesses' statue, your visage and theirs visible in Kaori's handheld camera. The camera clicks; you side-eye Plain Jane, who smiles.

"With the debuts of most of your peers having come and gone, I had hoped there'd be enough room to at least earn a solid victory under your belt before you were summoned to action, but I suppose it is in character for the Nightmare to kick down the door this way," Plain Jane says, pursing her thin lips. "It does exist to spread dread and terror after all."

By now, you've accustomed yourself to reality. The Horrors have invaded Tracen and you, or them, can't do much about it. It pisses you off in a major, vicious fashion. Were the Nightmare was a living being, you'd jump on it with your cleats and stomp it to bone fragments and putrid stupid grey matter lumps. But, you can't, so you grudgingly recite cheki motions as you fantasize about sandbags.

The question is why? Why is the Nightmare here? Has it infested Tokyo in a disastrous arrival of the end times? These are prompts you type on a notepad app on your phone, its frame dangling in your grip at the correct angle, so that Plain Jane can crouch down and peer at them.

"It would be more accurate to say that it was summoned. The races of the mortal times bring much excitement, indeed, yet that is born from the hopes for a spectator's chosen uma to succeed. And from that hope, despair, or the fear of such, lies in the shadows. A prayer clutched in the man who never before believed in God; a Trainer unable to watch her struggling trainee—such doubts and fears spread forth in spiderwebs of noxiousness, affecting the moods of others, planting ash piles of negativity that smolder upwards, attracting the Nightmare like a vulture towards carrion. It is made worse by greed: the gamblers in their dens, the policemen walking past with one eye closed," Plain Jane says.

Are you screwed?

"No. The Nightmare's presence at Hanshin is weaker compared to your last bout. The Three Goddesses watch over us regular umamusume, extending favor to humanity as per their ancient friendships, while the Goddess of Victory enforces her stranglehold on the races and the setup those entail. The sun has long been a symbol of warmth and comfort. Together, these forces push back the Nightmare and its Horror to the extent that they are unable to manifest their full power. They are intangible, like classic ghosts. The most they can do is lash out and scream, perhaps inject irritating tactile sensation or create distractions via foul aromatics, but they will be unable to harm your physical form or your soul."

For example, that Horror would have tripped you up and made you twist your ankle?

"Correct?"

That…wow. Oh no.

"There's a silver lining. At such low potency, they will be unable to interfere with the track, nor the race itself."

At least there's another place safe in Hanshin.

Jordan then demands you take a selfie with her. She spends two minutes fussing over your hair and complexion. The question, that's a relief; also it doesn't sound like how physics works, is left floundering for that long.

"Fire eliminates water, and light beats darkness. Think of these deities as a set of new elements on the periodic table. They clash together and strengthen or weaken each other, akin to chemical bonding." Plain Jane leans from her new seat atop the second goddess's amphora, craning her neck downwards. "Or, hold on now, mayhaps I use another metaphor? Do you know what these chemistry terms mean, Ruby?"

You send her an emoji of an uma sticking her tongue out, followed by a frowning emoji.

"Apologies. I am only attempting to inject a spot of levity in this worst-case scenario."

You grow somber. Is it really that bad?

"It is. Hanshin is not alone in my aforementioned description of that breeding pile of negativity. I dare say Horrors shall manifest in the background of every single one of your races."

Horrors. Plural.

"Indeed."

She gestures towards the bubble's edge.

Your nation's citizenry are at least obedient enough not to interfere with your team in broad daylight. That does not preclude them from observing. Indeed, a crowd almost as large as the previous has gathered, its participants gawping and clicking and doing the usual business. And, similar to before, within the cracks of those regular flesh-and-blood bodies, aberrations seep through. Umas that crawl with their foreheads grinding against the pavement. A balloon in the shape of a human head, its rope too long and thick and pinkish to be a string. A pocket of a snowstorm, through which a distant, lithe feminine form stands, wrapped in white. Birds with CCTVs for heads circle the fringes.

These aberrations, too, are spectators, born from the hidden underbelly of everyone else's existence. Like their compatriot, they dare not approach the Goddesses' territory. They pin you with their gazes, and they wait with predatory patience.

"You live in two worlds, Ruby. One of the supernatural, one of the mundane. Both dinghies must sail through the night, unabated."

You yank your head around at her. Is she seriously suggesting what you're thinking?

"Yes, I am suggesting you proceed with your plans for today, as a regular uma would, and not run straight to the change room and hiding there. You must not show fear to the Horrors, for they are born on the Nightmare and will feed on such. Otherwise, they will detect your fragility, register it, process it into an identification of weakness; and once you enter the Nightmare's true depths, they will devour you with their newfound knowledge and destroy your soul," Plain Jane says. Her tone is cool, her expression a mask of granite. "For your sake, Ruby, and to avoid faltering at the first step, face down the Nightmare at Hanshin here, and withstand their assault, if not conquering them to the utmost."

You listen to this, and instinctively shudder.

"Ruby?" Kaori asks.

"I'm okay," you say, "I just…remembered something cringe."

"Pot calling the—" Jordan shuts up as Kaori taps her on the shoulder.

Plain Jane refuses to listen to your insult. She hops off the statue and strides up next to you.

"I suppose the Nightmare's appearance here is a blessing in disguise. These grounds will serve as a tutorial for the real exploration."

Why? Why is this happening to you?

"Reality isn't a television show, Ruby. The villains will not wait for the heroines to carefully craft their plans in the background."

Somewhere in the distance, a wounded animal howls.

>>THE NIGHTMARE HAS AWOKEN…

[New Active Effect registered.]

Horrors will now manifest in the near vicinity of large-scale, daytime-occuring racing events. The Horrors are intangible and cannot harm either your physical form or your soul. They can still generate tactile sensation, sound and aromas in attempts to disrupt you.

EXP: 80/240 (1 LEVEL UP PENDING…)

The Nightmare does not tolerate breaches into its system. It will attempt to destroy you by sending all manner of entities at you, ranging from monsters, and artifacts to anomalous locations and traps. To overcome this, you must perform Nightmare Exploration, in which you receive the entities the Nightmare commands, and deal with them while attempting to derive as much reward and bear as little physical & mental damage as possible.

Rules:

At the beginning of Exploration, the QM rolls 2d12 for X amount of events, where is X a number determined by difficulty and plot context (minimum: three). Unlike Daily Life events, Nightmare Exploration uses a modified table with different weights and the result capping out at Good. Critical failure and critical hits are preserved as normal.

Each Exploration event will present an entity for you to deal with. The narration will analyze the entity, make a judgment in accordance with any skill checks & its Observation Rate (i.e. how much knowledge you possess about the entity's nature, behavior, history, etc.), and present 1+ choices. Choices will either result in a positive, neutral or negative outcome, depending on how the entity functions.

Not all entities are necessarily hostile to you, but a great deal of them will be.

An Exploration event's difficulty is based both on the dice results and the overall Exploration Difficulty, which will be presented at the before the events are rolled.

Events are singleton and do not affect each other. There will always be an option to engage. There will always be an option to attempt to disengage. The higher the Observation Rate, the more knowledge about the entity is displayed, the easier interacting with it becomes, and the further along its story shall progress. Observation Rate cannot decrease. Some choices, however, may increase it faster than others (minimum increase: 15%). Some choices offer active Attribute checks. (ATTRIBUTE_LEVEL + a 2d12 die roll) must equal or surpass a numerical threshold, which will be listed. The intensity of penalties for failure will be listed as well. Passing these checks will generally offer positive results. These checks' difficulties may increase or decrease, dependent on skill checks. These checks are unaffected by starting gate Advantage/Disadvantage dice, unless they involve starting gates. Future teammates can perform for skill or Attribute checks in your stead.

The QM is well aware that RNG may be frustrating. To compensate, a Global Observation Rate will be offered. It will increase at a slower rate (minimum: 8.5%), but will do so regardless of an Event's outcome. Once it reaches 100%, it will provide high amounts of information for the most unknown entity in the lineup, then reset back down to 0%.

Your Health and Morale are at risk during Exploration. Positive outcomes may restore either; negative outcomes may reduce either.

Health is now calculated through 1 + (Highest Physical Attribute / 2). Morale is now calculated through 1 + (Highest Mental Attribute / 2). Health and Morale will be gained or lost in values of 1 and more. Health and Morale levels will persist past Exploration and into any content that occurs within the Nightmare. Checks within Exploration events do not grant EXP. Engaging with an event will always grant 5 EXP, with further rewards determined based on choice outcomes. (e.g. emerging unscathed, maxing out an entity's Observation Rate, etc.).

Further rewards can include:

More EXP Temporary stat buffs Permanent stat increases Advantage starting gate dice Further Observation Rate increases Special items Information

Penalties for failing can include:

Lost EXP (if Godolphin's Grace from your regalia is somehow disabled) Temporary stat debuffs Permanent stat debuffs (if Godolphin's Grace from your regalia is somehow disabled) Disadvantage starting gate dice Loss of information Nightmare Exploration event table:

ValueResult2Critical failure.3-7Bad8-12Below-Average13-19Average20-23Good24Critical success.

I will now display an example event and have you vote for it. Following that, I will roll 4 Exploration events. As Plain Jane mentioned, this is merely the tutorial, so the difficulty won't be high and the penalties not severe. I will also convert Critical Failures into merely Bad results for this Exploration only. Lose too much Health and Morale, however, and your performance will be affected afterwards…

A statue of the Three Goddesses. It stands proud and regal above the podium surrounded by the crystal-clear water. Their forms are elegant, bearing the composed, compassionate strength of ancient umamusume.

To the left, discipline and strength. To the right, grace and generosity. In the center, courage and individuality. Though you are not well-learned in their stories, you understand the virtues they uphold without a second's thought.

The manifestation of the Three Goddesses aided you before. Therefore, they will not harm you.

They would never harm any of their kin, unless it was for a good reason.
