>>I choose the foundation. (Threshold: 18; Penalty: Very Low)

Discipline to endure a rigorous regime, grace to acknowledge the self's shortcomings, and the courage to contest your opponents. What do these three boons possess in common?

Or, more accurately, from what foundational desire do the goddesses' kin beg their boons for?

You know the answer. The foundation of these is the desire to win. The utmost faith that out of the dozens, hundreds, of umamusume living under the URA's shadow, it is you, and only you, who shall seize the winner's crown at the end of the race, despite statistics to the contrary. It may encroach in the territory of blind faith, yet without this desire, an umamusume's efforts shall only bear empty fruit, when the time comes to advance that final step.

You tell your answer to the statue.

The left side trembles with a grudging appreciation. The right side vibrates with satisfaction. The center side exudes a lapping warmth, then the scent of a grassland far headier, sweeter and older than any stalk or stem you've seen. The invisible gift that deposits in your hand is the shape of crude white cloth.

Perhaps, this desire was born within the roving packs of ancient umamusume during the primordial ages. The leading umamusume was said to be the smartest and the strongest, back then.

[-10 to the threshold of Skill checks occurring in the next race's homestretch.]

You step away from the statue, satisfied, and wait.

Nothing happens.

It seems this statue, and any future occurrences, will be safe zones within the turbulent Nightmare.

Bzzt. Bzzt. Pew!

An uma-sized figure shoots past. It smashes through the gap of time between a fan's thumb flicking and his camera clicking. The cheki photo spits out on the screen, displaying a frustrated grimace etched on your features, and the other seventy-five percent of the photo obscured by a messy black-and-blue blur.

"D-id I do something wrong?" your fan whimpers. The man has the hunched posture of the average office worker, hunched shoulders with neck extended outwards. The cardboard headband bearing your chibi form sits loosely round his sweaty forehead. "Oh God, did I press record instead of photo again?"

"No, no!" You quickly turn your frown upside down. You glance around, trying to catch the blur, but it's gone. Again. "Uh, uh…maybe a fly landed on the back of my neck or something."

Your fan quivers his lip. "Do I smell? Should I come back later? A-am I ruining your day, my goddess?"

You quickly calm them down, because some of these guys have worse self-esteem than you did as a middle schooler, despite them being twice as old.

"No, no, no! Nothing of the sort. I promised you a photo together, my good man, and you're going to get it." You say that, then wink and pat him once on the back, causing him to shiver in hopeful delight.

Of course, it's easy to say that, when in reality it's this photobombing freak's fault. It's woven in and out of this umadol meet-and-greet, its velocity whining like a laundry machine threaded through the center of a spinning needle. It dashes, dodges, and bounces while curled up in imitation of a living pinball.

Bzzt. Bzzt. Bzzt bzzt bzzt bzzt pew!

[Instinct check: 40/70 -> Failure.]

[Inspection check: 37/70 -> Failure.]

Pew!

The thing is so fast that you can barely discern anything regarding its form. The photos are no help either. They're normal on a technical level, but in each one so far, you appear as if you bit your tongue at best or tasted a lemon at worst.

Pew, pew, pow pow pow!

Popping sounds rattle off, machine gun fire translated from the core of a larynx. Ethereal grit and dust kicks up in a gale, smacking you on the back of the head. Your concentration is once again ruined.

[Damage taken. -1 Morale.]

Metal keys ring in a tinny jingle.

No, incorrect. They're glass beads clacking instead. Ahead of you: ghostly toy balls bounce and roll, vanishing into the air. Flashes of soft kimono fabric disappear around the trousers of adults, then tiny footprints plant grooves in the road, deep enough to wonder if the concrete is secretly the soft dirt found in fields during the humid months. The scent of old copper trails behind childish, girlish giggles.

The copper may taste bitter, but where it is found, fortune is soon to come around.

[Gained 10 EXP.]

Following the footprints out of curiosity, you discover a fellow Tracen uma staring in the same direction, looking lost. At first, you see it as a coincidence, since the number of umas who can perceive the otherworldly at Hanshin can be counted on a single hand.

The uma turns to you and looks troubled. They walk up to you.

"Did you hear something weird too?" is the gist of what comes out of their mouth.

You stare at them.

Snow in summer. It shouldn't be possible, yet snowflakes rain down from a vertical slice of land and sky, coating the view in front of you in white. Within the swirling winds, a figure in a muted gray kimono stands, the sash melting into the falling snow.

She smiles as the chill whips forth. It bites down your loose sleeves and bites at the tender flesh below. It chips at your bloodstream. You open your mouth and feel it fill with frost that doesn't exist.

[(Guts check: 10/11 || Nutrition check: 67/95) -> Failure.]
